*Notes on the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's auxiliary structure*
(per [@MG-Sphere2026 §5.2, §11.2]): one law $dx_4/dt = ic$; one
action-quantization postulate (substrate carries one quantum of action
per fundamental oscillation cycle, defining $\hbar$); three inputs ---
(i) global uniformity of $+ic$ across $\mathcal{M}$; (ii) Schwarzschild
self-consistency $r_S = \lambda$ identifying
$\ell_* = \ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^3}$ via Newton's $G$ as third
dimensional input; (iii) Compton-frequency coupling, condition (M).
Under this construction, $c$ and $\hbar$ are derived expressions of the
framework rather than fundamental inputs; only $G$ remains as a
dimensional constant. The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework is the only
framework in which every row is a theorem; other frameworks borrow,
postulate, or add structure post-hoc, and all other frameworks take $c$,
$\hbar$, $G$ as three independent fundamental constants.

### Foundational Principle: $dx_4/dt = ic$ and its Descent to $x_4= ict$ {#ssec:FoundationalPrinciple .unnumbered}

Throughout the present unified treatment, the object is the McGucken
Principle $$\label{eq:McGuckenPrinciple}
\boxed{\;\;\frac{dx_4}{dt} \;=\; ic\;\;}$$ which is a
*physical-geometric law*, not a postulate, axiom, formal trick, or
interpretive convention. Its physics is the statement that the fourth
dimension $x_4$ is expanding outward, at every event of spacetime, at
the velocity of light $c$ in a spherically symmetric manner. The factor
$i$ in
[\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"} is the perpendicularity marker
recording that $x_4$ is geometrically perpendicular to the three spatial
directions $(\hat{x}_1, \hat{x}_2, \hat{x}_3)$; it is the geometric
statement that $x_4$-advance is a $90^\circ$ rotation away from purely
spatial advance [@MG-McGSpace; @MG-FatherSym].

**The physical state of the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$: the
fourth dimension expanding as a spherically-symmetric wavefront at $c$
carries wavelength, frequency, phase, and therefore action --- so $c$
and $\hbar$ are twin properties of the one advance.** This is the heart
of the principle, and it is the heart of the present paper. The McGucken
Principle
[\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"} states that the fourth dimension is
expanding as a spherically symmetric wavefront at velocity $c$. A
wavefront expanding at $c$ is a *wavefront* --- a physical, propagating,
geometric structure with intrinsic wavelength, frequency, phase, and
therefore action. The substrate's intrinsic length is $\ell_*$, the
substrate's intrinsic period is $t_*$, and the principle fixes their
ratio as $c = \ell_*/t_*$; per one action-quantization postulate (one
quantum of action accumulated per fundamental oscillation cycle of the
substrate), the substrate's per-tick action is $\hbar$; per
Schwarzschild self-consistency $r_S = \lambda$, the substrate's
wavelength is identified as $\ell_* = \ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^3}$
[@MG-Sphere2026 §5.2, §11.2]. *The velocity $c$ and the action quantum
$\hbar$ are not two independent constants of nature that happen to
appear together in physics; they are twin properties of the one
$x_4$-advance, with $c$ as the advance's spatial-temporal ratio and
$\hbar$ as its per-tick action.* The Lorentz-invariance of $c$ and the
empirical universality of $\hbar$ are the same kind of theorem: the
substrate is the same substrate in every inertial frame, with the same
wavefront expanding at the same velocity with the same per-tick action
quantum.

**The spinor lives on the wavefront that already has the Compton
frequency.** Matter, in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, is
identified by the matter orientation condition (M): a $x_4$-oriented
standing wave at positive Compton frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ in
the $+ic$ direction [@MG-Dirac; @MG-McGSpace]. The spinor $\psi$ of the
Dirac equation is the field-theoretic encoding of a particular kind of
structure *on the wavefront itself* --- the $x_4$-perpendicular
standing-wave structure at the Compton frequency, with the chirality
(left vs. right) selected by the unique single-sided action of spatial
bivectors preserving (M)
(Theorem [82](#thm:SingleSided){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SingleSided"} of the present paper). The wavefront
expands at $c$; the wavefront carries the Compton frequency
$\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ as the rate at which a $x_4$-oriented standing
wave winds perpendicular through $x_4$ at three-rest
(Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"} of the present paper); the spinor is
the natural representation of matter's $x_4$-orientation under the
half-angle action that the perpendicularity of $x_4$ to three-space
forces. *The Dirac equation does not need to be discovered or derived
from a separate principle --- the spinor lives on a wavefront that
already has the Compton frequency, and the wavefront is what
$dx_4/dt = ic$ generates from every event.*

**The dynamics were in the premise.** The standard practice of
contemporary theoretical physics is to postulate a Lagrangian, derive
equations of motion via variational machinery, and supply the dynamics
of the theory through the postulated action. The McGucken Principle
inverts this practice: *the dynamics were in the premise*. The principle
$dx_4/dt = ic$ is itself a first-order dynamical equation --- a rate of
change of $x_4$ with respect to $t$, equated to a specified value. The
premise is dynamics. No separate Lagrangian or Hamiltonian postulate is
needed to bring the dynamics in; they are already there, in the rate
$ic$ on the right-hand side, with its two sources ($i$ as
perpendicularity marker, $c$ as wavefront velocity) supplying the
algebraic-symmetry and geometric-propagation from which all of Channel A
and Channel B derivations descend
(Theorem [5](#thm:TwoSourceRHS){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:TwoSourceRHS"} of the present paper). Lagrangian,
Hamiltonian, Schrödinger evolution, Heisenberg evolution, Dirac
propagation, Maxwell's equations, Einstein's field equations --- all are
theorems descending from the one premise that the fourth dimension is
expanding as a spherically symmetric wavefront at $c$
[@MG-Master2Chains-2026; @MG-Lagrangian; @MG-Sphere2026].

*The physical state of the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, stated in
one sentence:* $x_4$ expanding as a spherically symmetric wavefront at
$c$ carries wavelength, frequency, phase, and therefore action; $c$ and
$\hbar$ are twin properties of the one advance; the spinor lives on a
wavefront that already has the Compton frequency; the dynamics were in
the premise. This is the heart and soul of the framework, and the source
of every theorem in the chain that follows.

The McGucken Principle traces its written record to Dr. Elliot
McGucken's NSF-funded UNC Chapel Hill doctoral dissertation appendix
(1998--99) on time as an emergent phenomenon arising from $x_4$'s
physical expansion [@MG-Dissertation1998], with conceptual antecedents
in undergraduate research with John Archibald Wheeler at Princeton on
Schwarzschild time dilation and Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen / delayed-choice
experiments (late 1980s) [@Wheeler-LetterMcGucken]. It was developed as
Moving Dimensions Theory in the period 2003--2006, formalized in five
FQXi essay-contest papers
[@MG-FQXi2008; @MG-FQXi2009; @MG-FQXi2011; @MG-FQXi2012; @MG-FQXi2013]
(2008--2013), consolidated in books
[@MG-LTDBook2016; @MG-RelativityDerived2017; @MG-Entanglement2017]
(2016--2017), and is currently the subject of approximately forty
technical papers at <https://elliotmcguckenphysics.com> (October
2024--present). The priority of $dx_4/dt = ic$ as a written equation of
motion of the fourth dimension dates from 1998--99
[@MG-Dissertation1998], with the FQXi-essay sequence 2008--2013
[@MG-FQXi2008; @MG-FQXi2009; @MG-FQXi2011; @MG-FQXi2012; @MG-FQXi2013]
establishing the public archival record. The Father Symmetry priority of
$dx_4/dt = ic$ over every principal symmetry of contemporary physics is
established at full rigor in [@McGuckenSymmetry2026] via nine theorems
(Theorems 30--38) corresponding to the nine major symmetries (Lorentz,
Poincaré, Noether, $U(1) \times \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathrm{SU}(3)$,
quantum unitary, CPT, supersymmetry, diffeomorphism invariance, string
dualities); the present paper realizes the gauge-group instance in
detail. The original gauge-groups paper [@MG-GaugeGroupsOriginal] stated
the $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ derivation in shorter form; the present treatment
expands that derivation and unifies it with the colour, hypercharge,
Higgs, and predictions content. The present paper draws on this corpus
throughout.

**Channel decomposition.** The principle
[\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"} carries two distinct channels of
physics, both essential to the present derivations:

-   **Channel A (algebraic-symmetry):** the imaginary unit $i$ as
    perpendicularity marker generates the local $U(1)$ phase symmetry
    $\psi(x) \to e^{i\alpha(x)}\psi(x)$ of $x_4$-spherical wavefronts
    [@MG-McGSpace], supplies the canonical commutation relation
    $[\hat{q},\hat{p}] = i\hbar$ [@MG-CCR], generates the
    Heisenberg/Schrödinger evolution structure of quantum mechanics
    [@MG-QM; @MG-Hilbert], and through the suppression-map analysis
    [@MG-Wick] unifies all twelve "factor of $i$" insertions across
    quantum theory (canonical quantization, Schrödinger evolution, the
    canonical commutation relation, Dirac propagation, path-integral
    weight, the $+i\epsilon$ Feynman prescription, Wick substitution,
    Fresnel diffraction, $iS_M = -S_E$, the $U(1)$ gauge phase, spinor
    complex structure, the KMS condition) as a single feature of $x_4$'s
    perpendicularity. In particular, the $+i\epsilon$ Feynman
    prescription receives, via [@MG-SecondQuantization2026 §VIII.2], an
    explicit operator-level geometric interpretation: positive-frequency
    modes (matter-oriented, $+I k x_4$ phase) propagate forward in
    $x_4$, negative-frequency modes (antimatter-oriented, $-I k x_4$
    phase) backward, with the infinitesimal damping $+i\epsilon$
    selecting the direction $dx_4/dt = +ic$ rather than $-ic$. The
    Feynman-Stückelberg picture is thereby made literal: time-ordering
    in the propagator is the directionality of $x_4$-expansion.

-   **Channel B (geometric-propagation):** the velocity of light $c$
    together with the spherical symmetry of $x_4$-expansion forces the
    spherical wavefront --- the McGucken Sphere
    $\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}(p,t)$ --- with full $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ symmetry
    as a Channel B feature [@MG-FatherSym; @MG-Huygens], thereby
    supplying the geometric-propagation (Huygens' principle, Second Law,
    spherical expansion of $x_4$ from every spacetime event).

**The four-fold ontological structure.** The McGucken Principle
[\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"} organizes the kinematical universe
into a canonical four-fold structure [@MG-McGSpace; @MG-FatherSym]:

1.  **Absolute rest in $x_1 x_2 x_3$:** a massive particle at spatial
    rest has its entire four-velocity budget directed into $x_4$-advance
    at the velocity of light; the particle's $x_4$-phase accumulates at
    the Compton frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$.

2.  **Absolute rest in $x_4$:** a photon, on a null worldline, has share
    $v_{x_4} = 0$ in the universal $x_4$-expansion (from
    $v^2 + v_{x_4}^2 = c^2$ at $v = c$), and instead "rides the
    wavefront" of the $x_4$-expansion. The coordinate rate
    $dx_4/dt = ic$ is unchanged at every event the photon crosses; what
    vanishes is the photon's share of the expansion, not the expansion.
    The photon is at absolute rest in $x_4$ while moving at $c$ in the
    spatial triple.

3.  **Absolute motion:** the $x_4$-expansion at $ic$ from every
    spacetime event is the absolute reference for all motion; this is
    the geometry of the cosmological frame.

4.  **CMB frame:** the isotropic cosmological $x_4$-expansion identifies
    the cosmological microwave background frame as the unique frame in
    which the $x_4$-expansion is observed as spherically symmetric to
    all distant observers --- the empirical realization of the
    absolute-motion frame.

Every theorem of the present treatment traces to the active expansion in
items (i)--(iv); the coordinate label $x_4= ict$ is the mere integrated
shadow of
[\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"}, not the postulate.

**The descent $dx_4/dt = ic \Rightarrow x_4= ict$.** The familiar
Minkowski/Wick-rotation expression $$\label{eq:Wickform}
x_4\;=\; ict$$ is *not* the object. Rather,
[\[eq:Wickform\]](#eq:Wickform){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:Wickform"} is the elementary first-integral of
[\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"} obtained by integrating in proper time
from a source event with the convention $x_4(t_0) = 0$:
$$x_4(t) \;=\; x_4(t_0) + \int_{t_0}^{t} \frac{dx_4}{dt'}\,dt' \;=\; \int_{t_0}^{t} ic\,dt' \;=\; ic(t - t_0),$$
yielding $x_4= ict$ when the origin is set at $t_0 = 0$. Equation
[\[eq:Wickform\]](#eq:Wickform){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:Wickform"} therefore descends as a derived corollary of
[\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"}, and inherits its physics
(perpendicular fourth dimension expanding spherically at $c$) from the
rate equation. The constraint-projection
$$\Phi_{\mathrm{M}}\;:=\; x_4- ict \;=\; 0$$ that appears throughout the
present paper (in particular in the McGucken-Higgs treatment of Part IV)
is exactly the statement that the world-tube of any worldline lies on
the integral surface of
[\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"}; whenever $\Phi_{\mathrm{M}}= 0$ is
invoked below, the reader should understand it as shorthand for "the
integral consequence of $dx_4/dt = ic$."

**The Minkowski signature as a consequence of $dx_4/dt = ic$.** The
Lorentzian metric signature $\eta = \mathrm{diag}(-1, +1, +1, +1)$ used
throughout the present paper is not imposed as an independent assumption
--- it descends from
[\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"}. The argument, drawn from [@MG-Dirac
§II.1] and reproduced here for self-containment, is as follows. The
infinitesimal invariant interval built from $(dx_1, dx_2, dx_3, dx_4)$
in the McGucken-Euclidean coordinates is
$$ds^2 \;=\; dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 + dx_4^2,$$ which superficially
appears Euclidean. But substituting $dx_4= ic\,dt$ from
[\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"} gives
$dx_4^2 = (ic\,dt)^2 = -c^2\,dt^2$, so
$$ds^2 \;=\; dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 - c^2\,dt^2,$$ which is the
Minkowski interval with signature $\eta = \mathrm{diag}(+1, +1, +1, -1)$
or equivalently $\mathrm{diag}(-1, +1, +1, +1)$ after time-first
indexing. The Lorentzian signature is not imposed --- it emerges
directly from the factor $i$ in
[\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"}. The Wick rotation, conventionally
presented as a calculational trick for converting between Euclidean and
Lorentzian frameworks, is in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework the
statement that real proper time $t$ and complex coordinate $x_4$ are
related by the principle itself, with the twelve $i$'s of quantum theory
unified by the suppression map of [@MG-Wick].

**Matter as a $x_4$-standing wave at Compton frequency.** The McGucken
Principle
[\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"} identifies matter, geometrically, as a
standing oscillation in $x_4$ at the Compton frequency [@MG-Dirac
§II.2]: $$\label{eq:ComptonWave}
\psi(x_4) \;\propto\; \exp(i k x_4), \qquad k \;=\; \frac{mc}{\hbar}.$$
For a particle at rest, all of its kinematical content is the
$x_4$-expansion at rate $c$; the rest energy $E = mc^2$ is the rate of
$x_4$-phase accumulation per unit proper time. A photon, having no rest
frame, is a pure $x_4$-expansion mode with $k_0 = 0$; it "rides" the
$x_4$-wavefront at $c$ with no standing-wave component. This
interpretation of matter as a $x_4$-phase structure --- not a point
particle sitting in spacetime, but a phase structure carried forward by
the $x_4$-expansion --- is central to the chirality assignment derived
in Part I, the electroweak symmetry-breaking pattern derived in Part IV,
and the no-proton-decay prediction of Part V.

The matter-orientation constraint, in the rigorous algebraic form of
[@MG-Dirac §IV.2], is the statement that an even-grade multivector
$\Psi \in \mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ carries matter $x_4$-orientation at
Compton frequency $k > 0$ if there exists a rest-frame amplitude
$\Psi_0 \in \mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ such that $$\label{eq:OrientationM}
\Psi(\mathbf{x}, x_4) \;=\; \Psi_0(\mathbf{x}) \cdot \exp(+ I k x_4), \qquad k > 0, \tag{M}$$
with the multiplication performed on the *right*, and where
$I = \gamma^0 \gamma^1 \gamma^2 \gamma^3$ is the Clifford pseudoscalar
of $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)$. The corresponding condition for antimatter is
$\Psi = \Psi_0 \cdot \exp(- I k x_4)$. The constraint (M) is the
algebraic specification of how the McGucken-Principle's directed
expansion enters the spinor structure; the choice of $x_4$-orientation
distinguishes matter from antimatter, and the right-multiplication picks
out a preferred side of bivector action on $\Psi$. As established by
[@MG-Dirac Theorem IV.3], single-sided (left) action is the unique
action on matter fields that preserves the constraint (M) across all
bivector generators, and it is this uniqueness that forces the
half-angle in the spinor rotation --- the geometric root of
spin-$\tfrac{1}{2}$.

**The pseudoscalar $I$ as the geometric embodiment of $i$ in
$dx_4/dt = ic$.** A central identification, established in [@MG-Dirac
§III.4 and §VIII.2] and used throughout the present paper, is that the
Clifford pseudoscalar $$\label{eq:PseudoscalarI}
I \;=\; \gamma^0 \gamma^1 \gamma^2 \gamma^3$$ satisfies $I^2 = -1$ (by
direct Clifford-algebra computation using
$\{\gamma^\mu, \gamma^\nu\} = 2\eta^{\mu\nu}$ with the Lorentzian
signature derived above), anticommutes with every vector $\gamma^\mu$,
and commutes with every bivector $\gamma^\mu \gamma^\nu$ (for
$\mu \neq \nu$). $I$ serves as a natural "$i$" for the 4D Clifford
algebra. In the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, this $I$ is the
geometric embodiment of the $i$ in $dx_4/dt = ic$: the $i$ appearing in
matter-field phases $e^{i k x_4}$ in
[\[eq:ComptonWave\]](#eq:ComptonWave){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:ComptonWave"} is $I$ in disguise; when the Dirac equation
is written in full Clifford-algebraic form via the Hestenes formulation
[@Hestenes1966; @Hestenes1967; @DoranLasenby2003], the complex structure
of quantum mechanics emerges as the pseudoscalar structure of 4D
spacetime. The three perspectives --- the $i$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$, the
pseudoscalar $I$ of 4D Clifford geometry, and the imaginary unit of
quantum-mechanical phase --- are the same object viewed from three
angles, unified by the suppression-map analysis of [@MG-Wick] as a
single feature of $x_4$'s perpendicularity.

**The McGucken corpus machinery: an inventory.** The derivations of the
present paper consume the following pre-established McGucken-corpus
theorems as inputs, every one of which is itself a theorem of
$dx_4/dt = ic$:

1.  The **McGucken Space** $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}$ and its physics as
    the source space generating spacetime, Hilbert space, and the
    physical-arena hierarchy [@MG-McGSpace]; the foundational paper of
    the corpus, establishing the McGucken Principle as the generative
    law of the framework.

2.  The **McGucken Sphere** $\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}(p,t)$, the spherically
    symmetric wavefront of $x_4$-expansion from every event $p$ at
    proper time $t$, with $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ as its maximal connected
    compact isometry group [@MG-McGSpace; @MG-Huygens].

3.  The **McGucken-Dirac equation** and the four-component spinor
    structure, with the linear-square-root requirement on the McGucken
    Operator $D_{\mathrm{M}}= \partial_t + ic \partial_{x_4}$ forcing
    the Clifford anticommutation
    $\{\gamma^\mu, \gamma^\nu\} = 2\eta^{\mu\nu}$ [@MG-Dirac §III]; this
    is the rigorous mathematics of "Dirac's reasoning applied to the
    McGucken Operator."

4.  The **$x_4$-reversal-as-charge-conjugation theorem** [@MG-Dirac
    Theorem VIII.7], which establishes that the McGucken-Dirac equation
    $(\gamma^\mu \partial_\mu - mc/\hbar)\psi = 0$ transforms
    covariantly under $x_4\to -x_4$ if and only if $\psi$ transforms by
    the charge-conjugation operator $C = i\gamma^2 K$; this is the
    identification that feeds the chirality lemma of Part I.

5.  The **matter orientation constraint (M)** [@MG-Dirac §IV] and the
    single-sided-preservation theorem [@MG-Dirac Theorem IV.3]:
    single-sided (left) action by spatial bivectors is the unique
    transformation preserving (M) across all bivector generators,
    forcing the half-angle spinor rotation that is the geometric root of
    spin-$\tfrac{1}{2}$.

#### The Wick-rotation conundrum and the McGucken Principle as its physical-principle resolution {#ssec:WickConundrum .unnumbered}

Within the orthodox formalism of quantum field theory, the relationship
between the Lorentzian operator formalism and the Euclidean
path-integral formalism has remained unsettled for the entire period
since the introduction of the Wick rotation
[@Wick1954RotationToImaginary]. Woit [@Woit2024Unification] has recently
articulated this unsettled status sharply, identifying it as one of the
technical conundrums of the contemporary unification programme. We
engage Woit's articulation directly, both because his statement of the
conundrum is precise and because his proposed mathematical apparatus for
addressing it (Osterwalder--Schrader reconstruction with a distinguished
imaginary-time direction) overlaps with the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework's pre-existing identification of the physical direction at
every spacetime event.

###### Woit's statement of the conundrum.

In his July 2025 talk at the "Rethinking the Foundations of Physics"
conference, Woit articulates the technical problem as follows
[@Woit2024Unification at 1:03--1:08]:

> "Here's the problem when you try and do this in quantum field theory.
> If you change time on \[the field operators\], you're conjugating by
> the Hamiltonian operator. ... The Hamiltonian, its eigenvalues are the
> energy. ... So now your problem is that you've got these two
> operators, $e^{\tau H}$ and $e^{-\tau H}$. If $\tau$ is positive, this
> one is going to make sense ... whereas this one is going to be a
> problem. ... There's just a fundamental issue, which \[is that\]
> everything we know about quantum field theories and the operator
> formalism, you can't analytically continue the theory. ... But the
> other formalism you have for writing down quantum field theories has
> the opposite. If you write them down as path integrals, if you go to
> imaginary time, it's Euclidean spacetime, then the path integrals are
> $e^{-\text{(something positive and large)}}$ and they make perfect
> sense. ... But if you try and do this in Minkowski spacetime or real
> time, then ... you're integrating this wildly varying phase over an
> infinite-dimensional space, and this just doesn't make sense in any
> sense as a measure or as a real integral. ... There is no such thing
> as any kind of full theory formalism which depends upon complex time
> analytically and allows you to analytically continue between time and
> imaginary time. There just is no such thing."

Woit's diagnosis is correct as a statement within the orthodox
formalism. The operator formalism, organised around the Hamiltonian $H$
with spectrum bounded below but unbounded above, supports analytic
continuation in only one direction of $\tau$. The path-integral
formalism, organised around the Euclidean action $S_E$ with weight
$e^{-S_E/\hbar}$ as a real measure, supports a well-defined integral
only in Euclidean signature. The two formalisms are related not by
analytic continuation but by reconstruction theorems
(Osterwalder--Schrader [@OsterwalderSchrader1973] in the rigorous
direction; Wightman-to-Schwinger [@Wightman1956] in the reverse
direction). What is not a theorem of either formalism is a single
complex-analytic object that interpolates between them.

###### The conundrum, restated.

The conundrum can be stated in three asymmetries:

1.  **Formalism asymmetry.** The operator formalism works in Lorentzian
    signature; the path-integral formalism works in Euclidean signature.
    Each is well-defined in its own signature; neither analytically
    continues to the other.

2.  **Direction-of-time asymmetry.** The Lorentzian operator formalism
    has no distinguished direction of time --- positive and negative
    timelike cones are symmetric in the construction. The Euclidean
    path-integral formalism, by contrast, requires a distinguished
    direction (the imaginary-time direction) for Osterwalder--Schrader
    reflection-positivity and for reconstruction of operators and
    states.

3.  **Spinor asymmetry.** For scalar fields, the reconstruction is
    well-understood. For spinor fields, the relationship between the
    Euclidean spinor representation (where
    $\mathrm{Spin}(4) = \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_R$
    factorises) and the Lorentzian spinor representation (where
    $\mathrm{Spin}^+(1,3) \cong \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{C})$ does not
    factorise) is more complex. Woit [@Woit2024Unification at
    1:09--1:18] emphasizes that the spinor case is where "something
    really unexpected happens" --- specifically, the distinguished
    gamma-matrix corresponding to the imaginary-time direction (which
    Woit denotes $\gamma_0$) interchanges left- and right-handed
    Euclidean Weyl spinors and breaks the $\mathrm{SO}(4)$ symmetry to
    the spatial $\mathrm{SO}(3)$.

###### What Woit's mathematical framework supplies, and what it does not.

Woit's positive proposal [@Woit2021; @Woit2024Unification] is to start
in Euclidean signature with
$\mathrm{Spin}(4) = \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_R$ and
reconstruct Lorentzian physics via Osterwalder--Schrader. He identifies
the Higgs field with the geometric data specifying the choice of
imaginary-time direction in this reconstruction. The mathematical
machinery is internally consistent and addresses the formalism asymmetry
by accepting that the Euclidean theory is fundamental and the Lorentzian
theory is reconstructed.

*What this mathematical framework supplies*: a coherent technical scheme
for organising the operator/path-integral relationship without claiming
analytic continuation; a reading of $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ as the internal
weak-interaction symmetry distinct from the spatial $\mathrm{SU}(2)_R$
(gauging the latter giving Ashtekar-variable gravity); a candidate
identification of the Higgs field with the imaginary-time-direction
data.

*What this mathematical framework does not supply*: a physical
principle. The imaginary-time direction in Woit's framework is external
mathematical data --- the framework requires it to be specified but does
not say what it physically is, what rate (if any) it advances at,
whether it is globally uniform across spacetime, or how matter couples
to it. Woit's framework does not derive quantum mechanics, general
relativity, thermodynamics, the second law, time's arrows, nonlocality,
the McGucken Sphere as wavefront, or the unified picture of conservation
laws and the second law from a common physical-geometric law. It is a
mathematical reorganisation of the existing formalism, not a derivation
of physics from a principle. *This distinction is central: Woit is
engaged in the mathematical-cleanup of orthodox quantum field theory;
the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework is engaged in the physical
derivation of physics from a single physical-geometric law
$dx_4/dt = ic$.*

###### The McGucken Principle as the physical-principle resolution of the Wick-rotation conundrum.

The three asymmetries (1)--(3) are not separate technical problems
requiring separate technical fixes within the orthodox formalism; they
are three observable signatures of the same underlying physical fact:
*the fourth dimension $x_4$ is physically expanding at velocity $c$ at
every spacetime event, with the factor $i$ in $dx_4/dt = ic$ as the
perpendicularity marker of this physical direction.* Once this physical
principle is accepted, each asymmetry receives a physical-principle
reading rather than a mathematical-formalism patch.

::: {#thm:McGuckenWickResolution .theorem}
**Theorem 1** (The McGucken-Wick rotation as the physical-principle
resolution of the broken-analytic-continuation conundrum). *Let the
McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$
(Equation [\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"}) be the physical-geometric law, with
$x_4$ a real perpendicular fourth dimension physically advancing at
velocity $c$ from every event of $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}$, and let the
factor $i = (dx_4/dt)/c$ be the algebraic perpendicularity marker per
Theorem 21.6bis.1 of [@MGWick]. Then the broken-analytic-continuation
conundrum of [@Woit2024Unification at 1:03--1:08] dissolves at the
physical-principle level as follows:*

1.  ***The Wick rotation is not an analytic continuation.** The
    transformation $t \to -i\tau$ that connects the Lorentzian and

    $\Phi_{\mathrm{M}}= x_4- ict = 0$ on the real four-manifold

    The McGucken-Wick rotation is a real geometric coordinate rotation

    parameter $\theta \in [0, \pi/2]$ corresponding to a physical
    rotation between the Lorentzian projection ($\theta = 0$, $x_4= ict$

    ($\theta = \pi/2$, $x_4$ projects to a real Euclidean fourth axis).
    The Kontsevich--Segal admissible domain of complex metrics
    [@KontsevichSegal2021] is identified as the algebraic image of this
    real geometric rotation family [@MG-Connes Theorem C].*

2.  ***The distinguished imaginary-time direction is the physical
    $x_4$-direction.** The Osterwalder--Schrader reflection-positivity
    condition requires a distinguished direction in Euclidean signature
    [@OsterwalderSchrader1973]. Within the orthodox formalism, this
    direction is mathematical data that must be specified externally.
    Under the McGucken Principle, this direction is identified

    expanding at velocity $c$ at the spacetime event in question. The
    distinguished direction is the local $+ic$ direction encoded by the

    $p \in \mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}$ via

    $E_A \circ E_B^{-1}$ with content

3.  ***The operator/path-integral asymmetry is the projection asymmetry

    Lorentzian operator formalism captures the projection of $x_4$'s

    Euclidean path-integral formalism captures the projection onto the

    Each formalism is mathematically well-defined in its own projection;

    analytic continuations of each other --- they are two projections of

4.  ***The spinor asymmetry is the matter-orientation condition (M)

    (Theorem [86](#thm:Gamma4Theorem){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:Gamma4Theorem"} of the present paper, drawn from

    (Definition [80](#def:OrientationM){reference-type="ref"
    reference="def:OrientationM"}) when acting on the chiral

**The content of
Theorem [1](#thm:McGuckenWickResolution){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:McGuckenWickResolution"}:* the four asymmetries Woit
identifies are not four separate technical problems that the McGucken

#### Internal versus external symmetries, the $i$-placement diagnostic, and the two-source of the right-hand side of the McGucken Principle {#ssec:InternalExternalAsTwoSource .unnumbered}

The Wick-rotation subsection above engaged the technical conundrum of
how the Lorentzian operator formalism and the Euclidean path-integral
formalism relate. A second feature of the unanswered-questions catalogue
raised by Woit [@Woit2024Unification] concerns the relationship between
the two classes of symmetry that orthodox quantum field theory treats as
fundamentally separate: *internal symmetries* (the gauge symmetries
$U(1)_Y$, $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$, $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$, acting on field
indices) and *external symmetries* (the spacetime symmetries:
translations, Lorentz transformations, rotations, acting on spacetime
coordinates). Woit identifies that internal symmetries have no clear
physical referent in the orthodox formalism --- the integers labelling
representations and the $i$ inside $e^{i\alpha T^a}$ in the field
transformation rule are accepted as empirical input with no
spacetime-geometric meaning --- and that the Coleman--Mandula
segregation of internal from external symmetries is a fact of
$3+1$-dimensional quantum field theory whose physical source is not
identified by the orthodox formalism. We engage these features at the
principle level, showing that they admit a single physical reading from
the McGucken Principle: *the right-hand side of $dx_4/dt = ic$ carries
two sources --- the imaginary unit $i$ and the velocity $c$ --- and the
two classes of symmetry descend from these two sources via a sharp
$i$-placement diagnostic, with the orthogonality to the dual-channel
architecture's two derivational routes intact and the Coleman--Mandula
commutativity reading as a consequence of $x_4$-perpendicularity.*

###### The $i$-placement diagnostic.

Before stating the theorems, we record the observation that
distinguishes the two classes of symmetry. The diagnostic is precise:

::: {#def:IPlacementDiagnostic .definition}
**Definition 4** (The $i$-placement diagnostic for internal versus
external symmetries). A symmetry of the field theory has the imaginary
unit $i$ *interior* to its transformation rule if the transformation
cannot be expressed as a real action on the field's underlying
classical-coordinate structure without $i$. Equivalently: the $i$
appears in the field's transformation law itself, not merely on
promotion to a Hermitian generator on the quantum Hilbert space. A
symmetry has the imaginary unit $i$ *exterior* if the transformation is
a real action on the classical-coordinate structure (real coordinate
shift, real orthogonal rotation, real Lorentz transformation), with $i$
entering only via the promotion to a Hermitian generator $G = -iX$ where
$X$ is the real classical generator.

A symmetry is classified as *internal* if its $i$-placement is interior,
and *external* if its $i$-placement is exterior.
:::

The diagnostic is sharp: under removal of $i$ from the transformation
rule, an internal symmetry collapses to the trivial identity
($e^{i\alpha T^a} \to e^{0} = \mathbf{1}$, since the underlying
generator is anti-Hermitian and the transformation rule has no real
continuous-group form), while an external symmetry survives intact
($\psi(x) \to \psi(\Lambda^{-1}x)$ is a well-defined real coordinate
action; the $i$ in the Hermitian-generator form is a consequence of
operator-algebraic conventions on the quantum Hilbert space rather than
a feature of the underlying spacetime action). The diagnostic is
therefore not heuristic --- it is a classification that the orthodox
formalism implicitly uses without naming.

###### The two-source reading of the right-hand side of $dx_4/dt = ic$.

We now state the observation that sharpens the Father-Symmetry priority
of Theorem 14.4.3 of [@MG-McG6-2026]: the right-hand side $ic$ of the
McGucken Principle visibly contains *two sources*, both present in one
first-order equation.

::: {#thm:TwoSourceRHS .theorem}
**Theorem 5** (Two-source of the right-hand side of $dx_4/dt = ic$).
*Let the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$
(Equation [\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"}) be the physical-geometric law. The
right-hand side $ic$ contains two distinct sources, both visible in the
single first-order equation:*

1.  ***The perpendicularity-marker source $i$.** The factor $i$ is the
    algebraic signature of the perpendicularity of $x_4$ to three-space
    [@MGWick Theorem 21.6bis.1]: $i = (dx_4/dt)/c$, where the
    perpendicular direction $x_4$ carries the algebra of orthogonality
    to the three real spatial axes $\hat{x}_1, \hat{x}_2, \hat{x}_3$.
    The factor $i$ is the source of the twelve $i$'s of quantum theory
    cataloged in [@MGWick Theorem-clusters I--XIII]: the canonical
    commutator $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$; the Schrödinger evolution
    $i\hbar \partial_t \psi = H\psi$; the path-integral weight
    $e^{iS/\hbar}$; the Wick substitution $t \to -i\tau$; the local
    $U(1)$ phase rotation $e^{i\alpha(x)}$; the Dirac operator's
    $i\gamma^\mu \partial_\mu$; the spinor complex structure; and so
    on.*

2.  ***The wavefront-velocity source $c$.** The velocity $c$ is the rate
    at which $x_4$ expands from every event of
    $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}$. The factor $c$ is the source of the
    spherical wavefront structure --- the McGucken Sphere
    $\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}(p, t)$ of radius $c(t - t_0)$ centered on each
    event $p_0$ --- with full $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ rotational symmetry as a
    Channel B feature [@MG-McGSpace; @MG-FatherSym; @MG-Huygens]. The
    factor $c$ is the source of the spatial $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ symmetry of
    the wavefront, the Lorentzian null-cone structure
    ([@MG-Master2Chains-2026], GR T1: the Master Equation
    $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$), the constancy of the velocity of light in
    special relativity, and the Huygens-wavefront propagation underlying
    both the wave equation and the spherical second-law content.*

*The two sources are visibly present on the same side of one first-order
equation. They are not two independent postulates that happen to be
coupled by convention; they are coupled by the physical fact that the
fourth dimension is a real perpendicular direction expanding at the
velocity of light.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 documentary at [@MGWick Theorem 21.6bis.1] for the
identification of $i$ as perpendicularity marker, and G1 documentary at
[@MG-FatherSym §4] and [@MG-Huygens §2] for the identification of $c$ as
wavefront-velocity source. The identification that both sources are
visible on the same RHS of the same first-order equation is G1 by direct
inspection of
[\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"}. ◻
:::

::: {#thm:InternalExternalAsTwoSource .theorem}
**Theorem 6** (Internal symmetries as the $i$-source of $dx_4/dt = ic$;
external symmetries as the $c$-source). *Assume the McGucken Principle,
the $i$-placement diagnostic
(Definition [4](#def:IPlacementDiagnostic){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:IPlacementDiagnostic"}), and the two-source theorem
(Theorem [5](#thm:TwoSourceRHS){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:TwoSourceRHS"}). Then:*

1.  ***Internal symmetries descend from the $i$-source.** Each
    internal-symmetry transformation rule (a) carries $i$ interior to
    the rule, and (b) acts on field structure that is geometrically
    perpendicular to three-space: the $x_4$-winding phase for $U(1)_Y$
    (acted on by $e^{i\alpha(x)}$ with $\alpha(x)$ rotating the
    perpendicular-$x_4$-direction phase); the $x_4$-orientation Weyl
    doublet for $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ (acted on by
    $e^{i\alpha^a(x) \tau^a/2}$ rotating the orientation of the
    perpendicular-$x_4$ direction in the doublet space); the
    substrate-scale spatial-direction bimodule for $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$
    (acted on by $e^{i\alpha^a(x) \lambda^a/2}$ on the three
    perpendicular-spatial-direction bimodule indices). In each case, the
    $i$ interior to the transformation rule is identifiable with the
    perpendicularity-marker $i = (dx_4/dt)/c$ of [@MGWick
    Theorem 21.6bis.1].*

2.  ***External symmetries descend from the $c$-source.** Each
    external-symmetry transformation is (a) a real action on the
    spacetime coordinate structure (translations, Lorentz
    transformations, rotations, boosts), and (b) acts on the
    wavefront-in-three-space content of $x_4$'s expansion: spatial
    rotations rotate the three-space wavefront slice; translations shift
    the centre event of the wavefront; Lorentz boosts change the
    worldline through the wavefront. In each case, the underlying
    classical action involves the wavefront velocity $c$ (the wavefront
    radius is $c(t - t_0)$; the Lorentzian metric carries $c^2$ in the
    null-cone condition; Lorentz transformations preserve the invariant
    $c$) and does not require $i$ in its definition. The $i$ enters only
    on promotion to Hermitian generators on the quantum Hilbert space,
    where the convention $G = -iX$ (with $X$ a real classical generator:
    $X = \partial_\mu$ for translations,
    $X = x_\mu \partial_\nu - x_\nu \partial_\mu$ for rotations, etc.)
    introduces the $i$ exterior to the underlying classical action.*

3.  ***The classification is sharp.** A symmetry is internal if and only
    if its transformation rule carries $i$ interior, which holds if and
    only if the symmetry acts on the perpendicular-$x_4$ substrate of
    $dx_4/dt = ic$. A symmetry is external if and only if its $i$ is
    exterior, which holds if and only if the symmetry acts on the
    three-space-parallel wavefront. The diagnostic is therefore not a
    coincidence of conventions; it is the marker of which of the two RHS
    sources of the McGucken Principle generates the symmetry's
    transformation content.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G2 identification, with G1 documentary backing at each clause.

*Property (i).* Each internal-symmetry transformation rule is examined:
$U(1)_Y$ acts on the perpendicular-$x_4$ phase per the local $U(1)$
derivation of [@MG-McGSpace §2] (which exhibits the local $U(1)$ as the
symmetry of phase rotation of the $x_4$-perpendicular wavefront);
$\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ acts on the perpendicular-$x_4$ Weyl doublet per the
lift of the McGucken-Sphere $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ to
$\mathrm{Spin}(3) \cong \mathrm{SU}(2)$ established in Lemmas of Part I
of the present paper; $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ acts on the substrate-scale
spatial-direction bimodule per the substrate-scale Connes spectral
triple of Part III. In each case the $i$ in the transformation rule is
the perpendicularity-marker $i$ of [@MGWick Theorem 21.6bis.1].

*Property (ii).* Each external symmetry's underlying real classical
action is exhibited: translations are real coordinate shifts; rotations
are real orthogonal transformations; Lorentz transformations are real
pseudo-orthogonal transformations preserving $c$; boosts are real
hyperbolic transformations of the wavefront's timelike axis. The
Hermitian-generator promotion $G = -iX$ on the quantum Hilbert space (a
representation-theoretic convention required for unitary representations
of real Lie groups, distinct from the field's classical-action
transformation) is the exterior-$i$ entry. The underlying
wavefront-in-three-space content involves $c$ (the wavefront radius, the
null-cone, the invariant velocity) and does not require $i$.

*Property (iii).* The biconditional follows from the construction: a
symmetry's transformation rule either does or does not carry $i$ in its
classical form, and this is exactly determined by whether the symmetry
acts on the perpendicular substrate (where $i$ marks the
perpendicularity) or the parallel wavefront (where the action is real).
The two conditions are equivalent characterizations of the same
feature. ◻
:::

::: {#thm:OrthogonalityOfDecompositions .theorem}
**Theorem 7** (Orthogonality of the Channel A/B decomposition and the
internal/external decomposition). *Let Channel A and Channel B be the
two derivational routes of the dual-channel architecture [@MG-McG6-2026
Theorem 14.11], [@MG-Master2Chains-2026]: Channel A (algebraic-symmetry)
foregrounding the $i$-as-perpendicularity-marker content of
$dx_4/dt = ic$, and Channel B (geometric-propagation) foregrounding the
$c$-as-spherical-expansion-velocity. Let the internal/external
classification be the $i$-placement diagnostic of
Definition [4](#def:IPlacementDiagnostic){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:IPlacementDiagnostic"}. Then:*

1.  ***The two decompositions are orthogonal.** The Channel A/B
    decomposition classifies *derivational routes* (each named symmetry
    admits both a Channel A derivation and a Channel B derivation, with
    the dual-channel disjoint-route convergence on the same canonical
    object as the convergent overdetermination signature). The
    internal/external decomposition classifies *symmetries* (each named
    symmetry is either internal, with $i$ interior to its transformation
    rule, or external, with $i$ exterior). The two classifications are
    independent: every symmetry has a Channel A derivation and a Channel
    B derivation regardless of whether it is internal or external.*

2.  ***Every named symmetry has both Channel A and Channel B
    derivations.** Lorentz invariance (external): Channel A derivation
    via the algebraic solution space of $X^T \eta + \eta X = 0$ giving
    $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$ [@MG-Master2Chains-2026 §5, Theorem 24];
    Channel B derivation via the McGucken Sphere null-cone structure
    [@MG-Master2Chains-2026 §5, Proposition 25]. $U(1)$ gauge invariance
    (internal): Channel A derivation via the local phase-invariance
    forcing the connection through Noether [@MG-Master2Chains-2026 §9,
    Theorem 36]; Channel B derivation via the line bundle
    $L \to \mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}$ with parallel transport along
    Huygens wavefronts [@MG-Master2Chains-2026 §9, Lemma 38]. The same
    dual-derivation pattern holds for every theorem of the 47-theorem
    GR + QM corpus and the 18-theorem thermodynamics corpus, supporting
    the Bayesian likelihood ratio $\Lambda \geq 10^{141}$ of
    [@MG-McG6-2026 Theorem 14.11].*

3.  ***Within each derivation, the $i$-content lives on the Channel A
    side and the $c$-content lives on the Channel B side.** The Channel
    A derivation of any symmetry uses the $i$-as-perpendicularity-marker
    content most prominently in the algebraic-symmetry route (Lie
    algebra brackets, Hermitian generators, phase rotations); the
    Channel B derivation of any symmetry uses the
    $c$-as-wavefront-velocity most prominently in the
    geometric-propagation route (null cones, parallel transport,
    wavefront geometry). *However, every derivation in both channels
    uses both sources*, because the principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ couples $i$
    and $c$ on its right-hand side: the Lorentzian metric
    $\eta = \mathrm{diag}(-1, +1, +1, +1)$ used in every Channel B
    derivation carries the algebra of $i^2 = -1$ absorbed via $x_4= ict$
    [@MG-Master2Chains-2026 Lemma 1]; the Hermitian-generator brackets
    used in every Channel A derivation are referred ultimately to
    spacetime structure on which the wavefront velocity $c$ is
    invariant.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 documentary for the dual-derivation structure of
[@MG-Master2Chains-2026] (Properties (i) and (ii) are statements about
the structure of the existing 47+18-theorem corpus). G2 identification
for Property (iii), which reads the foregrounding pattern of the two

::: {#thm:ColemanMandulaAsPerpendicularity .theorem}
**Theorem 8** (The Coleman--Mandula commutativity as the disjointness of
$x_4$-perpendicular and three-space-parallel substrate features). *The
Coleman--Mandula theorem of orthodox $3+1$-dimensional quantum field
theory establishes that internal symmetries and external symmetries
factor into commuting subgroups of the total symmetry group of the
$S$-matrix, with no nontrivial mixing possible except via the
anti-commuting supersymmetry generators (which empirically have not been
observed). Within the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, this
commutativity admits a reading:*

1.  ***Internal symmetries act on perpendicular substrate.** Per
    Theorem [6](#thm:InternalExternalAsTwoSource){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:InternalExternalAsTwoSource"} Property (i): internal
    symmetries act on the $x_4$-perpendicular content of the McGucken
    Sphere structure --- the $x_4$-winding phase, the $x_4$-orientation
    Weyl doublet, the substrate-scale spatial-direction bimodule.*

2.  ***External symmetries act on parallel substrate.** Per
    Theorem [6](#thm:InternalExternalAsTwoSource){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:InternalExternalAsTwoSource"} Property (ii): external
    symmetries act on the three-space-parallel content of the McGucken
    Sphere wavefront --- rotations of the three-space directions,
    translations of the wavefront's centre, boosts of the worldline
    through the wavefront.*

3.  ***The two substrate features are geometrically disjoint.** The
    perpendicularity of $x_4$ to three-space (encoded by the $i$ marker
    per [@MGWick Theorem 21.6bis.1]) is the fact that the
    $x_4$-perpendicular content and the three-space-parallel content are
    geometrically disjoint substrate features of the same McGucken
    Sphere structure. The internal-symmetry actions (on perpendicular
    features) and the external-symmetry actions (on parallel features)
    therefore act on disjoint substrate.*

4.  ***Coleman--Mandula commutativity reads as substrate-disjointness.**
    Symmetry actions on geometrically disjoint substrate features
    commute by necessity: the internal $U(1)_Y$ phase rotation does not
    mix with the external Lorentz boost because $U(1)_Y$ acts on the
    perpendicular-$x_4$ phase while the Lorentz boost acts on the
    parallel three-space-time worldline, and these are perpendicular
    substrate features. The orthodox Coleman--Mandula theorem observes
    this commutativity as a consequence of $S$-matrix analyticity and
    Poincaré covariance; the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework reads it
    as the consequence of $x_4$-perpendicularity to three-space.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G2 identification. The orthodox Coleman--Mandula theorem
([@ColemanMandula1967]) establishes the commutativity as a theorem of
$S$-matrix analyticity; the McGucken-framework reading does not
re-derive this orthodox theorem but identifies the source of the
commutativity in the perpendicularity of the $x_4$ direction to
three-space. The identification rests on
Theorem [6](#thm:InternalExternalAsTwoSource){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:InternalExternalAsTwoSource"} (the substrate-content
readings of internal and external symmetry actions) together with the
perpendicularity of $x_4$ to three-space (the geometry of
[\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"}, encoded algebraically by the $i$
marker of [@MGWick Theorem 21.6bis.1]). The orthodox formalism's
observation that internal and external symmetries factor is reproduced;
the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework supplies the geometric source of
the factorisation. ◻
:::

::: {#rem:FatherSymmetryRefined .remark}
*Remark 9* (Father-Symmetry priority of $dx_4/dt = ic$ over Noether's
theorem itself, sharpened by the two-source RHS reading). The Father
Symmetry priority of $dx_4/dt = ic$ established in [@MG-FatherSym
Theorems 30--38] and [@MG-McG6-2026 Theorem 14.4.3] states that every
principal named symmetry of contemporary physics (Lorentz, Poincaré,
Noether, $U(1) \times \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathrm{SU}(3)$,
quantum-unitary, CPT, supersymmetry, diffeomorphism invariance, the
standard string-theoretic dualities) descends as a theorem of
$dx_4/dt = ic$. Theorem [5](#thm:TwoSourceRHS){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:TwoSourceRHS"} sharpens the priority claim materially:
the right-hand side of $dx_4/dt = ic$ visibly contains, in one
first-order equation, the two sources from which the two principal
classes of symmetry descend:

-   The factor $i$ on the RHS is the perpendicularity-marker source of
    all internal-symmetry transformation content
    ($U(1)_Y, \mathrm{SU}(2)_L, \mathrm{SU}(3)_c$, the canonical
    commutators, the Schrödinger evolution, the full $i$-interior
    algebraic-symmetry structure of quantum field theory).

-   The factor $c$ on the RHS is the wavefront-velocity source of all
    external-symmetry transformation content (translations, Lorentz,
    rotations, boosts, the full real-classical-action spacetime
    structure of relativity).

Noether's theorem of orthodox physics establishes that every continuous
symmetry generates a conservation law. Father-Symmetry priority
establishes the converse-and-more: every named symmetry of physics
descends from one principle, and the two principal classes of symmetry
descend from the two sources visible on the RHS of that principle. The
McGucken Principle is therefore prior to Noether's theorem itself:
Noether identifies the consequence of symmetry (conservation laws);
Father-Symmetry priority identifies the source of every named symmetry
(the two-source RHS of $dx_4/dt = ic$). Noether's theorem is recovered
as a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via the Lagrangian-and-action descent
[@MG-Lagrangian]; the deeper fact is that the symmetries Noether's
theorem operates on are themselves theorems of the same principle.
:::

::: {#rem:NaturalLanguageAsymmetry .remark}
*Remark 10* (Natural-language asymmetry between the two channels, with
explicit non-collapse of the dual-channel architecture). A finer reading
of the relationship between Channel A/B and internal/external is the
following. Per the definitional foregrounding of
[@MG-Master2Chains-2026], Channel A is named for its foregrounding of
the $i$-as-perpendicularity-marker content; Channel B for its
foregrounding of the $c$-as-spherical-expansion-velocity. This naming
makes Channel A the *natural language* for internal symmetries (whose
$i$ is interior to the transformation rule and is therefore most
transparently expressed via Channel A's algebraic-symmetry vocabulary):
the local $U(1)_Y$ phase rotation $\psi \to e^{i\alpha(x)}\psi$, the
doublet rotation $\psi \to e^{i\alpha^a(x)\tau^a/2}\psi$, the bracket
structure $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$. And it makes Channel B the
natural language for external symmetries (whose action on the spacetime
wavefront is most transparently expressed via Channel B's
geometric-propagation vocabulary): the McGucken Sphere wavefront
$\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}(p, t)$ with $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ symmetry, the null
cone at velocity $c$, the spatial translations of the wavefront's
centre.

*The naming is about foregrounding, not exclusivity.* Per
Theorem [7](#thm:OrthogonalityOfDecompositions){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:OrthogonalityOfDecompositions"} Property (iii), every
derivation in both channels uses both sources, because the principle
$dx_4/dt = ic$ couples $i$ and $c$ on its right-hand side. The Channel B
derivation of an internal symmetry exists (via parallel transport along
Huygens wavefronts at velocity $c$, with the line-bundle connection
carrying the $i$-content reconstructed from the geometric structure
rather than displayed up front); the Channel A derivation of an external
symmetry exists (via Hermitian-generator algebra with the convention
$G = -iX$, with the wavefront-velocity carrying through the Lorentzian
metric absorbed via $x_4= ict$). The dual-channel disjoint-route
convergence of [@MG-McG6-2026 Theorem 14.11] on the same canonical
object across $47$ GR + QM theorems and $18$ thermodynamics theorems is
intact: each theorem has both derivations, each derivation uses both
sources, and the convergence on the same object is the convergent
overdetermination signature supporting the Bayesian likelihood ratio
$\Lambda \geq 10^{141}$.

The natural-language asymmetry is therefore a statement about which
vocabulary makes which class of symmetry most transparent, not a
statement that one channel can derive only one class of symmetry. The
orthogonality of the two decompositions (Channel A/B as derivational
routes; internal/external as $i$-placement classification) is preserved;
what the natural-language asymmetry adds is the observation that the
principle's coupling of $i$ and $c$ on its RHS is what allows both
channels to derive both classes of symmetry --- the two sources are tied
together in the single first-order equation, and the two channels are
two ways of unpacking that coupling.
:::

#### Resolution-content diagnosis of the McGucken Duality: Lorentz-invariant discreteness and continuity simultaneously realized through Channel A and Channel B {#ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis .unnumbered}

The dual-channel architecture established in the preceding subsections
(Wick-rotation:
§[\[ssec:WickConundrum\]](#ssec:WickConundrum){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:WickConundrum"}; internal/external symmetries:
§[\[ssec:InternalExternalAsTwoSource\]](#ssec:InternalExternalAsTwoSource){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:InternalExternalAsTwoSource"}) admits a third diagnosis
at the resolution level. We establish that Channel A is uniformly
continuous (mono-resolution); that Channel B carries both continuous and
discrete readings (bi-resolution) related by the Planck-scale cutoff
applied to the same McGucken Sphere structure; that the discreteness of
Channel B is Lorentz-invariant by construction; that the three-space
$(x_1, x_2, x_3)$ remains continuous in every reading; and that two
no-go obstructions against discrete-spacetime models --- Weyl's 1949
Tile Argument [@Weyl1949PMNS] and the Nielsen--Ninomiya 1981 theorem
[@NielsenNinomiya1981I; @NielsenNinomiya1981II] --- are evaded by the
framework's specific configuration of where the discreteness lives.

###### The resolution question.

The orthodox-tradition position on spacetime discreteness has been
stalemated for decades. On one side: the Planck scale
$\ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^3}$ appears in important places
(Bekenstein--Hawking entropy $S_{\rm BH} = k_B A/(4\ell_P^2)$
[@Bekenstein1973BlackHoleEntropy; @Hawking1975Particle], holographic
mode counts [@tHooft1993Dimensional; @Susskind1995World], and
quantum-gravity heuristics) carrying the signature of discreteness. On
the other side: Weyl's 1949 Tile Argument [@Weyl1949PMNS p. 43]
establishes that a discrete spatial lattice cannot reproduce the
Pythagorean theorem and the isotropy of three-space; Nielsen--Ninomiya
1981 [@NielsenNinomiya1981I; @NielsenNinomiya1981II] establishes that
chiral fermions on a regular lattice with hermiticity, locality,
translation invariance, bilinear action, and locally conserved charge
necessarily produce equal numbers of left- and right-handed species
(fermion doubling), preventing a lattice formulation of the weak
interaction. The Doubly Special Relativity programme
[@AmelinoCamelia2002; @MagueijoSmolin2002] was constructed in part to
attempt observer-independent Planck-scale discreteness via a deformed
Lorentz group. The orthodox tradition has been unable to reconcile the
discreteness of horizon entropy with the continuity demanded by Lorentz
invariance, the Pythagorean theorem, and chiral fermion dynamics.

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework supplies the resolution at the
physical-principle level: the discreteness exists, it is
Lorentz-invariant, and it is located *not* in a 3-space lattice but on
$x_4$ (a Lorentz-scalar perpendicular axis) and on the McGucken Sphere
2-surface (an $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-Haar-symmetric 2-manifold). Three-space
remains continuous. The resolution diagnosis establishes this at theorem
grade.

::: {#thm:ResolutionContentDiagnosis .theorem}
**Theorem 12** (Resolution-content diagnosis of the McGucken Duality).
*Assume the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$
(Equation [\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"}); the Channel A / Channel B
decomposition
(§[\[ssec:WickConundrum\]](#ssec:WickConundrum){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:WickConundrum"},
§[\[ssec:InternalExternalAsTwoSource\]](#ssec:InternalExternalAsTwoSource){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:InternalExternalAsTwoSource"}; [@MG-McG6-2026 Theorem
14.11], [@MG-Master2Chains-2026]); the substrate-scale construction of
$\ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^3}$ via Steps (i)--(iii)
(§[\[ssec:FoundationalPrinciple\]](#ssec:FoundationalPrinciple){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:FoundationalPrinciple"}; [@MG-Sphere2026 §5.2, §11.2]);
the substrate-scale identification of McGucken Spheres with
Chamseddine--Connes--Mukhanov quanta of geometry (Theorem H of
[@MG-Connes]); and the Bekenstein--Hawking area-entropy theorem
$S_{\rm BH} = k_B A/(4\ell_P^2)$
[@Bekenstein1973BlackHoleEntropy; @Hawking1975Particle] of the
framework's existing framework. Then:*

1.  ***Channel A is mono-resolution: uniformly continuous.** The
    algebraic-symmetry of Channel A --- Lie group structure (Poincaré
    $\mathrm{ISO}(1,3)$, gauge groups
    $U(1)_Y \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{SU}(3)_c$), Hermitian
    generators on Hilbert space, continuous one-parameter unitary
    representations via Stone's theorem, canonical commutator
    $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$, Heisenberg/Schrödinger evolution, the
    Wigner classification of particle states by continuous-group
    representations --- is tied to continuity. *Lie groups have no
    nontrivial finite subgroups acting as the full structure;
    discretization breaks the group structure required for Channel A's
    algebraic-symmetry derivations.* Channel A has no native
    discreteness.*

2.  ***Channel B is bi-resolution: both continuous and discrete.** The
    geometric-propagation of Channel B --- McGucken Sphere wavefronts at
    velocity $c$, Huygens' principle, $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-Haar symmetry on
    the 2-sphere, the substrate-scale tiling --- admits two compatible
    readings related by the Planck-scale resolution cutoff:*

    -   **Continuous reading.* Above the substrate scale
        ($E \ll M_P c^2$, $\ell \gg \ell_P$), the McGucken Sphere
        $\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}(p, t)$ is a smooth 2-surface of radius
        $c(t - t_0)$, the wavefront propagation is smooth, and the
        differential machinery (wave equation, retarded Green's
        function, classical fluid dynamics) applies. This is the
        long-wavelength effective description.*

    -   **Discrete reading.* At substrate scale ($\ell \sim \ell_P$),
        the McGucken Sphere decomposes into Planck-area cells, with each
        cell carrying one $x_4$-stationary mode per Planck area
        $\ell_P^2$. The mode count on a Sphere of area $A$ is
        $N_{\rm modes} = A/\ell_P^2$ --- the Bekenstein--Hawking content
        of horizon entropy. The Sphere's continuous 2-surface and its
        discrete Planck-cell tiling are two resolution readings of the
        same geometric object, with the Planck length $\ell_P$ as the
        resolution scale separating them.*

3.  ***The discreteness is Lorentz-invariant.** The Planck length
    $\ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^3}$ is built from three Lorentz scalars
    ($c$, $\hbar$, $G$). The framework's existing framework
    (§[\[ssec:FoundationalPrinciple\]](#ssec:FoundationalPrinciple){reference-type="ref"
    reference="ssec:FoundationalPrinciple"}; [@MG-Sphere2026 §5.2,
    §11.2]) establishes $\ell_P$ as the substrate's intrinsic wavelength
    rather than as a length-of-an-object subject to Lorentz contraction;
    the Doubly Special Relativity motivating problem ("how can $\ell_P$
    be observer-independent if Lorentz contraction shrinks lengths?") is
    dissolved at source. Each inertial observer sees their own McGucken
    Sphere centered on the event they call "now," with their own area
    $A$ and their own mode count $N_{\rm modes} = A/\ell_P^2$; the
    Lorentz-area transformations relating different observers' Spheres
    preserve the area-to-cell ratio. The discretization is therefore
    observer-independent without modification of the Lorentz group.*

4.  ***The Sphere mode count is $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-Haar invariant, not
    Cartesian-lattice.** The McGucken Sphere is
    $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-homogeneous as the orbit space
    $\mathrm{SO}(3)/\mathrm{SO}(2)$ [@MG-McGSpace §4], [@MG-FatherSym
    §2], and the unique $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-invariant probability measure
    on $\mathrm{SO}(3)/\mathrm{SO}(2)$ is the $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-Haar
    measure. The Planck-cell distribution on the Sphere's 2-surface is
    determined by this Haar measure: cells are distributed by the
    $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-invariant area measure, with the cell area
    $\ell_P^2$ fixed by the Planck-scale resolution. *There is no
    preferred axis on the Sphere; the discretization is rotationally
    symmetric to within the cell-area resolution, and the symmetry
    becomes exact in the cell-area-to-zero continuum limit.* This is the
    discretization Weyl's Tile Argument cannot touch.*

5.  ***Three-space $(x_1, x_2, x_3)$ remains continuous in all
    readings.** The framework's substrate is *not* $\mathbb{R}^3$
    discretized on a Cartesian lattice. The discreteness lives in
    $x_4$-stepping (one $\ell_P$ step per Planck time $t_P = \ell_P/c$)
    and on the 2-surface of the McGucken Sphere (one mode per $\ell_P^2$
    cell). Three-space itself remains the continuum $\mathbb{R}^3$; the
    Pythagorean theorem $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$ holds exactly in
    $(x_1, x_2, x_3)$ because $(x_1, x_2, x_3)$ is a continuum.*

6.  ***Channel B's $+ic$ asymmetry is intrinsically tied to the discrete
    $x_4$-stepping.** Each Planck step advances $x_4$ by $+\ell_P$, not
    by $\pm \ell_P$. The macroscopic strict Second Law $dS/dt > 0$
    (Theorem 9 of [@MG-Entropy]) and the discrete unidirectional
    $x_4$-stepping at Planck scale are *the same $+ic$ asymmetry
    observed at two scales*: at macroscopic resolution the asymmetry
    manifests as the irreversibility of thermodynamic time; at Planck
    resolution it manifests as the unidirectional $x_4$-tick. One source
    ($+ic$ rather than $\pm ic$), two readings.*

7.  ***Five readings of $dx_4/dt = ic$ simultaneously available.**
    Combining the channel decomposition with the resolution and the
    McGucken-Wick rotation, the framework supplies five distinct
    readings of the same principle, each anchored in empirics:*

      ***Reading***                    ***Channel***   ***Resolution***   ***Empirical anchor***
      -------------------------------- --------------- ------------------ -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      *Continuous Lorentzian*          *A*             *continuous*       *Stone's theorem, Wigner classification, gauge theory, Poincaré algebra*
      *Continuous Lorentzian*          *B*             *continuous*       *Huygens wavefront propagation, retarded Green's function, classical wave equation*
      *Discrete (Lorentz-invariant)*   *B*             *Planck-scale*     *Bekenstein--Hawking entropy $S_{\rm BH} = k_B A/(4\ell_P^2)$ [@Bekenstein1973BlackHoleEntropy]; Hawking temperature [@Hawking1975Particle]; holographic mode count [@tHooft1993Dimensional; @Susskind1995World]*
      *Continuous Euclidean*           *B*             *continuous*       *Wiener process, classical diffusion, Boltzmann--Gibbs measure*
      *Discrete Euclidean*             *B*             *Planck-scale*     *Gibbons--Hawking saddle-point on Wick-rotated cigar [@GibbonsHawking1977], Euclidean Schwarzschild partition function*

    *Channel A occupies a single cell (continuous Lorentzian only).
    Channel B occupies the other four cells, with the McGucken-Wick
    rotation
    (Theorem [1](#thm:McGuckenWickResolution){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:McGuckenWickResolution"}, Property (i)) as the
    Lorentzian/Euclidean bridge and the Planck-scale cutoff as the
    continuous/discrete bridge. The five readings are not separate
    theories; they are five resolution-and-signature projections of the
    same physical structure $dx_4/dt = ic$.*

**The content of
Theorem [12](#thm:ResolutionContentDiagnosis){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ResolutionContentDiagnosis"}:* the Channel A / Channel B
decomposition of $dx_4/dt = ic$ is not symmetric at the resolution
level. Channel A is mono-resolution because its content is
Lie-group-symmetry that requires continuity; Channel B is bi-resolution

::: {#thm:WeylTileEvaded .theorem}
**Theorem 13** (Weyl's Tile Argument is evaded by the McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's relocation of discreteness from spatial
lattice to $x_4$-stepping plus Sphere mode count). *Weyl's Tile Argument
[@Weyl1949PMNS p. 43] establishes that a discrete spatial lattice cannot
reproduce the Pythagorean theorem $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$ in three-space and
cannot reproduce the isotropy of three-space, on the grounds that a
square built of miniature tiles has "as many tiles along the diagonal as
there are along the side; thus the diagonal should be equal in length to
the side" (Weyl 1949, verbatim, p. 43 of the Princeton University Press
edition [@Weyl1949PMNS]). The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework evades
Weyl's Tile Argument because the framework's discreteness is *not* in a
3-space lattice:*

1.  ***Weyl's argument requires a 3-space lattice.** Weyl's argument
    considers a square region tiled by miniature tiles in three-space.
    The argument operates on a fixed Cartesian (or hexagonal, or any
    other directional) tiling of $\mathbb{R}^2$ or $\mathbb{R}^3$. The
    argument's two failure modes (Pythagoras-violation and
    isotropy-violation) both rest on the existence of preferred lattice
    axes.*

2.  ***The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework places discreteness
    elsewhere.** Per
    Theorem [12](#thm:ResolutionContentDiagnosis){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:ResolutionContentDiagnosis"}, Properties (ii) and
    (v), the framework's discreteness lives in $x_4$-stepping (one
    $\ell_P$ step per Planck time along the perpendicular fourth axis)
    and on the McGucken Sphere 2-surface (one mode per $\ell_P^2$ cell,
    distributed by $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-Haar). Three-space $(x_1, x_2, x_3)$
    remains continuous.*

3.  ***Pythagoras holds in three-space because three-space is
    continuous.** For any triangle with sides $a, b$ and hypotenuse
    along the diagonal in three-space, $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$ holds exactly
    because three-space is the continuum $\mathbb{R}^3$, not a tiled
    lattice. Weyl's argument cannot fire because its crucial assumption
    (3-space lattice) is violated by the framework.*

4.  ***Isotropy holds because the Sphere mode discretization is
    $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-Haar.** The discreteness on the Sphere is the
    $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-invariant Planck-cell distribution. There is no
    preferred axis on the Sphere; the discretization is rotationally
    symmetric to within the cell-area resolution. Weyl's
    isotropy-violation does not apply.*

**Conclusion:* Weyl's Tile Argument is a no-go theorem with two crucial
assumptions --- (W1) discreteness lives in 3-space, and (W2) the
discretization is on a fixed lattice with preferred axes. The McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's discreteness violates both: (W1) is violated
because the framework's discreteness is on $x_4$ and on the Sphere
2-surface, not in 3-space; (W2) is violated because the Sphere mode
distribution is $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-Haar invariant, not on a fixed-axis
lattice. The argument does not bite the framework's configuration.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 documentary at Weyl [@Weyl1949PMNS p. 43] for the
argument's primary-source statement. G1 documentary at
Theorem [12](#thm:ResolutionContentDiagnosis){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ResolutionContentDiagnosis"}, Properties (ii), (iv), (v),
of the present paper for the framework's placement of discreteness. G2
identification at the no-go assumption-violation analysis: the
argument's assumptions are explicitly named (3-space lattice with
preferred axes) and the framework's structure is explicitly checked
against each, with both violated. ◻
:::

::: {#thm:NielsenNinomiyaEvaded .theorem}
**Theorem 14** (Nielsen--Ninomiya is evaded by the McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's continuous-Lorentzian placement of chiral
fermions). *The Nielsen--Ninomiya theorem (Nielsen-Ninomiya 1981 (I)
Nucl. Phys. B 185:20 [@NielsenNinomiya1981I]; (II) Nucl. Phys. B 193:173
[@NielsenNinomiya1981II]) establishes that chiral fermions placed on a
regular lattice satisfying five technical conditions --- (a)
hermiticity, (b) locality, (c) regular lattice with translational
invariance and Lorentz-recovered continuum limit, (d) bilinear action of
the form $\bar\psi M \psi$, (e) locally conserved quantized charge ---
necessarily produce equal numbers of left- and right-handed Weyl species
in the continuum limit (fermion doubling), preventing a lattice
formulation of the weak interaction or any chiral gauge theory. The
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework evades Nielsen--Ninomiya because the
framework's chiral fermions are not placed on a regular spatial
lattice:*

1.  ***Nielsen--Ninomiya requires chiral fermions on a regular
    lattice.** The five technical conditions of the theorem all
    reference a lattice formulation: locality is locality on the
    lattice, translational invariance is invariance under lattice
    translations, the bilinear action is over lattice sites, and the
    locally conserved charge is conserved at lattice nodes. The theorem
    operates on a Kogut--Susskind-type or equivalent regular lattice.*

2.  ***The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's chiral fermions live in
    the continuous Lorentzian spacetime.** Per Part I of the present
    paper, chiral fermions are derived from the matter orientation
    condition (M)
    (Definition [80](#def:OrientationM){reference-type="ref"
    reference="def:OrientationM"}) acting on $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$
    Weyl-spinor doublets in the continuous Lorentzian manifold
    $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}= \mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}^{1,3}$.
    Chirality is defined by the continuous Lorentz structure of
    $\gamma_5$ and the Weyl projections
    $P_\pm = (\mathbf{1} \pm \gamma_5)/2$; the single-sided action of
    spatial bivectors preserving (M)
    (Theorem [82](#thm:SingleSided){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:SingleSided"}) selects one chirality at theorem
    grade.*

3.  ***The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's discreteness is
    orthogonal to where chirality is defined.** Per
    Theorem [12](#thm:ResolutionContentDiagnosis){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:ResolutionContentDiagnosis"}, the framework's
    discreteness is in $x_4$-stepping and Sphere mode count, not in a
    3-space lattice. Channel A (which carries the algebraic-symmetry
    including $\gamma_5$, Hermitian gauge generators, and the Weyl
    projections) is uniformly continuous; Channel B's discrete reading
    does not place fermions on a 3-space lattice but on the Sphere
    2-surface, with the cell distribution being $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-Haar
    invariant.*

4.  ***The five Nielsen--Ninomiya conditions are not satisfied by the
    framework's configuration.***

    -   **Condition (c) violation: regular lattice with translational
        invariance.* The framework's substrate is
        $\mathbb{R}^3 \times (\ell_P \cdot \mathbb{Z})_{x_4}$, with
        three-space continuous and only the perpendicular $x_4$-axis
        discretized. This is *not* a regular 4D lattice; the
        translational invariance of the substrate is the continuous
        Lorentz invariance of $\mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}$ on
        three-space + time, not lattice translation invariance.*

    -   **Condition (d) modification: bilinear action.* The framework's
        matter action is the McGucken Lagrangian ([@MG-Lagrangian §4]),
        with bilinear structure on the continuous spinor field $\psi(x)$
        rather than on a lattice-discretized field $\psi(x_n)$.*

    -   **Where chirality lives.* Chirality is defined by the
        continuous-Lorentz $\gamma_5$, not by lattice operators. The
        continuum chirality projection
        $P_\pm = (\mathbf{1} \pm \gamma_5)/2$ is well-defined on the
        continuous spinor field; there is no lattice-induced fermion
        doubling because there is no lattice on which to double.*

5.  ***The framework's configuration is not in the Nielsen--Ninomiya
    domain.** The theorem's premises require a regular 3-space lattice
    (or 4D Euclidean lattice in the Wick-rotated formulation) on which
    chiral fermions live. The framework's chiral fermions live in
    continuous Lorentzian spacetime with discreteness elsewhere. The
    Nielsen--Ninomiya configuration and the framework's configuration
    are different objects; the theorem's conclusion (fermion doubling)
    is silent on the framework's configuration.*

**Conclusion:* Nielsen--Ninomiya is a no-go theorem with explicit
premises about where chiral fermions live (on a regular lattice). The
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework places chiral fermions in continuous
Lorentzian spacetime with the discreteness orthogonal to the chirality
structure. The premises of Nielsen--Ninomiya are not satisfied by the
framework's configuration; the theorem's conclusion does not apply.*
:::
