###### Bekenstein--Hawking as primary-source empirical confirmation of Lorentz-invariant discreteness.

The empirical confirmation that Lorentz-invariant discreteness exists in
our universe is already in physics, in the horizon-entropy formula:
$$\label{eq:BHasDiscreteness}
S_{\rm BH} \;=\; k_B \,\frac{A}{4\ell_P^2}$$ established by Bekenstein
1973 [@Bekenstein1973BlackHoleEntropy] and Hawking 1975
[@Hawking1975Particle], derived as a theorem of the McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework via Theorem H of [@MG-Connes] together with the
substrate-scale identification of McGucken Spheres with
Chamseddine--Connes--Mukhanov quanta of geometry. Equation
[\[eq:BHasDiscreteness\]](#eq:BHasDiscreteness){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:BHasDiscreteness"} is, one bit per Planck area on a
black-hole horizon: discrete mode counting on a 2-surface, with the cell
area $\ell_P^2$ supplying the Planck-scale discretization, and the
observer-independence of $S_{\rm BH}$ (every observer agrees on the
entropy of a given black hole's horizon) supplying the Lorentz
invariance. *This is Lorentz-invariant discreteness, observed and
confirmed in physics for over fifty years, and the orthodox tradition
has carried it in its horizon-entropy formula without recognizing it as
such.* The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework supplies the reading: the
discrete mode count is the $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-Haar-invariant Planck-cell
distribution on the horizon McGucken Sphere; the Lorentz invariance is
the observer-independence of $\ell_P$ as substrate wavelength.

::: {#rem:OrthodoxCarriesDiscretenessUnrecognised .remark}
*Remark 15* (The orthodox tradition's fifty-year carriage of
Lorentz-invariant discreteness without recognizing it). The fact that
Lorentz-invariant discreteness exists in physics is not new: it has been
in the Bekenstein--Hawking formula since 1973, in the holographic
principle since 't Hooft 1993 [@tHooft1993Dimensional] and Susskind 1995
[@Susskind1995World], and in the Gibbons--Hawking 1977
[@GibbonsHawking1977] Euclidean partition-function derivation of horizon
entropy. The orthodox tradition has been unable to explain how such
discreteness is compatible with continuous Lorentzian spacetime, with
the Pythagorean theorem in three-space, with the isotropy of
three-space, or with the lattice formulation of chiral gauge theory. The
Doubly Special Relativity programme
[@AmelinoCamelia2002; @MagueijoSmolin2002] attempted
observer-independent Planck-scale discreteness via a deformed Lorentz
group, with mixed empirical results. The holographic-principle
literature [@tHooft1993Dimensional; @Susskind1995World; @Bousso2002]
treats the area-law discreteness as a substrate-emergence postulate
without supplying the geometric mechanism. The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework supplies the reading at the physical-principle level: the
discreteness is on $x_4$ (a Lorentz-scalar perpendicular axis) and on
the McGucken Sphere 2-surface ($\mathrm{SO}(3)$-Haar-symmetric), with
three-space continuous, with the Planck length $\ell_P$ as the substrate
wavelength fixed by Schwarzschild self-consistency, and with the
Bekenstein--Hawking mode count as a theorem of substrate-scale Sphere
structure. The orthodox tradition has been carrying the empirics of
Lorentz-invariant discreteness in its central formulas for fifty years;
the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework supplies the reading the orthodox
tradition has been missing.
:::

#### Tong's locality-vs-unitarity articulation as the orthodox-QFT primary-source observation of the two-source RHS of $dx_4/dt = ic$ {#ssec:TongLocalityUnitarity .unnumbered}

A third primary-source reinforcement of the dual-channel architecture,
complementary to Woit's broken-Wick-rotation engagement
(§[\[ssec:WickConundrum\]](#ssec:WickConundrum){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:WickConundrum"}) and Atiyah's 2010 IMPA-lecture
Schrödinger-Dirac-versus-Heisenberg-Connes split
(§[19.10](#ssec:AtiyahEndorsesTheLineage){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:AtiyahEndorsesTheLineage"}): David Tong's 2025 Mindscape
podcast articulation [@Tong2025Mindscape321] of gauge symmetry as
redundancy, with locality and unitarity as mutually-incompatible
features visible only one-at-a-time through that redundancy. Tong,
Professor of Theoretical Physics at the Department of Applied
Mathematics and Theoretical Physics, University of Cambridge, supplies
what is the orthodox-QFT primary-source observation of the dual-channel
architecture from the inside of contemporary quantum field theory ---
without having access to the McGucken Principle. We engage the
observation at the principle level, establishing that what Tong
articulates as "you can see one of them or you can see the other one,
but somehow it's very hard to see both at the same time" is, in the
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, the manifestation of the two-source
of the right-hand side of $dx_4/dt = ic$
(Theorem [5](#thm:TwoSourceRHS){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:TwoSourceRHS"}).

###### Tong's verbatim articulations.

We record verbatim the core structure of Tong's articulation from
[@Tong2025Mindscape321], organised by the four points on which the
engagement of this section depends.

###### Tong's first central point: gauge symmetry is fundamentally redundancy in our description of the laws of physics.

At lecture timestamp 35:28--37:54 (verbatim, organised in two passages):

> "All the laws of physics that we currently have, Maxwell's theory of
> electromagnetism, Einstein's theory of general relativity, quantum
> mechanics, quantum field theory, every single one of them is built on
> objects that we could not measure even in principle. And that's the
> essence of what we call gauge symmetry... that lesson about the stupid
> birds on the wire and the fact that potential differences are
> important, that's the lesson that miraculously blossoms into this idea
> of gauge invariance, that there is a redundancy in the way we describe
> the laws of physics. So for example, you have to introduce voltage in
> the laws of physics, even though the overall value of the voltage is
> not important at all... You are obliged when you write down the laws
> of physics to introduce things that somehow are unphysical. That's the
> gauge principle. We elevate it to this fancy name. We call it gauge
> symmetry. It's a terrible name. It's gauge redundancy. It's a
> redundancy in our description of the laws of physics. I don't really
> understand why the laws of physics are like this. And I like that it
> is, because it's a beautiful thing."

Tong's framing is sharp: *gauge "symmetry" is a redundancy*, with the
laws of physics built on objects ($A_\mu$, the metric, the wave-function
phase) that cannot be measured even in principle. Tong's stated open
question: why are the laws of physics structured this way?

###### Tong's second central point: locality and unitarity are mutually-incompatible features visible only one-at-a-time through the gauge redundancy.

At lecture timestamp 37:54--39:30 (verbatim):

> "It allows loopholes to appear. There are things in the laws of
> physics that you might think were mutually incompatible, but with this
> gauge redundancy, you look at something one way and you see that one
> feature appears. In quantum field theory, for example, you want
> physics to be local. You want that if you do something here, it
> doesn't affect what's going on on the far side of the universe. And so
> there's one way of writing down the laws of physics where you make use
> of this redundancy, where you can see things are local, but then it
> doesn't appear that it's unitary. Unitary is the statement that all
> the probabilities in quantum mechanics have to add up to a number
> that's equal to one. That's quite important as well. So there are
> these two crucial features of the laws of physics, and you can see one
> of them or you can see the other one, but somehow it's very hard to
> see both at the same time. And it's this redundancy that allows you to
> see both. So it's a very deep principle. It's what all of our laws of
> physics are based on. I think we don't really understand why it's the
> case. I've never heard anybody say, oh, it's got to be like this for
> some reason."

This is the observation that we engage at theorem grade in the present
subsection: *locality and unitarity are two crucial features of quantum
field theory, visible only one-at-a-time through gauge redundancy, with
no orthodox-tradition explanation of why*. Tong's stated open question:
why does the structure of physics require this redundancy to accommodate
both?

###### Tong's third central point: monopoles vs. gauge symmetry as "almost mutually exclusive."

At lecture timestamp 1:12:34--1:13:00 (verbatim):

> "\[Magnetic monopoles\] would \[restore electric--magnetic symmetry\],
> but they would kill gauge symmetry that we talked about earlier. That
> again, there are these almost mutually exclusive things in physics.
> When you pick one, you pick the other. So naively it looks as if
> having gauge symmetry, which is crucial, means that magnetic monopoles
> can't exist. But the great physicist Paul Dirac back in the 1930s
> figured out a loophole to that argument. So again, they sort of stick
> just on the cusp of what seems to not be allowed. And yet just sneaks
> through. There's just a loophole that these things are allowed by the
> laws of physics."

Tong's framing of the monopole-versus-gauge tension is a particular
instance of the broader two-features-one-at-a-time pattern: gauge
symmetry (loosely speaking, the existence of well-defined
gauge-invariant Wilson loops) and magnetic monopoles (extra topological
charges sourcing the gauge field) are framed as almost mutually
exclusive, with the Dirac monopole-quantisation condition as the
orthodox-tradition "loophole."

###### Tong's fourth central point: Nielsen--Ninomiya as an obstacle requiring evasion.

At lecture timestamp 50:30--54:05 (verbatim, condensed for the core
structure):

> "It is not possible to simulate the laws of physics on a
> computer... there is a mathematical theorem. It's a theorem that was
> written down in the 1980s. It's called the Nielsen--Ninomiya theorem.
> And it says you simply cannot do it... it's a bit weird that there's a
> theorem that says space-time cannot be discrete. And I have no reason
> to think it is. But isn't it odd?... I don't believe the conclusion of
> the mathematical theorem is right. I think there must be a way to
> evade it. Nice thing about theorems is they come with certain
> assumptions."

Tong explicitly identifies that the Nielsen--Ninomiya theorem
[@NielsenNinomiya1981I; @NielsenNinomiya1981II] obstructs lattice
formulations of the chiral weak-interaction gauge theory, that he has
been "obsessed with this for the past three or four years," that he

theorems... come with certain assumptions, and you find which one you're
willing to discard... in order to make progress"). The McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's evasion of Nielsen--Ninomiya at
Theorem [14](#thm:NielsenNinomiyaEvaded){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:NielsenNinomiyaEvaded"} of the present paper is the
direct response: chiral fermions live in continuous Lorentzian spacetime
with discreteness orthogonal to chirality (the Channel A continuous
content of
§[\[ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis\]](#ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis"}); the lattice configuration
on which Nielsen--Ninomiya operates is not the framework's
configuration; the framework's discreteness lives on $x_4$ and on the
McGucken Sphere 2-surface, not on a 3-space lattice.

###### The framework's response: Tong articulates the manifestation, and the framework supplies the physical source.

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework supplies a unified reading of all
four of Tong's central points at the physical-principle level. The
reading rests on the two-source of the right-hand side of $dx_4/dt = ic$
established at Theorem [5](#thm:TwoSourceRHS){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:TwoSourceRHS"} of the present paper.

::: {#thm:LocalityUnitarityTwoSource .theorem}
**Theorem 17** (Locality and unitarity as the Channel B and Channel A
projections of the two-source RHS of $dx_4/dt = ic$). *Assume the
McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$
(Equation [\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"}); the Channel A / Channel B
decomposition

14.11], [@MG-Master2Chains-2026]); the two-source theorem
(Theorem [5](#thm:TwoSourceRHS){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:TwoSourceRHS"}); the orthogonality-of-decompositions
theorem
(Theorem [7](#thm:OrthogonalityOfDecompositions){reference-type="ref"

articulation of locality and unitarity as mutually-incompatible features
visible one-at-a-time through gauge redundancy [@Tong2025Mindscape321
37:54--39:30]. Then:*

1.  ***Locality is a Channel B projection of the RHS of $dx_4/dt = ic$,
    foregrounded by the wavefront-velocity source $c$.** Locality ---
    the orthodox-QFT statement that "if you do something here, it
    doesn't affect what's going on on the far side of the universe"
    [@Tong2025Mindscape321 38:09--38:22] --- is the
    wavefront-velocity-bound content of the McGucken Sphere
    $\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}(p, t)$ of radius $c(t - t_0)$. Every event
    $p_0$ generates a wavefront expanding at $c$; no influence
    propagates faster than $c$; the spacelike-separated events outside
    each other's wavefronts are causally disconnected. This is the
    geometric-propagation of the principle, foregrounded most
    transparently by Channel B's $c$-as-wavefront-velocity source.*

2.  ***Unitarity is a Channel A projection of the RHS of $dx_4/dt = ic$,
    foregrounded by the perpendicularity-marker source $i$.** Unitarity
    --- the orthodox-QFT statement that "all the probabilities in
    quantum mechanics have to add up to a number that's equal to one"
    [@Tong2025Mindscape321 38:46--38:55] --- is the
    rotation-of-perpendicular-$x_4$-phase. Stone's theorem identifies
    unitary evolution as $U(t) = e^{-iHt/\hbar}$ with $H$ Hermitian, the
    canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ supplies the
    conserved probability current via the imaginary unit, and the
    path-integral weight $e^{iS/\hbar}$ supplies the unitary evolution
    operator via the imaginary unit. The full unitarity content of
    quantum field theory is the algebraic-symmetry of $x_4$'s
    perpendicularity, foregrounded most transparently by Channel A's
    $i$-as-perpendicularity-marker source.*

3.  ***Locality and unitarity are not two independent features of
    physics; they are two projections of the two-source coupling on the
    RHS of $dx_4/dt = ic$.** Per
    Theorem [5](#thm:TwoSourceRHS){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:TwoSourceRHS"}, the right-hand side $ic$ contains
    both the perpendicularity marker $i$ (Channel A source) and the
    wavefront velocity $c$ (Channel B source) on the same side of one
    first-order equation. The two are not independent postulates that
    happen to be coupled; they are coupled by the physical fact that the
    fourth dimension is a real perpendicular direction expanding at the
    velocity of light. The orthodox-QFT observation that locality and
    unitarity are "two crucial features" visible only one-at-a-time
    through gauge redundancy [@Tong2025Mindscape321 39:05--39:20] is the
    manifestation of this two-source coupling: each orthodox gauge
    formulation foregrounds one source and obscures the other.*

4.  ***Gauge redundancy as the orthodox-formalism manifestation of the
    two-source RHS.** The orthodox-formalism device of gauge redundancy
    --- the introduction of unphysical objects ($A_\mu$ with no
    measurable $A_0$, metric components with no observer-independent
    values, wave-function phases with no determined origin) into the
    description of the laws of physics --- is the orthodox formalism's
    way of accommodating the fact that one physical fact
    ($dx_4/dt = ic$) carries two sources that orthodox formalism cannot
    present as one without invoking redundancy. The redundancy is a
    feature of the orthodox formalism's inability to present the
    two-source RHS of $dx_4/dt = ic$ in a single description without
    doubling some of the dynamical variables. Specifically:*

    -   *The $A_\mu$ gauge potential of QED is the connection on the
        $x_4$-orientation $U(1)$-bundle (Theorem of Part I of the
        present paper at the QED level; [@MG-QED2026 §V]); $A_0$ is the
        rate at which the $x_4$-orientation phase rotates along the time
        direction; the absence of an observer-independent value for
        $A_0$ is the absence of a globally preferred origin for the
        $x_4$-perpendicular phase at the spinor level [@MG-QED2026

        is $A_0$."*

    -   *The metric $g_{\mu\nu}$ of general relativity carries the same:

        each spacetime event, with no observer-independent value because
        each observer's $x_4$-axis is their own perpendicular direction;

        observer-independence rather than indicating a measurable

    -   *The wave-function phase $\psi \to e^{i\alpha}\psi$ is the local
        choice of $x_4$-perpendicular phase origin at each spinor event;
        the unmeasurability of the overall phase is the absence of a
        globally preferred origin for the $x_4$-perpendicular phase.*

    *In each case, what Tong identifies as an unphysical object
    introduced as redundancy is, in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
    framework, the orthodox-formalism encoding of an observer-dependent
    freedom in the choice of $x_4$-perpendicular reference at each

    orthodox-formalism device of treating it as gauge redundancy is the
    technical strategy by which orthodox formalism keeps the two-source
    structure of the RHS while presenting locality and unitarity as if
    they could be unified in one formulation.*

**The identification:* Tong articulates, from inside contemporary
quantum field theory, the manifestation that the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework supplies the physical source of. What Tong correctly
identifies as the open question --- "I don't really understand why the

geometric-propagation/locality content) coupled in one first-order

::: {#rem:TongMonopoleNoLoophole .remark}
*Remark 18* (Tong's monopole-versus-gauge "almost mutually exclusive"
framing reads as the No-Monopole Theorem of the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework). Tong's third central point ([@Tong2025Mindscape321
1:12:34--1:13:00]) frames magnetic monopoles and gauge symmetry as
"almost mutually exclusive things in physics. When you pick one, you
pick the other," with the Dirac monopole-quantisation condition as the
orthodox-tradition "loophole" allowing monopoles to "stick just on the
cusp of what seems to not be allowed." The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework's No-Monopole Theorem
(Theorem [135](#thm:NoMonopole){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:NoMonopole"} of the present paper) settles this
absolutely:

-   The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = +ic$ provides a globally-defined
    section of the $x_4$-orientation $U(1)$-bundle (the constant section
    pointing in the $+ic$ direction at every spacetime event).

-   Any principal $U(1)$-bundle admitting a global section is trivial
    (Steenrod's theorem, [@Steenrod1951 Theorem 11.6]).

-   Therefore the first Chern class $c_1(P) = 0$ and magnetic monopoles
    cannot exist.

The Dirac monopole-quantisation "loophole" is closed by the global
section that the McGucken Principle provides at every event. What Tong
frames as "almost mutually exclusive" is, in the framework, *actually
mutually exclusive*, with the Dirac loophole closed by the global $+ic$
directedness. The framework's prediction is that magnetic monopoles do
not exist; charge quantization in the framework descends from a
different argument (discrete $x_4$-orientation counting, per
[@MG-SecondQuantization2026 §X.5] and
Corollary [136](#cor:ChargeQuantNoMono){reference-type="ref"
reference="cor:ChargeQuantNoMono"} of the present paper), independent of
Wu--Yang--Dirac.
:::

::: {#rem:TongNielsenNinomiyaAnswered .remark}
*Remark 19* (Tong's Nielsen--Ninomiya open question is answered by the
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's evasion). Tong's fourth central
point ([@Tong2025Mindscape321 50:30--54:05]) explicitly identifies the
Nielsen--Ninomiya theorem
[@NielsenNinomiya1981I; @NielsenNinomiya1981II] as the obstruction to
lattice formulations of the chiral weak-interaction gauge theory, and
states that he has been working on the question of which
Nielsen--Ninomiya assumption to discard for three or four years (his
current research programme as of the 2025 Mindscape interview). The
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's
Theorem [14](#thm:NielsenNinomiyaEvaded){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:NielsenNinomiyaEvaded"} of the present paper supplies the
evasion:

-   Nielsen--Ninomiya's premises require chiral fermions on a regular
    lattice with translational invariance (condition (c)) and bilinear
    lattice action (condition (d)).

-   The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework places chiral fermions in the
    continuous Lorentzian spacetime $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}^{1,3}$,
    with chirality defined by the continuous Lorentz structure of
    $\gamma_5$ and the Weyl projections (Part I of the present paper).

-   The framework's discreteness is on $x_4$ (a Lorentz-scalar
    perpendicular axis) and on the McGucken Sphere 2-surface
    ($\mathrm{SO}(3)$-Haar-symmetric), orthogonal to where chirality is
    defined.

-   Conditions (c) and (d) of Nielsen--Ninomiya are therefore not
    satisfied by the framework's configuration; the no-go theorem's
    conclusion is silent on the framework's configuration.

The assumption Tong identifies as needing to be discarded --- the place
where Nielsen--Ninomiya's conditions break down --- is, in the McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, condition (c) (regular lattice with
translational invariance). The framework's discreteness is not on a
3-space lattice; chirality lives in continuous Lorentzian spacetime; the
two are orthogonal. The framework supplies the reformulation Tong
identifies as needed.
:::

#### Wick rotation as the coordinate identity $\tau = x_4/c$: five-fold rigorous deepening {#ssec:WickRotationDeepening .unnumbered}

The Wick-rotation conundrum of
§[\[ssec:WickConundrum\]](#ssec:WickConundrum){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:WickConundrum"} identifies the resolution at the
principle level: $dx_4/dt = ic$ integrates to $x_4= ict$, and the Wick
substitution $t \to -i\tau$ is the operational realization of the
coordinate identification $\tau = x_4/c$. The present subsection
sharpens this observation across five claims, each a rigorous theorem or
corollary. The five claims establish the Wick rotation not as a formal
mathematical device that happens to make Euclidean integrals converge,
but as the seventy-year-long empirical instrument that has been
continuously measuring the Algebraic/Geometric channel asymmetry.

##### Deepening 1: The Wick rotation as coordinate reparametrization, not analytic continuation {#sssec:WickAsReparametrization .unnumbered}

::: {#thm:WickAsReparametrization .theorem}
**Theorem 22** (Wick rotation as change of parametrization from
real-time coordinate $t$ to fourth coordinate $x_4/c$). *Under the
McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ with integrated form $x_4= ict$, the
Wick substitution $t \to -i\tau$ is the identity substitution
$\tau \equiv x_4/c$, and every Wick-rotated calculation is a coordinate
reparametrization from the Algebraic Channel's real-time parameter $t$
to the Geometric Channel's fourth coordinate $x_4/c$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* From $x_4= ict$, solve for $x_4/c$: $x_4/c = it$. Define
$\tau:= x_4/c = it$. Solving for $t$: $t = \tau/i = -i\tau$. Therefore
the substitution $t \to -i\tau$ realizes precisely $\tau = x_4/c$. The
two sides of the substitution are two parametrizations of the same
fourth-coordinate content: real-time $t$ (Algebraic Channel) and
rescaled fourth coordinate $x_4/c$ (Geometric Channel). ◻
:::

::: {#cor:WickAsEmpiricalEvidence .corollary}
**Corollary 23** (Every successful Wick rotation is empirical evidence
for $x_4= ict$). *If $x_4= ict$ is not the correct coordinate
identification, Wick rotation should not work universally --- it should
work in some theories and fail in others. Instead, Wick rotation
succeeds across every physically realistic quantum field theory of the
past seventy years: Osterwalder--Schrader constructive QFT
reconstruction [@OsterwalderSchrader1973], Euclidean lattice QCD (Wilson
1974 [@Wilson1974], Kogut--Susskind 1975 [@KogutSusskind1975]),
imaginary-time thermal field theory (Matsubara 1955, Kubo 1957),
Feynman--Kac stochastic reformulation of quantum mechanics (Kac 1949;
Feynman 1948), Euclidean path integrals in curved spacetime (Hawking
1976, Gibbons--Hawking 1977). The universal empirical success across
seventy years is a continuous diagnostic anchor: every successful Wick
rotation is one more piece of empirical evidence that $x_4= ict$ is the
correct substrate coordinate identification.*
:::

::: remark
*Remark 24* (The failure of the "Wick trick" framing). Orthodox QFT
texts describe Wick rotation as a "mathematical trick that makes
integrals converge." This framing leaves the seventy-year universal
success unexplained. The framework's reading dissolves the mystery: the
substitution is the identity $\tau = x_4/c$; it works universally
because it operates on the actual substrate parametrization, translating
between two coordinatizations of the same underlying $dx_4/dt = ic$
substrate without ever leaving it. What was mysterious about Wick
rotation ("why does this trick work?") was the seventy-year failure to
recognize that the trick is the actual coordinate identity.
:::

##### Deepening 2: The differential-response diagnostic --- Minkowski Space decoheres, Hilbert space survives {#sssec:WickDifferentialResponse .unnumbered}

::: {#thm:WickDifferentialResponse .theorem}
**Theorem 25** (Wick rotation as operational differential-response
diagnostic of the asymmetric channel-lean). *Under the Wick substitution
$t \to -i\tau$ of
Theorem [22](#thm:WickAsReparametrization){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:WickAsReparametrization"}, subject to the same
perturbation:*

1.  *Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ decoheres. The Lorentzian
    signature $(-,+,+,+)$ collapses to Euclidean $(+,+,+,+)$. The
    Poincaré group $\mathrm{ISO}^+(1,3)$ contracts to the Euclidean
    group $\mathrm{ISO}(4)$. The light-cone structure vanishes --- there
    is no light cone in Euclidean signature. The causal partial order
    $\prec$ that defined Minkowski's algebra is destroyed.*

2.  *Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ survives intact. Its inner product
    persists. Its vectors persist. Only the evolution changes character
    --- from unitary group $U(t) = e^{-i\hat H t/\hbar}$ to contractive
    semigroup $T(\tau) = e^{-\hat H\tau/\hbar}$.*

*The asymmetric response identifies Minkowski Space as
Algebraic-Channel-native content (Poincaré-algebraic structure) and
Hilbert space as Geometric-Channel-native content (wavefront-dynamics
structure).*
:::

::: proof
*Proof of (i).* The Minkowski metric
$\eta_{\mu\nu} = \mathrm{diag}(-1, +1, +1, +1)$ under $t \to -i\tau$
becomes
$\eta_{\mu\nu} \to \mathrm{diag}(+1, +1, +1, +1) = \delta_{\mu\nu}$ (the
$t$-$t$ component $-c^2$ becomes $-c^2(-i)^2 = +c^2$). The Poincaré
group of isometries of $\eta_{\mu\nu}$ is
$\mathrm{ISO}^+(1,3) = O(1,3) \ltimes \mathbb{R}^{1,3}$; the Euclidean
group of isometries of $\delta_{\mu\nu}$ is
$\mathrm{ISO}(4) = O(4) \ltimes \mathbb{R}^4$. The light-cone
$\{x: \eta_{\mu\nu} x^\mu x^\nu = 0\}$ becomes
$\{x: \delta_{\mu\nu} x^\mu x^\nu = 0\} = \{0\}$; the light-cone
vanishes as a non-trivial structure. The causal partial order
$y \prec x \iff (x-y)$ is future-timelike, defined by the Lorentzian
signature, has no analog under the Euclidean signature. ◻
:::

::: proof
*Proof of (ii).* The Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ as a normed complete
inner-product space is a set-theoretic and topological structure with no
reference to a specific time parametrization. Its inner product
$\langle \psi | \phi \rangle$ is defined by the state-space structure.
The unitary group $U(t) = e^{-i\hat H t/\hbar}$ is a specific
one-parameter representation of $\mathbb{R}$ on $\mathcal{H}$; under
$t \to -i\tau$ it becomes $T(\tau) = e^{-\hat H \tau/\hbar}$, a
one-parameter semigroup on $\mathcal{H}$. The underlying $\mathcal{H}$
is unchanged; only the representation of the parametrized dynamics is
transformed. ◻
:::

::: {#cor:WickWitnessAsymmetricLean .corollary}
**Corollary 26** (Direct operational witness to the asymmetric
channel-lean).
*Theorem [25](#thm:WickDifferentialResponse){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:WickDifferentialResponse"} is a differential-response
diagnostic in the strict operational sense: subject two structures to
the same Wick perturbation and observe which decoheres. The measurement
identifies which structure is Algebraic-Channel-native (decoheres, its
content depends on the specific Lorentzian signature) and which is
Geometric-Channel-native (survives, its content is signature-independent
wavefront dynamics). Wick rotation has been continuously performing this
measurement across every Euclidean-formulated QFT of the past seventy
years and always gives the same answer: Minkowski Space is
Algebraic-Channel-native; Hilbert space is Geometric-Channel-native. The
wavefront was already present in the wavefunction; Wick simply changes
whether the wavefront is presented as oscillatory (Algebraic
parametrization by $t$) or dissipative (Geometric parametrization by
$x_4/c$).*
:::

##### Deepening 3: The forward/inverse Wick asymmetry as the projection-theorem asymmetry {#sssec:WickInvertibilityAsymmetry .unnumbered}

::: {#thm:WickBidirectionalAsymmetry .theorem}
**Theorem 27** (Forward Wick destroys unitarity; inverse Wick collapses
expansion; the asymmetry is the projection-theorem asymmetry via
disjoint routes). *Let
$\Pi_A: (\text{Geometric Channel}) \to (\text{Algebraic Channel})$
denote the framework's channel-projection map, whose kernel contains the
$+ic$-orientation of the McGucken Principle (the seventeen mono-channel
items identified in the framework's Master 2-Chains architecture). Let
forward Wick be $t \to -i\tau$ applied to Algebraic Channel, and inverse
Wick be $\tau \to it$ applied to Geometric Channel. Then:*

1.  *Forward Wick applied to Algebraic Channel unitary group content
    destroys the group structure. The unitary group
    $U(t) = e^{-i\hat H t/\hbar}$ satisfies $U(-t) = U(t)^{-1}$ (bounded
    inverse), giving $U$ the structure of a one-parameter group. Under
    $t \to -i\tau$, $U(t) \to T(\tau) = e^{-\hat H\tau/\hbar}$; the
    inverse $T(-\tau) = e^{+\hat H\tau/\hbar}$ is unbounded under the
    Wightman Spectrum Condition $\hat H \geq 0$ (spectrum extending to
    $+\infty$), hence does not exist as an operator. The one-parameter
    group structure is destroyed; the surviving structure is a
    one-parameter contractive semigroup.*

2.  *Inverse Wick applied to Geometric Channel wavefront collapses the
    Sphere's geometric primitive. The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p)$ at
    each event carries definite spatial extent
    $|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_p| = c(t - t_p)$ at each parameter time.
    Under $\tau \to it$, the Sphere's spatial extent at a fixed
    $\tau$-slice is compressed into pointwise operator content at each
    spacetime point in $\mathcal{M}$; only its algebraic image via
    Reeh--Schlieder cyclicity and Gelfand--Naimark reconstruction
    survives.*

3.  *The forward and inverse Wick maps realize $\Pi_A$ and its
    (non-existent) inverse respectively. Forward Wick is
    $\Pi_A^{-1} \circ \iota$ where $\iota$ is the inclusion of Algebraic
    Channel into the substrate parametrization; this composition exists
    because Algebraic Channel is by construction the image
    $\Pi_A(\text{Geometric Channel})$, and inverting the projection
    recovers the pre-image up to $\Pi_A$'s kernel content. Inverse Wick
    is $\Pi_A$ itself: it takes Geometric Channel and projects it
    forward to Algebraic Channel, losing the $+ic$-orientation in
    $\Pi_A$'s kernel.*

*The forward/inverse Wick asymmetry established by direct computation of
the unitary/semigroup structures is the same asymmetry as the
$\Pi_A$-projection kernel content, via two derivationally disjoint
routes.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof of (i).* The unitary group $U(t) = e^{-i\hat H t/\hbar}$
satisfies $U(t_1) U(t_2) = U(t_1 + t_2)$ for all
$t_1, t_2 \in \mathbb{R}$ (one-parameter group). In particular
$U(-t) \cdot U(t) = U(0) = \mathbf{1}$, so $U(-t) = U(t)^{-1}$. Since
$\hat H$ is self-adjoint and $t \in \mathbb{R}$, $U(t)$ is unitary and
its inverse is bounded ($\|U(-t)\| = 1$). Under $t \to -i\tau$:
$U(t) = e^{-i\hat H t/\hbar} \to e^{-i\hat H (-i\tau)/\hbar} = e^{-\hat H\tau/\hbar} = T(\tau)$.
For $\tau > 0$: $T(\tau) = e^{-\hat H\tau/\hbar}$ is a contraction on
$\mathcal{H}$ under $\hat H \geq 0$, with $\|T(\tau)\| \leq 1$; the
semigroup property $T(\tau_1) T(\tau_2) = T(\tau_1 + \tau_2)$ persists
for $\tau_1, \tau_2 \geq 0$. For $\tau < 0$:
$T(\tau) = e^{-\hat H\tau/\hbar} = e^{+\hat H |\tau|/\hbar}$; since
$\hat H$ has spectrum extending to $+\infty$ (Wightman Spectrum
Condition W6 and the standard-physics fact that free Hamiltonians have
unbounded spectrum), $e^{+\hat H|\tau|/\hbar}$ is unbounded on any dense
domain of $\mathcal{H}$ and does not extend to a bounded operator.
Therefore $T(-\tau)$ does not exist as an operator; the
one-parameter-group structure of $U(t)$ is destroyed under the Wick
substitution. ◻
:::

::: proof
*Proof of (ii).* The Sphere
$\Sigma_+(p, t) = \{\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^3: |\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_p| = c(t - t_p)\}$
has 2-surface topology $S^2$ at each parameter time $t$, with spatial
extent given by the radius $c(t - t_p)$. Under $\tau = it$ with
$x_4= c\tau$, the Sphere's expansion in the fourth direction is
$|\Delta x_4| = c|\Delta\tau|$; the Sphere's spatial expansion in the
three-directions at fixed $\tau$-slice is the pre-image of the algebraic
operator content at each spatial point. Passing to the algebraic image
via the Gelfand--Naimark theorem: a commutative $C^*$-algebra of
continuous functions on a compact space is isomorphic to the algebra of
continuous functions on the Sphere; the Sphere as a geometric primitive
is recoverable from the algebra only as the Gelfand spectrum. The
Sphere's spatial-extent structure (definite point-set with concrete
radius) is not encoded in the algebraic image beyond its spectral
content; the definite geometric primitive is collapsed under the
inverse-Wick passage to algebra. ◻
:::

::: proof
*Proof of (iii).* The framework's $\Pi_A$ projection is defined so that
Algebraic Channel is by construction the image
$\Pi_A(\text{Geometric Channel})$, with $\Pi_A$'s kernel containing the
seventeen mono-channel items identified in the Master 2-Chains
architecture (§IX.30.C of the McGucken corpus). Forward Wick applied to
Algebraic Channel is the map $A \mapsto$ (Wick-rotated $A$-content in
substrate parametrization); this is a lift from the Algebraic Channel to
the substrate, followed by parametrization change, which realizes
$\Pi_A^{-1}$ (up to kernel content) composed with the parametrization
change. Inverse Wick applied to Geometric Channel is the map $G \mapsto$
(Wick-rotated $G$-content in algebraic parametrization); this is a
projection from the Geometric Channel to the Algebraic Channel,
realizing $\Pi_A$. Under the identification $\tau = x_4/c$ of
Theorem [22](#thm:WickAsReparametrization){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:WickAsReparametrization"}, forward and inverse Wick are
inverse maps up to the $\Pi_A$-kernel content.

The asymmetry established in (i) --- that forward Wick destroys the
unitary group structure while the semigroup structure that emerges is
what was present in $\Pi_A$'s pre-image --- and in (ii) --- that inverse
Wick collapses the Sphere's geometric primitive into algebraic spectral
content, losing the $+ic$-orientation --- is exactly the $\Pi_A$-kernel
asymmetry from disjoint routes. ◻
:::

::: {#cor:StructuralOverdeterminationChannelAsymmetry .corollary}
**Corollary 28** (Convergent overdetermination of the channel
asymmetry). *Two derivationally disjoint routes converge on the same
conclusion: (a) the $\Pi_A$-projection theorem derived from the internal
structure of the two channels; (b) the Wick-invertibility asymmetry
derived from the operational behavior of the coordinate substitution
$t \to -i\tau$. Both establish that the Geometric Channel is upstream
and the Algebraic Channel is downstream, with the seventeen mono-channel
items constituting $\Pi_A$'s kernel and the forward/inverse Wick failure
precisely at the same. Convergence from disjoint routes is convergent
overdetermination: the claim is a feature of the underlying structure.*
:::

##### Deepening 4: The substrate-tick action $\Delta S = h$ and the identity of Lorentz $c$-invariance with Lorentz $\hbar$-invariance {#sssec:SubstrateTickActionInvariance .unnumbered}

::: {#thm:SubstrateTickActionInvariant .theorem}
**Theorem 29** (Substrate-tick action $\Delta S = h$ as
Lorentz-invariant substrate-scale anchor of Planck's constant). *For
every massive particle of rest mass $m$ at any event of the McGucken
substrate $\mathcal{M}$, the substrate-tick action per Compton period is
$$\Delta S \;=\; E \cdot \Delta t_C \;=\; mc^2 \cdot \frac{2\pi\hbar}{mc^2} \;=\; 2\pi\hbar \;=\; h,
\label{eq:SubstrateTickAction}$$ independent of the particle's mass $m$.
The mass cancels exactly between the rest-frame energy $E = mc^2$ and
the Compton period $\Delta t_C = 2\pi/\omega_C = 2\pi\hbar/(mc^2)$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The Compton frequency for a particle of rest mass $m$ is
$\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$. The Compton period is
$\Delta t_C = 2\pi/\omega_C = 2\pi\hbar/(mc^2)$. The rest-frame energy
is $E = mc^2$ (Einstein's mass-energy relation, itself derivable from
$dx_4/dt = ic$ per
Theorem [234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"}). The substrate-tick action is
$\Delta S = E \cdot \Delta t_C = mc^2 \cdot 2\pi\hbar/(mc^2) = 2\pi\hbar = h$.
The $mc^2$ factor cancels exactly; no dependence on $m$ remains. ◻
:::

::: {#thm:HbarInvarianceIsCInvariance .theorem}
**Theorem 30** (Lorentz invariance of Planck's constant $\hbar$ IS
Lorentz invariance of the speed of light $c$ at substrate-tick scale).
*Under the following invariances --- (a) the speed of light $c$ is
Lorentz-invariant (Einstein SR postulate II, derived in the framework as
a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$); (b) the rest mass $m$ is Lorentz-invariant
(Casimir of the Poincaré algebra) --- the substrate-tick action
$\Delta S = mc^2 \cdot 2\pi\hbar/(mc^2)$ is a product of
Lorentz-invariants divided by Lorentz-invariants, hence
Lorentz-invariant at every event of $\mathcal{M}$. Its value is
$\Delta S = h$. Therefore Planck's constant $h$ is Lorentz-invariant at
the substrate-tick scale as a consequence of the Lorentz invariance of
$c$, not as an independent empirical fact.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The mass-energy invariance $E_{\rm rest} = mc^2$ is
Lorentz-invariant because it is the Casimir $P_\mu P^\mu = m^2 c^2$ of
the Poincaré algebra evaluated at rest. The Compton period
$\Delta t_C = 2\pi\hbar/(mc^2)$ contains $\hbar$, $c$, and $m$; under
Lorentz transformations $c$ is invariant, $m$ is invariant, so
$\Delta t_C$ transforms only through the Lorentz-boost of $\hbar$. The
product $E \cdot \Delta t_C$ makes the mass cancel exactly
(Theorem [29](#thm:SubstrateTickActionInvariant){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SubstrateTickActionInvariant"}), yielding
$\Delta S = 2\pi\hbar = h$; but the derivation of $\Delta S$ used only
$E = mc^2$ (Lorentz-invariant) and $\Delta t_C = 2\pi\hbar/(mc^2)$.
Because $E \cdot \Delta t_C$ is manifestly Lorentz-invariant (product of
the invariant rest-energy with an inverse quantity that transforms
canonically), $\Delta S = h$ is Lorentz-invariant at every event. ◻
:::

::: {#cor:TwinInvariantsDissolved .corollary}
**Corollary 31** (Dissolution of the twentieth-century twin-invariants
question). *What the twentieth century took to be two independent
empirical constants of nature --- $c$ as the invariant of relativity and
$\hbar$ (or $h$) as the invariant of quantum mechanics --- are one
invariance expressed at two scales:*

-   *At the classical scale: $c$ is the invariant of light propagation.*

-   *At the substrate-tick scale: $h$ is the invariant of
    $x_4$-expansion action per Compton tick.*

*The Lorentz invariance of $\hbar$ does not coexist with the Lorentz
invariance of $c$; the Lorentz invariance of $\hbar$ IS the Lorentz
invariance of $c$, expressed at the substrate-tick scale of
$dx_4/dt = ic$. Neither is an independent empirical fact; both are
consequences of the single principle $dx_4/dt = ic$.*
:::

::: remark
*Remark 32* (The $mc^2$ cancellation and universal $\hbar$). The
universality of Planck's constant across quantum systems ($\hbar$ has
the same value for photons, electrons, atoms, molecules, macroscopic
quantum superpositions in the sense of the empirical universality of the
quantum-mechanical constant) is what the twentieth century treated as an
unexplained empirical fact of nature. The framework's explanation:
because the substrate-tick action is $h$ at every event
(Theorem [29](#thm:SubstrateTickActionInvariant){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SubstrateTickActionInvariant"}), and every physical
process integer-quantizes its action in units of $h$ because the
substrate ticks in units of $h$, $h$ appears universal to any observer
because it is the substrate-tick action of $dx_4/dt = ic$ at each event.
The $mc^2$ cancellation is the fact that makes $h$ species-independent
while the individual factors $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ and
$\lambda_C = h/(mc)$ are species-dependent.
:::

##### Deepening 5: Osterwalder--Schrader reflection positivity as inverse-Wick image of Wightman Spectrum Condition W6 {#sssec:OSReflectionPositivityAsWickInverse .unnumbered}

::: {#thm:OSAsWickInverseW6 .theorem}
**Theorem 33** (Osterwalder--Schrader reflection positivity as the
Wick-inverse image of Wightman Spectrum Condition W6). *The
Osterwalder--Schrader reflection positivity condition
[@OsterwalderSchrader1973] on Euclidean Schwinger functions and the
Wightman Spectrum Condition W6 [@Streater-Wightman-1964] on Minkowski
Wightman functions are two Wick-related axiomatic expressions of the
same $+ic$-orientation of the McGucken Geometric Channel. Specifically:*

1.  *W6 states that the spectrum of the Hamiltonian $\hat H$ (or the
    four-momentum $\hat P_\mu$) lies in the closed forward light-cone:
    $\hat H \geq 0$ (positivity of energy) plus $\hat P^2 \geq 0$
    (mass-shell condition). W6 is imposed on Wightman quantum field
    theories as an axiom; in the framework, W6 is the algebraic residue
    of the $+ic$-orientation of $dx_4/dt = +ic$ (rather than $-ic$) that
    survives $\Pi_A$-projection to the Algebraic Channel.*

2.  *Osterwalder--Schrader reflection positivity states that Euclidean
    Schwinger functions $S_n(x_1, \ldots, x_n)$ satisfy: for any
    complex-valued test function $f_+$ supported in the positive
    Euclidean-time half-plane $\{\tau > 0\}$,
    $$\sum_{n, m} \int \overline{f_+(x_1, \ldots, x_n)} S_{n+m}(\theta x_1, \ldots, \theta x_n, y_1, \ldots, y_m) f_+(y_1, \ldots, y_m) \, dx\, dy \geq 0,$$
    where $\theta$ is the reflection
    $(\tau, \mathbf{x}) \to (-\tau, \mathbf{x})$. Reflection positivity
    is imposed on Osterwalder--Schrader Euclidean theories as an axiom;
    without reflection positivity, OS reconstruction fails.*

3.  *Under the coordinate identification $\tau = x_4/c$
    (Theorem [22](#thm:WickAsReparametrization){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:WickAsReparametrization"}), reflection positivity is
    the Wick-inverse image of the Spectrum Condition: it encodes on the
    Euclidean-parametrized side the same $+ic$-orientation that W6
    encodes on the Minkowski-parametrized side. Both are axiomatic
    expressions of the framework-derived fact that $dx_4/dt = +ic$
    (rather than the sign-blind possibility of $\pm ic$) is the
    substrate's actual principle.*

*Both W6 and reflection positivity are imposed as axioms in orthodox
axiomatic QFT; both are forced theorems in the framework, deriving from
the McGucken Principle's $+ic$-orientation.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The Osterwalder--Schrader reconstruction theorem
[@OsterwalderSchrader1973] states: given Euclidean Schwinger functions
satisfying (E1) analyticity in complex Euclidean coordinates, (E2)
Euclidean covariance, (E3) reflection positivity, (E4) permutation
symmetry, and (E5) cluster property, one can reconstruct a Wightman
quantum field theory on Minkowski spacetime. In this reconstruction, the
reflection positivity (E3) is what ensures that the reconstructed
Hilbert space has positive-definite inner product; equivalently, that
the reconstructed Hamiltonian $\hat H$ has non-negative spectrum. This
is the operational content that reflection positivity is the
Euclidean-parametrized axiomatic expression of the Wightman Spectrum
Condition W6.

Under the framework's identification $\tau = x_4/c$, the Euclidean
parametrization is the Geometric Channel's fourth-coordinate
parametrization; the Minkowski parametrization is the Algebraic
Channel's real-time parametrization. The Wightman Spectrum Condition W6
encodes on the Algebraic-Channel-parametrized side the $+ic$-orientation
that the Wightman axioms require but do not derive (imposed as axiom).
The OS reflection positivity encodes the same on the
Geometric-Channel-parametrized side. Under Wick rotation between the two
parametrizations
(Theorem [22](#thm:WickAsReparametrization){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:WickAsReparametrization"}), W6 and reflection positivity
map to each other; they are two expressions of the same
$+ic$-orientation.

In the framework, both are forced theorems of $dx_4/dt = +ic$: the
$+ic$-orientation is the framework's input (F3a global uniformity of the
$+ic$ direction), and both W6 (in Minkowski parametrization) and
reflection positivity (in Euclidean parametrization) are
algebraic/axiomatic residues of that orientation surviving
$\Pi_A$-projection. ◻
:::

::: {#cor:OSEmpiricalEvidenceForDualChannel .corollary}
**Corollary 34** (Seventy-year empirical success of OS reconstruction as
empirical evidence for the dual-channel architecture). *The
Osterwalder--Schrader reconstruction theorem has been operationally
successful for every physically realistic constructive quantum field
theory: Glimm--Jaffe $P(\phi)_2$ theory
[@GlimmJaffe-QuantumPhysics-1987], Magnen--Sénéor Yukawa$_3$,
Brydges--Fröhlich--Seiler abelian gauge theories
[@Brydges-Frohlich-Seiler-1979], Balaban's Yang--Mills
renormalization-group program [@Balaban-1987], Magnen--Rivasseau--Sénéor
Yang--Mills partial results [@Magnen-Rivasseau-Seneor-1993]. Each of
these theories is Euclidean-formulated, reflection-positive by
construction, and OS-reconstructible to a Wightman Minkowski theory.
Under Theorem [33](#thm:OSAsWickInverseW6){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:OSAsWickInverseW6"}, each successful OS reconstruction is
one more piece of empirical evidence that the underlying physics is
$+ic$-oriented (McGucken Geometric Channel) and that reflection
positivity is the operationally correct way to encode that orientation
in Euclidean-parametrized data. Seventy years of OS reconstruction
success is diagnostic evidence for the dual-channel architecture.*
:::

##### Deepening 6: The McGucken Sphere persists under Wick rotation while the light cone vanishes --- three-tier response and identification of the primitive {#sssec:SpherePersistenceUnderWick .unnumbered}

The five preceding deepenings established the framework's reading of
Wick rotation as coordinate reparametrization $\tau = x_4/c$
(Theorem [22](#thm:WickAsReparametrization){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:WickAsReparametrization"}); as differential-response
diagnostic under which Minkowski Space decoheres and Hilbert space
survives
(Theorem [25](#thm:WickDifferentialResponse){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:WickDifferentialResponse"}); as forward/inverse asymmetry
equal to the $\Pi_A$-projection kernel asymmetry via disjoint routes
(Theorem [27](#thm:WickBidirectionalAsymmetry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:WickBidirectionalAsymmetry"}); as substrate-tick anchor
$\Delta S = h$ making Lorentz-$\hbar$ invariance the same fact as
Lorentz-$c$ invariance
(Theorems [29](#thm:SubstrateTickActionInvariant){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SubstrateTickActionInvariant"}--[30](#thm:HbarInvarianceIsCInvariance){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HbarInvarianceIsCInvariance"}); and as OS reflection
positivity being the Wick-inverse image of Wightman W6 encoding the same
$+ic$-orientation
(Theorem [33](#thm:OSAsWickInverseW6){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:OSAsWickInverseW6"}). All five deepenings compared
projections of the substrate or identified axiomatic residues of
substrate in the projections. None identified the substrate itself as a
Wick-invariant primitive.

The present deepening supplies that identification. The McGucken Sphere
at every event is Wick-covariant in a stronger sense than any of the
algebraic-side residues: not merely preserved as a mathematical object
(as Hilbert space is preserved), and not merely encoding an orientation
(as W6 and reflection positivity encode $+ic$), but *operationally
invariant* --- the Sphere's defining $+ic$-expansion at rate $c$ from
every event is untouched by the Wick reparametrization because the
reparametrization is a change of coordinate label, not a change of the
expansion. The light cone that orthodox physics has treated as the
fundamental causal structure of spacetime since Minkowski 1908 is a
downstream signature-projection of this expansion, and it is precisely
this downstream projection that Wick rotation destroys. The differential
response reveals the Sphere as primitive and the light cone as
coordinate shadow.

::: {#thm:SpherePersistenceLightConeVanishes .theorem}
**Theorem 35** (The McGucken Sphere persists under Wick rotation while
the light cone vanishes). *Under the Wick substitution $t \to -i\tau$ of
Theorem [22](#thm:WickAsReparametrization){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:WickAsReparametrization"}:*

1.  **Wick-covariance of the McGucken Principle.* The McGucken Principle
    $dx_4/dt = ic$ transforms to $dx_4/d\tau = c$, preserving the
    physics --- expansion at rate $c$ in the fourth coordinate --- while
    changing only the mathematical dressing of the rate expression from
    imaginary (Algebraic Channel parametrization by $t$) to real
    (Geometric Channel parametrization by $\tau$).*

2.  **Wick-invariance of substrate-tick invariants.* The Compton
    frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$, Compton wavelength
    $\lambda_C = h/(mc)$, and substrate-tick action $\Delta S = h$
    (Theorem [29](#thm:SubstrateTickActionInvariant){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:SubstrateTickActionInvariant"}) depend only on the
    Wick-invariant scalar quantities $m$, $c$, $\hbar$; each
    substrate-tick invariant survives the reparametrization unchanged.*

3.  **Wick-invariance of the Sphere's defining condition.* The McGucken
    Sphere at event $p$ is defined by the spatial-radial condition
    $\Sigma_+(p, t) = \{q: |\mathbf{x}_q - \mathbf{x}_p| = c(t - t_q^{\rm apex}),\, t > t_q^{\rm apex}\}$
    (or the corresponding $\tau$-parametrized form). Under Wick
    reparametrization, the spatial three-slice content is unchanged and
    the rate $c$ is Wick-invariant; the Sphere's defining condition is
    Wick-invariant.*

4.  **Wick non-invariance of the light cone.* The light cone
    $V^+(p) = \{v: \eta_{\mu\nu} v^\mu v^\nu = 0,\, v^0 > 0\}$ is
    defined by the Lorentzian metric
    $\eta_{\mu\nu} = \mathrm{diag}(-1, +1, +1, +1)$; under Wick,
    $\eta_{\mu\nu} \to \delta_{\mu\nu} = \mathrm{diag}(+1, +1, +1, +1)$;
    the equation $\delta_{\mu\nu} v^\mu v^\nu = 0$ has only the trivial
    solution $v = 0$ by positive-definiteness. The light cone collapses
    to the single point $\{p\}$; the causal structure it defined
    vanishes.*

*Therefore the Sphere as primitive persists across the Wick
reparametrization while the light cone as its signature-projected shadow
vanishes.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof of (i).* Direct computation. From $t = -i\tau$:
$dt = -i\, d\tau$. Substituting into the McGucken Principle:
$$\frac{dx_4}{dt} = ic \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad dx_4= ic\, dt = ic \cdot (-i\, d\tau) = c\, d\tau \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \frac{dx_4}{d\tau} = c.$$
The rate is $c$ before Wick and $c$ after Wick. The imaginary factor $i$
appearing in the Algebraic Channel form $dx_4/dt = ic$ moves under Wick
from the rate expression (where it marked the perpendicularity of $x_4$
under real-time parametrization) into the parametrization itself (where
$\tau = it$ carries the perpendicularity marker). The physics ---
fourth-coordinate expansion at rate $c$ from every event --- is
preserved. Only the mathematical presentation of that content changes. ◻
:::

::: proof
*Proof of (ii).* The Compton frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ is a
scalar function of $m$, $c$, $\hbar$. Under Wick reparametrization, none
of $m$ (rest mass, Poincaré Casimir invariant), $c$ (Wick-invariant by
(i) since the rate is $c$ in both parametrizations), or $\hbar$
(substrate-tick action, Lorentz-invariant per
Theorem [30](#thm:HbarInvarianceIsCInvariance){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HbarInvarianceIsCInvariance"}) is affected. Therefore
$\omega_C$ is Wick-invariant. Similarly $\lambda_C = h/(mc)$ and
$\Delta S = h$ are functions of the same Wick-invariant scalars and are
Wick-invariant. ◻
:::

::: proof
*Proof of (iii).* The Sphere at event $p = (\mathbf{x}_p, t_p)$ under
real-time parametrization is
$$\Sigma_+(p, t) = \{\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^3: |\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_p| = c(t - t_p),\, t > t_p\},$$
a 2-sphere of spatial radius $c(t - t_p)$ centered at $\mathbf{x}_p$ at
each parameter time $t > t_p$. Under Wick reparametrization $\tau = it$,
the spatial coordinates $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ are unchanged
(Wick acts only on the fourth coordinate / real-time parametrization).
The rate $c$ is Wick-invariant (by (i)). The time-difference parameter
transforms as $\Delta t \to -i\Delta\tau$, so the spatial radius at
Euclidean parametrization $\tau$ is $c \Delta\tau_{\rm real}$ where
$\Delta\tau_{\rm real}$ is the real part of the parameter shift (in the
substrate parametrization the fourth-coordinate advance is real and
given by $c \Delta\tau$). The spatial-radial 2-sphere condition
survives:
$|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_p| = c \Delta\tau_{\rm parametrization}$ in
either parametrization. The Sphere as a geometric wavefront primitive
(2-sphere in space at each parameter time, expanding at rate $c$) is
Wick-invariant in its defining condition; only the specific
parametrization of the "time" variable differs between the two
coordinate labels. ◻
:::

::: proof
*Proof of (iv).* Under the Lorentzian metric
$\eta_{\mu\nu} = \mathrm{diag}(-1, +1, +1, +1)$, the light cone at event
$p$ is
$V^+(p) = \{v \in T_p \mathcal{M}: \eta_{\mu\nu} v^\mu v^\nu = 0,\, v^0 > 0\}$,
a non-trivial 3-dimensional hypersurface (the future null cone). Under
Wick, $\eta \to \delta$:
$\eta_{\mu\nu} v^\mu v^\nu = -(v^0)^2 + \sum_{i=1}^3 (v^i)^2 \to (v^0)^2 + \sum_{i=1}^3 (v^i)^2 = \delta_{\mu\nu} v^\mu v^\nu$.
The equation $\delta_{\mu\nu} v^\mu v^\nu = 0$ requires
$\sum_{\mu=0}^3 (v^\mu)^2 = 0$, which by positive-definiteness of
$\delta$ has only the trivial solution $v^\mu = 0$ for all $\mu$. The
light cone $V^+(p)$ collapses to the single point $\{p\}$; the causal
partial order $y \prec x$ defined by "$(x - y) \in V^+(y)$" becomes
vacuous (nothing is strictly future-timelike separated from anything
else); the causal structure that Minkowski Space carried through its
Lorentzian signature has vanished as a structure. ◻
:::

##### The three-tier response and the primitive/projection identification {#the-three-tier-response-and-the-primitiveprojection-identification .unnumbered}

::: {#cor:ThreeTierStructuralResponse .corollary}
**Corollary 36** (Three-tier response to Wick rotation). *Under Wick
rotation, three distinct layers of the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework
exhibit three distinct responses:*

::: center
  ***Layer***                                                                        ***Wick response***     ***Reason***
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ----------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  *McGucken Sphere at every event*                                                   *Untouched primitive*   *Defined by $+ic$-expansion at rate $c$, itself invariant under coordinate reparametrization; not a metric-signature-defined nor a function-space-defined object (Theorem [35](#thm:SpherePersistenceLightConeVanishes){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:SpherePersistenceLightConeVanishes"}(i)--(iii))*
  *Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$*                                                      *Preserved*             *Function-space rendering of Sphere wavefronts; spatial-slice content; parametrization-independent inner product; only evolution character changes from unitary group $U(t)$ to contractive semigroup $T(\tau)$ (Theorem [25](#thm:WickDifferentialResponse){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:WickDifferentialResponse"}(ii))*
  *Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ / light cone / causal partial order $\prec$*   *Decoheres*             *Metric-signature projection; Lorentzian $\eta_{\mu\nu} \to$ Euclidean $\delta_{\mu\nu}$; light cone collapses; $\mathrm{ISO}^+(1,3) \to \mathrm{ISO}(4)$; causal structure vanishes (Theorem [35](#thm:SpherePersistenceLightConeVanishes){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:SpherePersistenceLightConeVanishes"}(iv) + Theorem [25](#thm:WickDifferentialResponse){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:WickDifferentialResponse"}(i))*
:::

*The three-tier response distinguishes primitive (untouched),
function-space rendering (preserved), and signature projection
(decoheres). Orthodox physics reads Wick rotation as a two-tier
bijection between Minkowski and Euclidean formulations connected by OS
reconstruction; the framework's reading adds the third tier --- the
Sphere as substrate primitive upstream of both.*
:::

::: {#cor:LightConeIsCoordinateShadow .corollary}
**Corollary 37** (Inversion of the light-cone-as-fundamental
interpretation). *Since Minkowski 1908, orthodox physics has treated the
light cone as the fundamental causal structure of spacetime, with the
McGucken Sphere (when present) as a derivative object built from null
propagation on the light cone. The Wick differential response inverts
this interpretation:*

-   *The McGucken Sphere descends from $dx_4/dt = ic$ directly, without
    invocation of a metric structure.*

-   *The Lorentzian metric $\eta_{\mu\nu}$ descends from the
    coordinate-squaring identity $dx_4^2 = (ic \cdot dt)^2 = -c^2 dt^2$,
    applied to the Sphere-defining rate.*

-   *The light cone descends from the Lorentzian metric as the null
    hypersurface $\{\eta_{\mu\nu} v^\mu v^\nu = 0\}$.*

*Under Wick reparametrization, step (a) preserves physics (the Sphere
expands at rate $c$ in either parametrization); step (b) flips sign
($dx_4^2 = -c^2 dt^2 \to +c^2 d\tau^2$); step (c) collapses the null
hypersurface to the trivial solution. The Sphere is upstream; the light
cone is downstream signature-projected shadow. Physical primitives are
invariant under coordinate reparametrizations; content that vanishes
under reparametrization is coordinate-dependent bookkeeping. Wick
rotation is the operational test that distinguishes them.*
:::

##### Historical position in the physics literature {#historical-position-in-the-physics-literature .unnumbered}

::: {#rem:HistoricalPositionSpherePersistence .remark}
*Remark 38* (The individual technical facts are established; the
diagnostic synthesis is new). Each individual technical fact underlying
Theorem [35](#thm:SpherePersistenceLightConeVanishes){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SpherePersistenceLightConeVanishes"} and
Corollary [36](#cor:ThreeTierStructuralResponse){reference-type="ref"
reference="cor:ThreeTierStructuralResponse"} is traceable to a specific
standard reference:

\(1\) *Metric-signature change under Wick rotation.* Wick 1954
[@Wick1954RotationToImaginary]; standard textbook material (Glimm--Jaffe
[@GlimmJaffe-QuantumPhysics-1987]; Streater--Wightman
[@Streater-Wightman-1964]).

\(2\) *Light-cone destruction under Wick rotation.* Explicit statement
in Visser [@Visser-2017-WickRotation] on Wick-rotating generic curved
spacetime, quote: "*After Wick rotating from Minkowski space to
Euclidean space these causality constraints survive in a modified form
as 'Osterwalder--Schrader positivity' (OS positivity) of the Euclidean
version of the field theory. On the other hand, in the usual formulation
of the transition from Lorentzian signature gravity to Euclidean
signature quantum gravity the effects of the causal structure of the
Lorentzian signature theory seem to disappear completely as no analogue
of OS positivity is manifest. This circumstance is profoundly
disturbing, and suggests that something crucial is missing in the naive
analysis.*" Visser's interpretation identifies the destruction as a
defect of the naive Wick prescription requiring metric-deformation
repair. The framework's inversion: the disappearance is diagnostic
evidence for the three-tier architecture with the Sphere as the
primitive that survives.

\(3\) *Hilbert space preservation via OS reflection positivity.*
Osterwalder--Schrader [@OsterwalderSchrader1973], Theorem E and §5 of
[@OsterwalderSchrader1973]. The Hilbert space is the shared object
between Minkowski and Euclidean formulations; the two evolution
structures ($U(t)$ and $T(\tau)$) are different presentations of the
same underlying Hilbert-space content.

\(4\) *Kontsevich--Segal formal asymmetric-status framework.*
Kontsevich--Segal [@KontsevichSegal2021AllowableComplexMetrics],
extended by Witten [@Witten2021AllowableGravity] for gravity: "*We
propose a new axiom system for unitary quantum field theories on curved
space-time backgrounds, by postulating that the partition function and
the correlators extend analytically to a certain domain of
complex-valued metrics. Ordinary Riemannian metrics are contained in the
allowable domain, while Lorentzian metrics lie on its boundary.*"
Kontsevich--Segal place Lorentzian metrics on the boundary of the
allowable domain of complex metrics with Riemannian metrics in the
interior --- a formal statement of asymmetric status closest in spirit
to the framework's reading. Their motivation on the Hilbert-space side
is aligned: "*the states of a system are represented by the rays in a
complex Hilbert space $H$, and the time evolution is given by a
one-parameter group of unitary operators... Positivity of the energy
corresponds to the fact that $H$ is positive-semidefinite*"; Hilbert
space is treated as the constant substrate, the metric structure is what
varies analytically. Their interpretation is via holomorphic extension
of the partition function, not via source-and-projection from an
upstream primitive; the framework goes further by identifying the Sphere
as the primitive that neither the Lorentzian-boundary metric nor the
interior Riemannian metrics are, both being projections of it.

\(5\) *Woit's Minkowski/Euclidean chirality asymmetry.* Woit
[@Woit2023SpacetimeRightHanded], [@Woit2024Unification]: "*only the
diagonal $SU(2)$ subgroup of $\mathrm{Spin}(4)$ acts non-trivially on
Wick-rotated spacetime. The rest of the $\mathrm{Spin}(4)$ group acts
trivially on Wick-rotated spacetime and behaves like an internal
symmetry, opening up new possibilities for the unification of internal
and spacetime symmetries.*" Woit observes an asymmetric-response feature
(one $SU(2)$ becomes spacetime, the other becomes internal); the
diagnosis is chirality-based (right-handed spacetime program), distinct
from the framework's Sphere-persistence three-tier reading.

\(6\) *The synthetic three-tier response with Sphere as untouched
primitive.* The framing that Wick rotation is a live
differential-response test on candidate substrates --- the primitive
that survives (Sphere), the function-space rendering that is preserved
(Hilbert), the signature projection that decoheres (Minkowski/light
cone) --- distinguishing primitive from projection via operational Wick
response, is not stated in the literature search results.
Kontsevich--Segal is the closest orthodox precedent (Lorentzian on
boundary, Riemannian in interior), and the framework's reading extends
theirs by naming the Sphere as the primitive that both metric-signature
domains project. This appears to be new to the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework, with the caveat that the literature is vast and older or
non-English contributions may exist which the searchable results have
not surfaced.
:::

::: {#rem:PhysicalMeaningThreeTierResponse .remark}
*Remark 40* (The physical meaning of the three-tier response). The
three-tier response admits a direct physical statement. The McGucken
Sphere is a physical process --- the fourth-coordinate expansion at rate
$c$ from every event, per the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$.
Physical processes survive coordinate reparametrizations; they are what
does not depend on how we label our coordinates. The light cone is a
specific mathematical description --- the Lorentzian null hypersurface
of a specific metric convention. Specific mathematical descriptions of
physical processes depend on the parametrization chosen; they need not
survive reparametrization. Wick rotation is the operational test: the
Sphere passes (physical primitive); the light cone fails (coordinate
shadow of the primitive under a specific parametrization).

This is parallel to the Minkowski/Hilbert differential response of
Theorem [25](#thm:WickDifferentialResponse){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:WickDifferentialResponse"}: Hilbert space contains
wavefunctions, which are the algebraic image of Sphere wavefronts
(Corollary [26](#cor:WickWitnessAsymmetricLean){reference-type="ref"
reference="cor:WickWitnessAsymmetricLean"}); this image is spatial-slice
content that does not depend on how the "time" parameter is labeled ($t$
or $\tau = x_4/c$), so it survives. Minkowski Space is the
Lorentzian-signature bookkeeping of the same underlying structure; the
bookkeeping depends on the signature choice, so it decoheres under
signature flip.

The universe, on the framework's reading, has three layers under the
Wick perturbation: the physical primitive that Wick cannot touch (the
Sphere), the function-space rendering that Wick preserves (Hilbert
space), and the metric-signature projection that Wick destroys
(Minkowski Space and its light-cone causal structure). Every claim to
build fundamental physics on "Minkowski spacetime as fundamental" is
claiming as fundamental the layer that Wick rotation demonstrably
destroys; this is diagnostic evidence that the correct fundamental layer
is the Sphere, not the Lorentzian-signature bookkeeping.
:::

##### Deepening 7: Two observer perspectives on the same substrate --- Noether's theorem and Born's rule as dual empirical signatures of $dx_4/dt = ic$ {#sssec:TwoObserverPerspectives .unnumbered}

Deepenings 1--6 established the framework's reading of Wick rotation at
the mathematical level: coordinate reparametrization $\tau = x_4/c$;
differential-response diagnostic; forward/inverse asymmetry as
$\Pi_A$-projection kernel; substrate-tick $\Delta S = h$; OS reflection
positivity as inverse-Wick image of Wightman W6; Sphere persistence with
three-tier response. The present deepening supplies the
physical-interpretation content: what does the observer do in each
channel, and what does the observer empirically measure? The observer is
the same in both channels; the substrate is the same $dx_4/dt = ic$;
only the measurement context differs, and the measurement context
determines which channel description empirically applies.

::: {#thm:TwoObserverPerspectivesNoetherBorn .theorem}
**Theorem 41** (Two observer perspectives on the same substrate;
Noether/Born as dual empirical signatures). *Let an observer at event
$p$ perform measurements on the substrate $\mathcal{M}$ obeying
$dx_4/dt = ic$. Then:*

1.  **Algebraic Channel = observer-at-rest perspective.* The observer
    treats themselves as at rest with respect to the fourth coordinate
    $x_4= ict$; the substrate's $+ic$-oriented expansion appears to pass
    through them at rate $c$, carrying substrate-tick invariants
    $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$, $\lambda_C = h/(mc)$, and $\Delta S = h$
    per Compton tick
    (Theorem [29](#thm:SubstrateTickActionInvariant){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:SubstrateTickActionInvariant"}). Applying Noether's
    theorem to the substrate's symmetries produces the standard
    conservation laws as direct algebraic signatures of the
    substrate-tick invariants:*

    -   *Time-translation invariance of the substrate $\to$ energy
        conservation with $E = \hbar\omega$ (Planck 1900);*

    -   *Space-translation invariance of the substrate $\to$ momentum
        conservation with $p = h/\lambda$ (de Broglie 1924);*

    -   *Spherical-symmetry (rotation invariance) of the McGucken Sphere
        at every event $\to$ angular momentum conservation with
        $L = \hbar\ell$;*

    -   *$U(1)$ phase invariance of the Compton-clock $x_4$-winding
        $\to$ electric charge conservation.*

    *Empirical outputs of this perspective: discrete quantum spectra,
    conservation laws, unitary evolution.*

2.  **Geometric Channel = observer-surfing-wavefront perspective.* The
    observer rides the McGucken Sphere as it expands at rate $c$ from
    source events; the observer's own worldline is a substrate-tick
    chain within the Sphere-network structure, inheriting the Sphere's
    dispersion. Sphere-Recruited-Fabric coupling with ambient Sphere
    produces Brownian diffusion with coefficient
    $$D = \omega_C \bar\lambda_C^2 / 2 = (mc^2/\hbar) \cdot (\hbar/mc)^2 / 2 = \hbar/(2m),
    \label{eq:DiffusionCoefficient}$$ matching Nelson 1966 stochastic
    mechanics via independent derivation. The wavefunction
    $\psi(\mathbf{x}, t)$ is the Sphere-wavefront amplitude at spatial
    slice; the modulus-squared $|\psi(\mathbf{x}, t)|^2$ is the
    probability distribution over that slice. Empirical outputs of this
    perspective: interference patterns, wave-packet spreading
    (dispersion of probabilities), Brownian motion, quantum probability
    distributions, Born-rule statistics.*

3.  **Both perspectives are Wick-related descriptions of the same
    substrate.* By
    Theorem [22](#thm:WickAsReparametrization){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:WickAsReparametrization"} and
    Corollary [36](#cor:ThreeTierStructuralResponse){reference-type="ref"
    reference="cor:ThreeTierStructuralResponse"}, the two channels are
    related by the coordinate reparametrization $\tau = x_4/c$; both
    describe the same observer, the same substrate, and the same
    physical events; only the specific measurement context determines
    which channel description empirically applies.*

4.  **Noether's theorem and Born's rule are dual empirical signatures.*
    Every quantum measurement exhibits both simultaneously: energy is
    conserved AND the outcome is drawn from a probability distribution;
    momentum is conserved AND the wavefunction diffracts; angular
    momentum is conserved AND spin correlations are nonlocal; electric
    charge is conserved AND charged particles diffuse. The simultaneous
    validity of Noether conservation and Born probability in every
    quantum experiment is the direct empirical signature of the
    dual-channel architecture applied to the same substrate events.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof of (I).* The observer-at-rest with respect to $x_4= ict$ treats
the fourth coordinate as an external parameter passing by; the
substrate's $+ic$-oriented expansion at rate $c$ (per $dx_4/dt = ic$)
appears to the observer as a substrate flow through their location at
that rate. The observer sees substrate-tick invariants of
Theorem [29](#thm:SubstrateTickActionInvariant){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SubstrateTickActionInvariant"}: $\omega_C$, $\lambda_C$,
and $\Delta S = h$ per Compton tick, each Lorentz-invariant at the
substrate scale by
Theorem [30](#thm:HbarInvarianceIsCInvariance){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HbarInvarianceIsCInvariance"}.

Noether's theorem (1918): for every continuous symmetry of the action,
there is a conserved current. Applying to the substrate's symmetries:
(a) time-translation invariance of the substrate produces the energy
current with conserved charge $E = \hbar\omega$ (Planck's law), where
$\omega$ is the substrate-tick frequency of the measured object; (b)
space-translation invariance produces the momentum current with
conserved charge $p = h/\lambda$ (de Broglie 1924); (c) rotation
invariance of the Sphere ($SO(3)$ at each event) produces the
angular-momentum current with conserved charge $L = \hbar\ell$ where
$\ell \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ labels the $SO(3)$-representation
content; (d) $U(1)$ phase invariance of the Compton-clock $x_4$-winding
produces the electromagnetic current with conserved charge
$Q = \sum q_i$. Each conservation law is the Noether-shadow of a
substrate symmetry.

Empirical outputs: discrete spectra (energy eigenstates
$E_n = \hbar\omega_n$ from bound-state substrate-tick frequencies);
conservation laws (Noether-shadow content); unitary evolution
($U(t) = e^{-i\hat H t/\hbar}$ is the algebraic evolution of
substrate-tick phase at each event). ◻
:::

::: proof
*Proof of (II).* The observer-surfing-the-wavefront treats themselves as
a substrate-tick chain within the Sphere-network structure of §15.11.9a
of the QFT paper corpus. Each Compton tick of the observer's own
worldline couples with ambient Sphere via the Sphere-Recruited-Fabric
mechanism (past-Sphere chain-overlap of §14.5.5 of the QFT corpus). The
coupling produces Brownian diffusion with coefficient computable
directly from the substrate-tick invariants:
$D = \omega_C \bar\lambda_C^2 / 2$, where $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ is the
Compton-tick frequency and $\bar\lambda_C = \hbar/(mc)$ is the reduced
Compton wavelength (the fourth-coordinate advance per Compton tick, per
Theorem [29](#thm:SubstrateTickActionInvariant){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SubstrateTickActionInvariant"} plus the identification
$|\Delta x_4| = \lambda_C$). Direct substitution gives
[\[eq:DiffusionCoefficient\]](#eq:DiffusionCoefficient){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:DiffusionCoefficient"}:
$D = (mc^2/\hbar)(\hbar/mc)^2/2 = \hbar/(2m)$. This matches the
coefficient Nelson postulated in 1966 stochastic mechanics via
independent derivation --- Nelson found the coefficient by matching to
Schrödinger; the framework derives it from substrate-tick geometry.

The wavefunction $\psi(\mathbf{x}, t)$ in this perspective is the
Sphere-wavefront amplitude at spatial slice at parameter time $t$; the
modulus-squared $|\psi(\mathbf{x}, t)|^2$ is the probability
distribution of the observer's own substrate-tick chain over that
spatial slice, produced by the Sphere-expansion dispersion.

Empirical outputs: interference patterns (Huygens-iterated Sphere
wavefronts from source events); wave-packet spreading (dispersion of
substrate-tick chain over expanding Sphere); Brownian motion
(substrate-tick chain jitter under Sphere-Recruited-Fabric coupling);
Born-rule statistics ($|\psi|^2$ as probability density of
substrate-tick chain endpoint). ◻

::: proof
*Proof of (III).* Direct application of
Theorem [22](#thm:WickAsReparametrization){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:WickAsReparametrization"}: the Wick substitution
$t \to -i\tau$ realizes the coordinate identification $\tau = x_4/c$;
the observer-at-rest parametrization uses the real-time $t$ as its
independent variable; the observer-surfing-wavefront parametrization
uses the fourth-coordinate-scaled $\tau = x_4/c$ as its independent
variable. Both parametrize the same substrate at the same events; the
reparametrization exchanges the descriptions. ◻
:::

::: proof
*Proof of (IV).* Consider any specific quantum measurement, e.g., a
double-slit experiment with electrons. In the Algebraic Channel
(observer-at-rest) description, the observer measures conserved
quantities on the detector: total electron count is conserved
(particle-number conservation, $U(1)$ current), electron energy on
detection matches source energy (energy conservation, time-translation
Noether), electron total momentum matches source momentum (momentum
conservation, space-translation Noether). In the Geometric Channel
(observer-surfing-wavefront) description, the observer measures
