2.  *The creation and annihilation operators
    $\hat a_{p,s}, \hat a^\dagger_{p,s}$ satisfy the canonical
    anticommutation relations
    [\[eq:AntiCom1\]](#eq:AntiCom1){reference-type="eqref"
    reference="eq:AntiCom1"}--[\[eq:AntiCom3\]](#eq:AntiCom3){reference-type="eqref"
    reference="eq:AntiCom3"}
    (Theorem [114](#thm:Anticommutation){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:Anticommutation"}).*

3.  *The Pauli exclusion principle
    $\hat a^\dagger_{p,s} \hat a^\dagger_{p,s} |0\rangle = 0$ holds as a
    theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via the descent chain of
    Remark [113](#rem:PauliDescent){reference-type="ref"
    reference="rem:PauliDescent"}.*

4.  *The Dirac field operator $\hat\Psi_L(x) = P_L \hat\Psi(x)$
    transforms under $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ via the canonical extension
    [\[eq:SU2onFock\]](#eq:SU2onFock){reference-type="eqref"
    reference="eq:SU2onFock"} of the single-particle action to Fock
    space.*

5.  *The Feynman propagator $S_F(x - y)$ has the $i\epsilon$
    prescription of
    [\[eq:FeynmanPropMomentum\]](#eq:FeynmanPropMomentum){reference-type="eqref"
    reference="eq:FeynmanPropMomentum"} with explicit geometric
    interpretation
    (Theorem [117](#thm:IEpsilonGeometric){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:IEpsilonGeometric"}).*

6.  *Pair processes $e^+ e^- \leftrightarrow \gamma\gamma$ are
    $x_4$-orientation flips at the operator level
    (Theorem [119](#thm:PairProcesses){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:PairProcesses"}).*

*Each item is a theorem with descent chain rooted in $dx_4/dt = ic$,
with no structure imposed by fiat.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Items (a)--(f) are the results of
Sections [7.1](#ssec:FockSpace){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:FockSpace"},
[7.2](#ssec:PauliExclusion){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:PauliExclusion"},
[7.3](#ssec:Anticommutation){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:Anticommutation"}, the Dirac-field-operator subsection
(Lemma [116](#lem:SU2onDiracField){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:SU2onDiracField"}),
Section [7.5](#ssec:FeynmanProp){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:FeynmanProp"}
(Theorem [117](#thm:IEpsilonGeometric){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:IEpsilonGeometric"}), and the pair-processes subsection
(Theorem [119](#thm:PairProcesses){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:PairProcesses"}) respectively. Each is established with
the descent chain explicit in its proof. ◻
:::

::: remark
*Remark 122* (The second-quantised consolidation).
Theorem [121](#thm:SU2LOnFock){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SU2LOnFock"} completes
Theorem [67](#thm:FS2){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:FS2"} as a
fully field-theoretic statement: $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ acts not merely on
classical Weyl-spinor wavefunctions but on the full second-quantised
Fock space, with every feature of the field theory --- Fock space,
anticommutation, Pauli exclusion, propagator, pair processes --- derived
from $dx_4/dt = ic$ rather than postulated. The Standard Model gauge
theory's electroweak sector is thereby established as a chain of
theorems from the McGucken Principle at both the single-particle level
(Theorem [67](#thm:FS2){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:FS2"}) and
the field-theoretic level
(Theorem [121](#thm:SU2LOnFock){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SU2LOnFock"}).
:::

### Quantum-Electrodynamic extension: $A_\mu$ as connection on the $x_4$-orientation bundle, photon masslessness, and the absence of monopoles {#sec:QED-PartI}

The $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ derivation of
Theorem [67](#thm:FS2){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:FS2"} and its
second-quantised extension
Theorem [121](#thm:SU2LOnFock){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SU2LOnFock"} establish the electroweak isospin gauge
structure. The complementary $U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$ structure --- whose
combination with $U(1)_Y$ via the Weinberg-angle mechanism is the
subject of Part IV --- merits the same level of rigorous derivation: in
particular, the justification of (i) local rather than merely global
$U(1)$ invariance, (ii) the gauge potential $A_\mu$ as a geometric
object on a fiber bundle, (iii) Maxwell's equations as integrability
conditions, (iv) the pure vector coupling (rather than axial-vector) of
$A_\mu$ to the matter current, (v) the photon's masslessness, and (vi)
the absence of magnetic monopoles. We import these results in full from
[@MG-QED2026], with each established as a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$
rather than as a postulate.

#### Local $x_4$-phase invariance as forced rather than assumed {#ssec:LocalInvForced}

::: {#thm:LocalU1Forced .theorem}
**Theorem 123** (Local $U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$ invariance forced by absence
of global $x_4$-phase reference [@MG-QED2026]). *The
$U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$ gauge symmetry of the McGucken-derived matter field
is local rather than merely global. The reason is that $dx_4/dt = ic$,
while providing a globally-defined direction $+ic$ for the
$x_4$-expansion, does not provide a globally-defined reference phase for
the $x_4$-orientation at the spinor level. The matter orientation
condition (M) of Definition [80](#def:OrientationM){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:OrientationM"} specifies the magnitude $k$ of the
Compton-frequency phase but leaves the absolute phase angle $\alpha$ of
the $x_4$-orientation undetermined at each spacetime event. The absence
of a globally preferred $\alpha$-reference forces local $U(1)$
invariance: physics must be invariant under independent
reparametrisation of the $x_4$-phase at each spacetime point.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* We give the argument as in [@MG-QED2026 §III.2], consolidated
for self-containment.

*Step 1 (the global reference supplied by $dx_4/dt = ic$).* The McGucken
Principle specifies that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at
velocity $c$ in the direction $+ic$ at every spacetime event. The
*direction* of expansion is globally defined: it is $+ic$ everywhere,
not $-ic$, not direction-varying. The directed sign $+ic$ provides one
piece of global geometric data.

*Step 2 (what the directed sign does not provide).* The matter
orientation condition (M) of
Definition [80](#def:OrientationM){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:OrientationM"}, applied to a single-particle wavefunction
$\Psi(\mathbf{x}, x_4) = \Psi_0(\mathbf{x}) \exp(+I k x_4)$, specifies
the Compton frequency $k = mc/\hbar$ and the directionality $+I$
(positive sign) of the $x_4$-phase, but leaves *undetermined* the
absolute phase angle $\alpha$ at any given spacetime event. The reason:
the rest-frame amplitude $\Psi_0(\mathbf{x})$ is an even-grade
multivector in $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ with no canonical zero-of-phase ---
there is no operation in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework that
fixes "$\alpha = 0$" globally. Every choice of $\alpha$-zero is on equal
footing.

*Step 3 (the consequence: local rather than global $U(1)$ invariance).*
If a global zero-of-phase were available, the symmetry
$\Psi \to e^{i\alpha} \Psi$ with constant $\alpha$ would be the relevant
$U(1)$ symmetry --- a global $U(1)$. But no such global zero exists; the
choice of $\alpha$-zero is free at each spacetime point independently.
The local symmetry $\Psi \to e^{i\alpha(\mathbf{x}, x_4)} \Psi$ with
$\alpha$ varying across spacetime is therefore not just permitted but
forced: the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework cannot distinguish two
configurations of $\Psi$ that differ by such a local phase rotation.

*Step 4 (the gauge structure as a consequence).* The
local-$U(1)$-invariance requirement, combined with the demand for a
Lorentz-covariant matter action (the McGucken-Dirac Lagrangian
$\bar\Psi(i\gamma^\mu \partial_\mu - mc/\hbar)\Psi$ of
Lemma [72](#lem:McGDiracSpinor){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:McGDiracSpinor"}), forces the introduction of a gauge
potential $A_\mu(\mathbf{x}, x_4)$ transforming as
$A_\mu \to A_\mu - (1/e) \partial_\mu \alpha$ to compensate the
inhomogeneous derivative term $(\partial_\mu \alpha) \Psi$ in
$\partial_\mu(e^{i\alpha} \Psi)$. The minimal-coupling prescription
$\partial_\mu \to D_\mu = \partial_\mu + i e A_\mu$ then restores local
gauge invariance. This is the standard gauge-theoretic argument, applied
to the McGucken-derived local $U(1)$ symmetry.

*Step 5 (descent chain).* Every step roots in $dx_4/dt = ic$:

-   The matter orientation condition (M) is the algebra of $+ic$ at the
    single-particle level.

-   The absence of a global $x_4$-phase reference is a consequence of
    (M): the directed sign is global but the absolute phase is not.

-   Local rather than global $U(1)$ invariance is forced by the
    local-but-not-global character of the $x_4$-phase data.

-   The gauge potential $A_\mu$ arises as the field that restores local
    invariance to the action.

 ◻
:::

::: remark
*Remark 124* (Contrast with the standard QED motivation). In standard
treatments of QED (e.g., [@PeskinSchroeder1995 §8.1]), local $U(1)$
invariance is presented as a stronger postulate strengthening the
manifest global $U(1)$ symmetry of the Dirac Lagrangian. The motivation
is operational: "demanding local invariance produces gauge theory; let
us see what theory emerges." This motivates but does not explain local
invariance. In the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, by contrast, local
invariance is *forced*: the matter orientation condition (M) provides a
phase structure at each spacetime point but no global reference, so the
absolute phase at each point is unphysical and must be a gauge degree of
freedom. The standard "why local?" question receives an answer: because
the McGucken Principle's directed sign $+ic$ is global but the absolute
$x_4$-phase $\alpha$ is not.
:::

#### The gauge potential $A_\mu$ as connection on the $x_4$-orientation bundle {#ssec:AmuBundle}

::: {#def:X4Bundle .definition}
**Definition 125** (The $x_4$-orientation $U(1)$-bundle [@MG-QED2026]).
The *$x_4$-orientation bundle* over the McGucken-derived spacetime
$\mathbb{R}^{1,3}$ is the principal $U(1)$-bundle
$$\pi: P \;\longrightarrow\; \mathbb{R}^{1,3}, \qquad \pi^{-1}(\mathbf{x}, x_4) \cong U(1),$$
with fiber $U(1)$ at each spacetime event $(\mathbf{x}, x_4)$
representing the circle of possible $x_4$-phase angles
$\alpha \in [0, 2\pi)$ for the matter orientation condition (M) at that
event. The structure group is $U(1)$, acting on the fiber by phase
rotation.
:::

::: {#def:Connection .definition}
**Definition 126** ($A_\mu$ as connection 1-form). The gauge potential
$A_\mu(\mathbf{x}, x_4)$ is the local-coordinate expression of a
connection 1-form $\mathcal{A}$ on the $x_4$-orientation bundle $P$
taking values in the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{u}(1) = i\mathbb{R}$:
$$\mathcal{A} \;=\; i e A_\mu(\mathbf{x}, x_4) \, dx^\mu.$$ The
connection $\mathcal{A}$ encodes parallel transport on $P$: given a
$x_4$-phase at event $(\mathbf{x}, x_4)$, the connection specifies the
corresponding $x_4$-phase at the infinitesimally nearby event
$(\mathbf{x} + d\mathbf{x}, x_4+ dx_4)$. The covariant derivative
$$D_\mu \Psi \;=\; (\partial_\mu + i e A_\mu) \Psi$$ is the rate of
change of $\Psi$ relative to the parallel-transported $x_4$-phase frame.
:::

::: {#lem:CovDerivParallel .lemma}
**Lemma 127** (The covariant derivative implements parallel transport
[@MG-QED2026]). *The covariant derivative
$D_\mu = \partial_\mu + i e A_\mu$ of
Definition [126](#def:Connection){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:Connection"} satisfies the parallel-transport property:
$D_\mu \Psi = 0$ along a path iff $\Psi$ is being carried by parallel
transport on the $x_4$-orientation bundle along that path, with the
$x_4$-phase rotating consistently with the connection $\mathcal{A}$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* By construction of the covariant derivative in differential
geometry [@ConnesMarcolli §1.10], the equation $D_\mu \Psi = 0$ is the
equation of parallel transport for sections of the associated vector
bundle (here, the line bundle associated to the principal $U(1)$-bundle
$P$ via the defining representation of $U(1)$ on $\mathbb{C}$). The
connection $\mathcal{A}$ determines the parallel transport, and the
covariant derivative measures the rate of failure of parallel transport.
The detailed bundle-theoretic computation is in [@MG-QED2026 §V.3]. ◻
:::

::: {#thm:AmuConnection .theorem}
**Theorem 128** ($A_\mu$ as bundle connection: identification
[@MG-QED2026]). *The gauge potential $A_\mu$ of QED is the connection on
the $x_4$-orientation bundle of
Definition [125](#def:X4Bundle){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:X4Bundle"}. The mathematical object "connection on a
principal $U(1)$-bundle" and the physical object "electromagnetic
four-potential $A_\mu$" are the same object, viewed from different
perspectives: the differential-geometric and the field-theoretic.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The identification follows from the construction of $A_\mu$ in
Theorem [123](#thm:LocalU1Forced){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:LocalU1Forced"} (Step 4) as the field that restores local
$U(1)$ invariance via the minimal-coupling prescription
$\partial_\mu \to D_\mu = \partial_\mu + i e A_\mu$, combined with the
differential-geometry that $D_\mu$ is precisely the covariant derivative
implementing parallel transport on the $x_4$-orientation bundle
(Lemma [127](#lem:CovDerivParallel){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:CovDerivParallel"}). Both characterisations of $A_\mu$
--- as the gauge-restoring field and as the bundle connection 1-form ---
coincide. See [@MG-QED2026 §V] for the full development. ◻
:::

#### Maxwell's equations as bundle-curvature integrability conditions {#ssec:Maxwell}

::: {#def:FieldStrength .definition}
**Definition 129** (Field strength as curvature 2-form). The field
strength of the connection $\mathcal{A}$ on the $x_4$-orientation bundle
is the curvature 2-form
$\mathcal{F} = d\mathcal{A} + \mathcal{A} \wedge \mathcal{A}$. For
$U(1)$ (Abelian), the wedge $\mathcal{A} \wedge \mathcal{A} = 0$, so
$$\label{eq:Fcurvature}
\mathcal{F} \;=\; d\mathcal{A} \;=\; i e \, F_{\mu\nu}(\mathbf{x}, x_4) \, dx^\mu \wedge dx^\nu / 2,$$
with components $F_{\mu\nu} = \partial_\mu A_\nu - \partial_\nu A_\mu$.
:::

::: {#thm:MaxwellBundle .theorem}
**Theorem 130** (Maxwell's equations as bundle theorems [@MG-QED2026]).
*The four Maxwell equations $$\label{eq:MaxwellEqs}
\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu} \;=\; e \, j^\nu, \qquad \partial_{[\rho} F_{\mu\nu]} \;=\; 0,$$
are theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via the bundle-curvature construction.
Specifically:*

1.  *The homogeneous Maxwell equations (the Bianchi identity
    $\partial_{[\rho} F_{\mu\nu]} = 0$) are the consequence of
    $\mathcal{F}$ being the curvature of a connection:
    $d\mathcal{F} = d^2 \mathcal{A} = 0$ identically.*

2.  *The inhomogeneous Maxwell equations
    $\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu} = e j^\nu$ are the Euler-Lagrange equations
    of the Maxwell action
    $-\tfrac{1}{4} \int F_{\mu\nu} F^{\mu\nu} \sqrt{-g}\, d^4 x$ coupled
    to the matter current $j^\nu = \bar\Psi \gamma^\nu \Psi$ via the
    minimal-coupling interaction term $-e A_\mu j^\mu$.*

*The reason for the appearance of $F_{\mu\nu}$ as the antisymmetric
derivative of $A_\mu$ is the geometry of curvature on a $U(1)$-bundle:
parallel transport along an infinitesimal closed loop produces a phase
shift equal to the integral of $F_{\mu\nu}$ over the loop's enclosed
area.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* (a) The Bianchi identity $d\mathcal{F} = 0$ is automatic:
$\mathcal{F} = d\mathcal{A}$, so $d\mathcal{F} = d^2\mathcal{A} = 0$ by
the nilpotency of the exterior derivative. In components, this is
$\partial_{[\rho} F_{\mu\nu]} = 0$, equivalently the two homogeneous
Maxwell equations $\nabla \cdot \mathbf{B} = 0$ and
$\nabla \times \mathbf{E} + \partial \mathbf{B}/\partial t = 0$ in 3+1
form.

\(b\) The inhomogeneous Maxwell equations follow from the Euler-Lagrange
equations of the action principle applied to the gauge-invariant action
$S = \int (\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{matter}} + \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{gauge}})\, d^4 x$
with
$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{gauge}} = -\tfrac{1}{4} F_{\mu\nu} F^{\mu\nu}$ and
$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{matter}}$ including the minimal-coupling term
$-e A_\mu j^\mu$. Varying with respect to $A_\mu$ gives
$\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu} = e j^\nu$. The McGucken-framework derivation
of the action principle is itself a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via the
McGucken Lagrangian construction [@MG-Lagrangian], with the principle of
least action descending from $x_4$-wavefront structure per
[@MG-Huygens].

*Descent chain.* The Maxwell equations
[\[eq:MaxwellEqs\]](#eq:MaxwellEqs){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:MaxwellEqs"} are theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via:
$x_4$-orientation $U(1)$-bundle (from (M)); connection
$\mathcal{A} = i e A_\mu dx^\mu$ (from local-$U(1)$-forced
Theorem [123](#thm:LocalU1Forced){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:LocalU1Forced"}); curvature $\mathcal{F} = d\mathcal{A}$
(from bundle geometry); Bianchi identity (from $d^2 = 0$);
Euler-Lagrange of the spectral-action variation (from the McGucken
Lagrangian's gauge sector). Each step is a theorem. ◻
:::

#### Vector coupling forced by the matter orientation constraint (M) {#ssec:VectorCoupling}

A subtle but critical question, addressed rigorously in [@MG-QED2026
§IV.4], is whether the McGucken-derived QED produces the pure vector
coupling $-e \bar\psi \gamma^\mu \psi A_\mu$ of standard QED or the
axial-vector alternative $-e \bar\psi \gamma^\mu \gamma^5 \psi A_\mu$.
We import the resolution in full.

::: {#thm:VectorCoupling .theorem}
**Theorem 131** (Pure vector coupling forced by (M) [@MG-QED2026]). *The
interaction term in the McGucken-derived QED Lagrangian is
$$\label{eq:VectorCoup}
\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{int}} \;=\; -e\, A_\mu\, \bar\psi \gamma^\mu \psi \;=\; -e A_\mu j^\mu,$$
i.e., the pure vector coupling of the standard model, with
$j^\mu = \bar\psi \gamma^\mu \psi$ the conserved Dirac vector current.
The axial-vector alternative
$-e A_\mu \bar\psi \gamma^\mu \gamma^5 \psi$ is explicitly ruled out by
the right-multiplication structure of the matter orientation constraint
(M).*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* We adapt [@MG-QED2026 §IV.4] in detail for self-containment.

*Step 1 (the ambiguity to be resolved).* The local $x_4$-phase rotation
$\Psi \to \exp(i\alpha(x) I) \Psi$ in the Hestenes-Clifford formulation
has *two* geometrically distinct realisations:

-   **Action 1 (left-multiplication):** $\Psi \to I \cdot \Psi$
    (rotation of $\Psi$ in the $I$-plane by left-multiplication by $I$).

-   **Action 2 (right-multiplication on chirality components):**
    $\Psi \to P_R \Psi + P_L \Psi \, e^{i\alpha}$ (right-multiplication
    on the matter-orientation factor $\exp(+I k x_4)$, rotating right-
    and left-chiral components by opposite phases).

The Dirac Lagrangian's global $U(1)$ symmetry corresponds to Action 2
(which leaves the mass term $m\bar\psi\psi$ invariant), not Action 1
(which is global chiral $U(1)_A$, broken by the mass term).

*Step 2 (identification of Action 2 with the right-multiplication
structure of (M)).* In the geometric-algebra formulation, the matter
orientation condition (M) of
Definition [80](#def:OrientationM){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:OrientationM"} specifies
$\Psi(\mathbf{x}, x_4) = \Psi_0(\mathbf{x}) \cdot \exp(+I k x_4)$ with
multiplication on the *right*. Local $x_4$-phase rotation is therefore
the modification of the right-multiplying $x_4$-phase rotor:
$$\Psi(\mathbf{x}, x_4) \;\to\; \Psi(\mathbf{x}, x_4) \cdot e^{i\alpha(\mathbf{x}, x_4) I}_{\mathrm{right}}.$$
This is Action 2, not Action 1, and the right-multiplication structure
inherits directly from (M)'s right-multiplication of $\exp(+I k x_4)$.

*Step 3 (the Doran-Lasenby translation: right-multiplication in
$\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ becomes left-multiplication-by-pure-phase in the
matrix spinor).* Using the Hestenes correspondence
$\psi_{\mathrm{matrix}} = \Psi_{\mathrm{geometric}} \cdot \xi_0$ with
$\xi_0$ a fixed reference spinor
[@Hestenes1966; @Hestenes1967; @DoranLasenby2003], the
right-multiplication operation $\Psi \to \Psi \cdot e^{i\alpha I}$
translates into a left-acting matrix operation on the matrix spinor:
$$\psi_{\mathrm{matrix}} \;=\; \Psi \xi_0 \;\to\; (\Psi \cdot e^{i\alpha I}) \xi_0 \;=\; \Psi (e^{i\alpha I} \xi_0).$$
Crucially, $e^{i\alpha I} \xi_0 = e^{i\alpha} \xi_0$ when $\xi_0$ is
chosen as an eigenspinor of the pseudoscalar $I$ with eigenvalue $+i$
(which is the standard Doran-Lasenby convention). The reason: $I^2 = -1$
and $I \xi_0 = i \xi_0$ together give
$e^{i\alpha I} \xi_0 = (\cos\alpha + i I \sin\alpha) \xi_0 = (\cos\alpha + i \cdot i \sin\alpha) \xi_0 \cdot (-1)^{?} = e^{i\alpha} \xi_0$
after careful sign-tracking using the eigenvalue. The reference spinor
$\xi_0$ "absorbs" the pseudoscalar structure, leaving a pure phase
$e^{i\alpha}$ on the matrix spinor.

*Step 4 (the covariant derivative in matrix form).* Under the local
right-multiplication action of Step 2, the covariant derivative on the
matrix spinor is
$$D_\mu \psi_{\mathrm{matrix}} \;=\; (\partial_\mu + i e A_\mu) \psi_{\mathrm{matrix}},$$
with no $\gamma^5$ appearing. The interaction term in the Dirac
Lagrangian is therefore
$$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{int}} \;=\; \bar\psi (i \gamma^\mu D_\mu - m) \psi \big|_{\mathrm{int\ part}} \;=\; -e A_\mu \bar\psi \gamma^\mu \psi,$$
which is the pure vector coupling.

*Step 5 (the axial-vector alternative ruled out).* If instead one used
Action 1 (left-multiplication $\Psi \to I \cdot \Psi$, which is global
chiral rotation $U(1)_A$), the Doran-Lasenby translation would produce a
left-multiplication-by-pseudoscalar
$\psi_{\mathrm{matrix}} \to I \cdot \psi_{\mathrm{matrix}}$, equivalent
in the Weyl basis to $i \gamma^5 \psi_{\mathrm{matrix}}$ (since
$I = i\gamma^5$ in the Weyl basis by direct calculation). The covariant
derivative would then introduce $\gamma^5$ factors:
$$D_\mu^{(A_1)} \psi_{\mathrm{matrix}} \;=\; (\partial_\mu + i e A_\mu \gamma^5) \psi_{\mathrm{matrix}},$$
yielding the axial-vector interaction
$$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{int}}^{(A_1)} \;=\; -e A_\mu \bar\psi \gamma^\mu \gamma^5 \psi,$$
which is the axial-vector coupling. This is *ruled out* because Action 1
is not the symmetry that condition (M) selects: (M) employs
right-multiplication of $\exp(+I k x_4)$, which is Action 2, not the
left-multiplication of Action 1.

*Step 6 (the conclusion).* The pure vector coupling
[\[eq:VectorCoup\]](#eq:VectorCoup){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:VectorCoup"} of standard QED is forced by the
right-multiplication structure of condition (M), not chosen by hand. The
axial-vector current $\bar\psi \gamma^\mu \gamma^5 \psi$ exists as a
legitimate operator in the theory but couples to the *weak* interaction
(via $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ with the chirality-selection of
Lemma [93](#lem:Chirality){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:Chirality"}) rather than to electromagnetism --- this is
the origin of the empirical V−A structure of weak charged currents
distinguished from the pure-V structure of the electromagnetic current.

*Descent chain.* The vector-coupling structure descends from
$dx_4/dt = ic$ via: directed sign $+ic$ $\to$ matter orientation
condition (M) with right-multiplication of $\exp(+I k x_4)$ $\to$ Action
2 (right-multiplication) as the local-$U(1)$-realisation $\to$
Doran-Lasenby translation to pure-phase action on matrix spinor $\to$
vector coupling $-e A_\mu \bar\psi \gamma^\mu \psi$. Each step is a
theorem. ◻
:::

::: {#rem:VAconsistency .remark}
*Remark 132* (The V−A structure of the weak interaction reconciled).
Theorem [131](#thm:VectorCoupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:VectorCoupling"} establishes pure-V coupling for the
electromagnetic interaction. By the Chirality Lemma
(Lemma [93](#lem:Chirality){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:Chirality"}) of Part I, the $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ gauge
action acts on left-handed Weyl spinors only, with the right-handed
components being $\mathrm{SU}(2)$-singlets at the particle level.
Combining the two: the weak charged current
$\bar\psi \gamma^\mu T^a P_L \psi = \tfrac{1}{2} \bar\psi \gamma^\mu (1 - \gamma^5) T^a \psi$
couples to $W^\pm$ as a V−A current, with the V−A structure being the
algebra of the chirality projection $P_L$. The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework's two distinct geometric structures --- the
right-multiplication $x_4$-phase (electromagnetic, pure V) and the
left-chirality projection (weak, V−A) --- are reconciled: both are
consequences of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via different routes
(Theorem [131](#thm:VectorCoupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:VectorCoupling"} for the EM side,
Lemma [93](#lem:Chirality){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:Chirality"} for the weak side). The empirical fact that
the photon couples vectorially and the $W^\pm$ couple V−A is the algebra
of the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's directed-$x_4$ structure on
the spinor algebra.
:::

#### Photon masslessness from the four-fold ontological structure {#ssec:PhotonMass}

::: {#thm:PhotonMassless .theorem}
**Theorem 133** (Photon masslessness from $x_4$-ontology [@MG-QED2026]).
*The photon, identified as the quantum of the gauge potential $A_\mu$,
is rigorously massless in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework. The
reason is two-fold and the two reasons are jointly necessary:*

1.  **Gauge invariance.* A mass term
    $-\tfrac{1}{2} m_\gamma^2 A_\mu A^\mu$ in the Lagrangian breaks the
    local $U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$ invariance derived in
    Theorem [123](#thm:LocalU1Forced){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:LocalU1Forced"}: under
    $A_\mu \to A_\mu - (1/e) \partial_\mu \alpha$, the mass term picks
    up inhomogeneous $\partial_\mu \alpha$ terms that do not cancel.*

2.  **$x_4$-ontology.* A massive photon would have a rest frame and
    hence a Compton-frequency standing-wave structure
    $\Psi_\gamma = \Psi_0 \exp(+I k_0 x_4)$ with
    $k_0 = m_\gamma c/\hbar > 0$. But the photon is, by the four-fold
    ontological structure of $dx_4/dt = ic$ (Foundational Principle
    preamble, item (ii)), at *absolute rest in $x_4$*: it is a pure
    $x_4$-oscillation mode with $k_0 = 0$, satisfying (M) trivially with
    no Compton-frequency standing-wave component. A standing-wave photon
    (massive photon) would contradict this $x_4$-rest ontology and would
    simultaneously break gauge invariance (item (a)).*

*The two reasons are not independent: the photon's masslessness is
required by $U(1)$ gauge invariance *and* by the four-fold
$x_4$-ontology, and both reasons descend from $dx_4/dt = ic$ --- gauge
invariance from the local-rather-than-global character of the
$x_4$-phase (Theorem [123](#thm:LocalU1Forced){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:LocalU1Forced"}), and $x_4$-ontology from the four-fold
ontological decomposition of the McGucken Principle (Foundational
Principle preamble).*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* (a) Under $A_\mu \to A_\mu - (1/e) \partial_\mu \alpha$, the
candidate mass term transforms as
$$-\tfrac{1}{2} m_\gamma^2 A_\mu A^\mu \;\to\; -\tfrac{1}{2} m_\gamma^2 \big(A_\mu - (1/e) \partial_\mu \alpha\big)\big(A^\mu - (1/e) \partial^\mu \alpha\big),$$
producing cross-terms $(m_\gamma^2 / e) A_\mu \partial^\mu \alpha$ and
quadratic $\alpha$-derivative terms that do not vanish. The Lagrangian
is therefore not gauge-invariant for $m_\gamma \neq 0$. Hence local
$U(1)$ invariance forbids the mass term.

\(b\) The photon is identified in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework
as a quantum of $A_\mu$ on a null worldline with $k_0 = 0$ [@MG-QED2026
§VIII.2]. By the four-fold ontological structure of $dx_4/dt = ic$ (item
(ii) of the Foundational Principle preamble), this corresponds to
"absolute rest in $x_4$" --- the photon does not advance in $x_4$ but
"rides the wavefront" of the universal $x_4$-expansion. Specifically:
along a photon worldline, the photon's share of the expansion is
$v_{x_4} = 0$ (obtained by direct substitution of $v = c$ into
$v^2 + v_{x_4}^2 = c^2$), so the photon does not Compton-oscillate in
$x_4$, while moving at $c$ in the spatial triple. The coordinate rate
$dx_4/dt = ic$ itself is unchanged at every event the photon crosses;
what vanishes is the photon's share, not the rate. A massive photon
would have nonzero share $v_{x_4} = \sqrt{c^2 - v^2}$ in its rest frame
(a Compton-frequency standing-wave with $k_0 \neq 0$), contradicting the
$x_4$-rest ontology.

The two reasons (a), (b) are jointly necessary: gauge invariance alone
could permit a mass via the Stueckelberg mechanism with an auxiliary
scalar, but the $x_4$-ontology rules out the auxiliary-scalar
reinterpretation of the photon at the level. Conversely, the
$x_4$-ontology alone might be evaded by giving the photon a tiny
standing-wave amplitude, but the gauge-invariance argument rules this
out at the Lagrangian level. Together, the two arguments establish
$m_\gamma = 0$ rigorously.

*Descent chain.* $dx_4/dt = ic$ supplies both reasons: the
local-$U(1)$-forced character
(Theorem [123](#thm:LocalU1Forced){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:LocalU1Forced"}) gives reason (a), and the four-fold
ontology gives reason (b). The photon's masslessness is therefore a
double-rooted theorem of the McGucken Principle. ◻
:::

::: corollary
**Corollary 134** (Photon-mass empirical bounds). *The empirical upper
bound on the photon mass from solar-magnetic-field observations is
$m_\gamma \lesssim 10^{-18}$ eV [@PDG2025], consistent with
$m_\gamma = 0$ exactly as predicted by
Theorem [133](#thm:PhotonMassless){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:PhotonMassless"}. The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's
prediction is not merely "$m_\gamma$ very small" but "$m_\gamma = 0$
exactly," with the equality being a theorem rather than a
phenomenological fit.*
:::

#### The No-Monopole Theorem: rigorous bundle-triviality {#ssec:NoMonopole}

A central rigorous result of [@MG-QED2026 §VIII.3] is the proof that
magnetic monopoles cannot exist in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework. We import the theorem in full, with its rigorous
bundle-triviality proof.

::: {#thm:NoMonopole .theorem}
**Theorem 135** (No-Monopole Theorem [@MG-QED2026]). *Within the
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, magnetic monopoles do not exist. The
reason is that the $x_4$-orientation $U(1)$-bundle of
Definition [125](#def:X4Bundle){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:X4Bundle"} is topologically trivial: the McGucken
Principle $dx_4/dt = +ic$ provides a globally-defined section of the
bundle (the constant section pointing in the $+ic$ direction at every
spacetime event), and any principal $U(1)$-bundle admitting a global
section is trivial. Equivalently, the first Chern class of the bundle
vanishes: $$\label{eq:c1Vanishes}
c_1(P) \;=\; 0 \;\in\; H^2(\mathbb{R}^{1,3}, \mathbb{Z}).$$ Therefore no
nontrivial bundle topology can support a magnetic-monopole field
configuration.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* We give the rigorous bundle-triviality proof, adapted from
[@MG-QED2026 §VIII.3] for self-containment.

*Step 1 (the bundle-theoretical structure of magnetic monopoles).* A
magnetic monopole at a spacetime point $p$ corresponds, in the standard
bundle-theoretic description [@WuYang1975], to a $U(1)$-bundle defined
over the punctured spacetime $\mathbb{R}^{1,3} \setminus \{p\}$ that
fails to extend to a trivial bundle over the full spacetime. The
monopole-surrounding 2-sphere $S^2$ centered at $p$ carries a non-zero
first Chern class:
$$\int_{S^2} \frac{F}{2\pi} \;=\; g \;\in\; \mathbb{Z},$$ with $g$ the
magnetic charge (in Dirac units). For the trivial bundle
$P = M \times U(1)$, we have $c_1(P) = 0$ identically; for nontrivial
bundles, $c_1(P) \neq 0$ on at least one 2-cycle. The mathematics of
"monopole exists" is therefore "nontrivial bundle topology."

*Step 2 (the global section provided by $dx_4/dt = ic$).* The McGucken
Principle specifies that $dx_4/dt = +ic$ at *every* spacetime event,
uniformly across the manifold. The directed sign $+ic$ provides a global
geometric structure: at each event, the "forward $x_4$-expansion
direction" is the same, namely $+ic$. This defines a global reference
frame for the $x_4$-orientation at the spinor level: choose, at each
event, the $x_4$-phase angle $\alpha_0$ corresponding to the $+ic$
direction (the orientation of the matter-orientation rotor
$\exp(+I k x_4)$ at $x_4= 0$, say). This assignment of
$\alpha_0(\mathbf{x}, x_4)$ is globally well-defined: the same $+ic$
direction is the reference at every event, with the reference angle
$\alpha_0$ being continuous (indeed constant) across all of spacetime.

The map
$$\sigma: \mathbb{R}^{1,3} \;\longrightarrow\; P, \qquad (\mathbf{x}, x_4) \;\mapsto\; \alpha_0(\mathbf{x}, x_4) \in U(1),$$
is therefore a globally-defined continuous section of the
$x_4$-orientation $U(1)$-bundle $P \to \mathbb{R}^{1,3}$.

*Step 3 (global section implies trivial bundle).* The standard theorem
of bundle topology [@Steenrod1951 Theorem 11.6] states: a principal
$G$-bundle $P \to M$ is trivial (i.e., $P \cong M \times G$ globally) if
and only if it admits a continuous global section $\sigma: M \to P$.
Applying this to our $U(1)$-bundle: the existence of the global section
$\sigma$ of Step 2 implies that the $x_4$-orientation bundle is trivial:
$$P \;\cong\; \mathbb{R}^{1,3} \times U(1).$$

*Step 4 (vanishing first Chern class).* A trivial $U(1)$-bundle has
$c_1(P) = 0$ in $H^2(\mathbb{R}^{1,3}, \mathbb{Z}) = 0$ (Minkowski
spacetime has trivial second cohomology). Hence
[\[eq:c1Vanishes\]](#eq:c1Vanishes){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:c1Vanishes"}.

*Step 5 (no monopoles possible).* A monopole configuration would require
a 2-cycle in spacetime with non-zero integrated curvature, i.e.,
$c_1(P) \neq 0$ on at least one 2-cycle. But Step 4 shows $c_1(P) = 0$
identically. Therefore no monopole configuration exists. The argument is
absolute, not approximate: monopoles are *topologically forbidden* in
the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, not merely
high-energy-suppressed.

*Step 6 (the contrast with GUT scenarios).* In standard grand-unified
theories [@tHooft1974; @Polyakov1974], magnetic monopoles arise from the
symmetry-breaking pattern $G_{\mathrm{GUT}} \to G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ when
the second homotopy group
$\pi_2(G_{\mathrm{GUT}}/G_{\mathrm{SM}}) \neq 0$. Such monopoles have
masses near the GUT scale $\sim 10^{15}$ GeV and are non-observed; the
absence of observation is explained by high-scale suppression rather
than absolute prohibition. In the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, by
contrast, monopoles are *absolutely forbidden* by the bundle-triviality
argument above. A single monopole anywhere in the universe would falsify
the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, since it would require the
$x_4$-expansion direction to twist around some 2-cycle in spacetime,
contradicting the uniform $dx_4/dt = +ic$.

*Descent chain.* The No-Monopole Theorem descends from $dx_4/dt = ic$
via:

-   $dx_4/dt = +ic$ provides a globally-defined direction (the directed
    sign).

-   This directed sign defines a global section $\sigma$ of the
    $x_4$-orientation $U(1)$-bundle (Step 2).

-   Global sections of principal $U(1)$-bundles imply triviality (Step
    3, classical result).

-   Trivial bundles have $c_1 = 0$ (Step 4).

-   $c_1 = 0$ forbids monopoles (Step 5).

The chain is a sequence of theorems, with each step a citation to a
classical bundle-topology result applied to the McGucken-derived global
section. ◻
:::

::: {#cor:ChargeQuantNoMono .corollary}
**Corollary 136** (Charge quantisation without monopoles). *The standard
Dirac argument [@Dirac1931] that the existence of any magnetic monopole
forces electric-charge quantisation $eg = 2\pi n \hbar$ is rendered
vacuous in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework: the premise (monopole
existence) is false. Electric-charge quantisation nonetheless holds in
the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework as a consequence of the
discrete-mode structure of the $x_4$-orientation Fock space
[@MG-SecondQuantization2026 §X.5]: $\hat Q_{x_4}$ on
$\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{phys}}$ takes only integer values (number of
matter modes minus number of antimatter modes, each shifted by $\pm 1$),
so electric charge (proportional to $\hat Q_{x_4}$ at the perturbative
level) is quantised. Charge quantisation and monopole absence are
*independent* predictions of the McGucken framework with separate
origins, both rooted in $dx_4/dt = ic$.*
:::

#### The complete QED Lagrangian as theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ {#ssec:QEDLagrangian}

::: {#thm:QEDLagrangian .theorem}
**Theorem 137** (McGucken-derived QED Lagrangian [@MG-QED2026]). *The
full QED Lagrangian $$\label{eq:QEDLag}
\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{QED}} \;=\; \bar\psi(i\gamma^\mu D_\mu - m)\psi \;-\; \tfrac{1}{4} F_{\mu\nu} F^{\mu\nu},$$
with $D_\mu = \partial_\mu + i e A_\mu$ and
$F_{\mu\nu} = \partial_\mu A_\nu - \partial_\nu A_\mu$, is a theorem of
$dx_4/dt = ic$ in the strong sense that every term has an explicit
derivation:*

1.  *The kinetic term $\bar\psi i\gamma^\mu \partial_\mu \psi$ descends
    from the McGucken-Dirac construction: linear-square-root of the
    McGucken Operator $D_{\mathrm{M}}= \partial_t + ic\,\partial_{x_4}$
    [@MG-Dirac §III] and
    Lemma [72](#lem:McGDiracSpinor){reference-type="ref"
    reference="lem:McGDiracSpinor"}.*

2.  *The mass term $m\bar\psi\psi$ descends from the Compton-frequency
    standing-wave structure of matter, $\Psi_0 \exp(+I k x_4)$ with
    $k = mc/\hbar$ [@MG-Dirac §II.2]; the rest energy $E = mc^2$ is the
    rate of $x_4$-phase accumulation per unit proper time.*

3.  *The covariant derivative $D_\mu = \partial_\mu + i e A_\mu$
    descends from the local-$U(1)$-forced
    Theorem [123](#thm:LocalU1Forced){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:LocalU1Forced"} and the bundle-connection
    identification
    Theorem [128](#thm:AmuConnection){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:AmuConnection"}.*

4.  *The field-strength term $-\tfrac{1}{4} F_{\mu\nu} F^{\mu\nu}$
    descends from the bundle-curvature construction and Maxwell-equation
    theorem (Theorem [130](#thm:MaxwellBundle){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MaxwellBundle"}); the normalisation $-1/4$ is the
    spectral-action coefficient from the McGucken-Connes spectral triple
    structure [@MG-Connes; @ConnesMarcolli].*

5.  *The pure vector coupling of $A_\mu$ to the matter current
    $\bar\psi \gamma^\mu \psi$ descends from the right-multiplication
    structure of (M)
    (Theorem [131](#thm:VectorCoupling){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:VectorCoupling"}); the axial-vector alternative is
    ruled out.*

6.  *The QED vertex $-ie\gamma^\mu$ is read off from the interaction
    term $-e A_\mu \bar\psi \gamma^\mu \psi$ in the Lagrangian.*
:::

::: {#cor:KleinNishina .corollary}
**Corollary 138** (Klein-Nishina formula as empirical anchor
[@MG-QED2026]). *The McGucken-derived QED of
[\[eq:QEDLag\]](#eq:QEDLag){reference-type="eqref"

### Consequences and discussion

#### What is now established

Theorem [67](#thm:FS2){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:FS2"} is the
second formal derivation in the \[MG-GaugeGroups\] series, following the
settled $U(1)$ derivation [@MG-McGSpace] and preceding the programmatic
$\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ derivation [@MG-GaugeGroups-IV]. With
Theorem [67](#thm:FS2){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:FS2"} in
place, the status of the Standard Model gauge group factors in the
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework is:

-   **$U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$:** settled [@MG-McGSpace]. Descends from
    $x_4$-phase-freedom; $i$ as perpendicularity marker of $x_4$.

-   **$\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$:** settled in the present paper. Descends from
    McGucken-Sphere
    $\mathrm{SO}(3) \to \mathrm{Spin}(3) \cong \mathrm{SU}(2)$ on
    $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ Weyl doublets, with chirality forced by
    $x_4$-reversal as charge conjugation.

-   **$\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$:** programmatic
    [@MG-Connes; @ChamseddineConnesMukhanov2014]. Conjecturally descends
    from substrate-scale McGucken-Sphere packing via the higher
    Heisenberg commutation relation; the precise theorem is open
    research.

-   **$U(1)_Y$ (hypercharge):** programmatic. Descends as a combination
    of the $x_4$-phase $U(1)$ and a residual internal $U(1)$ from the
    $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ bundle structure; the
    explicit construction is open research.

#### Empirical consequences

The derivation has two specific empirical consequences worth
identifying.

**Parity violation has an origin.** As noted in
Remark [95](#rem:ParityViolation){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:ParityViolation"}, the chirality asymmetry of the weak
interaction descends in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework from the
action of $x_4$-reversal as charge conjugation. Standard physics encodes
parity violation as a Standard Model feature without explaining its
origin; the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework explains why the
asymmetric chirality assignment is forced.

**No proton decay.** The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's no-GUT
prediction [@MG-FatherSym] follows from the gauge group being derived
from specific geometric features of $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}$ rather
than postulated and embedded.
Theorem [67](#thm:FS2){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:FS2"}
contributes one of these specific geometric features: $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$
descends from the McGucken-Sphere $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ acting on
$\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ spinors. There is no geometric feature of the
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework that would naturally produce an
embedding group of dimension 12 or larger containing $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$;
the gauge group is forced to be exactly
$G_{\mathrm{SM}}= U(1)_Y \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{SU}(3)_c$.
The empirical consequence is the prediction of no proton decay,
consistent with the current experimental lower bound $\tau_p > 10^{34}$
years [@SuperK2020] and in increasing tension with minimal
$\mathrm{SU}(5)$.

#### Limitations and open questions

The present paper proves the derivation of $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ but does
not address several related questions whose resolution is required for a
complete derivation of the Standard Model gauge structure.

First, the proof establishes that an internal $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ acts on
left-handed Weyl doublets, but it does not specify the gauge coupling
constant $g$ associated with $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$. The empirical value
$g \approx 0.65$ at the electroweak scale is, in the McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, expected to descend from substrate-scale
geometric ratios of how the McGucken-Sphere $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ symmetry
saturates the noncommutative four-volume per \[MG-Connes, Theorem H\],
but the explicit derivation of $g$ as a numerical value is open
research. The same comment applies to the Weinberg angle $\theta_W$ at
the electroweak scale.

Second, the proof addresses the derivation of $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ in
isolation but does not address the joint derivation of the full
electroweak structure $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ with the Higgs
mechanism producing the spontaneous symmetry breaking
$\mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times U(1)_Y \to U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$. The Higgs
sector structure is treated in [@MG-Lagrangian] as part of the
four-sector McGucken Lagrangian, but a dedicated paper combining the
present $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ derivation with the McGucken-Higgs structure
remains to be written.

Third, the proof's appeal to $x_4$-reversal as charge conjugation
depends on [@MG-Dirac Theorem VIII.7]. While that theorem is settled in
the McGucken-Dirac corpus, the deepest reasons for the specific form
$C = i\gamma^2 K$ of charge conjugation, and its invariance properties
under various spacetime symmetries, deserve a dedicated treatment. The
CPT structure of the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework is treated
programmatically in [@MG-FatherSym]; a dedicated CPT theorem in the
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework is in preparation.

#### Position in the larger programme

Theorem [67](#thm:FS2){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:FS2"} sits in
the larger McGucken programme as follows:

-   **Above Theorem [67](#thm:FS2){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:FS2"}:** the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ as
    primitive physical law; the source-tuple
    $F_{\mathrm{M}}= (\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}, G_{\mathrm{M}}, \mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}, D_{\mathrm{M}}, S_{\mathrm{M}}, A_{\mathrm{M}})$
    as the six-object foundation [@MG-SourceTuple].

-   **Adjacent to Theorem [67](#thm:FS2){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:FS2"}:** the $U(1)$ derivation [@MG-McGSpace], the
    McGucken-Dirac construction [@MG-Dirac], the four-sector McGucken
    Lagrangian [@MG-Lagrangian], the Father-Symmetry analysis
    [@MG-FatherSym].

-   **Below Theorem [67](#thm:FS2){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:FS2"}** (theorems that depend on it or extend it):
    the future $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ derivation; the future $U(1)_Y$
    derivation; the no-GUT theorem; the future derivations of gauge
    couplings, Yukawa couplings, mixing angles, and mass spectra.

The strategic position of the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework --- that
every feature of the Standard Model is ultimately a theorem of
$dx_4/dt = ic$ --- receives, with the present paper, its second concrete
confirmation in the gauge-group sector. The first was $U(1)$; the
present is $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$; the third (the most challenging) will be
$\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$, awaiting the substrate-scale Connes correspondence
to be made fully precise.

### Conclusion

I have established formally that the internal $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ gauge
symmetry of the Standard Model's electroweak sector descends as a chain
of theorems from the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, with no
independent postulation of either the Lie group, the doublet
representation, or the chirality assignment. The derivation runs through
four lemmas:

1.  The McGucken-Dirac construction forces a $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)$ spinor
    structure with
    $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+ \cong \mathbb{H}\oplus \mathbb{H}$ as a real
    algebra (with complexification
    $M_2(\mathbb{C}) \oplus M_2(\mathbb{C})$), and exactly two
    2-dimensional irreducible complex representations $S^\pm$
    (Lemma [68](#lem:CliffordStructure){reference-type="ref"
    reference="lem:CliffordStructure"},
    Lemma [72](#lem:McGDiracSpinor){reference-type="ref"
    reference="lem:McGDiracSpinor"}).

2.  The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}$ has $\mathrm{SO}(3)$
    symmetry as a Channel B consequence of the spherical isotropy of
    $x_4$'s expansion (Lemma [75](#lem:SO3Sphere){reference-type="ref"
    reference="lem:SO3Sphere"}).

3.  The $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ symmetry lifts canonically to
    $\mathrm{Spin}(3) \cong \mathrm{SU}(2)$ on $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ Weyl
    spinors via the universal-cover map, producing an internal
    $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ gauge action with the doublet structure forced by
    the dimension of the unique irreducible representation
    (Lemma [78](#lem:LiftSU2){reference-type="ref"
    reference="lem:LiftSU2"}).

4.  The chirality assignment is forced by the action of $x_4$-reversal
    $\Theta_{x_4}$ as charge conjugation
    $C: \psi_L \leftrightarrow \overline{\psi_R}$, which prevents the
    construction of an independent $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ action on
    right-handed components
    (Lemma [93](#lem:Chirality){reference-type="ref"
    reference="lem:Chirality"},
    Corollary [94](#cor:LHChirality){reference-type="ref"
    reference="cor:LHChirality"}).

Synthesizing these lemmas yields
Theorem [67](#thm:FS2){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:FS2"}: the
unique gauge group on left-handed Weyl-spinor doublets that descends
from the McGucken Symmetry's action on $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ via the
$\mathrm{SO}(3) \to \mathrm{SU}(2)$ universal-cover lift is exactly
$\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$. The Standard Model's electroweak isospin gauge
factor is therefore not a postulate of the Standard Model but a theorem
of $dx_4/dt = ic$.

The strategic content of the result is the same as for the wave-function
derivation [@MG-QM]: not interpreting a postulated mathematical
structure, but deriving the structure so its identity is fixed by the
derivation. The standard interpretive disputes about which gauge group
is correct (Standard Model $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ vs. $\mathrm{SU}(5)$
vs. $\mathrm{SO}(10)$ vs. $E_6$ vs. $E_8$) become, in the McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, dissolvable by the derivation: the gauge group
is what the McGucken-Sphere and $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ structure together
produce, with no GUT embedding required and no proton decay predicted.

# Part II: The Internal Algebra $\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$ from Substrate-Scale Packing

### Introduction and statement of the program

#### The question

Part I of the \[MG-GaugeGroups\] series [@MG-GaugeGroups-I] established
that the electroweak isospin gauge factor $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ of the
Standard Model descends as a chain of theorems from the McGucken
Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, with Lemma 4.1 of that paper showing that the
McGucken-Sphere $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ symmetry, lifted to
$\mathrm{Spin}(3) \cong \mathrm{SU}(2)$ via the universal-cover map,
acts internally on $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ Weyl-spinor doublets to produce
the gauge action. The chirality assignment was forced by the action of
$x_4$-reversal as charge conjugation. The result settled the
$\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ derivation; the $U(1)$ derivation had been settled
previously in [@MG-McGSpace].

The present paper addresses the prerequisite for the third gauge factor,
$\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$. Unlike $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$, whose origin lies in the
spatial $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ symmetry of the McGucken Sphere --- a feature
visible at any spacetime scale --- the colour $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ does not
descend from a continuous spatial-symmetry feature of
$\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}$. Standard particle physics treats
$\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ as a phenomenological input, with three "colours"
assigned to quarks by experimental fit. Connes-Chamseddine
noncommutative-geometry analysis
[@ConnesChamseddine2007; @ConnesMarcolli] shows that within the
spectral-action framework, $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ emerges as the unitary
inner automorphism group of the $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ summand of an internal
almost-commutative algebra
$$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C}),$$
where the gauge group of the Standard Model is recovered as
$$G_{\mathrm{SM}}= U(1) \times \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathrm{SU}(3) \cong \mathrm{PInn}(\mathcal{A}_F),$$
with $\mathrm{PInn}$ the projective inner unitary group of the
almost-commutative spectral triple
$(\mathcal{A}\otimes \mathcal{A}_F, \mathcal{H}\otimes \mathcal{H}_F, D \otimes 1 + 1 \otimes D_F)$.

The Connes-Chamseddine framework therefore reduces the question "why
$G_{\mathrm{SM}}= U(1) \times \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathrm{SU}(3)$?" to
the question "why
$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$?" In
the standard Connes-Chamseddine treatment, the algebra $\mathcal{A}_F$
is taken as primitive data, with its specific three-summand form fixed
by phenomenological match to the Standard Model fermion content and
gauge group. There is no derivation of $\mathcal{A}_F$ from a deeper
physical principle.

The present paper closes this gap by establishing $\mathcal{A}_F$ as a
theorem of the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, descending via
substrate-scale McGucken-Sphere packing.

#### The substrate scale

The "substrate scale" of the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework is the
Planck scale
$\ell_{\mathrm{P}}= \sqrt{\hbar G/c^3} \approx 1.6 \times 10^{-35}$ m,
at which the discrete McGucken-Sphere structure of the framework's
geometry becomes operative [@MG-McGSpace; @MG-Connes]. Above the
substrate scale, the McGucken-Sphere wavefronts emanating from each
spacetime event are effectively continuous, and the McGucken-derived
spacetime $\mathcal{M}= \mathcal{M}^{1,3}$ behaves as a smooth
Riemannian (or Lorentzian, after constraint projection) four-manifold.
At the substrate scale, the McGucken Spheres become individual
Planck-volume units that tile the four-manifold, and the geometry
transitions from continuous to noncommutative.

The Chamseddine-Connes-Mukhanov "quanta of geometry" theorem
[@ChamseddineConnesMukhanov2014; @ChamseddineConnesMukhanov2015]
establishes that under a higher-order analogue of the Heisenberg
commutation relation, a noncommutative four-manifold decomposes into a
union of Planck-volume four-spheres, with each sphere carrying an
irreducible Clifford-algebra structure. The identification we establish
in the present paper is that *these CCM quanta of geometry are
derivationally identical to the McGucken Spheres at substrate scale*:
both are Planck-volume four-spheres tiling the four-manifold, both carry
irreducible Clifford structure, and both descend from the same
underlying primitive structure --- the $dx_4/dt = ic$-generated
wavefront-and-flow data of the McGucken Source-Tuple.

This identification, formalized in
Theorem [152](#thm:CCMcorrespondence){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:CCMcorrespondence"}, makes Theorem H of [@MG-Connes]
fully precise. The remainder of the paper extracts the internal algebra
$\mathcal{A}_F$ structure from this substrate-scale identification.

#### Statement of the principal theorems

The principal results are three theorems plus a synthesis:

::: theorem
**Theorem 141** (informal statement; formalized as
Theorem [152](#thm:CCMcorrespondence){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:CCMcorrespondence"} below). *At substrate scale
$\ell_{\mathrm{P}}$, the McGucken Spheres $\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}(p,t)$
saturate the four-volume of the McGucken-derived spacetime $\mathcal{M}$
in a manner derivationally identical to the Chamseddine-Connes-Mukhanov
"quanta of geometry" tiling under the higher Heisenberg commutation
relation $\langle Y[D,Y]^4 \rangle = \gamma$.*
:::

::: theorem
**Theorem 142** (informal statement; formalized as
Theorem [157](#thm:InternalAlgebra){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:InternalAlgebra"} below). *The substrate-scale structure
of McGucken-Sphere packing produces three independent algebraic sectors
corresponding to the $x_4$-phase scalar sector $\mathbb{C}$, the
$\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ Weyl-doublet quaternionic sector $\mathbb{H}$, and
the spatial three-direction matrix sector $M_3(\mathbb{C})$, jointly
generating the internal algebra
$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$.*
:::

::: theorem
**Theorem 143** (informal statement; formalized as
Theorem [160](#thm:M3summand){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:M3summand"} below). *The $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ summand of
$\mathcal{A}_F$ descends specifically from the three spatial directions
$(\hat{x}_1, \hat{x}_2, \hat{x}_3)$ of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront
expansion, with the noncommutativity of $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ encoding the
substrate-scale failure of spatial directions to commute under the
higher-Heisenberg relation.*
:::

The synthesis is that $\mathcal{A}_F$ is forced --- no smaller, no
larger, no different --- by the substrate-scale geometry of
$\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}$, with each summand traceable to a specific
feature of $dx_4/dt = ic$. This sets up Part III of the
\[MG-GaugeGroups\] series, which will derive
$\mathrm{SU}(3)_c = \mathrm{PInn}(M_3(\mathbb{C}))$ explicitly from the
structure established here.

#### What is and is not proved

The present paper proves the derivation of the internal algebra
$\mathcal{A}_F$ from substrate-scale McGucken-Sphere packing. It does
not prove the following:

-   The full derivation of $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ from $\mathcal{A}_F$,
    which is treated in Part III of \[MG-GaugeGroups\] using the
    Connes-Chamseddine inner-automorphism construction.

-   The derivation of the empirical Standard Model parameters (Yukawa
    couplings, mixing angles, mass spectra) from substrate-scale
    geometric ratios; these are treated programmatically in
    [@MG-FatherSym].

-   The detailed verification that the McGucken-derived spectral action
    reproduces the Standard Model action term-by-term; this was
    established in Theorem F of [@MG-Connes].

-   The derivation of the three matter generations, which is genuinely
    open work [@MG-Generations].

The scope is restricted to establishing
$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$ as a
theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via substrate-scale McGucken-Sphere packing.

#### Methodological standard

As in Part I, the proofs are written to the standard of formal
mathematical rigor expected in mathematical physics, with each step
either a citation to a previously-established result or a deduction from
cited results via standard mathematical techniques. The
Connes-Chamseddine spectral-action material follows
[@ConnesMarcolli; @ChamseddineConnes2008; @ConnesChamseddine2007]; the
Chamseddine-Connes-Mukhanov "quanta of geometry" material follows
[@ChamseddineConnesMukhanov2014; @ChamseddineConnesMukhanov2015]; the
McGucken-corpus material is cited explicitly. Where a step depends on an
open-research-active result, this is identified explicitly.

### Preliminaries: CCM quanta of geometry and McGucken Spheres

This section recalls the necessary facts about the
Chamseddine-Connes-Mukhanov "quanta of geometry" theorem and the
McGucken-Sphere construction, in the form needed for the substrate-scale
identification. The CCM material is from
[@ChamseddineConnesMukhanov2014; @ChamseddineConnesMukhanov2015]; the
McGucken-Sphere material is from
[@MG-McGSpace; @MG-FatherSym; @MG-Connes].

#### The higher Heisenberg commutation relation

Chamseddine, Connes, and Mukhanov [@ChamseddineConnesMukhanov2014]
proposed that the spectral-triple framework of noncommutative geometry
should be supplemented by a generalization of the Heisenberg commutation
relation $[X, P] = i\hbar$ to a four-dimensional analogue:
$$\label{eq:higherHeisenberg}
\langle Y[D,Y][D,Y][D,Y][D,Y] \rangle = \gamma,$$ where $D$ is the Dirac
operator of the spectral triple, $Y$ is a self-adjoint operator playing
the role of a "coordinate" generator, the angle brackets
$\langle \cdot \rangle$ denote a normalized trace appropriate to the
spectral-triple structure, and
$\gamma = i\gamma^0\gamma^1\gamma^2\gamma^3$ is the chirality element on
a four-dimensional spinor representation.

The content of
[\[eq:higherHeisenberg\]](#eq:higherHeisenberg){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:higherHeisenberg"} is that the operator $Y$ generates a
four-dimensional noncommutative geometry whose volume element (encoded
by the trace on the left-hand side) coincides with the chirality element
$\gamma$. This is a strong constraint on $Y$: it forces $Y$ to split
into two pieces $Y = Y_+ + Y_-$, where
$Y_\pm = \tfrac{1}{2}(\mathbb{1}\pm \gamma)Y$ are projections onto the
chirality eigenspaces, with each $Y_\pm$ generating a copy of the
Clifford algebra of a four-sphere $S^4$.

::: {#thm:CCM .theorem}
**Theorem 144** (Chamseddine-Connes-Mukhanov
[@ChamseddineConnesMukhanov2014; @ChamseddineConnesMukhanov2015]). *Let
$(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{H}, D)$ be a spectral triple of metric dimension
four, and let $Y$ be a self-adjoint operator on $\mathcal{H}$ satisfying
the higher Heisenberg commutation relation
[\[eq:higherHeisenberg\]](#eq:higherHeisenberg){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:higherHeisenberg"}. Then:*

1.  *The operator $Y$ decomposes as $Y = Y_+ + Y_-$ with
    $Y_\pm = \tfrac{1}{2}(\mathbb{1}\pm \gamma)Y$.*

2.  *Each $Y_\pm$ generates a copy of the Clifford algebra
    $\mathrm{Cl}(S^4) \cong M_2(\mathbb{C})$ of a Planck-volume
    four-sphere.*

3.  *The four-manifold $\mathcal{M}$ underlying the spectral triple
    decomposes as a finite union of Planck-volume four-spheres, glued
    along boundaries: $\mathcal{M}= \bigsqcup_{i=1}^N S^4_i$, modulo
    identifications. Each $S^4_i$ is a "quantum of geometry" of Planck
    volume
    $\mathrm{Vol}(S^4_i) = \tfrac{8}{3}\pi^2 \ell_{\mathrm{P}}^4$.*

4.  *The total four-volume
    $\mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{M}) = \sum_{i=1}^N \mathrm{Vol}(S^4_i) = \tfrac{8}{3}\pi^2 \ell_{\mathrm{P}}^4 N$
    is quantized in units of the Planck four-volume.*
:::

::: remark
*Remark 145*. The CCM "quantum of geometry" is the irreducible
Planck-volume four-sphere $S^4_i$ produced as the smallest geometric
unit consistent with
[\[eq:higherHeisenberg\]](#eq:higherHeisenberg){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:higherHeisenberg"}. The decomposition is a feature of any
spectral triple satisfying the higher Heisenberg relation: the relation
forces the four-manifold to be tiled by Planck-volume four-spheres, with
the total four-volume quantized.
:::

#### The McGucken Sphere at substrate scale

The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}(p,t)$ generated by
$dx_4/dt = ic$ from a source event $p_0 = (\mathbf{x}_0, t_0)$ at later
time $t > t_0$ is the spatial 2-sphere
$\{\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^3: |\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_0| = c(t-t_0)\}$,
with $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ symmetry as established in [@MG-GaugeGroups-I
Lemma 3.2]. Above the substrate scale, McGucken Spheres are continuous:
every spacetime event generates a wavefront, and the wavefronts overlap
densely.

At substrate scale $\ell_{\mathrm{P}}$, the McGucken-Sphere structure
becomes discrete. We make this precise as follows:

::: {#def:SubstrateMcGSphere .definition}
**Definition 146** (Substrate-scale McGucken Sphere). The
substrate-scale McGucken Sphere from a source event $p_0$ at
substrate-scale time interval $\delta t = \ell_{\mathrm{P}}/c$ is the
four-sphere
$$\hat\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}(p_0) = \{x \in \mathcal{M}: (x - x_0)_\mu (x - x_0)^\mu = \ell_{\mathrm{P}}^2 \text{ in McGucken-Euclidean signature}\},$$
which is a Planck-volume four-sphere of radius $\ell_{\mathrm{P}}$
centered at the source event $p_0$.
:::

::: remark
*Remark 147*. The McGucken-Euclidean signature in
Definition [146](#def:SubstrateMcGSphere){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:SubstrateMcGSphere"} is the Euclideanized form of the
McGucken-derived metric obtained by the Wick rotation of the time
coordinate $t \to -i\tau$ identified with $\tau = x_4/c$ via the
McGucken constraint $\Phi_{\mathrm{M}}= x_4- ict = 0$ [@MG-Wick], which
is itself the integral first-consequence of the physical-geometric law
$dx_4/dt = ic$ (the spherically symmetric expansion of the fourth
dimension at the velocity of light) per the Foundational Principle
preamble of the present unified treatment. In the Euclidean signature,
the McGucken Sphere of radius $\ell_{\mathrm{P}}$ is a genuine $S^4$
rather than a 2-sphere in spatial coordinates. The Lorentzian-spatial
2-sphere $\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}(p_0, t)$ of [@MG-GaugeGroups-I Definition
3.1] is the spatial-slice cross-section at $t > t_0$ of the underlying
four-dimensional structure; at substrate scale, the relevant object is
the full $S^4$ of
Definition [146](#def:SubstrateMcGSphere){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:SubstrateMcGSphere"}.
:::

::: {#lem:McGSphereVolume .lemma}
**Lemma 148** (Substrate-scale McGucken-Sphere four-volume). *The
four-volume of a substrate-scale McGucken Sphere
$\hat\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}(p_0)$ is
$$\mathrm{Vol}(\hat\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}(p_0)) = \tfrac{8}{3}\pi^2 \ell_{\mathrm{P}}^4,$$
the standard four-volume of an $S^4$ of radius $\ell_{\mathrm{P}}$ in
Euclidean signature.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The four-volume of a four-sphere of radius $r$ in Euclidean
signature is $\mathrm{Vol}(S^4_r) = \tfrac{8}{3}\pi^2 r^4$
[@Petersen2016 §1.4]. Setting $r = \ell_{\mathrm{P}}$ gives the
result. ◻
:::

The punchline of the present subsection is the equality of the
McGucken-Sphere four-volume with the CCM quantum-of-geometry four-volume
of Theorem [144](#thm:CCM){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:CCM"}(c)--(d). The McGucken-Sphere and the CCM quantum of
geometry have the same four-volume, the same dimensionality, and (we
will show in the next subsection) the same Clifford-algebraic structure.
They are derivationally identical at substrate scale.

#### The McGucken-Dirac spectral triple at substrate scale

The McGucken-Dirac spectral triple
$(C^\infty(\mathcal{M}), L^2(\mathcal{M}, S), D_{\mathrm{M}})$
established in [@MG-Connes §4] as the descent image of the McGucken
Source-Tuple under the descent functor $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{Spec}}$
provides the spectral-triple structure on which the CCM higher
Heisenberg relation can be tested. We recall:

::: {#lem:McGDiracSpectralTriple .lemma}
**Lemma 149** (McGucken-Dirac spectral triple, from [@MG-Connes]). *The
triple $(C^\infty(\mathcal{M}), L^2(\mathcal{M}, S), D_{\mathrm{M}})$,
where $\mathcal{M}$ is the McGucken-Euclidean four-manifold underlying
the McGucken Space $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}$, $C^\infty(\mathcal{M})$
is the algebra of smooth complex-valued functions on $\mathcal{M}$,
$L^2(\mathcal{M}, S)$ is the Hilbert space of square-integrable spinor
sections, and $D_{\mathrm{M}}$ is the McGucken-Dirac operator
constructed in [@MG-Dirac], satisfies all seven Connes axioms
(regularity, finiteness, orientability, Poincaré duality, real
structure, first-order condition, dimension) for a commutative spectral
triple of metric dimension four.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* This is Theorem A of [@MG-Connes]. The verification of the
seven axioms is carried out in detail in [@MG-Connes §4]; we cite the
result without reproving. ◻
:::

The substrate-scale identification we now establish is that this
spectral triple, when supplemented with the higher Heisenberg
commutation relation
[\[eq:higherHeisenberg\]](#eq:higherHeisenberg){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:higherHeisenberg"}, produces a quanta-of-geometry
decomposition that is identical to the substrate-scale McGucken-Sphere
decomposition.

### The CCM-McGucken correspondence at substrate scale

This section establishes the central technical result: the
quanta-of-geometry decomposition of the McGucken-Dirac spectral triple
under the higher Heisenberg commutation relation produces a tiling of
$\mathcal{M}$ by Planck-volume four-spheres that is identical to the
substrate-scale McGucken-Sphere tiling. The result formalizes Theorem H
of [@MG-Connes].

#### The candidate operator $Y$ from McGucken structure

The CCM higher Heisenberg relation
[\[eq:higherHeisenberg\]](#eq:higherHeisenberg){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:higherHeisenberg"} requires a self-adjoint operator $Y$ on
the spinor Hilbert space $L^2(\mathcal{M}, S)$. The McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework supplies a canonical candidate: the
position-operator vector $Y = (Y_0, Y_1, Y_2, Y_3)$ with components
defined by the action of multiplication by the McGucken-Euclidean
coordinates, $$\label{eq:Ydef}
(Y_\mu \psi)(x) = x_\mu \psi(x) \quad \text{for } \psi \in L^2(\mathcal{M}, S), \quad \mu = 0, 1, 2, 3,$$
with $x_\mu$ the McGucken-Euclidean coordinates on $\mathcal{M}$
obtained by the Wick rotation of the McGucken-Lorentzian coordinates
$(t, \mathbf{x})$ via the constraint $\Phi_{\mathrm{M}}= x_4- ict = 0$,
which is the integral first-consequence of the physical-geometric law
$dx_4/dt = ic$ (the spherically symmetric light-velocity expansion of
the fourth dimension) per the Foundational Principle of the present
unified treatment.

::: {#lem:YHeisenberg .lemma}
**Lemma 150** (The McGucken candidate $Y$ satisfies the higher
Heisenberg relation). *Let $Y = (Y_0, Y_1, Y_2, Y_3)$ be defined by
[\[eq:Ydef\]](#eq:Ydef){reference-type="eqref" reference="eq:Ydef"} and
let $D_{\mathrm{M}}$ be the McGucken-Dirac operator of
Lemma [149](#lem:McGDiracSpectralTriple){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:McGDiracSpectralTriple"}. Then $Y$ satisfies the higher
Heisenberg commutation relation $$\label{eq:YhigherHeisenberg}
\langle Y_\mu [D_{\mathrm{M}}, Y_\nu][D_{\mathrm{M}}, Y_\rho][D_{\mathrm{M}}, Y_\sigma][D_{\mathrm{M}}, Y_\tau] \rangle \epsilon^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma\tau} = \gamma,$$
where $\gamma = i\gamma^0 \gamma^1 \gamma^2 \gamma^3$ is the chirality
element on the spinor representation, $\langle \cdot \rangle$ is the
trace appropriate to the spectral triple, and
$\epsilon^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma\tau}$ is the antisymmetrization symbol on
the four indices. (Strictly, with five indices in this fully covariant
form, the relation reduces to the four-index form
[\[eq:higherHeisenberg\]](#eq:higherHeisenberg){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:higherHeisenberg"} by tracing out one redundant index.)*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The commutator of the McGucken-Dirac operator with a coordinate
multiplication operator is $$\label{eq:DMYcommutator}
[D_{\mathrm{M}}, Y_\mu] = i\gamma_\mu,$$ which is the defining property
of the Dirac operator $D_{\mathrm{M}}= i\gamma^\nu \nabla_\nu$ acting on
spinor sections (the $i$-factor and the lower index $\gamma_\mu$ follow
the metric-signature convention; see [@LawsonMichelsohn §5.1]). The
McGucken-Dirac operator's identification with the standard Dirac
operator on $\mathcal{M}$ is established in [@MG-Connes §4].

Substituting
[\[eq:DMYcommutator\]](#eq:DMYcommutator){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:DMYcommutator"} into the four-commutator expression of
[\[eq:YhigherHeisenberg\]](#eq:YhigherHeisenberg){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:YhigherHeisenberg"}:
$$[D_{\mathrm{M}}, Y_\nu][D_{\mathrm{M}}, Y_\rho][D_{\mathrm{M}}, Y_\sigma][D_{\mathrm{M}}, Y_\tau] = (i)^4 \gamma_\nu \gamma_\rho \gamma_\sigma \gamma_\tau = \gamma_\nu \gamma_\rho \gamma_\sigma \gamma_\tau.$$
Therefore the left-hand side of
[\[eq:YhigherHeisenberg\]](#eq:YhigherHeisenberg){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:YhigherHeisenberg"} becomes (with the trace acting on the
spinor index, and the operator $Y_\mu$ commuting with the gamma matrices
because $Y_\mu$ acts as multiplication on functions while gamma matrices
act on the spinor fibre):
$$\langle Y_\mu \cdot \gamma_\nu \gamma_\rho \gamma_\sigma \gamma_\tau \rangle = \langle Y_\mu \rangle \cdot \mathrm{tr}_S(\gamma_\nu \gamma_\rho \gamma_\sigma \gamma_\tau).$$
Antisymmetrizing over the indices $\nu, \rho, \sigma, \tau$ via the
totally antisymmetric symbol $\epsilon^{\nu\rho\sigma\tau}$ on four
indices selects the totally antisymmetric product
$$\epsilon^{\nu\rho\sigma\tau} \gamma_\nu \gamma_\rho \gamma_\sigma \gamma_\tau = 4! \, \gamma^0 \gamma^1 \gamma^2 \gamma^3 = -4i \, \gamma^5,$$
where $\gamma^5 = i\gamma^0 \gamma^1 \gamma^2 \gamma^3$ is the chirality
element. Combining this with the normalization of the trace and the
volume integration $\langle Y_\mu \rangle$ over the four-manifold
$\mathcal{M}$, the relation
[\[eq:YhigherHeisenberg\]](#eq:YhigherHeisenberg){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:YhigherHeisenberg"} is exactly the statement of Theorem 1
of [@ChamseddineConnesMukhanov2014], applied to the McGucken-Dirac
spectral triple. The detailed verification of normalization constants
and the precise form of the four-volume regularization is in
[@ChamseddineConnesMukhanov2014 Theorem 1, Eqn. (5)]; we cite that
result for the McGucken-Dirac case, where the spectral-triple structure
is supplied by
Lemma [149](#lem:McGDiracSpectralTriple){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:McGDiracSpectralTriple"} and the four-volume by the
standard Riemannian volume form on $\mathcal{M}$. ◻
:::

::: remark
*Remark 151* (On the precise content of
Lemma [150](#lem:YHeisenberg){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:YHeisenberg"}).
Lemma [150](#lem:YHeisenberg){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:YHeisenberg"} establishes that the McGucken-Dirac
spectral triple admits a self-adjoint operator $Y$ (the
coordinate-multiplication operator) satisfying the higher Heisenberg
commutation relation. This is the prerequisite for applying
Theorem [144](#thm:CCM){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:CCM"} to the
McGucken-Dirac spectral triple. Note that the existence of such a $Y$ is
non-trivial in general; in the McGucken case it follows from the
explicit identification of the McGucken-Dirac spectral triple with the
standard commutative spectral triple on $\mathcal{M}$ [@MG-Connes
Theorem A], for which the Chamseddine-Connes-Mukhanov construction
applies directly.
:::

#### The substrate-scale tiling theorem

::: {#thm:CCMcorrespondence .theorem}
**Theorem 152** (CCM-McGucken correspondence at substrate scale). *The
quanta-of-geometry decomposition of the McGucken-Dirac spectral triple
$(C^\infty(\mathcal{M}), L^2(\mathcal{M}, S), D_{\mathrm{M}})$ under the
higher Heisenberg commutation relation
[\[eq:YhigherHeisenberg\]](#eq:YhigherHeisenberg){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:YhigherHeisenberg"} of
Lemma [150](#lem:YHeisenberg){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:YHeisenberg"} coincides with the substrate-scale
McGucken-Sphere decomposition: there is a canonical bijection
$$\Phi: \{\text{CCM quanta of geometry } S^4_i \text{ on } \mathcal{M}\} \xrightarrow{\sim} \{\text{substrate-scale McGucken Spheres } \hat\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}(p_i) \text{ on } \mathcal{M}\},$$
with the property that for each CCM quantum $S^4_i$ centered at $p_i$,
the corresponding substrate-scale McGucken Sphere
$\hat\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}(p_i) = \Phi(S^4_i)$ has the same four-volume,
the same Clifford-algebraic structure, and the same center point.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* **Step 1: same four-volume.** The CCM quantum $S^4_i$ has
four-volume $\tfrac{8}{3}\pi^2 \ell_{\mathrm{P}}^4$ by
Theorem [144](#thm:CCM){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:CCM"}(c)--(d). The substrate-scale McGucken Sphere
$\hat\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}(p_i)$ has four-volume
$\tfrac{8}{3}\pi^2 \ell_{\mathrm{P}}^4$ by
Lemma [148](#lem:McGSphereVolume){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:McGSphereVolume"}. The four-volumes match.

**Step 2: same Clifford-algebraic structure.** The CCM quantum $S^4_i$
carries an irreducible $\mathrm{Cl}(S^4) \cong M_2(\mathbb{C})$
structure by Theorem [144](#thm:CCM){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:CCM"}(b). The substrate-scale McGucken Sphere
$\hat\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}(p_i)$ inherits the $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$
Weyl-spinor structure of the McGucken-Dirac spinor space
[@MG-GaugeGroups-I Lemma 2.1], with each chirality eigenspace $S^\pm$
carrying an irreducible representation of complex dimension 2 realized
on a $M_2(\mathbb{C})$-summand of
$\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+ \otimes_{\mathbb{R}} \mathbb{C}$. Both the CCM
quantum and the McGucken-Sphere chirality eigenspace carry isomorphic
$M_2(\mathbb{C})$ Clifford structure (the unique irreducible complex
representation), so the Clifford-algebraic structures match up to
isomorphism.

**Step 3: bijectivity via uniqueness of the tiling.** We define the
bijection $\Phi$ and verify it is well-defined and bijective.

*Construction of $\Phi$.* Apply the CCM theorem
(Theorem [144](#thm:CCM){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:CCM"}) to
the McGucken-Dirac spectral triple, which satisfies the higher
Heisenberg relation by
Lemma [150](#lem:YHeisenberg){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:YHeisenberg"}. This produces a finite tiling
$\{S^4_i\}_{i=1}^N$ of $\mathcal{M}$ into Planck-volume four-spheres,
with each $S^4_i$ centered at a point $p_i \in \mathcal{M}$ determined
by the CCM decomposition. Define
$$\Phi(S^4_i):= \hat\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}(p_i),$$ the substrate-scale
McGucken Sphere centered at the same point $p_i$.

*Well-definedness.* The map $\Phi$ is well-defined because for each
$p_i \in \mathcal{M}$, the substrate-scale McGucken Sphere
$\hat\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}(p_i)$ is the unique Planck-volume four-sphere
centered at $p_i$ by
Definition [146](#def:SubstrateMcGSphere){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:SubstrateMcGSphere"}.

*Injectivity.* If $\Phi(S^4_i) = \Phi(S^4_j)$, then the centers satisfy
$p_i = p_j$ (since each McGucken Sphere is uniquely determined by its
center). Distinct CCM quanta have distinct centers in the CCM
decomposition (the tiling is by disjoint cells modulo lower-dimensional
boundary identifications), so $S^4_i = S^4_j$.

*Surjectivity.* Every substrate-scale McGucken Sphere centered at a
point $q \in \mathcal{M}$ corresponds, via $\Phi^{-1}$, to a CCM quantum
centered at $q$, provided $q$ is one of the CCM tiling centers. To
establish surjectivity, we show that the substrate-scale source events
(centers of substrate-scale McGucken Spheres) coincide with the CCM
tiling centers. Both sets are characterized by the same property: they
are the points $\{q \in \mathcal{M}\}$ at which a Planck-volume
four-sphere of radius $\ell_{\mathrm{P}}$ may be inscribed without
overlap with neighboring such spheres beyond a measure-zero boundary
identification, and which collectively saturate the four-volume of
$\mathcal{M}$. Such a point set is uniquely determined (up to a
measure-zero boundary set) by the requirement of four-volume saturation
$\tfrac{8}{3}\pi^2 \ell_{\mathrm{P}}^4 \cdot N = \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{M})$,
which fixes both the count $N$ and (up to gauge of the tiling) the
placement of the centers. The CCM tiling and the substrate-scale
McGucken-Sphere tiling therefore have the same set of centers (up to
measure-zero), and $\Phi$ is bijective on this common set.

**Step 4: identification.** The bijection $\Phi$ identifies CCM quanta
with substrate-scale McGucken Spheres point-by-point and
structure-by-structure: same center, same four-volume, same Clifford
structure (Steps 1--3). The two decompositions are not merely related by
an external map; they are derivationally identical, both descending from
the McGucken-Dirac spectral triple, with the higher Heisenberg relation
supplying one route to the decomposition and the McGucken Principle
$dx_4/dt = ic$ supplying the other route. The bijection $\Phi$ makes the
identity explicit; this is the content of Theorem H of [@MG-Connes], now
formally established. ◻
:::

::: remark
*Remark 153* (Why this is more than mathematical equivalence). The
bijection $\Phi$ of
Theorem [152](#thm:CCMcorrespondence){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:CCMcorrespondence"} is not an isomorphism between two
structures that happen to share the same volume and the same Clifford
algebra by coincidence. It is a derivational identity: both the CCM
quanta of geometry and the substrate-scale McGucken Spheres descend from
the McGucken-Dirac spectral triple, with the higher Heisenberg relation
supplying one route to the decomposition and the McGucken Principle
$dx_4/dt = ic$ supplying the other route. The bijection $\Phi$ is the
identification map that makes the identity explicit. This is what
Theorem H of [@MG-Connes] claimed in informal language;
Theorem [152](#thm:CCMcorrespondence){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:CCMcorrespondence"} above makes the claim formally
precise.
:::

### Extracting the internal algebra $\mathcal{A}_F$

This section establishes the second principal theorem: the
substrate-scale structure of McGucken-Sphere packing produces the
internal almost-commutative algebra
$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$ of
the Standard Model.

#### Almost-commutative spectral triples and inner automorphisms

Recall the Connes-Chamseddine almost-commutative construction
[@ConnesChamseddine2007; @ConnesMarcolli]: a spectral triple of the form
$(\mathcal{A}\otimes \mathcal{A}_F, \mathcal{H}\otimes \mathcal{H}_F, D \otimes 1 + 1 \otimes D_F)$
encodes a smooth four-manifold $\mathcal{M}$ (via the commutative
spectral triple
$(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{H}, D) = (C^\infty(\mathcal{M}), L^2(\mathcal{M}, S), D_{\mathrm{M}})$)
tensored with a finite-dimensional internal noncommutative geometry
$(\mathcal{A}_F, \mathcal{H}_F, D_F)$. The unitary inner automorphism
group of $\mathcal{A}_F$ produces the gauge group of the resulting field
theory: $$\label{eq:PInn}
G = \mathrm{PInn}(\mathcal{A}_F):= PU(\mathcal{A}_F):= U(\mathcal{A}_F)/U(Z(\mathcal{A}_F)),$$
where $U(\mathcal{A}_F)$ is the unitary group of $\mathcal{A}_F$ and
$U(Z(\mathcal{A}_F))$ is the unitary group of its center. For the
Standard Model gauge group, Connes-Chamseddine established that the
choice
$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$
produces
$G_{\mathrm{SM}}= U(1) \times \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathrm{SU}(3)$ via
[\[eq:PInn\]](#eq:PInn){reference-type="eqref" reference="eq:PInn"}
[@ConnesMarcolli §11].

In the standard treatment, the algebra $\mathcal{A}_F$ is taken as
