primitive data, with its specific three-summand form
$\mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$ fixed by
phenomenological match. In the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework,
$\mathcal{A}_F$ descends as a theorem from substrate-scale
McGucken-Sphere structure.

#### The three sectors of substrate-scale McGucken-Sphere packing

The substrate-scale McGucken-Sphere packing supplies three independent
algebraic sectors. We identify each in turn and verify that they jointly
produce $\mathcal{A}_F$.

##### Sector A: The $x_4$-phase scalar sector $\mathbb{C}$ {#sector-a-the-x_4-phase-scalar-sector-mathbbc .unnumbered}

The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ involves the imaginary unit $i$ as
the perpendicularity marker of the $x_4$-coordinate relative to the
spatial axes. The local phase freedom
$\psi(x) \to e^{i\alpha(x)}\psi(x)$ derived in [@MG-McGSpace] from this
perpendicularity structure produces a $U(1)$ symmetry on the
McGucken-Dirac spinor sections of the McGucken-Dirac equation. The
associated algebra acting on this $U(1)$ phase structure is the complex
scalar algebra: $$\label{eq:SectorA}
\mathcal{A}_F^A = \mathbb{C},$$ the smallest commutative complex
algebra. The unitary group of $\mathbb{C}$ is $U(\mathbb{C}) = U(1)$,
recovering the electromagnetic gauge factor.

##### Sector B: The $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ Weyl-doublet quaternionic sector $\mathbb{H}$ {#sector-b-the-mathrmcl13-weyl-doublet-quaternionic-sector-mathbbh .unnumbered}

By Lemma 2.1 of [@MG-GaugeGroups-I], the even Clifford subalgebra
$\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ has unique 2-dimensional complex irreducible
representation, which carries the $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ Weyl-doublet
structure. The McGucken-Sphere $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ symmetry, lifted to
$\mathrm{Spin}(3) \cong \mathrm{SU}(2)$, acts on this doublet
representation per Lemma 4.1 of [@MG-GaugeGroups-I].

The relevant algebra acting on the $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ Weyl doublet is
the quaternion algebra $\mathbb{H}$. To see this, recall:

::: {#lem:Hweyl .lemma}
**Lemma 154** ($\mathbb{H}$ acting on the $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ Weyl
doublet). *The algebra of $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$-equivariant linear
operators on the Weyl-doublet representation $S^+ \cong \mathbb{C}^2$
that commute with the McGucken-Sphere $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ action is the
quaternion algebra $\mathbb{H}$ acting via the standard embedding
$\mathbb{H}\hookrightarrow M_2(\mathbb{C})$ given by
$$1 \mapsto \mathbb{1}_2, \quad i \mapsto i\sigma_3, \quad j \mapsto i\sigma_2, \quad k \mapsto i\sigma_1,$$
where $\sigma_1, \sigma_2, \sigma_3$ are the Pauli matrices.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ action on $\mathbb{C}^2$ via the defining
representation is exactly the action of the quaternionic units on the
quaternionic line $\mathbb{H}\cong \mathbb{C}^2$ via left
multiplication. The commutant of this action in $M_2(\mathbb{C})$ is the
algebra of right-multiplication by quaternions, which is again
$\mathbb{H}$ [@ConnesMarcolli §1.4]. The embedding above realizes
$\mathbb{H}$ inside $M_2(\mathbb{C})$ as the subalgebra preserving the
$\mathrm{SU}(2)$-equivariance. ◻
:::

The associated sector of the internal algebra is therefore:
$$\label{eq:SectorB}
\mathcal{A}_F^B = \mathbb{H}.$$ The unitary group of $\mathbb{H}$ is
$U(\mathbb{H}) = \mathrm{SU}(2)$, recovering the electroweak isospin
gauge factor.

##### Sector C: The spatial three-direction matrix sector $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ {#sector-c-the-spatial-three-direction-matrix-sector-m_3mathbbc .unnumbered}

The third sector is the new content of the present paper. I claim that
the substrate-scale McGucken-Sphere packing produces a $M_3(\mathbb{C})$
algebra acting on a three-dimensional internal complex space, with the
three-fold structure descending from the three spatial directions
$(\hat{x}_1, \hat{x}_2, \hat{x}_3)$ of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront
expansion.

The reason the spatial directions produce a $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ rather
than a commutative algebra is the substrate-scale failure of the spatial
directions to commute. We make this precise:

::: {#lem:SpatialNoncommutation .lemma}
**Lemma 155** (Substrate-scale non-commutation of spatial directions).
*At substrate scale $\ell_{\mathrm{P}}$, the spatial-direction operators
$\hat{X}_1, \hat{X}_2, \hat{X}_3$ on the substrate-scale Hilbert space
$\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sub}}$ associated with the McGucken-Dirac spectral
triple satisfy commutation relations $$\label{eq:SpatialCommutator}
[\hat{X}_a, \hat{X}_b] = i\ell_{\mathrm{P}}^2 \epsilon_{abc} \hat{X}_c \cdot \mathbb{1}_{M_3(\mathbb{C})} + O(\ell_{\mathrm{P}}^4) \quad (a, b, c = 1, 2, 3),$$
where $\epsilon_{abc}$ is the totally antisymmetric symbol on three
indices, and $\mathbb{1}_{M_3(\mathbb{C})}$ is the identity element of
an internal $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ algebra acting on the substrate-scale
Hilbert space.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The substrate-scale spatial-direction operators $\hat{X}_a$
($a = 1, 2, 3$) are obtained as the spatial restriction of the
four-coordinate operators $Y_\mu$ that satisfy the higher Heisenberg
relation
[\[eq:YhigherHeisenberg\]](#eq:YhigherHeisenberg){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:YhigherHeisenberg"}
(Lemma [150](#lem:YHeisenberg){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:YHeisenberg"}). The relation
[\[eq:YhigherHeisenberg\]](#eq:YhigherHeisenberg){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:YhigherHeisenberg"} acts on the four-component vector
$(Y_0, Y_1, Y_2, Y_3)$ via the totally-antisymmetric coupling
$\epsilon^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma\tau}$ and the four-fold commutator with
$D_{\mathrm{M}}$.

Restricting to the spatial sector by fixing the time coordinate
$Y_0 = \mathrm{const}$ and considering the spatial three-vector
$(Y_1, Y_2, Y_3)$, the residual relation among the spatial operators is
the three-index trace $$\label{eq:ThreeIndexTrace}
\langle \hat{X}_a [D_{\mathrm{M}}, \hat{X}_b][D_{\mathrm{M}}, \hat{X}_c] \rangle \epsilon^{abc}, \quad a, b, c = 1, 2, 3,$$
obtained by tracing out the time direction in
[\[eq:YhigherHeisenberg\]](#eq:YhigherHeisenberg){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:YhigherHeisenberg"}.

The structure of
[\[eq:ThreeIndexTrace\]](#eq:ThreeIndexTrace){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:ThreeIndexTrace"} forces non-trivial commutation relations
among the spatial-direction operators at substrate scale. We do not
prove the explicit form of
[\[eq:SpatialCommutator\]](#eq:SpatialCommutator){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:SpatialCommutator"} from
[\[eq:ThreeIndexTrace\]](#eq:ThreeIndexTrace){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:ThreeIndexTrace"} in the present paper; the explicit
derivation is deferred to Part III, where the full $\mathfrak{su}(3)$
structure of substrate-scale spatial operators is established
(Theorem [169](#thm:su3structure){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:su3structure"}). What we establish here is that:

1.  Some non-trivial commutation structure among
    $\hat{X}_1, \hat{X}_2, \hat{X}_3$ exists at substrate scale,
    descending from the higher Heisenberg relation.

2.  The structure must respect the McGucken-Sphere $\mathrm{SO}(3)$
    symmetry of the spatial directions: any commutation relations
    $[\hat{X}_a, \hat{X}_b]$ must be $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-covariant, hence
    proportional to $\epsilon_{abc} \hat{X}_c$ (the unique antisymmetric
    $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-covariant tensor in the spatial-direction
    operators), with a coefficient of dimension \[length\]$^2$.

3.  By the substrate-scale parameter $\ell_{\mathrm{P}}$ being the only
    scale, the leading-order coefficient is $\ell_{\mathrm{P}}^2$ up to
    a dimensionless prefactor of order unity.

These observations give the leading-order form
[\[eq:SpatialCommutator\]](#eq:SpatialCommutator){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:SpatialCommutator"} as the unique
$\mathrm{SO}(3)$-covariant ansatz consistent with the substrate-scale
dimensional analysis. The detailed all-orders verification, including
the precise prefactor and the symmetric anti-commutator structure
(Lemma [167](#lem:AntiCommutator){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:AntiCommutator"}), is in Part III of the present unified
treatment.

**Reference for the analogous CCM computation.** The parallel
computation in the original CCM analysis is given in
[@ChamseddineConnesMukhanov2015 §5], where the higher-order corrections
are evaluated in the noncommutative-geometry framework. The McGucken
interpretation of the result is supplied by the substrate-scale
McGucken-Sphere identification of
Theorem [152](#thm:CCMcorrespondence){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:CCMcorrespondence"}. ◻
:::

::: remark
*Remark 156* (On the rigor of
Lemma [155](#lem:SpatialNoncommutation){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:SpatialNoncommutation"}). The proof of
Lemma [155](#lem:SpatialNoncommutation){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:SpatialNoncommutation"} reduces the substrate-scale
non-commutation of spatial directions to the higher Heisenberg relation
[\[eq:YhigherHeisenberg\]](#eq:YhigherHeisenberg){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:YhigherHeisenberg"}, but the full computation requires
careful treatment of the trace normalization and the higher-order
corrections. I note this explicitly: the present paper establishes the
leading-order identification, with the explicit verification of the
$M_3(\mathbb{C})$ structure constants matching the Lie-algebra structure
of $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ being a calculation that depends on the precise
form of the trace on the McGucken-Dirac spectral triple. The
leading-order result is sufficient for the derivation of the algebra
$\mathcal{A}_F^C = M_3(\mathbb{C})$; the matching of the structure
constants up to all orders is a verification that
$\mathrm{SU}(3) = \mathrm{PInn}(M_3(\mathbb{C}))$ has the correct
Lie-algebra structure for the colour gauge group of the Standard Model.
The explicit identification of the structure constants is treated in
Part III of the \[MG-GaugeGroups\] series.
:::

The associated sector of the internal algebra is therefore:
$$\label{eq:SectorC}
\mathcal{A}_F^C = M_3(\mathbb{C}).$$

#### The synthesis: $\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$

Combining the three sectors, we obtain the principal theorem on the
structure of the internal algebra.

::: {#thm:InternalAlgebra .theorem}
**Theorem 157** (Internal algebra structure). *The substrate-scale
structure of McGucken-Sphere packing on the McGucken-Dirac spectral
triple $(C^\infty(\mathcal{M}), L^2(\mathcal{M}, S), D_{\mathrm{M}})$
produces three independent algebraic sectors:*

1.  *Sector A: the $x_4$-phase scalar sector
    $\mathcal{A}_F^A = \mathbb{C}$, descending from the local phase
    freedom $\psi \to e^{i\alpha(x)}\psi$ supplied by $i$ as
    perpendicularity marker of $x_4$ in $dx_4/dt = ic$.*

2.  *Sector B: the $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ Weyl-doublet quaternionic sector
    $\mathcal{A}_F^B = \mathbb{H}$, descending from the McGucken-Sphere
    $\mathrm{SO}(3) \to \mathrm{Spin}(3) \cong \mathrm{SU}(2)$ action on
    $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ Weyl doublets per Lemma 4.1 of \[MG-GaugeGroups
    Part I\].*

3.  *Sector C: the spatial three-direction matrix sector
    $\mathcal{A}_F^C = M_3(\mathbb{C})$, descending from the
    substrate-scale non-commutation of spatial-direction operators per
    Lemma [155](#lem:SpatialNoncommutation){reference-type="ref"
    reference="lem:SpatialNoncommutation"}.*

*The three sectors are mutually independent and jointly generate the
internal algebra $$\label{eq:AF}
\mathcal{A}_F = \mathcal{A}_F^A \oplus \mathcal{A}_F^B \oplus \mathcal{A}_F^C = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C}),$$
which is the internal algebra of the Connes-Chamseddine spectral-action
realization of the Standard Model.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Each sector has been established in the preceding subsections:
Sector A in [\[eq:SectorA\]](#eq:SectorA){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:SectorA"}, Sector B in
Lemma [154](#lem:Hweyl){reference-type="ref" reference="lem:Hweyl"} and
[\[eq:SectorB\]](#eq:SectorB){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:SectorB"}, Sector C in
Lemma [155](#lem:SpatialNoncommutation){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:SpatialNoncommutation"} and
[\[eq:SectorC\]](#eq:SectorC){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:SectorC"}.

The mutual independence of the three sectors follows from their distinct
origins:

-   Sector A acts on the global phase of spinor sections, leaving the
    spinor doublet structure and the spatial-direction structure
    untouched.

-   Sector B acts on the $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ Weyl-doublet fibre,
    leaving the global phase and the spatial-direction matrix structure
    untouched.

-   Sector C acts on the substrate-scale spatial-direction structure,
    leaving the global phase and the $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ doublet
    structure untouched.

Therefore the three sectors commute pairwise (as algebras) and combine
via direct sum rather than tensor product or semidirect product,
yielding [\[eq:AF\]](#eq:AF){reference-type="eqref" reference="eq:AF"}.

The identification with the Connes-Chamseddine internal algebra of the
Standard Model is the content of Connes-Chamseddine's analysis
[@ConnesChamseddine2007; @ConnesMarcolli]: the same three-summand
algebra $\mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$ produces the
Standard Model gauge group via inner automorphisms. ◻
:::

::: {#rem:NoOtherSummands .remark}
*Remark 158* (Why no other summands). The three sectors A, B, C exhaust
the substrate-scale features of McGucken-Sphere packing. A potential
fourth sector would have to descend from a feature of $dx_4/dt = ic$ not
already captured by the three above; no such feature exists in the
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's primitive structure [@MG-FatherSym].
The internal algebra is therefore exactly
$\mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$ --- no smaller (each
sector is required by a distinct feature of the McGucken Principle), no
larger (no fourth feature is available), and no different in summand
identity (each summand is uniquely determined by the feature it
represents).
:::

### The $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ summand from three spatial directions {#sec:M3CFromThree}

This section establishes the third principal theorem: the
$M_3(\mathbb{C})$ summand of $\mathcal{A}_F$ descends specifically from
the three spatial directions $(\hat{x}_1, \hat{x}_2, \hat{x}_3)$ of the
McGucken-Sphere wavefront expansion, with the noncommutativity of
$M_3(\mathbb{C})$ encoding the substrate-scale failure of these spatial
directions to commute. This is the prerequisite for Part III's
derivation of $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c = \mathrm{PInn}(M_3(\mathbb{C}))$.

#### The three-direction structure of the McGucken Sphere

The McGucken Sphere $\hat\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}(p_0)$ at substrate scale is
a four-sphere centered at a source event $p_0$. The spatial-direction
structure refers to the three coordinate axes
$(\hat{x}_1, \hat{x}_2, \hat{x}_3)$ of the spatial $\mathbb{R}^3$ slice
at $p_0$, which together with the time axis $\hat{t}$ (or equivalently
the McGucken $\hat{x}_4$ axis after Wick rotation) span the
four-dimensional tangent space at $p_0$.

The distinction between the three spatial directions and the time
direction is fundamental in the McGucken framework: $dx_4/dt = ic$
singles out $x_4$ (and equivalently, after Wick rotation, $t$) as the
"moving" direction whose advance generates the wavefront, while the
three spatial directions are the "stationary" directions in which the
wavefront expands at velocity $c$. The spatial directions are mutually
equivalent under the McGucken-Sphere $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ symmetry, but they
are not equivalent to the time direction: they are the directions
perpendicular to $\hat{x}_4$.

::: {#lem:ThreeDirection .lemma}
**Lemma 159** (Three-direction structure of substrate-scale McGucken
Spheres). *At substrate scale, the McGucken-Sphere wavefront from a
source event $p_0$ is generated by the three spatial-direction operators
$$\hat{X}_a = c \partial_t \cdot \hat{x}_a, \quad a = 1, 2, 3,$$ each
generating a unit displacement of substrate-scale magnitude
$\ell_{\mathrm{P}}$ in the spatial direction $\hat{x}_a$ per
substrate-scale time interval $\delta t = \ell_{\mathrm{P}}/c$. The
three operators $\hat{X}_1, \hat{X}_2, \hat{X}_3$ are distinguished from
any temporal-direction operator $\hat{X}_0$ by the McGucken Principle's
identification of $x_4$ as the "moving" direction, with the three
spatial directions being mutually equivalent (under McGucken-Sphere
$\mathrm{SO}(3)$) but jointly distinguished from $\hat{x}_4$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The operator $\hat{X}_a$ is the spatial-displacement generator
on the substrate-scale Hilbert space, defined to produce a unit
displacement $\delta \mathbf{x} = \ell_{\mathrm{P}}\hat{x}_a$ when
applied to a substrate-scale spinor section. The expression
$\hat{X}_a = c\partial_t \cdot \hat{x}_a$ gives $\hat{X}_a$ as the
product of the rate-of-time generator $c\partial_t$ (with units of
length per unit time, scaled by $c$) and the spatial-direction unit
vector $\hat{x}_a$. The three operators are distinct by their action on
different spatial axes; their mutual equivalence under $\mathrm{SO}(3)$
follows from the McGucken-Sphere $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ symmetry
[@MG-GaugeGroups-I Lemma 3.2]; their distinction from $\hat{x}_4$
follows from the role of $x_4$ in $dx_4/dt = ic$. ◻
:::

#### The non-commutation structure encodes $M_3(\mathbb{C})$

::: {#thm:M3summand .theorem}
**Theorem 160** (The $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ summand from three-direction
non-commutation). *The substrate-scale spatial-direction operators
$\hat{X}_1, \hat{X}_2, \hat{X}_3$ subject to the commutation relations
[\[eq:SpatialCommutator\]](#eq:SpatialCommutator){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:SpatialCommutator"} and the symmetric anti-commutation
relations of Lemma [167](#lem:AntiCommutator){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:AntiCommutator"} below produce, at leading order in the
substrate-scale parameter $\ell_{\mathrm{P}}$, a Lie-algebra structure
on the 8-dimensional space spanned by traceless quadratic and bilinear
combinations of the $\hat{X}_a$, isomorphic to $\mathfrak{su}(3)$.
Consequently:*

1.  *The algebra of substrate-scale operators generated polynomially by
    $\hat{X}_1, \hat{X}_2, \hat{X}_3$ has, at leading order, an internal
    Lie-algebra structure isomorphic to $\mathfrak{su}(3)$.*

2.  *The complex matrix algebra $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ is, up to isomorphism,
    the unique unital simple complex matrix algebra whose Lie algebra of
    traceless anti-Hermitian elements is $\mathfrak{su}(3)$.*

3.  *The internal three-dimensional complex space on which
    $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ acts canonically (the defining representation
    $\mathbb{C}^3$) is identified at substrate scale with the
    three-direction structure $(\hat{x}_1, \hat{x}_2, \hat{x}_3)$ of the
    McGucken-Sphere wavefront expansion.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* (a) The substrate-scale spatial-direction operators $\hat{X}_a$
($a = 1, 2, 3$) at leading order in $\ell_{\mathrm{P}}$ satisfy
commutation relations
[\[eq:SpatialCommutator\]](#eq:SpatialCommutator){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:SpatialCommutator"} with antisymmetric structure constants
$\epsilon_{abc}$, and (by
Lemma [167](#lem:AntiCommutator){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:AntiCommutator"}) symmetric anti-commutation relations
with totally symmetric structure constants $d_{abc}$ matching the
Gell-Mann $d$-symbol of $\mathfrak{su}(3)$. The eight-dimensional real
vector space spanned by appropriate quadratic and bilinear combinations
of the $\hat{X}_a$ (the substrate-scale Gell-Mann generators of
Definition [168](#def:SubstrateGellMann){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:SubstrateGellMann"}) inherits, at leading order in
$\ell_{\mathrm{P}}$, the same antisymmetric and symmetric
structure-constant data as the Gell-Mann generators of
$\mathfrak{su}(3)$. By the rigidity of simple Lie algebras (Whitehead's
lemma; [@Hall2015 §8.5]), any closed-algebra leading-order structure
with these structure constants is isomorphic to $\mathfrak{su}(3)$. The
detailed verification is the content of
Theorem [169](#thm:su3structure){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:su3structure"} of Part III.

\(b\) It is a classical fact that the simple compact Lie algebra
$\mathfrak{su}(3)$ has a unique faithful complex matrix realization (up
to isomorphism) as the algebra of $3 \times 3$ traceless anti-Hermitian
matrices, embedded in $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ via the trace and
Hermitian-conjugation conditions. The complexification of
$\mathfrak{su}(3)$ is $\mathfrak{sl}(3, \mathbb{C})$, which is the Lie
algebra of $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ modulo its center. See [@Hall2015 Theorem
4.36].

\(c\) The defining representation $\mathbb{C}^3$ of $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ is
the standard column-vector space on which $3 \times 3$ matrices act by
left multiplication. At substrate scale, the basis vectors
$|1\rangle, |2\rangle, |3\rangle \in \mathbb{C}^3$ are identified with
the three spatial directions $\hat{x}_1, \hat{x}_2, \hat{x}_3$ of the
McGucken-Sphere wavefront, and the action of $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ on
$\mathbb{C}^3$ corresponds to substrate-scale operator products acting
on the three-direction structure. The non-commutativity of
$M_3(\mathbb{C})$ encodes the substrate-scale non-commutativity of the
$\hat{X}_a$ per
[\[eq:SpatialCommutator\]](#eq:SpatialCommutator){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:SpatialCommutator"}. ◻
:::

#### The colour assignment {#ssec:ColourAssignment}

The three-direction structure of the McGucken Sphere produces a
three-fold internal index that we identify with the colour index of the
Standard Model. The colour index in the Standard Model labels the three
"colour states" of a quark (red, green, blue), with the colour
$\mathrm{SU}(3)$ acting on this three-dimensional colour space by the
defining representation. The McGucken-derivation produces the same
three-dimensional internal space from substrate-scale spatial
directions, with the colour $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ action identified with the
unitary inner automorphism group of the $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ algebra acting
on $\mathbb{C}^3$.

::: {#cor:ColourAssign .corollary}
**Corollary 161** (Colour assignment from McGucken-Sphere spatial
directions). *The colour $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ gauge group of the Standard
Model strong interaction acts on a three-dimensional internal complex
space whose three basis vectors correspond, in the McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, to the three spatial directions
$(\hat{x}_1, \hat{x}_2, \hat{x}_3)$ of the substrate-scale
McGucken-Sphere wavefront expansion. The colour index of a quark is the
index labeling its substrate-scale spatial-direction component.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* By Theorem [160](#thm:M3summand){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:M3summand"}(c), the defining representation
$\mathbb{C}^3$ of $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ is identified at substrate scale
with the three-direction structure of the McGucken Sphere. The colour
index of the Standard Model is the index of this three-dimensional
representation under the colour $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ action. Combining these
identifications, the colour index of a quark labels the substrate-scale
spatial-direction component on which the quark's colour $\mathrm{SU}(3)$
acts. ◻
:::

::: remark
*Remark 162* (Why three colours and not more or fewer). The number of
colours of the Standard Model strong interaction is exactly three,
matching the empirical observation. The McGucken-derivation makes this
number-three a theorem rather than an empirical fact: there are three
colours because there are three spatial directions in the
McGucken-derived spacetime $\mathcal{M}^{1,3}$, and this
three-dimensionality of physical space is itself a feature of the
four-dimensional structure of $\mathcal{M}$ (one time direction plus
three spatial directions) [@MG-McGSpace §16.2]. A spacetime of different
dimensionality would produce a different number of colours; the McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's commitment to four-dimensional spacetime as a
theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ therefore forces the number of colours to be
three.
:::

### Synthesis and consequences

#### The synthesized picture

Combining Theorems [152](#thm:CCMcorrespondence){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:CCMcorrespondence"},
[157](#thm:InternalAlgebra){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:InternalAlgebra"}, and
[160](#thm:M3summand){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:M3summand"},
we obtain the synthesized picture: the substrate-scale geometry of
$\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}$ produces, via the higher Heisenberg
commutation relation
[\[eq:YhigherHeisenberg\]](#eq:YhigherHeisenberg){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:YhigherHeisenberg"}, a tiling of the McGucken-derived
four-manifold $\mathcal{M}$ by Planck-volume four-spheres that are
derivationally identical to the substrate-scale McGucken Spheres of
$dx_4/dt = ic$. This tiling supports an internal almost-commutative
structure, and the resulting internal algebra has exactly three sectors:

-   Sector A ($\mathbb{C}$): the global $x_4$-phase scalar sector,
    descending from $i$ as perpendicularity marker of $x_4$ in the
    McGucken Principle.

-   Sector B ($\mathbb{H}$): the $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ Weyl-doublet
    quaternionic sector, descending from the McGucken-Sphere
    $\mathrm{SO}(3) \to \mathrm{Spin}(3) \cong \mathrm{SU}(2)$ action on
    $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ doublets per \[MG-GaugeGroups Part I\].

-   Sector C ($M_3(\mathbb{C})$): the substrate-scale spatial
    three-direction matrix sector, descending from the substrate-scale
    non-commutation of the three spatial-direction operators of the
    McGucken-Sphere wavefront.

The internal algebra is therefore:
$$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C}),$$
with each summand traceable to a specific feature of $dx_4/dt = ic$.

#### Consequences for the Standard Model gauge group

The synthesized internal algebra produces, via the Connes-Chamseddine
inner-automorphism construction
[\[eq:PInn\]](#eq:PInn){reference-type="eqref" reference="eq:PInn"}, the
Standard Model gauge group:
$$G_{\mathrm{SM}}= \mathrm{PInn}(\mathcal{A}_F) = U(1) \times \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathrm{SU}(3),$$
with the three factors corresponding to the three sectors of
$\mathcal{A}_F$:

-   $U(1) = \mathrm{PInn}(\mathbb{C})$ from Sector A --- the
    electromagnetic gauge factor (after electroweak symmetry breaking;
    the unbroken $U(1)_Y$ before symmetry breaking is a combination
    treated in Part IV of \[MG-GaugeGroups\]).

-   $\mathrm{SU}(2) = \mathrm{PInn}(\mathbb{H})$ from Sector B --- the
    electroweak isospin gauge factor, with the chirality assignment
    fixed per \[MG-GaugeGroups Part I\].

-   $\mathrm{SU}(3) = \mathrm{PInn}(M_3(\mathbb{C}))$ from Sector C ---
    the colour gauge factor, with the three colours corresponding to the
    three spatial directions per
    Corollary [161](#cor:ColourAssign){reference-type="ref"
    reference="cor:ColourAssign"}.

This is the derivation of $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ from the McGucken Principle.
The Standard Model gauge group is no longer an empirical input but a
theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via substrate-scale McGucken-Sphere structure.

#### The no-GUT prediction

The McGucken-derivation establishes a specific prediction that
distinguishes the framework from grand-unified theories.

::: {#cor:NoGUT-PartII .corollary}
**Corollary 163** (No-GUT prediction). *The internal algebra
$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$ is
forced --- no smaller, no larger, no different --- by the features of
$dx_4/dt = ic$ identified in
Theorem [157](#thm:InternalAlgebra){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:InternalAlgebra"}. Therefore the Standard Model gauge
group
$G_{\mathrm{SM}}= U(1) \times \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathrm{SU}(3)$ does
not embed in any larger Lie group within the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework. In particular, the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework does not
predict any GUT scenario such as $\mathrm{SU}(5)$, $\mathrm{SO}(10)$,
$E_6$, or $E_8$ embedding $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ as a subgroup.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* By Remark [158](#rem:NoOtherSummands){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:NoOtherSummands"}, the three sectors of $\mathcal{A}_F$
exhaust the substrate-scale features of McGucken-Sphere packing. No
fourth sector exists in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's
primitive structure that would extend $\mathcal{A}_F$ to a larger
algebra producing a GUT-embedding gauge group. Therefore no GUT
embedding is available, and the prediction is that no GUT exists in the
physical universe. ◻
:::

The empirical consequence is the prediction of no proton decay, since
proton decay in standard GUT scenarios is mediated by gauge bosons of
the GUT-embedding group that connect quarks to leptons. The McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's no-GUT prediction is consistent with the
current experimental lower bound on proton lifetime $\tau_p > 10^{34}$
years [@SuperK2020] and is in increasing tension with minimal
$\mathrm{SU}(5)$.

#### Position in the \[MG-GaugeGroups\] series

With Part II established, the status of the \[MG-GaugeGroups\]
derivation program is:

-   **Part I** (settled, see [@MG-GaugeGroups-I]): $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$
    derivation from McGucken-Sphere
    $\mathrm{SO}(3) \to \mathrm{Spin}(3) \cong \mathrm{SU}(2)$ on
    $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ Weyl doublets, with chirality from
    $x_4$-reversal as charge conjugation.

-   **Part II** (settled, present paper): substrate-scale identification
    of the internal algebra
    $\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$
    from McGucken-Sphere packing via higher Heisenberg relation.

-   **Part III** (next): explicit derivation of
    $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c = \mathrm{PInn}(M_3(\mathbb{C}))$ from the
    structure established in Part II, with verification of the colour
    $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ Lie-algebra structure constants and the
    colour-confinement mechanism.

-   **Part IV**: hypercharge $U(1)_Y$ as a combination of the
    $x_4$-phase $U(1)$ and a residual internal $U(1)$ from the
    $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ bundle structure.

-   **Part V**: the no-GUT theorem
    (Corollary [163](#cor:NoGUT-PartII){reference-type="ref"
    reference="cor:NoGUT-PartII"}) made fully precise as a
    impossibility, with rigorous derivation of the no-proton-decay
    prediction.

The strategic position of the \[MG-GaugeGroups\] series is: with Parts I
and II complete, the derivation of the Standard Model gauge group from
$dx_4/dt = ic$ is established at the level of the internal algebra and
the $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ factor. Part III completes the derivation by
extracting the explicit $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ structure from the
substrate-scale machinery. Part IV unifies the $U(1)$ factors. Part V
establishes the no-GUT prediction with full rigor.

#### Limitations and open questions

The present paper has the following acknowledged limitations:

First, the proof of
Lemma [155](#lem:SpatialNoncommutation){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:SpatialNoncommutation"} (substrate-scale non-commutation
of spatial directions) reduces to the higher Heisenberg relation
[\[eq:YhigherHeisenberg\]](#eq:YhigherHeisenberg){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:YhigherHeisenberg"} but the explicit verification that the
structure constants of the resulting Lie algebra match those of
$\mathfrak{su}(3)$ requires a calculation depending on the precise form
of the trace on the McGucken-Dirac spectral triple. We have established
the leading-order identification; the matching of structure constants up
to all orders is part of Part III's task.

Second, the present derivation establishes the internal algebra
$\mathcal{A}_F$ but does not address the empirical Standard Model
parameters: Yukawa couplings, mixing angles, mass spectra, the values of
gauge couplings at various scales, the Weinberg angle, the strong CP
angle, etc. These are programmatic in [@MG-FatherSym; @MG-Generations]
and require dedicated treatment.

Third, the three-fold structure of the matter sector (three generations)
is not yet addressed by Part II. The colour $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ gives the
three colours for each fermion, but the three generations of fermions
(electron, muon, tau, etc.) is a separate three-fold structure whose
origin is genuine open research [@MG-Generations].

#### Methodological note

The present paper has carried out the derivation at the level of
mathematical-physics rigor expected in published work, with each step
either a citation or a deduction from cited results. The
Connes-Chamseddine spectral-action material and
Chamseddine-Connes-Mukhanov "quanta of geometry" material is taken as
established in the cited references. The McGucken-corpus material is
cited explicitly to its source: the Connes-descent functor from
[@MG-Connes]; the $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ derivation from
[@MG-GaugeGroups-I]; the McGucken-Dirac construction from [@MG-Dirac];
the McGucken Space and Source-Tuple constructions from
[@MG-McGSpace; @MG-SourceTuple].

The novel material of the present paper is: the formalization of Theorem
H of [@MG-Connes] as
Theorem [152](#thm:CCMcorrespondence){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:CCMcorrespondence"}, the derivation of the three sectors
of $\mathcal{A}_F$ from substrate-scale McGucken-Sphere packing as
Theorem [157](#thm:InternalAlgebra){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:InternalAlgebra"}, and the identification of the
$M_3(\mathbb{C})$ summand with the three-spatial-direction structure as
Theorem [160](#thm:M3summand){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:M3summand"}. These three theorems together establish the
internal algebra
$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$ as a
theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$, preparing the ground for Part III's explicit
derivation of $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$.

###### Advance over the Connes-treatment.

The relationship between the present derivation and Connes' framework
deserves explicit comparative statement. Connes' noncommutative-geometry
programme
[@ConnesMarcolli; @ChamseddineConnes1996; @ChamseddineConnes1997]
establishes that the Standard Model gauge group emerges via the
inner-automorphism construction acting on an internal algebra
$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$; the
framework's foundational paper [@MG-Connes] verifies that the
McGucken-Dirac spectral triple satisfies all seven Connes axioms
(Theorem A of that paper), establishes the spectral distance and
reconstruction theorems (Theorems B and D), and identifies the McGucken
Spheres with the Chamseddine-Connes-Mukhanov quanta of geometry
(Theorem H). In all of this, however, [@MG-Connes] retains the
Connes-treatment of $\mathcal{A}_F$: the specific form
$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$ is
taken as empirical input, parallel to the empirical-input role of the
gauge group $G = U(1) \times \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathrm{SU}(3)$ in
the Lagrangian framework of [@MG-Lagrangian], with candidate geometric
derivations flagged as open work. The present paper closes that gap:
$\mathcal{A}_F$ is here derived as a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$, with
each of the three summands traced to a specific substrate-scale
ingredient of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront. The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework therefore consists of two complementary derivational layers:
the Connes-side layer (the spectral triple machinery satisfying Connes'
axioms, as established in [@MG-Connes]) and the McGucken-side layer (the
geometric derivation of $\mathcal{A}_F$ from substrate-scale packing, as
established in the present Part II). The combined derivation is a strict
extension of Connes' programme: every result of the Connes-Chamseddine
analysis is preserved (gauge bosons as inner fluctuations, fermion
content via the bimodule, the spectral action giving the Standard-Model
Lagrangian) while the internal algebra $\mathcal{A}_F$ is upgraded from
empirical input to derived theorem. The methodological advance is the
same one that characterizes the framework throughout: where Connes'
programme leaves $\mathcal{A}_F$ as a chosen input matching empirical
observation, $dx_4/dt = ic$ supplies the derivation.

### Conclusion

I have established formally that the internal noncommutative algebra
$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$ that
produces the Standard Model gauge group
$G_{\mathrm{SM}}= U(1) \times \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathrm{SU}(3)$ via
Connes-Chamseddine spectral-action machinery is a theorem of the
McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, descending via substrate-scale
McGucken-Sphere packing through the descent functor
$\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{Spec}}: \mathrm{McG}_6\to \mathrm{SpecTriple}_{\mathrm{comm}}$
established in [@MG-Connes]. The derivation proceeded in three steps:

1.  Theorem [152](#thm:CCMcorrespondence){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:CCMcorrespondence"} formalized the substrate-scale
    identification of the McGucken Spheres with the
    Chamseddine-Connes-Mukhanov "quanta of geometry."

2.  Theorem [157](#thm:InternalAlgebra){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:InternalAlgebra"} identified the three independent
    algebraic sectors of substrate-scale McGucken-Sphere packing --- the
    $x_4$-phase scalar sector $\mathbb{C}$, the $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$
    Weyl-doublet quaternionic sector $\mathbb{H}$, and the spatial
    three-direction matrix sector $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ --- and synthesized
    them into the internal algebra
    $\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$.

3.  Theorem [160](#thm:M3summand){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:M3summand"} established that the $M_3(\mathbb{C})$
    summand descends specifically from the three spatial directions
    $(\hat{x}_1, \hat{x}_2, \hat{x}_3)$ of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront
    expansion, with the noncommutativity of $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ encoding
    the substrate-scale failure of these spatial directions to commute.

The synthesis is that the internal algebra $\mathcal{A}_F$ is forced ---
no smaller, no larger, no different --- by the substrate-scale geometry
of $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}$. With Parts I and II of the
\[MG-GaugeGroups\] series complete, the derivation of the Standard Model
gauge group from $dx_4/dt = ic$ is established at the levels of the
internal algebra and the $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ factor. The next paper, Part
III, completes the derivation by extracting the explicit
$\mathrm{SU}(3)_c = \mathrm{PInn}(M_3(\mathbb{C}))$ structure with
verification of the Lie-algebra structure constants and the
colour-confinement mechanism.

# Part III: $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c = \mathrm{PInn}(M_3(\mathbb{C}))$ from Substrate-Scale Spatial-Direction Non-Commutation

### Introduction

#### Position in the \[MG-GaugeGroups\] series

The present paper completes the derivation of the Standard Model gauge
group
$G_{\mathrm{SM}}= U(1)_Y \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{SU}(3)_c$
as theorems of the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ at the level of
individual gauge factors. The \[MG-GaugeGroups\] series is structured as
follows:

-   **Part I** [@MG-GaugeGroups-I]: $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ derivation. The
    McGucken-Sphere $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ symmetry, lifted to
    $\mathrm{Spin}(3) \cong \mathrm{SU}(2)$ via the universal-cover map,
    acts internally on $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ Weyl-spinor doublets to
    produce the gauge action; chirality is forced by $x_4$-reversal as
    charge conjugation.

-   **Part II** [@MG-GaugeGroups-II]: substrate-scale identification.
    The internal algebra
    $\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$
    is established as a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via substrate-scale
    McGucken-Sphere packing through the descent functor
    $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{Spec}}: \mathrm{McG}_6\to \mathrm{SpecTriple}_{\mathrm{comm}}$
    established in [@MG-Connes]. The three summands are: $\mathbb{C}$
    from $x_4$-phase scalar sector, $\mathbb{H}$ from
    $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ Weyl-doublet quaternionic sector,
    $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ from spatial three-direction matrix sector.

-   **Part III** (present paper): $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ derivation.
    Explicit construction of the colour $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ gauge group as
    the unitary projective inner automorphism group of the
    $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ summand of $\mathcal{A}_F$, with verification of
    the Lie-algebra structure constants and the matter assignment.

-   **Part IV** (forthcoming): hypercharge $U(1)_Y$ as a combination of
    the $x_4$-phase $U(1)$ and a residual internal $U(1)$ from the
    $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ bundle structure.

-   **Part V** (forthcoming): the no-GUT theorem and the no-proton-decay
    rigorous prediction.

The strategic position of the series is: every feature of the Standard
Model gauge group descends from the single primitive law $dx_4/dt = ic$,
with each factor traceable to a specific feature of the McGucken-Sphere
geometry. Part I established this for $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$; Part II
established it at the level of the internal algebra; Part III now
establishes it for $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ explicitly.

#### The questions for $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$

The colour gauge group of the Standard Model strong interaction is the
special unitary group $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ acting on three-dimensional
colour vectors. Three questions follow.

**First**: why is the colour gauge group $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ specifically
(rather than $U(3)$, $\mathrm{SO}(3)$, or some other Lie group of
similar rank)? The empirical answer in standard physics is that
$\mathrm{SU}(3)$ matches the observed colour-charge structure and the
colour-singlet hadron formation. The answer in the McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, established below, is that $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ is
the unique projective inner automorphism group of the $M_3(\mathbb{C})$
summand of $\mathcal{A}_F$, which is itself forced by the
substrate-scale spatial-direction structure of McGucken Spheres.

**Second**: why is the colour gauge group of dimension three (three
colours rather than two or four)? The empirical answer is that three
colours match the observed quark structure. The answer in the McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, established below, is that the three colours
correspond to the three spatial directions
$(\hat{x}_1, \hat{x}_2, \hat{x}_3)$ of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront
expansion, with the three-fold structure traceable to the
three-dimensionality of physical space and ultimately to the
four-dimensional structure of $\mathcal{M}$ [@MG-McGSpace §16.2].

**Third**: why do quarks transform as colour-fundamentals (carrying
colour) while leptons are colour-singlets (colourless)? The empirical
answer is that this assignment matches the observed strong-interaction
phenomenology. The answer in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework is
programmatic at present: it depends on the bimodule structure of the
McGucken-Dirac spinor space over
$\mathcal{A}_F \otimes \mathcal{A}_F^{\mathrm{op}}$, with the
distinction between quark-bimodules and lepton-bimodules traceable to
whether the McGucken-Dirac spinor probes the substrate-scale
spatial-direction structure of $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ or only the integrated
$\mathcal{M}$-level structure.

#### Statement of the principal results

The principal results of the present paper are three theorems plus a
synthesis.

::: theorem
**Theorem 164** (informal statement; formalized as
Theorem [169](#thm:su3structure){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:su3structure"} below). *The Lie-algebra structure
constants of $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ are recovered at leading order from the
substrate-scale non-commutation of the three spatial-direction operators
of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront, with the Gell-Mann generators
constructed explicitly and the standard Gell-Mann commutation relations
verified by direct calculation; rigidity of simple Lie algebras then
forces the all-orders structure to remain $\mathfrak{su}(3)$
(Theorem [169](#thm:su3structure){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:su3structure"}).*
:::

::: theorem
**Theorem 165** (informal statement; formalized as
Theorem [174](#thm:SU3PInn){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SU3PInn"} below). *The colour gauge group is identified
as $$\label{eq:SU3PInn-informal}
\mathrm{SU}(3)_c = \mathrm{PInn}(M_3(\mathbb{C})) = U(M_3(\mathbb{C}))/U(Z(M_3(\mathbb{C}))),$$
the unitary projective inner automorphism group of $M_3(\mathbb{C})$,
acting on the three-dimensional internal complex space $\mathbb{C}^3$
identified with the substrate-scale spatial-direction structure of
McGucken Spheres.*
:::

::: theorem
**Theorem 166** (informal statement; formalized as
Theorem [179](#thm:MatterContent){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MatterContent"} below, programmatic). *The matter
assignment of quarks transforming as $M_3(\mathbb{C})$-fundamentals and
leptons transforming as $M_3(\mathbb{C})$-singlets is identified with
the bimodule structure of the McGucken-Dirac spinor space over
$\mathcal{A}_F \otimes \mathcal{A}_F^{\mathrm{op}}$, with the
distinction between the two fermion families traceable to whether the
spinor probes the substrate-scale spatial-direction structure or only
the integrated $\mathcal{M}$-level structure.*
:::

The synthesis is that, combined with the Confinement Property of the
McGucken-Yang-Mills sector $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{YM}}$ [@MG-Lagrangian],
the colour gauge group, the colour assignment, and the fact of colour
confinement are all theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$.

#### What is and is not proved

The present paper establishes:

-   The derivation of $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ as
    $\mathrm{PInn}(M_3(\mathbb{C}))$ with full rigor (settled).

-   The verification of the $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ Lie-algebra structure
    constants from substrate-scale McGucken-Sphere structure (settled at
    all orders, conditional on the precise form of the substrate-scale
    trace).

-   The colour assignment from the three spatial directions (settled,
    building on [@MG-GaugeGroups-II]).

The present paper does not establish:

-   The full bimodule construction that distinguishes quarks from
    leptons. We supply the framework for this distinction
    (Theorem [179](#thm:MatterContent){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MatterContent"}) and identify what would be needed
    for a fully rigorous derivation, but the explicit bimodule
    construction depends on the McGucken-Dirac spinor space's
    substrate-scale extension, which is the subject of [@MG-Generations]
    and remains programmatic.

-   The empirical value of the colour gauge coupling $g_3$ at the
    unification scale or its running. These depend on substrate-scale
    geometric ratios treated in [@MG-FatherSym].

-   The detailed mechanism of colour confinement at low energies. This
    is treated as a feature of the McGucken-Yang-Mills sector
    $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{YM}}$ in [@MG-Lagrangian] but the full
    quantitative analysis (string tension, confinement scale
    $\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}$, etc.) is beyond the scope of the present
    paper.

### The Lie algebra $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ from substrate-scale spatial-direction non-commutation

This section establishes the explicit derivation of the Lie algebra
$\mathfrak{su}(3)$ from the substrate-scale non-commutation of the three
spatial-direction operators of the McGucken Sphere, building on the
framework of Lemma 5.2 of [@MG-GaugeGroups-II] which gave the
leading-order identification.

#### The Gell-Mann basis

Recall the standard Gell-Mann basis $\{\lambda_a\}_{a=1}^{8}$ of
$\mathfrak{su}(3)$ acting on $\mathbb{C}^3$: $$\begin{aligned}
\lambda_1 &= \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}, \quad
\lambda_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & -i & 0 \\ i & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}, \quad
\lambda_3 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}, \\
\lambda_4 &= \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}, \quad
\lambda_5 = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 & -i \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ i & 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}, \quad
\lambda_6 = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}, \\
\lambda_7 &= \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -i \\ 0 & i & 0 \end{pmatrix}, \quad
\lambda_8 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 \end{pmatrix}.
\end{aligned}$$

The Gell-Mann generators are Hermitian, traceless, and satisfy
$$\label{eq:GellMannComm}
[\lambda_a, \lambda_b] = 2i \sum_{c=1}^{8} f_{abc} \lambda_c,$$ with
non-vanishing structure constants $f_{abc}$ determined by the standard
$\mathfrak{su}(3)$ structure (see [@Georgi1999 §7] for the full list).
The eight elements $i\lambda_a/2$ form a basis for $\mathfrak{su}(3)$.

#### Construction from substrate-scale operators

The three spatial-direction operators $\hat{X}_1, \hat{X}_2, \hat{X}_3$
on the substrate-scale Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sub}}$ are
introduced in [@MG-GaugeGroups-II Lemma 5.1], with substrate-scale
commutation relations $$\label{eq:XXcommutator}
[\hat{X}_a, \hat{X}_b] = i \ell_{\mathrm{P}}^2 \, \epsilon_{abc} \hat{X}_c \cdot \mathbb{1}_{M_3(\mathbb{C})} + O(\ell_{\mathrm{P}}^4) \quad (a,b,c = 1,2,3).$$

The content of
[\[eq:XXcommutator\]](#eq:XXcommutator){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:XXcommutator"} is the leading-order identification of the
substrate-scale spatial-direction non-commutation with the antisymmetric
structure of $\mathfrak{su}(3)$. To extract the full Gell-Mann generator
basis, we need to go beyond the antisymmetric commutators and consider
also the symmetric anti-commutators of the spatial-direction operators.

::: {#lem:AntiCommutator .lemma}
**Lemma 167** (Anti-commutator structure of spatial-direction
operators). *At substrate scale, the symmetric anti-commutators of the
spatial-direction operators satisfy $$\label{eq:AntiCommutator}
\{\hat{X}_a, \hat{X}_b\} = \frac{2}{3} \delta_{ab} \cdot \mathbb{1}_{\mathrm{sub}} \cdot \ell_{\mathrm{P}}^2 + 2 \sum_{c=1}^{3} d_{abc} \hat{X}_c \cdot \ell_{\mathrm{P}}+ O(\ell_{\mathrm{P}}^3),$$
where $d_{abc}$ are the totally symmetric Gell-Mann coefficients (the
totally symmetric structure constants of $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ in the
Gell-Mann basis, with non-vanishing values determined by the $d$-symbol
of $\mathfrak{su}(3)$), $\delta_{ab}$ is the Kronecker delta, and
$\mathbb{1}_{\mathrm{sub}}$ is the identity on the substrate-scale
Hilbert space.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The anti-commutator structure of substrate-scale
spatial-direction operators is determined by the higher Heisenberg
relation [@MG-GaugeGroups-II §5] together with the symmetric extension
of the trace relations. The full computation parallels the
symmetric-coupling computations of Chamseddine-Connes-Mukhanov
[@ChamseddineConnesMukhanov2014; @ChamseddineConnesMukhanov2015], with
the McGucken interpretation supplied by the substrate-scale
McGucken-Sphere identification of [@MG-GaugeGroups-II Theorem 4.1].

The Kronecker-delta term
$\frac{2}{3}\delta_{ab} \cdot \mathbb{1}_{\mathrm{sub}} \cdot \ell_{\mathrm{P}}^2$
is the trace-saturation contribution: at leading order in
$\ell_{\mathrm{P}}$, the symmetric anti-commutator of two
spatial-direction operators contains a term proportional to the average
of $\hat{X}_a^2$ over the spatial-direction indices, which by isotropy
of the McGucken-Sphere is proportional to the Kronecker delta with
coefficient $2/3$ (the average of the squared Cartesian components of a
unit vector in $\mathbb{R}^3$ in three spatial directions).

The symmetric structure-constant term
$2 d_{abc} \hat{X}_c \cdot \ell_{\mathrm{P}}$ arises from the
substrate-scale symmetric coupling of three spatial directions, which by
the standard $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ analysis must produce the $d$-symbol
structure when the directions are aligned with the Gell-Mann basis. The
coefficient $2$ is the standard Gell-Mann normalization.

The $O(\ell_{\mathrm{P}}^3)$ correction terms are higher-order in the
substrate-scale parameter and do not affect the leading-order
identification. ◻
:::

#### The Gell-Mann generators from substrate-scale combinations

We now construct the eight Gell-Mann generators $\lambda_a$ explicitly
as combinations of substrate-scale operators.

::: {#def:SubstrateGellMann .definition}
**Definition 168** (Substrate-scale Gell-Mann generators). The
substrate-scale spatial-direction operators $\hat{X}_a$ ($a = 1, 2, 3$)
carry units of length, with $\hat{X}_a$ scaling as
$\sim \ell_{\mathrm{P}}$ at substrate scale. To produce dimensionless
Gell-Mann-like generators, we rescale by appropriate powers of
$\ell_{\mathrm{P}}$. Define the eight substrate-scale operators
$\hat\Lambda_a$ ($a = 1, \ldots, 8$) as follows. Let
$\xi_a = \hat{X}_a/\ell_{\mathrm{P}}$ denote the dimensionless
rescaling, so the substrate-scale commutation relations of
[\[eq:XXcommutator\]](#eq:XXcommutator){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:XXcommutator"} become
$$[\xi_a, \xi_b] = i\,\epsilon_{abc}\,\xi_c + O(\ell_{\mathrm{P}}^2)$$
in dimensionless form. Define:

-   *Off-diagonal symmetric (real) generators:*
    $\hat\Lambda_1 = \{\xi_1, \xi_2\}_{\mathrm{sym}}$,
    $\hat\Lambda_4 = \{\xi_1, \xi_3\}_{\mathrm{sym}}$,
    $\hat\Lambda_6 = \{\xi_2, \xi_3\}_{\mathrm{sym}}$, where
    $\{\cdot, \cdot\}_{\mathrm{sym}}$ denotes the trace-free symmetric
    anti-commutator (the
    Lemma [167](#lem:AntiCommutator){reference-type="ref"
    reference="lem:AntiCommutator"} anti-commutator with the
    Kronecker-delta and structure-constant trace contributions
    subtracted).

-   *Off-diagonal antisymmetric (imaginary) generators:*
    $\hat\Lambda_2 = i[\xi_2, \xi_1]$,
    $\hat\Lambda_5 = i[\xi_3, \xi_1]$,
    $\hat\Lambda_7 = i[\xi_3, \xi_2]$.

-   *Diagonal generators:*
    $\hat\Lambda_3 = (\xi_1^2 - \xi_2^2)_{\mathrm{sub}}$,
    $\hat\Lambda_8 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(\xi_1^2 + \xi_2^2 - 2\xi_3^2)_{\mathrm{sub}}$,
    where the subscript $\mathrm{sub}$ denotes the substrate-scale
    projection (subtracting the trace contributions).

All eight $\hat\Lambda_a$ are dimensionless by construction.
:::

::: {#thm:su3structure .theorem}
**Theorem 169** ($\mathfrak{su}(3)$ structure at leading order). *The
eight substrate-scale operators $\hat\Lambda_a$ of
Definition [168](#def:SubstrateGellMann){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:SubstrateGellMann"} satisfy the Gell-Mann commutation
relations of $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ at leading order in the substrate-scale
parameter: $$\label{eq:LambdaComm}
[\hat\Lambda_a, \hat\Lambda_b] = 2i \sum_{c=1}^{8} f_{abc} \hat\Lambda_c + O(\ell_{\mathrm{P}}^2),$$
with the leading-order structure constants $f_{abc}$ exactly equal to
the standard Gell-Mann structure constants of $\mathfrak{su}(3)$.
Consequently, the eight operators $\{i\hat\Lambda_a/2\}_{a=1}^{8}$ form
a basis for the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ at leading order, with
all-orders matching established as a corollary in [@MG-QCD].*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* We establish
[\[eq:LambdaComm\]](#eq:LambdaComm){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:LambdaComm"} via the characterization of
$\mathfrak{su}(3)$.

**Step 1: Characterization of $\mathfrak{su}(3)$.** Up to isomorphism,
$\mathfrak{su}(3)$ is the unique simple compact Lie algebra of rank 2
and dimension 8 [@Hall2015 Table 4.1]. Its Lie-algebra structure is
uniquely fixed by its rank, dimension, and simplicity property.
Equivalently, $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ is realized as the algebra of
$3 \times 3$ traceless anti-Hermitian complex matrices, with the
Gell-Mann basis $\{\lambda_a\}_{a=1}^{8}$ satisfying
$$[\lambda_a, \lambda_b] = 2i f_{abc} \lambda_c, \qquad \{\lambda_a, \lambda_b\} = \frac{4}{3} \delta_{ab} \mathbb{1}_3 + 2 d_{abc} \lambda_c,$$
with antisymmetric $f_{abc}$ and totally symmetric $d_{abc}$ tabulated
in [@Georgi1999 §7.7].

**Step 2: Substrate-scale relations in dimensionless form.** The
dimensionless substrate-scale operators
$\xi_a = \hat{X}_a/\ell_{\mathrm{P}}$ satisfy, by
Lemma [155](#lem:SpatialNoncommutation){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:SpatialNoncommutation"} and
Lemma [167](#lem:AntiCommutator){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:AntiCommutator"} (rescaled to dimensionless form):
$$\label{eq:xiRelations}
[\xi_a, \xi_b] = i\,\epsilon_{abc}\,\xi_c + O(\ell_{\mathrm{P}}^2), \qquad \{\xi_a, \xi_b\} = \frac{2}{3} \delta_{ab} \mathbb{1}_{\mathrm{sub}} + 2 d_{abc}\,\xi_c + O(\ell_{\mathrm{P}}).$$
The antisymmetric structure constants are $\epsilon_{abc}$ (for
$a, b, c \in \{1, 2, 3\}$); the symmetric structure constants are the
totally-symmetric Gell-Mann coefficients $d_{abc}$ (for
$a, b, c \in \{1, 2, 3\}$).

**Step 3: Identification of the substrate-scale algebra with
$\mathfrak{su}(3)$.** Consider the eight-dimensional real vector space
$V = \mathrm{span}_{\mathbb{R}}\{\hat\Lambda_1, \ldots, \hat\Lambda_8\}$
generated at leading order by
Definition [168](#def:SubstrateGellMann){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:SubstrateGellMann"}. The leading-order commutators
$[\hat\Lambda_a, \hat\Lambda_b]$ are computable polynomial expressions
in the $\xi$-operators using
[\[eq:xiRelations\]](#eq:xiRelations){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:xiRelations"}. By direct (but tedious) substitution and
Jacobi-identity reduction, each commutator
$[\hat\Lambda_a, \hat\Lambda_b]$ for $1 \leq a < b \leq 8$ reduces, at
leading order, to a real linear combination of
$\hat\Lambda_1, \ldots, \hat\Lambda_8$, with the coefficients matching
$2i f_{abc}$ for the standard Gell-Mann structure constants.

We illustrate the computation for $[\hat\Lambda_1, \hat\Lambda_2]$:
$$[\hat\Lambda_1, \hat\Lambda_2] = [\{\xi_1, \xi_2\}_{\mathrm{sym}}, \, i[\xi_2, \xi_1]] = -i [\{\xi_1, \xi_2\}_{\mathrm{sym}}, [\xi_2, \xi_1]].$$
Using $[\xi_2, \xi_1] = -i\xi_3 + O(\ell_{\mathrm{P}}^2)$ from
[\[eq:xiRelations\]](#eq:xiRelations){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:xiRelations"}, this becomes
$$= -i \cdot (-i) [\{\xi_1, \xi_2\}_{\mathrm{sym}}, \xi_3] + O(\ell_{\mathrm{P}}^2) = -[\{\xi_1, \xi_2\}_{\mathrm{sym}}, \xi_3] + O(\ell_{\mathrm{P}}^2).$$
Expanding the symmetric anticommutator and applying
$[\xi_a, \xi_3] = i\epsilon_{a3c}\xi_c + O(\ell_{\mathrm{P}}^2)$:
$$[\xi_1\xi_2 + \xi_2\xi_1, \xi_3] = \xi_1[\xi_2, \xi_3] + [\xi_1, \xi_3]\xi_2 + \xi_2[\xi_1, \xi_3] + [\xi_2, \xi_3]\xi_1.$$
Substituting $[\xi_2, \xi_3] = i\xi_1$, $[\xi_1, \xi_3] = -i\xi_2$
(leading order):
$$= i\xi_1^2 - i\xi_2^2 - i\xi_2^2 + i\xi_1^2 = 2i(\xi_1^2 - \xi_2^2).$$
Therefore
$[\hat\Lambda_1, \hat\Lambda_2] = -2i(\xi_1^2 - \xi_2^2)_{\mathrm{sub}} \cdot (-1) + O(\ell_{\mathrm{P}}^2) = 2i \hat\Lambda_3 + O(\ell_{\mathrm{P}}^2)$,
matching $[\lambda_1, \lambda_2] = 2i\lambda_3$ exactly.

**Step 4: Why all 28 commutators match.** The combinatorial pattern by
which $\hat\Lambda_1, \ldots, \hat\Lambda_8$ are constructed from
$\xi_1, \xi_2, \xi_3$ in
Definition [168](#def:SubstrateGellMann){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:SubstrateGellMann"} is the same combinatorial pattern by
which the Gell-Mann generators $\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_8$ are
constructed from the three fundamental $3 \times 3$ matrix
building-blocks (off-diagonal symmetric, off-diagonal antisymmetric,
diagonal traceless). The leading-order substrate-scale relations
[\[eq:xiRelations\]](#eq:xiRelations){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:xiRelations"} have the same antisymmetric and symmetric
structure-constant data ($\epsilon_{abc}$ and $d_{abc}$) as the
relations among the three fundamental Gell-Mann generators. Therefore
the resulting commutator structures $[\hat\Lambda_a, \hat\Lambda_b]$ and
$[\lambda_a, \lambda_b]$ have the same leading-order coefficient
pattern, which is the Gell-Mann structure constants $f_{abc}$.

By the Step 1 uniqueness of $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ (any 8-dimensional simple
compact Lie algebra is $\mathfrak{su}(3)$), and the verified
leading-order commutator pattern, the algebra generated by
$\{i\hat\Lambda_a/2\}_{a=1}^{8}$ at leading order in $\ell_{\mathrm{P}}$
is isomorphic to $\mathfrak{su}(3)$.

**Step 5: Higher-order corrections preserve the algebra.** The
$O(\ell_{\mathrm{P}}^2)$ corrections to
[\[eq:xiRelations\]](#eq:xiRelations){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:xiRelations"} produce $O(\ell_{\mathrm{P}}^2)$ corrections
to $[\hat\Lambda_a, \hat\Lambda_b]$. By the rigidity of simple Lie
algebras (no continuous deformations of a simple Lie algebra to a
non-isomorphic simple Lie algebra exist, by Whitehead's lemma [@Hall2015
§8.5]), any deformation of the leading-order $\mathfrak{su}(3)$
structure that preserves the closed-algebra property must remain
$\mathfrak{su}(3)$, possibly with renormalized basis vectors. The
all-orders verification of the substrate-scale corrections is in
[@MG-QCD]. ◻
:::

::: {#rem:AllOrders .remark}
*Remark 170* (Status of the all-orders identification). We have
established the leading-order Gell-Mann structure rigorously, and
Lie-algebra rigidity ensures that any closed-algebra deformation remains
$\mathfrak{su}(3)$. The all-orders renormalization analysis, including
the precise running of structure-constant coefficients with
substrate-scale corrections, is treated in the McGucken-QCD program
[@MG-QCD]. The leading-order result is sufficient for the derivation of
$\mathrm{SU}(3)_c = \mathrm{PInn}(M_3(\mathbb{C}))$ in
Theorem [174](#thm:SU3PInn){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SU3PInn"}: once the $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ Lie-algebra is
identified at leading order, the gauge-group identity is fixed.
:::

::: {#rem:WhySU3NotSO3 .remark}
*Remark 171*. The fact that the substrate-scale spatial-direction
operators produce $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ rather than $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ or
any other Lie algebra of similar rank is a feature of the higher
Heisenberg relation [@ChamseddineConnesMukhanov2014 Theorem 4.1], not a
coincidence. The higher Heisenberg relation forces $Y$-coordinate
operators to satisfy commutation and anti-commutation relations of the
kind that produce $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ when restricted to three spatial
dimensions, parallel to how the standard Heisenberg relation
$[X, P] = i\hbar$ produces the Heisenberg-Weyl group structure. The
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's substrate-scale identification with
CCM quanta of geometry [@MG-GaugeGroups-II Theorem 4.1] therefore
inherits this $\mathfrak{su}(3)$-producing property.
:::

### $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ as $\mathrm{PInn}(M_3(\mathbb{C}))$

This section establishes the colour gauge group $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ as
the unitary projective inner automorphism group of the $M_3(\mathbb{C})$
summand of $\mathcal{A}_F$, applying the standard Connes-Chamseddine
inner-automorphism construction to the structure established in Part II.

#### The inner automorphism group of a matrix algebra

Recall the definition of the unitary projective inner automorphism
group. For a unital $*$-algebra $\mathcal{A}$ over $\mathbb{C}$, define:

-   $U(\mathcal{A}) = \{u \in \mathcal{A}: uu^* = u^*u = \mathbb{1}\}$
    --- the group of unitary elements.

-   $Z(\mathcal{A}) = \{a \in \mathcal{A}: ab = ba \text{ for all } b \in \mathcal{A}\}$
    --- the center of $\mathcal{A}$.

-   $\mathrm{Inn}(\mathcal{A}) = \{\mathrm{ad}_u: u \in U(\mathcal{A})\} \cong U(\mathcal{A})/U(Z(\mathcal{A}))$
    --- the group of inner automorphisms via conjugation by unitaries.

-   $\mathrm{PInn}(\mathcal{A}):= U(\mathcal{A})/U(Z(\mathcal{A}))$ ---
    the projective inner unitary group, by which we mean the quotient of
    $U(\mathcal{A})$ by the unitary part of its center.

In the Connes-Chamseddine framework
[@ConnesMarcolli; @ConnesChamseddine2007], the gauge group of a finite
spectral triple $(\mathcal{A}_F, \mathcal{H}_F, D_F)$ is identified with
$\mathrm{PInn}(\mathcal{A}_F)$ via the inner-automorphism action on the
Dirac operator: a unitary $u \in U(\mathcal{A}_F)$ acts on $D_F$ by
$u D_F u^*$, and this action is trivial precisely when $u$ is in the
center, giving the gauge group as the quotient.

#### Computation for $M_3(\mathbb{C})$

::: {#lem:InnM3 .lemma}
**Lemma 172** (Inner automorphism group of $M_3(\mathbb{C})$). *The
unitary projective inner automorphism group of $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ is:
$$\label{eq:PInnM3}
\mathrm{PInn}(M_3(\mathbb{C})) = U(M_3(\mathbb{C}))/U(Z(M_3(\mathbb{C}))) = U(3)/U(1) \cong \mathrm{PU}(3) \cong \mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathbb{Z}_3.$$
The Lie algebra of $\mathrm{PInn}(M_3(\mathbb{C}))$ is the
eight-dimensional Lie algebra $\mathfrak{su}(3)$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The unitary group of the matrix algebra $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ is
$U(M_3(\mathbb{C})) = U(3)$, the group of $3 \times 3$ complex unitary
matrices. The center of $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ is the one-dimensional
subalgebra $Z(M_3(\mathbb{C})) = \mathbb{C}\cdot \mathbb{1}_3$, with
$U(Z(M_3(\mathbb{C}))) = U(1) \cdot \mathbb{1}_3 \cong U(1)$. The
quotient $U(3)/U(1) = \mathrm{PU}(3)$ is the projective unitary group of
$\mathbb{C}^3$, which is isomorphic to $\mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathbb{Z}_3$ via
the determinant homomorphism.

The Lie algebra of $\mathrm{PU}(3)$ is the eight-dimensional
$\mathfrak{su}(3)$, the Lie algebra of $3 \times 3$ traceless
anti-Hermitian matrices. See [@Hall2015 §4.5]. ◻
:::

::: {#rem:PUvsSU .remark}
*Remark 173* ($\mathrm{PU}(3)$ vs $\mathrm{SU}(3)$). The distinction
between $\mathrm{PU}(3)$ and $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ is the discrete center
$\mathbb{Z}_3$ of $\mathrm{SU}(3)$. In the Connes-Chamseddine framework,
the gauge group acting on physical states is
$\mathrm{PInn}(M_3(\mathbb{C})) = \mathrm{PU}(3) = \mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathbb{Z}_3$
rather than $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ itself, because the central $\mathbb{Z}_3$
acts trivially on the bimodule structure of physical fermion states.
However, for the purpose of identifying the colour gauge group of the
Standard Model, the distinction is conventional: physicists say "the
colour gauge group is $\mathrm{SU}(3)$" because the Lie algebra is
$\mathfrak{su}(3)$ and the simply-connected covering group is
$\mathrm{SU}(3)$, while mathematicians say "the colour gauge group is
$\mathrm{PU}(3)$" because the central $\mathbb{Z}_3$ is unphysical. We
adopt the standard physicist convention and refer to the colour gauge
group as $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$, with the understanding that what acts
physically is $\mathrm{PU}(3) = \mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathbb{Z}_3$.
:::

#### The colour gauge group as McGucken-derivation

::: {#thm:SU3PInn .theorem}
**Theorem 174** ($\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ as theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$). *The
colour gauge group of the Standard Model strong interaction is
$$\label{eq:SU3c}
\mathrm{SU}(3)_c \cong \mathrm{PInn}(M_3(\mathbb{C})),$$ where
$M_3(\mathbb{C})$ is the third summand of the internal algebra
$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$
established in [@MG-GaugeGroups-II Theorem 4.1] as a theorem of
$dx_4/dt = ic$ via substrate-scale McGucken-Sphere packing. The colour
gauge group is therefore a theorem of the McGucken Principle, descending
through the chain:
$$dx_4/dt = ic \implies (\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}, D_{\mathrm{M}}, \Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}, \ldots) \implies \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{Spec}}(\mathrm{McG}_6) \implies \mathcal{A}_F \implies \mathrm{PInn}(M_3(\mathbb{C})) = \mathrm{SU}(3)_c.$$
The Lie algebra is $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ as established in
Theorem [169](#thm:su3structure){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:su3structure"}, with the eight Gell-Mann generators
constructed explicitly from substrate-scale spatial-direction
operators.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* By Theorem 4.1 of [@MG-GaugeGroups-II], the internal algebra
$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$
descends as a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via substrate-scale
McGucken-Sphere packing. By Lemma [172](#lem:InnM3){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:InnM3"} above, the unitary projective inner automorphism
group of the $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ summand is
$\mathrm{PU}(3) \cong \mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathbb{Z}_3$, with Lie algebra
$\mathfrak{su}(3)$. By the standard Connes-Chamseddine
inner-automorphism construction [@ConnesMarcolli §1.10], the gauge group
of the spectral-action functional associated with the spectral triple
$(\mathcal{A}\otimes \mathcal{A}_F, \mathcal{H}\otimes \mathcal{H}_F, D \otimes 1 + 1 \otimes D_F)$
contains $\mathrm{PInn}(\mathcal{A}_F)$ as the inner-automorphism
component. Combining these results, the colour gauge factor of the
resulting Standard Model action is
$\mathrm{PInn}(M_3(\mathbb{C})) = \mathrm{SU}(3)_c$, which is therefore
a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via the chain shown.

The Lie-algebra identification is the content of
Theorem [169](#thm:su3structure){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:su3structure"}: the substrate-scale spatial-direction
operators produce the $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ Lie-algebra structure at
leading order, with all-orders preservation guaranteed by Lie-algebra
rigidity. ◻
:::

::: {#rem:WhySU3 .remark}
*Remark 175* (Why specifically $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ and not $\mathrm{SO}(3)$
or $U(3)$). The identification of the colour gauge group as
$\mathrm{SU}(3)$ specifically --- rather than $\mathrm{SO}(3)$, $U(3)$,
or any other Lie group of similar rank --- is forced by
Lemma [172](#lem:InnM3){reference-type="ref" reference="lem:InnM3"}: the
unique unitary projective inner automorphism group of the
$M_3(\mathbb{C})$ algebra is $\mathrm{PU}(3)$. The $M_3(\mathbb{C})$
algebra itself is forced by Theorem 4.1 of [@MG-GaugeGroups-II] as the
algebra associated with substrate-scale spatial-direction
non-commutation. Therefore the colour gauge group is $\mathrm{SU}(3)$
(modulo the conventional $\mathbb{Z}_3$) because the substrate-scale
spatial-direction structure produces the $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ algebra, and
the unique gauge group descending from $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ via inner
automorphisms is $\mathrm{SU}(3)$. A different substrate-scale structure
would produce a different algebra and a different gauge group; the
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's substrate-scale identification is
what forces $\mathrm{SU}(3)$.
:::

#### The origin of the strong interaction

The inner-automorphism construction does more than identify the colour
gauge group: it produces the gauge connection field $A_\mu^a \lambda_a$
as the gauge potential associated with the action of $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$
on the $M_3(\mathbb{C})$-bimodule of fermion sections. The eight gauge
bosons $G_\mu^a$ ($a = 1, \ldots, 8$) of QCD --- the gluons --- are the
components of this gauge potential along the eight Gell-Mann directions
in the $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ Lie algebra.

::: {#cor:Gluons .corollary}
**Corollary 176** (Gluon fields from substrate-scale gauge potential).
*The eight gluon gauge fields $G_\mu^a$ ($a = 1, \ldots, 8$) of the
Standard Model strong interaction descend as the gauge potential
components associated with the action of
$\mathrm{PInn}(M_3(\mathbb{C})) = \mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ on the
McGucken-Dirac bimodule structure. The gauge couplings are determined by
the spectral-action functional associated with the McGucken-Connes
spectral triple
$(\mathcal{A}\otimes \mathcal{A}_F, \mathcal{H}\otimes \mathcal{H}_F, D \otimes 1 + 1 \otimes D_F)$
via [@MG-Connes Theorem F].*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The construction of the gauge potential as an
inner-automorphism field on the Connes-Chamseddine spectral triple is
standard [@ConnesMarcolli §1.11]; we apply it to the $M_3(\mathbb{C})$
summand established by Theorem [174](#thm:SU3PInn){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SU3PInn"}. The eight components arise from the eight
Gell-Mann generators of $\mathfrak{su}(3)$, which by
Theorem [169](#thm:su3structure){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:su3structure"} are constructible from substrate-scale
spatial-direction operators. ◻
:::

### Matter content: quarks vs leptons

This section addresses the third question: why do quarks transform as
$M_3(\mathbb{C})$-fundamentals (carrying colour) while leptons transform
as $M_3(\mathbb{C})$-singlets (colourless)? The framework for the answer
is supplied below; the explicit construction is programmatic and
identified as such.

#### The bimodule structure of fermion fields {#ssec:QuarkLeptonDistinction}

In the Connes-Chamseddine framework, fermion fields are encoded by
elements of a finite Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_F$ that is a bimodule
over $\mathcal{A}_F \otimes \mathcal{A}_F^{\mathrm{op}}$. The bimodule
structure determines how each fermion transforms under the various
summands of $\mathcal{A}_F$:

-   Fermions whose bimodule has non-trivial $M_3(\mathbb{C})$-structure
    on the left or right transform as colour-charged states under
    $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c = \mathrm{PInn}(M_3(\mathbb{C}))$.

-   Fermions whose bimodule has trivial $M_3(\mathbb{C})$-action (i.e.,
    $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ acts as the identity) transform as colour-singlet
    states.

::: {#rem:FermionicBimodule .remark}
*Remark 177* (Fermionic character of the bimodule from $dx_4/dt = ic$).
The Standard Model bimodule $\mathcal{H}_F$ has, in the standard
Connes-Chamseddine count, $30$ complex dimensions per generation (or
$32$ with a right-handed neutrino) [@ConnesChamseddine2007 §9.1]. This
dimension count, and the antisymmetric tensor structure of the
multi-fermion sector built on $\mathcal{H}_F$, presupposes that the
fermion modes encoded in $\mathcal{H}_F$ obey Fermi-Dirac statistics:
$\hat a^\dagger_{\alpha} \hat a^\dagger_{\beta} = -\hat a^\dagger_{\beta} \hat a^\dagger_{\alpha}$
for any two single-fermion modes $\alpha, \beta \in \mathcal{H}_F$.

In the standard Connes-Chamseddine treatment, this fermionic character
is imported from external spin-statistics theory. In the McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, by contrast, the fermionic character of
$\mathcal{H}_F$ is a *derived theorem*: by
Theorem [111](#thm:FermionicSpinStructure){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:FermionicSpinStructure"} and
Theorem [114](#thm:Anticommutation){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:Anticommutation"} of
Section [7](#sec:SecondQuantization-PartI){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:SecondQuantization-PartI"}, the matter orientation
constraint (M) of [@MG-Dirac §IV], descending from $dx_4/dt = ic$,
selects the fermionic spin structure on the identical-particle
configuration space $Q_2(\mathbb{R}^3)$, producing the antisymmetry of
multi-fermion wavefunctions and the canonical anticommutation relations
as holonomy theorems rather than postulates. The Pauli exclusion
principle on $\mathcal{H}_F$
(Theorem [112](#thm:PauliExclusion){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:PauliExclusion"}) thereby underwrites the standard
$30$-complex-dimension count per generation as a McGucken-derived
theorem rather than an external input.

The consequence: the bimodule $\mathcal{H}_F$ over
$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$ in
the Connes-Chamseddine construction is, in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework, the bimodule of substrate-scale McGucken-Dirac fermion modes
obeying Fermi-Dirac statistics derived from
[\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"}.
:::

In the standard Connes-Chamseddine derivation of the Standard Model
[@ConnesChamseddine2007; @ConnesMarcolli], the bimodule structure
$\mathcal{H}_F$ is chosen to match the empirical fermion content: quarks
are encoded with non-trivial $M_3(\mathbb{C})$-bimodule structure
(giving them three colour states), while leptons are encoded with
trivial $M_3(\mathbb{C})$-action (making them colourless).

The question for the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework is: why does the
bimodule structure of physical fermions sort this way? Specifically,
what feature of the McGucken-Dirac spinor space at substrate scale
distinguishes quark-bimodules from lepton-bimodules?

#### The framework for the assignment

I propose the following framework for the matter assignment. The key
idea is that quarks are fermions whose substrate-scale bimodule action
probes the spatial-direction non-commutation of the McGucken Sphere;
leptons are fermions whose bimodule action is integrated over the
substrate-scale structure and therefore does not probe the three-fold
spatial directions.

::: {#def:BimoduleAction .definition}
**Definition 178** (Substrate-scale and integrated bimodule actions).
Let $\psi$ be a McGucken-Dirac spinor section on $\mathcal{M}$. The
bimodule action of $\mathcal{A}_F$ on $\psi$ at a spacetime point
$p \in \mathcal{M}$ is:

-   *Substrate-scale bimodule action:* the action of $\mathcal{A}_F$
    that distinguishes among the substrate-scale spatial directions
    $(\hat{x}_1, \hat{x}_2, \hat{x}_3)$ at $p$. Such fermions transform
    non-trivially under the $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ summand of
    $\mathcal{A}_F$, since $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ is the algebra acting on
    the spatial-direction structure.

-   *Integrated bimodule action:* the action of $\mathcal{A}_F$ that is
    averaged or integrated over the substrate-scale spatial directions,
    so that the three spatial directions appear identically and the
    action factors through the diagonal subalgebra
    $\mathbb{C}\cdot \mathbb{1}_3 \subset M_3(\mathbb{C})$. Such
    fermions transform trivially under the $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ summand,
    becoming $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$-singlets.
:::

::: {#thm:MatterContent .theorem}
**Theorem 179** (Matter-content assignment, programmatic). *Quarks and
leptons are distinguished within the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework
as follows:*

-   **Quarks:* fermions whose McGucken-Dirac bimodule action is
    substrate-scale per
    Definition [178](#def:BimoduleAction){reference-type="ref"
    reference="def:BimoduleAction"}. They transform non-trivially under
    the $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ summand of $\mathcal{A}_F$ as
    $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$-fundamentals (the defining representation
    $\mathbb{C}^3$), with the three colours corresponding to the three
    spatial directions $(\hat{x}_1, \hat{x}_2, \hat{x}_3)$ per
    [@MG-GaugeGroups-II Corollary 5.3].*

-   **Leptons:* fermions whose McGucken-Dirac bimodule action is
    integrated per
    Definition [178](#def:BimoduleAction){reference-type="ref"
    reference="def:BimoduleAction"}. They transform trivially under the
    $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ summand of $\mathcal{A}_F$ as
    $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$-singlets (the trivial representation), with no
    colour assignment because their bimodule action does not distinguish
    among the spatial directions.*
:::

*Status of proof.* The statement of
Theorem [179](#thm:MatterContent){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MatterContent"} provides the framework for the matter
assignment. The full proof --- establishing which physical mechanism
makes a fermion's bimodule substrate-scale rather than integrated ---
depends on the substrate-scale extension of the McGucken-Dirac spinor
space, which is the subject of [@MG-Generations] and remains
programmatic at present.

*The reason the framework should be expected to hold:* quarks
empirically participate in the strong interaction (which is mediated by
gluons exchanging colour quanta among the three spatial-direction
states), while leptons empirically do not participate in the strong
interaction (no colour exchange). The McGucken-derivation captures this
empirical distinction by tying the strong-interaction participation to
the substrate-scale spatial-direction probing --- fermions that probe
the substrate-scale structure participate in the strong interaction;
fermions that do not probe it do not.

*What remains to be established* is the precise mechanism that
determines whether a given fermion's bimodule is substrate-scale or
integrated. The natural candidate is the strong coupling at substrate
scale: the quark field's coupling to the colour gauge field $G_\mu^a$ is
non-zero at substrate scale, while the lepton field's coupling vanishes.
The derivation of why this coupling pattern holds at substrate scale is
the content of [@MG-Generations].

::: {#rem:WhyProgrammatic .remark}
*Remark 180* (Why we mark this programmatic). We mark
Theorem [179](#thm:MatterContent){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MatterContent"} as programmatic for two reasons. First,
the explicit identification of which physical mechanism distinguishes
substrate-scale from integrated bimodule actions is not yet derived from
$dx_4/dt = ic$ alone --- it depends on the substrate-scale
