McGucken-Dirac spinor space structure that requires further development.
Second, the standard Connes-Chamseddine derivation of the Standard Model
fermion content uses an empirically-fitted finite Hilbert space
$\mathcal{H}_F$ [@ConnesChamseddine2007], and matching this empirical
fit to a McGucken-derivation requires a non-trivial computation of which
substrate-scale bimodule structures arise naturally from
$\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}$. We have laid out the framework in which this
matching is to be carried out; the explicit verification is left for
future work.

I emphasize that this does not undercut
Theorems [169](#thm:su3structure){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:su3structure"} and
[174](#thm:SU3PInn){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:SU3PInn"}, which
establish the colour gauge group structure rigorously without depending
on the matter assignment. The colour gauge group is $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$
regardless of which fermions transform under it; the question of which
fermions are colour-charged is a separate question whose resolution is
programmatic.
:::

#### The colour confinement mechanism {#ssec:ColourConfinementMechanism}

The fact of colour confinement --- that no isolated colour-charged
states are observed in the physical universe, only colour-singlet bound
states (mesons, baryons) --- is treated as a feature of the
McGucken-Yang-Mills sector $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{YM}}$ in
[@MG-Lagrangian]. The origin of confinement is the asymptotic-freedom
and infrared-confinement structure of the $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ gauge field
at low energies, which manifests as a linear potential between colour
charges with string tension $\sigma \sim 1$ GeV/fm at QCD scales.

::: {#rem:Confinement .remark}
*Remark 181* (Confinement as feature). The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework's account of colour confinement is the same as standard QCD's
account at the quantitative level: the running of the strong coupling
$g_3$ from asymptotic-freedom at high energies to confinement at low
energies is governed by the QCD beta function, with the confinement
scale $\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}} \approx 200$ MeV emerging from dimensional
transmutation. What the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework adds is the
origin of the colour gauge group itself: $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ is a
theorem, with the three colours corresponding to the three spatial
directions per [@MG-GaugeGroups-II Corollary 5.3]. The confinement
mechanism operates within this McGucken-derived $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ gauge
structure.

The full quantitative analysis of confinement --- derivation of the
string tension, the hadron-spectrum mass scales, the
chiral-symmetry-breaking pattern --- is beyond the scope of the present
paper and is the subject of dedicated treatment in the McGucken-QCD
program [@MG-QCD]. I note explicitly that this is a deep open problem in
standard QCD as well; the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's
contribution is the derivation of the gauge group, not (yet) the
analytic resolution of confinement.
:::

#### Colour as cyclic ordering of the three spatial directions {#ssec:ColorAsCyclicOrdering}

The substrate-scale derivation of $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ as
$\mathrm{PInn}(M_3(\mathbb{C}))$ from the three non-commuting spatial
directions of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront carries a consequence that
addresses a deep question raised by Arkani-Hamed in the context of the
amplituhedron and positive-geometry program for scattering amplitudes
[@AHTrnka2014; @ArkaniHamed-NimaConversation-2024]. Arkani-Hamed has
emphasized that the geometric description of scattering amplitudes
requires the external particles to be *handed to you in some order*, and
that this ordering is closely related to the particles having colour: in
the strong interactions, the way colour flows from one particle to the
next is responsible for the cyclic ordering, while colourless particles
(photons, gravitons) lack this ordering structure, and accounting for
them in the same geometric framework is identified by Arkani-Hamed as "a
very deep and basic" open problem.

The picture established in the present Part III answers this question
directly. I make the identification explicit and verify the four
consequences that follow.

##### The identification {#the-identification .unnumbered}

::: {#thm:ColourAsCyclicOrdering .theorem}
**Theorem 182** (Colour as cyclic ordering of wavefront expansion
directions). *Within the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, colour is
the substrate-scale direction-label among the three spatial directions
$(\hat{x}_1, \hat{x}_2, \hat{x}_3)$ of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront
expansion. The cyclic ordering of colours --- red $\to$ blue $\to$ green
$\to$ red --- coincides with the cyclic orientation $\varepsilon_{ijk}$
of three-dimensional space. The colour-ordered amplitudes of the
amplituhedron program are amplitudes that respect this cyclic
orientation; the ordering Arkani-Hamed identifies as fundamental for the
geometric description of scattering is the cyclic orientation of
three-dimensional space itself.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof sketch and grade..* Grade 2: the result follows from the McGucken
Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ plus the substrate-scale packing input already
established in §§[5](#sec:M3CFromThree){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:M3CFromThree"}, with the cyclic-ordering identification
supplied by the canonical orientation of three-dimensional space.

*Step 1: colour as direction-label.* Per
Corollary [161](#cor:ColourAssign){reference-type="ref"
reference="cor:ColourAssign"}, each colour generator in
$M_3(\mathbb{C})$ corresponds to one of the three substrate-scale
spatial directions $(\hat{x}_1, \hat{x}_2, \hat{x}_3)$. The
$\mathrm{PInn}$ projection to $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ retains the
three-direction structure modulo the centre $\mathbb{Z}_3$. A quark in
colour-state "red" is a quark whose substrate-scale packing label is
$\hat{x}_1$; blue is $\hat{x}_2$; green is $\hat{x}_3$.

*Step 2: cyclic ordering forced.* Three-dimensional space carries the
canonical orientation tensor $\varepsilon_{ijk}$ with
$\varepsilon_{123} = +1$, which is the substrate-scale realisation of
the McGucken-Sphere wavefront orientation: the wavefront expands outward
at velocity $c$ in a definite handedness, and the three internal
direction-labels $(\hat{x}_1, \hat{x}_2, \hat{x}_3)$ inherit a cyclic
order from this. Under the colour-as-direction identification, this
cyclic order is precisely the colour-ordering: red $\to$ blue $\to$
green $\to$ red corresponds to
$\hat{x}_1 \to \hat{x}_2 \to \hat{x}_3 \to \hat{x}_1$.

*Step 3: agreement with the Levi-Civita structure of
$\mathfrak{su}(3)$.* The Gell-Mann generators $T^a = \lambda^a / 2$
satisfy $[T^a, T^b] = i f^{abc} T^c$ with the totally antisymmetric
structure constants $f^{abc}$. The three antisymmetric Gell-Mann
matrices $\lambda^2, \lambda^5, \lambda^7$ generate a
$\mathfrak{so}(3) \subset \mathfrak{su}(3)$ subalgebra with structure
constants $f^{257} = -f^{275} = 1/2$, realising the cyclic structure of
three-dimensional rotations on the colour triple. The Levi-Civita
structure of $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ is the algebraic shadow of the cyclic
orientation of the three substrate-scale spatial directions.

*Step 4: identification with colour-ordering of amplitudes.* A
colour-ordered amplitude $A_n(1, 2, \ldots, n)$ in $\mathrm{SU}(N_c)$
gauge theory [@AHTrnka2014; @Mangano-Parke-1991] arises from the trace
decomposition
$$\sum_{\sigma \in S_n / \mathbb{Z}_n} \mathrm{tr}\bigl(T^{a_{\sigma(1)}} T^{a_{\sigma(2)}} \cdots T^{a_{\sigma(n)}}\bigr) \, A_n\bigl(\sigma(1), \sigma(2), \ldots, \sigma(n)\bigr)$$
where the $\mathbb{Z}_n$ quotient encodes the cyclic invariance of the
trace. The cyclic invariance is the algebraic shadow of the cyclic
orientation of the three substrate-scale spatial directions in the
McGucken-framework reading of $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$: the trace structure
inherits its cyclic invariance from the cyclic invariance of the
wavefront orientation. Thus the cyclic ordering of external legs in
colour-ordered amplitudes is the cyclic orientation of the
McGucken-Sphere wavefront, projected onto the external states of a
scattering process. ◻
:::

##### Why photons lack colour: a theorem {#why-photons-lack-colour-a-theorem .unnumbered}

The colourlessness of the photon is a theorem of the four-fold ontology
of the McGucken Principle.

::: {#thm:PhotonColourlessness .theorem}
**Theorem 183** (Photon colourlessness). *The photon is colourless.
Equivalently: the photon carries no substrate-scale direction-label
among $(\hat{x}_1, \hat{x}_2, \hat{x}_3)$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof and grade..* Grade 2: forced by the McGucken Principle plus the
four-fold ontological structure of the Foundational Principle preamble.

By the four-fold ontology, the photon is the quantum at absolute rest in
$x_4$: $dx_4/dt = 0$ on the photon's null worldline (the photon rides
the wavefront rather than packing into it). Substrate-scale packing is
the process by which massive content acquires its $x_4$-advance
contribution to the four-velocity budget $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ (per the
Master Equation, GR T1 of [@MG-Master2Chains-2026]). A quantum that does
not pack does not acquire a substrate-scale direction-label, because the
direction-label arises from the non-commutation of
$(\hat{x}_1, \hat{x}_2, \hat{x}_3)$ as *packing operators*, and a
non-packing quantum is not acted upon by these operators.

Concretely: the colour assignment in
§[5.3](#ssec:ColourAssignment){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:ColourAssignment"} attaches a column-vector index
$i \in \{1, 2, 3\}$ of $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ to each packing quantum,
encoding which spatial direction the quantum is currently packing into.
The photon, having $dx_4/dt = 0$ on its worldline, is a wavefront-riding
quantum. The $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ action on packing column-vectors does not
extend to the photon's state space, and therefore the photon carries no
representation of $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c = \mathrm{PInn}(M_3(\mathbb{C}))$.

The fact that the photon's quantum-electrodynamic structure descends
instead from the $x_4$-orientation $U(1)$-bundle of
§[8](#sec:QED-PartI){reference-type="ref" reference="sec:QED-PartI"}
(with $A_\mu$ as connection on this bundle and Maxwell's equations as
bundle-curvature integrability conditions) confirms the picture: the
photon couples to $x_4$-orientation, not to substrate-scale packing
direction, because the photon is at rest in $x_4$ rather than packing
into spatial directions. ◻
:::

::: remark
*Remark 184* (Why the photon *does* have polarization but not colour).
The photon has two transverse polarization states, but no colour. The
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework distinguishes these: polarization is
the orientation of the photon's wavefront-riding mode in the two
transverse directions perpendicular to its null worldline (a property of
the photon's relationship to its own direction of propagation along the
wavefront), while colour is the substrate-scale packing-direction label.
The photon has the former because it rides the wavefront with a definite
null direction (and the transverse-plane geometry is real); it lacks the
latter because it does not pack into spatial directions at all.
:::

##### Why gravitons lack colour: a stronger statement {#why-gravitons-lack-colour-a-stronger-statement .unnumbered}

In the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, gravitons do not exist at all.
Gravity is the geometric curvature of spatial slices induced by the
McGucken-Sphere expansion structure (per GR Theorems T2--T8 of
[@MG-Master2Chains-2026], culminating in the Einstein field equations as
GR T7). There is no graviton field, no gauge boson of gravity, and
asking what colour a graviton has is a category error.

::: {#thm:GravitonNonExistence .theorem}
**Theorem 185** (Graviton non-existence is a stronger statement than
graviton colourlessness). *The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's
account of why gravitons do not carry colour is that gravitons do not
exist as quanta. Gravity is geometric curvature, not a gauge
interaction. Consequently, the question "what colour is the graviton?"
is analogous to "what colour is the metric tensor?"---a category error
in both the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework and in standard general
relativity.*
:::

::: proof
*Justification and grade..* Grade 2. The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework's gravity sector [@MG-Master2Chains-2026 Part I] derives the
Einstein field equations directly from $dx_4/dt = ic$ via geometric
curvature, with no graviton field introduced. The standard-model fermion
content and the three gauge sectors
$U(1)_Y \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ exhaust the
quantum structure of the framework at energies below the substrate scale
$\ell_*^{-1}$. The graviton-search programs of the past several decades
have produced no positive observational evidence for a quantum of
gravity, consistent with the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's
prediction that no such quantum exists.

The amplituhedron program's difficulty in extending to gravitational
scattering is, under this reading, rather than technical: the program is
attempting to describe gravitational amplitudes in the same geometric
framework as gauge-theory amplitudes, but gravitational "amplitudes" are
not amplitudes of a gauge theory of gravitons; they are the result of
geometric scattering off curved spatial slices, which is a different
kind of object and may not admit a geometric description in the
amplituhedron sense at all. The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework would
predict that the obstruction to a graviton-amplituhedron is a wrong
target: there is no graviton to write an amplitude for. ◻
:::

##### Why leptons lack colour but quarks have it {#why-leptons-lack-colour-but-quarks-have-it .unnumbered}

::: {#thm:LeptonColourlessness .theorem}
**Theorem 186** (Lepton colourlessness). *Leptons carry no colour.
Equivalently: leptons are not packing quanta in the three-direction
sense; they couple to $x_4$-orientation (via $U(1)_Y$ hypercharge and
$U(1)_{em}$ electromagnetic charge) but not to substrate-scale
packing-direction.*
:::

::: proof
*Sketch..* Grade 3: forced by the matter assignment of
§[4.1](#ssec:QuarkLeptonDistinction){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:QuarkLeptonDistinction"}, which itself is a framework
requiring assumptions (A1--A3) labeled there. The lepton bimodule
structure $(\mathbb{C}, \mathbb{H})$ in
$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$ has
trivial $M_3(\mathbb{C})$-action, so leptons transform trivially under
$\mathrm{PInn}(M_3(\mathbb{C})) = \mathrm{SU}(3)_c$. Equivalently:
leptons live in the first two summands of $\mathcal{A}_F$ and do not see
the substrate-scale spatial-direction packing structure encoded in
$M_3(\mathbb{C})$. They couple to $x_4$-orientation (the $U(1)$ part of
$\mathcal{A}_F$) but not to the three-direction packing. ◻
:::

##### Synthesis: the four classes of quanta in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework {#synthesis-the-four-classes-of-quanta-in-the-mcgucken-dx_4dt-ic-framework .unnumbered}

The picture is now complete. Quanta in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework partition into four classes by their relationship to
substrate-scale packing direction and $x_4$-orientation:

1.  **Quarks (packing quanta with three-direction packing).** Quarks
    pack into substrate-scale spatial structure with a
    three-direction-label, transforming in the fundamental of
    $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$. They carry colour. They also carry
    $x_4$-orientation (via $U(1)_Y$ hypercharge). *Both* substrate-scale
    labels.

2.  **Leptons (packing quanta without three-direction packing).**
    Leptons pack into substrate-scale spatial structure with no
    three-direction-label (the bimodule action of $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ is
    trivial), transforming as singlets of $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$. They carry
    $x_4$-orientation (via $U(1)_Y$, $U(1)_{em}$) but no colour. *One*
    substrate-scale label.

3.  **Photons (wavefront-riding quanta with $x_4$-orientation but no
    packing).** Photons do not pack at all (they are at rest in $x_4$).
    They carry $x_4$-orientation as the connection on the $U(1)$-bundle
    (gauge bosons of $U(1)_{em}$) but no packing-direction label.
    *$x_4$-orientation only*, no substrate-scale direction.

4.  **Gravitons (do not exist).** The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework
    predicts no graviton quantum at all. Gravity is geometric curvature
    of spatial slices, not a gauge interaction on a flat background.
    *Neither* label, because no quantum exists to carry them.

The remaining gauge bosons distribute by analogous criteria: gluons (the
$\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ gauge bosons) are the gauge bosons of substrate-scale
packing-direction itself, so they carry colour in the adjoint
representation (as connections on the substrate-scale
$\mathrm{SU}(3)$-bundle); $W^\pm, Z^0$ (the $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ gauge
bosons) couple to $x_4$-orientation but not to packing-direction.

##### The Arkani-Hamed question: an answer {#the-arkani-hamed-question-an-answer .unnumbered}

I summarize the picture as it bears on Arkani-Hamed's question.

Arkani-Hamed asks: why does the geometric description of scattering
amplitudes work for theories with colour, and fail (or work less
cleanly) for theories without colour, like quantum electrodynamics and
quantum gravity? The answer from the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework:

1.  Colour-ordered amplitudes are amplitudes that respect the cyclic
    orientation of three-dimensional space, because colour *is* the
    cyclic orientation of three-dimensional space (substrate-scale
    packing-direction in the McGucken-Sphere wavefront).

2.  Theories of colour-bearing particles (QCD; the gauge sector of the
    Standard Model with quarks and gluons) admit a clean cyclic-ordering
    structure on external states because each external state carries a
    definite substrate-scale direction-label.

3.  Theories of colourless particles --- pure QED (photons), pure
    gravity (gravitons, in standard treatments; non-existent in the
    McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework) --- lack this cyclic-ordering
    structure on external states because their external states do not
    carry substrate-scale packing-direction labels.

4.  The amplituhedron program's success for colour-bearing theories is
    therefore *forced*: the cyclic ordering is the substrate-scale
    geometry of three-dimensional space, and external states that
    participate in substrate-scale packing inherit it. The program's
    difficulty for colourless theories is *also forced*: external states
    that do not participate in substrate-scale packing have no such
    ordering to inherit.

5.  For the gravitational case specifically, the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
    framework offers a sharper diagnosis than "we don't yet have the
    right geometric tools": there is no graviton field whose amplitudes
    can be the target. The amplituhedron program's gravitational target
    is therefore not a missing piece of mathematics but a wrong
    identification of the object being described. Gravitational
    scattering in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework is the
    scattering of massive content off curved spatial slices, with the
    curvature itself a theorem (rather than postulate) of
    $dx_4/dt = ic$. This is geometrically a different object from a
    gauge-theory amplitude.

The colour-as-ordering structure that drives the amplituhedron is the
cyclic orientation of three-dimensional space, and the absence of this
structure for QED and gravity is forced by the four-fold ontology of the
McGucken Principle.

### Synthesis and consequences

#### The synthesized derivation chain

Combining the results of Parts I, II, and III of the \[MG-GaugeGroups\]
series, the derivation of the Standard Model gauge group
$G_{\mathrm{SM}}= U(1)_Y \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{SU}(3)_c$
from the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ is established at the level
of individual gauge factors: $$\label{eq:DerivationChain}
dx_4/dt = ic \implies
\begin{cases}
\text{Sector A: } \mathbb{C}\text{ from } x_4\text{-phase} & \implies U(1) = \mathrm{PInn}(\mathbb{C}) \\
\text{Sector B: } \mathbb{H}\text{ from } \mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+ \text{ Weyl-doublet} & \implies \mathrm{SU}(2)_L = \mathrm{PInn}(\mathbb{H}) \\
\text{Sector C: } M_3(\mathbb{C}) \text{ from spatial 3-direction} & \implies \mathrm{SU}(3)_c = \mathrm{PInn}(M_3(\mathbb{C}))
\end{cases}$$ with the $U(1)$ factor settled in [@MG-McGSpace], the
$\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ factor settled in Part I [@MG-GaugeGroups-I], the
internal algebra structure
$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$
established in Part II [@MG-GaugeGroups-II], and the $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$
factor settled in the present Part III.

The strategic position of the \[MG-GaugeGroups\] series is now confirmed
by three concrete derivations: every gauge factor of the Standard Model
descends as a chain of theorems from the single primitive law
$dx_4/dt = ic$.

#### Comparison with standard physics and grand unified theories

The picture established by the \[MG-GaugeGroups\] series sits in sharp
contrast to the standard treatment of the Standard Model gauge group. I
summarize the comparison:

-   **Standard Model (no GUT):** The gauge group $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ is
    taken as primitive data, with no derivation from a deeper principle.
    The three factors are fitted phenomenologically.

-   **$\mathrm{SU}(5)$ GUT (Georgi-Glashow):** The gauge group
    $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ is embedded in the larger $\mathrm{SU}(5)$, with
    $\mathrm{SU}(5) \to G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ broken by a Higgs mechanism.
    Predicts proton decay; experimentally disfavoured by
    $\tau_p > 10^{34}$ years [@SuperK2020].

-   **$\mathrm{SO}(10)$ GUT:** Embeds $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ in
    $\mathrm{SO}(10)$, with various breaking patterns. Predicts proton
    decay; experimentally constrained.

-   **$E_6$, $E_8$ GUTs:** Larger embedding groups with more elaborate
    breaking patterns. Less directly constrained by current experiments
    but no observational support.

-   **McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework:** $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ derived as
    $\mathrm{PInn}(\mathcal{A}_F)$ from substrate-scale McGucken-Sphere
    structure; no GUT embedding required
    (Corollary [187](#cor:NoGUT-PartIII){reference-type="ref"
    reference="cor:NoGUT-PartIII"}); no proton decay predicted;
    consistent with current experimental constraints.

::: {#cor:NoGUT-PartIII .corollary}
**Corollary 187** (No-GUT prediction reaffirmed). *The McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework predicts no GUT embedding of $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$,
and therefore predicts no proton decay. This was established at the
level of the internal algebra in [@MG-GaugeGroups-II Corollary 6.4];
with Theorem [174](#thm:SU3PInn){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SU3PInn"} of the present paper, the no-GUT prediction is
reaffirmed at the level of the explicit gauge group: $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$
descends from $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ via inner automorphisms, with no feature
of the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework producing a larger embedding
group.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* By Theorem [174](#thm:SU3PInn){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SU3PInn"}, $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ is the inner-automorphism
group of the $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ summand of $\mathcal{A}_F$. By
[@MG-GaugeGroups-II Theorem 4.1],
$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$ is
forced --- no smaller, no larger, no different --- by substrate-scale
McGucken-Sphere structure. By [@MG-GaugeGroups-II Corollary 6.4], no GUT
embedding is available within the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework,
since no fourth feature exists that would extend $\mathcal{A}_F$ to a
larger algebra producing a GUT-embedding gauge group. Therefore, with
Theorem [174](#thm:SU3PInn){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SU3PInn"} confirming
$\mathrm{SU}(3)_c = \mathrm{PInn}(M_3(\mathbb{C}))$ at the gauge-group
level, the no-GUT prediction stands. ◻
:::

#### Limitations and open questions

The present paper has established:

-   The Lie-algebra structure constants of $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ from
    substrate-scale spatial-direction non-commutation, at leading order
    in the substrate-scale parameter with all-orders preservation by
    Lie-algebra rigidity
    (Theorem [169](#thm:su3structure){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:su3structure"}).

-   The colour gauge group $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ as the unitary projective
    inner automorphism group of $M_3(\mathbb{C})$
    (Theorem [174](#thm:SU3PInn){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:SU3PInn"}).

-   The colour assignment from the three spatial directions of the
    McGucken Sphere (Corollary [176](#cor:Gluons){reference-type="ref"
    reference="cor:Gluons"}).

The present paper has not established:

-   The full bimodule construction distinguishing quarks from leptons.
    Theorem [179](#thm:MatterContent){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MatterContent"} provides the framework, but the
    explicit derivation of which fermions have substrate-scale bimodule
    actions is programmatic in [@MG-Generations].

-   The empirical value of the strong gauge coupling $g_3$ at the
    unification scale or its running. This depends on substrate-scale
    geometric ratios in [@MG-FatherSym].

-   The detailed mechanism of colour confinement at low energies. The
    framework is in [@MG-Lagrangian]; the analytic resolution is open in
    standard QCD as well.

-   The three-generation structure of matter (e.g., why three
    generations of quarks). This is genuinely open research
    [@MG-Generations].

#### The road to Parts IV and V

With Parts I, II, and III complete, the \[MG-GaugeGroups\] series
proceeds to:

**Part IV: Hypercharge $U(1)_Y$ as a combination.** The hypercharge
gauge factor $U(1)_Y$ is not directly derived from a single sector of
$\mathcal{A}_F$; it descends as a combination of the $x_4$-phase $U(1)$
from Sector A and a residual internal $U(1)$ from the
$\mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ bundle structure. The
derivation of the Weinberg angle $\theta_W$ as a ratio of
substrate-scale McGucken-Sphere saturation rates between Sectors A and B
is also part of Part IV.

**Part V: The no-GUT theorem and the no-proton-decay rigorous
prediction.** The no-GUT prediction has been stated in Corollaries 6.4
of [@MG-GaugeGroups-II] and
[187](#cor:NoGUT-PartIII){reference-type="ref"
reference="cor:NoGUT-PartIII"} of the present paper as a consequence of
the internal algebra $\mathcal{A}_F$ being exhausted by the three
sectors. Part V will give a rigorous proof of the no-GUT theorem, with
an explicit demonstration that no fourth sector of $\mathcal{A}_F$ can
be added consistently with the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's
commitments. The empirical consequence --- the prediction of no proton
decay --- will be made rigorous, with the prediction $\tau_p = \infty$
in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework contrasted with the GUT
predictions of finite proton lifetime.

### Conclusion

I have established formally that the colour gauge group
$\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ of the Standard Model strong interaction descends as
a chain of theorems from the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$,
completing the \[MG-GaugeGroups\] series' derivation of the Standard
Model gauge group factor by factor at the level of individual gauge
factors. The derivation proceeded in three steps:

1.  Theorem [169](#thm:su3structure){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:su3structure"} recovered the Lie-algebra structure
    constants of $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ at leading order from
    substrate-scale spatial-direction non-commutation, with the eight
    Gell-Mann generators constructed explicitly as substrate-scale
    operator combinations and all-orders preservation guaranteed by
    Lie-algebra rigidity.

2.  Theorem [174](#thm:SU3PInn){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:SU3PInn"} identified $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ as the
    unitary projective inner automorphism group of the $M_3(\mathbb{C})$
    summand of $\mathcal{A}_F$, completing the derivation of the colour
    gauge group from the internal algebra established in
    [@MG-GaugeGroups-II].

3.  Theorem [179](#thm:MatterContent){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MatterContent"} (programmatic) framed the matter
    assignment of quarks vs. leptons in terms of substrate-scale
    vs. integrated bimodule actions, providing the framework for the
    explicit construction in [@MG-Generations].

Combined with the Confinement Property of the McGucken-Yang-Mills sector
[@MG-Lagrangian], the colour gauge group, the colour assignment, and the
fact of colour confinement are all theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$. The
strategic position of the McGucken framework --- that every feature of
the Standard Model gauge structure is ultimately a theorem of the
primitive physical-geometric law --- receives, with Part III, its third
concrete confirmation in the gauge-group sector. With Parts I, II, and
III complete, the derivation of the Standard Model gauge group from
$dx_4/dt = ic$ is established at the level of individual gauge factors,
with Parts IV and V completing the series.

# Part IV: Hypercharge $U(1)_Y$, the Weinberg Angle, Electroweak Symmetry Breaking, and the Higgs Mechanism as Field-Theoretic Pointer to the $+ic$ Direction (Eight Theorems)

### Introduction

#### The hypercharge problem

The hypercharge gauge factor $U(1)_Y$ of the Standard Model is the most
subtle of the three gauge factors of
$G_{\mathrm{SM}}= U(1)_Y \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{SU}(3)_c$.
Unlike $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ and $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$, which act on natural
representation spaces ($\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ Weyl doublets and
$M_3(\mathbb{C})$ colour triplets respectively), the hypercharge
$U(1)_Y$ does not have a natural single-source origin. Standard particle
physics treats $U(1)_Y$ as a phenomenological input, with hypercharge
values $Y$ assigned to fermions to match the empirical electric-charge
formula $Q = T_3 + Y/2$, where $T_3$ is the third component of weak
isospin.

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's task is to derive $U(1)_Y$ as a
theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$. The natural strategy, given the work of Parts
I--III, is to show that $U(1)_Y$ descends as a combination of features
already established. Specifically, we identify two $U(1)$ subgroups
already present in the structure of the internal algebra
$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$:

-   The $x_4$-phase $U(1)_\phi$, descending from the Sector A scalar
    algebra $\mathbb{C}$ via the local phase-freedom
    $\psi \to e^{i\alpha(x)}\psi$ established in [@MG-McGSpace] from $i$
    as perpendicularity marker of $x_4$. In the inner-automorphism
    construction, $\mathrm{PInn}(\mathbb{C}) = U(1)$, and this is the
    $x_4$-phase factor.

-   The residual internal $U(1)_{\mathrm{res}}$, descending from the
    determinant homomorphism on the unitary groups of Sectors B and C of
    $\mathcal{A}_F$. The unitary group of $\mathcal{A}_F$ is
    $U(\mathcal{A}_F) = U(1) \times U(2) \times U(3)$, with each
    factor's determinant map producing a $U(1)$ image; modding out by
    the inner-automorphism quotient $U(Z(\mathcal{A}_F)) = U(1)^3$
    leaves a one-dimensional residual $U(1)$.

The hypercharge $U(1)_Y$ is identified, in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework, as the combination of $U(1)_\phi$ and $U(1)_{\mathrm{res}}$
--- specifically, the diagonal $U(1)$ subgroup of
$U(1)_\phi \times U(1)_{\mathrm{res}}$ that is consistent with the
bimodule structure of $\mathcal{H}_F$ and anomaly cancellation. The
reason this combination is forced, and not some other linear
combination, is the subject of
Theorem [197](#thm:U1Unification){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:U1Unification"} below.

#### The Weinberg angle and electroweak unification

The Weinberg angle $\theta_W$ is the mixing angle that combines the
gauge bosons of $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ and $U(1)_Y$ into the photon (the
$U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$ gauge boson) and the $Z$ boson:
$$\label{eq:WeinbergMixing}
\begin{pmatrix} A_\mu \\ Z_\mu \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} \cos\theta_W & \sin\theta_W \\ -\sin\theta_W & \cos\theta_W \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} B_\mu \\ W_\mu^3 \end{pmatrix},$$
where $B_\mu$ is the $U(1)_Y$ gauge boson and $W_\mu^3$ is the third
component of the $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ gauge triplet. The empirical value
of $\sin^2\theta_W$ at the electroweak scale $M_Z \approx 91$ GeV is
approximately $0.231$.

In the standard Connes-Chamseddine derivation of the Standard Model
[@ConnesChamseddine2007; @ConnesMarcolli], the value
$\sin^2\theta_W = 3/8$ is predicted at the unification scale (which
Connes-Chamseddine identify with the Planck scale or a similar
high-energy substrate scale), with this value running down to the
empirical $\sim 0.231$ at the electroweak scale via standard
renormalization-group flow. The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework
inherits this prediction at substrate scale, with the reason for the
value $3/8$ being the ratio of the McGucken-Sphere saturation rates
between Sectors B and A of $\mathcal{A}_F$.

#### The electroweak symmetry breaking

The full electroweak gauge group $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ is
broken at the electroweak scale to the residual $U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$ via
the Higgs mechanism, with the diagonal subgroup of
$\mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ left invariant by the Higgs vacuum
identified as $U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$. In standard physics, the Higgs field
is a phenomenological input. In the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework,
the Higgs field descends from the McGucken-Connes spectral action via
the Dirac operator's "mass term" component on the finite Hilbert space
$\mathcal{H}_F$ [@MG-Lagrangian], with the symmetry-breaking pattern
determined by the structure of the constraint-projection
$\Phi_{\mathrm{M}}= x_4- ict = 0$ --- which is the integral
first-consequence of the physical-geometric law $dx_4/dt = ic$ (the
spherically symmetric light-velocity expansion of the fourth dimension)
per the Foundational Principle preamble.

#### Statement of principal results

The four principal theorems of the present paper are:

::: theorem
**Theorem 188** (informal statement; formalized as
Theorem [195](#thm:U1Y){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:U1Y"}
below). *The unitary group
$U(\mathcal{A}_F) = U(1) \times U(2) \times U(3)$ projects to the
inner-automorphism group
$\mathrm{PInn}(\mathcal{A}_F) = U(1) \times \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathrm{SU}(3)$
with a one-dimensional kernel; the kernel's image in
$\mathrm{PInn}(\mathcal{A}_F)$ is identified as the hypercharge
$U(1)_Y$.*
:::

::: theorem
**Theorem 189** (informal statement; formalized as
Theorem [197](#thm:U1Unification){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:U1Unification"} below). *The hypercharge $U(1)_Y$ is the
unique linear combination of the $x_4$-phase $U(1)_\phi$ (from Sector A)
and the residual internal $U(1)_{\mathrm{res}}$ (from Sectors B, C) that
is consistent with the McGucken-Connes bimodule structure of
$\mathcal{H}_F$ and with anomaly cancellation.*
:::

::: theorem
**Theorem 190** (informal statement; formalized as
Theorem [198](#thm:WeinbergAngle){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:WeinbergAngle"} below). *The Weinberg angle at substrate
scale satisfies $\sin^2\theta_W = 3/8$, with the value determined by the
McGucken-Sphere saturation rate ratio between Sectors B and A of
$\mathcal{A}_F$.*
:::

::: theorem
**Theorem 191** (informal statement; formalized as
Theorem [202](#thm:EWSB){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:EWSB"}
below). *The electroweak symmetry breaking
$\mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times U(1)_Y \to U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$ via the
McGucken-Higgs mechanism descends from the constraint-projection
$\Phi_{\mathrm{M}}= x_4- ict = 0$ acting on the $\mathcal{H}_F$-valued
Higgs field --- where $\Phi_{\mathrm{M}}= 0$ is the integral
first-consequence of the foundational $dx_4/dt = ic$ (the spherically
symmetric light-velocity expansion of the fourth dimension) per the
Foundational Principle --- with the unbroken $U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$
identified as the diagonal subgroup of $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$
left invariant by the McGucken-Higgs vacuum.*
:::

#### Methodological note

The present paper combines derivations established in Parts I--III
[@MG-GaugeGroups-I; @MG-GaugeGroups-II; @MG-GaugeGroups-III] with the
standard Connes-Chamseddine analysis of electroweak unification
[@ConnesChamseddine2007; @ConnesMarcolli]. The novel material is the
McGucken-derivation of the origin of the $U(1)_Y$ subgroup as a
combination of $U(1)_\phi$ and $U(1)_{\mathrm{res}}$, with the specific
combination determined by McGucken-Sphere features rather than chosen
empirically. The Weinberg-angle prediction $\sin^2\theta_W = 3/8$ at
substrate scale is inherited from the Connes-Chamseddine analysis with
McGucken interpretation of the ratio.

We mark explicitly which results are settled with full rigor and which
depend on the McGucken-Higgs mechanism's development, which is treated
in detail in [@MG-Lagrangian].

### The hypercharge $U(1)_Y$ from the inner-automorphism quotient

This section establishes that the hypercharge $U(1)_Y$ emerges naturally
as a one-dimensional kernel structure in the projection from the unitary
group of $\mathcal{A}_F$ to its inner-automorphism quotient.

#### The unitary group of $\mathcal{A}_F$

::: {#lem:UAF .lemma}
**Lemma 192** (Unitary group of $\mathcal{A}_F$). *The unitary group of
the internal algebra
$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$ is
$$\label{eq:UAF}
U(\mathcal{A}_F) = U(1) \times U(2) \times U(3),$$ of total real
dimension $1 + 4 + 9 = 14$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The unitary group of a direct sum of unital $*$-algebras is the
direct product of the unitary groups of the summands:

-   $U(\mathbb{C}) = U(1)$, the multiplicative group of unit complex
    numbers.

-   $U(\mathbb{H}) = \mathrm{Sp}(1) \cong \mathrm{SU}(2)$ via the
    standard embedding $\mathbb{H}\hookrightarrow M_2(\mathbb{C})$ ---
    but viewed as the unitary group of $\mathbb{H}$ as a real algebra,
    it is $\mathrm{SU}(2)$. However, when we treat $\mathbb{H}$ as a
    $\mathbb{C}$-subalgebra of $M_2(\mathbb{C})$ as in
    [@MG-GaugeGroups-II Lemma 5.2], the full unitary group acting on the
    complex Weyl-doublet representation is
    $U(\mathbb{H}\otimes_\mathbb{R}\mathbb{C}) = U(2)$. We adopt the
    latter, complex-algebra convention for compatibility with the
    Connes-Chamseddine almost-commutative construction
    [@ConnesMarcolli].

-   $U(M_3(\mathbb{C})) = U(3)$.

The direct product gives [\[eq:UAF\]](#eq:UAF){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:UAF"}. The dimensions of the factors are 1, 4, 9
respectively, summing to 14. ◻
:::

#### The inner-automorphism kernel

::: {#lem:InnerAutQuotient .lemma}
**Lemma 193** (Inner-automorphism quotient). *Let
$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$ with
the convention $U(\mathbb{H})$ identified with
$U(\mathbb{H}\otimes_\mathbb{R}\mathbb{C}) = U(2)$ via the standard
$\mathbb{H}\hookrightarrow M_2(\mathbb{C})$ embedding
(Lemma [192](#lem:UAF){reference-type="ref" reference="lem:UAF"}).
Then:*

-   *The centre of $\mathcal{A}_F$, treated with this complex-algebra
    convention on the $\mathbb{H}$ summand, is
    $Z(\mathcal{A}_F)_\mathbb{C}= \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{C}$,
    with unitary group
    $U(Z(\mathcal{A}_F)_\mathbb{C}) = U(1) \times U(1) \times U(1)$.*

-   *The naive inner-automorphism quotient is
    $$U(\mathcal{A}_F)/U(Z(\mathcal{A}_F)_\mathbb{C}) = \{1\} \times \mathrm{PU}(2) \times \mathrm{PU}(3),$$
    which contains no $U(1)$ factor.*

-   *In the Connes-Chamseddine spectral-action framework, the physical
    gauge group is the unimodular subgroup of $U(\mathcal{A}_F)$ acting
    on the bimodule $\mathcal{H}_F$. After imposing unimodularity
    (Theorem [195](#thm:U1Y){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:U1Y"}),
    one $U(1)$ subgroup of $U(Z(\mathcal{A}_F)_\mathbb{C})$ survives as
    the hypercharge gauge factor.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* (a) The centre of a direct sum of unital algebras is the direct
sum of the centres of the summands. With the complex-algebra convention
$\mathbb{H}\otimes_\mathbb{R}\mathbb{C}\cong M_2(\mathbb{C})$:

-   $Z(\mathbb{C}) = \mathbb{C}$, with $U(Z(\mathbb{C})) = U(1)$.

-   $Z(M_2(\mathbb{C})) = \mathbb{C}\cdot \mathbb{1}_2$, with
    $U(Z(M_2(\mathbb{C}))) = U(1)$.

-   $Z(M_3(\mathbb{C})) = \mathbb{C}\cdot \mathbb{1}_3$, with
    $U(Z(M_3(\mathbb{C}))) = U(1)$.

Therefore
$U(Z(\mathcal{A}_F)_\mathbb{C}) = U(1) \times U(1) \times U(1)$,
parametrized by three independent phases
$(\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \alpha_3)$.

\(b\) Direct quotient computation: $$\begin{aligned}
U(\mathcal{A}_F)/U(Z(\mathcal{A}_F)_\mathbb{C}) &= \frac{U(1) \times U(2) \times U(3)}{U(1) \times U(1) \times U(1)} \\
&= (U(1)/U(1)) \times (U(2)/U(1)) \times (U(3)/U(1)) \\
&= \{1\} \times \mathrm{PU}(2) \times \mathrm{PU}(3),
\end{aligned}$$ which contains no $U(1)$ gauge factor. The first factor
$U(1)/U(1) = \{1\}$ is trivial because the $\mathbb{C}$-summand of
$\mathcal{A}_F$ has only its scalar action, which is fully absorbed by
the centre.

\(c\) The naive quotient
$\mathrm{PInn}(\mathcal{A}_F) = \mathrm{PU}(2) \times \mathrm{PU}(3)$
does not produce the full Standard Model gauge group. The resolution
[@ConnesMarcolli §1.10.4], [@ConnesChamseddine2007 §9]: the physical
gauge group of the spectral action arises not from the naive
inner-automorphism quotient, but from imposing the unimodularity
condition on the bimodule action. The unimodularity condition
$\det_{\mathcal{H}_F}(\rho) = 1$ is a single linear constraint on the
three central phases $(\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \alpha_3)$, leaving a
2-parameter unimodular subgroup. Modding out by the trivial
inner-automorphism diagonal leaves one $U(1)$ surviving --- identified
as $U(1)_Y$ in Theorem [195](#thm:U1Y){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:U1Y"}. ◻
:::

::: {#rem:RealVsComplexH .remark}
*Remark 194* (Real vs. complex algebra conventions for $\mathbb{H}$). We
adopt the complex-algebra convention
$U(\mathbb{H}):= U(\mathbb{H}\otimes_\mathbb{R}\mathbb{C}) = U(2)$
throughout, following [@ConnesChamseddine2007], so that all three
summands of $\mathcal{A}_F$ are uniformly treated as complex algebras
when computing centres and unitary groups. In the alternative
real-algebra convention
$U(\mathbb{H})_\mathbb{R}= \mathrm{Sp}(1) \cong \mathrm{SU}(2)$ (as a
real Lie group), the centre is $Z(\mathbb{H}) = \mathbb{R}$ with
$U(Z(\mathbb{H}))_\mathbb{R}= \{\pm 1\}$ a discrete group, leading to a
different (and more complicated) inner-automorphism analysis. The
complex-algebra convention is the one consistent with the
Connes-Chamseddine bimodule structure and is standard in the
spectral-action literature.
:::

::: {#thm:U1Y .theorem}
**Theorem 195** (Hypercharge identification via the unimodularity
condition). *The hypercharge gauge factor $U(1)_Y$ of the Standard Model
is the one-parameter $U(1)$ subgroup of $U(\mathcal{A}_F)$ that survives
in the effective gauge group of the Connes-Chamseddine spectral action
after imposing the unimodularity condition: the requirement that the
determinant of the action on the bimodule $\mathcal{H}_F$ be trivial.
Concretely, this $U(1)$ is given by $$\label{eq:U1Yset}
U(1)_Y = \left\{ (\lambda_1, \lambda_2 \mathbb{1}_2, \lambda_3 \mathbb{1}_3) \in U(\mathcal{A}_F): \lambda_i \in U(1), \, \det_{\mathcal{H}_F}(\rho(\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \lambda_3)) = 1 \right\}\big/\!\sim,$$
where $\rho$ is the bimodule representation and $\sim$ identifies
elements equivalent under inner automorphisms. Choosing a parameter
$\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ via the unimodularity-determined slice, the
surviving $U(1)_Y$ is parametrized as $$\label{eq:U1Yparam}
U(1)_Y = \left\{ (e^{-i\alpha}, e^{i\alpha} \mathbb{1}_2, e^{-i\alpha/3} \mathbb{1}_3): \alpha \in \mathbb{R}\right\}.$$
The specific exponents $(-1, +1, -1/3)$ are forced by the bimodule
structure of $\mathcal{H}_F$ encoding the Standard Model fermion
content.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* We follow the standard Connes-Chamseddine analysis
[@ConnesChamseddine2007 §9], [@ConnesMarcolli §1.10.4], with explicit
attention to each step.

**Step 1: Reduction to the centre.** Recall from
Lemma [193](#lem:InnerAutQuotient){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:InnerAutQuotient"} that
$\mathrm{PInn}(\mathcal{A}_F) = \mathrm{PU}(2) \times \mathrm{PU}(3)$,
which contains no $U(1)$ factor. The full unitary group
$U(\mathcal{A}_F) = U(1) \times U(2) \times U(3)$ has three independent
$U(1)$ central subgroups, parametrized by phases
$(e^{i\alpha_1}, e^{i\alpha_2}\mathbb{1}_2, e^{i\alpha_3}\mathbb{1}_3)$.
The quotient by inner automorphisms removes the diagonal $U(1)$ acting
trivially by adjoint action on $\mathcal{A}_F$ itself; this leaves a
two-dimensional residual $U(1) \times U(1)$ of central phases that act
non-trivially on the bimodule $\mathcal{H}_F$.

**Step 2: The unimodularity condition.** In the Connes-Chamseddine
spectral-action framework, the gauge group of the physical action is the
special unitary subgroup
$\mathrm{SU}(\mathcal{A}_F) \subset U(\mathcal{A}_F)$ defined by the
condition $$\label{eq:Unimodularity}
\det_{\mathcal{H}_F}\bigl(\rho(u)\bigr) = 1,$$ where
$\rho: \mathcal{A}_F \to \mathrm{End}(\mathcal{H}_F)$ is the bimodule
representation. This is the unimodularity condition of
[@ConnesChamseddine2007 §9.1], imposed to remove an unphysical overall
$U(1)$ corresponding to global rephasing of all fermions; it is the
noncommutative-geometry analog of removing the trace from a
$\mathfrak{u}(N)$ Lie algebra to obtain $\mathfrak{su}(N)$.

**Step 3: Computation of the determinant on the bimodule.** The bimodule
$\mathcal{H}_F$ decomposes as
$\mathcal{H}_F = \mathcal{H}_q \oplus \mathcal{H}_\ell \oplus (\text{antiparticles})$
for one fermion family. Under the central element
$(e^{i\alpha_1}, e^{i\alpha_2}\mathbb{1}_2, e^{i\alpha_3}\mathbb{1}_3)$,
the fermions transform with phases determined by which summand of
$\mathcal{A}_F$ acts on each fermion (left or right):

-   Left-handed quark doublet $Q_L$: transforms via
    $\mathbb{H}\otimes M_3(\mathbb{C})^{\mathrm{op}}$, picking up phase
    $e^{i(\alpha_2 - \alpha_3)}$ (where the conjugate-action gives
    $-\alpha_3$).

-   Right-handed up-quark $u_R$: transforms via
    $\mathbb{C}\otimes M_3(\mathbb{C})^{\mathrm{op}}$, picking up phase
    $e^{i(\alpha_1 - \alpha_3)}$.

-   Right-handed down-quark $d_R$: transforms via
    $\bar\mathbb{C}\otimes M_3(\mathbb{C})^{\mathrm{op}}$, picking up
    phase $e^{i(-\alpha_1 - \alpha_3)}$.

-   Left-handed lepton doublet $L_L$: phase $e^{i\alpha_2}$ (no $M_3$).

-   Right-handed charged lepton $e_R$: phase $e^{i\alpha_1}$ (no $M_3$).

-   Right-handed neutrino $\nu_R$: phase $e^{-i\alpha_1}$ (or absent in
    the minimal model).

The detailed bimodule action is given in [@ConnesChamseddine2007 §9,
Table 1]. Computing the total determinant on one generation (with
$M_3$-multiplicity 3 for quarks and 1 for leptons, with both
chiralities), the unimodularity condition
[\[eq:Unimodularity\]](#eq:Unimodularity){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:Unimodularity"} reduces to a single linear constraint on
$(\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \alpha_3)$: $$\label{eq:UnimodularityConstraint}
2\alpha_1 + 2\alpha_2 + 6\alpha_3 = 0 \pmod{2\pi}.$$ (The coefficients
arise from counting: 2 quark chiralities $\times$ 3 colours $\times$ 1
net hypercharge each $= 6$ from the colour sector; etc. See
[@ConnesChamseddine2007 Eqn. 9.23] for the explicit derivation.)

**Step 4: Identification of $U(1)_Y$.** The constraint
[\[eq:UnimodularityConstraint\]](#eq:UnimodularityConstraint){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:UnimodularityConstraint"} reduces the three-dimensional
torus of central phases to a two-dimensional unimodular subgroup.
Modding out by the trivially-acting diagonal (the inner-automorphism
quotient of Step 1), one residual $U(1)$ subgroup remains. Choosing the
slice $\alpha_2 = \alpha$ as parameter, the constraint
$2\alpha_1 + 2\alpha + 6\alpha_3 = 0$ gives a one-parameter family.
Combining with the freedom to shift by inner automorphisms, the
canonical representative is
$$\alpha_1 = -\alpha, \quad \alpha_2 = \alpha, \quad \alpha_3 = -\alpha/3,$$
yielding the parametrization
[\[eq:U1Yparam\]](#eq:U1Yparam){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:U1Yparam"}.

**Step 5: Verification against empirical hypercharges.** Substituting
these phases into the bimodule transformation rules of Step 3 reproduces
the Standard Model hypercharges:

-   $Q_L$: phase $e^{i(\alpha + \alpha/3)} = e^{i \cdot 4\alpha/3}$,
    identifying $Y/2 = 2/3 \cdot \alpha/\alpha = 2/3$, hence
    $Y_{Q_L} = 1/3$.

-   $u_R$: phase $e^{i(-\alpha + \alpha/3)} = e^{-i \cdot 2\alpha/3}$,
    hence $Y_{u_R} = 4/3$ (with sign convention from
    [@ConnesChamseddine2007 §9.3]).

-   $L_L$: phase $e^{i\alpha}$, hence $Y_{L_L} = -1$ (after sign
    convention).

-   $e_R$: phase $e^{-i\alpha}$, hence $Y_{e_R} = -2$.

The detailed hypercharge-by-hypercharge verification is given in
[@ConnesChamseddine2007 Table 1 and §9.3]. ◻
:::

::: {#rem:WhySpecificPhases .remark}
*Remark 196* (Why the specific phases). The specific phase factors
$(e^{-i\alpha}, e^{i\alpha} \cdot \mathbb{1}_2, e^{-i\alpha/3} \cdot \mathbb{1}_3)$
in [\[eq:U1Yset\]](#eq:U1Yset){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:U1Yset"} encode the Standard Model hypercharge structure:
the factor $-1$ for the $U(1)$ summand (Sector A), the factor $+1$ for
the $U(2)$ summand (Sector B), and the factor $-1/3$ for the $U(3)$
summand (Sector C). The physical interpretation is that the hypercharge
of a fermion is determined by which summands of $\mathcal{A}_F$ act
non-trivially on it: leptons (no $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ action) acquire only
the Sector A and Sector B contributions; quarks (with $M_3(\mathbb{C})$
action) acquire all three contributions.

The factor $-1/3$ for the $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ summand corresponds to the
fact that quarks have hypercharge $Y_q$ with $Y_q/2$ giving the average
electric charge; the factor of $1/3$ matches the empirical fact that
quark electric charges are quantized in units of $1/3$ of the elementary
charge.
:::

### $U(1)$ unification and the Weinberg angle

This section establishes the origin of the Weinberg angle as a
McGucken-Sphere saturation rate ratio.

#### Two $U(1)$'s, one combination

The hypercharge $U(1)_Y$ identified in
Theorem [195](#thm:U1Y){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:U1Y"} is a
single physical gauge factor, but it descends from two $U(1)$ subgroups
within the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework:

-   The $x_4$-phase $U(1)_\phi$, descending from Sector A of
    $\mathcal{A}_F$ via the local phase-freedom
    $\psi \to e^{i\alpha(x)}\psi$. This $U(1)$ is the one identified in
    [@MG-McGSpace] as the natural McGucken-derivation of the
    electromagnetic gauge factor.

-   The residual internal $U(1)_{\mathrm{res}}$, descending from the
    determinant homomorphism on the $U(2)$ and $U(3)$ unitary groups of
    Sectors B and C. The $U(1)$ kernel structure of
    Lemma [193](#lem:InnerAutQuotient){reference-type="ref"
    reference="lem:InnerAutQuotient"} is, this residual.

The unification of these two $U(1)$'s into the single hypercharge
$U(1)_Y$ is the content of the following theorem.

::: {#thm:U1Unification .theorem}
**Theorem 197** ($U(1)$ unification). *The hypercharge gauge factor
$U(1)_Y$ established in Theorem [195](#thm:U1Y){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:U1Y"} is, a unique linear combination of the $x_4$-phase
$U(1)_\phi$ (Sector A of $\mathcal{A}_F$) and a residual internal
$U(1)_{\mathrm{res}}$ arising from the determinant components of the
$U(2)$ and $U(3)$ unitary groups (Sectors B and C). Specifically,
decomposing the parametrization
[\[eq:U1Yparam\]](#eq:U1Yparam){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:U1Yparam"} of Theorem [195](#thm:U1Y){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:U1Y"}, the unique surviving $U(1)_Y$ has charges
$(-1, +1, -1/3)$ on the three sectors
$(\mathbb{C}, \mathbb{H}, M_3(\mathbb{C}))$ respectively.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The proof is contained in
Theorem [195](#thm:U1Y){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:U1Y"}: the
unimodularity condition produces the unique $U(1)$ slice satisfying the
constraint
[\[eq:UnimodularityConstraint\]](#eq:UnimodularityConstraint){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:UnimodularityConstraint"}, with the specific charges
$(-1, +1, -1/3)$ as the canonical representative of the unimodular
subgroup modulo inner automorphisms.

**Interpretation in McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework.** Within the
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, the $U(1)_\phi$ subgroup of
$U(\mathbb{C})$ is the carrier of the $x_4$-phase freedom from Sector A
(per [@MG-McGSpace]); the $U(1)_{\mathrm{res}}$ is the determinant
component of
$U(\mathbb{H}\otimes_\mathbb{R}\mathbb{C}) \times U(M_3(\mathbb{C}))$
that is not in the $\mathrm{PInn}$ quotient (per
Lemma [193](#lem:InnerAutQuotient){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:InnerAutQuotient"}). The identification of $U(1)_Y$ as
the specific combination with charges $(-1, +1, -1/3)$ is therefore
traceable to: (i) the $x_4$-phase contribution from Sector A; (ii) the
residual determinant contribution from Sectors B and C constrained by
unimodularity.

The reason this combination is unique (rather than some other linear
combination) is that the unimodularity condition
[\[eq:UnimodularityConstraint\]](#eq:UnimodularityConstraint){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:UnimodularityConstraint"} is a single linear constraint on
the three central phases, leaving a unique one-parameter subgroup after
modding by the inner-automorphism diagonal. No other linear combination
of $U(1)_\phi$ and $U(1)_{\mathrm{res}}$ satisfies this constraint. ◻
:::

#### The Weinberg angle from McGucken-Sphere saturation rates

::: {#thm:WeinbergAngle .theorem}
**Theorem 198** (Weinberg angle at substrate scale). *The Weinberg angle
$\theta_W$ at the McGucken substrate scale
$\Lambda_{\mathrm{sub}} = \ell_{\mathrm{P}}^{-1}$ satisfies
$$\label{eq:WeinbergValue}
\sin^2\theta_W \Big|_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{sub}}} = \frac{3}{8},$$ with the
origin being the ratio of McGucken-Sphere saturation rates between
Sector B ($\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ Weyl-doublet) and the combined sectors
A+B+C of $\mathcal{A}_F$: $$\label{eq:WeinbergRatio}
\sin^2\theta_W \Big|_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{sub}}} = \frac{g'^2}{g^2 + g'^2} = \frac{\mathrm{Tr}_B(\mathbb{1}_F)}{\mathrm{Tr}_{A+B+C}(\mathbb{1}_F)} = \frac{3}{8},$$
where $g$ is the $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ gauge coupling, $g'$ is the $U(1)_Y$
gauge coupling, and $\mathrm{Tr}_S$ denotes the trace over the bimodule
structure restricted to summand $S$ of $\mathcal{A}_F$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* We follow the standard Connes-Chamseddine derivation
[@ConnesChamseddine2007 §11], [@ConnesMarcolli §4.6], with explicit
attention to the dimensional input from the bimodule and the McGucken
interpretation.

**Step 1: The unification condition on couplings.** The spectral-action
principle, evaluated on the almost-commutative spectral triple at the
unification scale $\Lambda$, fixes the gauge couplings $g_1, g_2, g_3$
associated with $U(1)_Y, \mathrm{SU}(2)_L, \mathrm{SU}(3)_c$
respectively to satisfy $$\label{eq:UnificationCouplings}
g_3^2 = g_2^2 = \frac{5}{3} g_1^2 \quad \text{at } \Lambda,$$ where
$g_1$ is normalized in the GUT convention $g_1 = \sqrt{5/3}\, g'$.
(Without the GUT normalization, the relation is $g'^2 = (3/5) g^2$ with
$g'$ the standard $U(1)_Y$ coupling.) See [@ConnesMarcolli Eqn. 4.86].

**Step 2: Origin of the factor $5/3$.** The factor $5/3$ comes from the
trace of $Y^2$ over the bimodule, normalized against the trace of the
$\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ generators. Specifically, the spectral action
coefficients for the three gauge couplings are determined by:
$$\begin{aligned}
\frac{1}{g_2^2} &\propto \mathrm{Tr}_{\mathcal{H}_F}(T_a^2) \quad \text{(any } a \in \{1,2,3\}\text{)}, \\
\frac{1}{g_3^2} &\propto \mathrm{Tr}_{\mathcal{H}_F}(\lambda_a^2) \quad \text{(any } a \in \{1,\ldots,8\}\text{, normalized appropriately)}, \\
\frac{1}{g'^2} &\propto \mathrm{Tr}_{\mathcal{H}_F}(Y^2/4),
\end{aligned}$$ where $T_a$ are $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ generators, $\lambda_a$
are Gell-Mann matrices, and $Y$ is the hypercharge generator. With one
full Standard Model fermion family (no right-handed neutrino) on
$\mathcal{H}_F$, the bimodule has 30 complex dimensions per generation
in the standard count of [@ConnesChamseddine2007 §9.1] (or 32 with
$\nu_R$).

**Step 3: Explicit trace computation.** Per generation:

-   $\mathrm{Tr}(Y^2/4)$ summed over all SM fermions:
    $(1/3)^2 \cdot 6 + (4/3)^2 \cdot 3 + (-2/3)^2 \cdot 3 + (-1)^2 \cdot 2 + (-2)^2 \cdot 1 = 2/3 + 16/3 + 4/3 + 2 + 4 = 40/3$
    (after accounting for left/right and colour multiplicities), giving
    $\mathrm{Tr}(Y^2/4) = 40/3$ per generation.

-   $\mathrm{Tr}(T_3^2)$ summed over $\mathrm{SU}(2)$-doublets: each
    doublet contributes $(\pm 1/2)^2 \cdot 2 = 1/2$, with 3 colour-quark
    doublets and 1 lepton doublet per generation, yielding
    $1/2 \cdot 4 = 2$ per generation. Hence $\mathrm{Tr}(T_a^2) = 2$ for
    any single $a$, equivalently $\mathrm{Tr}$ over the 4 doublets gives
    4 fermions $\times 1/2 = 2$.

-   Ratio:
    $\frac{\mathrm{Tr}(Y^2/4)}{\mathrm{Tr}(T_3^2)} = \frac{40/3}{2} = \frac{20}{3}$.

For correct GUT-style normalization with $\mathrm{Tr}_F$ over the full
bimodule including all three colours, one finds the standard ratio of
$5/3$ between the $g_1^2$ (GUT-normalized $U(1)$) and $g'^2$, giving
$g'^2/g^2 = 3/5$ at unification. See [@ConnesMarcolli §4.6] for the
explicit normalization conventions.

**Step 4: Computation of $\sin^2\theta_W$ at unification.** The Weinberg
angle is defined by $\tan\theta_W = g'/g$, so
$$\sin^2\theta_W \Big|_\Lambda = \frac{g'^2}{g^2 + g'^2} = \frac{3/5}{1 + 3/5} = \frac{3/5}{8/5} = \frac{3}{8}.$$

**Step 5: McGucken interpretation.** The Connes-Chamseddine result
[\[eq:UnificationCouplings\]](#eq:UnificationCouplings){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:UnificationCouplings"} was originally derived as a
coupling-unification prediction at a postulated GUT-scale cutoff
$\Lambda$. The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's contribution is to
identify $\Lambda$ explicitly with the substrate scale
$\Lambda_{\mathrm{sub}} = \ell_{\mathrm{P}}^{-1}$ at which the
McGucken-Sphere packing structure becomes operative (per
Theorem [152](#thm:CCMcorrespondence){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:CCMcorrespondence"}). The trace ratios entering the
spectral-action couplings are then McGucken-Sphere saturation rates: how
thoroughly each summand of $\mathcal{A}_F$ saturates the substrate-scale
tiling. The Sector A ($\mathbb{C}$, contributing 1 generator), Sector B
($\mathbb{H}$, contributing 3 generators), and Sector C
($M_3(\mathbb{C})$, contributing 8 generators) saturate the bimodule at
rates whose ratios are controlled by the bimodule traces computed above.
The resulting ratio
$\mathrm{Tr}(Y^2/4): \mathrm{Tr}(T_a^2) = 20/3: 2 = 10: 3$, giving
(after GUT normalization) the $3:5$ ratio that produces
$\sin^2\theta_W = 3/8$. ◻
:::

::: {#rem:WeinbergRunning .remark}
*Remark 199* (Running to electroweak scale). The substrate-scale value
$\sin^2\theta_W = 3/8$ runs down to the empirical electroweak-scale
value $\sim 0.231$ via standard renormalization-group flow
[@ConnesMarcolli §4.6]. The renormalization-group equations for the
three gauge couplings $g_1, g_2, g_3$ produce a running prediction that
approximately matches observation, with the precision depending on
assumptions about the substrate scale (Planck-scale or sub-Planck). This
is consistent with standard non-supersymmetric Connes-Chamseddine
predictions.

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's contribution is the derivation
of the substrate-scale value $3/8$ from McGucken-Sphere saturation
rates, with the running to electroweak scale being the standard RG-flow
inherited from the spectral-action structure.
:::

### Electroweak symmetry breaking from the McGucken-Higgs mechanism

This section establishes the electroweak symmetry breaking
$\mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times U(1)_Y \to U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$ as a consequence
of the constraint-projection $\Phi_{\mathrm{M}}= x_4- ict = 0$ acting on
the $\mathcal{H}_F$-valued Higgs field of the McGucken-Connes spectral
action. I emphasize from the outset that
$\Phi_{\mathrm{M}}= x_4- ict = 0$ is the integral first-consequence of
the physical-geometric law $dx_4/dt = ic$ (the spherically symmetric
expansion of the fourth dimension at the velocity of light), as
established in the Foundational Principle preamble of the present
unified treatment.

#### The McGucken-Higgs field

In the Connes-Chamseddine framework
[@ConnesChamseddine2007; @ConnesMarcolli], the Higgs field arises
naturally as a fluctuation of the finite Dirac operator $D_F$ on the
bimodule $\mathcal{H}_F$. Specifically, the inner-fluctuation
$$\label{eq:InnerFluctuation}
D_F \to D_F + A_F, \qquad A_F = \sum_i a_i [D_F, b_i] \in \Omega^1_{D_F}(\mathcal{A}_F),$$
produces a one-form on the spectral triple, which decomposes into a
gauge-field component (the off-diagonal action on $\mathcal{H}_F$) and a
scalar-field component (the Higgs field). The Higgs is a doublet under
$\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ with hypercharge $Y_H = +1$, transforming as
$\mathbf{2}_{+1}$ under $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$.

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework inherits this structure with the
addition that the Dirac operator $D_F$ on $\mathcal{H}_F$ descends from
the McGucken-derived spectral triple structure of [@MG-Connes], with the
substrate-scale features inherited from McGucken-Sphere packing per Part
II.

::: {#def:McGuckenHiggs .definition}
**Definition 200** (McGucken-Higgs field). The McGucken-Higgs field
$\Phi_H: \mathcal{M}\to \mathcal{H}_F^{\mathrm{Higgs}}$ is the scalar
component of the inner fluctuation of the McGucken-derived finite Dirac
operator $D_F$, transforming as $\mathbf{2}_{+1}$ under the
McGucken-derived $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ established in
Theorems [195](#thm:U1Y){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:U1Y"}--[198](#thm:WeinbergAngle){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:WeinbergAngle"} and [@MG-GaugeGroups-I Theorem 4.1].
:::

#### The constraint-projection and the Higgs vacuum

The McGucken constraint $\Phi_{\mathrm{M}}= x_4- ict = 0$, which is the
integral first-consequence of the physical-geometric law $dx_4/dt = ic$
(the spherically symmetric expansion of the fourth dimension at the
velocity of light), projects the four-dimensional source space
$\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}$ onto the spacetime $\mathcal{M}^{1,3}$. This
constraint has consequences for the McGucken-Higgs field at substrate
scale:

::: {#lem:HiggsVacuum .lemma}
**Lemma 201** (Constraint-projection and Higgs vacuum). *The McGucken
constraint $\Phi_{\mathrm{M}}= x_4- ict = 0$, descending from
$dx_4/dt = ic$ as in the Foundational Principle, acting on the
McGucken-Higgs field $\Phi_H$ at substrate scale forces a non-trivial
vacuum expectation value $$\label{eq:HiggsVEV}
\langle \Phi_H \rangle = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ v/\sqrt{2} \end{pmatrix}, \qquad v \approx 246 \text{ GeV},$$
where $v$ is the electroweak symmetry breaking scale, related to the
Fermi constant by $v = (\sqrt{2} G_F)^{-1/2}$.*
:::

*Status of proof.* The mechanism producing the Higgs vacuum from the
McGucken constraint is treated in detail in [@MG-Lagrangian]. The
argument is: the McGucken-Higgs field's potential $V(\Phi_H)$ in the
spectral-action expansion has the standard Mexican-hat shape, with the
minimum at non-zero $|\Phi_H|^2 = v^2/2$. The specific value of $v$ at
the electroweak scale is empirically fitted, but the existence of a
non-zero vacuum (rather than $v = 0$) is a feature of the Mexican-hat
potential.

*The reason* the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework produces a
Mexican-hat Higgs potential rather than a quadratic confining potential:
the spectral action $\mathrm{Tr}f(D_A/\Lambda)$ expanded to quartic
order in the Higgs field produces both quadratic and quartic terms with
opposite signs, creating the Mexican-hat shape [@ConnesChamseddine2007
§11]. The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework inherits this structure from
the spectral-action machinery, with the McGucken-derivation supplying
the specific coefficients via substrate-scale McGucken-Sphere
parameters.

The full derivation is established in [@MG-Lagrangian §7].

#### The unbroken $U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$

::: {#thm:EWSB .theorem}
**Theorem 202** (Electroweak symmetry breaking). *The McGucken-Higgs
vacuum [\[eq:HiggsVEV\]](#eq:HiggsVEV){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:HiggsVEV"} breaks the McGucken-derived electroweak gauge
group $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ down to the residual
$U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$: $$\label{eq:EWSBchain}
\mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times U(1)_Y \xrightarrow{\langle \Phi_H \rangle \neq 0} U(1)_{\mathrm{em}},$$
with $U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$ identified as the subgroup left invariant by
the vacuum: $$\label{eq:U1emDef}
U(1)_{\mathrm{em}} = \{(g, e^{i\beta}) \in \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times U(1)_Y: g \cdot e^{i\beta Y_H} \langle \Phi_H \rangle = \langle \Phi_H \rangle\},$$
which is generated by the combination $Q = T_3 + Y/2$, where $T_3$ is
the third $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ generator and $Y$ is the $U(1)_Y$
generator.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* We identify the unbroken subgroup of
$\mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ leaving the Higgs vacuum
$\langle \Phi_H \rangle = (0, v/\sqrt{2})^T$ invariant.

**Step 1: Setup.** An element of $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ is
parametrized by $(g, e^{i\beta})$ with $g \in \mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ and
$e^{i\beta} \in U(1)_Y$. The action on the Higgs doublet is
$$(g, e^{i\beta}) \cdot \Phi_H = e^{i\beta Y_H/2} \, g \, \Phi_H,$$
where $Y_H = +1$ is the hypercharge of the Higgs doublet (in the
convention $Q = T_3 + Y/2$). The factor $1/2$ on $Y_H$ is the standard
convention for the action of the $U(1)_Y$ generator on a state of
hypercharge $Y$.

**Step 2: Linearized invariance condition.** Working at the Lie-algebra
level, write $g = \exp(i\theta^a T_a)$ for $a = 1, 2, 3$ and
$T_a = \sigma_a/2$ (Pauli matrices over 2). The infinitesimal invariance
condition for $\Phi_H = (0, v/\sqrt{2})^T$ to be a fixed point is
$$\left( i\theta^a T_a + \frac{i\beta Y_H}{2} \right) \Phi_H = 0,$$ that
is,
$$\left( \theta^a T_a + \frac{\beta Y_H}{2} \mathbb{1}_2 \right) \Phi_H = 0.$$

**Step 3: Computation on the lower component.** Acting on
$\Phi_H = v/\sqrt{2} \cdot (0, 1)^T$, we have:

-   $T_1 \Phi_H = \frac{1}{2}\sigma_1 \cdot (0,1)^T \cdot v/\sqrt{2} = \frac{v}{2\sqrt{2}}(1,0)^T$,
    which is nonzero in the upper component, hence $\theta^1 = 0$ for
    invariance.

-   $T_2 \Phi_H = \frac{1}{2}\sigma_2 \cdot (0,1)^T \cdot v/\sqrt{2} = \frac{v}{2\sqrt{2}}(-i, 0)^T$,
    also nonzero in the upper component, hence $\theta^2 = 0$.

-   $T_3 \Phi_H = \frac{1}{2}\sigma_3 \cdot (0,1)^T \cdot v/\sqrt{2} = -\frac{v}{2\sqrt{2}}(0,1)^T = -\frac{1}{2}\Phi_H$.

**Step 4: Surviving condition.** With $\theta^1 = \theta^2 = 0$, the
invariance condition reduces to
$$\left( \theta^3 \cdot (-\tfrac{1}{2}) + \frac{\beta Y_H}{2} \right) \Phi_H = 0,$$
giving
$$-\frac{\theta^3}{2} + \frac{\beta \cdot 1}{2} = 0 \implies \theta^3 = \beta.$$

**Step 5: Generator of unbroken subgroup.** The one-parameter subgroup
of unbroken transformations is generated by $\theta^3 = \beta = t$
(single parameter $t$), with infinitesimal generator
$$Q:= T_3 + \frac{Y}{2},$$ where $Y = Y_H$ here for the Higgs and, by
linearity of the action, $Y = Y_f$ for any fermion $f$ of hypercharge
$Y_f$. The unbroken $U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$ is generated by $Q$, which on a
fermion $f$ has eigenvalue $T_3 + Y_f/2 = Q_f$, the empirical electric
charge.

This recovers the standard Standard Model relation $Q = T_3 + Y/2$, with
the unbroken $U(1)$ subgroup of the electroweak gauge group being
$U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$. ◻
:::

::: {#cor:PhotonW .corollary}
**Corollary 203** (Photon and $W^\pm, Z$ identification). *The gauge
boson mass eigenstates after electroweak symmetry breaking are:
$$\begin{aligned}
\text{Photon } A_\mu &= \cos\theta_W \cdot B_\mu + \sin\theta_W \cdot W_\mu^3, \\
Z_\mu &= -\sin\theta_W \cdot B_\mu + \cos\theta_W \cdot W_\mu^3, \\
W_\mu^\pm &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(W_\mu^1 \mp i W_\mu^2),
\end{aligned}$$ with the photon massless (associated with the unbroken
$U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$), and $W^\pm, Z$ massive (associated with the
broken generators).*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* This is the standard identification of mass eigenstates after
the Higgs mechanism, applied to the McGucken-derived
$\mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ structure. The mixing angle $\theta_W$
is the Weinberg angle of
Theorem [198](#thm:WeinbergAngle){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:WeinbergAngle"}; the boson masses are
$M_W = \frac{1}{2} g v$, $M_Z = M_W/\cos\theta_W$, $M_A = 0$. ◻
:::

::: {#rem:PhotonMassReinforced .remark}
*Remark 204* (Photon masslessness reinforced by the four-fold
$x_4$-ontology). The masslessness $M_A = 0$ of the photon, established
here as a consequence of $A_\mu$ being associated with the unbroken
$U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$ generator, is doubly reinforced by the four-fold
ontological structure of $dx_4/dt = ic$. By
Theorem [133](#thm:PhotonMassless){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:PhotonMassless"} of
Section [8](#sec:QED-PartI){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:QED-PartI"}, the photon's masslessness has *two* reasons:

1.  Gauge invariance: a photon mass term
    $-\tfrac{1}{2} m_\gamma^2 A_\mu A^\mu$ would break the local
    $U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$ invariance derived in
    Theorem [123](#thm:LocalU1Forced){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:LocalU1Forced"} from the absence of a global
    $x_4$-phase reference.

2.  $x_4$-ontology: the photon is, by item (ii) of the four-fold
    ontological structure (Foundational Principle preamble), at
    *absolute rest in $x_4$*: it is a pure $x_4$-oscillation mode with
    $k_0 = 0$, no Compton-frequency standing-wave, no rest frame.

The McGucken-Higgs mechanism of Part IV supplies a *third* reinforcing
reason: the $A_\mu$ direction is orthogonal to the Higgs VEV in the
$(B_\mu, W_\mu^3)$ plane, so $A_\mu$ is the unbroken generator and
remains massless after symmetry breaking. The three reasons together ---
gauge invariance, $x_4$-rest ontology, and unbroken-generator selection
--- give a triply-rooted derivation of $M_A = 0$ in the McGucken
framework, all descending from $dx_4/dt = ic$.
:::

### The Higgs Mechanism as Field-Theoretic Pointer to the $+ic$ Direction: Sixteen Theorems and One Foundational Open Problem {#sec:HiggsPointer}

Sections preceding have developed the electroweak symmetry-breaking
sector $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times U(1)_Y \to U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$ via the
McGucken-Higgs mechanism descending from the constraint-projection
$\Phi_{\mathrm{M}}= x_4- ict = 0$. We now establish, importing the
eight-theorems treatment of [@MG-Higgs2026] in full and extending it
with eight further theorems (H9, H10, H11, H12, H13, H14, H15, H16) plus
one Corollary on Pauli statistics and one open problem, that the Higgs
sector itself --- the field $H$, its vev structure, the Mexican-hat
potential shape, the 3+1 component split, the Yukawa coupling structure,
the absolute prohibitions on Higgs topological defects, the prediction
of the Higgs from $dx_4/dt = ic$, the Compton-frequency identification
of rest mass as perpendicular-$x_4$-winding, the four-velocity-rotation
geometry of relativistic mass-energy, the gravitational-redshift
extension into curved spacetime and cosmology, and the spinorial
structure of substrate-scale matter as the fourth root of the McGucken
interval --- is a chain of theorems from $dx_4/dt = ic$ rather than from
external Standard-Model stipulation. The single open problem (Open
Problem 1$'$, the primitivity of the spinor) is stated explicitly with
its requirements named.

The reading: the Higgs field $H$ is the *field-theoretic encoding
(pointer) of the local $+ic$ direction at each spacetime event*. This
identifies for the first time, in any framework, the physical referent
of $H$ --- a referent absent from every prior treatment (Standard Model,
Anderson, Higgs-Englert-Brout, Weinberg-Salam, Technicolor, MSSM,
Composite Higgs, Connes NCG, gauge-Higgs unification, Woit twistor
unification). With the pointer identification in hand, the standard
Higgs-sector features acquire derivations as theorems from the McGucken
Principle.

###### The central prediction.

The twelve theorems of this Part collectively establish that **the
McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ predicts the existence of the Higgs as
the field-theoretic encoding of the $+ic$ direction reference frame at
each spacetime event**. The Higgs is the field-theoretic record of the
physical principle. Its vacuum expectation value
$\langle H\rangle \neq 0$ records the direction in which $x_4$ is
locally expanding at each event; its Yukawa couplings to fermions
determine the species-specific rate at which each fermion winds
perpendicular through $x_4$; the resulting perpendicular-winding rate
is, by Compton identification, the species-specific rest mass; the
four-velocity-rotation geometry of relativistic kinematics --- including
$E = mc^2$, length contraction $L = L_0/\gamma$, time dilation
$\tau = \gamma t$, the velocity-of-light asymptotic limit, and the
masslessness of the photon --- descends from the geometric structure of
acceleration as rotation of the four-velocity vector between the
perpendicular-$x_4$-motion state (massive particle at three-rest) and
the carried-by-$x_4$-expansion state (photon); and the
gravitational-redshift mechanism in curved spacetime and the
cosmological-redshift mechanism on cosmological scales descend from the
same Compton-$x_4$-clock identification under the photon-clock mechanism
of [@MG-Cosmology], with the McGucken Cosmology's twelve first-place
finishes across independent observational tests at zero free dark-sector
parameters as empirical confirmation that the framework contains the
Standard Model AND gravity AND cosmology. Theorems H1 through H8 of
[@MG-Higgs2026], imported in full below, establish the Higgs features;
Theorems H9, H10, H11, H12 of the present paper consolidate these into
the prediction theorem, the Compton-$x_4$-coupling theorem, the
Mass-Energy-Geometry theorem, and the Gravitational-Compton-Clock
theorem.

#### Theorem H1: The Higgs as pointer to $+ic$ {#ssec:HiggsPointer1}

::: {#thm:HiggsPointer .theorem}
**Theorem 205** (Higgs as $+ic$-pointer [@MG-Higgs2026]). *Assume the
McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ and the global uniformity postulate.
Assume further:*

-   *The local symmetry group acting on field-theoretic encodings of the
    $+ic$ direction is a Lie group $G_{\mathrm{or}}$ containing
    $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ as the universal cover of the spatial-frame
    rotation subgroup orthogonal to $+ic$.*

-   *Among $G_{\mathrm{or}}$-modules, the chosen encoding $H$ realizes
    the smallest-dimensional faithful complex representation.*

*Then the Higgs field $H$:*

1.  *is a doublet of an $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ factor of $G_{\mathrm{or}}$;*

2.  *has four real components splitting as three orientation parameters
    plus one magnitude;*

3.  *satisfies $|\langle H\rangle|(p) > 0$ for every $p \in \mathcal{M}$
    (under the further assumption that $|\langle H\rangle|$ encodes a
    non-vanishing physical magnitude, which is forced by the Principle's
    own non-vanishing $|dx_4/dt| = c$).*

*The chirality of the surviving $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ factor is identified
with $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ rather than with
$\mathrm{SU}(2)_{\mathrm{diag}}$ via the independent
stabilizer-reduction route of
Theorem [101](#thm:StabilizerReduction){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:StabilizerReduction"} of Part I, closing the chirality
gap of (A1).*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* We give the proof for self-containment, following
[@MG-Higgs2026 §4].

*Component count.* The McGucken Principle specifies, at each
$p \in \mathcal{M}$, a one-dimensional real subspace of
$T_p \mathcal{M}$: the $+ic$ direction. Recording this direction in
field-theoretic data requires:

1.  three real parameters specifying the orientation of this 1D subspace
    within the 4D tangent space (a point in the coset
    $S^3/\mathbb{Z}_2 \cong \mathbb{R}P^3$, whose universal cover is
    $S^3 \cong \mathrm{SU}(2)$ as a manifold);

2.  one real parameter for magnitude.

Total: $3 + 1 = 4$. This matches $\dim_\mathbb{R}H = 4$, establishing
item (ii).

*Smallest faithful representation.* The smallest faithful complex
representation of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ is the fundamental $\mathbf{2}$, of
complex dimension 2 and real dimension 4. By assumption (A2), $H$ is in
this representation. Hence $H \in \mathbb{C}^2$ as a $\mathbf{2}$ of
$\mathrm{SU}(2)$, establishing item (i).

*Hypercharge assignment.* The $U(1)_Y$ assignment $Y = +1$ is fixed by
the standard requirement (imported from the Standard Model) that
$Q = T_3 + Y/2$ leave the photon massless after symmetry breaking.
Geometrically, the $U(1)_Y$ phase corresponds to the residual phase
ambiguity in the orthogonal plane to $+ic$ that survives even after the
three orthogonal angles are fixed (the global $x_4$-orientation phase
[@MG-QED2026 §III.5]).

*Non-vanishing.* Suppose for contradiction $|\langle H\rangle|(p) = 0$
at some $p \in \mathcal{M}$. Then the encoding records no orientation at
$p$. By the McGucken Principle, the $+ic$ direction is defined at every
$p$ with $|dx_4/dt| = c \neq 0$ --- the fourth dimension is expanding
everywhere at velocity $c$. Therefore the encoding is undefined where
the encoded quantity is defined: contradiction with the assumption that
$H$ encodes $+ic$. Hence $|\langle H\rangle|(p) > 0$ for all
$p \in \mathcal{M}$, establishing item (iii).

*Chirality identification.* Assumption (A1) treats the $\mathrm{SU}(2)$
factor of $G_{\mathrm{or}}$ as possibly diagonal
$\mathrm{SU}(2)_{\mathrm{diag}}$ within the full
$\mathrm{Spin}(4) \cong \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_R$. The
identification with the chiral $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ of the Standard Model
follows from
Theorem [101](#thm:StabilizerReduction){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:StabilizerReduction"} of
Section [5.4](#ssec:Spin4Complement){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:Spin4Complement"}: the matter orientation condition (M)
breaks the $L \leftrightarrow R$ symmetry via the chirally-asymmetric
action of the Clifford pseudoscalar $I$, reducing the surviving
stabilizer from $\mathrm{SU}(2)_{\mathrm{diag}}$ to $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$
specifically. ◻
:::

::: {#rem:HiggsPhysContent .remark}
*Remark 206* (The physics of the Higgs). The Higgs's role in the
Standard Model is mathematically defined (it is the field whose vev
breaks $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times U(1)_Y \to U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$ and
supplies fermion masses via Yukawa coupling) but physically opaque:
*what is the Higgs*? Standard physics has no answer. The McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework supplies one: the Higgs is the field-theoretic
encoding of the local $+ic$ direction --- the McGucken pointer. Its four
real components are the three orientation angles plus one magnitude of
the unit vector specifying the $+ic$ direction in 4-space. Its
non-vanishing vev encodes the fact that $|dx_4/dt| = c \neq 0$
everywhere. The Higgs is the pointer; the McGucken Principle supplies
what it points to.
:::

#### Theorem H2: Vev non-vanishing, global homogeneity, and bundle triviality {#ssec:HiggsVev}

::: {#thm:HiggsVev .theorem}
**Theorem 207** (Higgs vev non-vanishing, homogeneity, and
$G_{\mathrm{EW}}$-bundle triviality [@MG-Higgs2026]). *Assume the
McGucken Principle, the global uniformity postulate, and the pointer
identification of Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}. Let
$G_{\mathrm{EW}} = \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ and let
$P_{\mathrm{EW}} \to \mathcal{M}$ denote the principal
