$G_{\mathrm{EW}}$-bundle whose associated $\mathbb{C}^2$-bundle has
$\langle H\rangle$ as a section. Then:*

1.  *$\langle H\rangle(p) \neq 0$ for all $p \in \mathcal{M}$.*

2.  *$|\langle H\rangle|(p) = v/\sqrt{2}$ is constant across
    $\mathcal{M}$.*

3.  *$P_{\mathrm{EW}}$ is trivial:
    $P_{\mathrm{EW}} \cong \mathcal{M} \times G_{\mathrm{EW}}$ on
    Minkowski $\mathcal{M}$ (and more generally on $\mathcal{M}$ with
    vanishing relevant cohomology).*

*The vev's non-vanishing and homogeneity are not Standard-Model
postulates or empirical inputs; they are theorems of the McGucken
Principle's non-vanishing and uniform $+ic$ direction.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* *(i) Non-vanishing.* Established in
Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}(iii): if $|\langle H\rangle|(p) = 0$, the
pointer encoding is undefined at $p$, contradicting the specification of
$+ic$ at every $p$.

*(ii) Homogeneity.* The global uniformity postulate states that the
$+ic$ direction is the same in tangent space at every point relative to
a globally consistent frame. The magnitude $|dx_4/dt| = c$ is also
globally uniform (part of the McGucken Principle's content: $c$ is
invariant). The pointer field $H$ encodes both direction and magnitude.
The encoded magnitude $|\langle H\rangle|$ is a gauge-invariant scalar:
under $H \to UH$ for $U \in G_{\mathrm{EW}}$ acting linearly on $H$,
$|\langle H\rangle|^2 = \langle H\rangle^\dagger \langle H\rangle$ is
preserved. A gauge-invariant scalar field recording a globally uniform
quantity is itself globally uniform on $\mathcal{M}$ (modulo
gauge-fixing artefacts, zero by definition). Hence
$|\langle H\rangle|(p) = v/\sqrt{2}$ for all $p$, where $v$ is the
constant set by the magnitude of the McGucken pointer.

*(iii) Bundle triviality.* We invoke the same Steenrod bundle-triviality
theorem already used in
Theorem [135](#thm:NoMonopole){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:NoMonopole"} of
Section [8](#sec:QED-PartI){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:QED-PartI"}: a principal $G$-bundle $P \to \mathcal{M}$
is trivial if and only if it admits a continuous global section
[@Steenrod1951 Theorem 11.6].

The associated bundle
$E = P_{\mathrm{EW}} \times_{G_{\mathrm{EW}}} \mathbb{C}^2 \to \mathcal{M}$
has $\langle H\rangle$ as a section. By (i), this section is everywhere
non-vanishing. The non-vanishing section $\langle H\rangle$ uniquely
determines (up to the residual $U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$ stabilizer of
$\langle H\rangle$) a section of $P_{\mathrm{EW}}$: at each $p$, choose
the bundle element $g(p) \in P_{\mathrm{EW}}|_p$ that maps the standard
basis element $(0, v/\sqrt{2})^\top$ to $\langle H\rangle(p)$. This is
well-defined modulo the stabilizer of $(0, v/\sqrt{2})^\top$ in
$G_{\mathrm{EW}}$, which is $U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$.

For Minkowski $\mathcal{M} = \mathbb{R}^{1,3}$, the manifold is
contractible and every principal bundle is trivial; the global section
extends to a global section of $P_{\mathrm{EW}}$. For general
spacetimes, additional cohomological conditions are required; we
restrict the present claim to $\mathcal{M}$ contractible (or with
appropriately vanishing obstruction classes).

For Minkowski spacetime --- the setting in which the Standard Model is
defined --- $P_{\mathrm{EW}}$ is trivial, $\langle H\rangle$ extends to
a globally defined nowhere-vanishing field, and the McGucken Principle's
globally uniform $+ic$ provides the canonical global section. ◻
:::

::: {#rem:VevNoMonoParallel .remark}
*Remark 208* (Parallel with the No-Monopole Theorem). The
bundle-triviality argument of
Theorem [207](#thm:HiggsVev){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsVev"}(iii) is the same argument as the No-Monopole
Theorem [135](#thm:NoMonopole){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:NoMonopole"} of
Section [8](#sec:QED-PartI){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:QED-PartI"}: in both, the McGucken Principle's globally
uniform $+ic$ provides a global section of the relevant principal
bundle, and Steenrod's theorem then gives triviality. The two results
--- vev existence/homogeneity and monopole absence --- have a common
bundle-topological root in $dx_4/dt = ic$. The McGucken framework's
bundle structure is rigid: the global section provided by the directed
$+ic$ trivializes both the $x_4$-orientation $U(1)$-bundle (forbidding
monopoles) and the electroweak $G_{\mathrm{EW}}$-bundle (forcing vev
homogeneity).
:::

#### Theorem H3: Topological non-vanishing under loop corrections and the hierarchy trichotomy {#ssec:HiggsHierarchy}

::: {#thm:VevLoopProtection .theorem}
**Theorem 209** (Topological non-vanishing protection [@MG-Higgs2026]).
*Assume the McGucken Principle, the global uniformity postulate, and
Theorem [207](#thm:HiggsVev){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsVev"}. Loop corrections in QFT correspond to
continuous deformations of field configurations; continuous deformations
cannot change the topological class. In particular, no finite-order
perturbative correction can drive $\langle H\rangle$ from its
non-vanishing homotopy class to the vanishing one. Hence
$|\langle H\rangle|$ is bounded away from zero by a topological
constraint that no perturbative dynamics can violate.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Continuous deformations preserve topological class. The
non-vanishing of $\langle H\rangle$ established in
Theorem [207](#thm:HiggsVev){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsVev"}(i) is a topological condition on the section:
it specifies that $\langle H\rangle$ is in the homotopy class of
nowhere-vanishing sections. Any continuous deformation, including those
generated by loop corrections, preserves this class. Loop corrections
can shift the magnitude $v$ of the section by amounts $\delta v$, but
cannot drive $v$ to zero --- this would require crossing into a
different topological class. ◻
:::

The topological non-vanishing protection of
Theorem [209](#thm:VevLoopProtection){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:VevLoopProtection"} is not the full hierarchy problem.
The full hierarchy problem decomposes into three logically distinct
subproblems, as follows.

::: {#thm:HierarchyTrichotomy .theorem}
**Theorem 210** (Hierarchy trichotomy [@MG-Higgs2026]). *Within the
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, the conventional "hierarchy problem"
splits into three logically distinct subproblems with distinct status:*

1.  ***Existence of $\langle H\rangle \neq 0$: *solved*.**
    Theorem [207](#thm:HiggsVev){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:HiggsVev"} establishes that $\langle H\rangle$ does
    not vanish anywhere on $\mathcal{M}$, via the bundle-section
    argument. Theorem [209](#thm:VevLoopProtection){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:VevLoopProtection"} establishes that this survives
    all radiative corrections, since the topological obstruction is
    independent of perturbative dynamics.*

2.  ***Magnitude of $|v| \approx 246$ GeV: *open*.**
    Theorem [207](#thm:HiggsVev){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:HiggsVev"} fixes direction but not magnitude. The
    McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework has natural scales at
    $M_{\mathrm{Pl}}$ (from the oscillatory-quantization postulate) and
    $\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}$ (from the Standard Model). The value
    $v \approx 246$ GeV is not currently expressible as a known function
    of these. The geometric mean
    $\sqrt{M_{\mathrm{Pl}} \cdot \Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}}$ misses $v$ by
    seven orders of magnitude; other simple combinations similarly fail.
    The numerical value of $v$ remains an empirical input.*

3.  ***Radiative-correction stability of $\mu^2$: *open*.** The Standard
    Model's quadratic divergence $\delta \mu^2 \sim \Lambda^2$ is not
    protected by any McGucken-framework symmetry currently known. Three
    Routes attempted in [@MG-Higgs2026 §8] all fail with explicit Honest
    Findings:*

    -   **Route 1 (Ward identity from $x_4$-translation):* The Noether
        current associated with $x_4$-translation is energy-momentum
        $T^{\mu 0}$; the Ward identity is energy conservation, which
        does not protect scalar masses (energy is conserved at every
        vertex of the Higgs self-energy diagram, yet the diagram still
        produces $\Lambda^2$).*

    -   **Route 2 (topological pinning of magnitude):*
        Theorem [207](#thm:HiggsVev){reference-type="ref"
        reference="thm:HiggsVev"} fixes direction but not magnitude.
        Naive combinations of $M_{\mathrm{Pl}}$ and
        $\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}$ fail by many orders of magnitude.*

    -   **Route 3 (oscillatory-quantization softening):* Truncating
        virtual frequencies below $M_{\mathrm{Pl}}$ conflicts with
        empirically-verified renormalization-group running of
        Standard-Model couplings.*

    *The framework does not currently supply a Ward identity,
    topological pinning, or oscillatory-quantization softening that
    would close the radiative-stability gap.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Item (1) is Theorem [207](#thm:HiggsVev){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsVev"} combined with
Theorem [209](#thm:VevLoopProtection){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:VevLoopProtection"}. Items (2) and (3) follow from the
Honest Findings detailed in [@MG-Higgs2026 §8.2--8.4], summarised
above. ◻
:::

::: remark
*Remark 211* (Why the trichotomy matters). Conflating (1)--(3) leads to
the impression that the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework either solves
the hierarchy problem entirely (an overclaim, since (2) and (3) are
open) or solves none of it (an underclaim, since (1) is closed and is
genuinely the most fundamental of the three: a framework that did not
establish (1) would not be a candidate Higgs theory at all). The
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework upgrades (1) from postulate to
theorem, leaves (2) open, and leaves (3) open. The advance is on (1);
claims about "solving the hierarchy problem" beyond (1) are not
supported by the present analysis. This is scoping in the style required
throughout the McGucken corpus: prove what can be proved, flag what is
open, do not overclaim.
:::

#### No fine-tuning, no multiverse: dissolving the Arkani-Hamed dichotomy {#ssec:NoFineTuningNoMultiverse}

The hierarchy trichotomy of
Theorem [210](#thm:HierarchyTrichotomy){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HierarchyTrichotomy"} carries a consequence for the
debate in fundamental physics over the past two decades. Arkani-Hamed
has argued, in talks delivered consistently from the late 2000s through
the present
[@ArkaniHamed-Colloquium-2013; @ArkaniHamed-NimaConversation-2024], that
the small value of the Higgs mass in Planck units forces a binary choice
between two possible futures for fundamental physics. I make explicit
the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's stance against this dichotomy
and identify the specific technical premise that the framework denies.

##### The Arkani-Hamed two-alternatives framing {#the-arkani-hamed-two-alternatives-framing .unnumbered}

As summarised by Woit [@Woit-ArkaniHamedColloquium-2013], Arkani-Hamed's
framing presents two and only two viable futures:

1.  **Natural-SUSY future.** The small value of the Higgs mass admits a
    "natural" symmetry-protection explanation, most likely via
    supersymmetry, in which case fundamental physics consists of
    unravelling the complexities of a SUSY-extended Standard Model.

2.  **Anthropic-multiverse future.** The small value indicates
    fine-tuning that can only have an anthropic explanation, parallel to
    the anthropic argument for the cosmological constant. Physics is
    determined by something like the string theory landscape; the
    McGucken-pattern of deriving fundamental constants from a single
    principle is abandoned in favour of statistical selection from a
    vast space of vacua.

As Arkani-Hamed himself acknowledges [@Woit-ArkaniHamedColloquium-2013],
the anthropic alternative is conceptually problematic: the ideas are "so
poorly defined, not clear if they make any kind of mathematical sense,"
and it is "not clear progress will happen anytime soon." Woit
[@Woit-ArkaniHamedColloquium-2013] characterises (A2) as what David
Gross has called "giving up": announcing that the problems one has not
solved can never be solved. Woit's response is: "If a long, complicated
argument leads you to the conclusion that the only viable alternative is
to give up, then it seems to me you have two choices: give up, or
examine more carefully your argument."

##### The hidden technical premise {#the-hidden-technical-premise .unnumbered}

The Arkani-Hamed dichotomy is not a logical necessity. It is the
conclusion of a chain of argument that rests on a specific technical
premise. I identify the premise:

::: {#thm:HiddenPremise .theorem}
**Theorem 212** (The hidden technical premise). *The Arkani-Hamed
two-alternatives dichotomy rests on the technical assumption that the
Higgs field, treated as a continuum quantum field with a Lagrangian and
Feynman rules, admits a valid effective-field-theory description up to a
cutoff scale $\Lambda$ on the order of the Planck scale
$M_{\mathrm{Pl}} \approx 10^{19}$ GeV, with the quadratic divergence
$\delta m_H^2 \sim (g/4\pi)^2 \Lambda^2 \sim (10^{-2})(10^{19}\,\mathrm{GeV})^2 \sim 10^{36}\,\mathrm{GeV}^2$
representing a genuine physical contribution requiring
symmetry-protected cancellation against a comparable bare parameter to
part in $10^{34}$.*

*This assumption is not a theorem of any framework. It is the assumption
that the continuum-EFT description applies all the way up to the Planck
scale --- in particular, that the Planck scale enters the calculation as
a UV cutoff in the EFT sense rather than as a scale at which the
continuum-field description itself ceases to apply.*

*If this assumption fails --- if the Planck scale enters the framework
as the scale at which the continuum-field description of the Higgs
terminates because the physical degrees of freedom are no longer those
of a continuum field --- then the quadratic divergence is not a physical
contribution to the Higgs mass. It is an artifact of applying the
continuum-EFT calculation outside its domain of validity. The dichotomy
(**A1**) or (**A2**) dissolves.*
:::

::: proof
*Sketch and grade..* Grade 2: the EFT calculation
$\delta m_H^2 \sim \Lambda^2$ is a calculation *within* a
continuum-field framework with cutoff $\Lambda$. It produces a
meaningful physical prediction only if the continuum-field framework is
valid up to $\Lambda$. Whether it is, is a separate question that must
be answered on grounds rather than within the EFT calculation itself. In
standard treatments, the assumption that EFT is valid up to
$M_{\mathrm{Pl}}$ is sometimes called the "desert hypothesis"---the
assertion that no new physical degrees of freedom enter between the
electroweak scale and $M_{\mathrm{Pl}}$. The hierarchy problem in its
Arkani-Hamed framing presupposes the desert hypothesis. If the desert
hypothesis fails because the Planck scale is the substrate-scale
terminus of continuum-field validity, the hierarchy problem in its
Arkani-Hamed framing does not arise. The diagnostic is at its
boundary. ◻
:::

##### The McGucken third alternative {#the-mcgucken-third-alternative .unnumbered}

I state the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's position on the
dichotomy explicitly.

::: {#thm:ThirdAlternative .theorem}
**Theorem 213** (The McGucken third alternative). *The McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework offers a third alternative to the Arkani-Hamed
dichotomy: a future in which fundamental physics is highly predictive
and mathematically beautiful, descending from a single
physical-geometric principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, with the entire Standard
Model gauge group, the Higgs sector, the constants $c$ and $\hbar$, and
the absolute prohibitions (No-GUT, No-Proton-Decay, No-Monopole,
No-Higgs-Domain-Wall) descending as theorems. The dichotomy is dissolved
by denying the technical premise of
Theorem [212](#thm:HiddenPremise){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiddenPremise"}: in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework, the Planck scale is the substrate-scale at which the
continuum-field description of the Higgs terminates, not a UV cutoff
into which continuum-EFT is integrated.*
:::

::: proof
*Sketch and grade..* Grade 2--3 depending on the component being
assessed. The Planck length $\ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G / c^3}$ is the
McGucken-Sphere wavelength at substrate scale, fixed by Schwarzschild
self-consistency $r_S = \lambda$ at the McGucken-Sphere wavefront level
[@MG-Sphere2026]. At this scale, the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's
ingredients --- discrete McGucken Spheres of size $\ell_P$, the
substrate-scale tiling theorem, the noncommutative algebra
$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$ at
substrate scale --- replace the continuum-field description. The Higgs
field $H$ is, in the framework, the field-theoretic encoding of the
local $+ic$ direction of the McGucken-Sphere expansion
(Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}); at substrate scale this encoding is
built directly from the McGucken-Sphere wavefront orientation, and the
continuum-field Lagrangian formulation of $H$ is an emergent
long-distance description.

The substrate-scale termination of continuum-field validity is supported
by two independent results from the McGucken-Connes paper [@MG-Connes].
*Theorem H of [@MG-Connes]* (the McGucken Sphere--Quanta of Geometry
Identification) establishes that the Chamseddine-Connes-Mukhanov "quanta
of geometry" --- the Planck-volume four-spheres into which a
noncommutative four-manifold decomposes under the higher Heisenberg
commutation relation $\frac{1}{4!}\langle Y[D, Y]^4\rangle = \gamma$ ---
are derivationally identical to the McGucken Spheres at substrate scale.
The Planck scale is therefore not a UV cutoff at which one extrapolates
continuum-EFT into a regime where its degrees of freedom remain valid;
it is the scale at which the spatial manifold decomposes into discrete
Planck-volume four-spheres, with the continuum-field description of
fields like $H$ ceasing to apply because the spatial manifold itself
ceases to be a continuum. Two independent frameworks (Connes' axiomatic
noncommutative geometry; the McGucken Principle) arrive at the same
Planckian spherical quantum of spacetime.

*Theorem F of [@MG-Connes]* (the Spectral Action Correspondence)
establishes the corresponding statement at the level of dynamics: the
heat-kernel asymptotic expansion of $\mathrm{Tr}f(D/\Lambda)$ at the
McGucken-substrate cutoff $\Lambda = M_P c^2/\hbar$ produces, in its
Seeley-DeWitt coefficients $a_0, a_2, a_4$, terms in correspondence with
the four sectors of the McGucken Lagrangian. The substrate-scale cutoff
$\Lambda$ in the spectral-action formulation is the scale at which the
spectral-truncation framework of Connes-van Suijlekom [@MG-Connes]
produces the long-distance effective Lagrangian. The continuum-field
Lagrangian formulation of the Higgs sector at energies $E \ll \Lambda$
is therefore an emergent long-distance description of the
substrate-resolved geometry; the quadratic divergence of the standard
EFT calculation, which formally integrates virtual states up to
$\Lambda \sim M_{\mathrm{Pl}}$, is integrating beyond the scale at which
the continuum-field description applies. In the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework, the relevant calculation cuts off at the substrate scale not
because of a UV regulator but because the physical degrees of freedom
change: the underlying structure at the Planck scale is the
noncommutative-geometric structure of
$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$
acting on the McGucken-Dirac spectral triple, with the McGucken Spheres
as the quanta of geometry, and the spectral truncation supplied by the
McGucken-substrate cutoff $\Lambda$.

The third alternative is therefore available within the framework: the
Higgs mass is not fine-tuned (no $10^{34}$ tuning is required, because
the continuum-EFT calculation that produces the apparent tuning does not
apply at the Planck scale), and no multiverse is required (the framework
predicts a single universe with one set of physical laws). The dichotomy
(**A1**) or (**A2**) is dissolved. ◻
:::

##### What the framework predicts {#what-the-framework-predicts .unnumbered}

The McGucken third alternative carries specific empirics that
distinguishes it from both (**A1**) and (**A2**):

1.  **No supersymmetry.** The chiral $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ Weyl-doublet
    structure of Part I does not double into a supermultiplet under any
    operation of the framework. There are no superpartners. The
    $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ chirality structure forbids the bosonic doublet
    structure required for the matter-multiplet half of an
    $\mathcal{N}=1$ supermultiplet. Falsifiable: detection of any
    superpartner falsifies the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework.

2.  **No grand unification.** The No-GUT Theorem of Part V establishes
    that the three gauge factors $U(1)_Y$, $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$,
    $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ are independent (each descending from a distinct
    substrate-scale ingredient) and do not embed in any larger simple
    group with a single coupling. Falsifiable: detection of proton
    decay, gauge-coupling unification at a single energy scale, or
    monopole-mediated processes falsifies the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
    framework.

3.  **No multiverse.** The framework predicts a single universe with one
    set of physical laws, all descending from the single principle
    $dx_4/dt = ic$. The constants $c$ and $\hbar$ are theorems of the
    framework, not selection-effect outputs from a landscape.
    Falsifiable in principle if one obtained empirical evidence for the
    existence of other universes with different physical laws, though no
    such evidence is currently available or expected.

4.  **The Higgs vev exists everywhere and is topologically protected.**
    Theorem [207](#thm:HiggsVev){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:HiggsVev"} establishes the existence and global
    homogeneity of $\langle H\rangle$ via the bundle-section argument.
    Theorem [209](#thm:VevLoopProtection){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:VevLoopProtection"} establishes its topological
    protection. The existence component of the hierarchy problem
    (subproblem (1) of
    Theorem [210](#thm:HierarchyTrichotomy){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:HierarchyTrichotomy"}) is solved as a theorem of
    $dx_4/dt = ic$, not protected by symmetry. Falsifiable: detection of
    Higgs domain walls, vortices, or textures (any spatial inhomogeneity
    in $|\langle H\rangle|$) falsifies the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
    framework.

5.  **The (H2) magnitude problem remains open.** The framework does not
    currently derive the specific value $v \approx 246$ GeV from
    $dx_4/dt = ic$. I note this: solving (H1) and reframing (H3) does
    not solve (H2). The magnitude of the electroweak scale remains an
    empirical input in the present treatment, and is an open problem of
    the framework. The framework's claim is that the dichotomy (**A1**)
    or (**A2**) is false because the technical premise it rests on does
    not hold.

##### Position relative to Woit's critique {#position-relative-to-woits-critique .unnumbered}

Woit [@Woit-ArkaniHamedColloquium-2013] writes: "what is needed is
instead a suspicion that one has been making a mistake somewhere for
quite a while now." Woit identifies that there is a weakness in the
chain of argument and recommends looking for it. The McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework goes further:

1.  Woit's stance: the chain of argument that leads to the
    SUSY-or-multiverse dichotomy contains a hidden technical assumption
    that may be wrong, and one should look carefully for the weakness.

2.  McGucken's stance: the weakness is identified. It is the assumption
    that the continuum-EFT description of the Higgs field applies up to
    a Planck-scale UV cutoff. The assumption fails because the Planck
    scale is, in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, the
    substrate-scale at which the continuum-field description terminates
    --- this is a consequence of the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$
    together with the substrate-scale identification $\ell_P = \ell_*$
    via Schwarzschild self-consistency [@MG-Sphere2026], and is formally
    established by Theorem H of [@MG-Connes] (the McGucken
    Sphere--Quanta of Geometry Identification, in which two independent
    frameworks arrive at the same Planckian spherical quantum of
    spacetime) and Theorem F of [@MG-Connes] (the Spectral Action
    Correspondence, in which the heat-kernel expansion at the
    McGucken-substrate cutoff produces the McGucken Lagrangian). The
    framework that replaces continuum-EFT at substrate scale is the
    noncommutative-geometric structure of
    $\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$
    acting on the McGucken-Dirac spectral triple, with the Higgs as the
    field-theoretic encoding of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront
    orientation in $+ic$.

The two stances agree in their diagnosis of the situation: the dichotomy
is generated by a flawed argument and should be rejected. They differ in
the level of specification: Woit identifies the location of the flaw to
be found; the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework supplies a specific
alternative picture in which the flaw is identifiable and the dichotomy
is dissolved.

##### Synthesis {#synthesis .unnumbered}

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's position on the debate is:

*The 20th century pattern of highly predictive, mathematically beautiful
fundamental theory was not an aberration. It continues, in the form of a
framework with one principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ from which the Standard
Model gauge group, the Higgs sector, the constants $c$ and $\hbar$, and
the absolute prohibitions descend as theorems. The Arkani-Hamed
dichotomy is dissolved because its hidden technical premise fails: the
Planck scale is the substrate-scale terminus of continuum-field
validity, not a UV cutoff in an EFT sense. No SUSY is needed, because
the radiative-correction calculation that generates the hierarchy
problem does not apply at the Planck scale. No multiverse is needed,
because the framework predicts a single universe with one set of laws
derivable from one principle. The (H2) magnitude problem $v \approx 246$
GeV remains open as an empirical input. The framework upgrades
subproblem (1) of the hierarchy trichotomy to a theorem, reframes
subproblem (3) by denial of the technical premise, and leaves subproblem
(2) open.*

This is the third alternative to the Arkani-Hamed dichotomy. It is not
equivalent to either (**A1**) or (**A2**). It is distinct, empirically
distinguishable from both via the predictions (**T1**)--(**T4**), and it
preserves the 20th-century pattern of fundamental physics as the
derivation of a predictive structure from a small set of principles.

#### Why the Higgs has been considered puzzling so often: a synthesis of seven distinct orthodox-tradition puzzles, each engaged as a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ or as an open problem {#ssec:SevenHiggsPuzzles}

The orthodox tradition has treated the Higgs as puzzling for at least
seven distinct reasons over the past sixty years (Higgs 1964
[@Higgs1964], Englert--Brout 1964 [@EnglertBrout1964PRL],
Guralnik--Hagen--Kibble 1964 [@GHK1964]). The seven puzzles are often
conflated in the orthodox literature as "the Higgs problem" or "the
hierarchy problem," obscuring that they are distinct and require
distinct engagements. We catalog the seven, state each at orthodox
grade, then engage each as a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ established
elsewhere in the present paper, as a reframing at theorem grade, or as
an open problem of the framework.

###### The disentangling.

The seven puzzles fall into three categories: *resolved as theorems of
$dx_4/dt = ic$* (Puzzles P1, P2, P6, P7); *reframed at theorem grade*
(Puzzle P4); and *open in both the framework and standard physics*
(Puzzles P3, P5). We treat each in turn.

::: {#thm:SevenHiggsPuzzlesCatalog .theorem}
**Theorem 214** (Why the Higgs has been considered puzzling so often: a
catalog of seven distinct orthodox-tradition puzzles, each engaged by
the McGucken framework as a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$, a reframing at
theorem grade, or an open problem). *The orthodox-tradition's repeated
puzzlement over the Higgs field decomposes into seven distinct puzzles.
We state each, identify the orthodox-tradition position, and identify
the framework's engagement. Throughout: the framework establishes that
the seven puzzles are distinct and require distinct engagement, with the
conflation in the orthodox literature being itself a source of
obscurity.*

***Puzzle P1: *What is the Higgs, physically?* (The ontology puzzle.)***

**Orthodox-tradition position:* The Higgs is introduced as a technical
device --- a scalar field with negative quadratic potential coefficient
$\mu^2 < 0$, chosen to produce spontaneous symmetry breaking of
$\mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ down to $U(1)_{\rm em}$, giving gauge
bosons their masses consistent with gauge invariance
[@Higgs1964; @EnglertBrout1964PRL; @GHK1964]. The orthodox tradition
offers no physical identity for the Higgs; it is "a scalar field that
happens to have a non-zero vacuum expectation value."*

**Framework engagement
(Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}, G2 grade):* The Higgs is identified at
theorem grade as the field-theoretic encoding of the local $+ic$
direction at each spacetime event --- the McGucken pointer. The four
real components split as three orientation angles parametrising the
unit-vector direction of $+ic$ in 4-space, plus one magnitude (the
gauge-invariant scalar surviving as the physical Higgs $h$). The Higgs
has a physical identity: it is the pointer to the direction of
$dx_4/dt = ic$.*

***Puzzle P2: *Why does the vev have to be non-zero?* (The existence
puzzle, subproblem H1 of the hierarchy trichotomy.)***

**Orthodox-tradition position:* The non-zero vev
$\langle H\rangle = v/\sqrt{2} \approx 174$ GeV is postulated by setting
$\mu^2 < 0$ in $V(H) = \mu^2 |H|^2 + \lambda |H|^4$. Both signs of
$\mu^2$ are mathematically consistent; the orthodox tradition has no
reason for $\mu^2 < 0$ rather than $\mu^2 > 0$.*

**Framework engagement
(Theorem [207](#thm:HiggsVev){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsVev"} +
Theorem [224](#thm:MexicanHat){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MexicanHat"}, G2 grade):* $|\langle H\rangle|(p) > 0$ at
every spacetime event $p$ is derived from $|dx_4/dt| = c \neq 0$
everywhere --- the pointer must be "on" because the fourth dimension is
always expanding at every event. The Mexican-hat shape is forced as the
unique simplest renormalisable $G_{\rm EW}$-invariant potential with
local maximum at $|H| = 0$ (energetically disfavoured because the
pointer must be on) and global minimum at $|H| = v/\sqrt{2}$ (encoding
the pointer-on magnitude). *Subproblem H1 is solved as a theorem of the
framework*: the pointer must point because the fourth dimension is
always advancing.*

***Puzzle P3: *Why is the vev magnitude $v \approx 246$ GeV?* (The
magnitude puzzle, subproblem H2 of the hierarchy trichotomy.)***

**Orthodox-tradition position:* The numerical value $v \approx 246$ GeV
is an empirical input from electroweak precision measurements. No
principle predicts it. The standard Quantum Field Theory formalism takes
it as a parameter to be fitted.*

**Framework engagement
(Theorem [210](#thm:HierarchyTrichotomy){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HierarchyTrichotomy"} subproblem H2, open):* The
framework does not currently derive $v \approx 246$ GeV from
$dx_4/dt = ic$. The magnitude of the electroweak scale remains an
empirical input. *This is named in the framework as one of its open
problems*, at the same scope as the open analytic problems in standard
physics: the QCD string tension $\sigma \approx 1$ GeV/fm, the
confinement scale $\Lambda_{\rm QCD} \approx 200$ MeV, the proton mass
$m_p \approx 938$ MeV, the fermion-mass hierarchy. All are
dimensional-magnitude problems in standard physics that the framework
does not solve numerically.*

***Puzzle P4: *Why is the Higgs mass $m_H \approx 125$ GeV so small
compared to the Planck scale $M_{\rm Pl} \approx 10^{19}$ GeV?* (The
hierarchy problem proper, subproblem H3 --- radiative stability.)***

**Orthodox-tradition position:* The Higgs is treated as a fundamental
scalar in continuum effective field theory; quantum corrections to
$m_H^2$ should grow as $\delta m_H^2 \sim \Lambda^2$ where $\Lambda$ is
the UV cutoff. If $\Lambda = M_{\rm Pl}$, the radiative correction is
$\sim 10^{34}$ times the observed $m_H^2$, requiring $10^{34}$
fine-tuning of the bare parameter. The standard responses are: (a)
supersymmetry to cancel quadratic divergences (empirically constrained
at LHC); (b) composite Higgs at TeV scale (empirically constrained); (c)
anthropic / multiverse selection
[@ArkaniHamed-Colloquium-2013; @ArkaniHamed-NimaConversation-2024]. Tong
(Mindscape 321, 2025, [@Tong2025Mindscape321 54:47--55:47]) records the
contemporary state of orthodox puzzlement explicitly: "Higgs is not
natural. The hierarchy problem does not have a solution. I'm shocked by
this."*

**Framework engagement
(Theorem [210](#thm:HierarchyTrichotomy){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HierarchyTrichotomy"} subproblem H3 +
§[5.4](#ssec:NoFineTuningNoMultiverse){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:NoFineTuningNoMultiverse"}, G2 reframing):* The
framework reframes H3 at the technical-premise level by denying the
desert hypothesis. The radiative-correction calculation
$\delta m_H^2 \sim \Lambda^2$ is a calculation within continuum
effective field theory with cutoff $\Lambda$; it produces a physically
meaningful prediction only if continuum-EFT is valid up to $\Lambda$. In
the framework, the Planck scale $\ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^3}$ is the
substrate-scale terminus of continuum-EFT validity
(Theorem [12](#thm:ResolutionContentDiagnosis){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ResolutionContentDiagnosis"} Property (ii)): at
$\Lambda \sim M_{\rm Pl}$, continuum-EFT does not apply because the
substrate-scale McGucken-Sphere discretisation takes over. The desert
hypothesis fails because the Planck scale is the boundary of
continuum-EFT, not a cutoff inside an EFT. Under this reframing:*

-   *No $10^{34}$ fine-tuning is required (the continuum-EFT calculation
    that produces the apparent tuning does not apply);*

-   *No supersymmetry is needed (no quadratic divergences to cancel
    within the valid domain of EFT);*

-   *No multiverse is needed (the framework predicts a single universe
    with one set of physical laws).*

*The Arkani-Hamed fine-tuning-or-multiverse dichotomy is dissolved at
the technical-premise level. *The framework does not solve H3 within the
orthodox EFT formalism; it denies that the orthodox formalism applies at
Planck scale.* This is a reframing at theorem grade, not a constructive
analytic resolution within orthodox formalism.*

***Puzzle P5: *Why do the Yukawa couplings span five orders of
magnitude* ($y_e \approx 3 \times 10^{-6}$ to $y_t \approx 1$)? *And why
three generations?* (The fermion-mass hierarchy puzzle.)***

**Orthodox-tradition position:* Yukawa couplings are empirical inputs
fitted to fermion masses. No principle predicts the hierarchy spanning
five orders of magnitude. The number of fermion generations (three) is
also an empirical input; the orthodox tradition has no reason for three
generations rather than one, two, four, or any other number.*

**Framework engagement
(Theorem [218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:YukawaWinding"}, identification; numerical magnitudes
open):* The Yukawa coupling $y_f$ is identified at theorem grade as the
species-specific $x_4$-winding rate
(Theorem [218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:YukawaWinding"}): each fermion species $f$ acquires
Compton frequency $k_C^{(f)} = y_f v c / (\sqrt{2}\hbar)$ in the broken
phase. *The identification is established at theorem grade; the
numerical magnitudes $y_e \approx 3 \times 10^{-6}$ through
$y_t \approx 1$ are not derived from $dx_4/dt = ic$.* The
three-generation count is the subject of a separate open programme in
the corpus, flagged at
Remark [217](#rem:HiggsHonestOpenProblems){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:HiggsHonestOpenProblems"} below.*

***Puzzle P6: *Why is the Higgs the only fundamental scalar in the
Standard Model?* (The scalar-uniqueness puzzle.)***

**Orthodox-tradition position:* All other Standard Model degrees of
freedom are spinors (fermions) or vectors (gauge bosons). The Higgs is
the only fundamental scalar. The orthodox tradition has no reason for
this. Beyond-Standard-Model extensions (axions, dilatons,
two-Higgs-doublet models, scalar dark matter candidates) freely add
additional scalars with no constraint other than empirical viability.*

**Framework engagement
(Theorem [215](#thm:HiggsUniqueness){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsUniqueness"} of the present subsection, G2 grade):*
The Higgs is the unique scalar field with pointer, because the framework
has exactly one direction ($+ic$) to be pointed at, at each spacetime
event. The Higgs Uniqueness Theorem is established below.*

***Puzzle P7: *Why are there no Higgs domain walls, vortices, textures,
or magnitude variations observed cosmologically?* (The
absence-of-defects puzzle.)***

**Orthodox-tradition position:* Spontaneously broken scalar fields with
non-trivial topology in their vacuum manifold generically produce
topological defects --- domain walls (broken $\mathbb{Z}_2$), vortices
(broken $U(1)$), monopoles (broken $\mathrm{SO}(3)/U(1)$), textures
(broken $\mathrm{SU}(2)$). Cosmological observations rule out heavy
Higgs-related topological defects at significant abundance
[@Vilenkin1985CosmicStrings; @KibbleMechanism1976]. The orthodox
tradition treats this as a fortunate cosmological constraint without a
reason for why no such defects exist.*

**Framework engagement
(Theorem [228](#thm:NoDomainWall){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:NoDomainWall"}, G2 grade):* An absolute
bundle-topological prohibition on Higgs domain walls, vortices,
textures, and magnitude variations is established at theorem grade from
the global uniformity of $+ic$. The vacuum manifold has a single
$G_{\rm EW}$-orbit regardless of how many Higgs multiplets are added,
because multiple disconnected components would require the $+ic$
direction to differ across spacetime, contradicting $dx_4/dt = +ic$
uniformly at every event. The absence of Higgs topological defects is
established not as a fortunate constraint but as a prediction of the
framework.*

***Synthesis: three categories of engagement.***

**Resolved as theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$ (P1, P2, P6, P7):* the ontology
of the Higgs (pointer to $+ic$,
Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}), the existence of
$\langle H\rangle \neq 0$ (forced by $|dx_4/dt| = c \neq 0$,
Theorem [207](#thm:HiggsVev){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsVev"}), the uniqueness of the Higgs as the unique
scalar with pointer
(Theorem [215](#thm:HiggsUniqueness){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsUniqueness"} below), and the absence of topological
defects (Theorem [228](#thm:NoDomainWall){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:NoDomainWall"}). These are advances over standard QFT on
*what the Higgs is* and *why it must have the properties it has*.*

**Reframed at theorem grade (P4):* The hierarchy problem in its
Arkani-Hamed framing is dissolved at the technical-premise level by
denial of the desert hypothesis; the Planck scale is the substrate-scale
terminus of continuum-EFT validity. The puzzle is reformulated, not
constructively solved within orthodox formalism. This is a reframing,
not an analytic resolution.*

**Honestly open in both the framework and standard physics (P3, P5):*
the numerical magnitude of $v \approx 246$ GeV (H2), the numerical
magnitudes of the Yukawa couplings $y_e$ through $y_t$, and the
three-generation count. These remain as open in the framework as they
are in standard physics. The framework supplies identifications (Higgs
as pointer, Yukawa as winding rate); the analytic-numerics is not yet
derived from $dx_4/dt = ic$.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade and scope..* Each of the seven puzzles is engaged at the grade
explicitly stated.

*P1 (ontology):* G2 via
Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"} establishing the pointer identification.
Documentary at [@MG-Higgs2026].

*P2 (existence, H1):* G2 via
Theorem [207](#thm:HiggsVev){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsVev"} (vev non-vanishing from $|dx_4/dt| = c \neq 0$
at every event) and Theorem [224](#thm:MexicanHat){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MexicanHat"} (Mexican-hat shape forced by pointer-on
energetics). Documentary at [@MG-Higgs2026].

*P3 (magnitude, H2):* Honest-open in the framework. Documentary at
Theorem [210](#thm:HierarchyTrichotomy){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HierarchyTrichotomy"} subproblem H2.

*P4 (hierarchy, H3):* G2 reframing via
Theorem [12](#thm:ResolutionContentDiagnosis){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ResolutionContentDiagnosis"} Property (ii) (Planck scale
as substrate-scale terminus of continuum-EFT) combined with the denial
of the desert hypothesis in
§[5.4](#ssec:NoFineTuningNoMultiverse){reference-type="ref"

*P5 (Yukawa hierarchy, generations):* Identification at G2 via

*P6 (scalar uniqueness):* G2 via

*P7 (no topological defects):* G2 via
