The scoped claim of the present subsection: the orthodox-tradition's
repeated puzzlement over the Higgs decomposes into seven distinct
puzzles; the framework engages each at the appropriate grade; the
conflation of these seven puzzles in the orthodox literature as "the
Higgs problem" or "the hierarchy problem" is itself a source of
obscurity that the present subsection's disentangling addresses. ◻
:::

::: {#thm:HiggsUniqueness .theorem}
**Theorem 215** (Higgs Uniqueness: the McGucken pointer is the unique
fundamental scalar field carrying pointer under $dx_4/dt = ic$). *Assume
the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$
(Equation [\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"}); the pointer identification of the
Higgs as the field-theoretic encoding of the local $+ic$ direction
(Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}); the global uniformity of $+ic$
(Theorem [207](#thm:HiggsVev){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsVev"}, the same $+ic$ at every spacetime event); and
the bundle-topological framework of
§[5](#sec:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:HiggsPointer"}. Then:*

1.  ***There is exactly one direction at each event.** The McGucken
    Principle specifies a single direction $+ic$ at each spacetime event
    $p \in \mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}$: the direction of $x_4$-expansion.
    There is no second direction in the framework. Any candidate "second
    direction" would have to be (a) a second time-like direction,
    contradicting the identification of $x_4$ as *the* perpendicular
    time-direction; or (b) a spatial direction, in which case it would
    be one of $(\hat x_1, \hat x_2, \hat x_3)$ already accounted for by
    the $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-Haar isotropy of the McGucken-Sphere
    (Theorem [12](#thm:ResolutionContentDiagnosis){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:ResolutionContentDiagnosis"} Property (iv)); or (c) a
    non-spacetime direction with no geometry, which by
    Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:HiggsPointer"} cannot serve as a pointer field. Only
    (a)--(c) are exhaustive, hence the direction is unique.*

2.  ***The pointer field is the unique fundamental scalar carrying
    pointer.** A fundamental scalar field $\phi$ is a Lorentz-scalar
    field whose value at each spacetime event is a number (not a tensor,
    spinor, or geometric quantity with internal indices). For such a
    field to carry pointer under $dx_4/dt = ic$, it must encode a
    direction or magnitude tied to the principle. By Property (i), there
    is exactly one direction $+ic$ to be encoded; the Higgs field $H$ is
    the field-theoretic encoding of this direction
    (Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}, four real components: three
    orientation angles plus one magnitude). *Any additional fundamental
    scalar would have no direction to point at, and would therefore not
    carry pointer under $dx_4/dt = ic$.**

3.  ***Beyond-Standard-Model scalars are not forbidden by the framework
    but are not primitively anchored.** The framework does not forbid
    the existence of additional scalar fields (axions, dilatons,
    dark-sector scalars, two-Higgs-doublet extensions, etc.) at the
    level of mathematical consistency; what the framework establishes is
    that any such additional scalars would be *primitively unanchored*,
    i.e., they would not be theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$ but additional
    empirical inputs without derivation. The Higgs is therefore
    distinguished from any candidate additional scalar by being the
    unique primitively-anchored fundamental scalar in the framework.*

4.  ***The prediction: the Standard Model contains exactly one
    fundamental scalar (the Higgs); no additional primitively-anchored
    fundamental scalars exist.** This is a falsifiable prediction.
    Empirical discovery of a fundamental scalar at any energy scale that
    admits a derivation from $dx_4/dt = ic$ (parallel to the Higgs's
    pointer identification) without invoking ad hoc empirical input
    would falsify the uniqueness theorem in its strong form. Empirical
    discovery of additional fundamental scalars that do not admit such a
    derivation would be consistent with the uniqueness theorem (which
    leaves room for primitively-unanchored beyond-Standard-Model scalars
    at the level of mathematical consistency).*

5.  ***The contrast with composite-Higgs and elementary-scalar landscape
    proposals.** Composite-Higgs proposals replace the fundamental Higgs
    scalar with a composite bound state at TeV scale (the Higgs is then
    not fundamental). The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework rejects
    composite Higgs: the Higgs is fundamental as the field-theoretic
    encoding of the foundational $+ic$ direction, with pointer that no
    composite bound state could carry without already presupposing the
    pointer-direction. Elementary-scalar landscape proposals (axions for
    strong-CP, additional Higgs doublets for flavour structure, scalar
    dark matter candidates) introduce additional fundamental scalars as
    solutions to puzzles in standard physics (strong-CP, flavour, dark
    matter). The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's uniqueness theorem
    does not forbid such proposals from being mathematically consistent
    extensions, but identifies them as primitively unanchored: they
    would not be theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$ but additional empirical
    inputs.*

**The identification:* the Higgs is the unique fundamental scalar in the
Standard Model because the McGucken Principle has exactly one direction
at each spacetime event ($+ic$) to be encoded as pointer, and the Higgs
is the field-theoretic encoding of that direction. Additional
fundamental scalars, if empirically discovered, would be primitively
unanchored extensions of the framework, not theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G2 identification with G1 documentary at the underlying
theorems.

*Property (i)* is an exhaustion argument over the three possible
characters a candidate "second direction" could have. The exhaustion is
over: (a) second time-like direction --- excluded by the framework's
single time-direction $x_4$ content; (b) spatial direction --- accounted
for by the existing $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-Haar structure of the
McGucken-Sphere; (c) non-geometric direction --- excluded by the
requirement of geometry for pointer-encoding. The exhaustion is, not
merely an enumeration: any candidate direction must fall into one of
these three categories by virtue of being either time-like, space-like,
or non-spacetime; the framework excludes each category for the reasons
given.

*Property (ii)* follows from combining Property (i) with
Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}: the Higgs is the field-theoretic encoding
of the unique direction $+ic$; any additional fundamental scalar would
have no direction to encode, hence would not carry pointer under
$dx_4/dt = ic$. The G2 identification: pointer requires a direction to
point at; the framework has exactly one direction; the Higgs is the
encoding of that direction.

*Property (iii)* is a separability-of-claims observation: the framework
does not claim that additional scalars are mathematically impossible;
the framework claims that any additional scalars would be primitively
unanchored. This is a precise distinction: mathematical-consistency
claims operate at the level of internal-consistency of the extended
Lagrangian; primary-anchoring claims operate at the level of derivation
from $dx_4/dt = ic$. The framework's uniqueness theorem operates at the
primary-anchoring level only.

*Property (iv)* is the falsifiable-prediction content of the theorem:
the framework's strong-form claim is that no additional fundamental
scalars admitting derivation from $dx_4/dt = ic$ exist. The weak-form
claim (primitively-unanchored additional scalars permitted at the level
of mathematical consistency) is not falsifiable in the same way. The
grade reflects the scope: the strong-form claim is what the framework
establishes.

*Property (v)* is the comparative-engagement content distinguishing the
framework's position from composite-Higgs and
elementary-scalar-landscape alternatives, with explicit identification
of where each alternative differs from the framework's commitment. ◻
:::

::: {#rem:DeeperReasonHiggsPuzzling .remark}
*Remark 216* (The deeper reason the Higgs has been puzzling for sixty
years). The synthesis of the seven puzzles via
Theorem [214](#thm:SevenHiggsPuzzlesCatalog){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SevenHiggsPuzzlesCatalog"} identifies the source of the
orthodox tradition's repeated puzzlement: *the orthodox tradition
postulates the Higgs as a technical device without supplying a physical
identity, then encounters multiple distinct difficulties (ontology,
existence, magnitude, radiative stability, Yukawa hierarchy, uniqueness,
defect absence) that the orthodox formalism cannot tell apart from each
other.* The conflation of seven distinct puzzles into "the Higgs
problem" or "the hierarchy problem" obscures that these puzzles require
distinct engagement.

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's advance: identifying the Higgs
as the field-theoretic pointer to $+ic$ at theorem grade gives the Higgs
a physical identity from which most of the puzzles dissolve at theorem
grade or are reframed at premise level. The framework leaves open
exactly the analytic-numerical magnitude problems that are also open in
standard physics: subproblem H2 (the magnitude $v \approx 246$ GeV) and
the Yukawa-coupling numerical magnitudes (subproblem P5).

*Standard physics has been puzzled about the Higgs for sixty years
because it took the Higgs as a technical device without a physical
identity.* The framework supplies the physical identity (pointer to
$+ic$) and finds that most of the puzzles were identification puzzles
that dissolve once the identity is established, with the residual
analytic puzzles being the same dimensional-magnitude problems that
beset every Quantum Field Theory (the GeV scale of $v$, the GeV scale of
$\Lambda_{\rm QCD}$, the eV-to-GeV span of fermion masses). The orthodox
tradition treats $v$, $\Lambda_{\rm QCD}$, and the fermion masses as
three separate puzzles; the framework recognises them as instances of
the same general open problem of
dimensional-magnitude-of-the-broken-scale, common to electroweak
symmetry breaking, QCD confinement, and chiral symmetry breaking. *The
framework neither solves this general open problem nor pretends to.*
:::

::: {#rem:HiggsHonestOpenProblems .remark}
*Remark 217* (Honest open problems and the framework's scope on the
Higgs). We name explicitly the framework's open problems on the Higgs
sector, alongside the parallel open problems in standard physics. The
framework does not solve any of these; the framework establishes that
they are distinct from the puzzles that the framework does solve at
theorem grade.

**Open problems in the framework on the Higgs sector:**

-   *The magnitude $v \approx 246$ GeV* (subproblem H2 of
    Theorem [210](#thm:HierarchyTrichotomy){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:HierarchyTrichotomy"}). Empirically determined; not
    derived from $dx_4/dt = ic$. Parallel to the QCD string-tension
    $\sigma$, the confinement scale $\Lambda_{\rm QCD}$, the proton mass
    $m_p$. Subject of the open MG-Higgs2026 programme [@MG-Higgs2026].

-   *The Yukawa coupling magnitudes $y_e$ through $y_t$, spanning five
    orders of magnitude.* Identification as $x_4$-winding rates
    established (Theorem [218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:YukawaWinding"}); numerical magnitudes not derived.
    Parallel to the corresponding open problem in standard physics.

-   *The three-generation count of Standard Model fermions.* The
    framework does not currently derive the number of generations from
    $dx_4/dt = ic$. Subject of the open MG-Generations programme (in
    preparation).

-   *The Higgs self-coupling $\lambda$ and its renormalisation-group
    running to the vacuum-stability boundary.* The Mexican-hat shape is
    established (Theorem [224](#thm:MexicanHat){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MexicanHat"}); the numerical value of $\lambda$ at
    the electroweak scale, and the question of whether the Standard
    Model vacuum is absolutely stable, metastable, or unstable at high
    field values, are not derived from $dx_4/dt = ic$. Standard
    precision-electroweak measurements give the running of $\lambda$.

**What the framework does establish at theorem grade on the Higgs
sector:**

-   Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}: the Higgs is the field-theoretic
    pointer to $+ic$.

-   Theorem [207](#thm:HiggsVev){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:HiggsVev"}: the vev is non-vanishing and globally
    homogeneous; the $G_{\rm EW}$-bundle is topologically trivial.

-   Theorem [224](#thm:MexicanHat){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MexicanHat"}: the Mexican-hat shape is forced by the
    pointer-on energetic requirement.

-   Theorem [218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:YukawaWinding"}: the Yukawa coupling is identified as
    the species-specific $x_4$-winding rate.

-   Theorem [220](#thm:MatterFeelsX4){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MatterFeelsX4"}: electroweak symmetry breaking is the
    switch turning on matter's coupling to $x_4$.

-   Theorem [226](#thm:ComponentSplit){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:ComponentSplit"}: the 3+1 component split is forced
    by the geometry of recording a direction in 4-space.

-   Theorem [228](#thm:NoDomainWall){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:NoDomainWall"}: absolute bundle-topological
    prohibition on Higgs domain walls, vortices, textures, and magnitude
    variations.

-   Theorem [210](#thm:HierarchyTrichotomy){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:HierarchyTrichotomy"}: the orthodox "hierarchy
    problem" splits into the three subproblems (H1, H2, H3), with H1
    solved at theorem grade, H3 reframed at premise level, and H2 open.

-   Theorem [214](#thm:SevenHiggsPuzzlesCatalog){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:SevenHiggsPuzzlesCatalog"}: the orthodox tradition's
    repeated puzzlement over the Higgs decomposes into seven distinct
    puzzles, with each engaged at the appropriate grade.

-   Theorem [215](#thm:HiggsUniqueness){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:HiggsUniqueness"}: the Higgs is the unique
    primitively-anchored fundamental scalar in the framework.

**The scope of the framework's Higgs treatment:** the framework
establishes ten theorems on the content of the Higgs sector; the
framework leaves four open problems (O1)--(O4); the framework's advance
over standard physics is in the identifications (ontology, existence,
Mexican-hat, Yukawa, EWSB, components, defects, uniqueness, puzzle
catalog) and in the reframing of the hierarchy problem; the framework's
open problems are the same dimensional-magnitude problems open in
standard physics.
:::

#### Theorem H4: Yukawa coupling as species-specific $x_4$-winding rate {#ssec:YukawaWinding}

::: {#thm:YukawaWinding .theorem}
**Theorem 218** (Yukawa as winding rate [@MG-Higgs2026]). *Assume the
matter orientation condition (M) and the broken phase
$\langle H\rangle = (0, v/\sqrt{2})^\top$. The Yukawa coupling $y_f$ of
each fermion species $f$ is identified as the dimensionless coefficient
setting the species-specific Compton-frequency $x_4$-winding rate:
$$\label{eq:YukawaWinding}
k_C^{(f)} \;=\; \frac{m_f c}{\hbar} \;=\; \frac{y_f v c}{\sqrt{2}\hbar}.$$
The wavefunction of species $f$ in the broken phase is therefore
$$\Psi^{(f)}(\mathbf{x}, x_4) \;=\; \Psi_0^{(f)}(\mathbf{x}) \cdot \exp\!\left(+I \cdot \frac{y_f v c}{\sqrt{2}\hbar} \cdot x_4\right),$$
winding around $x_4$ at the species-specific rate
$k_C^{(f)} \propto y_f$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* By the matter orientation condition (M) of
Definition [80](#def:OrientationM){reference-type="ref"
reference="def:OrientationM"}, a matter field of mass $m$ satisfies
$\Psi(\mathbf{x}, x_4) = \Psi_0(\mathbf{x}) \exp(+I k_C x_4)$ with
$k_C = mc/\hbar$. The standard Yukawa coupling in the broken phase
generates the mass $m_f = y_f v/\sqrt{2}$ from the vev
$\langle H\rangle = (0, v/\sqrt{2})^\top$. Substituting
$m_f = y_f v/\sqrt{2}$ into the Compton-frequency formula yields
[\[eq:YukawaWinding\]](#eq:YukawaWinding){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:YukawaWinding"}. ◻
:::

::: remark
*Remark 219* (The interpretive content of the Yukawa coupling).
Theorem [218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:YukawaWinding"} converts the Standard-Model Yukawa
coupling $y_f$ from an opaque dimensionless parameter into a interpreted
quantity: $y_f$ is the dial that, in the broken phase
$\langle H\rangle \neq 0$, sets the rate at which species $f$'s
wavefunction winds around the fourth dimension. The empirical Yukawa
hierarchy $y_e \approx 3 \times 10^{-6}$, $y_t \approx 1$ becomes the
empirical $x_4$-winding-rate hierarchy: the electron's wavefunction
winds slowly around $x_4$, the top quark's wavefunction at the
McGucken-pointer rate $v c/(\sqrt{2}\hbar)$. The Yukawa hierarchy is the
$x_4$-winding-rate hierarchy. (The numerical values of the individual
$y_f$ remain empirical inputs; the interpretation does not derive them.)
:::

#### Theorem H5: EWSB as the "matter feels $x_4$" switch {#ssec:MatterFeelsX4}

::: {#thm:MatterFeelsX4 .theorem}
**Theorem 220** (The matter-feels-$x_4$ switch [@MG-Higgs2026]). *Assume
the matter orientation condition (M). In the unbroken phase
$\langle H\rangle = 0$, every fermion species has $m_f = 0$, hence
$k_C^{(f)} = 0$, hence $\Psi(\mathbf{x}, x_4) = \Psi_0(\mathbf{x})$ is
independent of $x_4$. In the broken phase
$\langle H\rangle = (0, v/\sqrt{2})^\top$, each species has
$k_C^{(f)} = y_f v c/(\sqrt{2}\hbar) > 0$, hence $\Psi(\mathbf{x}, x_4)$
depends non-trivially on $x_4$ via the Compton phase.*

*The transition between the phases is electroweak symmetry breaking. In
the symmetric phase, matter does not couple to $x_4$ (the fourth
dimension is still expanding everywhere at velocity $c$, but matter is
decoupled from it); in the broken phase, it does (matter wavefunctions
pick up species-specific phase advances per unit $x_4$).*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* *(i) Unbroken phase.* If $\langle H\rangle = 0$, then
$m_f = y_f \cdot 0/\sqrt{2} = 0$ for every species. By (M),
$k_C = mc/\hbar = 0$, so
$\Psi(\mathbf{x}, x_4) = \Psi_0(\mathbf{x}) \cdot \exp(0) = \Psi_0(\mathbf{x})$
--- independent of $x_4$. The wavefunction's $x_4$-independence is the
statement that the fermion does not couple to the (still expanding)
fourth dimension: no phase advance, no winding, no coupling. The fermion
is decoupled from the McGucken background.

*(ii) Broken phase.* If
$\langle H\rangle = (0, v/\sqrt{2})^\top \neq 0$, then
$m_f = y_f v/\sqrt{2}$ is nonzero. By (M) and
Theorem [218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:YukawaWinding"},
$\Psi(\mathbf{x}, x_4) = \Psi_0(\mathbf{x}) \exp(+I k_C^{(f)} x_4)$,
non-trivial in $x_4$. The wavefunction's non-trivial $x_4$-dependence is
the statement that the fermion now couples to the spherically expanding
fourth dimension at the species-specific Compton rate.

*(iii) The transition.* The transition
$\langle H\rangle = 0 \to \langle H\rangle = (0, v/\sqrt{2})^\top$ is
precisely electroweak symmetry breaking, and is precisely the transition
between matter not feeling $x_4$ and matter feeling $x_4$. ◻
:::

::: remark
*Remark 221* (The deep physics of EWSB). The standard reading of EWSB
--- "the Higgs vev gives fermions mass via Yukawa coupling" --- is
restated in McGucken terms as: *EWSB turns on each species's coupling to
the fourth dimension*. The two readings have identical empirics; the
McGucken reading adds the physical referent. "Mass" is the rate at which
a particle's wavefunction winds around the spherically expanding fourth
dimension; "masslessness" is the absence of such winding. Photons and
gluons remain massless because they are pure $x_4$-oscillations on null
worldlines (item (ii) of the four-fold ontological structure of the
Foundational Principle); fermions and the $W^\pm, Z$ bosons acquire mass
because EWSB turns on their $x_4$-coupling at species-specific rates.
:::

#### Theorem H6: The Mexican-hat shape {#ssec:MexicanHat}

The Mexican-hat shape of the Higgs potential requires an additional
energetic postulate beyond the bare McGucken Principle. We state it
explicitly.

::: {#post:PointerOn .postulate}
**Postulate 222** (Pointer-on energetic preference [@MG-Higgs2026]).
Field configurations contradicting the McGucken Principle are
energetically disfavoured relative to configurations respecting it.
Specifically: among configurations of $H$ at fixed $\mathcal{M}$,
configurations with $|H| = 0$ at any point have higher energy than
configurations with $|H| > 0$ at every point.
:::

::: remark
*Remark 223* (Why this is a postulate, not a theorem). The McGucken
Principle is kinematical: it says the fourth dimension is expanding at
velocity $c$ from every event spherically symmetrically, with algebra
$dx_4/dt = ic$. It does not by itself supply an energy functional that
punishes deviations. To convert "the principle says $+ic$ is defined
everywhere" into "configurations violating this are higher-energy," an
additional dynamical input is required.
Postulate [222](#post:PointerOn){reference-type="ref"
reference="post:PointerOn"} is that input.
:::

::: {#thm:MexicanHat .theorem}
**Theorem 224** (Mexican-hat shape [@MG-Higgs2026]). *Assume the
McGucken Principle, the global uniformity postulate,
Postulate [222](#post:PointerOn){reference-type="ref"
reference="post:PointerOn"}, and the pointer identification of
Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}. The simplest renormalisable
$G_{\mathrm{EW}}$-invariant scalar potential $V(H)$ satisfying:*

1.  *local maximum at $|H| = 0$,*

2.  *global minimum at some $|H| = v_*/\sqrt{2} > 0$,*

*is $$\label{eq:MexHat}
V(H) \;=\; -\mu^2 H^\dagger H \;+\; \lambda (H^\dagger H)^2, \qquad \mu^2, \lambda > 0,$$
up to additive constants and total derivatives.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* *Step 1: $|H| = 0$ is unstable.* By
Postulate [222](#post:PointerOn){reference-type="ref"
reference="post:PointerOn"}, $V(0) > V(v_*/\sqrt{2})$ for any nonzero
$v_*$. Moreover, regions of spacetime cannot persist in $|H| = 0$ for
finite duration without violating the McGucken Principle's specification
of $+ic$ at every point. Hence $|H| = 0$ must be not merely a
higher-energy point but a dynamically unstable one --- small
fluctuations from $|H| = 0$ must be amplified rather than damped. An
unstable stationary point of a potential is a local maximum, requiring
$V'(0) = 0$ and $V''(0) < 0$.

*Step 2: $V$ depends only on $|H|^2$.* By gauge invariance of $V$ under
$G_{\mathrm{EW}}$, $V$ depends only on $G_{\mathrm{EW}}$-invariant
combinations of $H$. The unique gauge invariant of dimension at most 4
is $H^\dagger H = |H|^2$.

*Step 3: Polynomial form.* Write $V(H) = a + b|H|^2 + c|H|^4$. The
constant $a$ shifts the vacuum energy and is set to zero (or to the
cosmological constant) without loss of generality.

*Step 4: Sign constraints.* Stability at large $|H|$ requires $c > 0$.
Local maximum at $|H| = 0$ requires $V''(0) < 0$, i.e., $b < 0$. Writing
$b = -\mu^2$ and $c = \lambda$ with $\mu^2, \lambda > 0$ yields
[\[eq:MexHat\]](#eq:MexHat){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:MexHat"}.

*Step 5: Verification.* $V'(|H|) = 0$ gives $|H|^2 = \mu^2/(2\lambda)$,
i.e., $|H| = v_*/\sqrt{2}$ with $v_* = \sqrt{\mu^2/\lambda}$. The second
derivative is positive there (since $\lambda > 0$): global minimum.

*Step 6: Uniqueness of form, freedom of values.* The functional form is
uniquely the Mexican hat. The values of $\mu^2$ and $\lambda$ are not
fixed by the present argument; they remain empirical parameters. ◻
:::

::: remark
*Remark 225* (Open: derivation of $\lambda$). The numerical value
$\lambda \approx 0.13$ extracted from the observed Higgs mass
$m_h \approx 125$ GeV is not currently derived from the McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework. [@MG-Higgs2026 §14.2] conjectures a
$\mathbb{C}P^3$-sectional-curvature derivation; no completed derivation
is currently available. Until supplied, $\lambda$,
$v = \sqrt{\mu^2/\lambda}$, and $m_h = \sqrt{2\mu^2}$ remain empirical
inputs.
:::

#### Theorem H7: The 3+1 component split {#ssec:ComponentSplit}

::: {#thm:ComponentSplit .theorem}
**Theorem 226** (Geometric origin of the 3+1 split [@MG-Higgs2026]).
*Assume the McGucken Principle, the global uniformity postulate, and the
pointer identification of
Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}. The four real components of $H$ split, as
$G_{\mathrm{EW}}$-representations, into:*

-   *three real components forming a gauge-redundant orientation
    triplet, eaten by the broken-symmetry gauge bosons $W^\pm, Z$ via
    the Goldstone--Higgs mechanism;*

-   *one real component forming a gauge-invariant magnitude scalar, the
    physical Higgs $h$.*

*The match $3 + 1 = 4$ is forced by the geometry of recording a
direction in four-dimensional space.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* *Step 1: $H$'s components as orientation + magnitude.* By
Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}, $H$ has four real components, of which
three encode the orientation of $+ic$ in the local frame (parametrised
by $S^3 \cong \mathrm{SU}(2)$ as a manifold, up to spin double cover)
and one encodes magnitude. Total: $3+1=4$, matching
$\dim_\mathbb{R}H = 4$.

*Step 2: Orientation triplet is pure gauge.* The orientation parameters
depend on the choice of local frame in the 3-plane orthogonal to $+ic$.
By the global uniformity postulate the $+ic$ direction is fixed, but the
choice of orthogonal frame at each point is not specified --- different
choices at different points are physically equivalent. The
local-orientation symmetry group $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ (universal cover
$\mathrm{SU}(2)$) is therefore a gauge symmetry; the three orientation
parameters are pure gauge.

*Step 3: Goldstone and Higgs mechanism.* By Goldstone's theorem, the
breaking pattern $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times U(1)_Y \to U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$
involves three broken generators and produces three Goldstone bosons. By
the Higgs mechanism, in a gauge theory these Goldstones are absorbed by
the broken-symmetry gauge bosons as longitudinal modes, giving them
masses and removing the Goldstones from the physical spectrum.

The three Goldstones eaten by $W^\pm, Z$ are exactly the three
orientation parameters of Step 1.

*Step 4: Magnitude is gauge-invariant.* $|H|$ is invariant under
$G_{\mathrm{EW}}$, hence not a Goldstone, hence not eaten. It survives
as the physical scalar field $h(x) = |H(x)| - v/\sqrt{2}$, with mass
$m_h = \sqrt{2\mu^2}$ from
Theorem [224](#thm:MexicanHat){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MexicanHat"}.

*Counting check:* 4 real components = 3 gauge-redundant orientations
(eaten) + 1 gauge-invariant magnitude (physical $h$). ◻
:::

::: remark
*Remark 227* (Geometric meaning of the count). The Standard Model's
count of three Goldstones eaten arises from Goldstone's theorem applied
to the broken generators of $G_{\mathrm{EW}} \to U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$;
the count is mathematical, with no physical referent for the four real
components beyond their representation theory. The McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework adds the geometric meaning: the three eaten
components are the three orientation angles of $+ic$ in 4-space (the
spherically expanding fourth dimension's pointer direction), and the
surviving Higgs $h$ is the magnitude scalar of the pointer. The rigour
of the count is identical to the Standard-Model derivation; the meaning
is novel.
:::

#### Theorem H8: The No-Higgs-Domain-Wall Theorem {#ssec:NoDomainWall}

This is the sharpest empirically-falsifiable result of the Higgs sector
and the fourth "absolute prediction" of the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework (joining no proton decay, no monopoles, no fractional
charges).

::: {#thm:NoDomainWall .theorem}
**Theorem 228** (Absolute prohibition on Higgs topological defects
[@MG-Higgs2026]). *Assume the McGucken Principle, the global uniformity
postulate, and Theorem [207](#thm:HiggsVev){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsVev"}. Then in any extension of the Standard Model
Higgs sector consistent with these postulates, regardless of the number
of Higgs multiplets added:*

1.  *No Higgs domain walls (interfaces between gauge-inequivalent
    vacua).*

2.  *No Higgs vortices (line defects with non-trivial $\pi_1$ winding).*

3.  *No Higgs textures (point defects with non-trivial $\pi_2$
    winding).*

4.  *No spatial variation of $|\langle H\rangle|$ exceeding quantum
    fluctuations.*

*A single observation of any of (i)--(iv) refutes the McGucken
Principle's globally uniform $+ic$ assumption.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* We treat each case. The argument is bundle-topological,
generalising the No-Monopole proof of
Theorem [135](#thm:NoMonopole){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:NoMonopole"} in
Section [8](#sec:QED-PartI){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:QED-PartI"}.

*(ii) Vortices.* A vortex around a 1-cycle $S^1$ is classified by
$\pi_1$ of the vacuum manifold. For a single Higgs doublet, the vacuum
manifold is $S^3 = \{H \in \mathbb{C}^2: H^\dagger H = v^2/2\}$. Since
$\pi_1(S^3) = 0$, no vortices. (This holds in the SM as well; no
McGucken-specific input needed.)

*(iii) Textures.* Classified by
$\pi_2(\mathrm{vacuum\ manifold}) = \pi_2(S^3) = 0$. Same as (ii).

*(i) Domain walls --- the McGucken-specific result.* Domain walls
require the vacuum manifold to have multiple disconnected components,
with different spacetime regions sitting in different components.

In the SM with a single doublet: vacuum manifold $S^3$ is connected, so
no domain walls. In multi-Higgs SM extensions (two-Higgs-doublet models,
etc.): the vacuum manifold can have multiple disconnected components
(e.g., $\mathbb{Z}_2$-related vacua), permitting domain walls. *The SM
does not forbid these.*

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework forbids them. The argument:

By Theorems [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}
and [207](#thm:HiggsVev){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:HiggsVev"},
$\langle H\rangle$ records the $+ic$ direction at each point. By the
global uniformity postulate, the $+ic$ direction is globally uniform
across $\mathcal{M}$ relative to a globally consistent frame.
(Physically: the fourth dimension expands in the same direction at every
event of spacetime.) Therefore there is, up to gauge equivalence, a
single preferred Higgs configuration at each spacetime point: the one
aligned with the global $+ic$.

Configurations gauge-equivalent to this aligned configuration are
physically indistinguishable from it. Configurations not
gauge-equivalent to it would correspond to recording a $+ic$ direction
different from the global one, contradicting the global uniformity
postulate.

Therefore the McGucken-extended Higgs sector has a vacuum manifold
consisting of a single $G_{\mathrm{EW}}$-orbit: a single connected
component (modulo gauge). Multiple disconnected components are excluded
regardless of how many Higgs multiplets are added, because the
uniformity of $+ic$ is independent of the field content.

Domain walls are excluded.

*(iv) Magnitude variation.* By
Theorem [207](#thm:HiggsVev){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsVev"}(ii), $|\langle H\rangle|$ is constant on
$\mathcal{M}$. Quantum fluctuations of $|H|$ around this value are
permitted (these produce the physical Higgs $h$); persistent classical
spatial variation of $|\langle H\rangle|$ is excluded by the same
uniformity argument. ◻
:::

::: {#rem:NoDomainWallSharpness .remark}
*Remark 229* (Sharpness of the prediction). This is the sharpest
falsifiable prediction of the McGucken-Higgs framework, and the fourth
absolute prediction of the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework as a whole
(alongside no proton decay, no monopoles, no fractional charges). The
Standard Model and its multi-Higgs extensions permit domain walls under
appropriate cosmological conditions; the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework forbids them absolutely. Cosmological observations sensitive
to domain-wall networks --- gravitational-wave signatures from wall
annihilation, CMB anisotropy patterns characteristic of frozen-in walls,
large-scale-structure imprints --- can in principle detect or rule out
Higgs domain walls. A confirmed detection would refute the global
uniformity postulate, and through it the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework. To date, no such detection exists.

The prediction is sharper than any prediction made by any prior
framework on the same target. Connes' spectral noncommutative geometry's
prediction depends on the spectral triple chosen; gauge-Higgs
unification permits walls at multiple Wilson-loop vacua; Woit's
framework does not address walls; supersymmetric models with two Higgs
doublets permit walls in some parameter regions. Only the McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework gives an absolute, framework-defining
prohibition.
:::

#### Theorem H9: The prediction of the Higgs from $dx_4/dt = ic$ {#ssec:HiggsStructuralPrediction}

The eight Higgs theorems H1--H8 collectively establish a result not
previously named: the Higgs sector is a consequence of $dx_4/dt = ic$.
We make this explicit as Theorem H9.

::: {#thm:HiggsStructuralPrediction .theorem}
**Theorem 230** (Prediction of the Higgs from $dx_4/dt = ic$). *Assume
the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ and the auxiliary postulates
(A1)--(A3) of Part I (Clifford-algebra-compatible matter content,
Steenrod global-section topology on the $G_{\mathrm{EW}}$-bundle, and
Compton-frequency-compatible field-theoretic encoding). Then any field
theory consistent with the McGucken Principle must contain a field
$H: \mathcal{M} \to \mathbb{C}^2$ with the following properties:*

1.  ***Existence and doublet structure.** $H$ exists and transforms in
    the doublet representation of $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$.*

2.  ***Pointer identification.** $H$ is the field-theoretic encoding of
    the local $+ic$ direction of $x_4$'s expansion at each spacetime
    event $p \in \mathcal{M}$
    (Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}).*

3.  ***Non-vanishing vev.** $\langle H(p)\rangle \neq 0$ for every
    $p \in \mathcal{M}$
    (Theorem [207](#thm:HiggsVev){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:HiggsVev"}), with $|\langle H\rangle|$ globally
    homogeneous on $\mathcal{M}$.*

4.  ***Topological protection.** The vev is topologically protected
    against loop-level destabilisation
    (Theorem [209](#thm:VevLoopProtection){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:VevLoopProtection"}); subproblem (1) of the hierarchy
    trichotomy
    (Theorem [210](#thm:HierarchyTrichotomy){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:HierarchyTrichotomy"}) is solved as a theorem.*

5.  ***Mexican-hat shape.** The Higgs potential takes the Mexican-hat
    form $V(H) = -\mu^2|H|^2 + \lambda|H|^4$ with $\mu^2 > 0$,
    $\lambda > 0$ (Theorem [224](#thm:MexicanHat){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MexicanHat"}).*

6.  ***3+1 component split.** The four real components of $H$ split as 3
    (would-be Goldstone modes absorbed by $W^\pm$, $Z^0$) + 1 (the
    physical Higgs $h$)
    (Theorem [226](#thm:ComponentSplit){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:ComponentSplit"}).*

7.  ***Yukawa coupling structure.** The Yukawa couplings $y_f$ to
    fermion species $f$ are species-specific $x_4$-winding rates
    (Theorem [218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:YukawaWinding"}).*

8.  ***EWSB switch.** The non-vanishing vev is the field-theoretic
    "matter feels $x_4$" switch
    (Theorem [220](#thm:MatterFeelsX4){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MatterFeelsX4"}).*

9.  ***Absolute prohibition on topological defects.** No Higgs domain
    walls, vortices, textures, or vev magnitude variations
    (Theorem [228](#thm:NoDomainWall){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:NoDomainWall"}).*

10. ***Uniqueness within the framework.** $H$ is the unique scalar field
    of the framework; no second Higgs doublet, no additional scalar
    fields, no MSSM doubling are predicted.*

*The prediction is: any field theory consistent with $dx_4/dt = ic$ must
contain such a field $H$. The Higgs sector is forced.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade and sketch..* Grade 2: forced by $dx_4/dt = ic$ together with the
auxiliary postulates (A1)--(A3). Properties (i)--(ix) are established as
Theorems H1 through H8 of [@MG-Higgs2026], imported in
§§[5.1](#ssec:HiggsPointer1){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:HiggsPointer1"}--[5.10](#ssec:NoDomainWall){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:NoDomainWall"}. Property (x) follows from the uniqueness
of the $+ic$ direction encoding: there is one $x_4$-direction at each
event of $\mathcal{M}$, and one field-theoretic encoding suffices to
record it; introducing a second doublet would either redundantly encode
the same direction (and gauge-symmetrise to the single doublet) or
encode a different direction (and contradict the global uniformity
postulate of [@MG-Higgs2026]). Hence the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework predicts one and only one Higgs doublet. The combination of
(i)--(x) is the prediction theorem. ◻
:::

::: {#rem:HiggsPredictionEmpirical .remark}
*Remark 231* (Empirics of the prediction). The prediction
(Theorem [230](#thm:HiggsStructuralPrediction){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsStructuralPrediction"}) carries five specific
empirical predictions, each falsifiable:

1.  **One Higgs.** The framework predicts the existence of exactly one
    fundamental scalar doublet. The 2012 LHC discovery of the Higgs
    boson at $\approx 125$ GeV [@ATLAS2012; @CMS2012] is the empirical
    confirmation of (i)--(ii). Falsifiable by: discovery of a second
    fundamental scalar doublet (two-Higgs-doublet models, MSSM, etc.)
    would refute (x).

2.  **Doublet structure.** The Higgs is a doublet under
    $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$, not a singlet, not a higher representation. The
    four-component structure (CP-even neutral + CP-odd neutral +
    charged) is forced. Falsifiable by: discovery that the observed
    Higgs has a different group-theoretic structure under electroweak
    gauge symmetries.

3.  **Topologically protected globally non-zero vev.**
    $\langle H\rangle \neq 0$ everywhere in space, with
    $|\langle H\rangle|$ globally homogeneous. Falsifiable by: detection
    of Higgs domain walls (gravitational-wave signatures from wall
    annihilation), Higgs vortices (large-scale-structure imprints),
    Higgs textures (CMB anisotropy patterns), or spatial variation of
    $|\langle H\rangle|$.

4.  **Species-specific Yukawa couplings as $x_4$-winding rates.** The
    Yukawa couplings $y_f$ correspond, via $m_f = y_f v/\sqrt{2}$, to
    species-specific perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rates. Falsifiable by:
    detection of a fermion mass that does not match the
    Higgs-vev-times-Yukawa pattern.

5.  **Connection to cosmological $x_4$-expansion.** The Higgs vev is
    connected to $x_4$'s expansion at every spacetime event. The
    framework does not currently predict that $\langle H\rangle$ varies
    over cosmological time (this would require an extension of the
    present treatment), but it does predict that the connection between
    the Higgs and $x_4$-expansion is primary rather than coincidental.
    Open: empirical tests of cosmological evolution of
    $\langle H\rangle$ on cosmological timescales.

The five empirical predictions (P1)--(P5) jointly establish that the
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework is empirically distinguishable from
any framework not making the identification of the Higgs as the
$+ic$-pointer.
:::

#### Theorem H10: Rest mass as perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate at the Compton frequency {#ssec:ComptonX4Coupling}

We now establish the central physical-content theorem of the framework's
treatment of mass: rest mass is the rate at which a particle at
three-rest winds perpendicular through $x_4$, observed in three-space as
the Compton frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$.

::: {#thm:ComptonX4Coupling .theorem}
**Theorem 232** (Rest mass as perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate). *Assume
the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, the Master Equation
$u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ ([@MG-Master2Chains-2026 GR T1]), the four-fold
ontology of [@MG-Higgs2026; @MG-McGSpace], and
Theorems [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}
and [218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:YukawaWinding"}. Then for any massive fermion species $f$
of rest mass $m_f$:*

1.  ***Perpendicular-$x_4$-motion at three-rest.** The fermion at
    absolute three-rest has its four-velocity entirely in the
    perpendicular $x_4$-direction: $u^\mu = (c, 0, 0, 0)$ in the
    $(\hat x_4, \hat x_1, \hat x_2, \hat x_3)$ decomposition aligned
    with the local $+ic$ orientation. The fermion moves through $x_4$ at
    velocity $c$.*

2.  ***Compton-frequency winding.** The fermion's wavefunction phase
    advances at angular frequency $\omega_C = m_f c^2/\hbar$ along
    $x_4$: at three-rest,
    $\psi(p, x_4) \sim \exp(i m_f c/\hbar \cdot x_4)$, where the factor
    $i$ is the perpendicularity marker $i = (dx_4/dt)/c$ of
    Theorem 21.6bis.1 of [@MGWick]. The Compton frequency is the rate of
    perpendicular-$x_4$-winding of the fermion at three-rest.*

3.  ***Higgs-vev establishes the perpendicular direction.** The local
    $+ic$ direction at the fermion's spacetime location is encoded by
    $\langle H(p)\rangle$ via
    Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}: $\langle H\rangle$ records which
    direction $x_4$ is locally expanding, equivalently which direction
    the fermion at three-rest is locally winding through.*

4.  ***Yukawa coupling sets the species-specific winding rate.** The
    Yukawa coupling $y_f$ determines the rate at which species $f$ winds
    through this perpendicular direction at three-rest:
    $m_f = y_f v/\sqrt{2}$, where $v \approx 246$ GeV is the Higgs vev
    magnitude. The rest mass $m_f$ *is* the species-specific
    perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate, with units restored via
    $\omega_C^f = m_f c^2/\hbar = (y_f v/\sqrt{2}) c^2/\hbar$.*

5.  ***$E = m_0 c^2$ as the energy of perpendicular-$x_4$-motion.** The
    total energy of a massive particle at three-rest is the energy of
    its perpendicular-$x_4$-motion at velocity $c$:
    $E_{\mathrm{rest}} = m_0 c^2$. The famous mass-energy equivalence
    relation $E = mc^2$ is the energy of perpendicular-$x_4$-motion
    through the expanding fourth dimension; the factor $c^2$ is the
    velocity-squared of perpendicular-$x_4$-motion (with one $c$ from
    the magnitude of the four-velocity and one $c$ from the
    perpendicular-direction unit).*

6.  ***Photon limit.** A field with $y_f = 0$ (Yukawa coupling vanishes)
    has $m_f = 0$ and therefore no perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate.
    Such a field is stationary in $x_4$: it does not move perpendicular
    through $x_4$ but rather is carried by $x_4$'s expansion at velocity
    $c$. This is the photon state. The masslessness of the photon is the
    field-theoretic consequence of vanishing Yukawa-type coupling to the
    Higgs-encoded perpendicular direction; equivalently, the photon is
    at absolute rest in $x_4$, with $x_4$'s expansion at velocity $c$
    carrying the photon outward on the wavefront.*
:::

::: proof
*Sketch and grade..* Grade 2: each property follows by direct
calculation from the Master Equation, the four-fold ontology, and the
imported Theorems H1, H4 of [@MG-Higgs2026].

*Property (i)* follows from the Master Equation $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$
applied at three-rest. The four-velocity has magnitude $c$, and
three-rest means the spatial three-components vanish, leaving
$u^\mu = (c, 0, 0, 0)$ in the local frame aligned with $x_4$-expansion
at $+ic$. The fermion's worldline at three-rest is parametrised by
$x_4$-advance at rate $c$: $dx_4/d\tau = c$ where $\tau$ is proper time.

*Property (ii)* follows from Property (i) plus the quantum-mechanical
phase identification of [@MG-CCR Theorem 3.1]: the wavefunction phase
along the timelike direction (which is the integrated coordinate label
of $x_4$'s expansion) advances at angular frequency $mc^2/\hbar$, the
Compton frequency. Under the McGucken-framework identification, this is
the rate of perpendicular-$x_4$-winding at three-rest. The factor $i$ in
the phase is the perpendicularity marker per Theorem 21.6bis.1 of
[@MGWick]: $i = (dx_4/dt)/c$ is the algebraic signature of $x_4$'s
perpendicular orientation.

*Property (iii)* is
Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"} restated: $\langle H(p)\rangle$ encodes
the $+ic$ direction at event $p$.

*Property (iv)* is
Theorem [218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:YukawaWinding"} restated together with the standard
Higgs-mechanism mass formula $m_f = y_f v/\sqrt{2}$, with the
McGucken-framework reading that this is the species-specific
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate.

*Property (v) ($E = mc^2$).* The four-velocity of a rest particle has
magnitude $c$, entirely in the $x_4$-perpendicular direction. The rest
energy is the energy of this motion. Standard relativistic kinematics
gives $E_{\mathrm{rest}} = m_0 c^2$; the McGucken-framework reading is
that this is specifically the energy of perpendicular-$x_4$-motion at
velocity $c$. The $c^2$ factor decomposes naturally: the
kinetic-energy-like form $\frac{1}{2}m v^2$ generalises relativistically
to $m_0 c^2$ for $v = c$ perpendicular motion, with the factor of
$\frac{1}{2}$ absent because the motion is at fixed-magnitude $c$ rather
than along a Newtonian potential. The Einstein 1905 identification of
$E = mc^2$ is, under the McGucken reading, the empirical-observational
anchor for the perpendicular-$x_4$-motion identification: every
measurement of a rest particle's energy (including its conversion in
nuclear reactions and annihilation events) is a measurement of the
energy of its perpendicular-$x_4$-motion.

*Property (vi) (photon limit).* A field with $y_f = 0$ has $m_f = 0$ by
the Yukawa-mass formula. By Property (iv) reversed, vanishing winding
rate means the field is stationary in $x_4$. The field's worldline (or
null worldsurface) rides $x_4$'s expansion at velocity $c$, which is the
photon state. Equivalently: the four-velocity becomes a null vector
$p^\mu p_\mu = 0$, the wavefront condition. The photon is at absolute
rest in $x_4$; $x_4$'s expansion carries it outward on the
McGucken-Sphere wavefront. ◻
:::

::: {#rem:EinsteinAnchor .remark}
*Remark 233* (The Einstein 1905 anchor). The identification of
Property (v) --- $E = mc^2$ as the energy of perpendicular-$x_4$-motion
--- deserves explicit emphasis. The famous Einstein 1905 relation
[@Einstein1905MassEnergy], empirically confirmed in countless nuclear
and particle-physics experiments, is in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework not a mysterious mass-energy equivalence but a direct
statement of the energy of a massive particle's perpendicular motion
through $x_4$ at velocity $c$. The factor $c$ appears twice because the
perpendicular-motion is at the velocity-of-light magnitude in the
perpendicular direction: one factor of $c$ from the magnitude of the
four-velocity component in the perpendicular direction, one factor of
$c$ from the rate at which the perpendicular direction itself is
expanding (the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Principle). The combination $c^2$ is
therefore the velocity-magnitude-squared of the
perpendicular-$x_4$-motion that the particle is performing at
three-rest. Nuclear binding energies, mass defects in fission and
fusion, and the energy released in matter-antimatter annihilation are
all measurements of the energy of perpendicular-$x_4$-motion --- a deep
physics that the standard reading of $E = mc^2$ as "mass-energy
equivalence" does not articulate.
:::

#### Theorem H11: The Mass-Energy-Geometry Theorem --- four-velocity rotation between perpendicular-$x_4$-motion and carried-by-$x_4$-expansion {#ssec:MassEnergyGeometry}

We now establish the geometric source of all relativistic phenomena:
every relativistic phenomenon descends from the geometry of
four-velocity rotation between two extreme kinematic states, both
intrinsic to the $x_4$-expanding ontology of the McGucken Principle.

::: {#thm:MassEnergyGeometry .theorem}
**Theorem 234** (Mass-Energy-Geometry Theorem). *Assume the McGucken
Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, the Master Equation $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$, the
four-fold ontology, and
Theorems [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}, [218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:YukawaWinding"}, [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}. Then the four-velocity of any
particle in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework lies between two
extreme kinematic states:*

::: description
*The particle moves perpendicular through $x_4$ at velocity $c$; the
spatial three-velocity vanishes; the four-velocity is
$u^\mu = (c, 0, 0, 0)$ in the local frame aligned with $x_4$-expansion.
The particle has the maximum perpendicular-$x_4$-motion permitted by the
Master Equation. Energy: $E_{\mathrm{rest}} = m_0 c^2$. This is the
state of a massive particle at three-rest.*

*The particle is at absolute rest in $x_4$; $x_4$'s expansion at
velocity $c$ carries it outward on the McGucken-Sphere wavefront. Its
four-momentum is null: $p^\mu p_\mu = 0$. The particle has zero
perpendicular-$x_4$-motion. Energy: $E_{\mathrm{photon}} = h\nu$. This
is the photon state.*
:::

*The two states are dual in a precise sense: in state (i), the particle
moves through $x_4$ at velocity $c$ with $x_4$ providing the substrate;
in state (ii), the particle is fixed in $x_4$ and $x_4$'s expansion at
velocity $c$ carries the particle. In both cases, the relative velocity
between particle and $x_4$ is the velocity of light.*

*For a massive particle at intermediate three-velocity $0 < v < c$, the
four-velocity is rotated from state (i) toward state (ii) by the
rapidity $$\phi = \operatorname{arctanh}(v/c),$$ with the rotation
acting in the $(\hat x_4, \hat v)$ plane where $\hat v$ is the unit
vector along the three-velocity direction. The four-velocity decomposes
as
$$u^\mu = (\gamma c, \gamma v) = (c \cosh\phi, c \sinh\phi \cdot \hat v),$$
with $\gamma = \cosh\phi = (1-v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$. The total energy at
three-velocity $v$ is $$E(v) = \gamma m_0 c^2,$$ which decomposes into
the rest-mass component $m_0 c^2$ (the perpendicular-$x_4$-motion
energy, now reduced by $1/\gamma$ in proper-time terms but
lab-frame-modulated) and the kinetic component $(\gamma - 1) m_0 c^2$
(the energy of the rotated four-velocity in the wavefront-direction
component).*

*The following relativistic phenomena descend from this four-velocity
rotation geometry as direct kinematic consequences:*

1.  ***$E = mc^2$ at rest.** State (i) energy. The energy of
    perpendicular-$x_4$-motion at velocity $c$.*

2.  ***$E = \gamma m_0 c^2$ at intermediate velocity.** Total energy of
    the rotated four-velocity at rapidity $\phi$.*

3.  ***Relativistic momentum $p = \gamma m_0 v$.** The spatial component
    of the four-momentum after the rapidity rotation.*

4.  ***Length contraction $L = L_0/\gamma$.** The proper length of a
    particle defined in its rest frame as an extended
    perpendicular-$x_4$-winding object is foreshortened in the lab frame
    by the projection of the rest-frame perpendicular-$x_4$-extent onto
    the lab-frame three-space, with the projection ratio
    $\cos\phi_{\perp} = 1/\gamma$ for the longitudinal direction.*

5.  ***Time dilation $\tau_{\mathrm{proper}} = t/\gamma$.** The rate of
    perpendicular-$x_4$-winding (Compton clock) measured in the lab
    frame is slowed by $1/\gamma$ relative to the proper-frame rate,
    because in the lab frame part of the four-velocity has been rotated
    away from $x_4$ and toward the spatial direction; the lab-frame
    projection of the Compton-clock rate onto the $x_4$-direction is
    reduced.*

6.  ***Velocity-of-light asymptotic limit.** As $v \to c$,
    $\phi \to \infty$, $\gamma \to \infty$. The four-velocity rotates
    asymptotically toward state (ii). Reaching state (ii) (i.e.,
    $v = c$) would require complete rotation, which requires infinite
    rapidity and infinite energy. Massive particles can approach but
    never reach state (ii), which is the strict-photon state.*

7.  ***Masslessness of the photon.** A photon is permanently in
    state (ii). It has no rest frame (no $v = 0$ frame exists); it has
    zero perpendicular-$x_4$-motion; it is stationary in $x_4$; $x_4$'s
    expansion carries it on the wavefront. Its rest mass is zero
    because, having no perpendicular-$x_4$-motion in any frame, it has
    no rest-energy from that motion. Its energy $h\nu$ is the energy of
    being carried by $x_4$'s expansion at the wavefront frequency
    $\nu$.*

8.  ***Mass as resistance to four-velocity rotation.** Rotating the
    four-velocity from state (i) toward state (ii) costs energy. The
    energy cost scales with the magnitude of the
    perpendicular-$x_4$-motion component being rotated, which is
    $m_0 c$. A more massive particle has a larger
    perpendicular-$x_4$-motion component, and rotating it costs
    proportionally more energy. Hence higher rest mass corresponds to
    higher inertia against three-acceleration --- the standard
    identification of mass with inertia, given a geometric grounding in
    the perpendicular-$x_4$-motion picture.*

9.  ***LHC particles are hard to accelerate.** A proton at the Large
    Hadron Collider with $\gamma \approx 7000$ has its four-velocity
    rotated by rapidity $\phi \approx 9.55$. The remaining
    perpendicular-$x_4$-motion component is reduced to $m_0 c / \gamma$
    in lab-frame projection, with the energy gained from acceleration
    ($\approx 5.6$ TeV at $\gamma = 7000$ for a proton) residing in the
    wavefront-direction component. Approaching state (ii) more closely
    costs exponentially increasing energy: at $\gamma = 7000$, doubling
    $\gamma$ requires increasing the energy by approximately a factor of
    two (proton energy at $\gamma = 14000$ would be $\approx 13$ TeV);
    but the rapidity $\phi$ only changes from $9.55$ to $10.25$. The
    wavefront limit is asymptotic; reaching it would require infinite
    energy because the four-velocity rotation toward state (ii) is
    bounded by $\phi < \infty$.*
:::

::: proof
*Sketch and grade..* Grade 2: each property follows from standard
relativistic kinematics applied to the four-velocity rotation between
states (i) and (ii), with the McGucken-framework reading of the
geometry. Properties (i)--(iii) are the direct relativistic
energy-momentum relations applied at rapidity $\phi$. Property (iv)
follows from the rapidity rotation acting in the $(\hat x_4, \hat v)$
plane: the proper-length extent of a particle defined as
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding has a spatial-frame projection reduced by
the cosine of the rotation angle, which is $1/\gamma$ for the
longitudinal direction in standard relativistic kinematics. Property (v)
follows similarly: the Compton-clock rate is the rate of
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding, and its lab-frame projection onto the
$x_4$-direction is reduced by $1/\gamma$ when the four-velocity is
rotated by rapidity $\phi$ from state (i). Property (vi) is the standard
$\gamma \to \infty$ limit as $v \to c$. Property (vii) follows from the
photon's four-momentum being null: $p^\mu p_\mu = 0$ corresponds to
state (ii) directly. Property (viii) follows from the fact that rotating
a vector requires energy proportional to its magnitude; the
perpendicular-$x_4$-motion component has magnitude $m_0 c$, hence
rotation costs scale with $m_0$. Property (ix) is the numerical
instantiation of Property (viii) at LHC energies.

The McGucken-framework content is in the *identification* of the two
extreme states as the perpendicular-$x_4$-motion state and the
carried-by-$x_4$-expansion state, with all relativistic phenomena as
kinematic consequences of rotation between them. The rotation is in real
geometric space-time (specifically, the $(\hat x_4, \hat v)$ plane), not
in any abstract or formal sense. This is the geometry of relativistic
kinematics in the framework. ◻
:::

::: {#rem:HiggsNecessaryForMass .remark}
*Remark 235* (Why the Higgs is necessary for mass).
Theorems [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}
and [234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"} together establish the deep physical
reason why the Higgs is necessary for fermion mass. Without the Higgs
vev, no perpendicular direction reference is established at each
spacetime event. Without the perpendicular direction reference, there is
no direction for fermions to wind through; the only available kinematic
states are state (ii) (stationary in $x_4$, carried by $x_4$'s expansion
at velocity $c$). All fermions in such a Higgs-vev-less framework would
be photon-like (massless and travelling at $c$).

The Higgs vev creates the possibility of perpendicular-$x_4$-motion by
establishing the $+ic$-direction reference at every spacetime event. The
Yukawa coupling then sets the species-specific rate at which each
fermion species winds through this perpendicular direction. The
resulting winding rate is the species' rest mass, observed as the
Compton frequency $\omega_C = m_f c^2/\hbar$.

**In the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, the Higgs gives mass by
creating the perpendicular direction for fermions to wind through.
Without the Higgs, there would be no perpendicular direction --- and
therefore no mass for any fermion.** This is the reason for the standard
observation that the Higgs mechanism is responsible for fermion mass:
the Higgs vev provides the geometric reference frame that makes
perpendicular-$x_4$-motion possible.
:::

#### The Higgs--Inertia--Equivalence Principle--Principle of Least Action unification: closing the orthodox open problem identified by Synge 1960, Unnikrishnan--Gillies 2015, Ostoma--Trushyk 1999, and Bin Li 2025 {#ssec:EquivalencePrincipleUnification}

The orthodox tradition has carried an open problem for over sixty years:
the Higgs mechanism gives fundamental fermions their inertial mass via
Yukawa coupling, but no derivation within the Standard Model explains
why this Higgs-generated inertial mass should also be the gravitational
mass appearing in the geodesic equation of general relativity. This is
the equivalence-principle problem in its modern post-Higgs framing, and
it is documented as an open problem at primary-source grade across the
contemporary literature. We engage the open problem at theorem grade in
the present subsection, closing the chain that links the framework's
existing Theorems [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"},
[218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:YukawaWinding"},
[220](#thm:MatterFeelsX4){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MatterFeelsX4"},
[232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"},
and [234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"} to the equivalence principle, the
principle of least action, and the local invariance of $dx_4/dt = ic$
under spacetime curvature.

###### The orthodox open-problem status, documented at primary-source grade.

Four primary-source documentations establish the open-problem status
across sixty-five years of orthodox-tradition recognition.

*Synge 1960* [@Synge1960 Preface, pp. IX--X], verbatim:

> "I have never been able to understand this Principle. Does it mean
> that the effects of a gravitational field are indistinguishable from
> the effects of an observer's acceleration? If so, it is false. In
> Einstein's theory, either there is a gravitational field or there is
> none, according as the Riemann tensor does not or does vanish. This is
> an absolute property; it has nothing to do with any observer's
> world-line. Space-time is either flat or curved... The Principle of
> Equivalence performed the essential office of midwife at the birth of
> general relativity... I suggest that the midwife be now buried with
> appropriate honours and the facts of absolute space-time faced."

Synge's identification: the equivalence principle, in its post-1916
orthodox formulation, is a postulate that has never been derived from a
deeper principle. Synge's proposal to "bury the midwife" with honour
reflects the orthodox-tradition recognition that the equivalence
principle, while empirically extraordinarily well-confirmed (Eötvös
experiments, lunar laser ranging, MICROSCOPE 2017
[@Touboul2017MICROSCOPE] confirming the universality of free fall to one
part in $10^{15}$), is a postulate rather than a theorem in the orthodox
framework.

*Ostoma and Trushyk 1999* [@OstomaTrushyk1999EMQGSummary §B], verbatim:

> "IN GENERAL RELATIVITY, THE PRINCIPLE OF EQUIVALENCE MUST BE ACCEPTED
> ONLY AS A POSTULATE, AND CANNOT BE DERIVED. Why should there be
> equivalence between inertial and gravitational mass? After all, both
> these mass types are defined differently in conventional Newtonian
> physics. Inertial mass involves accelerated motion, but there appears
> to be no motion involved in the definition of gravitational mass. In
> general relativity, equivalence has still remained a postulate as
> first proposed by Einstein, in spite of 70 years of investigation,
> albeit a very well tested postulate."

The Ostoma--Trushyk electromagnetic-quantum-gravity programme
[@OstomaTrushyk1999EMQGEP; @OstomaTrushyk1999EMQGSummary] attempts a
quantum-vacuum-fluctuations derivation of the equivalence principle; we
record the Ostoma--Trushyk primary-source recognition of the
open-problem status, while noting that the EMQG programme has not been
adopted in mainstream physics.

*Unnikrishnan and Gillies 2015* [@UnnikrishnanGillies2015], Tata
Institute of Fundamental Research and University of Virginia, Gravity
Research Foundation 2015 Awards (honourable mention), published in
*International Journal of Modern Physics D* **24**(14):1544009 (2015).
The paper's title verbatim: "Is the Higgs Mechanism true to the
Equivalence Principle?" Verbatim abstract:

> "We raise and discuss the fundamental issue whether the
> interaction-induced inertia in the Higgs mechanism is the same as the
> charge of gravity, or the gravitational mass. True physical mass has
> to fulfill the dual role of inertia and the gravitational charge and
> should respect the weak equivalence principle. *This is not yet
> addressed in the standard model that does not incorporate gravity.*
> Hence the Higgs scenario still requires a gravitational completion."

The technical argument of Unnikrishnan--Gillies (verbatim from the body
of the paper): *"interaction-induced inertia need not always generate
equivalent gravity, as we now argue from a familiar example... the
effective mass of an electron in a solid can be negative or even diverge
in magnitude, seemingly without any gravitational signature, signifying
that the inertia generated by interaction in that case is only a
pseudo-mass without a gravitational implication... This fact instructs
us to be cautious about any scheme that merely provides inertia in the
sense of enhanced reluctance to free motion, without generating enhanced
gravitational field."* Their conclusion verbatim: *"Inertia that does
not contribute its full gravitational equivalence is not true mass.
Gravitational mass could be more fundamental than inertial mass and the
hardest task of the theory is to explain the origin of the gravitational
mass."*

*Bin Li 2025* [@BinLi2025ChrononFieldTheory], "Revisiting Mass
Generation: Higgs Mechanism and a Topological Alternative via Chronon
Field Theory," Preprints.org 202506.2073 (June 2025), DOI
10.20944/preprints202506.2073.v1, §3.4 verbatim:

> "Another deep shortcoming of the Higgs mechanism is its failure to
> illuminate the equivalence between inertial and gravitational
> mass... in the SM framework, mass arises from interactions with the
> Higgs field, a scalar field that does not couple to spacetime
> curvature in any fundamental way. The mechanism is agnostic about
> gravity: it describes how particles resist acceleration due to
> Higgs-mediated interactions, but not how they gravitate. *There is no
> derivation within the SM showing why a particle's inertial mass,
> generated by the Higgs field, should also be the quantity appearing in
> the geodesic equation of GR.*"

Bin Li's Chronon Field Theory proposal (a unit-norm future-directed
timelike vector field as the ontological substrate, with mass arising
from solitonic excitations producing both inertial and gravitational
mass) is the contemporary primary-source articulation closest in spirit
to the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework: both treat the fourth
(temporal) direction as the source, and both propose that inertial and
gravitational mass coincide because they have a common origin. The two
frameworks are distinct: Chronon Field Theory has a unit-norm timelike
vector field $\Phi^\mu$ with $\Phi^\mu \Phi_\mu = -1$, no derivation of
$c$ or $\hbar$ from the principle, no McGucken-Sphere wavefront, no
dual-channel architecture, and no unification with the Standard Model
gauge content; the McGucken framework has the principle $dx_4/dt = ic$
from which $c$ and $\hbar$ are derived
(§[\[ssec:FoundationalPrinciple\]](#ssec:FoundationalPrinciple){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:FoundationalPrinciple"}; [@MG-Sphere2026 §5.2, §11.2]),
the McGucken-Sphere wavefront, the dual-channel architecture, and
theorem-grade derivation of
$U(1)_Y \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ and the Higgs
sector. The two frameworks share the insight that the equivalence
problem is closed by identifying inertial and gravitational mass as the
same fundamental thing under a common principle, with distinct technical
content.

###### The framework's existing framework that closes the chain.

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework establishes, at theorem grade in
the existing manuscript, four identifications that together close the
equivalence-principle / Higgs-inertia / principle-of-least-action open
problem:

1.  **Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:HiggsPointer"} (Higgs as pointer to $+ic$):** the
    Higgs field $H$ is the field-theoretic encoding of the local $+ic$
    direction at each spacetime event, with four real components
    splitting as three orientation angles plus one magnitude.

2.  **Theorem [218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:YukawaWinding"} (Yukawa as $x_4$-winding rate):**
    each fermion species $f$ acquires Compton frequency
    $k_C^{(f)} = y_f v c / (\sqrt{2}\hbar)$ in the broken phase, with
    $y_f$ the species-specific Yukawa coupling.

3.  **Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"} (rest mass as
    perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate):** the rest mass $m_f$ of any
    fermion species is identified with the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding
    rate at Compton frequency $\omega_C^{(f)} = m_f c^2/\hbar$. *Rest
    mass IS the $x_4$-winding rate.*

4.  **Theorem [234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"} (Mass-Energy-Geometry,
    four-velocity rotation):** the four-velocity of any particle lies
    between two extreme kinematic states (full
    perpendicular-$x_4$-motion at three-rest; full
    carried-by-$x_4$-expansion at $v = c$ for a photon); inertia is the
    resistance to rotating the four-velocity away from straight-line
    motion in four-space, with the energy cost of rotation proportional
    to the $x_4$-component magnitude $m_0 c$.

The framework also has the principle of least action descending from
$x_4$-wavefront constructive interference at the McGucken-Sphere (per
[@MG-Huygens; @MG-Lagrangian; @MG-SingularMechanism2026], with the
latter paper's title naming the principle of least action verbatim as
one of the structures derived from $dx_4/dt = ic$).

*What the existing manuscript content does not yet establish
explicitly*: an Equivalence Principle Theorem stating that inertial mass
and gravitational mass are the same thing because both ARE the
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude. The present subsection
closes this gap.

::: {#thm:EquivalencePrinciple .theorem}
**Theorem 236** (The Equivalence Principle as theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$:
inertial mass and gravitational mass are the same thing because both ARE
the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude). *Assume the McGucken
Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$
(Equation [\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"}); the Higgs pointer identification
(Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}); the Yukawa-as-winding-rate
identification (Theorem [218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:YukawaWinding"}); the rest-mass identification as
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate
(Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}); the Mass-Energy-Geometry Theorem
(Theorem [234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"}); the four-velocity budget
$u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ ([@MG-Master2Chains-2026 GR T1]); and the McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's derivation of the Einstein field equations
from $dx_4/dt = ic$ ([@MG-Gravity2026 §8.4], [@MG-GR]). Then:*

1.  ***The inertial mass identified by the framework is the
    perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude.** Per
    Theorems [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}
    and [234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"}, the inertial mass of any
    massive fermion species $f$ is identified with the
    perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude at Compton frequency
    $\omega_C^{(f)} = m_f c^2/\hbar$. Inertia (resistance to
    acceleration) is the energy cost of rotating the four-velocity away
    from the species-specific perpendicular-$x_4$-winding state, with
    the cost proportional to the $x_4$-component magnitude $m_f c$.*

2.  ***The gravitational mass that sources spacetime curvature is the
    same perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude.** The stress-energy
    tensor $T_{\mu\nu}$ that sources the Einstein field equations
    $G_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi G T_{\mu\nu}/c^4$ encodes the energy density and
    momentum density of matter. For a perfect-fluid description of a
    localised mass distribution, $T^{00} = \rho c^2$ where $\rho$ is the
    rest-mass density. The rest-mass density is, per (i), the integrated
    perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate-magnitude density. *The
    gravitational mass that sources spacetime curvature IS the
    perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude of matter, the same
    identified as inertial mass in (i).**

3.  ***Inertial mass and gravitational mass are the same thing in the
    framework: both ARE the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate
    magnitude.** The orthodox-tradition equivalence-principle postulate
    "inertial mass equals gravitational mass" is, in the McGucken
    $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, not a postulate of equality between two
    separate quantities but the identity: *inertial mass = gravitational
    mass = perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude, all three names
    refer to the same physics*. The empirical universality of free fall
    (Eötvös, lunar laser ranging, MICROSCOPE 2017
    [@Touboul2017MICROSCOPE]) is the empirical signature of this
    identity.*

4.  ***The equivalence principle is a theorem, not a postulate, in the
    framework.** The orthodox open problem (documented at
    [@Synge1960; @OstomaTrushyk1999EMQGSummary; @UnnikrishnanGillies2015; @BinLi2025ChrononFieldTheory])
    is the absence of a derivation explaining why inertial and
    gravitational mass should be the same. The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
    framework supplies the derivation: they are the same because both
    are names for the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude under
    the principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, with the Higgs as the pointer encoding
    the $+ic$ direction
    (Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}), the Yukawa coupling as the
    species-specific winding rate
    (Theorem [218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:YukawaWinding"}), and the four-velocity-rotation cost
    as the inertia
    (Theorem [234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"}).*

5.  ***The Unnikrishnan--Gillies 2015 heavy-fermion counterexample is
    engaged.** Unnikrishnan and Gillies [@UnnikrishnanGillies2015] argue
    that interaction-induced inertia (the effective mass of an electron
    in a solid, which can be 1000$\times$ the bare mass, negative, or
    divergent) need not generate equivalent gravity. The framework's
    reading: heavy-fermion effective masses arise from condensed-matter
    electron-lattice-electron interactions *within* a continuum-field
    effective theory at energies well below the substrate scale; they do
    not modify the fundamental perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate
    magnitude of the underlying electron (which is the bare
    Yukawa-induced rest mass $m_e \approx 0.511$ MeV/$c^2$). The
    effective mass in condensed matter is an effective-theory parameter
    describing the band-structure response to external fields; it is not
    a perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude. The framework's
    identification (i)--(iii) therefore correctly distinguishes *true*
    inertial mass (perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude, identical
    to gravitational mass) from *effective-theory band-structure*
    inertial mass (a condensed-matter response parameter, not identical
    to gravitational mass). The Unnikrishnan--Gillies counterexample
    does not falsify the framework's identification; it confirms that
    the framework's identification operates at the fundamental-mass
    level, with band-structure effective masses correctly treated as
    effective-theory parameters that do not source proportionally
    enhanced gravity.*

**The conclusion:* the orthodox open problem documented by Synge 1960,
Ostoma--Trushyk 1999, Unnikrishnan--Gillies 2015, and Bin Li 2025 is
closed at theorem grade in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework. The
equivalence principle is an identity: inertial mass and gravitational
mass are the same thing because both are the
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude, with the Higgs supplying the
$+ic$ direction reference and the Yukawa coupling supplying the
species-specific winding rate.*
:::

::: {#thm:MassBendsSpaceX4Invariant .theorem}

[@MG-Sphere2026 §11.2.3]). Then:*

1.  ***Mass-energy curves the global spacetime geometry via the Einstein
    field equations.** The stress-energy tensor $T_{\mu\nu}$, sourced by
    the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate-magnitude of matter
    (Theorem [236](#thm:EquivalencePrinciple){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:EquivalencePrinciple"} (ii)), enters the right-hand
    side of $G_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi G T_{\mu\nu}/c^4$, producing curvature of
    the global four-dimensional spacetime metric $g_{\mu\nu}$. This is
    the McGucken-framework realisation of Wheeler's "matter tells
    spacetime how to curve."*

2.  ***The local rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ is invariant at every spacetime
    event.** At each spacetime event $p \in \mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}$,
    every observer in their local inertial rest frame at $p$ observes
    $x_4$ expanding spherically symmetrically at velocity $c$. The
    Lorentz-covariance of the substrate
    (§[15.2.6](#ssec:LorentzCovarianceDissolvesDSR){reference-type="ref"
    reference="ssec:LorentzCovarianceDissolvesDSR"}; [@MG-Sphere2026
    §11.2.3]) guarantees that the same $x_4$-expansion at the same rate
    $c$ is seen by every inertial observer in their own local frame. The
    principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ holds locally at every event with the same
    $c$.*

3.  ***The geodesic motion of freely falling particles in curved
    spacetime is the realisation of inertia under $dx_4/dt = ic$.** In
    flat spacetime, free particles follow straight lines (geodesics of
    Minkowski metric), corresponding to constant four-velocity,
    corresponding to no rotation of the four-velocity, corresponding to
    no inertia work done against the rotation cost identified in
    Theorem [234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"}. In curved spacetime, free
    particles follow geodesics of the local metric, corresponding to
    constant four-velocity in the local-inertial-frame sense (with the
    four-velocity parallel-transported along the geodesic),
    corresponding to no rotation of the four-velocity relative to the
    local frame, corresponding to no inertia work done. *Geodesic motion
    in curved spacetime IS the curved-spacetime generalisation of
    straight-line motion in flat spacetime, with the inertia (resistance
    to four-velocity rotation) preserved as the same quantity in both
    cases.**

4.  ***The local invariance of $dx_4/dt = ic$ under curved global
    geometry is the McGucken-framework realisation of the strong
    equivalence principle.** The strong equivalence principle states
    that the laws of physics are the same in every freely-falling local
    inertial frame. In the McGucken framework, this is realised: the
    McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ holds in every observer's local
    rest frame at every spacetime event with the same value of $c$. The
    principle is locally Lorentz-invariant at every event regardless of
    the global curvature of the metric. *The same substrate, with the
    same $x_4$-expansion at the same rate $c$, is observed by every
    freely-falling observer in their own local frame, regardless of
    where they are in the curved spacetime.**

**The conclusion:* the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework realises "mass
bends space" (curved global geometry via Einstein field equations
sourced by perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate-magnitude) and
"$dx_4/dt = ic$ locally invariant" (the substrate's $x_4$-expansion at
the same rate $c$ in every freely-falling local frame) as compatible
features of the same framework. Geodesic motion in curved spacetime is
the curved-spacetime generalisation of straight-line motion in flat
spacetime under the inertia of
Theorem [234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"}.*
:::
