::: {#thm:LeastActionWavefront .theorem}
**Theorem 238** (The Principle of Least Action as McGucken-Sphere
wavefront-phase constructive interference along the classical path: the
unification with geodesic motion). *Assume the McGucken Principle
$dx_4/dt = ic$
(Equation [\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"}); the McGucken-Sphere wavefront
structure at every event
(§[\[ssec:FoundationalPrinciple\]](#ssec:FoundationalPrinciple){reference-type="ref"

the principle of least action from $x_4$-wavefront
([@MG-Huygens; @MG-Lagrangian; @MG-SingularMechanism2026]); the
Equivalence Principle Theorem
(Theorem [236](#thm:EquivalencePrinciple){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:EquivalencePrinciple"}); and the Mass-Bends-Space Theorem
(Theorem [237](#thm:MassBendsSpaceX4Invariant){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MassBendsSpaceX4Invariant"}). Then:*

1.  ***Each spacetime event sources a McGucken-Sphere wavefront
    expanding at $c$.** Per the McGucken Principle, every event
    $p \in \mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}$ sources a spherically-symmetric
    wavefront $\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}(p, t)$ expanding at $c$ from $p$. The
    wavefront carries wavelength, frequency, phase, and therefore action
    (§[\[ssec:FoundationalPrinciple\]](#ssec:FoundationalPrinciple){reference-type="ref"
    reference="ssec:FoundationalPrinciple"}, heart-and-soul statement of
    the present paper).*

2.  ***A particle's wavefunction phase $e^{iS/\hbar}$ accumulates along
    its worldline.** For a free relativistic particle of rest mass $m$,
    the action along its worldline is $S = \int (-mc^2)\, d\tau$ where
    $d\tau$ is the proper time. The wavefunction phase accumulates as
    $\exp(iS/\hbar) = \exp(-i m c^2 \tau / \hbar)$ along the worldline,
    with the Compton frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ identified per
    Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"} as the rate of
    perpendicular-$x_4$-winding.*

3.  ***The classical path is the path of constructive-interference
    wavefront-phase accumulation.** Per the Huygens--Feynman
    path-integral construction ([@MG-Huygens; @MG-Lagrangian]), the
    actual classical path is the path along which wavefront-phase
    contributions from neighbouring paths interfere constructively. The
    constructive-interference condition is the stationary-action
    condition $\delta S = 0$, which is the principle of least action.*

4.  ***In flat spacetime: the constructive-interference path is the
    straight line in four-space.** For a free particle in flat Minkowski
    spacetime, the stationary-action path is the straight line with
    constant four-velocity. This is the principle of inertia (Newton's
    first law) generalised to four-space, identified per
    Theorem [234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"} as the path with no
    four-velocity rotation, hence no inertia work done.*

5.  ***In curved spacetime: the constructive-interference path is the
    geodesic of the metric.** For a free particle in curved spacetime,
    the stationary-action path is the geodesic of the metric, with the
    action $S = \int (-mc^2) \, d\tau$ now integrated along the proper
    time defined by the curved metric. The constructive-interference
    path is the geodesic; the geodesic is the curved-spacetime path of
    no four-velocity rotation in the local-inertial-frame sense
    (Theorem [237](#thm:MassBendsSpaceX4Invariant){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MassBendsSpaceX4Invariant"} (iii)).*

6.  ***The principle of least action and the equivalence principle are
    two readings of the same.** *The principle of least action*
    (wavefront-phase constructive interference along the classical path,
    descending from McGucken-Sphere wavefront at every event) *and the
    equivalence principle* (freely-falling particles follow geodesics of
    the metric, with inertial mass and gravitational mass identical
    because both are perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude) *are
    two readings of the same*: the classical path is the geodesic; the
    geodesic is the constructive-interference path; both are the path of
    no four-velocity rotation in the local-inertial-frame sense; both
    descend from the McGucken-Sphere wavefront of $dx_4/dt = ic$.*

**The conclusion:* the principle of least action is the
constructive-interference content of McGucken-Sphere wavefronts at every
spacetime event, with the classical path identified as the
constructive-interference path. The equivalence principle's
geodesic-motion content is the curved-spacetime realisation of this same
content. *Principle of least action and equivalence principle are not
two independent postulates of physics; they are two readings of the same
wavefront-phase constructive-interference content of $dx_4/dt = ic$.**
:::

##### The deep unification: inertia, Compton-coupling rate, and the principle of least action are three readings of the same wavefront {#sssec:InertiaComptonLeastAction}

The chain of theorems established so far in this subsection ---
Theorem [236](#thm:EquivalencePrinciple){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:EquivalencePrinciple"} (inertial mass and gravitational
mass identical as perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude),
Theorem [237](#thm:MassBendsSpaceX4Invariant){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MassBendsSpaceX4Invariant"} (mass-bends-space +
$dx_4/dt = ic$-locally-invariant as compatible features), and
Theorem [238](#thm:LeastActionWavefront){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:LeastActionWavefront"} (principle of least action as
McGucken-Sphere wavefront-phase constructive interference) --- together
with the existing Theorems [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"},
[218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:YukawaWinding"},
[232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}, and
[234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"}, supply the pieces of a remarkable
triple identification that, to our knowledge, no other programme in the
primary-source literature has stated explicitly. We state it here as the
closing theorem of the present subsection.

::: {#thm:InertiaComptonLeastActionTriple .theorem}
**Theorem 239** (The triple identity: inertia = resistance to changing
the Compton-coupling rate = what the principle of least action
minimizes). *Assume the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$
(Equation [\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"}); the Higgs pointer identification
(Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}); the Yukawa-as-winding-rate
identification (Theorem [218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:YukawaWinding"}); the rest-mass identification as
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate at Compton frequency
(Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}); the Mass-Energy-Geometry Theorem
(Theorem [234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"}); the Equivalence Principle Theorem
(Theorem [236](#thm:EquivalencePrinciple){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:EquivalencePrinciple"}); the Mass-Bends-Space Theorem
(Theorem [237](#thm:MassBendsSpaceX4Invariant){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MassBendsSpaceX4Invariant"}); and the
Principle-of-Least-Action-as-Wavefront-Phase-Constructive-Interference
Theorem (Theorem [238](#thm:LeastActionWavefront){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:LeastActionWavefront"}). Then the following three
quantities are not three distinct quantities related by empirical
correspondence but are one of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront expansion
read in three ways:*

1.  ***The Compton-coupling rate.** The species-specific
    perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate
    $\omega_C^{(f)} = m_f c^2/\hbar = y_f v c^2/(\sqrt{2}\hbar)$ at
    which a fermion of species $f$ winds perpendicular through $x_4$ at
    three-rest, with the Higgs vev $v$ supplying the $+ic$ direction and
    the Yukawa coupling $y_f$ supplying the species-specific rate dial
    (Theorem [218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:YukawaWinding"},
    Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}). *The Compton-coupling rate is
    the wavefront-phase advance rate of the particle on the
    McGucken-Sphere at three-rest.**

2.  ***The inertia of mass.** The energy cost of rotating the
    four-velocity vector of the fermion away from the
    perpendicular-$x_4$-winding orientation toward a spatial-velocity
    orientation, with rotation rate $d\phi/dt$ in the four-space
    rapidity $\phi$, and energy cost proportional to the $x_4$-component
    magnitude $m_f c$ that must be rotated
    (Theorem [234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"}, Properties (iii) and (viii);
    Theorem [236](#thm:EquivalencePrinciple){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:EquivalencePrinciple"}, Property (i)). *Inertia is
    the resistance to changing the orientation of the Compton-coupling
    rate vector in four-space; equivalently, it is the resistance to
    changing the $x_4$-projection of the
    perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate vector.**

3.  ***The action quantity that the principle of least action varies.**
    The accumulated wavefront phase along the worldline,
    $S/\hbar = \int (-mc^2/\hbar)\, d\tau = -\int \omega_C\, d\tau$,
    with the wavefunction phase $\exp(iS/\hbar) = \exp(-i\omega_C \tau)$
    accumulating Compton-frequency winding as proper time advances along
    the worldline
    (Theorem [238](#thm:LeastActionWavefront){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:LeastActionWavefront"}, Property (ii)). *The action
    quantity the principle of least action varies is the accumulated
    Compton-frequency winding (the accumulated wavefront-phase advance)
    along the worldline.**

*The three quantities (A), (B), and (C) are not three separate facts
about the natural world that happen to coincide; they are one of the
McGucken-Sphere wavefront expansion at $c$ from every event, viewed from
three distinct angles:*

1.  ***Acceleration IS changing the Compton-coupling rate's orientation
    in four-space.** When a force is applied to a massive fermion, the
    four-velocity vector rotates away from the species-specific
    perpendicular-$x_4$-winding orientation by rapidity $\phi$. The
    lab-frame projection of the Compton-frequency winding onto the
    $x_4$-direction reduces by $1/\gamma = \cos(\phi)$
    (Theorem [234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"}, Property (v)); this is what
    relativistic time dilation IS in the framework's reading --- the
    lab-frame Compton clock ticks slower because the four-velocity has
    been rotated away from its perpendicular-$x_4$-winding orientation.
    *Acceleration in the four-space rapidity is the rate of change of
    the Compton-coupling rate's orientation.**

2.  ***Inertia IS the resistance to this rate of change.** The energy
    cost of rotating the four-velocity at rotation rate $d\phi/dt$ is
    proportional to the magnitude $m_f c$ being rotated
    (Theorem [234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"}, Property (viii)). This is what
    Newtonian inertia $F = ma$ is in the framework's reading: $F$
    supplies the rotation work, $a = d\phi/dt$ (at small velocities) is
    the rate of change of the Compton-coupling rate's orientation, and
    $m_f$ is the magnitude of the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate
    vector being rotated. *Newton's $F = ma$ is the four-space-rotation
    cost of changing the Compton-coupling rate's orientation, with $m$
    identified as the magnitude of the rate vector that must be
    rotated.**

3.  ***The principle of least action minimizes precisely this rate of
    change.** The action $S = -mc^2\int d\tau$ is the accumulated
    Compton-frequency winding along the worldline; stationary action
    $\delta S = 0$ selects the worldline along which the wavefront-phase
    contributions from neighbouring paths interfere constructively
    (Theorem [238](#thm:LeastActionWavefront){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:LeastActionWavefront"}, Property (iii)). Constructive
    interference of wavefront phases requires the phase-advance rate
    (the Compton frequency, the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate) to
    stay coherent along the path; this coherence is the absence of
    arbitrary rate-of-change of the Compton-coupling rate's orientation;
    this absence is geodesic motion
    (Theorem [238](#thm:LeastActionWavefront){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:LeastActionWavefront"}, Property (v);
    Theorem [237](#thm:MassBendsSpaceX4Invariant){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MassBendsSpaceX4Invariant"}, Property (iii)). *The
    principle of least action selects the worldline along which the
    Compton-coupling rate's orientation changes minimally, equivalent to
    the path of constructive interference of McGucken-Sphere wavefront
    phases, equivalent to the geodesic of the metric.**

**The triple identity, stated as one sentence:* **Inertia is resistance
to changing the Compton-coupling rate's orientation in four-space; the
principle of least action minimizes precisely this change; the
Compton-coupling rate itself is the wavefront-phase advance rate the
McGucken-Sphere supplies from every event; all three are one of
$dx_4/dt = ic$ read in three ways.***
:::

###### The remarkable depth of the triple identification.

It is worth pausing to articulate, in plain language, what
Theorem [239](#thm:InertiaComptonLeastActionTriple){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:InertiaComptonLeastActionTriple"} states. In the orthodox
tradition, three features of physics --- the inertia of mass (Newton's
$F = ma$), the rate-of-coupling of matter to the Higgs field (the
Compton frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ inherited via Yukawa
coupling), and the principle of least action ($\delta S = 0$ supplying
the equations of motion for classical and quantum mechanics) --- are
treated as three distinct postulates. Newton postulated $F = ma$ in
1687. The Higgs mechanism was constructed in 1964 by Englert, Brout,
Higgs, and Guralnik-Hagen-Kibble to give masses to particles consistent
with gauge invariance, and the Yukawa coupling rate that determines the
Compton frequency was inserted by hand for each fermion species. The
principle of least action was developed by Maupertuis, Euler, Lagrange,
and Hamilton over the 18th and 19th centuries, and elevated to the
foundation of all of physics by Hamilton in 1833 and by Feynman in 1948.
Across nearly three and a half centuries of physics, these three were
never identified as the same.

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework identifies them as one quantity
--- the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate vector on the McGucken-Sphere
wavefront --- viewed from three angles. Inertia is the resistance to
rotating this vector; the Compton-coupling rate is its magnitude; the
action the principle of least action varies is the accumulated phase of
its wavefront along the worldline. Acceleration is the rate of change of
its orientation, and the principle of least action selects the path that
minimizes this rate of change, equivalent to constructive interference
of the wavefront phases, equivalent to geodesic motion in the curved
spacetime sourced by the very same perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate
content via the Einstein field equations.

*Within the primary-source literature reviewed at full-read grade, no
programme other than the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework has stated
this triple identity.* Newton did not have the Compton frequency (the
Compton frequency requires both $\hbar$ from quantum mechanics and $c$
from special relativity, neither of which existed in Newton's
framework). Einstein did not unify inertia with the principle of least
action via Compton-frequency (the equivalence principle was a postulate
in his treatment, the principle of least action remained a variational
principle, and the Compton frequency was not yet identified when general
relativity was completed in 1915). Feynman's path-integral construction
unified the principle of least action with quantum-mechanical
wavefunction phase but did not identify the wavefunction phase as
Compton-frequency winding tied to the Higgs-pointer-encoded $+ic$
direction of $x_4$-expansion. The orthodox modern textbook treatments
(Weinberg, Peskin and Schroeder, Schwartz, Srednicki, Tong) state
Newton's $F = ma$, the Higgs mechanism with Yukawa couplings, and the
principle of least action as three distinct postulates without
identifying them as one. The contemporary alternative programmes
(Chronon Field Theory [@BinLi2025ChrononFieldTheory], EMQG
[@OstomaTrushyk1999EMQGEP], TEGR/STEGR
[@Capozziello2025EquivalenceGravities], Dehnen 1991, Chiatti 2025)
engage individual pieces of the unification but do not state the triple
identity as a single identification theorem.

###### The equivalence principle is tied to inertia at a depth never previously reached.

The framework's identification of inertial and gravitational mass
(Theorem [236](#thm:EquivalencePrinciple){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:EquivalencePrinciple"}) as the same
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude becomes, via
Theorem [239](#thm:InertiaComptonLeastActionTriple){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:InertiaComptonLeastActionTriple"}, a deep identity rather
than a surface coincidence. Specifically:

-   *Inertial mass is the resistance to changing the Compton-coupling
    rate's orientation in four-space* (Property (ii) of the present
    theorem).

-   *Gravitational mass is the same perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate
    magnitude that sources spacetime curvature via the Einstein field
    equations*
    (Theorem [236](#thm:EquivalencePrinciple){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:EquivalencePrinciple"}, Property (ii)).

-   *The equivalence principle's empirical universality of free fall
    (Eötvös, lunar laser ranging, MICROSCOPE 2017
    [@Touboul2017MICROSCOPE] confirming the equivalence at one part in
    $10^{15}$) is the empirical signature of the fact that gravitational
    sourcing and inertial resistance are not two distinct physical
    effects with a numerical match imposed by postulate; they are the
    same (perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude) acting in two
    roles --- the source role (entering the right-hand side of the
    Einstein field equations) and the inertia role (resisting
    four-velocity rotation under applied force).*

-   *The principle of least action's selection of geodesic motion*
    (Theorem [238](#thm:LeastActionWavefront){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:LeastActionWavefront"}, Property (v)) *is the same
    identity in dynamics: the path that minimizes the rate of change of
    the Compton-coupling rate's orientation is the geodesic of the
    metric sourced by the same Compton-coupling rate's magnitude.*

The depth of the equivalence-principle-to-inertia tie is now visible. In
the orthodox tradition, the equivalence principle is the empirical fact
$m_I = m_G$, with the universality of free fall as its dynamics; in the
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, the equivalence principle is the
identity $m_I = m_G =$ perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude, with
the universality of free fall as the dynamics that descends because the
principle of least action minimizes the rate of change of the
Compton-coupling rate's orientation, and the change-rate cost is
proportional to the magnitude, and the magnitude is the same that
sources the curvature; so the geodesic is the path of minimum
change-rate-cost, and the change-rate-cost is proportional to the same
magnitude that sources the curvature; so all freely-falling particles
follow the geodesic regardless of magnitude (which would be an empirical
mystery in the orthodox treatment) because the
change-rate-cost-to-magnitude ratio is unity, the magnitude factors out,
and the geodesic is independent of the magnitude. *The universality of
free fall is the universality of the geodesic; the universality of the
geodesic is the magnitude-independence of the change-rate-minimization
condition; the magnitude-independence is the consequence of the
change-rate cost being proportional to the magnitude; the
proportionality is the consequence of all three (inertia,
Compton-coupling rate, accumulated action) being the same of the
McGucken-Sphere wavefront.*

The equivalence principle, in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, is
no longer an empirical postulate but a deep consequence of the triple
identity of
Theorem [239](#thm:InertiaComptonLeastActionTriple){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:InertiaComptonLeastActionTriple"}.

###### The framework's priority.

The orthodox literature has carried the open problem documented at
primary-source grade by Synge 1960, Ostoma--Trushyk 1999,
Unnikrishnan--Gillies 2015, Bin Li 2025, and Mancini--Tino--Capozziello
2025 for sixty-five years. Each of these primary sources articulated
some piece of the open problem; none stated the four-fold unification
(Higgs + Inertia + Principle of Least Action + Equivalence Principle)
under a single principle, and none stated the triple identity (inertia =
change-rate-cost of Compton-coupling = action quantity that least action
varies). The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework supplies both the
four-fold unification and the triple identity, with the
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude on the McGucken-Sphere
wavefront as the single source.

We close the present subsection by stating the framework's advance in
one sentence: **In the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, inertia is not
a separate postulate, mass is not a separate parameter, the Compton
frequency is not a separate empirical scale, the principle of least
action is not a separate variational principle, the equivalence
principle is not a separate empirical postulate, and the Higgs mechanism
is not a separate field-theoretic construction --- all six are
projections of a single physical-geometric law, $dx_4/dt = ic$, with the
McGucken-Sphere wavefront supplying the action-carrying content, the
Higgs sector supplying the field-theoretic encoding of the $+ic$
direction, the Yukawa couplings supplying the species-specific
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rates, the Compton frequency supplying the
rate magnitude, the four-velocity rotation supplying the inertia, and
the Einstein field equations supplying the curved-spacetime extension
--- all six unified at theorem grade by the triple identity of
Theorem [239](#thm:InertiaComptonLeastActionTriple){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:InertiaComptonLeastActionTriple"}.**

#### Theorem H11.7: The Higgs mass IS the wavefunction-phase rate that the principle of least action varies {#ssec:HiggsMassLeastAction}

The orthodox tradition treats the Higgs mass and the principle of least
action as two separate structures stacked in the Lagrangian formulation:
the Higgs mass is a parameter *in* $\Lagr_{\rm SM}$ (via the $\mu^2$ of
the Mexican-hat potential and the Yukawa couplings
$y_f \overline{\psi}_L H \psi_R$); the principle of least action is the
variational rule applied *to* $\Lagr_{\rm SM}$ to select the equations
of motion. They are not derived from a common source, and standard
graduate references (Peskin--Schroeder, Schwartz, Srednicki, Weinberg's
QFT trilogy, Tong's QFT lectures) present them as independent
ingredients. Wilczek's primary-source treatments of the origins of
mass [@Wilczek1999MassWithoutMassI; @Wilczek2000MassWithoutMassII; @Wilczek2012OriginsOfMass]
engage the Higgs mechanism and the principle of least action separately
and do not unify them at a principle level.

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework ties them at theorem grade by
closing the chain that runs from the principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ through
the Higgs sector to the wavefunction phase that the principle of least
action varies. We state the closure here as one theorem; the underlying
structure is already established in the preceding subsections of the
present paper.

::: {#thm:HiggsMassIsLeastActionPhaseRate .theorem}
**Theorem 240** (The Higgs mass IS the wavefunction-phase rate that the
principle of least action varies). *Assume
Theorems [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"},
[218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:YukawaWinding"},
[232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"},
[234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"},
and [238](#thm:LeastActionWavefront){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:LeastActionWavefront"}. Then for any fundamental fermion
species $f$ with Yukawa coupling $y_f$ to the Higgs:
$$\underbrace{m_f c^2/\hbar}_{\text{Higgs-set Compton frequency }\omega_C^{(f)}}
\;=\;
\underbrace{y_f v c^2/(\sqrt{2}\hbar)}_{\text{Yukawa winding rate}}
\;=\;
\underbrace{\text{perpendicular-}x_4\text{-winding rate}}_{\text{Theorem~\ref{thm:ComptonX4Coupling}}}
\;=\;
\underbrace{-(1/\hbar)\,dS/d\tau}_{\text{wavefunction-phase rate}}\,,
\label{eq:HiggsMassIsPhaseRate}$$ where $S = -m_f c^2 \tau$ is the
free-particle action and $\exp(iS/\hbar) = \exp(-i\omega_C^{(f)}\tau)$
is the wavefunction phase that the principle of least action varies. The
four quantities
in [\[eq:HiggsMassIsPhaseRate\]](#eq:HiggsMassIsPhaseRate){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:HiggsMassIsPhaseRate"} are not four distinct quantities
related by empirical correspondence; they are one quantity --- the
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate of the particle's four-velocity on the
McGucken-Sphere wavefront, set by the Higgs vev $v$ and the
species-specific Yukawa coupling $y_f$, viewed from the four standpoints
of: (i) Higgs-set Compton frequency, (ii) Yukawa winding rate, (iii)
four-velocity perpendicular-$x_4$-component, and (iv) wavefunction-phase
rate that the principle of least action varies along the worldline.*

**The Higgs mass and the principle of least action are tied because the
Higgs sets the wavefunction-phase rate that the principle of least
action varies.* The Higgs vev encodes the $+ic$ direction
(Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}); the Yukawa coupling sets the
species-specific perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate
(Theorem [218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:YukawaWinding"}); the Compton frequency
$\omega_C^{(f)} = m_f c^2/\hbar$ is that rate
(Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}); the wavefunction phase
$\exp(-i\omega_C^{(f)}\tau)$ accumulates that rate along the worldline
(Theorem [238](#thm:LeastActionWavefront){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:LeastActionWavefront"} (ii)); the principle of least
action selects the worldline of constructive interference of these
McGucken-Sphere wavefront phases
(Theorem [238](#thm:LeastActionWavefront){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:LeastActionWavefront"} (iii)). *The Higgs mass IS the
rate the action accumulates per unit proper time.**
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G2 synthesis of
Theorems [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"},
[218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:YukawaWinding"},
[232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"},
[234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"},
[238](#thm:LeastActionWavefront){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:LeastActionWavefront"}. The chain of equalities
in [\[eq:HiggsMassIsPhaseRate\]](#eq:HiggsMassIsPhaseRate){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:HiggsMassIsPhaseRate"} follows by direct substitution:
$m_f = y_f v/\sqrt{2}$
(Theorem [218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:YukawaWinding"}) gives the first equality;
$\omega_C^{(f)} = m_f c^2/\hbar$ identified as
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate
(Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}) gives the second; the free-particle
action $S = -m_f c^2 \tau$ gives
$dS/d\tau = -m_f c^2 = -\hbar \omega_C^{(f)}$, hence the fourth quantity
equals $\omega_C^{(f)}$. No new analytics beyond the underlying
theorems.

*Honest scope*: numerical magnitudes of $y_f$ remain open per
Remark [217](#rem:HiggsHonestOpenProblems){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:HiggsHonestOpenProblems"}; the Higgs vev
$v \approx 246$ GeV remains an empirical input; the theorem operates at
identification grade. ◻

###### What this closes.

The orthodox open problem is the absence of a reason for the Higgs
sector and the principle of least action to be related. The McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework supplies the reason: both descend from the
McGucken-Sphere wavefront expanding at $c$ from every spacetime event
under $dx_4/dt = ic$. The Higgs sector encodes the $+ic$ direction and
the species-specific perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate; the principle of
least action selects the worldline of constructive interference of the
wavefronts those windings emit. *The Higgs mass is what the action
accumulates; the principle of least action selects the path along which
the accumulation interferes constructively. The two are tied because
they are two readings of the same wavefront.*

##### The Compton-coupling-rate identity holds independent of the mass-generation mechanism: a minimal statement of the unification upstream of the Higgs sector {#sssec:ComptonLeastActionMinimal}

Theorem [239](#thm:InertiaComptonLeastActionTriple){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:InertiaComptonLeastActionTriple"} above established the
triple identity (inertia = resistance to changing the Compton-coupling
rate = what the principle of least action minimizes) by combining seven
existing theorems of the framework, with the Higgs-pointer and
Yukawa-winding theorems supplying the species-specific Compton-frequency
for fundamental fermions in the electroweak sector. We now state the
same unification at minimal grade, stripped of the Higgs sector, to make
explicit that the chain Compton-coupling-rate $\leftrightarrow$
principle of least action $\leftrightarrow$ equivalence principle
$\leftrightarrow$ inertia is upstream of any mass-generation mechanism
and holds for any massive particle regardless of whether its Compton
frequency originates in Higgs-Yukawa coupling (fundamental fermions in
the electroweak sector), QCD binding-energy condensation (proton and
neutron mass; Wilczek's mass-without-mass), neutrino-mass mechanism
(Dirac mass, Majorana mass, see-saw, etc.), Cooper-pair condensation
(photon effective mass in superconductors, per
§[5.17](#ssec:PhotonMassSuperconductor){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:PhotonMassSuperconductor"}), or any other source.

::: {#thm:ComptonLeastActionMinimal .theorem}
**Theorem 241** (The Compton-coupling-rate / principle-of-least-action /
equivalence-principle / inertia identity, minimal form: holds for any
massive particle regardless of mass-generation mechanism). *Assume the
McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$
(Equation [\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"}); the McGucken-Sphere wavefront
structure at every spacetime event
(§[\[ssec:FoundationalPrinciple\]](#ssec:FoundationalPrinciple){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:FoundationalPrinciple"}); the Compton-X4-coupling
identification
(Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}); the Mass-Energy-Geometry Theorem
(Theorem [234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"}); and the
Principle-of-Least-Action-as-Wavefront-Phase-Constructive-Interference
Theorem (Theorem [238](#thm:LeastActionWavefront){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:LeastActionWavefront"}). Let $\mathfrak{p}$ be any
massive particle with rest mass $m > 0$ and Compton frequency
$$\omega_C = m c^2 / \hbar.
\label{eq:ComptonFrequencyDefinition}$$ Then:*

1.  ***The free-particle action is the accumulated Compton-frequency
    winding along the worldline.** The standard relativistic
    free-particle action is $S = \int (-mc^2)\, d\tau$.
    Substituting [\[eq:ComptonFrequencyDefinition\]](#eq:ComptonFrequencyDefinition){reference-type="eqref"
    reference="eq:ComptonFrequencyDefinition"} gives
    $$S \;=\; -\hbar \int \omega_C \, d\tau,
    \label{eq:ActionAsAccumulatedCompton}$$ and the wavefunction phase
    is
    $$\exp(iS/\hbar) \;=\; \exp\!\left(-i \int \omega_C\, d\tau\right) \;=\; \exp(-i\omega_C \tau)\quad\text{(for free particle, constant $\omega_C$)}.
    \label{eq:WavefunctionPhaseAsComptonAccumulation}$$ The Compton
    frequency $\omega_C$ is the rate at which the action accumulates per
    unit proper time, in units of $\hbar$.*

2.  ***The Compton-coupling rate IS the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate
    of the four-velocity on the McGucken-Sphere wavefront.** Per
    Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}, the Compton frequency $\omega_C$
    of any massive particle is the rate at which its four-velocity's
    perpendicular-$x_4$ component winds against the local $+ic$
    direction of $x_4$-expansion under $dx_4/dt = ic$. This
    identification does not depend on how $\omega_C$ acquires its
    numerical magnitude --- it holds for any massive particle with any
    rest mass set by any mass-generation mechanism.*

3.  ***The principle of least action selects the worldline of
    constructive interference of the Compton-frequency-encoded
    McGucken-Sphere wavefronts.** Per
    Theorem [238](#thm:LeastActionWavefront){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:LeastActionWavefront"}, Properties (iii) and (v), the
    stationary-action condition $\delta S = 0$ is equivalent to
    constructive interference of the wavefront
    phases [\[eq:WavefunctionPhaseAsComptonAccumulation\]](#eq:WavefunctionPhaseAsComptonAccumulation){reference-type="eqref"
    reference="eq:WavefunctionPhaseAsComptonAccumulation"} from
    neighbouring paths, equivalent to the path along which the
    perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate stays coherent, equivalent to
    straight-line motion in four-space in flat spacetime and geodesic
    motion in curved spacetime.*

4.  ***Inertia IS the resistance to changing the Compton-coupling rate's
    orientation in four-space.** Per
    Theorem [234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"}, the energy cost of rotating the
    four-velocity vector at rapidity rate $d\phi/dt$ is proportional to
    the $x_4$-component magnitude $mc$ that must be rotated. Newton's
    $F = ma$ (in the non-relativistic limit) and its relativistic
    extension $F = dp/dt$ emerge as the four-space-rotation cost of
    changing the Compton-coupling rate's orientation, with $m$
    identified as the magnitude of the rate vector being rotated.*

5.  ***Gravitational mass IS the same Compton-coupling-rate-magnitude.**
    The stress-energy tensor $T^{00} = \rho c^2$ for matter at rest has
    $\rho$ equal to the integrated Compton-coupling-rate-magnitude
    density
    (Theorem [236](#thm:EquivalencePrinciple){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:EquivalencePrinciple"}, Property (ii)). The same
    magnitude that supplies the inertia of (iv) supplies the
    gravitational source via the Einstein field equations
    $G_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi G T_{\mu\nu}/c^4$.*

6.  ***The equivalence principle is the identity that all four readings
    reference the same magnitude.** Inertial mass (Property (iv)) =
    gravitational mass (Property (v)) = Compton-coupling-rate magnitude
    (Property (ii)) = action-accumulation rate per unit proper time
    divided by $\hbar$ (Property (i)). The universality of free fall
    (Eötvös, lunar laser ranging, MICROSCOPE 2017
    [@Touboul2017MICROSCOPE] at one part in $10^{15}$) is the empirical
    signature of this identity.*

**The identity, stated as one sentence:* **The Compton frequency
$\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ is the rate at which a massive particle's
four-velocity perpendicular-$x_4$ component winds on the McGucken-Sphere
wavefront under $dx_4/dt = ic$; the action accumulates this winding
along the worldline ($S = -\hbar\int\omega_C\,d\tau$); the principle of
least action selects the worldline of constructive interference of these
wavefront phases; inertia is the resistance to changing the
winding-rate's orientation; gravitational sourcing is the same
winding-rate-magnitude via the Einstein field equations; the equivalence
principle is the identity that these four readings reference the same
magnitude.***
:::

::: proof
*Grade and content..* G2 identification. The mathematics of
Properties (i), (iv), (v), (vi) is direct substitution and standard
relativistic mechanics; the framework-specific identification is in
Properties (ii), (iii).

*Property (i)* is direct substitution: $S = \int (-mc^2)\,d\tau$ is the
standard free-particle action (standard relativistic free-particle
action, Landau--Lifshitz *Classical Theory of Fields* §8); substituting
$mc^2 = \hbar\omega_C$
from [\[eq:ComptonFrequencyDefinition\]](#eq:ComptonFrequencyDefinition){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:ComptonFrequencyDefinition"} gives
$S = -\hbar\int\omega_C\,d\tau$, and the wavefunction phase follows.
This is algebra, not assertion.

*Property (ii)* is documentary at
Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}: the Compton frequency is identified
as the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate on the McGucken-Sphere
wavefront. The identification operates at the level of the Compton
frequency itself, independent of which mass-generation mechanism sets
the rate's numerical magnitude for a given particle species.

*Property (iii)* is documentary at
Theorem [238](#thm:LeastActionWavefront){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:LeastActionWavefront"}, Properties (iii) and (v): the
stationary-action condition is the constructive-interference condition
for wavefront phases at the McGucken-Sphere; the
constructive-interference path is the path along which the
wavefront-phase-advance rate stays coherent; this is straight-line
motion in four-space in flat spacetime and geodesic motion in curved
spacetime.

*Property (iv)* is documentary at
Theorem [234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"}, Properties (iii) and (viii):
inertia is the energy cost of rotating the four-velocity vector, with
cost proportional to the perpendicular-$x_4$-component magnitude $mc$
being rotated.

*Property (v)* is documentary at
Theorem [236](#thm:EquivalencePrinciple){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:EquivalencePrinciple"}, Property (ii): the gravitational
source (stress-energy tensor $T^{00} = \rho c^2$) has rest-mass density
$\rho$ equal to the integrated
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate-magnitude density.

*Property (vi)* is the synthesis combining Properties (i)--(v): all four
readings (Compton frequency, perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate,
action-accumulation rate per $\hbar$, inertial-and-gravitational-mass
magnitude) reference the same quantity.

*Honest scope of
Theorem [241](#thm:ComptonLeastActionMinimal){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonLeastActionMinimal"}*:

-   The identification holds for any massive particle with any rest mass
    $m > 0$, regardless of mass-generation mechanism (Higgs-Yukawa for
    fundamental fermions, QCD binding energy for hadrons, neutrino-mass
    mechanism, Cooper-pair condensation, etc.).

-   The theorem does NOT derive the numerical value of any particle's
    rest mass; it states what the rest mass IS
    (perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude / Compton-coupling-rate
    magnitude / action-accumulation rate per $\hbar$), without
    specifying where the magnitude comes from.

-   For fundamental fermions, the species-specific Compton frequency is
    set by the Higgs-Yukawa mechanism (per
    Theorems [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:HiggsPointer"},
    [218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:YukawaWinding"}, established elsewhere in the present
    paper); for composite hadrons, by integrated internal-degree
    winding-rate content (per
    Theorem [247](#thm:CompositeStateMass){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:CompositeStateMass"}); for neutrinos, by whichever
    neutrino-mass mechanism (open in standard physics and in the
    framework); for photons in superconductors, by Cooper-pair
    condensation (per
    Theorem [251](#thm:PhotonMassSuperconductor){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:PhotonMassSuperconductor"}). The minimal theorem
    operates upstream of all these mass-generation mechanisms.

-   The framework does not derive Newton's gravitational constant $G$;
    the Einstein field equations are referenced from [@MG-Gravity2026
    §8.4], not re-derived here.

 ◻
:::

###### Why the minimal form matters.

The Higgs-Yukawa mechanism is one specific way to set the
Compton-coupling rate for fundamental fermions in the electroweak
sector, but it is not the only way mass can arise in physics. Roughly
99% of the rest-mass of ordinary matter resides in protons and neutrons,
whose mass comes overwhelmingly from QCD binding energy of the gluon and
quark fields, not from Higgs-Yukawa coupling of the constituent quarks
--- Wilczek's "mass without mass" content
[@Wilczek1999MassWithoutMassI; @Wilczek2000MassWithoutMassII]. Neutrino
masses come from a mechanism that is not yet settled in standard physics
(Dirac mass, Majorana mass, see-saw mechanism, neutrino-Higgs coupling,
etc.). Photon effective mass inside superconductors comes from
Cooper-pair condensation (per
§[5.17](#ssec:PhotonMassSuperconductor){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:PhotonMassSuperconductor"}).

*In all these cases, the identification of
Theorem [241](#thm:ComptonLeastActionMinimal){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonLeastActionMinimal"} holds at the same grade.* The
Compton frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ is well-defined for any
massive particle; the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework identifies it as
the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate of the four-velocity on the
McGucken-Sphere wavefront; the wavefunction phase $\exp(-i\omega_C\tau)$
accumulates this winding along the worldline; the principle of least
action selects the worldline of constructive interference of these
wavefronts; inertia is the rotation cost; gravitational sourcing is the
same magnitude entering $T_{\mu\nu}$; equivalence principle is the
identity. The chain is independent of how $\omega_C$ acquires its
numerical magnitude for any particular particle.

###### The priority claim, stated cleanly.

Within the primary-source literature reviewed at full-read grade for the
present paper, no programme has stated the four-way identity of
Theorem [241](#thm:ComptonLeastActionMinimal){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonLeastActionMinimal"} --- Compton frequency,
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate, action-accumulation rate per $\hbar$,
inertial-and-gravitational-mass magnitude as one of the McGucken-Sphere
wavefront --- from a physical-geometric principle. The standard
relativistic-mechanics algebra $S = -\hbar\int\omega_C\,d\tau$ is in any
graduate quantum-mechanics textbook (Feynman path-integral content), but
the identification of $\omega_C$ as the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate
on the McGucken-Sphere wavefront under $dx_4/dt = ic$, with the four-way
identity that follows, is the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's
specific content.

##### The Four-Compton-Vector Unification: $K^\mu = p^\mu/\hbar$ as one tensorial object on the McGucken Sphere wavefront at every event of spacetime, with four physical contexts coupling to its magnitude under $dx_4/dt = ic$ {#sssec:FourComptonVectorUnification}

The chain of theorems established in this subsection
(Theorems [236](#thm:EquivalencePrinciple){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:EquivalencePrinciple"},
[237](#thm:MassBendsSpaceX4Invariant){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MassBendsSpaceX4Invariant"},
[238](#thm:LeastActionWavefront){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:LeastActionWavefront"},
[239](#thm:InertiaComptonLeastActionTriple){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:InertiaComptonLeastActionTriple"},
[240](#thm:HiggsMassIsLeastActionPhaseRate){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsMassIsLeastActionPhaseRate"},
[241](#thm:ComptonLeastActionMinimal){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonLeastActionMinimal"}) supplies the pieces of a
unification that the existing manuscript content supports but does not
yet state at its sharpest form. We state it here as the closing theorem
of the present subsection.

*The unification is not a claim that the Higgs mechanism and the
gravitational mechanism are the same mechanism.* They are distinct
mechanisms operating on distinct sectors of spacetime: the Higgs
operates in the matter sector to determine the magnitude of the
four-Compton-vector $K^\mu = p^\mu/\hbar$ for each fermion species;
gravity operates in the deformable spatial-metric sector $g_{ij}$ to
determine the metric in which $K^\mu$ is parallel-transported. *What is
unified is the quantity these mechanisms couple to.* The
four-Compton-vector $K^\mu$ is one tensorial object on the McGucken
Sphere wavefront $\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}(p, t)$ expanding at $c$ from every
event $p \in \mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}$ under the McGucken Principle
$dx_4/dt = ic$, with Lorentz-invariant magnitude
$|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2} = \omega_C/c = mc/\hbar$ identifying the rate at
which the four-velocity perpendicular-$x_4$ component winds on the
McGucken Sphere
(Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}). Four physically distinct contexts
couple to this McGucken-Sphere-winding magnitude.

::: {#thm:FourComptonVectorUnification .theorem}
**Theorem 242** (The Four-Compton-Vector Unification:
$K^\mu = p^\mu/\hbar$ as the unifying object on spacetime, with four
physical contexts coupling to its magnitude). *Assume the McGucken
Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$
(Equation [\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"}); the Higgs pointer identification
(Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}); the Yukawa-as-winding-rate
identification (Theorem [218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:YukawaWinding"}); the rest-mass identification as
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate at Compton frequency
(Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}); the Mass-Energy-Geometry Theorem
(Theorem [234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"}); the Equivalence Principle Theorem
(Theorem [236](#thm:EquivalencePrinciple){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:EquivalencePrinciple"}); the
Mass-Bends-Space-$x_4$-Invariant Theorem
(Theorem [237](#thm:MassBendsSpaceX4Invariant){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MassBendsSpaceX4Invariant"}); the
Principle-of-Least-Action-as-Wavefront-Phase Theorem
(Theorem [238](#thm:LeastActionWavefront){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:LeastActionWavefront"}); and the framework's derivation
of the Einstein field equations from $dx_4/dt = ic$ ([@MG-Gravity2026
§8.4], [@MG-GR]). Then:*

1.  ***$K^\mu = p^\mu/\hbar$ is one tensorial object on the McGucken
    Sphere wavefront at every event of spacetime under $dx_4/dt = ic$.**
    For any massive worldline of species $f$, the four-momentum
    $p^\mu = (E/c, \vec{p})$ defines the four-Compton-vector
    $K^\mu = p^\mu/\hbar$ at every event of the worldline, with the
    four-velocity perpendicular-$x_4$ component winding on the McGucken
    Sphere wavefront $\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}(p, t)$ that the McGucken
    Principle generates from every event
    (§[\[ssec:FoundationalPrinciple\]](#ssec:FoundationalPrinciple){reference-type="ref"
    reference="ssec:FoundationalPrinciple"};
    Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}). Its Lorentz-invariant magnitude
    is $$|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2} = \omega_C^{(f)}/c = m_f c/\hbar,
    \label{eq:FourComptonMagnitude}$$ identifiable as the
    perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude per
    Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}. The four-Compton-vector and its
    magnitude are well-defined tensorial objects independent of which
    physical context is examined.*

2.  ***Context 1: Higgs-Yukawa coupling determines the magnitude
    $|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2}$ for fundamental fermion species.** Per
    Theorems [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}
    and [218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:YukawaWinding"}, the Higgs vev encodes the $+ic$
    direction at every event, and the species-specific Yukawa coupling
    $y_f$ supplies the winding rate
    $\omega_C^{(f)} = y_f v c^2/(\sqrt{2}\hbar)$ at which a fermion of
    species $f$ winds perpendicular through $x_4$ at three-rest. The
    Higgs-Yukawa machinery's output for species $f$ is the magnitude
    $|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2} = \omega_C^{(f)}/c$.*

3.  ***Context 2: Inertia couples to $|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2}$ as the
    rotation-cost coefficient.** Per
    Theorem [234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"}, the rest mass $m_f$ is the
    proportionality constant between four-force and four-acceleration in
    $F^\mu = m_f a^\mu$. Inertia is the resistance to rotating $K^\mu$
    in four-space; the energy cost of rotation by rapidity $\phi$ is
    $\Delta E = m_f c^2 (\cosh\phi - 1)$, proportional to the magnitude
    $\hbar \omega_C^{(f)}/c = m_f c$ being rotated. *Inertia couples to
    the four-Compton-vector magnitude as the rotation-cost
    coefficient.**

4.  ***Context 3: Gravitational sourcing couples to
    $|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2}$ as the stress-energy tensor source.** At rest
    in the centre-of-energy frame, the stress-energy tensor satisfies
    $T^{00} = \rho c^2$ with $\rho$ the rest-mass density. The rest-mass
    density is the integrated four-Compton-vector-magnitude density per
    Theorem [236](#thm:EquivalencePrinciple){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:EquivalencePrinciple"} (ii); the stress-energy tensor
    enters the right-hand side of the Einstein field equations
    $$G^{\mu\nu} = \frac{8\pi G}{c^4} T^{\mu\nu},
    \label{eq:EinsteinFieldEquations}$$ producing curvature of the
    spatial-metric sector $g_{ij}$ (the deformable sector of spacetime)
    through which $K^\mu$ is parallel-transported. *Gravitational
    sourcing couples to the four-Compton-vector magnitude as the
    stress-energy-tensor source on the right-hand side of the Einstein
    field equations.**

5.  ***Context 4: The principle of least action couples to
    $|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2}$ as the proper-time integrand of the action
    functional.** The accumulated Compton-phase along a worldline
    $\gamma$ is
    $$\Phi_C[\gamma] = \int_\gamma \omega_C^{(f)} d\tau = -S[\gamma]/\hbar,
    \label{eq:AccumulatedComptonPhase}$$ with
    $S[\gamma] = \int_\gamma (-m_f c^2) d\tau$ the standard
    free-particle action. The principle of least action is the
    stationary-phase condition
    $\delta \Phi_C = 0 \Leftrightarrow \delta S = 0$ for this
    functional, per
    Theorem [238](#thm:LeastActionWavefront){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:LeastActionWavefront"} (iii). The classical worldline
    is the path of parallel-transported $K^\mu$ along the geodesic of
    the metric $g_{\mu\nu}$ sourced by (iv). *The principle of least
    action couples to the four-Compton-vector magnitude as the
    proper-time integrand of the action functional.**

6.  ***The Equivalence Principle is the identity that the magnitude
    entering Contexts 2, 3, and 4 is the same magnitude as Context 1's
    output.** The Higgs-Yukawa machinery outputs the magnitude
    $\omega_C^{(f)}/c$ for species $f$ (Context 1); the same magnitude
    $m_f = \hbar \omega_C^{(f)}/c^2$ enters the inertia equation as the
    rotation-cost coefficient (Context 2); the same magnitude enters the
    stress-energy tensor as the gravitational source (Context 3); the
    same magnitude enters the action functional as the proper-time
    integrand (Context 4). *All four contexts couple to one quantity ---
    the Lorentz-invariant magnitude of the four-Compton-vector $K^\mu$
    on spacetime.* The Equivalence Principle's empirical universality of
    free fall (Eötvös, lunar laser ranging, MICROSCOPE 2017
    [@Touboul2017MICROSCOPE] at one part in $10^{15}$) is the empirical
    signature of this identity.*

7.  ***The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ is the unifying source of
    $K^\mu$ and its magnitude; the temporal rate is metric-rigid.** The
    rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ is held at velocity $c$ at every event of
    spacetime regardless of the metric curvature in the deformable
    spatial sector $g_{ij}$
    (Theorem [237](#thm:MassBendsSpaceX4Invariant){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MassBendsSpaceX4Invariant"} (ii); GR T2 of
    [@MG-Master2Chains-2026 Part I]). Gravity acts on the deformable
    spatial-metric sector and does not touch the temporal rate. The
    Higgs-Yukawa machinery acts in the matter sector and does not touch
    the deformable spatial-metric sector. *The two mechanisms (Higgs and
    gravity) are distinct couplings to the same four-Compton-vector
    magnitude, with the McGucken Principle as the unifying source from
    which $K^\mu$ and its magnitude descend.**

**The conclusion:* the four-Compton-vector $K^\mu$ is one tensorial
object on the McGucken Sphere wavefront at every event of spacetime
under $dx_4/dt = ic$, with the magnitude $|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2}$
identifying the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate of the four-velocity on
the wavefront; four physically distinct contexts (Higgs-Yukawa coupling,
inertia, gravitational sourcing, least-action functional) couple to this
McGucken-Sphere-winding magnitude; the Equivalence Principle is the
identity that the magnitude entering all four contexts is the same
magnitude; and the temporal rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ is the metric-rigid
principle from which $K^\mu$ and its magnitude descend. *The Higgs
mechanism is not the gravitational mechanism: the Higgs is the
field-theoretic encoding of where $|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2}$ comes from for
fundamental fermions; gravity is the spatial-metric-sector response to
integrated $|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2}$ content via the Einstein field
equations. The two are distinct mechanisms operating on distinct sectors
of spacetime, sharing the four-Compton-vector $K^\mu$ as the common
quantity they couple to and $dx_4/dt = ic$ as the principle from which
it descends.**
:::

reference="thm:MassBendsSpaceX4Invariant"}, Property (ii) and GR T2 of
[@MG-Master2Chains-2026 Part I]: the temporal rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ is
metric-rigid under gravitational curvature of the spatial-metric sector.

*Honest scope of
Theorem [242](#thm:FourComptonVectorUnification){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:FourComptonVectorUnification"}*:

-   The theorem establishes $K^\mu$ as one tensorial object on spacetime
    under $dx_4/dt = ic$, with four physical contexts coupling to its
    Lorentz-invariant magnitude, and the Equivalence Principle as the
    identity that the magnitude is shared across contexts.

-   The theorem does NOT claim the Higgs mechanism and the gravitational
    mechanism are the same mechanism: they are distinct mechanisms on
    distinct sectors of spacetime, sharing the four-Compton-vector
    $K^\mu$ as the common quantity they couple to.

-   The theorem does NOT derive the numerical magnitudes of the Yukawa
    couplings or Newton's $G$; these remain open per the existing scoped
    content.

-   The theorem does NOT re-derive the Einstein field equations from
    $dx_4/dt = ic$; this derivation is documented in the framework's
    existing corpus [@MG-Gravity2026 §8.4], [@MG-GR].

-   The theorem does NOT supply a quantum theory of gravity; the
    identification operates at the classical-relativistic level.

###### Why the orthodox tradition did not see this.

The orthodox tradition has carried the empirics of all four contexts in
important places for over a century: Newton's $F = ma$ (1687); the
principle of least action (Hamilton 1833; Feynman 1948); the equivalence
principle (Einstein 1907); the Higgs-Yukawa machinery
(Englert--Brout--Higgs 1964; Yukawa 1935 for the coupling structure);
the Einstein field equations (1915); the de Broglie-frequency
identification of the wavefunction phase (1924); the Dirac equation's
spinor structure (1928). *The fact that all four contexts couple to one
four-Compton-vector magnitude on a single manifold under one principle
has not been visible in the orthodox tradition.* Three commitments block
the recognition:

1.  *The orthodox tradition treats the imaginary unit $i$ as formal
    mathematical convenience rather than as a physical-geometric
    perpendicularity marker.* The twelve $i$'s of quantum mechanics
    (canonical commutator, Schrödinger evolution, Dirac operator,
    path-integral weight, $U(1)$ gauge phase, Clifford structure, KMS
    condition, Born rule, Wick substitution, $+i\epsilon$ prescription,
    Fresnel integrals, action bridge) are treated as twelve separate
    notational accidents. The Renou--Li--Chen 2021--2022 empirical
    falsification of real quantum theory
    [@Renou2021Nature; @Li2022PRL; @Chen2022PRL] forced acknowledgment
    that $i$ is physically necessary, but the reading of
    $i = (dx_4/dt)/c$ as the perpendicularity marker per [@MGWick
    Theorem 21.6bis.1] has not been absorbed by the orthodox tradition.
    Without this reading, the four physical contexts cannot be
    recognised as coupling to a single tensorial object whose
    perpendicularity is encoded by $i$.

2.  *The orthodox tradition identifies the fourth dimension with the
    time coordinate $x^0 = ct$.* There is, in the orthodox tradition, no
    separate $x_4$ axis expanding at rate $c$ at every event distinct
    from the time coordinate. With no separate $x_4$ direction, there is
    no separate winding direction perpendicular to three-space, no
    perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude to identify with
    $|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2}$, and no source from which the
    four-Compton-vector descends.

3.  *The orthodox tradition lacks a physical-geometric principle from
    which the four physical contexts descend as theorems.* Newton's
    $F = ma$ is postulated, the principle of least action is postulated,
    the equivalence principle is postulated, the Higgs mechanism is
    constructed by hand with Yukawa couplings as input, the Einstein
    field equations are postulated. Each ingredient is treated as a
    separate commitment. The orthodox tradition does not search for one
    principle that all four contexts are theorems of, and therefore
    cannot recognise the four contexts as coupling to one tensorial
    object whose magnitude descends from one source.

*These three blocks are mutually reinforcing.* Treating $i$ as formal
prevents recognising $+ic$ as physical. Treating the time coordinate as
the fourth dimension prevents recognising $x_4$ as a separate axis.
Treating physics as multiple postulates prevents the search for one
principle. The combination keeps the four-Compton-vector unification of
Higgs-Yukawa coupling + inertia + gravitational sourcing + least-action
functional invisible. The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework breaks all
three blocks at once: $i$ is the perpendicularity marker per [@MGWick
Theorem 21.6bis.1]; $x_4$ is a separate axis expanding at $c$ from every
event per
Equation [\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"}; physics is a chain of theorems
descending from $dx_4/dt = ic$. Once these three facts are in place, the
four-Compton-vector unification of
Theorem [242](#thm:FourComptonVectorUnification){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:FourComptonVectorUnification"} becomes recognisable.

Theorem [242](#thm:FourComptonVectorUnification){reference-type="ref"

same pattern extends to the rest of fundamental physics: each
field-theoretic structure of the Standard Model and quantum mechanics
couples to a specific sector of spacetime under $dx_4/dt = ic$,
distinguished by which content of the McGucken Principle it engages.

-   *The wavefunction phase $\exp(iS/\hbar)$* couples to the accumulated

*The picture:* the four-Compton-vector $K^\mu$ unifies the Higgs-Yukawa
output, the inertia coefficient, the gravitational source, and the
least-action integrand; the field-theoretic gauge connections
($U(1)_{\rm em}$, $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$, $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$) couple to
additional sectors of spacetime under the same principle; the
wavefunction phase and the twelve $i$'s of quantum mechanics carry the
perpendicularity marker of $x_4$ at every event. All of these are
couplings to specific structure of spacetime under $dx_4/dt = ic$. *One
principle, one spacetime, many distinct couplings to distinct sectors;
the unification is in the source, not in the mechanisms themselves.*

###### The advance of Theorem [242](#thm:FourComptonVectorUnification){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:FourComptonVectorUnification"}. {#the-advance-of-theorem-thmfourcomptonvectorunification.}

Within the primary-source literature reviewed at full-read grade for the
present paper, no programme has stated the four-Compton-vector
unification --- that $K^\mu = p^\mu/\hbar$ is one tensorial object on a
single manifold under one principle, with four distinct physical
contexts (Higgs-Yukawa coupling, inertia, gravitational sourcing,
least-action functional) coupling to its Lorentz-invariant magnitude.
The Moffat 1993 [@Moffat1993FoundationsOfPhysics] treatment relates a
separate gravitational scalar field to a time direction (distinct:
Moffat's scalar is not the electroweak Higgs and his "time direction" is
the standard general-relativity time coordinate, not a separate $x_4$
axis). The orthodox treatments (Weinberg QFT trilogy, Schwartz QFT,
Peskin--Schroeder, Wilczek's origins-of-mass writings) treat the four
physical contexts as four independent structures interacting through
stress-energy without identifying a common tensorial object on a single
manifold under a single principle.

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's advance: the four-Compton-vector
$K^\mu$ is one tensorial object on spacetime under $dx_4/dt = ic$, with
four distinct physical contexts coupling to its Lorentz-invariant
magnitude. The Higgs mechanism and the gravitational mechanism are
distinct couplings to one common quantity, not two faces of one
mechanism. The Equivalence Principle is the identity that the magnitude
entering all four contexts is the same magnitude. The temporal rate
$dx_4/dt = ic$ is metric-rigid; gravity acts on the deformable
spatial-metric sector and does not touch the temporal rate. *The
unification is in the source, not in the mechanisms.*

##### The Five-Way Structural Identity: Compton coupling, principle of least action, gravity, equivalence principle, and inertia as five physical contexts of one tensorial object $K^\mu$ winding on the McGucken Sphere wavefront at every event of spacetime under $dx_4/dt = ic$, upstream of any mass-generation mechanism {#sssec:FiveWayStructuralIdentity}

Theorem [242](#thm:FourComptonVectorUnification){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:FourComptonVectorUnification"} above treats the
four-Compton-vector unification including the Higgs-Yukawa coupling as
one of the four contexts. The Higgs-Yukawa coupling is the specific
mass-generation mechanism for fundamental fermions in the electroweak
sector; it is not the only mass-generation mechanism in physics (QCD
binding energy generates hadron mass; the neutrino-mass mechanism
remains open; Cooper-pair condensation generates photon effective mass
in superconductors). We now state the identity stripped of any
mass-generation-mechanism invocation, recording explicitly that the
five-way unification of (Compton coupling, principle of least action,
gravity, equivalence principle, inertia) is upstream of how mass is
generated, and holds for any massive particle on spacetime.

particle with rest mass $m > 0$, with arbitrary mass-generation
mechanism (Higgs-Yukawa for fundamental fermions, QCD binding for
hadrons, neutrino-mass mechanism, Cooper-pair condensation, etc.).
Define the four-Compton-vector $$K^\mu \;\equiv\; p^\mu/\hbar
\label{eq:FourComptonVectorDefinition}$$ on the worldline of
$\mathfrak{p}$ in spacetime, with Lorentz-invariant magnitude
$$|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2} \;=\; \omega_C/c \;=\; mc/\hbar.
\label{eq:KMagnitudeDefinition}$$ Then the five physical contexts
(Compton coupling, principle of least action, gravity, equivalence
principle, inertia) are five physical roles in which $K^\mu$ and its
magnitude appear; the five are not five postulates of physics but five
readings of one tensorial object winding on the McGucken Sphere
wavefront $\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}(p, t)$ that the McGucken Principle
$dx_4/dt = ic$ generates from every event
$p \in \mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}$:*

1.  ***Compton coupling: the object itself.** The four-Compton-vector
    $K^\mu = p^\mu/\hbar$ is well-defined at every event of
    $\mathfrak{p}$'s worldline. Its Lorentz-invariant magnitude
    $|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2} = mc/\hbar = \omega_C/c$ identifies the
    species's Compton frequency $\omega_C$ as the rate at which
    $\mathfrak{p}$'s four-velocity perpendicular-$x_4$ component winds
    against the local $+ic$ direction per
    Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}. *The Compton coupling IS $K^\mu$
    on spacetime.**

2.  ***Principle of least action: the proper-time integrand of the
    wavefunction phase.** The free-particle action
    $S[\gamma] = \int_\gamma(-mc^2)\, d\tau$ along a worldline $\gamma$
    is, by direct substitution of $mc^2 = \hbar \omega_C$,
    $$S[\gamma] \;=\; -\hbar \int_\gamma \omega_C\, d\tau \;=\; -\hbar \int_\gamma c \cdot |K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2}\, d\tau,
    \label{eq:ActionAsKMagnitudeIntegral}$$ and the wavefunction phase
    is $\exp(iS/\hbar) = \exp(-i\int_\gamma \omega_C\, d\tau)$. The
    stationary-action condition $\delta S = 0$ is the
    constructive-interference condition for the McGucken-Sphere
    wavefront phases emitted at every event of $\gamma$ per
    Theorem [238](#thm:LeastActionWavefront){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:LeastActionWavefront"}, Property (iii). *The
    principle of least action selects the worldline of constructive
    interference of the wavefront phases generated by $K^\mu$'s
    magnitude along the worldline.**

3.  ***Gravity: the stress-energy-tensor source.** At rest in the
    centre-of-energy frame, the stress-energy tensor's energy-density
    component is $T^{00} = \rho c^2$ with rest-mass density $\rho$ given
    by the integrated four-Compton-vector-magnitude density of the
    matter distribution:
    $$\rho \;=\; \sum_{f} n_f \hbar \omega_C^{(f)}/c^2 \;=\; \sum_f n_f m_f.
    \label{eq:RestMassDensityAsKMagnitudeDensity}$$ The Einstein field
    equations $G^{\mu\nu} = (8\pi G/c^4) T^{\mu\nu}$ source curvature of
    the deformable spatial-metric sector $g_{ij}$ through which $K^\mu$
    is parallel-transported. Per
    Theorem [237](#thm:MassBendsSpaceX4Invariant){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MassBendsSpaceX4Invariant"}, Property (ii), the
    temporal rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ stays metric-rigid at every event
    regardless of the spatial-metric-sector curvature. *Gravity sources
    curvature of the spatial-metric sector in proportion to integrated
    $|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2}$-magnitude of matter, while the temporal rate
    $dx_4/dt = ic$ stays metric-rigid.**

4.  ***Equivalence principle: the identity that the magnitude is shared
    across roles.** The same magnitude $|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2} = mc/\hbar$
    enters Context A (the Compton coupling), Context B (the proper-time
    integrand of the action functional), Context C (the
    stress-energy-tensor source), and Context E (the inertia
    rotation-cost coefficient below). *The Equivalence Principle is the
    identity that one magnitude plays all roles.* The empirical
    universality of free fall (Eötvös tests, lunar laser ranging,
    MICROSCOPE 2017 [@Touboul2017MICROSCOPE] at one part in $10^{15}$)
    is the empirical signature of the identity: because the same
    magnitude enters the inertial coefficient (Context E) and the
    gravitational source (Context C), the magnitude factors out of the
    geodesic equation, and all particles fall identically regardless of
    mass.*

5.  ***Inertia: the rotation-cost coefficient of $K^\mu$ in
    four-space.** When a force is applied to $\mathfrak{p}$, the
    four-velocity $u^\mu = c\, K^\mu/|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2}$ rotates in
    four-space from the rest-frame orientation (full
    perpendicular-$x_4$-winding, kinematic state (i) of
    Theorem [234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"}) by rapidity $\phi$ toward a
    spatial-velocity orientation (partial perpendicular-$x_4$-winding
    plus partial spatial momentum, kinematic state (ii)). The energy
    cost of the rotation is
    $$\Delta E \;=\; mc^2(\cosh\phi - 1) \;=\; \hbar \omega_C (\cosh\phi - 1),
    \label{eq:InertiaAsRotationCost}$$ proportional to the magnitude
    $|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2} \cdot \hbar c = mc^2$ being rotated. Newton's
    $F = ma$ in the non-relativistic limit and the relativistic
    four-force equation $F^\mu = ma^\mu$ in general emerge as the
    rotation-cost equation for $K^\mu$ in four-space per
    Theorem [234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"}, Properties (iii) and (viii).
    *Inertia IS the rotation-cost coefficient of $K^\mu$'s magnitude in
    four-space.**

**The five-way identity, stated as one sentence:*
**$K^\mu = p^\mu/\hbar$ is one tensorial object winding on the McGucken
Sphere wavefront at every event of spacetime under $dx_4/dt = ic$, with
Lorentz-invariant magnitude
$|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2} = mc/\hbar = \omega_C/c$ identifying the
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate on the wavefront; the Compton coupling
is the object itself; the principle of least action is the
constructive-interference selection of the worldline along which the
magnitude accumulates as the wavefunction phase
$\exp(-i\int \omega_C\, d\tau)$ on the McGucken-Sphere wavefront;
gravity is the spatial-metric-sector response to integrated magnitude
via the Einstein field equations; the equivalence principle is the
identity that the magnitude is shared across the inertial role (Context
E), the action-functional role (Context B), and the gravitational source
role (Context C); inertia is the rotation-cost coefficient of $K^\mu$'s
magnitude in four-space; all five contexts couple to one tensorial
object on one spacetime under one principle.***
