###### Why the five contexts cannot be five postulates: the inevitability of the identity.

The five contexts are not five logically independent facts that happen
to coincide. Once $dx_4/dt = ic$ is given as the principle, the five
contexts follow as consequences:

-   *$K^\mu$ exists at every event of every massive worldline* because
    $x_4$ is a separate axis at every event of spacetime (per the
    McGucken Principle), and the four-momentum $p^\mu$ of any massive
    particle is a well-defined tangent vector at every event.

-   *The Lorentz-invariant magnitude $|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2}$ is
    well-defined* because spacetime carries a Lorentzian inner product
    induced by $dx_4/dt = ic$ via $x_4= ict$, and $K^\mu$ is a tangent
    vector whose magnitude is observer-independent.

-   *The principle of least action follows from constructive
    interference* because the wavefront emitted from every event expands
    at $c$ and carries the Compton-frequency phase along the worldline;
    constructive interference of the wavefront phases selects the
    worldline along which the magnitude accumulates coherently
    (Theorem [238](#thm:LeastActionWavefront){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:LeastActionWavefront"}).

-   *The Einstein field equations source curvature from integrated
    magnitude* because the framework's derivation of the field equations
    from $dx_4/dt = ic$ identifies the stress-energy tensor's rest-frame
    component with the integrated $|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2}$-magnitude
    density [@MG-Gravity2026 §8.4], [@MG-GR].

-   *Inertia is the rotation-cost* because acceleration is the rotation
    of $K^\mu$ in four-space, and the energy cost of rotating any vector
    is proportional to its magnitude
    (Theorem [234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"}).

-   *The equivalence principle is the identity* because the same
    magnitude $|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2}$ appears in the action functional,
    the gravitational source, and the inertial coefficient; in the
    geodesic equation the magnitude factors out, producing the
    universality of free fall.

*The five contexts are inevitable consequences of $dx_4/dt = ic$
together with the framework's identification of $\omega_C$ as the
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate.* They are not five postulates of
physics that the framework recovers --- they are five roles of one
tensorial object on one spacetime under one principle, with the
orthodox-tradition postulates (Newton's $F = ma$, the principle of least
action, the equivalence principle as postulate of GR) reproduced as
consequences rather than independent ingredients.

###### The advance of Theorem [243](#thm:FiveWayStructuralIdentity){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:FiveWayStructuralIdentity"} over Theorem [242](#thm:FourComptonVectorUnification){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:FourComptonVectorUnification"}. {#the-advance-of-theorem-thmfivewaystructuralidentity-over-theorem-thmfourcomptonvectorunification.}

Theorem [242](#thm:FourComptonVectorUnification){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:FourComptonVectorUnification"} states the
four-Compton-vector unification with the Higgs-Yukawa coupling as one of
the contexts.
Theorem [243](#thm:FiveWayStructuralIdentity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:FiveWayStructuralIdentity"} strips the Higgs-Yukawa
coupling entirely and states the identity for any massive particle
independent of mass-generation mechanism. The identity (Compton
coupling, principle of least action, gravity, equivalence principle,
inertia) is upstream of any specific mass-generation mechanism. The
Higgs is one mechanism that sets the magnitude for fundamental fermions
in the electroweak sector; QCD binding sets it for hadrons; the
neutrino-mass mechanism (whatever it turns out to be) sets it for
neutrinos; Cooper-pair condensation sets it for photons in
superconductors. The five-way identity holds for all of these cases
uniformly.

*This matters because the unification is not Higgs-dependent.* The
orthodox tradition treats the equivalence principle as a postulate of
general relativity (1907), the principle of least action as a separate
variational principle (Maupertuis 1744, Hamilton 1833, Feynman 1948),
Newton's $F = ma$ as a separate dynamical law (Newton 1687), and the
Higgs mechanism as a 1964 construction for giving particles mass in the
electroweak sector. These four are treated as four independent
commitments in the orthodox tradition, with the equivalence principle's
coincidence of inertial and gravitational mass an empirical fact
requiring no derivation. The framework supplies the derivation: all four
(plus the Compton coupling as the fifth) are five physical contexts in
which one tensorial object $K^\mu$ on spacetime under $dx_4/dt = ic$
appears, with the equivalence principle's empirics as the signature of
the magnitude-sharing across contexts.

###### Empirical contact: atom-interferometric tests of the equivalence principle as direct probes of the five-way identity.

The recent controversy in atom interferometry between
Müller--Peters--Chu 2010 [@MullerPetersChu2010Nature] and
Wolf--Blanchet--Bordé--Reynaud--Salomon--Cohen-Tannoudji 2011
[@WolfEtAl2011CQG] is direct empirical-and-theoretical contact with the
five-way identity. The Müller--Peters--Chu interpretation reads atom
interferometry as a measurement of the Compton-frequency phase
accumulation along worldlines through different gravitational
potentials, identifying the atom as a clock at the Compton frequency
$mc^2/\hbar$. The Wolf et al. critique argues that the Compton-phase
difference between paths is zero in any consistent metric theory using a
single Lagrangian and the principle of least action, because the
magnitude factors out (the universality of free fall content).

*The framework's identity dissolves the controversy.* Both sides are
reading the same identity from different angles. Müller--Peters--Chu
correctly identify the Compton frequency as the physical
phase-accumulation rate (Context B of the present theorem); Wolf et
al. correctly observe that the magnitude factors out of the geodesic
equation (Context D's universality-of-free-fall content). The two are
not in conflict: the framework's identity says that the same magnitude
appears in both the phase-accumulation role and the geodesic-equation
role, with the cancellation in the geodesic equation being the signature
of the magnitude-sharing. Atom interferometry is simultaneously a test
of the universality of free fall (Wolf et al.) and a measurement of the
Compton-frequency phase accumulation (Müller--Peters--Chu), because the
underlying fact is one magnitude playing both roles. The framework's
reading: atom interferometry is a direct empirical probe of the five-way
identity of
Theorem [243](#thm:FiveWayStructuralIdentity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:FiveWayStructuralIdentity"}, with current precision of
one part in $10^{15}$ (MICROSCOPE 2017 [@Touboul2017MICROSCOPE] on the
universality-of-free-fall side; $\sim 10^{-9}$ on the Compton-phase side
[@MullerPetersChu2010Nature]) confirming the identity across both
contexts.

###### Why this picture has been unavailable to the orthodox tradition.

The five-way identity requires three facts that the orthodox tradition
has not adopted:

1.  *$x_4$ is a separate axis from the time coordinate $x^0 = ct$,
    expanding at velocity $c$ from every event of spacetime.* The
    orthodox tradition identifies the fourth dimension with the time
    coordinate, leaving no separate $x_4$ direction at every event
    against which the four-velocity perpendicular-component can wind at
    the Compton frequency. Without the separate $x_4$ axis, the
    identification of the Compton frequency with the
    perpendicular-winding rate is unavailable, and $K^\mu$ does not
    appear as a tensorial object on a manifold with a separate $x_4$
    direction.

2.  *The imaginary unit $i$ is the physical-geometric perpendicularity
    marker $i = (dx_4/dt)/c$ per [@MGWick Theorem 21.6bis.1], not a
    formal mathematical convenience.* The orthodox tradition treats the
    twelve $i$'s of quantum mechanics (canonical commutator, Schrödinger
    evolution, Dirac operator, path-integral weight, $U(1)$ gauge phase,
    Clifford structure, KMS condition, Born rule, Wick substitution,
    $+i\epsilon$ prescription, Fresnel integrals, action bridge) as
    twelve separate notational accidents. Without the reading of $i$ as
    the perpendicularity marker, the wavefunction phase
    $\exp(iS/\hbar) = \exp(-i\int\omega_C\, d\tau)$ cannot be recognised
    as the accumulated perpendicular-$x_4$-winding along the worldline.

3.  *Physics descends from a single physical-geometric principle, with
    the orthodox-tradition postulates ($F = ma$, principle of least
    action, equivalence principle, geodesic motion, action functional)
    as theorems.* The orthodox tradition treats these as five
    independent postulates. Without the search for a single principle
    that all five are theorems of, the unification of the five contexts
    as readings of one tensorial object on one manifold cannot come into
    view.

*The three facts are mutually reinforcing.* The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework adopts all three at once: $x_4$ as separate axis
(Equation [\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"}); $i$ as perpendicularity marker
([@MGWick Theorem 21.6bis.1]); physics as a chain of theorems descending
from $dx_4/dt = ic$. Once these three facts are in place, the five-way
identity becomes recognisable as the content the orthodox tradition has
been carrying in important places (Newton's $F = ma$ since 1687;
Hamilton's principle of least action since 1833; Einstein's equivalence
principle since 1907; the Compton-frequency identification of rest mass
since de Broglie 1924; geodesic motion in curved spacetime since
Einstein 1915; the wavefunction phase $\exp(iS/\hbar)$ since Dirac 1933
and Feynman 1948) without supplying the source.

###### Priority claim.

Within the primary-source literature reviewed at full-read grade for the
present paper, no programme has stated the five-way identity --- that
the Compton coupling, the principle of least action, gravity (the
Einstein field equations and geodesic motion), the equivalence principle
(universality of free fall), and inertia (Newton's $F = ma$ and its
relativistic extension) are five physical contexts of one tensorial
object $K^\mu = p^\mu/\hbar$ on a single manifold under one
physical-geometric principle. The Müller--Peters--Chu
[@MullerPetersChu2010Nature] programme identifies the Compton frequency
as the phase-accumulation rate in atom interferometry but does not state
the five-way identity; the Wolf et al. [@WolfEtAl2011CQG] critique
identifies the magnitude-cancellation in metric theories using the
principle of least action but does not identify the cancellation as the
equivalence-principle signature of one magnitude playing multiple roles.
The orthodox treatments (Misner--Thorne--Wheeler, Wald, Weinberg's
*Gravitation and Cosmology*, Wilczek's origins-of-mass writings) treat
the five contexts as five independent structures with empirical
correspondences between them.

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's advance: the five contexts are
not five independent postulates but five physical roles of one tensorial
object $K^\mu$ winding on the McGucken Sphere wavefront at every event
of spacetime under one principle $dx_4/dt = ic$. The equivalence
principle is the identity that the magnitude $|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2}$ is
shared across the roles; the universality of free fall is the empirical
signature of the magnitude-sharing; the principle of least action and
Newton's $F = ma$ are theorems of the McGucken Sphere's wavefront
structure and rotation-cost geometry rather than independent postulates.
*The unification is in the source ($dx_4/dt = ic$) and in the unifying
object ($K^\mu$ on spacetime), with the five physical contexts as
distinct readings of one.*

##### The Substrate-Origin Unity Theorem: the five physical contexts (and, when included, the Higgs sector) are forced theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$ on distinct sectors of spacetime, descending from the same substrate axiom {#sssec:SubstrateOriginUnity}

Theorems [242](#thm:FourComptonVectorUnification){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:FourComptonVectorUnification"}
and [243](#thm:FiveWayStructuralIdentity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:FiveWayStructuralIdentity"} above establish that the five
physical contexts (Compton coupling, principle of least action, gravity,
equivalence principle, inertia) are five physical roles of one tensorial
object $K^\mu$ winding on the McGucken Sphere wavefront at every event
of spacetime under $dx_4/dt = ic$. The framework's existing framework
establishes, in parallel, that the Higgs sector is itself forced by
$dx_4/dt = ic$ (Theorems H1--H8 of
§[5](#sec:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:HiggsPointer"}; [@MG-Higgs2026]) when the question of how
species-specific mass magnitudes are set for fundamental fermions in the
electroweak sector is engaged. The present subsubsection states the
unity that the existing chains establish: the substrate-origin unity is
what the existing forced-derivation chains amount to when read together.

::: {#thm:SubstrateOriginUnity .theorem}
**Theorem 244** (Substrate-Origin Unity: the five physical contexts and
the Higgs sector are forced theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$ on distinct
sectors of spacetime, descending from the same substrate axiom). *Per
the framework's existing forced-derivation from the McGucken Principle
$dx_4/dt = ic$:*

1.  ***The five physical contexts are forced theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$

    (Theorem [236](#thm:EquivalencePrinciple){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:EquivalencePrinciple"}), and inertia
    (Theorem [234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"}) are five physical roles of one
    tensorial object $K^\mu$ winding on the McGucken Sphere wavefront,
    with Lorentz-invariant magnitude
    $|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2} = mc/\hbar = \omega_C/c$ identifying the
    perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate. *This holds upstream of any

2.  ***The Higgs sector is a forced theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ on the
    matter sector of spacetime.** When the species-specific
    mass-magnitude of fundamental fermions in the electroweak sector is
    engaged, the Higgs as field-theoretic encoding of the local $+ic$

    (Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"

    Theorem [207](#thm:HiggsVev){reference-type="ref"

3.  ***The gravitational sector is a forced theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ on

    reference="thm:MassBendsSpaceX4Invariant"} of the present paper).
    The spatial-metric sector responds to integrated $K^\mu$-magnitude;

4.  ***The Higgs sector and the gravitational sector are distinct.**
    They operate on distinct sectors of spacetime (matter sector
    vs. spatial-metric sector) with distinct field-theoretic apparatus
    (scalar field $H$ with Mexican-hat potential and Yukawa couplings

5.  ***The two sectors couple to the same tensorial object $K^\mu$ on

    descending from $dx_4/dt = ic$
    (Theorems [242](#thm:FourComptonVectorUnification){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:FourComptonVectorUnification"}
    and [243](#thm:FiveWayStructuralIdentity){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:FiveWayStructuralIdentity"}).*

**The unity, stated directly:* the five physical contexts and the Higgs
sector are forced theorems of one substrate axiom $dx_4/dt = ic$
operating on distinct sectors of spacetime (the McGucken Sphere
wavefront for the five physical contexts; the matter sector for the
Higgs; the spatial-metric sector for gravity). The common coupling to
$K^\mu$ on the McGucken Sphere wavefront is the signature of the shared
substrate origin. *The Higgs sector, the gravitational sector, and the
five physical contexts of the four-Compton-vector unification are not
independent inputs to physics; they are forced theorems of the same
substrate principle on distinct sectors of spacetime.**

###### The orthodox tradition treats the Higgs and gravity as independent inputs; the framework establishes them as twin forced theorems of one axiom.

The orthodox tradition treats the Higgs mechanism (Englert--Brout--Higgs
1964) and general relativity (Einstein 1915) as two independent
constructions in physics, with the equivalence principle as postulate of
GR and the Higgs vev structure as independent postulate of the
electroweak sector. The McGucken framework establishes both as forced
theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$ operating on distinct sectors of spacetime,
with their common coupling to $K^\mu$ on the McGucken Sphere wavefront
as the signature of the shared substrate origin. *The substrate-origin
unity is the framework's advance over the orthodox treatment of Higgs
and gravity as independent inputs: they are not independent; they are
twin forced theorems of one axiom.*

###### Illustration: the electron gets its rest mass from $dx_4/dt = ic$ and feels gravity because of $dx_4/dt = ic$ --- same axiom, both ends, one $K^\mu$.

Theorem [244](#thm:SubstrateOriginUnity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SubstrateOriginUnity"} above is most transparently seen
in the concrete case of the electron.

The electron's rest mass IS the magnitude of its four-Compton-vector
$K^\mu_e$, identified per
Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"} as the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding
rate of the electron's four-velocity on the McGucken Sphere wavefront at
every event in its worldline. This magnitude is set by $dx_4/dt = ic$ at
every event in the matter sector of spacetime via the Higgs-Yukawa
mechanism, with the Higgs vev as the field-theoretic recording of the
local $+ic$ direction
(Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}) and the electron-Yukawa coupling
$y_e \approx 2.94 \times 10^{-6}$ supplying the species-specific winding
rate (Theorem [218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:YukawaWinding"}).

The electron feels gravity because the spatial-metric sector $g_{ij}$
curves around integrated $|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2}$-magnitude via the
Einstein field equations $G^{\mu\nu} = (8\pi G/c^4)T^{\mu\nu}$ (with
stress-energy tensor $T^{\mu\nu}$ sourced by integrated
four-Compton-vector-magnitude of matter, per
Theorem [236](#thm:EquivalencePrinciple){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:EquivalencePrinciple"}, Property (ii)), and the
electron's $K^\mu_e$ parallel-transports through that curved
spatial-metric geometry along its worldline. Throughout the parallel
transport, the temporal rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ stays metric-rigid at every
event regardless of the curvature
(Theorem [237](#thm:MassBendsSpaceX4Invariant){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MassBendsSpaceX4Invariant"}, Property (ii)).

*Same axiom. Both ends. One $K^\mu$.* The substrate principle
$dx_4/dt = ic$ acts at the source-setting end of $K^\mu$ (matter-sector
Higgs-Yukawa mechanism, fixing the magnitude of $K^\mu_e$) and at the
transport end (geometric-sector Einstein equations sourced by integrated
magnitude, fixing the curved spatial-metric geometry through which
$K^\mu_e$ parallel-transports). The two ends are not two separate
mechanisms but two consequences of one substrate axiom, as
Theorem [244](#thm:SubstrateOriginUnity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SubstrateOriginUnity"} establishes.

::: {#rem:FrameworkFirstInLiterature .remark}
*Remark 245* (The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework as the first
programme to derive Higgs + Inertia + Principle of Least Action +
Equivalence Principle from a single principle). Per the primary-source
literature review documented at the opening of the present subsection:

-   Standard Model (with the Higgs mechanism postulated): supplies the
    Higgs and Yukawa-induced inertial mass, but not the equivalence
    principle (open problem per
    [@UnnikrishnanGillies2015; @BinLi2025ChrononFieldTheory]), not the
    principle of least action (postulated variational principle), and
    not inertia from a principle.

-   General relativity (with the equivalence principle postulated):
    supplies the geodesic-equation content of gravitational mass, but
    not the Higgs mechanism (separate physics) and not the equivalence
    principle's derivation (it is a postulate per
    [@Synge1960; @OstomaTrushyk1999EMQGSummary]).

-   Chronon Field Theory ([@BinLi2025ChrononFieldTheory], June 2025
    preprint, not yet peer-reviewed): proposes
    inertial-and-gravitational mass coincidence via solitons in a
    unit-norm timelike vector field; closest in spirit to the McGucken
    $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework on this specific point but lacks the
    McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's derivation of $c, \hbar$,
    McGucken-Sphere wavefront, dual-channel architecture, and Standard
    Model gauge content from a single principle.

-   TEGR/STEGR (Mancini, Tino, & Capozziello 2025
    [@Capozziello2025EquivalenceGravities], *Foundations of Physics*
    55:69): the equivalence principle is recovered a posteriori in
    teleparallel formulations of gravity, not postulated a priori; the
    problem "how we can justify the coincidence between gravitational
    and inertial mass" is explicitly listed by the authors as one of
    eight foundational EP problems associated with GR; the Higgs
    mechanism is not engaged.

-   EMQG ([@OstomaTrushyk1999EMQGEP; @OstomaTrushyk1999EMQGSummary],
    1999): attempts a quantum-vacuum-fluctuations derivation of the
    equivalence principle; not adopted in mainstream physics; the Higgs
    mechanism is not engaged.

-   Other proposals (Dehnen 1991, Chiatti 2025, Supanyo 2021): partial
    engagements; none derives the Higgs mechanism, the principle of
    least action, the inertia, AND the equivalence principle from a
    single principle.

*Within the primary-source literature reviewed, no programme other than
the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework has derived the Higgs mechanism,
the principle of least action, the inertia of mass, and the equivalence
principle from a single principle.* The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$

The empirical equivalence-principle confirmation at one part in
$10^{15}$ (MICROSCOPE 2017) is the empirical signature of this identity.
The framework's contribution to the open problem documented by Synge,
Ostoma--Trushyk, Unnikrishnan-Gillies, and Bin Li is derivation, not
analytic-numerical resolution. The analytic-numerics (Yukawa magnitudes,
Newton's $G$, three-generation count) remains as open in the framework
as in standard physics; the identification is the framework's advance.
:::

#### Theorem H11.5: Composite-state mass as integrated $x_4$-winding rate of internal degrees of freedom --- the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's reading of Wilczek's "mass without mass" {#ssec:CompositeStateMass}

Theorems H10 and H11 established the framework's identification of rest
mass with the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate for elementary fermions,
with the Higgs vev as the $+ic$-direction encoder and the Yukawa
coupling as the species-specific winding-rate dial. This covers the
elementary fermions (electrons, charged leptons, quarks) and the gauge
bosons that acquire mass through electroweak symmetry breaking ($W^\pm$,
$Z$). It does not yet address the dominant numerical contribution to the
mass of ordinary visible matter: the proton's mass, of which only a
small fraction is contributed by the valence-quark Yukawa-induced
winding. Wilczek's three treatments
[@Wilczek1999MassWithoutMassI; @Wilczek2000MassWithoutMassII; @Wilczek2012OriginsOfMass]
establish the empirical fact: the bulk of the mass of ordinary matter
arises from the back-reaction of color gluon fields in the QCD vacuum
upon the confined quarks, not from the quarks' intrinsic Higgs-induced
masses. The question for the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework is
therefore: in the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate reading of mass, what
is the corresponding identification for composite states?

###### Wilczek's three statements of the QCD-binding-energy mass.

For self-containment, we record the three primary statements:

-   *Wilczek 1999* [@Wilczek1999MassWithoutMassI p. 11]: "The bulk of
    the mass of ordinary matter (better than 99%) comes from the masses
    of protons and neutrons. ... Let us set \[the up and down quark
    masses\] to zero. Now our resulting truncated, approximate version
    of QCD contains no mass terms at all. ... Yet, if we use it to
    calculate the mass of protons and neutrons --- the mass of ordinary
    matter --- we find it is accurate to within 10%! ... The energy in
    this field is ... what mostly makes us weigh. It thus provides,
    quite literally, 'mass without mass.'" The accompanying mechanism:
    "energy stored in the motion of the quarks, and energy in the color
    gluon fields that connect them. This bundling of energy makes the
    proton's mass." Wilczek attributes the original phrase "mass without
    mass" to Wheeler [@Wheeler1962Geometrodynamics].

-   *Wilczek 2000* [@Wilczek2000MassWithoutMassII p. 13]: "Most of the
    mass of ordinary matter, for sure, is the pure energy of moving
    quarks and gluons. The remainder, a quantitatively small but
    qualitatively crucial remainder --- it includes the mass of
    electrons --- is all ascribed to the confounding influence of a
    pervasive medium, the Higgs field condensate."

-   *Wilczek 2012* [@Wilczek2012OriginsOfMass §III, pp. 10--11]: "Most
    ($\sim 95\%$) of the mass of protons and neutrons, and thus of
    ordinary matter, is due to the back-reaction of color gluon fields
    resisting accelerated motion of the quarks and gluons inside. Very
    detailed and impressive calculations, based on direct numerical
    solution of the equations and exploiting the full power of modern
    computers, stand behind those words." Wilczek calls the
    parameter-free QCD theory used for this calculation "QCD Lite" ---
    QCD with the three lightest quark masses set to zero and the heavy
    quarks decoupled. "QCD Lite is a theory containing no explicit mass
    parameters; its only dimensional scale is set by the coupling
    evolution. Yet it supports a rich spectrum of massive excitations,
    notably including protons and neutrons, that closely resembles the
    spectrum of QCD proper."

The empirical fact recorded by Wilczek across these three sources is
unambiguous: of the proton mass $m_p \approx 938.3$ MeV, the
contribution from the valence quarks' Higgs-induced rest masses
($2 m_u + m_d \approx 2 \cdot 2.16 + 4.67 = 8.99$ MeV with PDG 2024
central values) is approximately $1\%$, with the remaining $\sim 99\%$
arising dynamically from the QCD vacuum's interaction with the confined
quarks and gluons. The contemporary popular-literature articulation by
Strassler [@Strassler2024Waves] reproduces this empirics for a general
audience.

###### The question for the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework.

The mass identification of
Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"} (rest mass as
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate, with the Higgs vev as the
$+ic$-direction encoder) covers the Higgs-coupling contribution to
elementary-fermion mass. The QCD-binding-energy contribution to proton
mass is a separate phenomenon at the level of mechanism: the proton's
mass arises from confined-internal-degrees-of-freedom field energy, not
from any Higgs-mediated winding. The physics question to be answered is
whether the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate identification *extends* to
composite states whose internal degrees of freedom carry their own
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rates, or whether composite-state mass
requires a separate identification.

::: {#thm:CompositeStateMass .theorem}
**Theorem 247** (Composite-state mass as integrated
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate of internal degrees of freedom).
*Assume the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$,
Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"} (rest mass as
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate),
Theorem [234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"} (mass-energy as four-velocity
rotation), and the validity of relativistic energy-momentum conservation
for bound states. Let $|B\rangle$ be a bound state of internal degrees
of freedom (constituent fields, gauge-field configurations,
vacuum-fluctuation modes), with total four-momentum $P^\mu$. Define the
rest mass $m_B$ of the bound state by $P^\mu P_\mu = -m_B^2 c^2$ in the
bound-state's rest frame (centre-of-energy frame). Then:*

1.  ***Composite Compton frequency.** The bound state's wavefunction
    (centre-of-energy wavefunction, treating the bound state as a
    localised quantum object) winds at the composite Compton frequency
    $\omega_C^B = m_B c^2/\hbar$. This is a direct application of
    Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}, Property (ii), to the bound
    state as a localised quantum entity with definite rest mass $m_B$ in
    its rest frame.*

2.  ***Composite four-velocity is perpendicular to three-space at
    three-rest.** By the Master Equation $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ applied to
    the centre-of-energy four-velocity, the bound state at three-rest
    has its four-velocity entirely in the perpendicular-$x_4$ direction:
    $u^\mu_B = (c, 0, 0, 0)$ in the local
    $(\hat x_4, \hat x_1, \hat x_2, \hat x_3)$ decomposition. The bound
    state, as a whole, winds through $x_4$ at velocity $c$.*

3.  ***Energy accounting in the bound-state rest frame.** The total
    energy of the bound state at three-rest decomposes into the
    contributions of its internal degrees of freedom in the
    centre-of-energy frame: $$\label{eq:CompositeEnergyDecomposition}
    E_B^{\rm rest} = m_B c^2 = \sum_{\rm constituent\ fermions} \left[ m_f c^2 + K_f \right] + E_{\rm gauge-fields} + E_{\rm vacuum-fluctuations} + E_{\rm potential},$$
    where $K_f$ is the kinetic energy of constituent fermion $f$ in the
    bound-state rest frame, $E_{\rm gauge-fields}$ is the energy stored
    in the configuration of gauge fields binding the constituents (for
    the proton, the colour-electric and colour-magnetic gluon-field
    energies), $E_{\rm vacuum-fluctuations}$ is the energy of
    virtual-particle fluctuations (sea quarks, gluon self-interactions,
    and any contributions from confined-state vacuum-modification), and
    $E_{\rm potential}$ encodes any binding-potential contributions not
    separately attributable to a single field configuration. This is
    standard relativistic energy-conservation for a bound system in its
    rest frame, applied to the QCD picture of the proton.*

4.  ***Each internal degree of freedom contributes its own
    perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate.** By
    Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}, each constituent fermion at
    instantaneous rest in some local frame contributes a winding-rate
    term $m_f c^2/\hbar$ at the Compton frequency, and (by relativistic
    generalization with kinetic energy $K_f > 0$) contributes total
    $x_4$-winding-relevant energy $\sqrt{(m_f c^2)^2 + (p_f c)^2}$ where
    $p_f$ is its three-momentum in the bound-state rest frame. The
    gauge-field configurations contribute through the field-theoretic
    identification $T^{00}_{\rm gauge} = (E_a^2 + B_a^2)/2$ for the
    colour electric and magnetic gluon-field components (per Gluon mode
    $a = 1, \ldots, 8$). The vacuum-fluctuation contributions are
    field-theoretic interaction-energy contributions evaluated in the
    QCD vacuum.*

5.  ***Composite winding rate is the integrated internal-degree winding
    rate.** Combining (iii) and (iv) with $E_B^{\rm rest} = m_B c^2$ and
    substituting the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate readings of all
    internal-degree contributions:
    $$\label{eq:CompositeIntegratedWinding}
    \omega_C^B = \frac{m_B c^2}{\hbar} = \frac{1}{\hbar} \sum_{\rm internal\ d.o.f.} E_i^{\rm rest-frame}.$$
    *The composite Compton frequency is the sum of the
    perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate equivalents of all internal degrees
    of freedom in the bound-state rest frame.* In particular, the
    gauge-field-energy contributions (gluon-field energies, for the
    proton) contribute directly to the composite winding rate, even
    though the gauge-field quanta themselves (gluons) carry no
    Yukawa-induced winding rate at the elementary level (gluons are
    massless on null worldlines per
    Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}, Property (vi)).*
:::

::: proof
*Sketch and grade..* Grade 2: standard relativistic-bound-state
kinematics composed with the framework's
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate identification of
Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}.

*Property (i):*
Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}, Property (ii), applies to any state
with definite rest mass $m$ in its rest frame, including composite bound
states with definite $m_B$. The bound state's centre-of-energy
wavefunction has phase advance $e^{-im_B c^2 \tau_B/\hbar}$ along its
proper time $\tau_B$, with angular frequency $m_B c^2/\hbar$.

*Property (ii):* Master Equation applied to the centre-of-energy
four-velocity in the bound-state rest frame.

*Property (iii):* Standard relativistic decomposition of the bound-state
total energy in the rest frame. The sum on the right-hand side of
[\[eq:CompositeEnergyDecomposition\]](#eq:CompositeEnergyDecomposition){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:CompositeEnergyDecomposition"} is the rest-frame
Hamiltonian's expectation value $\langle B | \hat H | B \rangle$ in the
bound-state quantum state, with constituent and gauge-field
contributions decomposed conventionally. This is QCD's textbook
accounting of proton mass into quark-rest-mass, quark-kinetic, and
gluon-field-energy contributions; see for example
[@Yang2018ProtonMassDecomposition Eqs. (6.1)--(6.5)] for the modern
lattice-QCD decomposition.

*Property (iv):* Each term on the right-hand side of
[\[eq:CompositeEnergyDecomposition\]](#eq:CompositeEnergyDecomposition){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:CompositeEnergyDecomposition"} contributes through
standard relativistic energy-mass equivalence: a contribution of energy
$E_i$ in the rest frame contributes $E_i/c^2$ to the composite mass and
$E_i/\hbar$ to the composite Compton winding rate. The
constituent-fermion contributions decompose into rest-mass and kinetic
terms; the gauge-field contributions are pure field energy with no
Higgs-induced winding component; the vacuum-fluctuation contributions
are field-theoretic interaction energies in the QCD vacuum.

*Property (v):* Combining (i), (ii), (iii), (iv):
$\omega_C^B = m_B c^2/\hbar = E_B^{\rm rest}/\hbar = (\sum_i E_i^{\rm rest})/\hbar = \sum_i (E_i^{\rm rest}/\hbar)$. ◻
:::

::: {#cor:WilczekMassWithoutMass .corollary}
**Corollary 248** (Wilczek's "mass without mass" is the
McGucken-framework statement that internal-degree
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate contributions can dominate the
composite-state perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate). *For the proton
$|p\rangle$, Theorem [247](#thm:CompositeStateMass){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:CompositeStateMass"}, Property (v), specialised to the
QCD bound state: $$\label{eq:ProtonComptonDecomposition}
\omega_C^p = \frac{m_p c^2}{\hbar} = \frac{1}{\hbar}\Big[\underbrace{(2 m_u c^2 + m_d c^2)}_{\sim 1\%\ \rm valence\ quark\ rest\ mass} + \underbrace{K_q^{\rm valence}}_{\rm valence\ kinetic} + \underbrace{E_{\rm gluon-fields}}_{\rm gluon\ field\ energy} + \underbrace{E_{\rm sea}}_{\rm sea-quark\ \&\ sea-gluon\ fluctuations} + \cdots\Big].$$
The numerics of
[\[eq:ProtonComptonDecomposition\]](#eq:ProtonComptonDecomposition){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:ProtonComptonDecomposition"} is, with PDG 2024 central
values and the lattice-QCD-extracted decomposition of
[@Yang2018ProtonMassDecomposition] for the proton's energy budget:*

-   *Valence-quark rest-mass contribution: $2 m_u + m_d \approx 8.99$
    MeV, contributing $\approx 0.96\%$ of $m_p c^2 \approx 938.3$ MeV.*

-   *Quark kinetic-energy contribution (lattice QCD): $\approx 33\%$.*

-   *Gluon-field-energy contribution (lattice QCD): $\approx 36\%$.*

-   *Trace-anomaly + sigma-term + sea-quark contributions:
    $\approx 30\%$.*

*(Exact lattice-QCD percentages depend on the renormalisation scheme;
the qualitative breakdown is robust across schemes. See
[@Yang2018ProtonMassDecomposition; @Lorce2018ProtonMassDecomp] for
current values.)*

**The McGucken-framework reading of Wilczek's "mass without mass":* The
proton's perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate $\omega_C^p$ is the integrated
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate of all internal degrees of freedom. The
valence quarks contribute approximately $1\%$ through their
Higgs-induced individual winding rates
(Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"} applied to each); the remaining
$\approx 99\%$ comes from the kinetic motion of the valence quarks, the
energy stored in the gluon-field configurations binding the quarks, and
the contributions of the sea-quark/sea-gluon vacuum fluctuations within
the proton. Every one of these contributions, through
Theorem [247](#thm:CompositeStateMass){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:CompositeStateMass"}, Property (iv), contributes to the
composite-state perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate. Wheeler's phrase "mass
without mass" (1962) and Wilczek's 1999--2012 elaborations are the
empirical-experimental confirmation that, for the proton, the bulk of
the composite-state perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate arises from
non-Higgs sources: the gluon-field-energy contribution alone exceeds the
Higgs-mediated valence-quark contribution by a factor of approximately
$36$.*
:::

::: {#rem:UnifiedMassReading .remark}
*Remark 249* (The unified reading of mass across all three
Wilczek-Strassler mass mechanisms). The contemporary popular treatment
by Strassler [@Strassler2024Waves Chapters 19--21], with the
corresponding general-audience video presentation
[@HiggsMassYouTube2026], articulates the post-Higgs-discovery situation
as "mass" referring to "at least three distinct things": (a) the mass
that elementary fermions get from the Higgs field via Yukawa coupling,
(b) the mass that composite particles (protons, neutrons, nuclei) get
from the binding energy of the strong force, (c) the mass that neutrinos
have through some mechanism not yet identified (Dirac, Majorana, or
seesaw). The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework reduces these three
apparent "mechanisms" to one identification of *what mass is*, with
three different energy sources contributing into the same
identification:

1.  **Mass is perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate.**
    Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}: for any state of definite rest
    mass $m$, the rest mass *is* the rate at which the state's
    wavefunction winds perpendicular through $x_4$ at three-rest,
    observed in three-space as the Compton frequency
    $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$. This is the framework's identification of
    what "mass" is. It applies to elementary fermions, gauge bosons,
    composite hadrons, atoms, nuclei, and macroscopic bound states
    alike.

2.  **Three energy sources feed into the same identification.**

    -   *Strassler-(a) Higgs/Yukawa source.* For elementary fermions,
        the Higgs vev establishes the $+ic$ direction at each spacetime
        event (Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
        reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}), and the Yukawa coupling $y_f$
        sets the species-specific winding rate
        (Theorem [218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
        reference="thm:YukawaWinding"}):
        $\omega_C^f = (y_f v/\sqrt{2}) c^2/\hbar$.

    -   *Strassler-(b) QCD-binding-energy source.* For composite hadrons
        (protons, neutrons, hyperons, etc.),
        Theorem [247](#thm:CompositeStateMass){reference-type="ref"
        reference="thm:CompositeStateMass"} and
        Corollary [248](#cor:WilczekMassWithoutMass){reference-type="ref"
        reference="cor:WilczekMassWithoutMass"}: the composite Compton
        frequency $\omega_C^B$ is the integrated
        perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate of all internal degrees of
        freedom, with the gluon-field-energy and quark-kinetic
        contributions dominating over the Higgs-mediated valence-quark
        contribution.

    -   *Strassler-(c) Neutrino mechanism.* For neutrinos, the source of
        perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate at the substrate level remains
        open in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, as in standard
        physics. The framework accommodates either a Dirac Yukawa-type
        coupling (per
        Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
        reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}, treating the neutrino as a
        standard fermion with very small $y_\nu$) or a Majorana mass
        term (with the corresponding extension of the matter orientation
        condition (M) of
        Definition [80](#def:OrientationM){reference-type="ref"
        reference="def:OrientationM"} to lepton-number-violating
        couplings); the choice between these is an empirical question
        that the framework's current content does not resolve.

3.  **The three sources are three different energy contributors to the
    same perpendicular-$x_4$-winding identification.** The framework's
    advance over the Strassler "three distinct things" framing is the
    recognition that the apparent multiplicity is at the level of
    *energy source contributing into the winding rate*, not at the level
    of *what mass is*. Mass is one thing --- the
    perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate --- with three (or more) physically
    distinct energy contributors. The Higgs mechanism, the QCD
    binding-energy mechanism, and the neutrino-mass mechanism are three
    energy-source-to-winding-rate channels, all feeding into the same
    quantity $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$.

The unification is not an extra postulate of the framework; it follows
directly from Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"} applied to elementary fermions and
Theorem [247](#thm:CompositeStateMass){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:CompositeStateMass"} applied to composite states. The
framework's reading is therefore: *Wilczek 1999 and Strassler 2024 are
correct that the proton's mass arises "without Higgs" --- the
gluon-field-energy contribution dominates the Higgs-induced
valence-quark contribution by a factor of $\sim 36$. The McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework adds the physical reading of what *is*
happening: the gluon-field energy contributes to the proton's composite
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate, exactly as a winding rate is what mass
is.*
:::

::: {#rem:CompositeMassHonestScope .remark}
*Remark 250* (Honest-scope statement on what
Theorem [247](#thm:CompositeStateMass){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:CompositeStateMass"} does and does not establish). We
state the scope of the present subsection's content explicitly.
Theorem [247](#thm:CompositeStateMass){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:CompositeStateMass"} together with
Corollary [248](#cor:WilczekMassWithoutMass){reference-type="ref"
reference="cor:WilczekMassWithoutMass"} and
Remark [249](#rem:UnifiedMassReading){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:UnifiedMassReading"} establish:

-   *A physical reading* of how the QCD-binding-energy contribution to
    proton mass enters the framework's perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate
    identification of mass. The reading is that the composite-state
    winding rate is the integrated winding rate of internal degrees of
    freedom, including gauge-field-energy contributions, even when those
    gauge-field quanta carry no Higgs-induced individual winding rate.

-   *A unification* of the apparent multiplicity of mass-generating
    mechanisms (Higgs-Yukawa for elementary fermions, QCD binding for
    hadrons, and the open neutrino-mass mechanism) into a single
    identification of mass with one principle ($\omega = mc^2/\hbar$)
    and multiple energy contributors.

-   *An empirical confirmation* that the framework's
    perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate identification of mass is
    consistent with the lattice-QCD computation of the proton mass: the
    bulk of the proton's composite Compton frequency arises from
    gluon-field-energy and quark-kinetic contributions, not from the
    Higgs-mediated valence-quark contribution, and this is exactly what
    the framework expects for any composite bound state whose internal
    degrees of freedom carry their own perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate
    equivalents.

The scope of what the present subsection does *not* establish:

-   The numerical value $m_p \approx 938.3$ MeV is not derived in the
    present paper. This is the QCD analogue of the open (H2)
    magnitude-of-$v$ problem identified in the hierarchy trichotomy of
    Theorem [210](#thm:HierarchyTrichotomy){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:HierarchyTrichotomy"}, and the derivation requires
    non-perturbative QCD methods (lattice QCD, Dyson-Schwinger
    equations, holographic-QCD approaches) that are open problems within
    standard physics as well. The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's
    gauge-group derivation of $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ from $dx_4/dt = ic$
    (Part III of the present paper) provides the backing for the QCD
    framework within which the proton mass is computable; the analytic
    resolution of the confinement problem and the numerical value of
    $\Lambda_{\rm QCD}$ remain open.

-   The numerical values of the individual Yukawa couplings $y_f$ remain
    empirical inputs. The Strassler 2024 puzzle of "why is the muon
    $207$ times heavier than the electron" is the same puzzle the
    Standard Model presents: the framework reads $y_\mu/y_e = 206.7$ as
    the ratio of perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rates of the muon and
    electron, but does not derive this ratio. This is the (H2) magnitude
    problem extended to the Yukawa-coupling spectrum.

-   The three-generation count of fermions is not derived in the present
    paper. The framework reproduces the three-generation structure as
    input to the species spectrum (Move H of the Riemann section,
    Theorem [440](#thm:NumericalZerosNaive){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:NumericalZerosNaive"}, uses three generations as
    input) but does not derive that count $= 3$.

-   The neutrino-mass mechanism remains open.
    Theorem [247](#thm:CompositeStateMass){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:CompositeStateMass"} applies to any state with
    definite rest mass and so subsumes the empirics of neutrino mass
    into the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate identification regardless
    of whether the underlying mass is Dirac, Majorana, or some seesaw
    construction; the choice between mechanisms is an empirical question
    that lies beyond the present paper.

The contribution of the present subsection is therefore: the framework
extends its perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate identification of mass from
the elementary-particle case (covered by
Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}) to the composite-state case (covered
by Theorem [247](#thm:CompositeStateMass){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:CompositeStateMass"}), with the natural identification
that internal-degree winding-rate contributions sum to the
composite-state winding rate. This is a extension; it is not a
derivation of numerical mass values.
:::

#### Theorem H11.6: Photon mass in superconductors as McGucken-Sphere wavefront-coupling at condensed-matter scale --- the deep reason the Anderson-Higgs mechanism in superconductors and the electroweak Higgs mechanism share the same mathematical equations {#ssec:PhotonMassSuperconductor}

Theorems H10 and H11.5 established the framework's identification of
mass with the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate at species-specific
Compton frequency, with the Higgs vev as $+ic$-direction encoder and the
Yukawa coupling (or, for composite states, the integrated
internal-degree winding-rate) as the species-specific rate dial. The
orthodox literature has long recognised that the *same mathematical
structure* that gives fundamental fermions and electroweak gauge bosons
their masses via the Higgs mechanism also gives photons inside
superconductors an effective mass via the Anderson-Higgs mechanism. The
question for the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework is therefore: *what
is the deeper physical reason the same mathematical equations govern
both the cosmological electroweak Higgs sector and the condensed-matter
superconductor sector?* We engage this question at theorem grade in the
present subsection.

###### The orthodox-literature primary-source recognition: same equations, same mechanism, separated only by what condenses and at what energy scale.

The same-mathematical-equations recognition is documented at
primary-source grade across the orthodox literature from 1935 to the
present:

*London and London 1935* [@LondonLondon1935] (Fritz London and Heinz
London, *The electromagnetic equations of the supraconductor*,
Proc. Roy. Soc. A **149**:71--88, 1 March 1935): the original London
equations for the supraconducting state postulate
$\vec{j}_s = -(n_s e^2/m_e c) \vec{A}$, which together with the Maxwell
equations $\nabla \times \vec{B} = (4\pi/c) \vec{j}_s$ produce the
modified wave equation
$$\nabla^2 \vec{B} = \frac{1}{\lambda_L^2} \vec{B}, \qquad \lambda_L \equiv \sqrt{\frac{m_e c^2}{4\pi n_s e^2}}\,,
\label{eq:LondonEquation}$$ where $\lambda_L$ is the London penetration
depth. This is mathematically equivalent to the static Klein-Gordon
equation with photon mass $m_\gamma = \hbar/(c\lambda_L)$
[@Anderson1963PlasmonsGaugeInvarianceMass; @deBruynOuboterOmelyanchouk2017].

*Anderson 1963* [@Anderson1963PlasmonsGaugeInvarianceMass] (Philip
W. Anderson, Bell Telephone Laboratories, *Plasmons, Gauge Invariance,
and Mass*, Physical Review **130**(1):439--442, 1 April 1963). Verbatim
abstract: "Schwinger has pointed out that the Yang-Mills vector boson
implied by associating a generalized gauge transformation with a
conservation law (of baryonic charge, for instance) does not necessarily
have zero mass, if a certain criterion on the vacuum fluctuations of the
generalized current is satisfied. We show that the theory of plasma
oscillations is a simple nonrelativistic example exhibiting all of the
features of Schwinger's idea. It is also shown that Schwinger's
criterion that the vector field $m = 0$ implies that the matter spectrum
before including the Yang-Mills interaction contains $m = 0$, but that
the example of superconductivity illustrates that the physical spectrum
need not." Anderson's 1963 paper is the primary source establishing the
equivalence: *superconductor photon-mass and Yang-Mills gauge-boson-mass
share the same gauge-invariance-breaking mechanism*. The
eaten-Nambu-Goldstone-boson-becomes-longitudinal-vector-mode content of
the Anderson-Higgs mechanism in superconductors is mathematically
identical to that of the electroweak Higgs mechanism in particle
physics, separated only by which scalar field condenses (Cooper-pair
density $|\psi_s|^2$ in superconductors; Higgs doublet vev
$\langle H\rangle$ in particle physics) and at what energy scale the
condensation occurs (a few Kelvin in superconductors; the electroweak
scale $v \approx 246$ GeV at the early-universe temperature
$\sim 10^{15}$ K in particle physics).

*Wilczek 2005* [@Wilczek2005SearchSymmetryLost] (Frank Wilczek, *In
search of symmetry lost*, Nature **433**(7023):239--247, 20 January
2005). Wilczek states the equivalence verbatim: "Unlike the photon,
which acquires mass only inside superconductors, $W$ and $Z$ are massive
particles even in empty space. The equations of gauge symmetry, in their
pristine form, predict the existence of these particles, but require
that their masses vanish. To account for the masses of $W$ and $Z$, we
must suppose that what we perceive as empty space is, in reality, a new
form of superconductor, not for electromagnetism, but for its
near-relation gauge interactions." This is the canonical Wilczek
formulation: *empty space is a superconductor for the electroweak gauge
field*, with the Higgs condensate playing the role the Cooper-pair
condensate plays in conventional electromagnetic superconductors.

*Allen 2013* [@Allen2013LAEBHGHKW] (Roland E. Allen, Texas A&M
University, *The
London-Anderson-Englert-Brout-Higgs-Guralnik-Hagen-Kibble-Weinberg
mechanism and Higgs boson reveal the unity and future excitement of
physics*, arXiv:1306.4061, 18 June 2013). Allen's primary-source
articulation of the unity, verbatim: "It is a true demonstration of the
unity of physics that this Meissner effect in a superconducting metal
and the short range of the weak nuclear force in the universe have the
same origin: In each case the vector bosons (photons or $W$ and $Z$
bosons) grow masses because they are coupled to a field which forms a
condensate at low temperature, as the metal is cooled in the laboratory
or the universe expands and cools after the Big Bang."

*De Bruyn Ouboter and Omelyanchouk 2017*
[@deBruynOuboterOmelyanchouk2017] (R. de Bruyn Ouboter, Kamerlingh Onnes
Laboratory, Leiden, and A. N. Omelyanchouk, B. Verkin Institute for Low
Temperature Physics, Kharkiv, *On massive photons inside a
superconductor as follows from London and Ginzburg-Landau theory*, Low
Temperature Physics / Fizika Nizkikh Temperatur **43**(7):1109--1112, 25
May 2017). Read in full at primary source. The primary-source
identification of the photon's effective mass in a superconductor with
its Compton frequency, verbatim from p. 1109: "A phenomenological
derivation is given that photons behave inside a superconductor as if
they have mass by comparison of the original first equation of the
London's and the equations for the electromagnetic field with the
time-dependent relativistic Schrödinger equation. The photons move
through a medium, the Ginzburg-Landau free energy density, inside the
superconductor in which they acquire mass. *The Compton wave length of
the massive photons is equal to $2\pi$ times the London penetration
depth and the mass of the photon is equal to $\hbar/c\lambda_L$.*"
Verbatim from p. 1110 on the Ginzburg-Landau "Higgs field"
identification: "We plot the relevant Ginzburg-Landau free energy
density $F$ versus $|\psi_s|^2$, which is often called the 'Higgs
field', for both $T > T_c$ and $T < T_c$ when the symmetry of the 'Higgs
field' is broken...The photon in the superconductor does interact with
the Ginzburg-Landau or 'Higgs field', it interacts with this field,
gains energy, slows down, the 'field' dragged on the photon and the
interaction with the particle photon and the field is manifested as a
resistance of the photon particle acceleration. When the photon particle
moves at constant velocity it is not affected by the 'field'...During
the cooling of the superconductor from $T > T_c$ to $T < T_c$ each
photon inside the superconductor acquires an energy $mc^2$."

###### The same-equations.

The orthodox literature establishes the following mathematical
equivalence between the two contexts, recorded at primary-source grade.
In both cases, the wave equation for the gauge field acquires a
Klein-Gordon mass term:
$$\left(\frac{1}{c^2}\frac{\partial^2}{\partial t^2} - \nabla^2 + \frac{1}{\lambda^2}\right) \vec{A} = 0,
\label{eq:UnifiedMassEquation}$$ with the characteristic length
$\lambda$ identified as:

-   **Superconductor (Anderson-Higgs in condensed matter):**
    $\lambda = \lambda_L = \sqrt{m_e c^2/(4\pi n_s e^2)}$, the London
    penetration depth, with the photon Compton wavelength satisfying
    $\lambda_C^{\rm photon} = 2\pi \lambda_L$ and photon effective mass
    $m_\gamma = \hbar/(c\lambda_L)$ (typically a few eV/$c^2$ for
    $\lambda_L \sim 50$ nm). The condensate supplying the mass is the
    Cooper-pair condensate $|\psi_s|^2$.

-   **Electroweak sector (Anderson-Higgs in particle physics):**
    $\lambda = 1/M_W = \hbar/(M_W c)$, the inverse $W$-boson mass times
    $c$, with $W$-boson mass $M_W = gv/2 \approx 80.4$ GeV/$c^2$ (giving
    $\lambda \sim 2.5 \times 10^{-18}$ m, the weak-interaction range).
    The condensate supplying the mass is the Higgs doublet vev
    $\langle H\rangle = v/\sqrt{2} \approx 174$ GeV.

The mathematical structure is identical; what differs is the condensate
and the energy scale at which it forms. This is the orthodox-tradition
recognition documented at
[@LondonLondon1935; @GinzburgLandau1950; @Anderson1963PlasmonsGaugeInvarianceMass; @EnglertBrout1964PRL; @Higgs1964PLB; @GuralnikHagenKibble1964PRL; @Weinberg2005QFTVol2; @Wilczek2005SearchSymmetryLost; @Allen2013LAEBHGHKW; @deBruynOuboterOmelyanchouk2017].

###### The deeper reason: McGucken Principle reading.

The orthodox tradition recognises the same-mathematical-equations but
does *not* supply the deeper physical reason why the same equations
should hold in two such different contexts. Wilczek's framing "empty
space is a superconductor" is a metaphor that captures the parallel but
does not identify what physics is shared between the two contexts. The
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework supplies the content.

###### Wilczek's "empty space is a superconductor" is the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's identity.

The Wilczek 2005 verbatim formulation [@Wilczek2005SearchSymmetryLost]
reads: "we must suppose that what we perceive as empty space is, in
reality, a new form of superconductor, not for electromagnetism, but for
its near-relation gauge interactions." This metaphor captures the
parallel between the electroweak Higgs sector and the conventional
electromagnetic superconductor, but it leaves open the deeper question:
*what physics is shared between empty space and a superconductor that
makes them act as the same kind of system?*

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework supplies the identification. Empty
space and a superconductor are not just metaphorically similar; they
share the same underlying physics at theorem grade. The shared content
is:

-   *Both are domains in which the McGucken-Sphere wavefront expands at
    $c$ from every event* (per $dx_4/dt = ic$, which holds universally
    in spacetime regardless of the local-matter content).

-   *Both are domains in which a non-zero scalar condensate adds a
    perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate contribution to gauge-boson
    propagation* (the Higgs vev $\langle H\rangle = v/\sqrt{2}$ in empty
    space at the electroweak scale; the Cooper-pair density $|\psi_s|^2$
    in superconductors at the condensed-matter scale).

-   *Both are domains in which the same Klein-Gordon-type wave equation
    [\[eq:UnifiedMassEquation\]](#eq:UnifiedMassEquation){reference-type="eqref"
    reference="eq:UnifiedMassEquation"} governs gauge-boson propagation
    with the condensate-induced effective Compton-frequency winding-rate
    term* (with $W^\pm, Z$ acquiring mass from the Higgs in empty space;
    with the photon acquiring mass from the Cooper-pair condensate in
    superconductors).

*Empty space is a superconductor not just metaphorically but at the
level of underlying physics: both are McGucken-Sphere-wavefront domains
with a non-zero scalar condensate adding a
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate contribution to gauge-boson
propagation.* The framework supplies the deeper identity Wilczek's
metaphor captured but did not articulate.

###### The advance of Theorem [251](#thm:PhotonMassSuperconductor){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:PhotonMassSuperconductor"}. {#the-advance-of-theorem-thmphotonmasssuperconductor.}

The orthodox tradition has recognised the same-mathematical-equations of
the electroweak Higgs mechanism and the Anderson-Higgs superconductor
mechanism since Anderson's 1963 *Phys. Rev.* **130** paper. Anderson
supplied the mathematical equivalence at primary-source grade. Wilczek
2005 supplied the "empty space is a superconductor" metaphor that
captures the parallel. De Bruyn Ouboter and Omelyanchouk 2017 supplied
the empirical identification of the superconducting photon's Compton
wavelength with $2\pi \lambda_L$. *What the orthodox tradition did not
supply --- and what the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework now supplies
at theorem grade --- is the deeper physical reason the same equations
govern both contexts.*

The deeper reason: the same McGucken-Sphere wavefront acts at every
spacetime event in both contexts, with the condensate (Higgs vev or
Cooper-pair density) acting as the switch that adds a
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate component to the gauge boson's
four-velocity. The same Klein-Gordon-type wave equation governs both
because the same wavefront governs both; the condensate scale differs
(electroweak vev $v \approx 246$ GeV vs. Cooper-pair binding energy
$\sim$ meV), but the mechanism
(condensate-supplies-perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate-component) is
identical.

*The orthodox tradition's primary-source recognition of the
same-mathematical-equations is, in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework, the empirical signature of the same-physical-content fact:
$dx_4/dt = ic$ holds at every spacetime event, the McGucken-Sphere
wavefront expands at $c$ from every event, and any condensate that
establishes a non-zero magnitude at a given event adds a
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate contribution to gauge bosons
propagating on that wavefront.* The Anderson-Higgs mechanism in
superconductors and the electroweak Higgs mechanism in particle physics
are two scale-separated instances of the same physical-geometric
mechanism, recognised at theorem grade by the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework.

#### Theorem H12: Gravitational redshift as gravitational slowing of the Compton-$x_4$-clock, and the McGucken Cosmology as empirical confirmation {#ssec:GravitationalComptonClock}

Theorems H10 and H11 established the framework's identification of rest
mass as the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate observed as the Compton
frequency, with the Higgs vev as the $+ic$-direction encoder. The same
identification carries through into curved spacetime and into cosmology,
producing two further empirically-anchored results: *gravitational
redshift is the gravitational slowing of the Compton-$x_4$-clock;
cosmological redshift is the cumulative effect of
cosmologically-evolving spatial geometry on the same Compton clock.* The
McGucken Cosmology paper [@MG-Cosmology] establishes these results as
theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$ and provides the empirical record of twelve
first-place finishes across independent cosmological tests with zero
free dark-sector parameters. We incorporate the results here as Theorem
H12 and document the relationship to the Higgs sector.

##### The photon-clock mechanism (physics of gravitational time dilation) {#the-photon-clock-mechanism-physics-of-gravitational-time-dilation .unnumbered}

A photon clock consists of a photon bouncing between two mirrors a fixed
proper distance $L$ apart in $x_1 x_2 x_3$, with the tick rate set by
the round-trip transit time $2L/c$. In flat space, $L$ equals the
coordinate distance between the mirrors and the tick rate is the
flat-space rate. Near a mass $M$, with the mirrors at coordinate-fixed
positions separated by $dr$ in the radial direction, the proper distance
between the mirrors is stretched relative to the coordinate distance:
$$L_{\mathrm{proper}} = \int \frac{dr}{\sqrt{1 - r_s/r}} > L_{\mathrm{coord}} = \int dr,$$
where $r_s = 2GM/c^2$ is the Schwarzschild radius. The photon,
propagating at the invariant speed $c$ in proper-distance terms (because
$dx_4/dt = ic$ forces null worldlines to satisfy $ds^2 = 0$ in the full
four-dimensional geometry), therefore takes longer to complete a round
trip when measured against coordinate-time at infinity. The wristwatch
at the mass-proximate event ticks slower not because $dx_4/dt = ic$ has
changed (it has not; it is strictly invariant) but because the photon
has more stretched $x_1 x_2 x_3$ to traverse while maintaining its
invariant $ic$ expansion through $x_4$. The principle stays invariant;
the wristwatch responds to the stretched $x_1 x_2 x_3$.

This is the physical mechanism of gravitational time dilation per
[@MG-Cosmology §X.3b.2], supplying the physics that the standard
general-relativistic derivation lacks. The standard derivation accepts
the metric coefficient $N^2(r) = (1 - r_s/r)$ as the source of time
dilation through the proper-time relation
$d\tau = \sqrt{-g_{\mu\nu} dx^\mu dx^\nu / c^2} = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}\,dt$
without further geometry; the McGucken-framework derivation identifies
time dilation as the wristwatch-rate response to the photon traversing
locally-stretched $x_1 x_2 x_3$ while $dx_4/dt = ic$ stays invariant.

##### The Compton-$x_4$-clock identification with the photon clock {#the-compton-x_4-clock-identification-with-the-photon-clock .unnumbered}

A massive fermion at three-rest is itself a Compton clock: by
Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}, the fermion winds perpendicular
through $x_4$ at angular frequency $\omega_C = m_f c^2/\hbar$, with the
wavefunction phase advancing along $x_4$ at this rate. The Higgs vev
establishes the $+ic$ direction in which the winding occurs; the Yukawa
coupling sets the species-specific winding rate. Each oscillation cycle
of the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding is one tick of the fermion's internal
clock; the wristwatch-rate of the fermion at three-rest is its Compton
frequency.

The identification: *the photon clock of the cosmology paper's
gravitational-redshift mechanism and the Compton-$x_4$-clock of the
Higgs paper's rest-mass mechanism are the same clock, viewed at
different time scales.* The photon clock has tick rate $2L/c$ for
round-trip transit between mirrors at proper distance $L$; the Compton
clock has tick rate $\hbar/(m_f c^2)$ for one cycle of
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding at the species-specific rate. Both clocks
are governed by the same invariant: $dx_4/dt = ic$ remains invariant at
every event; the wristwatch-rate response is to the local $x_1 x_2 x_3$
geometry in both cases.

::: {#thm:GravitationalComptonClock .theorem}
**Theorem 254** (Gravitational redshift as gravitational slowing of the
Compton-$x_4$-clock). *Assume the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, the
four-fold ontology,
Theorems [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}, [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}, and the Schwarzschild Theorem of
[@MG-Cosmology Theorem 12]. Let $M$ be a localized mass producing the
standard Schwarzschild-domain metric stretching of $x_1 x_2 x_3$ around
it. Then for any massive fermion species $f$ of rest mass $m_f$ located
at coordinate-fixed radial position $r$ from $M$:*

1.  ***Compton-frequency dilation.** The Compton frequency of the
    fermion, measured against coordinate-time at infinity, is dilated by
    the Schwarzschild factor:
    $$\omega_C^{\mathrm{lab}}(r) = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}\, \omega_C^{\mathrm{proper}} = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}\, \frac{m_f c^2}{\hbar}.$$
    The fermion's perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate, measured at
    infinity, is reduced by $\sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$ because the fermion's
    wristwatch is ticking more slowly (by the same factor) due to the
    locally-stretched $x_1 x_2 x_3$ that the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding
    must traverse.*

2.  ***Gravitational redshift identification.** A photon emitted by the
    fermion via a Compton-frequency transition (e.g., an atomic
    transition whose frequency depends on rest-mass-energy differences
    via $\Delta E = \hbar \omega = \Delta(mc^2)$) is emitted at
    frequency $\omega_C^{\mathrm{lab}}(r)$ as measured at infinity. A
    photon received at infinity from emission at radius $r$ is therefore
    redshifted by the factor $\sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$ relative to a photon
    emitted at infinity with the same proper-frequency emission. The
    gravitational redshift is the frequency-domain shadow of the
    Compton-clock dilation.*

3.  ***Equivalence-principle consistency.** A freely-falling observer at
    radius $r$ accumulates proper time at the rate
    $d\tau_{\mathrm{local}}/dt_{\mathrm{coord}} = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$
    relative to coordinate-time at infinity, by the standard
    Schwarzschild result. The freely-falling fermion's Compton clock
    ticks at the local proper rate
    $\omega_C^{\mathrm{proper}} = m_f c^2/\hbar$; an observer at
    infinity records this clock as ticking at
    $\omega_C^{\mathrm{lab}} = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}\, \omega_C^{\mathrm{proper}}$.
    The Compton-clock dilation is the
    local-observer-vs-infinity-observer comparison of the fermion's
    wristwatch rate.*

4.  ***The mass-energy of the perpendicular-$x_4$-motion is preserved
    under gravitational redshift.** The rest-mass energy
    $E_{\mathrm{rest}} = m_f c^2$ is the energy of the fermion's
    perpendicular-$x_4$-motion at velocity $c$
    (Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}(v)). The infinity-observer
    measures this energy as $E_{\infty} = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}\, m_f c^2$,
    reduced by the gravitational redshift factor. This is the standard
    gravitational-redshift result; in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
    framework, it is the dilation of the perpendicular-$x_4$-motion
    frequency as seen by the infinity-observer.*

5.  ***Photon limit consistency.** A photon emitted at radius $r$ with
    proper frequency $\omega$ is received at infinity with frequency
    $\omega_{\infty} = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}\, \omega$. The photon, having
    $dx_4/dt = 0$ on its null worldline
    (Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}(vi)), is carried by $x_4$'s
    expansion at velocity $c$. The redshift arises because the
    proper-distance traversal of the photon through stretched
    $x_1 x_2 x_3$ takes more coordinate time than in flat space; the
    photon's wavefront-riding rate is fixed at $c$ in proper-distance
    terms but the relation between proper-distance and
    coordinate-distance is modified by the metric stretching.*
:::

::: proof
*Sketch and grade..* Grade 2: each property follows from the
photon-clock theorem of [@MG-Cosmology §X.3b.3] together with the
Compton-$x_4$-clock identification of
Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}. The two clocks are governed by the
same invariant ($dx_4/dt = ic$ stays strictly invariant) and the same
response mechanism (the local $x_1 x_2 x_3$ stretching modulates the
wristwatch rate). Property (i) is the Compton-clock formulation of the
standard gravitational-time-dilation result; properties (ii)--(v) are
direct consequences of Property (i) combined with the standard relations
between Compton frequency, rest mass, and atomic-transition energies.

The novel material of Theorem H12 relative to the standard
gravitational-redshift result: the dilation is identified as the
dilation of the fermion's *perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate* (the
Compton clock), with the Higgs vev as the unchanged direction encoder
(the $+ic$ direction is locally unchanged at every event; what is
modulated is the rate at which the fermion winds through this
direction). The Higgs vev does not change under gravitational
stretching; the Compton-frequency winding rate does. The fermion's
mass-content $m_f c^2$ is the proper-frame energy of
perpendicular-$x_4$-motion; the infinity-observer's measurement of this
energy is gravitationally redshifted by $\sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$. ◻
:::

##### Cosmological redshift extension {#cosmological-redshift-extension .unnumbered}

The Compton-$x_4$-clock identification extends to cosmological scales as
well. Per [@MG-Cosmology §V.2-V.3, §X.3b.4], the cosmological redshift
$z = a_{\mathrm{now}}/a_{\mathrm{emit}} - 1$ arises from the cumulative
stretching of $x_1 x_2 x_3$ between the emission event and the reception
event, with $dx_4/dt = ic$ invariant at both events. A photon emitted at
cosmological time $t_{\mathrm{emit}}$ with proper-frame frequency
$\omega_{\mathrm{emit}}$ is received at the present epoch with frequency
$\omega_{\mathrm{now}} = \omega_{\mathrm{emit}}/(1+z)$, redshifted by
the cumulative $x_1 x_2 x_3$ stretching factor $1+z$ between the two
epochs.

The same applies to fermion Compton clocks: a fermion at the emission
event has Compton frequency $\omega_C^{\mathrm{emit}} = m_f c^2/\hbar$
in its local proper frame; this frequency, viewed from the reception
epoch in our present-day observational frame, is redshifted by $(1+z)$.
The fermion's rest-mass energy, as measured by an observer at the
present cosmological epoch with respect to the cosmologically-evolving
spatial geometry between emission and reception, is reduced by the same
factor.

##### The McGucken Cosmology as empirical confirmation: twelve first-place finishes with zero free dark-sector parameters {#the-mcgucken-cosmology-as-empirical-confirmation-twelve-first-place-finishes-with-zero-free-dark-sector-parameters .unnumbered}

The McGucken Cosmology paper [@MG-Cosmology] establishes that
$dx_4/dt = ic$, with its single principle and *zero free dark-sector
parameters*, takes first place across twelve independent observational
tests in cosmology:

1.  The SPARC baryonic Tully-Fisher relation slope of exactly $4$ across
    $123$ disk galaxies, derived from $x_4$'s SO(3) expansion with zero
    free parameters.

2.  The dark-energy equation of state $w(z = 0) = -0.983$ from
    cumulative spatial contraction $\Omega_m(0)/(6\pi)$ with zero free
    parameters, against the DESI 2024 BAO+CMB+SN combined fit at under
    $1\%$ deviation.

3.  The radial-acceleration relation across $2{,}528$ data points from
    $175$ SPARC galaxies (McGaugh-Lelli-Schombert 2016), with
    $\chi^2/N = 0.46$ versus the McGaugh-Lelli benchmark
    $\chi^2/N = 1.46$ ($50.3\sigma$ improvement with zero free
    parameters).

4.  The $H_0$ tension as cumulative gravitational time dilation along
    the SH0ES distance ladder, identifying the $8.3\%$ Planck-vs-SH0ES
    gap as cumulative $\psi(t)$ contraction since recombination.

5.  The dwarf-galaxy radial-acceleration-relation universality across
    $71$ SPARC dwarfs and $77$ ultra-faint galaxies as principle-level
    geometric necessity.

6.  The Bullet Cluster lensing-versus-gas spatial offset as the
    differential stretching pattern between the dark-matter-like lensing
    trace ($x_4$-derived) and the visible gas ($x_1 x_2 x_3$-derived).

7.  Cosmic birefringence as a theorem of the $+i$ sign of $dx_4/dt = ic$
    (the parity-asymmetric structure of $x_4$'s expansion).

8.  Cosmological flatness ($k = 0$) as a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$
    without inflation, distinguishing local stretching from global
    curvature.

9.  The horizon problem solved without inflation, via the shared $x_4$
    origin at the Big Bang.

10. The CMB preferred frame as the maximum-wristwatch-rate frame,
    derived from the same photon-clock mechanism as
    Theorem [254](#thm:GravitationalComptonClock){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:GravitationalComptonClock"}.

11. The $S_8$ tension and structure formation through Scenario-A local

12. The CMB acoustic peaks and DESI BAO ratios consistent with the

The twelve first-place finishes are accomplished with *zero free
dark-sector parameters*, against competing frameworks with parameter

Cosmology Telescope DR6 final data release confirming
$H_0 = 68.22 \pm 0.36$ km/s/Mpc, the DESI DR2 confirmation at

showing closer-to-present anchors give larger $H_0$, and the Calabrese
et al. 2025 systematic elimination of approximately thirty extended
$\Lambda$CDM models --- jointly confirm the McGucken Cosmology's
prediction that the $H_0$ tension is the signature of $x_4$'s invariant
expansion at $c$ against $x_1 x_2 x_3$ [@MG-Cosmology §V.3].

##### What this establishes: the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework contains the Standard Model AND gravity AND cosmology {#what-this-establishes-the-mcgucken-dx_4dt-ic-framework-contains-the-standard-model-and-gravity-and-cosmology .unnumbered}

The integration of

[@MG-Cosmology] establishes a substantial fact about the framework:
**the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ is the source of (i) the entire

$G_{\mathrm{SM}}= U(1)_Y \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{SU}(3)_c$,
(ii) the Higgs sector as field-theoretic encoding of the $+ic$

catalogued in the McGucken Cosmology paper's twelve first-place

The Higgs sector and the gravitational sector are two readings of the
same principle: on the Higgs side, the Compton-$x_4$-clock is the
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding at the species-specific
Yukawa-coupling-determined rate, observable as rest mass; on the gravity
side, the photon-clock is the wavefront-rider rate of a photon
traversing locally-stretched $x_1 x_2 x_3$, observable as gravitational
time dilation and cosmological redshift. Both are governed by the same
invariant ($dx_4/dt = ic$ stays strictly invariant at every event) and

modulates the rate). The Higgs vev encodes the perpendicular direction;
gravity modulates the rate at which perpendicular-$x_4$-winding occurs
against the local stretched spatial geometry.

::: remark
*Remark 255* (The convergent overdetermination signature). The
framework's convergent overdetermination signature deserves explicit
emphasis. The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ is a single
physical-geometric statement (one principle, no free parameters in its
statement). It is shown across the corpus to derive: the gauge group
$G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ as theorems (Parts I--III of the present paper); the
Higgs sector with eleven labeled theorems (Part IV); the constants $c$
and $\hbar$ as theorems [@MG-Sphere2026]; the Einstein field equations
and the Schwarzschild metric as theorems [@MG-Cosmology §X.3]; the
gravitational-redshift mechanism
(Theorem [254](#thm:GravitationalComptonClock){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:GravitationalComptonClock"}); the
cosmological-observational record (twelve first-place finishes, zero
free dark-sector parameters); the absolute prohibitions of Part V
(No-GUT, No-Proton-Decay, No-Monopole, No-Higgs-Domain-Wall). One
principle, all of physics. The convergent overdetermination signature: a
single principle deriving so many independent empirical and results,
with no free parameters and no observational anomalies, is what we
expect from a correct theory rather than a phenomenological fit.

The framework is therefore not in competition with the Standard Model or
with general relativity; *it contains them as theorems*. The Standard
Model gauge group, the Higgs sector with its $\approx 125$ GeV mass
observed at the LHC, and the gravitational-redshift mechanism observed
in countless terrestrial and astrophysical experiments are all
consequences of $dx_4/dt = ic$. The framework does not add to the
Standard Model or modify gravity; it identifies the underlying principle
from which both descend, with the cosmological record [@MG-Cosmology] as
the empirical confirmation that the same principle handles the
cosmological domain that the Standard Model and general relativity
