#### Empirical comparison and falsifiability

::: {#cor:EmpiricalSignatures .corollary}
**Corollary 308** (Empirical signatures). *The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework's prediction $\tau_p = \infty$ is empirically distinguishable
from grand-unified theories:*

-   *Minimal $\mathrm{SU}(5)$ predicts $\tau_p \sim 10^{31}$ years;
    excluded by current experiments.*

-   *Flipped $\mathrm{SU}(5)$ predicts $\tau_p \sim 10^{34}$--$10^{35}$
    years; tested by current experiments at
    $\tau_p > 2.4 \times 10^{34}$ years [@SuperK2020]; the next
    generation of experiments (Hyper-Kamiokande, DUNE) will probe up to
    $\tau_p \sim 10^{35}$--$10^{36}$ years.*

-   *$\mathrm{SO}(10)$ predicts $\tau_p \sim 10^{34}$--$10^{36}$ years;
    testable in the next generation.*

-   *McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework predicts $\tau_p = \infty$;
    consistent with all current experiments and distinguishable from
    GUTs in long-duration future experiments.*

*The falsification criterion: a single observation of a proton-decay
event with the kinematic signature of GUT-mediated decay (e.g.,
$p \to e^+ \pi^0$ with the specific energy distribution predicted by GUT
models) would falsify the No-GUT Theorem and therefore the McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's gauge-group derivation.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The current experimental landscape: Super-Kamiokande has set
lower bounds $\tau_p/B(p \to e^+ \pi^0) > 2.4 \times 10^{34}$ years
[@SuperK2020]. This excludes minimal $\mathrm{SU}(5)$ (whose prediction
$\tau_p \sim 10^{31}$ years is already three orders of magnitude below
the experimental bound) and is reaching the predictions of flipped
$\mathrm{SU}(5)$ and small-$M_X$ $\mathrm{SO}(10)$ scenarios.

The next-generation experiments: Hyper-Kamiokande (under construction in
Japan) will have a fiducial mass approximately ten times that of
Super-K, with corresponding sensitivity reaching $\tau_p \sim 10^{35}$
years over its expected operational lifetime [@HyperK2018]. DUNE (under
construction in the US) will test similar mass-scales with different
decay-channel sensitivities. Both experiments will probe the predictions
of more elaborate GUT scenarios.

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's prediction $\tau_p = \infty$ is
consistent with the current bound and remains consistent with any future
bound short of an actual proton-decay observation. A single observed
proton-decay event would falsify the prediction. ◻
:::

#### The four-fold reinforcement of the no-decay, no-monopole, and no-defect predictions {#ssec:ThreeFoldReinforcement}

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's cornerstone empirical
predictions --- $\tau_p = \infty$ (absolute proton stability),
$g_{\mathrm{mag}} = 0$ (absolute absence of magnetic monopoles), and the
absolute absence of Higgs domain walls, vortices, textures, and
magnitude variations --- are not merely consequences of a single
argument; the framework's predictions are reinforced by *four*
independent arguments, all rooted in $dx_4/dt = ic$ via different
routes. We collect the four-fold structure here for synthesis.

::: {#thm:ThreeFoldReinforcement .theorem}
**Theorem 309** (Four-fold reinforcement). *The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework's predictions of absolute proton stability $\tau_p = \infty$,
absolute monopole absence $g_{\mathrm{mag}} = 0$, and absolute
Higgs-topological-defect absence are each established by independent
arguments, all descending from $dx_4/dt = ic$:*

1.  **Top-down (no-GUT-from-no-fourth-summand):* By
    Theorem [303](#thm:NoGUT){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:NoGUT"}, the internal algebra
    $\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$
    is maximal: no fourth summand is available within the McGucken
    $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's substrate-scale features. Therefore no
    GUT-embedding gauge group exists; therefore no GUT-mediated
    proton-decay channel; therefore no GUT-induced monopoles from
    spontaneous symmetry breaking via the 't Hooft-Polyakov mechanism
    [@tHooft1974; @Polyakov1974].*

2.  **Bottom-up (no-$x_4$-orientation-flip-operator):* By
    Theorem [306](#thm:NoProtonDecaySQ){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:NoProtonDecaySQ"} of
    Section [3.3](#sec:NoProtonDecay-Reinforced){reference-type="ref"
    reference="sec:NoProtonDecay-Reinforced"}, no operator in the
    McGucken-derived second-quantised gauge theory flips the net
    $x_4$-orientation count $\hat Q_{x_4}$. Baryon number, being
    identified with the net forward-$x_4$-orientation count of quarks
    via Theorem [305](#thm:BaryonAsQ4){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:BaryonAsQ4"}, is exactly conserved in the
    perturbative gauge theory. Therefore no perturbative decay channel
    exists for $p \to e^+ \pi^0$ or any other $B$-violating process.*

3.  **Bundle-topological (no-nontrivial-$U(1)$-bundle):* By
    Theorem [135](#thm:NoMonopole){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:NoMonopole"} of
    Section [8](#sec:QED-PartI){reference-type="ref"
    reference="sec:QED-PartI"}, the $x_4$-orientation $U(1)$-bundle of
    Definition [125](#def:X4Bundle){reference-type="ref"
    reference="def:X4Bundle"} is topologically trivial: $dx_4/dt = +ic$
    provides a global section, and any principal $U(1)$-bundle admitting
    a global section is trivial [@Steenrod1951 Theorem 11.6]. Therefore
    $c_1(P) = 0$ and no magnetic-monopole field configuration exists.
    This rules out monopoles absolutely (not high-scale-suppressed) and
    rules out the Wu-Yang-Dirac-quantisation route to charge
    quantisation [@Dirac1931; @WuYang1975]; charge quantisation holds
    independently in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework via the
    discrete $x_4$-orientation-counting argument of
    [@MG-SecondQuantization2026 §X.5] and
    Corollary [136](#cor:ChargeQuantNoMono){reference-type="ref"
    reference="cor:ChargeQuantNoMono"}.*

4.  **Vacuum-uniformity (no-disconnected-vacuum-component):* By
    Theorem [228](#thm:NoDomainWall){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:NoDomainWall"} of
    Section [5](#sec:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
    reference="sec:HiggsPointer"}, the electroweak vacuum manifold
    consists of a single $G_{\mathrm{EW}}$-orbit: the global uniformity
    of $+ic$ admits, up to gauge equivalence, only one Higgs
    configuration at each spacetime point (the one aligned with the
    global $+ic$). Therefore the vacuum manifold has a single connected
    component, regardless of how many Higgs multiplets are added; Higgs
    domain walls (which require multiple disconnected components) are
    absolutely forbidden. The same uniformity argument forbids magnitude
    variations, vortices, and textures, the latter two being also
    forbidden in the Standard Model with a single doublet but the
    domain-wall prohibition being McGucken-specific.*

*The four arguments are independent: argument (1) is at the level of the
internal algebra $\mathcal{A}_F$; argument (2) is at the level of the
second-quantised operator algebra; argument (3) is at the level of the
$x_4$-orientation $U(1)$-bundle topology; argument (4) is at the level
of the electroweak vacuum manifold's connected-component structure. All
four converge on absolute empirical predictions:*

-   *No proton decay: $\tau_p = \infty$.*

-   *No magnetic monopoles: $g_{\mathrm{mag}} = 0$.*

-   *No fractional electric charge: $Q \in \tfrac{1}{3} \mathbb{Z}$
    exactly (from $x_4$-orientation discreteness).*

-   *No Higgs domain walls, vortices, textures, or persistent magnitude
    variations (from vacuum-uniformity).*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Each of the four arguments is established in its corresponding
theorem: argument (1) in Theorem [303](#thm:NoGUT){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:NoGUT"}; argument (2) in
Theorem [306](#thm:NoProtonDecaySQ){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:NoProtonDecaySQ"}; argument (3) in
Theorem [135](#thm:NoMonopole){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:NoMonopole"}; argument (4) in
Theorem [228](#thm:NoDomainWall){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:NoDomainWall"}. The independence of the four arguments is
verified by inspection: (1) uses the exhaustion property of
$\mathcal{A}_F$; (2) uses the operator-algebra conservation of
$\hat Q_{x_4}$; (3) uses the bundle-triviality theorem from the global
section provided by $dx_4/dt = +ic$; (4) uses the
single-connected-component property of the vacuum manifold from global
uniformity. The four converging predictions follow as corollaries of the
four theorems separately, and the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's
overall position is reinforced by the convergence: any falsification of
one of the predictions (a single proton-decay event, a single magnetic
monopole, a single fractional-charge particle, a single observed Higgs
domain wall) would simultaneously falsify the relevant arguments via the
same root cause --- the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$. ◻
:::

::: {#rem:ThreeFoldEmpirical .remark}
*Remark 310* (The empirics of the four-fold reinforcement). The
four-fold reinforcement gives the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework a
uniquely sharp empirical position:

-   In GUT scenarios (Georgi-Glashow $\mathrm{SU}(5)$,
    $\mathrm{SO}(10)$, $E_6$, etc.), monopoles and proton decay are
    predicted but at high suppression scales; non-observation is
    consistent with the predictions because of high-scale dilution.

-   In string-theoretic scenarios, monopoles can arise from compactified
    extra dimensions with nontrivial topology, with prediction scales
    depending on compactification details.

-   In the Standard Model alone (no GUT, no string-theoretic extension),
    baryon-and-lepton-number conservation is "accidental" --- a
    consequence of the gauge-invariant operator content at the
    renormalisable level, but with no deeper reason. Multi-Higgs SM
    extensions permit domain walls under appropriate cosmological
    conditions.

-   In supersymmetric models with two Higgs doublets, domain walls are
    permitted in some parameter regions. Composite Higgs models with
    multiple pseudo-Goldstone scalars also permit walls.

-   In the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, by contrast,
    $\tau_p = \infty$, $g_{\mathrm{mag}} = 0$,
    $Q \in \tfrac{1}{3}\mathbb{Z}$, and Higgs domain walls absent, are
    *absolute* predictions: each is derived from $dx_4/dt = ic$ via
    independent arguments, and any positive observation would refute the
    principle directly.

This sharpness --- four absolute predictions with multiple independent
arguments converging on each --- distinguishes the McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework from all other approaches to fundamental
physics. It is what makes the framework empirically falsifiable in a
strong sense: a single observation of any of the four forbidden
phenomena would falsify $dx_4/dt = ic$ directly, not merely some
auxiliary assumption.
:::

# Part VI: The Comparative Landscape --- Prior Attempts to Derive the Standard Model Gauge Group {#part-vi-the-comparative-landscape-prior-attempts-to-derive-the-standard-model-gauge-group .unnumbered}

### Introduction: the half-century of attempts

The attempt to derive the Standard Model gauge group
$G_{\mathrm{SM}}= U(1)_Y \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{SU}(3)_c$
from a deeper principle is one of the longest-running programs in
theoretical physics. The question *why this gauge group and not
another?* has been pursued continuously since 1974, when Georgi and
Glashow proposed the first Grand Unified Theory [@GeorgiGlashow1974]
embedding $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ in $\mathrm{SU}(5)$. In the half-century
since, six major lines of attack have emerged, each producing serious
accomplishments and serious unresolved problems. The McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's gauge-group derivation, established in Parts
I--V of the present unified treatment, sits among them as the newest and
arguably most primitively compact.

The purpose of the present Part VI is to situate the McGucken derivation
within the comparative landscape of prior attempts, with three goals:

1.  to identify the similarities and differences between the McGucken
    approach and the prior programs;

2.  to assess the empirical and theoretical status of each prior program
    in 2026;

3.  to clarify where the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's
    contribution is genuinely novel, where it overlaps with prior work
    (especially the Connes-Chamseddine spectral action), and where it
    remains programmatic in ways that the prior programs have or have
    not addressed.

The methodological standard adopted in this Part is the same as in Parts
I--V: every claim about a prior program is sourced to its primary
literature; every empirical bound is sourced to current experimental
publications; acknowledgment of unresolved issues, whether in the prior
programs or in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, is provided
wherever such acknowledgment is warranted.

#### The six major programs

The six major lines of attack on the gauge-group-derivation problem are:

1.  **The Grand Unified Theory program** (GUTs:
    $\mathrm{SU}(5), \mathrm{SO}(10), E_6, E_8$, etc.; 1974--present).
    Embed $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ in a larger Lie group that breaks at high
    energy.

2.  **The Connes-Chamseddine noncommutative geometry program** (NCG;
    1991--present). Derive the Standard Model action from the spectral
    action principle on an almost-commutative spectral triple, with the
    gauge group emerging as the inner-automorphism group of an internal
    algebra $\mathcal{A}_F$.

3.  **The string theory program** (1984--present). Compactify a
    10-dimensional string theory; the resulting low-energy 4D physics
    should include the Standard Model with gauge group as a feature of
    the compactification geometry.

4.  **The Pati-Salam program** (1974--present). Embed $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$
    in $\mathrm{SU}(4) \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_R$,
    treating lepton number as a fourth "color".

5.  **Algebraic / division-algebra approaches** (Dixon, Furey,
    Boyle-Farnsworth; 1990--present). Derive $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ from
    purely algebraic structures --- the real, complex, quaternionic, and
    octonionic division algebras, and their tensor products.

6.  **The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework** (2024--2026; the present
    unified treatment). Derive $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ as a chain of theorems
    descending from the single primitive physical-geometric law
    $dx_4/dt = ic$, with each gauge factor traceable to a specific
    feature of the substrate-scale McGucken-Sphere geometry.

The remainder of this Part discusses each program in turn
(Sections [7](#sec:GUTs){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:GUTs"}--[12](#sec:McGuckenComparative){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:McGuckenComparative"}), provides three master comparison
tables for the gauge-group-derivation problem
(Section [13](#sec:MasterTables){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:MasterTables"}), then expands the comparative landscape
with two further sections specifically targeting the McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's advance:
Section [14](#sec:HiggsComparative){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:HiggsComparative"} addresses the Higgs sector with a full
framework-by-framework analysis (Anderson, HEB/GHK, Weinberg-Salam,
Technicolor, SUSY, Composite Higgs, Connes NCG, Gauge-Higgs Unification,
Woit ETU) and Master Table D on the coverage of the eight Higgs
readings, and
Section [15](#sec:UnifiedMoreFromLess){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:UnifiedMoreFromLess"} provides Master Table E --- the
unified "more from less" comparison across all major physical structures
(spacetime, QM, Dirac, second quantization, the full gauge group, the
Higgs sector, gravity, thermodynamics, and four absolute empirical
predictions) demonstrating that the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework
derives more from a more compact postulate set than any prior framework.
The Part concludes with an assessment of where the McGucken contribution
stands relative to the half-century of prior work
(Section [22](#sec:ClosingAssessment){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:ClosingAssessment"}).

### The Grand Unified Theory program (1974--present) {#sec:GUTs}

#### Strategy and historical achievements

The GUT program, initiated by Georgi and Glashow with $\mathrm{SU}(5)$
in 1974 [@GeorgiGlashow1974], takes the following strategic position:
the Standard Model gauge group $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ is a remnant of a
larger gauge symmetry that exists at high energy and breaks down to
$G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ via the Higgs mechanism (or generalizations thereof)
at intermediate scales. The "naturalness" of GUTs comes from the
observation that the three Standard Model gauge couplings, when run via
renormalization-group equations to high energy, approximately meet at a
common scale near $10^{16}$ GeV --- suggesting that they were unified
there.

The principal GUT scenarios are:

-   **$\mathrm{SU}(5)$ (Georgi-Glashow, 1974)** [@GeorgiGlashow1974]:
    the smallest simple Lie group containing $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$. The
    single $\mathbf{24}$ representation contains all twelve gauge
    bosons; the $\bar{\mathbf{5}} \oplus \mathbf{10}$ contains a single
    fermion family; the symmetry breaks at
    $M_{\mathrm{GUT}} \sim 10^{15-16}$ GeV via the Higgs in the
    $\mathbf{24}$ (or $\mathbf{75}$) representation.

-   **$\mathrm{SO}(10)$ (Fritzsch-Minkowski, Georgi 1975)**
    [@FritzschMinkowski1975]: the spinor representation $\mathbf{16}$
    contains a complete fermion family including a right-handed
    neutrino, accommodating the empirical neutrino masses via the seesaw
    mechanism. Larger structure than $\mathrm{SU}(5)$ but more "natural"
    inclusion of neutrino sector.

-   **$E_6$ (Gürsey-Ramond-Sikivie 1976)** [@GurseyRamondSikivie1976]:
    the $\mathbf{27}$ representation contains a fermion family with
    additional exotic states. Connects naturally to heterotic string
    theory's $E_8 \times E_8$.

-   **Flipped $\mathrm{SU}(5)$ and $E_8$**: variant structures with
    modified embeddings or larger groups.

-   **Supersymmetric versions (MSSM-GUTs, 1980s--present)**: extend each
    of the above with supersymmetry to address the hierarchy problem and
    improve gauge-coupling unification.

#### The proton-decay prediction

The principal empirical prediction of GUTs is the existence of $X$ and
$Y$ gauge bosons (in $\mathrm{SU}(5)$ language; analogous structures in
larger groups) that connect quarks to leptons, mediating processes like
$u + d \to e^+ + \bar\nu_e$ at the constituent level. These processes
lead to proton decay channels such as $p \to e^+ + \pi^0$,
$p \to \mu^+ + \pi^0$, $p \to \bar\nu + K^+$, and others.

The proton lifetime in standard GUT scenarios is approximately:
$$\label{eq:GUTprotonlifetime}
\tau_p^{\mathrm{GUT}} \sim \frac{M_X^4}{m_p^5 \alpha_{\mathrm{GUT}}^2},$$
with $M_X$ the GUT-scale gauge boson mass, $m_p$ the proton mass, and
$\alpha_{\mathrm{GUT}}$ the unified coupling. For different GUT
scenarios this gives:

-   Minimal non-supersymmetric $\mathrm{SU}(5)$:
    $\tau_p \sim 10^{29-31}$ years. Excluded by experiment.

-   Minimal supersymmetric $\mathrm{SU}(5)$: $\tau_p \sim 10^{32-34}$
    years (dominant channel $p \to \bar\nu K^+$). Currently in
    significant tension with experimental bounds.

-   $\mathrm{SO}(10)$ scenarios: $\tau_p \sim 10^{34-36}$ years
    (model-dependent). Within reach of next-generation experiments.

-   Flipped $\mathrm{SU}(5)$: $\tau_p \sim 10^{34-35}$ years. Within
    reach of next-generation experiments.

The current Super-Kamiokande experimental lower bounds are:

-   $\tau_p / B(p \to e^+ \pi^0) > 2.4 \times 10^{34}$ years (90% CL)
    [@SuperK2020].

-   $\tau_p / B(p \to K^+ \bar\nu) > 6.61 \times 10^{33}$ years (90% CL)
    [@PDG2025].

These bounds have ruled out non-supersymmetric minimal $\mathrm{SU}(5)$
definitively and place minimal SUSY $\mathrm{SU}(5)$ under significant
tension; $\mathrm{SO}(10)$ and flipped $\mathrm{SU}(5)$ remain viable
but increasingly constrained.

#### Status assessment

The GUT program has produced extensive theoretical machinery but is in
serious empirical trouble after fifty years. Beyond the proton-decay
constraints:

-   **Magnetic monopole non-observation**: GUTs predict topological
    magnetic monopoles at the GUT scale; the MoEDAL detector at the LHC
    has not observed them [@MoEDAL2017], though this is a less stringent
    constraint.

-   **Doublet-triplet splitting problem**: in $\mathrm{SU}(5)$ and most
    other GUTs, the Higgs scalar appears in a
    $\mathbf{5}$-representation with both the electroweak doublet
    (light) and a colored triplet (which must be GUT-scale heavy). The
    fine-tuning required to split these masses by 14 orders of magnitude
    is considered one of the deepest problems in GUT model-building.

-   **Supersymmetry non-observation**: SUSY-GUTs require superpartners
    at TeV scale; LHC searches have placed lower bounds on squark and
    gluino masses around 1.5--2 TeV, putting standard SUSY scenarios
    under increasing pressure.

-   **Gauge coupling unification mismatch**: in non-SUSY models, the
    three Standard Model gauge couplings do not actually meet at a
    single scale; SUSY improves the unification but is itself
    empirically constrained.

#### The deeper problem

The deepest critique of the GUT program from a standpoint is that GUTs
do not actually derive the gauge group from a deeper principle. They
postulate a different (larger) gauge group as primitive and then break
it. The "why this group?" question is pushed up one level rather than
answered: instead of asking "why
$\mathrm{SU}(3) \times \mathrm{SU}(2) \times U(1)$?", the GUT program
asks us to accept "why $\mathrm{SU}(5)$?" or "why $\mathrm{SO}(10)$?" or
"why $E_6$?" --- with no compelling principle selecting among these
candidates. After fifty years of work, no GUT has uniquely emerged as
the correct extension, and the empirical evidence (proton stability) is
increasingly hostile to the program's central prediction.

### The Connes-Chamseddine noncommutative geometry program (1991--present) {#sec:NCG}

#### Strategy and historical achievements

The noncommutative geometry approach to the Standard Model, initiated by
Connes and Lott (1990) [@ConnesLott1990] and developed by Chamseddine
and Connes (1996, 1997) [@ChamseddineConnes1996; @ChamseddineConnes1997]
into the spectral action principle, takes a different approach from
GUTs. Rather than embedding $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ in a larger gauge group,
the NCG program represents spacetime as a noncommutative geometric
structure --- a "spectral triple" $(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{H}, D)$
consisting of an algebra $\mathcal{A}$, a Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ of
spinor sections, and a Dirac operator $D$. The Standard Model emerges as
the spectral action evaluated on an "almost-commutative" spectral triple
$$\label{eq:AlmostCommSpecTriple}
(\mathcal{A}\otimes \mathcal{A}_F, \mathcal{H}\otimes \mathcal{H}_F, D \otimes 1 + 1 \otimes D_F),$$
where $(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{H}, D)$ encodes commutative
four-dimensional spacetime and $(\mathcal{A}_F, \mathcal{H}_F, D_F)$
encodes a finite-dimensional internal noncommutative geometry.

The principal achievements of the NCG program:

-   **Spectral action principle** [@ChamseddineConnes1997]: the action
    functional
    $$S[D] = \mathrm{Tr}f(D/\Lambda) + \langle \psi | D | \psi \rangle,$$
    with $f$ a positive even function and $\Lambda$ a cutoff scale,
    evaluated on the almost-commutative spectral triple, reproduces the
    bosonic and fermionic action of the Standard Model coupled to
    Einstein-Weyl gravity to leading order.

-   **Internal algebra identification**: Chamseddine, Connes, and
    Marcolli [@ConnesChamseddine2007] showed that taking
    $$\label{eq:AFNCG}
    \mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C}),$$
    together with appropriate bimodule structure, produces
    $G_{\mathrm{SM}}= U(1) \times \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathrm{SU}(3)$
    via the inner-automorphism construction. This is the same algebraic
    structure that the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework derives from
    substrate-scale McGucken-Sphere packing in \[MG-GaugeGroups Part
    II\].

-   **Gauge coupling relations**: the spectral action predicts relations
    between the three gauge coupling constants that, at the unification
    scale, give $\sin^2\theta_W = 3/8$. This matches the
    Connes-Chamseddine framework's identification of the unification
    scale with a high-energy "cutoff" $\Lambda$ comparable to the GUT
    scale.

-   **Higgs mass prediction**: the spectral action principle uniquely
    predicts the Higgs self-coupling at unification scale, leading to a
    Higgs mass prediction that, after RG running, comes within a factor
    of order unity of the observed 125 GeV.

-   **Quanta of geometry**
    [@ChamseddineConnesMukhanov2014; @ChamseddineConnesMukhanov2015]:
    the Chamseddine-Connes-Mukhanov "quanta of geometry" theorem
    proposes a higher Heisenberg commutation relation
    $\langle Y [D, Y]^4 \rangle = \gamma$ that decomposes any spectral
    triple of metric dimension four into Planck-volume four-spheres.
    This is the structure that the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's
    \[MG-GaugeGroups Part II\] identifies with substrate-scale McGucken
    Spheres.

#### Open problems and empirical tensions

Despite these achievements, the Connes-Chamseddine NCG program has
serious unresolved issues:

-   **Why $\mathcal{A}_F$?** The internal algebra
    $\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$
    is itself postulated in the standard Connes-Chamseddine treatment,
    with its specific three-summand form fixed by phenomenological match
    to the Standard Model fermion content and gauge group. There is no
    derivation of $\mathcal{A}_F$ from a deeper physical principle in
    the prior NCG literature. This is precisely the gap that the
    McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's \[MG-GaugeGroups Part II\]
    addresses: $\mathcal{A}_F$ descends from substrate-scale
    McGucken-Sphere packing as a theorem.

-   **Doublet-triplet problem analog**: Besnard's analysis
    [@Besnard2020] showed that the $B$-$L$ extended spectral Standard
    Model suffers from a mass-splitting problem similar to the
    doublet-triplet problem of GUTs, with constraints on quartic
    coupling constants that are incompatible with the observed top-quark
    and Higgs-boson masses. This is an empirical tension that the NCG
    program has not resolved.

-   **Fermion doubling**: the original Connes-Chamseddine model
    (pre-2007) suffered from a "fermion doubling" issue where each
    physical fermion was effectively counted multiple times in the
    Hilbert space. Subsequent work by Connes-Chamseddine-Marcolli and
    Bochniak-Sitarz has addressed this but the resolutions remain
    technically delicate.

-   **Lorentzian signature**: most NCG analyses are carried out in
    Euclidean signature, with Wick rotation to Lorentzian signature
    treated as an analytic prescription. The Lorentzian Standard Model
    has been investigated by Besnard-Brouder [@BesnardBrouder2020] but
    the program's natural home remains Euclidean.

-   **Three generations**: the NCG framework accommodates the three
    matter generations as a $3\times$ multiplicity in the Hilbert space,
    but does not derive the number three from the spectral structure.

-   **KO-dimension 6 vs. 0**: [@nLabCLCB] the Connes-Chamseddine
    spectral triple has KO-dimension 6 (mod 8) for the internal space
    rather than 0, which is a non-trivial feature whose physical
    interpretation remains debated.

#### Status assessment

The NCG program is the closest in spirit to the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework's gauge-group derivation among the prior programs. Its
principal achievement is the identification of the Standard Model gauge
group with the inner-automorphism group of
$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$; its
principal limitation is that $\mathcal{A}_F$ itself is postulated rather
than derived from a deeper principle.

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's contribution relative to the NCG
program is to fill the gap that NCG leaves open: the substrate-scale
geometric origin of $\mathcal{A}_F$. \[MG-GaugeGroups Part II\]
formalizes Theorem H of [@MG-Connes] as the substrate-scale
identification of McGucken Spheres with Chamseddine-Connes-Mukhanov
"quanta of geometry," from which the three sectors $\mathbb{C}$ (from
$x_4$-phase), $\mathbb{H}$ (from $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ Weyl-doublet
structure), and $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ (from spatial three-direction
non-commutation) are derived. This makes the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework a strict extension of the Connes-Chamseddine program: every
result of the NCG analysis is preserved, with the additional material
that $\mathcal{A}_F$ is now a theorem rather than a postulate.

The correspondence extends to the spectral action. Theorem F of
[@MG-Connes] establishes that the heat-kernel asymptotic expansion of
$\mathrm{Tr}f(D/\Lambda)$ at the McGucken-substrate cutoff
$\Lambda = M_P c^2/\hbar$ produces, in its Seeley-DeWitt coefficients
$a_0, a_2, a_4$, terms in correspondence with the four sectors of the
McGucken Lagrangian
$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{McG}} = \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{kin}} + \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Dirac}} + \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{YM}} + \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{EH}}$
established in [@MG-Lagrangian]: cosmological constant
$\leftrightarrow a_0$, Einstein-Hilbert $\leftrightarrow a_2$,
Yang-Mills + Higgs potential $\leftrightarrow a_4$. The Connes-van
Suijlekom operator-system extension handling spectral truncation at the
McGucken-substrate cutoff $\Lambda_M$ is the natural
noncommutative-geometric realization of substrate-resolved geometry: the
McGucken-framework's substrate-scale cutoff at the Planck-scale
McGucken-Sphere is what Connes-van Suijlekom encode algebraically
through spectral truncation. The two frameworks --- the
McGucken-framework's $dx_4/dt = ic$ generating substrate-scale McGucken
Spheres at scale $\ell_P$, and Connes' noncommutative-geometry framework
with spectral truncation at $\Lambda_M$ --- are not competing accounts;
they are complementary descriptions of the same substrate-scale physical
structure, with the McGucken-side supplying the dynamical-geometric
mechanism ($x_4$'s perpendicular expansion at $c$) and the Connes-side
supplying the formal noncommutative-geometric expression.

### The string theory program (1984--present) {#sec:String}

#### Strategy and historical achievements

The string theory program, beginning with the Green-Schwarz anomaly
cancellation in Type I string theory [@GreenSchwarz1984] and the
Gross-Harvey-Martinec-Rohm heterotic string construction [@Gross1985],
takes the strategic position that all of physics --- gauge interactions,
gravity, matter --- emerges from the dynamics of one-dimensional
extended objects (strings) propagating in a higher-dimensional
spacetime. The Standard Model gauge group $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ is then
expected to emerge from the compactification geometry of the unobserved
spatial dimensions.

The principal scenarios:

-   **Heterotic $E_8 \times E_8$** [@Gross1985]: the most studied case.
    The 10-dimensional theory has gauge group $E_8 \times E_8$, and
    compactification on a Calabi-Yau threefold (or orbifold) breaks one
    $E_8$ to an observable gauge group containing $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$,
    with the second $E_8$ becoming a "hidden sector."

-   **Heterotic $\mathrm{SO}(32)$**: similar but with a different
    starting gauge group; less commonly studied for Standard Model
    phenomenology.

-   **Type IIA/IIB with D-branes**: gauge fields live on D-brane
    worldvolumes; the Standard Model arises from configurations of
    intersecting branes with appropriate gauge symmetries.

-   **F-theory**: 12-dimensional formulation with $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$
    arising from singular fibers of an elliptic fibration over a
    4-dimensional base.

The string theory program has produced enormous theoretical machinery
and is responsible for genuine breakthroughs in mathematics (mirror
symmetry, the AdS/CFT correspondence [@Maldacena1997], exact
computations of black-hole entropy) as well as in the conceptual
structure of quantum gravity. Its achievements relative to gauge-group
derivation include:

-   **Consistent quantum gravity**: string theory provides a
    perturbatively-consistent formulation of quantum gravity, with gauge
    interactions emerging automatically from the worldsheet formulation
    rather than being added in by hand.

-   **Anomaly cancellation**: the requirement that the 10-dimensional
    theory be free of gauge, gravitational, and mixed anomalies forces
    specific gauge groups ($E_8 \times E_8$ or $\mathrm{SO}(32)$) and
    constrains the matter content.

-   **Models containing $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$**: explicit compactification
    examples (Calabi-Yau, orbifold, free-fermionic) that produce the
    Standard Model gauge group with three generations have been
    constructed; thousands of such "string Standard Model" candidates
    exist in the literature.

#### The landscape problem

The principal problem with the string theory program for gauge-group
derivation is the so-called "landscape" of string vacua. Different
compactification choices lead to different 4-dimensional effective
theories, with different gauge groups, different matter content,
different couplings, and different cosmological constants. Estimates of
the size of the string landscape vary from $10^{500}$ to higher
[@Susskind2003], with no known mechanism that uniquely selects the
vacuum corresponding to our observed universe.

This is a vast space of possibilities, of which the Standard Model gauge
group is one option. The critique [@Smolin2006; @Woit2006] is that
string theory has not made unique falsifiable predictions about
$G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ specifically because the landscape allows so much
variation that no specific gauge group is forced.

#### Open problems

Beyond the landscape problem, the string theory program faces several
specific challenges for gauge-group derivation:

-   **Selection mechanism**: there is no principle within string theory
    that uniquely selects the Standard Model gauge group out of the
    landscape. Anthropic arguments (the universe must be hospitable to
    observers) do not uniquely select $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$.

-   **Compactification stability**: producing a stable compactification
    at TeV scale that reproduces $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ requires fine-tuning
    of moduli stabilization, with the KKLT mechanism [@KKLT2003] being
    the most-studied example but itself being subject to ongoing
    controversy.

-   **Supersymmetry**: most string-theoretic Standard Models require
    low-scale supersymmetry, which has not been observed at the LHC up
    to current bounds.

-   **Three generations**: the number of fermion generations corresponds
    to the Hodge number of the compactification manifold. Manifolds with
    the right Hodge number exist but no unique selection principle picks
    them out.

-   **Predictivity**: the program has not yet produced unique
    predictions for gauge couplings, Yukawa matrices, or proton lifetime
    that are sharper than those of GUT models.

#### Status assessment

After forty years and substantial intellectual investment, the string
theory program has produced extensive mathematical machinery and several
genuine breakthroughs (AdS/CFT, mirror symmetry, microscopic black-hole
entropy) but has not produced a unique derivation of the Standard Model
gauge group. The landscape problem replaces "what is the gauge group?"
with "which of $10^{500}$ vacua corresponds to our universe?" --- a
question on which no progress has been made.

The program's status relative to gauge-group derivation is therefore:
exploratory and inconclusive. String theory may eventually identify a
unique vacuum that produces $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$, but at present no such
identification exists, and the program does not make sharp falsifiable
predictions about gauge structure that distinguish it from alternatives.

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's contribution relative to the
string theory program is that it predicts $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ uniquely (as
an exhaustion of substrate-scale McGucken-Sphere features) rather than
as one option among $10^{500}$. The compactification of unobserved
dimensions, the selection of Calabi-Yau topology, the stabilization of
moduli --- none of these enter the McGucken derivation, which works
directly with the four-dimensional structure of $\mathcal{M}^{1,3}$ and
the substrate-scale features of $dx_4/dt = ic$.

### The Pati-Salam program (1974--present) {#sec:PatiSalam}

#### Strategy and historical achievements

The Pati-Salam program, proposed by Pati and Salam in 1974
[@PatiSalam1974] contemporaneously with Georgi-Glashow $\mathrm{SU}(5)$,
takes a different unification strategy: rather than embedding
$G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ in a single simple Lie group, the Pati-Salam scheme
embeds $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ in $$\label{eq:PatiSalamGroup}
G_{PS} = \mathrm{SU}(4)_C \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_R,$$
where $\mathrm{SU}(4)_C$ extends the colour $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ by
treating lepton number as a "fourth color." Specifically, the
$\mathrm{SU}(4)$ acts on the four-dimensional representation
$$(r, g, b, \ell)$$ where $r, g, b$ are the three quark colours and
$\ell$ is the lepton index. The right-handed $\mathrm{SU}(2)_R$ provides
parity restoration at high energy, with the empirical left-handedness of
the weak interaction emerging via a left-right-symmetry-breaking
mechanism at intermediate scales.

The principal achievements of the Pati-Salam program:

-   **Lepton-number unification**: lepton number is treated on the same
    footing as colour, providing a partial explanation for the observed
    quark-lepton symmetry.

-   **Right-handed neutrinos**: the program naturally accommodates
    right-handed neutrinos, which are required for neutrino masses via
    the seesaw mechanism. This is more elegant than $\mathrm{SU}(5)$,
    which requires ad-hoc additions.

-   **Parity restoration**: the parity violation of the weak interaction
    is treated as a low-energy effect, with parity restored at high
    energy.

-   **Embedding in larger structures**: $G_{PS}$ embeds naturally in
    $\mathrm{SO}(10)$, providing a connection to the larger GUT
    scenarios.

#### Predictions and constraints

The Pati-Salam scheme makes several distinctive predictions:

-   **Right-handed gauge bosons $W^\pm_R, Z_R$**: at the left-right
    symmetry-breaking scale (typically $\sim 10^3$--$10^{16}$ GeV
    depending on the model). LHC searches have constrained
    $M_{W_R} \gtrsim 5$ TeV in most scenarios [@ATLAS2024].

-   **Leptoquark gauge bosons**: arising from the $\mathrm{SU}(4)$ that
    connects quarks to leptons. These mediate processes like
    $\mu \to e \gamma$ and $K^0 \to \mu e$ at suppressed rates.

-   **Proton decay**: present in most Pati-Salam scenarios but typically
    suppressed compared to $\mathrm{SU}(5)$, with predicted lifetimes
    $\tau_p \sim 10^{34-37}$ years in canonical models.

-   **Neutrino masses**: accommodated; the seesaw mechanism naturally
    produces small left-handed neutrino masses.

#### Status assessment

The Pati-Salam program is less popular than $\mathrm{SU}(5)$/
$\mathrm{SO}(10)$ in current literature but remains under active
investigation. The empirical status is mixed: right-handed currents have
not been directly observed (constraining the left-right symmetry
breaking scale); leptoquark searches at LHC have placed bounds but not
excluded the program; neutrino masses (now empirically established) are
accommodated more naturally than in minimal $\mathrm{SU}(5)$.

The program's principal limitation, like other GUT-style programs, is
that the unification group is postulated rather than derived. The choice
of $\mathrm{SU}(4) \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_R$ is
motivated (lepton number as fourth color, parity restoration) but is not
derived from a deeper principle.

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's contribution relative to
Pati-Salam: the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework does not embed
$G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ in any larger group --- the No-GUT Theorem (Theorem
2.2 of \[MG-GaugeGroups Part V\]) establishes that no embedding is
available. The "lepton number as fourth color" insight of Pati-Salam is
reflected differently in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework: leptons
are $M_3(\mathbb{C})$-singlets while quarks are
$M_3(\mathbb{C})$-fundamentals, with the distinction being whether the
bimodule action probes the substrate-scale spatial-direction structure
(programmatic in \[MG-GaugeGroups Part III, Theorem 4.2\]).

### Algebraic and division-algebra approaches {#sec:Algebraic}

#### Strategy and historical context

A distinct line of attack on the gauge-group-derivation problem proceeds
via purely algebraic structures, using the four normed division algebras
$\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{C}, \mathbb{H}, \mathbb{O}$ (real, complex,
quaternionic, octonionic) and their tensor products. The strategic
position is that the Standard Model's gauge structure --- specifically
its dimensions, representation content, and chirality assignments ---
might emerge from the algebraic properties of these four division
algebras and their combinations, without requiring postulation of a
larger gauge group or compactification of higher dimensions.

The principal contributors:

-   **Geoffrey Dixon (1990s--present)** [@Dixon1994]: derived features
    of the Standard Model from the algebra
    $\mathbb{R}\otimes \mathbb{C}\otimes \mathbb{H}\otimes \mathbb{O}$,
    with the four division algebras supplying spacetime structure
    ($\mathbb{C}, \mathbb{H}$) and internal gauge structure
    ($\mathbb{C}, \mathbb{O}$).

-   **Cohl Furey (2010s--present)** [@Furey2018]: derived
    $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ from $\mathbb{C}\otimes \mathbb{O}$ via the action
    of left-multiplication operators on the algebra itself, with the
    gauge group emerging as the symmetry group preserving certain
    algebraic structures.

-   **John Baez & John Huerta** [@BaezHuerta2010]: provided a clean
    group-theoretic derivation of $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ from the embedding
    $G_{\mathrm{SM}}\subset \mathrm{SU}(5) \subset \mathrm{Spin}(10)$,
    with the octonionic structure entering via the connection to the
    exceptional Lie group $E_6$.

-   **Latham Boyle & Shane Farnsworth (2013--present)**
    [@FarnsworthBoyle2013]: extended the Connes-Chamseddine spectral
    action principle to non-associative geometries, using the octonions
    to produce a $G_2$ gauge theory coupled to gravity. The
    non-associativity of $\mathbb{O}$ is used to access exceptional Lie
    group structures unavailable in associative spectral triples.

#### Achievements

The algebraic approaches have produced several genuine insights:

-   **Natural emergence of $\mathrm{SU}(3)$**: the automorphism group of
    the octonions is the exceptional Lie group $G_2$, which contains
    $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ as a subgroup. The colour gauge group thus has a
    natural algebraic origin in octonionic structure.

-   **Three-fold structure**: the octonions naturally encode a
    three-fold structure (via the imaginary octonion units organized
    into a Fano plane) that has been suggested as the origin of the
    three quark colors and/or the three matter generations.

-   **Connection to exceptional Lie groups**: the octonions connect
    naturally to the exceptional series $G_2, F_4, E_6, E_7, E_8$, which
    contain $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ as subgroups in various ways. This
    suggests a deeper algebraic structure underlying the Standard Model.

-   **Anomaly cancellation**: certain algebraic constructions produce
    anomaly-free gauge theories without requiring fine-tuning of the
    matter content.

#### Open problems

The algebraic approaches face several challenges:

-   **No unique falsifiable model**: while the algebraic approaches
    produce suggestive features, no specific model has emerged that
    uniquely produces the Standard Model with falsifiable predictions.
    The space of possible algebraic constructions is broad.

-   **Why $\mathbb{C}\otimes \mathbb{O}$?**: the choice of which
    algebraic structure to start with (e.g.,
    $\mathbb{C}\otimes \mathbb{O}$
    vs. $\mathbb{R}\otimes \mathbb{C}\otimes \mathbb{H}\otimes \mathbb{O}$
    vs. pure $\mathbb{O}$) is selected for its empirical match to the
    Standard Model.

-   **Connection to spacetime**: the division-algebra approaches are
    typically agnostic about the relationship between the algebraic
    structure and physical spacetime. Why should physical particles
    transform according to division-algebra representations? This
    question has not been definitively answered.

-   **Three generations**: most algebraic approaches accommodate three
    generations only by hand or via additional algebraic structures
    (e.g., taking three copies of the basic representation), not as a
    derivation.

-   **Mass spectrum**: the algebraic approaches do not yet derive the
    empirical mass spectra or Yukawa couplings.

#### Status assessment

The algebraic / division-algebra program is a research program with
suggestive features rather than a finished theory. It has produced
beautiful mathematical structures but has not produced uniquely
falsifiable predictions about the Standard Model that distinguish it
from alternatives.

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's contribution relative to
algebraic approaches: where algebraic approaches treat division algebras
as primitive data, the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework derives the
relevant algebra
($\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$)
from substrate-scale McGucken-Sphere structure. The $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)$
Clifford algebra appears in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework not as
a postulated algebraic structure but as the consequence of the
four-dimensional structure of $\mathcal{M}^{1,3}$, which is itself a
feature of $dx_4/dt = ic$. This is an advance: the algebra is a theorem
rather than a postulate, with the physical principle providing the
explanatory grounding that pure algebraic approaches lack.

It is worth noting that the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's
$\mathbb{H}$ summand (Sector B of $\mathcal{A}_F$) is closely related to
Furey's $\mathbb{C}\otimes \mathbb{O}$ work and Dixon's
$\mathbb{R}\otimes \mathbb{C}\otimes \mathbb{H}\otimes \mathbb{O}$
structure: both involve quaternionic structure acting on
$\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)$ Weyl-doublet fermions. The McGucken derivation
differs in specifying *why* the quaternionic structure appears (the
McGucken-Sphere
$\mathrm{SO}(3) \to \mathrm{Spin}(3) \cong \mathrm{SU}(2)$ lift on
$\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ doublets per \[MG-GaugeGroups Part I\]) rather than
postulating it.

### The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework in comparative context {#sec:McGuckenComparative}

#### The strategy of the present unified treatment

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, established in Parts I--V of the
present unified treatment, takes a different approach from each of the
prior programs. The key strategic moves:

1.  **Single primitive law**: the entire derivation descends from one
    equation, $dx_4/dt = ic$ (the McGucken Principle), with no
    additional postulates beyond standard mathematical machinery
    (Clifford algebra, spectral triples, Lie group theory).

2.  **Substrate-scale exhaustion**: the substrate-scale features of
    $dx_4/dt = ic$ are exactly three (the $x_4$-phase scalar feature,
    the $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$ Weyl-doublet feature, and the spatial
    three-direction feature), and each contributes exactly one summand
    to the internal algebra
    $\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$.
    No fourth feature exists. This is the No-GUT Theorem (Theorem 2.2 of
    Part V).

3.  **Inheritance from Connes-Chamseddine**: once $\mathcal{A}_F$ is
    established, the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework inherits the
    entire Connes-Chamseddine inner-automorphism construction to obtain
    $G_{\mathrm{SM}}= \mathrm{PInn}(\mathcal{A}_F) = U(1) \times \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathrm{SU}(3)$.
    The McGucken contribution is to derive $\mathcal{A}_F$ rather than
    postulating it.

4.  **Falsifiable empirical prediction**: the No-GUT Theorem entails the
    No-Proton-Decay Prediction $\tau_p^{\mathrm{McG}} = \infty$ (Theorem
    3.1 of Part V), which sharply distinguishes the McGucken
    $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework from all GUT scenarios.

5.  **Unification across physics**: the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
    framework is not narrowly a gauge-group-derivation program. The same
    primitive law $dx_4/dt = ic$ is shown elsewhere in the McGucken
    corpus to derive general relativity (constraint-projection of
    $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}$, see [@MG-GR]), the wave function and
    Born rule [@MG-Measurement], the path integral via Huygens iteration
    [@MG-Huygens], the canonical commutation relations [@MG-CCR], and
    the Hilbert space structure [@MG-Hilbert].

#### Where the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework is novel relative to prior programs

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's gauge-group derivation is novel
in three specific ways relative to prior programs:

-   **Relative to GUTs**: the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework does not
    embed $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ in a larger group; it derives
    $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ from below. The No-GUT Theorem (Part V, Theorem
    2.2) establishes that no embedding is available, in sharp contrast
    to the GUT program's embed-and-break strategy. The accompanying
    No-Proton-Decay Prediction is the empirical discriminator.

-   **Relative to Connes-Chamseddine NCG**: the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
    framework derives the internal algebra $\mathcal{A}_F$ directly
    (Part II, Theorem 4.1) rather than postulating it. This addresses
    the gap left open in the standard NCG program. The McGucken
    $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework is therefore a strict extension of the NCG
    program: every result of the NCG analysis is preserved, with the
    additional material that $\mathcal{A}_F$ is now a theorem.

-   **Relative to string theory**: the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework
    predicts $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ uniquely (no landscape, no
    compactification choices) as an exhaustion of substrate-scale
    features. Where string theory has $10^{500}$ vacua and no selection
    mechanism, the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework has one answer.

#### Where the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework overlaps with prior programs

In other respects, the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework overlaps
substantially with prior programs:

-   **The Connes-Chamseddine inner-automorphism construction**: the
    McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework uses this machinery essentially
    unchanged. The only difference is what fills the role of
    $\mathcal{A}_F$.

-   **The Chamseddine-Connes-Mukhanov "quanta of geometry"**: the
    McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework identifies these with
    substrate-scale McGucken Spheres (Part II, Theorem 4.1). This is an
    identification, not a replacement: the CCM machinery is used as is,
    with the McGucken interpretation supplying the physical-geometric
    origin.

-   **Quaternionic structure on $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)$ Weyl doublets**:
    shared with the algebraic / division-algebra approaches of Dixon,
    Furey, and others. The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework specifies
    the origin (McGucken-Sphere $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ lift via
    $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)^+$) rather than postulating the quaternionic
    structure.

-   **The Weinberg angle prediction $\sin^2\theta_W = 3/8$ at
    unification scale**: shared with $\mathrm{SU}(5)$ GUTs and
    Connes-Chamseddine NCG. The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework
    reproduces this prediction with substrate-scale McGucken-Sphere
    saturation rate ratios as the origin.

#### Where the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework remains programmatic

Honest acknowledgment of what remains open:

-   **Bimodule construction**: the explicit construction distinguishing
    quark-bimodules (with $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ action) from
    lepton-bimodules ($M_3(\mathbb{C})$-singlets) is identified as
    programmatic in \[MG-GaugeGroups Part III, Theorem 4.2\], with the
    framework supplied but the explicit derivation requiring further
    work.

-   **Three matter generations**: the three-generation structure is
    genuine open research [@MG-Generations], as it is in every
    alternative program.

-   **Empirical Yukawa couplings, mass spectra, mixing angles**: these
    are not yet derived from substrate-scale geometric ratios; only
    their origins are identified.

-   **Strong CP angle**: the empirical near-vanishing of
    $\bar\theta < 10^{-10}$ is not yet derived.

These programmatic items are not unique to the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework; every alternative program has analogous open issues. The
comparison asks which program's open issues are most tractable --- a
question on which the comparative landscape provides no decisive answer.

#### Reading the tables together

The three tables, read together, suggest a picture:

-   **The GUT program** has produced extensive theoretical machinery but
    is in serious empirical trouble. Its principal prediction (proton
    decay) has not been observed; minimal $\mathrm{SU}(5)$ is excluded;
    SUSY-versions are in increasing tension. After 52 years, no GUT has
    uniquely emerged as compelling.

-   **The Connes-Chamseddine NCG program** is the closest in spirit to
    the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework. Its principal achievement is
    the spectral identification of $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ with
    $\mathrm{PInn}(\mathcal{A}_F)$ for a specific $\mathcal{A}_F$; its
    principal limitation is that $\mathcal{A}_F$ is postulated rather
    than derived. The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's contribution
    is to fill this gap.

-   **The string theory program** has produced enormous mathematical
    machinery but suffers from the landscape problem: $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$
    is one of $\sim 10^{500}$ possible vacua, with no selection
    mechanism. After 42 years, no unique gauge-group derivation has
    emerged.

-   **The Pati-Salam program** is elegant but its distinctive
    predictions ($W_R, Z_R$ at intermediate scale) have not been
    observed.

-   **The algebraic / division-algebra approaches** have produced
    suggestive features but no uniquely falsifiable models.

-   **The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework** is newly proposed (2
    years), with theorems established in the present unified treatment.
    Its falsifiable prediction ($\tau_p = \infty$) is consistent with
    current experimental bounds and is sharply distinguishable from all
    GUT scenarios.

### The Higgs sector comparative landscape {#sec:HiggsComparative}

The comparative discussion to this point has focused on the
gauge-group-derivation problem. The Higgs sector presents an analogous
but distinct comparison: which prior frameworks have addressed the seven
items of opacity in the Standard Model's Higgs sector (the existence of
$H$, the sign of $\mu^2$, the magnitude of $v$, the shape of $V(H)$, the
Yukawa pattern, the hierarchy problem, the cosmological homogeneity of
$\langle H\rangle$), and how does the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework's eight-theorem treatment of
Section [5](#sec:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:HiggsPointer"} compare? The Higgs paper [@MG-Higgs2026]
contains a detailed framework-by-framework analysis, which we import
here in full for self-containment.

#### The opacity of the Higgs in the standard treatment {#ssec:HiggsOpacity}

The Standard Model's Higgs Lagrangian
$\mathcal{L}_H = (D_\mu H)^\dagger (D^\mu H) - V(H)$ with
$V(H) = -\mu^2 H^\dagger H + \lambda (H^\dagger H)^2$ contains seven
stipulated elements, each required for the mechanism to function but
none of which has a physical origin within the Standard Model framework:

1.  *The existence of $H$.* The only justification for postulating a
    scalar doublet field is functional: without it, the electroweak
    gauge bosons cannot acquire mass and the chiral fermions cannot
    acquire mass while preserving renormalisability and gauge
    invariance. This is functional necessity, not derivation from any
    deeper principle.

2.  *The sign of $\mu^2$.* The potential is required to have $\mu^2 > 0$
    so that $\langle H\rangle = 0$ is unstable. The Standard Model
    offers no reason why $\mu^2 > 0$ rather than $\mu^2 < 0$ (which
    would give an unbroken electroweak symmetry, no fermion masses, no
    atoms, no chemistry).

3.  *The magnitude of $v$.* The vev
    $v = \sqrt{\mu^2/\lambda} \approx 246$ GeV is determined by
    potential parameters that are inputs. The number 246 GeV has no
    explanation.

4.  *The Mexican-hat shape.* The quartic-in-$H^\dagger H$ potential is
    chosen because it works, not derived.

5.  *The Yukawa coupling pattern.* Each fermion species has its own
    Yukawa $y_f$. The values $y_e \approx 3 \times 10^{-6}$,
    $y_t \approx 1$ span six orders of magnitude with no Standard-Model
    explanation.

6.  *The hierarchy problem.* The mass parameter
    $\mu^2 \approx (88\,\mathrm{GeV})^2$ receives quadratic radiative
    corrections $\delta\mu^2 \sim \Lambda^2$ at cutoff
    $\Lambda = M_{\mathrm{Pl}}$, requiring fine-tuning of $\sim 1$ part
    in $10^{34}$.

7.  *The cosmological homogeneity of $\langle H\rangle$.* The vev is
    observed to be the same value across the entire observable universe.
    The Standard Model permits in-principle vev variation if
    appropriately coupled to dynamical scalar fields [@Chakrabarti2024];
    the homogeneity is observed but not explained.

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, via the eight theorems of
Section [5](#sec:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:HiggsPointer"}, supplies physics for each: (1) the
existence of $H$ follows from the need for a field-theoretic encoding of
the local $+ic$ direction
(Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}); (2) the sign of $\mu^2$ follows from the
pointer-on energetic requirement
(Postulate [222](#post:PointerOn){reference-type="ref"
reference="post:PointerOn"},
Theorem [224](#thm:MexicanHat){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MexicanHat"}); (3) the magnitude of $v$ remains open,
flagged; (4) the Mexican-hat shape follows from (1)+(2) plus
renormalisability (Theorem [224](#thm:MexicanHat){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MexicanHat"}); (5) the Yukawa pattern acquires
interpretation as the species-specific $x_4$-winding-rate hierarchy
(Theorem [218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:YukawaWinding"}) but specific values remain open; (6) the
existence of $\langle H\rangle \neq 0$ is topologically protected
(Theorem [209](#thm:VevLoopProtection){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:VevLoopProtection"}) with the radiative stability of
$\mu^2$ flagged open
(Theorem [210](#thm:HierarchyTrichotomy){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HierarchyTrichotomy"}); (7) the cosmological homogeneity
is a theorem from the global uniformity of $+ic$
(Theorem [207](#thm:HiggsVev){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsVev"}). Items (1), (2), (4), (5)-interpretation,
(6)-existence, and (7) are now *theorems*; items (3), (5)-values, and
(6)-radiative stability are flagged *open*.

#### Prior frameworks: what each addresses and what each leaves opaque {#ssec:PriorHiggsFrameworks}

We catalogue the prior frameworks that have addressed the Higgs sector's
opacity, identifying in each case what is addressed and what is left
opaque relative to the McGucken eight-theorem treatment.

##### Anderson (1962): the superconductivity analogy

Anderson's 1962 paper "Plasmons, Gauge Invariance, and Mass"
[@Anderson1963] anticipated the Higgs mechanism by analogy with the
Meissner effect: in a superconductor, a charged condensate of Cooper
pairs gives the photon an effective mass while preserving gauge
invariance.

*What Anderson supplies:* An existence proof that charged condensates
can give gauge bosons mass while preserving the gauge structure.

*What Anderson does not supply:* A physical reason why nature should
have a fundamental scalar field whose vev is non-zero in vacuum. In a
superconductor, the Cooper pair condensate is emergent and conditional
(it exists only in specific materials at specific temperatures); the
Standard Model Higgs is fundamental and universal. The analogy provides
mechanism but no foundation.

##### Higgs, Englert, Brout, Guralnik, Hagen, Kibble (1964): the formal mechanism

The three near-simultaneous 1964 papers
[@EnglertBrout1964PRL; @Higgs1964; @GHK1964] established the formal
mechanism by which a scalar field acquiring a vev produces massive gauge
bosons. Higgs's paper additionally noted that the mechanism implies a
massive scalar boson, whose discovery in 2012 confirmed the mechanism.

*What this supplies:* The mathematical machinery; the functional
correctness of the mechanism.

*What this does not supply:* A physical reading of why the scalar field
is there, why its potential has the Mexican-hat shape, why $\mu^2 > 0$,
why the vev takes the value it does, or why fermions couple to the Higgs
at the rates they do.

##### Weinberg-Salam (1967--1968): electroweak unification

The Weinberg-Salam electroweak unification [@Weinberg1967] combined the
Higgs mechanism with the $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ gauge
structure, producing a renormalisable quantum field theory.

*What Weinberg-Salam supplies:* A complete renormalisable QFT of the
electroweak interaction, empirically successful to high precision.

*What Weinberg-Salam does not supply:* The Higgs doublet $H$, the
potential $V(H)$, and the Yukawa couplings $y_f$ are introduced as
separate elements, each chosen for its functional role. The number of
free parameters in the Higgs sector alone --- $\mu^2$, $\lambda$, nine
Yukawa couplings for charged fermions, plus mixing parameters --- is
large. The 246 GeV vev is empirical input. Weinberg-Salam is where the
Higgs becomes operationally central while remaining physically opaque.

##### Technicolor (Susskind, Weinberg, 1976--1979)

Technicolor [@Weinberg1976; @Susskind1979] proposed that electroweak
symmetry breaking arises dynamically from a new strong force at the TeV
scale, with technifermions forming a chiral condensate breaking the
electroweak symmetry without a fundamental scalar.

*What technicolor supplies:* A dynamical mechanism for EWSB; the
hierarchy problem is dissolved at the level of $\mu^2$ since there is no
fundamental scalar.

*What technicolor does not supply:* Realistic models require extended
technicolor or walking technicolor, which face severe FCNC constraints.
The 2012 LHC discovery of a light fundamental-like scalar at 125 GeV is
incompatible with technicolor's prediction of heavier composite scalars;
the original form is excluded. The framework also does not address the
Yukawa hierarchy, the cosmological homogeneity of the vev, or the
geometry of the orientation in $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ space.

##### Supersymmetry (1970s--present)

Supersymmetry [@GolfandLikhtman1971; @WessZumino1974] proposes a
symmetry between bosons and fermions; applied to the hierarchy problem
[@DimopoulosGeorgi1981; @Witten1981], the quadratic loop corrections to
$\mu^2$ from boson loops are cancelled by superpartner fermion loops,
leaving only logarithmic corrections.

*What supersymmetry supplies:* A solution to the radiative-correction
piece of the hierarchy problem; $\delta\mu^2$ becomes logarithmic rather
than quadratic in the cutoff.

*What supersymmetry does not supply:* The superpartners have not been
observed at the Tevatron, LHC Run-1, Run-2, or Run-3. The MSSM's
parameter space is severely constrained; the original naturalness
motivation (superpartners at or below the TeV scale) is in serious
tension with experimental bounds. Supersymmetry does not address why the
Higgs exists, why its vev takes the value it does, why the Yukawas have
their hierarchy, or why $\mu^2 > 0$. It addresses one specific symptom
(the radiative hierarchy) at the cost of approximately doubling the
particle content, none of which has been observed.

##### Composite Higgs (Kaplan-Georgi 1984; modern variants)

Composite Higgs models
[@KaplanGeorgi1984; @ContinoNomura2003; @AgasheContinoPomarol2005]
propose that the Higgs is a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson of a
spontaneously broken global symmetry of a strongly-coupled sector.

*What composite Higgs supplies:* Naturalness for the Higgs mass through
Goldstone-boson protection.

*What composite Higgs does not supply:* New strongly-coupled sector at
the TeV scale with composite resonances that should be observable at the
LHC; these have not been definitively observed. The Yukawa hierarchy is
addressed via partial compositeness, but this introduces additional
empirical parameters rather than reducing them. The cosmological
homogeneity of $\langle H\rangle$, the physical origin of the
$\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ orientation, and the question of why there is a Higgs
sector at all remain unaddressed.

##### Connes' spectral noncommutative geometry (1996--present)

Connes' spectral NCG programme
[@Connes1996; @ChamseddineConnes1997; @ChamseddineConnesMarcolli2007]
formulates the Standard Model plus gravity as a spectral triple, with
the Higgs field as the connection in the discrete (internal) direction
of a noncommutative product manifold.

*What spectral NCG supplies:* A unified geometric reading of the SM
gauge fields plus the Higgs plus gravity, with the spectral action
producing the SM Lagrangian.

*What spectral NCG does not supply:* The noncommutative algebra is
postulated rather than derived from a deeper physics. The original
Chamseddine-Connes Higgs-mass prediction $m_h \approx 170$ GeV conflicts
with the measured 125 GeV; subsequent modifications introduce additional
fields. Crucially, the framework gives no physical reason for the
noncommutative product, no principle from which the algebra emerges, and
no physical reading of the Higgs vev's homogeneity across spacetime. The
geometry is mathematical rather than physical. *The McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's contribution relative to NCG is to fill this
gap*: the eight Higgs theorems of
Section [5](#sec:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:HiggsPointer"} establish the physics (pointer to $+ic$)
and the homogeneity (from global uniformity of $+ic$) that NCG leaves
opaque.

##### Gauge-Higgs unification (Manton 1979; Hosotani 1983; modern variants)

Gauge-Higgs unification [@Manton1979; @Hosotani1983; @CsakiEtAl2004]
identifies the Higgs as a component of a higher-dimensional gauge field,
with EWSB arising from the Wilson loop around an extra compact
dimension.

*What gauge-Higgs unification supplies:* Geometric origin for the Higgs
as a gauge-field component, and natural protection against quadratic
divergences (since five-dimensional gauge symmetry forbids a local Higgs
mass term).

*What gauge-Higgs unification does not supply:* The framework requires
extra compact dimensions of size $\sim \mathrm{TeV}^{-1}$; none have
been observed. The compactification radius, Wilson loop, and fermion
localisation profiles all introduce additional empirical parameters. The
physical reading of the Higgs vev as a Wilson loop expectation value is
geometrically suggestive but provides no postulate explaining why the
extra dimension exists or why its compactification scale takes the value
it does.

##### Woit's Euclidean Twistor Unification (2021)

Woit's 2021 proposal [@Woit2021] takes Euclidean signature spacetime as
fundamental, with
$\mathrm{Spin}(4) = \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_R$
factorising into two independent $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ factors; one is gauged
to give the chiral spin connection of gravity, the other to give the
weak $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$. Lorentzian reconstruction requires choosing an
imaginary time direction; Woit identifies the field specifying this
choice as the Higgs.

*What Woit supplies:* A geometric framework in which $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$
and the chiral spin connection both arise from the 4D rotation group,
exploiting the special factorisation
$\mathrm{Spin}(4) = \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathrm{SU}(2)$ that
$\mathrm{Spin}(p,q)$ for $pq \neq 0$ does not have.

*What Woit does not supply:* Woit's framework requires the
imaginary-time direction as *external mathematical data* --- a degree of
freedom that must be introduced for the Lorentzian reconstruction to
work. The framework does not address: why this direction exists, what
rate (if any) it advances at, whether it is globally uniform across
spacetime, or how it couples to matter. These four physical contents ---
existence, rate, uniformity, matter coupling --- are absent from Woit's
framework.

Specifically: Woit has no rate $ic$ attached to the imaginary-time
direction, so it cannot supply the ten Poincaré conservation laws as
theorems of $x_4$'s expansion (these depend on the specific rate $ic$ of
the master equation $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$). It has no global uniformity
for $+ic$, so it cannot derive the absence of Higgs domain walls
(Theorem [228](#thm:NoDomainWall){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:NoDomainWall"}). It has no matter orientation condition
coupling matter to $x_4$, so it cannot supply the Yukawa-as-winding-rate
reading (Theorem [218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:YukawaWinding"}) or the matter-feels-$x_4$ switch
(Theorem [220](#thm:MatterFeelsX4){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MatterFeelsX4"}).

The relationship between the two programmes is therefore one-way: Woit's
mathematical machinery exploits the $\mathrm{Spin}(4)$ decomposition
that the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework also uses, but the physics is
McGucken's. The McGucken Principle, formulated under Wheeler's
supervision at Princeton in the late 1980s [@Wheeler-LetterMcGucken] and
developed publicly across the UNC Chapel Hill dissertation appendix
(1998--99) [@MG-Dissertation1998], FQXi essays (2008--2013)
[@MG-FQXi2008; @MG-FQXi2009; @MG-FQXi2011; @MG-FQXi2012; @MG-FQXi2013],
books (2016--2017)
[@MG-LTDBook2016; @MG-RelativityDerived2017; @MG-Entanglement2017], and
the ongoing derivation programme at <https://elliotmcguckenphysics.com>
(2024--2026), predates Woit's proposal by more than two decades, comes
from an entirely different direction, and stands on its own physical
foundation. They are not to be confused: Woit's framework, lacking the
four physical contents (existence, rate, uniformity, matter coupling),
cannot supply the eight Higgs readings.

    (Theorem [207](#thm:HiggsVev){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:HiggsVev"}).

3.  **Hierarchy:** the hierarchy trichotomy with topological protection

    (Theorems [209](#thm:VevLoopProtection){reference-type="ref"

The reason for this coverage gap is simple: each prior framework
supplies some piece of the physics needed to read the Higgs sector
geometrically, but none supplies all four pieces required. The Standard
Model has no fourth dimension; technicolor has no fourth dimension;
supersymmetry has no fourth dimension; composite Higgs has extra
dimensions of a different type without rate or uniformity; Connes'
framework has noncommutative directions without rate or uniformity;
gauge-Higgs unification has compact extra dimensions without rate or
uniformity; Woit has an imaginary-time direction without rate,
uniformity, or matter coupling. Only the McGucken Principle supplies all
four physical contents and so only it can prove the eight theorems of
Section [5](#sec:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:HiggsPointer"}.

### The unified "more from less" comparison: McGucken across all physics {#sec:UnifiedMoreFromLess}

The advance of the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework is not confined to
the gauge-group derivation or the Higgs sector. The McGucken Principle
$dx_4/dt = ic$ is a single physical-geometric law, and from it the
framework has derived as theorems an unusually broad range of physical
structures. We catalogue these in a master comparative table,
contrasting what the McGucken framework derives from $dx_4/dt = ic$
against what each prior framework requires as input.
