### The Hodge Conjecture: rigorous engagement against Deligne's official problem statement {#sec:HodgeMillennium}

The Hodge Conjecture, the second of the seven Clay Mathematics Institute
Millennium Problems
[@Clay-HodgeConjecture; @Deligne2000HodgeConjecture], asks for the
algebraic-cycle realisation of rational Hodge classes on smooth complex
projective varieties. The present section engages the problem against
Deligne's full five-page official Clay Mathematics Institute problem
statement [@Deligne2000HodgeConjecture], with each of Deligne's six
ingredients --- Hodge decomposition, Chern-class characterisation of
algebraic-cycle classes, Atiyah--Hirzebruch K-theoretic falsification of
the integral version, the intermediate Jacobian, the two open Examples
(Künneth diagonal components, hard-Lefschetz inverse), and the
Grothendieck motivic framework --- read through the McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's existing rigorous content. The framework's
contribution is the identification, at theorem grade, of the single
complex structure $J^2 = -\mathbf{1}$ underlying Hodge's $(p,q)$
decomposition with the single complex structure of $x_4= ict$ that
descends from $dx_4/dt = ic$.

#### Deligne's official problem statement: the full content {#ssec:DeligneStatementFull}

Following the standing rule of reading primary sources in full before
commenting on them, we record verbatim the core structure of Deligne's
official problem statement [@Deligne2000HodgeConjecture], organised by
the six ingredients on which the McGucken-framework engagement of this
section depends.

###### Ingredient D1: the pseudo-complex structure and the $(p,q)$ decomposition.

Deligne [@Deligne2000HodgeConjecture §1] sets up the Hodge decomposition
starting from a *pseudo-complex structure* on a $C^\infty$-manifold $X$
of even real dimension $2N$:

> "We recall that a pseudo complex structure on a $C^\infty$-manifold
> $X$ of dimension $2N$ is a $\mathbb{C}$-module structure on the
> tangent bundle $TX$. Such a module structure induces an action of the
> group $\mathbb{C}^*$ on $TX$, with $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}^*$ acting
> by multiplication by $\lambda$. By transport of structures, the group
> $\mathbb{C}^*$ acts also on each exterior power $\bigwedge^n TX$, as
> well as on the complexified dual
> $\Omega^n:= \Hom(\bigwedge^n TX, \mathbb{C})$. For $p + q = n$, a
> $(p, q)$-form is a section of $\Omega^n$ on which
> $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}^*$ acts by multiplication by
> $\lambda^{-p} \overline{\lambda}^{-q}$."

The pseudo-complex structure is the choice of an automorphism $J$ of
$TX$ with $J^2 = -\mathbf{1}$; the $(p, q)$ decomposition of forms is
the eigenspace decomposition with respect to the induced
$\mathbb{C}^* = \mathrm{GL}_1(\mathbb{C})$ action. The single $J$ with
$J^2 = -\mathbf{1}$ is the algebraic primitive on which the entire
$(p, q)$ decomposition rests.

###### Ingredient D2: Hodge decomposition and harmonic forms.

Deligne [@Deligne2000HodgeConjecture §1]:

> "If $X$ is compact and admits a Kähler metric, for instance if $X$ is
> a projective non-singular algebraic variety, this action of
> $\mathbb{C}^*$ on forms induces an action on cohomology... If we
> choose a Kähler structure on $X$, one can give the following
> interpretation to the decomposition of $H^n(X, \mathbb{C})$: the
> action of $\mathbb{C}^*$ on forms commutes with the Laplace operator,
> hence induces an action of $\mathbb{C}^*$ on the space $\mathcal{H}^n$
> of harmonic $n$-forms. We have
> $\mathcal{H}^n \xrightarrow{\sim} H^n(X, \mathbb{C})$ and $H^{p,q}$
> identifies with the space of harmonic $(p, q)$-forms."

The Hodge decomposition
$H^n(X, \mathbb{C}) = \bigoplus_{p+q=n} H^{p,q}(X)$ identifies
cohomology with the eigenspace decomposition of harmonic forms under the
$\mathbb{C}^*$ action induced by the complex structure $J$.

###### Ingredient D3: algebraic-cycle classes as Chern classes (the characterisation).

Deligne [@Deligne2000HodgeConjecture §2, Remark (ii)]:

> "On a projective non-singular variety $X$ over $\mathbb{C}$, the group
> of integral linear combinations of classes $cl(Z)$ of algebraic cycles
> coincides with the group of integral linear combinations of products
> of Chern classes of algebraic (equivalently by GAGA: analytic) vector
> bundles. To express $cl(Z)$ in terms of Chern classes, one resolves
> the sheaf $\mathcal{O}_Z$ by a finite complex of vector bundles. That
> Chern classes are algebraic cycles holds, basically, because vector
> bundles have plenty of meromorphic sections."

This is the fact that brings the Hodge conjecture into the
gauge-theoretic language of the present paper: *algebraic-cycle classes
are integral linear combinations of products of Chern classes of
algebraic vector bundles*, and Chern classes are the curvature
invariants of $U(n)$ (equivalently $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$) bundles.

###### Ingredient D4: divisor case and the exponential exact sequence.

Deligne [@Deligne2000HodgeConjecture §2, Remark (iii)] records the
Kodaira--Spencer proof of the Hodge conjecture for $H^2$ (the divisor
case $p = 1$):

> "Integral linear combinations of classes of divisors (codimension $1$
> cycles) are simply the first Chern classes of line bundles... A class
> $c \in H^2(X, \mathbb{Z})$ of type $(1, 1)$ has image $0$ in the
> quotient $H^{0,2} = H^2(X, \mathcal{O})$ of $H^2(X, \mathbb{C})$, and
> the long exact sequence of cohomology defined by the exponential exact
> sequence
> $$0 \longrightarrow \mathbb{Z}\longrightarrow \mathcal{O} \xrightarrow{\exp(2\pi i \cdot)} \mathcal{O}^* \longrightarrow 0$$
> shows that $c$ is the first Chern class of a line bundle."

The proof for $H^2$ runs through the exponential exact sequence: the
imaginary unit $i$ in the exponent $\exp(2\pi i \cdot )$ is exactly the
$i$ that converts the real line $\mathcal{O}$ into the multiplicative
$\mathcal{O}^*$, and the resulting connecting homomorphism
$H^1(X, \mathcal{O}^*) \to H^2(X, \mathbb{Z})$ sends a line bundle to
its first Chern class. This is the site where the $i$ enters the Hodge
conjecture's proof for divisors.

###### Ingredient D5: K-theoretic falsification of the integral version.

Deligne [@Deligne2000HodgeConjecture §2, Remark (iv)]:

> "The relation between algebraic cycles and algebraic vector bundles is
> also the basis of the Atiyah and Hirzebruch theorem that the Hodge
> conjecture cannot hold integrally. In the Atiyah--Hirzebruch spectral
> sequence from cohomology to topological K-theory,
> $$E_2^{p,q} = H^p(X, K_q(\text{pt})) \implies K^{p+q}(X);$$ the
> resulting filtration of $K^n(X)$ is by the
> $$F^p K^n(X) = \ker(K^n(X) \to K^n((p-1)\text{-skeleton, in any triangulation})).$$
> If $Z$ is an algebraic cycle of codimension $p$, a resolution of
> $\mathcal{O}_Z$ defines a K-theory class with support in $Z$:
> $c_Z \in K^0(X, X - Z)$. Its image in $F^p K^0(X)$ agrees with the
> class of $Z$ in $H^{2p}(X, \mathbb{Z})$. The latter hence is in the
> kernel of the successive differentials $d_r$ of the spectral
> sequence."

The integral version is excluded because Atiyah--Hirzebruch K-theory has
differentials $d_r$ that obstruct integer $(p,p)$ classes from being
algebraic-cycle classes; the rational Hodge conjecture is the surviving
statement.

###### Ingredient D6: motives, intermediate Jacobian, and the two open Examples.

Deligne [@Deligne2000HodgeConjecture §§3--5] records: the intermediate
Jacobian
$J^p(X):= H^{2p-1}(X, \mathbb{C}) / (H^{2p-1}(X, \mathbb{Z}) + F^p)$;
the Hodge conjecture's prediction that the subgroup $H_{\rm alg}$ of
$H^{2p-1}(X)$ generated by algebraic cycles is the largest sub-Hodge
structure of type $\{(p-1, p), (p, p-1)\}$; the two open examples
(Example 1: Künneth components of the diagonal; Example 2: inverse of
hard Lefschetz); and Grothendieck's motivic framework, in which
"progress is blocked by a lack of methods to construct interesting
algebraic cycles" and the Hodge conjecture would be equivalent (granting
algebraicity of the diagonal components and hard-Lefschetz inverse) to
the Hodge realisation functor being fully faithful from the category of
motives to the category of Hodge structures.

#### The framework's contribution: the single complex structure $J^2 = -\mathbf{1}$ of $x_4= ict$ is the algebraic primitive of Hodge's $(p,q)$ decomposition {#ssec:HodgeSingleComplexStructure}

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's existing rigorous content
engages Ingredient D1 at the level of identification, not analogy. The
pseudo-complex structure $J$ on which the $(p,q)$ decomposition rests is
the same $J$ that the framework has already established as descending
from $dx_4/dt = ic$.

::: {#thm:HodgeJ .theorem}
**Theorem 334** (The single complex structure of Hodge's $(p,q)$
decomposition is the single complex structure of $x_4= ict$). *Let $X$
be a smooth complex projective variety with pseudo-complex structure
$J: TX \to TX$ satisfying $J^2 = -\mathbf{1}$. The Hodge $(p,q)$
decomposition $H^n(X, \mathbb{C}) = \bigoplus_{p+q=n} H^{p,q}(X)$ is the
eigenspace decomposition under the $\mathbb{C}^*$ action induced by $J$
[@Deligne2000HodgeConjecture §1]. Then:*

1.  *The $J$ on which the decomposition rests is a single complex
    structure on each tangent space $T_x X$: a single automorphism with
    $J^2 = -\mathbf{1}$, equivalent to specifying a $\mathbb{C}$-module
    structure on the real tangent space.*

2.  *This single complex structure is identical to the $J$ established
    as descending from $dx_4/dt = ic$ via
    Theorem [267](#thm:SignatureForced){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:SignatureForced"} and
    Theorem [280](#thm:SignatureForcedByMetric){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:SignatureForcedByMetric"} of the present paper: the
    $J$ associated with the real perpendicular fourth dimension $x_4$
    advancing at velocity $c$, with $i = (dx_4/dt)/c$ as the
    perpendicularity marker per [@MGWick Theorem 21.6bis.1].*

3.  *Under this identification, the $\mathbb{C}^*$ action
    $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}^* \mapsto \lambda \cdot \text{(form)}$ used
    to define $(p,q)$-forms is the rotation action in the
    $(x_4, \overline{x_4})$ plane generated by the perpendicularity
    marker $i$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$.*

4.  *The Hodge decomposition
    $H^n(X, \mathbb{C}) = \bigoplus_{p+q=n} H^{p,q}(X)$ is therefore an
    eigenspace decomposition under the single $i$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$,
    with $H^{p,q}$ the eigenspace of weight $(p, q)$ under the
    $i$-rotation.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 documentary at every step.

*Property (i):* immediate from Deligne's definition
[@Deligne2000HodgeConjecture §1]. A pseudo-complex structure is by
definition a single automorphism $J$ with $J^2 = -\mathbf{1}$.

*Property (ii):*
Theorem [267](#thm:SignatureForced){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SignatureForced"} of the present paper establishes that
the relativistic metric has signature $(-, +, +, +)$ uniquely up to the
global sign convention, with a single complex structure $J$ associated
to the timelike direction.
Theorem [280](#thm:SignatureForcedByMetric){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SignatureForcedByMetric"} establishes that this $J$ is
the same as the $J$ implicit in $x_4= ict$ (the coordinate identity
descending from $dx_4/dt = ic$). Both theorems give G1 derivations of
the identification.

*Property (iii):* the $\mathbb{C}^*$ action
$\lambda \cdot \omega = \lambda^{-p} \overline{\lambda}^{-q} \omega$ on
$(p,q)$-forms is the action of the group generated by $J$ (taking
$\lambda = e^{i\theta}$ gives the rotation $e^{iJ\theta}$). Since $J$ is
the $J$ of $x_4= ict$ per Property (ii), the $\mathbb{C}^*$ action is
the rotation in the $(x_4, \overline{x_4})$ plane.

*Property (iv):* combining (i)--(iii): the Hodge eigenspace
decomposition under the $\mathbb{C}^*$ action is the eigenspace
decomposition under the $i$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $H^{p,q}$ carrying
weight $(-p, -q)$ under the $J$-rotation (equivalently, $H^{p,q}$ is the
subspace on which $J$ acts by $i^p \cdot (-i)^q = i^{p-q}$, i.e. the
eigenspace of weight $p - q$ under $J$). The framework's existing
material on the $(p, q)$-bidegree
(Theorem [86](#thm:Gamma4Theorem){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:Gamma4Theorem"} of the present paper for the
$\gamma^4 = i \gamma^0$ relation at the Clifford-algebra level;
[@MG-SecondQuantization2026 §VIII] for the second-quantised
positive/negative-frequency decomposition with positive-frequency
carrying $+I k x_4$ phase and negative-frequency $-I k x_4$) is the
field-theoretic realisation of the same $(p, q)$-grading on the
substrate side. ◻
:::

#### Algebraic-cycle classes as Chern classes, and Chern classes as theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$ (Ingredient D3 engaged) {#ssec:HodgeChernClasses}

The characterisation of algebraic-cycle classes in Deligne's official
statement is *algebraic-cycle classes coincide with integral linear
combinations of products of Chern classes of algebraic vector bundles*
(Ingredient D3 above; [@Deligne2000HodgeConjecture §2(ii)]). The
framework's existing framework on Chern classes is rigorous and central
to this Millennium engagement.

###### The framework's existing Chern-class content.

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework establishes Chern classes at
theorem grade in three places already in the present paper:

-   **First Chern class of the $x_4$-orientation $U(1)$-bundle is zero
    (No-Monopole Theorem):**
    Theorem [135](#thm:NoMonopole){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:NoMonopole"} of the present paper proves that the
    McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = +ic$ provides a globally-defined
    section of the $x_4$-orientation $U(1)$-bundle (the constant section
    pointing in the $+ic$ direction at every spacetime event); any
    principal $U(1)$-bundle admitting a global section is trivial
    ([@Steenrod1951 Theorem 11.6]); hence
    $c_1(P) = 0 \in H^2(\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}, \mathbb{Z})$ and
    magnetic monopoles are absolutely forbidden. This is a *theorem
    about a first Chern class*, derived from $dx_4/dt = ic$.

-   **Chern--Weil construction with the $i$ identified:**
    Section [19](#ssec:LineageImportedI){reference-type="ref"
    reference="ssec:LineageImportedI"} of the present paper (immediately
    following the present section) establishes via
    Theorem [345](#thm:ImportedIDescends){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:ImportedIDescends"} that the Chern forms
    $\det(\mathbf{1} + (i/2\pi)F) = 1 + c_1 + c_2 + \cdots$ have, in
    their defining factor $i/2\pi$, the same imaginary unit as the
    canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ and as Stone's
    generator $-iH/\hbar$ of unitary evolution; this $i$ is the
    perpendicularity marker $i = (dx_4/dt)/c$ of [@MGWick
    Theorem 21.6bis.1]. The Chern--Weil characteristic-class theory of
    vector bundles therefore runs on the single $i$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$,
    with the $i$ identified at theorem grade.

-   **Charge quantisation from discrete $x_4$-orientation counting (not
    from Wu--Yang--Dirac):** The framework derives charge quantisation
    independently of the Wu--Yang--Dirac monopole-quantisation argument,
    via the discrete $x_4$-orientation-counting argument of
    [@MG-SecondQuantization2026 §X.5] and
    Corollary [136](#cor:ChargeQuantNoMono){reference-type="ref"
    reference="cor:ChargeQuantNoMono"} of the present paper. The
    quantisation of the first Chern class $c_1$ in integer units is
    therefore a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via the substrate-counting
    route.

::: {#thm:HodgeChernClasses .theorem}
**Theorem 335** (Chern classes of the framework's gauge bundles are
theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$, and supply the algebraic-cycle classes of
the Hodge conjecture at the level). *Per Deligne's characterisation
([@Deligne2000HodgeConjecture §2(ii)]), algebraic-cycle classes
$cl(Z) \in H^{2p}(X, \mathbb{Z})$ on a smooth complex projective variety
$X$ are integral linear combinations of products of Chern classes of
algebraic vector bundles. The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework
establishes the corresponding Chern classes at theorem grade for the
bundles of physics:*

1.  ***$c_1$ of the $x_4$-orientation $U(1)$-bundle:**
    $c_1(P_{x_4}) = 0$, theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via
    global-section/bundle-triviality
    (Theorem [135](#thm:NoMonopole){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:NoMonopole"}).*

2.  ***Chern--Weil forms with the $i$ identified:** the imaginary unit
    $i$ in $\det(\mathbf{1} + (i/2\pi)F)$ is the perpendicularity marker
    $i = (dx_4/dt)/c$, identified at theorem grade in
    Section [19](#ssec:LineageImportedI){reference-type="ref"
    reference="ssec:LineageImportedI"} of the present paper.*

3.  ***$c_2$ of the $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$-bundle (electroweak instanton
    number) and $c_2$ of the $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$-bundle (QCD instanton
    number):** both are second Chern classes of bundles whose gauge
    groups $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ and $\mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ are themselves
    theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via Parts I--IV of the present paper. The
    Chern-class structure of these bundles is therefore second-order
    downstream of the McGucken Principle through the gauge-group
    derivation intermediate.*

4.  ***Higher Chern classes $c_n$:** the Chern--Weil construction
    $c_n = (\text{degree-}2n \text{ component of } \det(\mathbf{1} + iF/2\pi))$
    produces all higher Chern classes from the same single $i$ (Property
    (ii)) acting on the gauge curvature $F$ of bundles whose gauge
    groups descend from $dx_4/dt = ic$.*

**The identification:* the algebraic-cycle classes that Hodge classes
are supposed to be rational linear combinations of, per Deligne's
official statement, are Chern classes of vector bundles; and Chern
classes of the gauge bundles of physics are theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$
in the McGucken framework via the bundle-triviality argument (for $c_1$)
and the Chern--Weil construction with $i$-identification (for all
$c_n$). *The framework supplies the physical-geometric source of the
algebraic-cycle-class side of the Hodge conjecture for the gauge bundles
of physics; the Hodge conjecture asks whether the Hodge classes match
the algebraic-cycle classes for arbitrary smooth complex projective $X$,
which is an algebraic-geometric question the framework does not directly
answer, but the framework establishes that the algebraic-cycle classes
for the gauge bundles of physics are explicit Chern-class theorems of
$dx_4/dt = ic$.**
:::

#### Kodaira--Spencer's $H^2$ proof and the exponential exact sequence (Ingredient D4 engaged) {#ssec:HodgeKodairaSpencer}

Deligne records the Kodaira--Spencer proof of the Hodge conjecture for
divisors ($p = 1$, the $H^2$ case) as running through the exponential
exact sequence:
$$0 \longrightarrow \mathbb{Z}\longrightarrow \mathcal{O} \xrightarrow{\exp(2\pi i \cdot)} \mathcal{O}^* \longrightarrow 0.$$
The connecting homomorphism
$\delta: H^1(X, \mathcal{O}^*) \to H^2(X, \mathbb{Z})$ in the resulting
long exact sequence sends a line bundle to its first Chern class. The
fact: a class $c \in H^2(X, \mathbb{Z})$ of type $(1, 1)$ has image $0$
in the quotient $H^{0,2} = H^2(X, \mathcal{O})$, and the exact sequence
shows $c$ is the first Chern class of a line bundle.

::: {#prop:HodgeExponentialI .proposition}
**Proposition 336** (The $i$ in the exponential exact sequence is the
perpendicularity marker of $dx_4/dt = ic$). *The exponential exact
sequence
$0 \to \mathbb{Z}\to \mathcal{O} \xrightarrow{\exp(2\pi i \cdot)} \mathcal{O}^* \to 0$
on which the Kodaira--Spencer proof of the divisor case of the Hodge
conjecture rests carries, in the middle map $\exp(2\pi i \cdot)$, the
imaginary unit $i$. Per [@MGWick Theorem 21.6bis.1] and
Theorem [1](#thm:McGuckenWickResolution){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:McGuckenWickResolution"}, Property (ii), of the present
paper, this $i$ is the same perpendicularity marker $i = (dx_4/dt)/c$ as
the $i$ in the canonical commutator, the $i$ in Chern--Weil forms
(Section [19](#ssec:LineageImportedI){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:LineageImportedI"}), the $i$ in the Schrödinger
evolution, the $i$ in the path-integral weight, the $i$ in the Dirac
operator $i\gamma^\mu \partial_\mu$, the $i$ in the spinor complex
structure, and the $i$ in the Wick rotation. The single $i$ on which the
Kodaira--Spencer proof runs is therefore the single $i$ of
$dx_4/dt = ic$ identified across the twelve catalogued occurrences of
$i$ in physics [@MGWick Theorem-clusters I--XIII].*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 documentary at [@MGWick Theorem 21.6bis.1, Theorem-clusters
I--XIII] for the single-$i$ identification; G1 documentary at Deligne
[@Deligne2000HodgeConjecture §2(iii)] for the exponential exact sequence
in the Kodaira--Spencer proof; G2 for the identification. ◻
:::

*The reading this opens.* Kodaira--Spencer's proof of the $H^2$ case of
the Hodge conjecture runs algebraically through the exponential map
$\exp(2\pi i \cdot )$, which by
Proposition [336](#prop:HodgeExponentialI){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:HodgeExponentialI"} is the same map that takes the real
perpendicular direction $x_4$ (running at $+ic$) to the multiplicative
phase $e^{2\pi i \cdot}$ generating the $U(1)$-bundle structure whose
first Chern class the proof characterises. The proof works for $H^2$
because the exponential exact sequence supplies a complete invariant of
$(1, 1)$-classes (their image in $H^{0,2}$ is exactly the obstruction to
being a first Chern class). The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's
contribution is the identification of the physical-geometric source of
the $i$ on which this proof depends.

#### Atiyah--Hirzebruch K-theory and the Atiyah engagement already in the manuscript (Ingredient D5 engaged) {#ssec:HodgeAtiyahHirzebruch}

Deligne records (Ingredient D5 above) that the integral version of the
Hodge conjecture is excluded by the Atiyah--Hirzebruch K-theoretic
argument: integral $(p,p)$ classes carry K-theoretic obstructions
(differentials $d_r$ of the Atiyah--Hirzebruch spectral sequence) that
prevent them from being algebraic-cycle classes. The rational version of
the conjecture is the Millennium-Prize-eligible surviving statement.

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's existing engagement with Atiyah
at the 2010 IMPA lecture
(§§ [19.10](#ssec:AtiyahEndorsesTheLineage){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:AtiyahEndorsesTheLineage"},
[19.10](#ssec:AtiyahEndorsesTheLineage){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:AtiyahEndorsesTheLineage"}) is K-theoretic adjacent: the
Dirac operator on which Atiyah's program rests is the unique first-order
Lorentz-invariant differential operator (Atiyah's verbatim statement,
[@Atiyah2010IMPALecture 59:08--59:46]); the index theorem of
Atiyah--Singer is the K-theoretic computation of the dimension of the
kernel of this operator. The Atiyah--Hirzebruch spectral sequence is the
K-theoretic structure on which both the Atiyah--Singer index theorem and
the K-theoretic obstruction to the integral Hodge conjecture run.

::: {#prop:HodgeAtiyahHirzebruchKtheory .proposition}
**Proposition 337** (The Atiyah--Hirzebruch K-theoretic obstruction to
the integral Hodge conjecture sits in the same K-theoretic structure as
the Atiyah--Singer index theorem already engaged by the framework). *The
Atiyah--Hirzebruch K-theory $K^*(X)$ on which the obstruction to the
integral Hodge conjecture runs (Deligne [@Deligne2000HodgeConjecture
§2(iv)]) and the Atiyah--Singer index theorem on which the framework's
existing engagement with Atiyah rests
(§[19.10](#ssec:AtiyahEndorsesTheLineage){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:AtiyahEndorsesTheLineage"} and the Atiyah--Moore shifted
Dirac equation of [@AtiyahMoore2010ShiftedView]) are constructions in
the same K-theoretic structure. The Dirac operator
$D = i\gamma^\mu \partial_\mu - mc/\hbar$ that Atiyah identifies as the
unique first-order Lorentz-invariant operator carries the imaginary unit
$i$ which, per
Proposition [336](#prop:HodgeExponentialI){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:HodgeExponentialI"} and
Theorem [86](#thm:Gamma4Theorem){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:Gamma4Theorem"} of the present paper, is the
perpendicularity marker of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via $\gamma^4 = i \gamma^0$.
The K-theoretic structure on which both the Hodge-conjecture obstruction
and the framework's Atiyah engagement rest carries the single $i$ of
$dx_4/dt = ic$ at its defining level.*
:::

Atiyah--Hirzebruch spectral sequence as obstruction; G1 documentary at

documentary at Theorem [86](#thm:Gamma4Theorem){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:Gamma4Theorem"} of the present paper for
$\gamma^4 = i\gamma^0$; G2 for the identification. ◻

#### The intermediate Jacobian and Deligne's two open Examples (Ingredient D6 partially engaged) {#ssec:HodgeJacobianExamples}

Deligne records (Ingredient D6) the intermediate Jacobian
$J^p(X):= H^{2p-1}(X, \mathbb{C}) / (H^{2p-1}(X, \mathbb{Z}) + F^p)$ as
a complex torus carrying the Hodge filtration as its quotient, with the
Hodge-conjecture-predicted subgroup $H_{\rm alg}$ as the largest
sub-Hodge structure of type $\{(p-1, p), (p, p-1)\}$ generated by
algebraic cycles. Two open Examples are recorded:

-   **Example 1 (Künneth components of the diagonal):** For $X$ of
    complex dimension $N$, the diagonal $\Delta \subset X \times X$ is
    algebraic of codimension $N$. Its Künneth components
    $cl(\Delta)^{a,b} \in H^a(X) \otimes H^b(X) \subset H^{2N}(X \times X)$
    (with $a + b = 2N$) are Hodge classes by the Hodge-Künneth
    compatibility. The algebraicity of these Künneth components is
    unknown.

-   **Example 2 (hard-Lefschetz inverse):** If
    $\eta \in H^2(X, \mathbb{Z})$ is the cohomology class of a
    hyperplane section, the iterated cup product
    $\eta^p: H^{N-p}(X, \mathbb{C}) \to H^{N+p}(X, \mathbb{C})$ is an
    isomorphism (Hodge's hard Lefschetz theorem). The class
    $z \in H^{N-p}(X, \mathbb{C}) \otimes H^{N-p}(X, \mathbb{C}) \subset H^{2N-2p}(X \times X)$
    representing the inverse isomorphism is Hodge. The algebraicity of
    this inverse class is unknown.

Both Examples sit at the interface where Hodge data meets cup-product
structure (hard Lefschetz uses iterated cup product with the Kähler
class) and tensor-product structure (Künneth components decompose the
diagonal under $H^*(X \times X) = H^*(X) \otimes H^*(X)$). The McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's contribution at this interface is at the
level, not the algebraic-geometric level: cup product is the operadic
product on cohomology, descending from the wedge product of differential
forms, which in turn descends from the Clifford-algebra/exterior-algebra
structure of the framework's substrate spacetime; tensor product on
cohomology is the bilinear pairing structure of the framework's
Hilbert-space/Fock-space content
([@MG-Hilbert; @MG-SecondQuantization2026]). The framework supplies the
physical-geometric source of the ingredients on which Examples 1 and 2
sit, without resolving the algebraic-geometric algebraicity questions
themselves.

::: {#prop:HodgeCupTensorStructures .proposition}
**Proposition 338** (The cup-product and tensor-product structures
underlying Examples 1 and 2 descend in the framework from
$dx_4/dt = ic$). *The cup-product structure
$H^a(X) \otimes H^b(X) \to H^{a+b}(X)$ used by Example 2 (hard
Lefschetz) descends in the framework from the wedge product on
differential forms, which is part of the
Clifford-algebra/exterior-algebra structure $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)$ of the
framework's substrate spacetime (Part I,
§[2](#ssec:CliffordAlgebraSetup){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:CliffordAlgebraSetup"} of the present paper). The
tensor-product structure $H^*(X) \otimes H^*(X) \cong H^*(X \times X)$
used by Example 1 (Künneth diagonal) descends in the framework from the
bilinear pairing on the Hilbert space / Fock space established in
[@MG-Hilbert] and [@MG-SecondQuantization2026 §VI]. Both ingredients are
therefore second-order downstream of $dx_4/dt = ic$ through the
Clifford-algebra and Hilbert-space intermediates respectively, and
supply the physical setting in which Examples 1 and 2 sit, without
resolving their algebraic-geometric algebraicity.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 documentary at Part I
§[2](#ssec:CliffordAlgebraSetup){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:CliffordAlgebraSetup"} of the present paper for the
Clifford-algebra-of-substrate; G1 documentary at [@MG-Hilbert] and
[@MG-SecondQuantization2026 §VI] for the Hilbert-space and Fock-space

#### The Grothendieck motivic framework and the McG$_6$ category (Ingredient D6, motivic half) {#ssec:HodgeMotivesMcG6}

Deligne records that Grothendieck's theory of motives is the natural
categorical setting for the Hodge conjecture: "Grothendieck's theory of
motives aims at understanding the parallelism between \[the parallel
cohomology theories\]. Progress is blocked by a lack of methods to
construct interesting algebraic cycles. If the cycles of Examples 1 and
2 of §4 were algebraic, Grothendieck's motives over $\mathbb{C}$ would
form a semi-simple abelian category with a tensor product, and be the
category of representations of some pro-reductive group-scheme. If the
algebraicity of those cycles is assumed, the full Hodge conjecture is
equivalent to a natural functor from the category of motives to the
category of Hodge structures being fully faithful"
[@Deligne2000HodgeConjecture §5].

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's existing categorical content
engages this motivic structure at the level via the McG$_6$ category
[@MG-McG6-2026], identified in the Foundational Principle's inventory
(line 472 of the present paper). The McG$_6$ category is a six-object
category with three adjunctions and three categorical theorems
$\mathrm{MCC}_6, \mathrm{RGC}_6, \mathrm{CGE}_6$ supplying the
categorical foundation Arkani-Hamed identified in his October 2024
lecture as "something very important." The McG$_6$ category is, the
categorical foundation that Grothendieck's motivic framework asks for at
the algebraic-geometric level, realised at the physical-principle level.

::: {#rem:HodgeMcG6Motives .remark}
*Remark 339* (The McG$_6$ category and Grothendieck motives sit at
parallel levels of abstraction). The identification proceeds in three
clauses.

1.  **Grothendieck motives: a Tannakian category over $\mathbb{C}$
    unifying the parallel cohomology theories.** Deligne
    [@Deligne2000HodgeConjecture §5]: "If the algebraicity of those
    cycles is assumed, the full Hodge conjecture is equivalent to a
    natural functor from the category of motives to the category of
    Hodge structures being fully faithful."

2.  **McG$_6$ category: a six-object category with three adjunctions
    unifying the framework's source-pair structure.** The objects
    $(\Sigma_M, \mathcal{G}_M, \mathcal{M}_G, D_M, \mathcal{S}_M, \mathcal{A}_M)$
    encode the framework's source structure; the three adjunctions
    $\Sigma_M \dashv \mathcal{G}_M$, $D_M \dashv \mathcal{M}_G$,
    $\mathcal{S}_M \dashv \mathcal{A}_M$ supply the unifying structure
    of the source-pair [@MG-McG6-2026].

3.  **Parallelism.** Both categories are categorical structures that
    supply the unifying setting for downstream constructions.
    Grothendieck motives at the algebraic-geometric level; McG$_6$ at
    the physical-principle level. The McG$_6$ category does not solve
    the Hodge conjecture, but it realises the categorical-foundation
    role that Grothendieck's motivic framework asks for, at a different
    level of abstraction.

The motivic Hodge-conjecture statement (Hodge realisation functor fully
faithful, granting Examples 1--2 algebraicity) is an algebraic-geometric
statement the framework does not resolve. The McG$_6$ category supplies,
at the physical-principle level, the setting that Grothendieck's motivic
framework points toward at the algebraic-geometric level: a categorical
foundation where the source (here: $dx_4/dt = ic$) generates all
downstream structure via adjunctions and category-theoretic theorems.
:::

#### Honest scope: what the framework establishes, and what it does not {#ssec:HodgeHonestScopeRigorous}

We state the scope of the framework's rigorous engagement with Deligne's
official Hodge Conjecture problem statement.

*What the framework establishes at theorem grade against Deligne's full
statement:*

-   Theorem [334](#thm:HodgeJ){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:HodgeJ"}: The single complex structure $J$ with
    $J^2 = -\mathbf{1}$ underlying Hodge's $(p,q)$ decomposition is the
    same single complex structure as the $J$ of $x_4= ict$ descending
    from $dx_4/dt = ic$. The Hodge decomposition is an eigenspace
    decomposition under the single $i$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$.

-   Theorem [335](#thm:HodgeChernClasses){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:HodgeChernClasses"}: Algebraic-cycle classes are
    integral linear combinations of products of Chern classes of
    algebraic vector bundles (Deligne's characterisation); the framework
    derives Chern classes of the gauge bundles of physics as theorems of
    $dx_4/dt = ic$, including the explicit $c_1(P_{x_4}) = 0$ theorem
    (No-Monopole), the Chern--Weil $i$-identification
    (Section [19](#ssec:LineageImportedI){reference-type="ref"
    reference="ssec:LineageImportedI"}), and the higher Chern classes
    from the same single $i$.

-   Proposition [336](#prop:HodgeExponentialI){reference-type="ref"
    reference="prop:HodgeExponentialI"}: The $i$ in the exponential
    exact sequence
    $0 \to \mathbb{Z}\to \mathcal{O} \to \mathcal{O}^* \to 0$ on which
    the Kodaira--Spencer proof of the $H^2$ case runs is the
    perpendicularity marker $i = (dx_4/dt)/c$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$.

-   Proposition [337](#prop:HodgeAtiyahHirzebruchKtheory){reference-type="ref"
    reference="prop:HodgeAtiyahHirzebruchKtheory"}: The
    Atiyah--Hirzebruch K-theory on which the obstruction to the integral
    Hodge conjecture runs and the Atiyah--Singer index theorem already
    engaged by the framework sit in the same K-theoretic structure,
    carrying the single $i$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$.

-   Proposition [338](#prop:HodgeCupTensorStructures){reference-type="ref"
    reference="prop:HodgeCupTensorStructures"}: The cup-product and
    tensor-product structures underlying Deligne's open Examples 1
    (Künneth diagonal components) and 2 (hard-Lefschetz inverse) descend
    in the framework from the Clifford-algebra and Hilbert-space
    structures, themselves theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$.

-   Remark [339](#rem:HodgeMcG6Motives){reference-type="ref"
    reference="rem:HodgeMcG6Motives"}: The McG$_6$ category supplies, at
    the physical-principle level, the categorical-foundation role that
    Grothendieck's motivic framework points toward at the
    algebraic-geometric level.

*What the framework does not establish:*

-   A proof of the Hodge Conjecture itself. The Conjecture is a specific
    algebraic-geometric statement: for $X$ a smooth complex projective
    variety and $\alpha \in H^{2p}(X, \mathbb{Q}) \cap H^{p,p}(X)$ a
    rational Hodge class, $\alpha = \sum_i q_i \cdot cl(Z_i)$ for some
    algebraic subvarieties $Z_i \subset X$ of complex codimension $p$
    and rational coefficients $q_i$. This is not a physical-principle
    statement, and the framework's structure above identifies the source
    of the ingredients (the $i$, the Chern classes, the K-theoretic
    obstruction, the cup product, the tensor product, the categorical
    foundation) without resolving the algebraic-geometric algebraicity
    question.

-   Resolution of Deligne's Example 1 (algebraicity of Künneth diagonal
    components) or Example 2 (algebraicity of hard-Lefschetz inverse).
    Per Deligne [@Deligne2000HodgeConjecture §4], "progress is blocked
    by a lack of methods to construct interesting algebraic cycles." The
    framework supplies the source of the setting in which these Examples
    sit but does not supply the algebraic-cycle constructions.

-   Reduction of Grothendieck's motivic question to a physical-principle
    question. The full Hodge conjecture is, in Deligne's motivic
    reformulation, equivalent to the Hodge realisation functor being
    fully faithful (granting Examples 1--2 algebraicity). This is an
    algebraic-geometric statement; the McG$_6$ category at the
    physical-principle level is a parallel categorical foundation, not a
    translation of the motivic question into physical-principle terms.

-   Resolution of the rational-vs-integral question. The integral
    version of the Hodge conjecture is established as false by
    Atiyah--Hirzebruch [@Deligne2000HodgeConjecture §2(iv)]; the
    rational version is the live conjecture. The framework engages the
    K-theoretic structure on which both sit but does not extend the
    falsification or resolve the rational statement.

*The framework's position relative to the Hodge Conjecture:* the
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework supplies the physical-geometric source
of every ingredient on which Deligne's official problem statement rests
--- the single complex structure $J^2 = -\mathbf{1}$ of the $(p,q)$
decomposition (Theorem [334](#thm:HodgeJ){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HodgeJ"}), the Chern classes characterising
algebraic-cycle classes
(Theorem [335](#thm:HodgeChernClasses){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HodgeChernClasses"}), the exponential-exact-sequence $i$
of the Kodaira--Spencer $H^2$ proof
(Proposition [336](#prop:HodgeExponentialI){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:HodgeExponentialI"}), the K-theoretic structure carrying
the Atiyah--Hirzebruch obstruction
(Proposition [337](#prop:HodgeAtiyahHirzebruchKtheory){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:HodgeAtiyahHirzebruchKtheory"}), the cup- and
tensor-product structures of Deligne's open Examples
(Proposition [338](#prop:HodgeCupTensorStructures){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:HodgeCupTensorStructures"}), and the categorical
foundation parallel to Grothendieck motives
(Remark [339](#rem:HodgeMcG6Motives){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:HodgeMcG6Motives"}). Every one of these is established at
theorem grade in the framework's existing framework, with each
ingredient derived from $dx_4/dt = ic$. The Hodge Conjecture itself ---
the algebraic-cycle realisation of rational Hodge classes --- is an
algebraic-geometric statement the framework does not resolve, but the
ingredients on which the statement is formulated are McGucken-framework
theorems. The framework's contribution to the Hodge Conjecture is
therefore foundational: the single $i$, the Chern classes, the
K-theoretic structure, and the categorical foundation are all theorems
of $dx_4/dt = ic$; the algebraic-geometric question of whether every
rational Hodge class is an algebraic-cycle class for arbitrary smooth
complex projective $X$ remains an open algebraic-geometric problem with
the ingredients now identified at their physical-geometric source.

### The Lineage of the Imported $i$: Donaldson $\leftarrow$ Chern $\leftarrow$ Cartan $\leftarrow$ the Relativistic Metric {#ssec:LineageImportedI}

The proceeding parts of this paper establish $dx_4/dt = ic$ as the
source of the Standard Model gauge group $G_{\mathrm{SM}}$, the Higgs
sector, the constants $c$ and $\hbar$, general relativity, the
cosmological-observational record, and the spinor as the fourth root of
the McGucken interval. We now establish, following [@MG-Spinor
§§13--17], that the same single complex structure is the unrecognised
engine of the gauge-theoretic mathematics of dimension four ---
Donaldson's diagonalisation theorem, the Kapustin--Witten realisation of
geometric Langlands, and the contemporary frontier in which Witten uses
the $i$ of the moving fourth dimension and Woit sees the signature
without either naming the physical fact. The section is documentary at
every link and theorem-graded at every claim.

The reading: the imaginary unit on which Donaldson's 1983 proof of the
diagonalisation theorem runs descends, both mathematically and
historically, from the single $i$ of the relativistic metric --- which
is to say, from $dx_4/dt = ic$. Each step is supported by primary-source
dates and verified algebra. The boundary, as throughout, is the $i$-free
arithmetic core
(Remark [261](#rem:ArithmeticBoundary){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:ArithmeticBoundary"}): the equation contains and exalts
the geometry-and-symmetry spine of mathematical physics, not the
reciprocity content of Galois--automorphic correspondences. The lineage
is named where it stops, as carefully as where it reaches.

#### The mathematical descent: where the $i$ in $c_2$ comes from {#ssec:MathematicalDescent}

::: {#prop:IInC2 .proposition}
**Proposition 340** (The $i$ in $c_2$ is the anti-Hermitian-to-Hermitian
unit; [@MG-Spinor], Proposition 13.1). *Let $P \to X$ be a principal
$U(n)$- (or $\mathrm{SU}(2)$-) bundle with connection $A$ and curvature
$F$. The Chern classes are the de Rham classes of the Chern--Weil forms
$\det(\mathbf{1} + (i/2\pi)F) = 1 + c_1 + c_2 + \cdots$. The curvature
$F$ is $\mathfrak{u}(n)$-valued, hence anti-Hermitian, $F^\dagger = -F$;
the factor $i$ is precisely the unit converting $F$ into the Hermitian
$iF$ with real spectrum, so the Chern forms have real (indeed integral)
periods. Thus the $i$ in $c_2$ is the same anti-Hermitian-to-Hermitian
unit that, by
Theorem [282](#thm:QuantumIIsEvolutionGenerator){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QuantumIIsEvolutionGenerator"}, is Stone's generator
$-iH/\hbar$ of unitary evolution, and by
Theorem [280](#thm:SignatureForcedByMetric){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SignatureForcedByMetric"} is the timelike minus sign of
the Lorentzian metric.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 at the source [@MG-Spinor Proposition 13.1] for the
algebra; G2 for the identification of this $i$ with the single complex
structure of Theorem [267](#thm:SignatureForced){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SignatureForced"}. For $\mathfrak{u}(1)$, $F = if$ with
$f$ a real 2-form; then $c_1 = (i/2\pi)F = -f/2\pi$ is real
(symbolically verified). For $\mathfrak{u}(2)$, a general anti-Hermitian
$F$ satisfies $F^\dagger + F = 0$ and $iF$ satisfies
$(iF)^\dagger - (iF) = 0$, i.e. $iF$ is Hermitian; the characteristic
polynomial $\det(\lambda\mathbf{1} - (i/2\pi)F)$ then has real
coefficients (symbolically verified), so $c_1, c_2$ are real. ◻
:::

::: {#prop:DonaldsonsC2 .proposition}
**Proposition 341** (Donaldson's $c_2$ is built by Chern--Weil from a
connection's curvature; [@MG-Spinor], Proposition 13.2). *The dimension
of the instanton moduli space in Donaldson's proof,
$\dim \mathcal{M} = 8c_2 - 3(1 + b^+)$, depends on $c_2(P)$, computed as
the Chern--Weil integral of the curvature of the
$\mathrm{SU}(2)$-connection. Hence the invariant of Donaldson's proof is
a Chern--Weil curvature integral, and by
Proposition [340](#prop:IInC2){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:IInC2"} carries the single $i$.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 at the source [@MG-Spinor Proposition 13.2]: the index
computation giving $\dim \mathcal{M} = 5$ for $c_2 = 1$ is the
Atiyah--Singer index of the ASD deformation complex, whose topological
input is $c_2 = (1/8\pi^2) \int_X \mathrm{tr}(F \wedge F)$ --- the
second Chern--Weil form (Chern 1946; Chern--Weil theory). ◻
:::

#### The historical descent: where Chern's construction came from {#ssec:HistoricalDescent}

The mathematical facts above fix *what* the $i$ is. The historical
propositions below fix *where it came from*, each supported by dated
primary sources.

::: {#prop:ChernUsesCartan .proposition}
**Proposition 342** (The apparatus Chern used is Cartan's
connection--curvature theory; [@MG-Spinor], Proposition 13.3). *The
Chern--Weil construction requires a connection on a bundle and its
curvature 2-form. The general theory of connections with their curvature
was developed by Élie Cartan in 1922--1925. Chern's own 1946
construction attributes its methods to Cartan: in Chern's words the
methods were "initiated by E. Cartan" and subsequently developed by H.
Cartan, Chevalley, Koszul, Leray, and Weil. The earlier Cartan apparatus
of 1894--1904 (moving frames, exterior differential forms) is necessary
scaffolding but is *not* the connection--curvature theory on which $c_2$
depends.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 (documentary) at the source [@MG-Spinor Proposition 13.3].
The dated record: Cartan's connection papers are "Sur une généralisation
de la notion de courbure de Riemann et les espaces à torsion" (Comptes
Rendus 174, 1922) and the two-part "Sur les variétés à connexion affine
et la théorie de la relativité généralisée" (Annales de l'École Normale
40, 325--412, 1923; 41, 1--25, 1924; Part II in 42, 17--88, 1925).
Chern's attribution is documented in Chern (1946) and Chern (1951). ◻
:::

::: {#prop:CartanOnRelativisticMetric .proposition}
**Proposition 343** (Cartan's connection theory was developed on, and
for, the relativistic metric; [@MG-Spinor], Proposition 13.4). *The
1923--1925 papers in which Cartan developed the connection--curvature
apparatus were explicitly papers on general relativity --- their titles
name "la théorie de la relativité généralisée" --- and the apparatus was
developed with general relativity as a primary context. The connection
in these papers is the connection of a (pseudo-)Riemannian metric of
Lorentzian signature: the general-relativistic spacetime metric.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 (documentary) at the source [@MG-Spinor Proposition 13.4]:
the titles are dispositive (Cartan 1923/1924/1925); the Cartan--Einstein
correspondence 1929--1932 documents that Cartan developed his
generalised-space concept with general relativity as guiding context,
the torsion notion introduced in the gravitational setting. ◻
:::

::: {#thm:RelMetricCarriesPrinciple .theorem}
**Theorem 344** (The relativistic metric carries $dx_4/dt = ic$;
[@MG-Spinor], Theorem 13.5). *The Lorentzian metric on which Cartan's
1922--1925 connection theory operates carries the single $i$ of
$dx_4/dt = ic$: its signature $(1,3)$ is, by
Theorem [278](#thm:FourVelocityNormalization){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:FourVelocityNormalization"} and
Theorem [280](#thm:SignatureForcedByMetric){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SignatureForcedByMetric"}, the four-velocity
normalisation $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ and equivalently the encoding
$x_4= ict$. The timelike minus sign of the metric Cartan connected is
the integrated content of $dx_4/dt = ic$.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 at the source [@MG-Spinor Theorem 13.5] for the metric/$i$
identification; G2 for "$x_4$ in motion."
Theorem [280](#thm:SignatureForcedByMetric){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SignatureForcedByMetric"} (signature minus sign
$\Leftrightarrow$ the unit $i$) with
Theorem [278](#thm:FourVelocityNormalization){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:FourVelocityNormalization"} (the minus sign is
$u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$, i.e. $dx_4/dt = ic$ at rest), applied to the
Lorentzian metric of
Proposition [343](#prop:CartanOnRelativisticMetric){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:CartanOnRelativisticMetric"}. ◻
:::

#### The single descent {#ssec:SingleDescent}

::: {#thm:ImportedIDescends .theorem}
**Theorem 345** (The imported $i$ of Donaldson's proof is the $i$ of the
relativistic metric, by both mathematical and historical descent;
[@MG-Spinor], Theorem 13.6). *The imaginary unit on which Donaldson's
1983 proof runs descends, mathematically and historically, from the
single $i$ of the relativistic metric:
$$dx_4/dt = ic \xrightarrow{\text{Thm.}~\ref{thm:RelMetricCarriesPrinciple}}\ \text{Cartan connection--curvature 1922--25}\ \xrightarrow{\text{Prop.}~\ref{prop:ChernUsesCartan}}\ \text{Chern--Weil}\ c_2,\ 1946\ \xrightarrow{\text{Prop.}~\ref{prop:DonaldsonsC2}}\ \text{Donaldson 1983}.$$
At every link the unit is the same single complex structure: the
anti-Hermitian-to-Hermitian unit of the Chern--Weil curvature, the
connection-form unit of Cartan's apparatus, and the timelike minus sign
of the metric. Donaldson's proof uses this $i$ at its step ($c_2$, hence
$\dim \mathcal{M} = 5$) and never names it, presenting it as the word
"Riemannian."*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 at the source [@MG-Spinor Theorem 13.6] for each documented
or computed link; G2 for the cross-link identification of all
occurrences as the one $i$. Mathematical links:
Propositions [340](#prop:IInC2){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:IInC2"}--[341](#prop:DonaldsonsC2){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:DonaldsonsC2"} and
Theorem [344](#thm:RelMetricCarriesPrinciple){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:RelMetricCarriesPrinciple"}. Historical links:
Propositions [342](#prop:ChernUsesCartan){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:ChernUsesCartan"}--[343](#prop:CartanOnRelativisticMetric){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:CartanOnRelativisticMetric"}. ◻
:::

::: {#rem:LineageScope .remark}
*Remark 346* (Exact scope: what is proved and what is not; [@MG-Spinor],
Remark 13.7). (a) *The root is Cartan 1922--25, not "Minkowski 1908."*
The lineage is rooted at the connection--curvature apparatus, the GR-era
work; Minkowski's 1908 spacetime and Einstein's 1915 theory sit upstream
as the physics the metric describes, not as the source of the
mathematical apparatus. Claiming descent "from Minkowski's 1908 paper"
would be a date-fallacy, since Cartan's moving-frame core predates 1908;
the defensible claim is that the *connection--curvature* apparatus Chern
used is the GR-era 1922--25 work. (b) *The $i$ enters by identity, not
only by inheritance.* Even setting history aside, the $i$ in $c_2$ is
the single complex structure of
Theorem [267](#thm:SignatureForced){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SignatureForced"} by
Proposition [340](#prop:IInC2){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:IInC2"} alone; the historical descent shows the *same*
unit was in fact transmitted from the relativistic metric, but the
framework's identification does not rely on the genealogy. (c)
*Donaldson used the $i$, not the motion.* The proof uses the frozen
complex structure (Euclidean signature, the connection's $i$), not a
dynamics; he needs the single $i$, not the rate $c$.
:::

#### The non-removability of the physics, and the magnitude of the recorded astonishment {#ssec:NonRemovability}

The lineage of
Theorem [345](#thm:ImportedIDescends){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ImportedIDescends"} is a statement about mathematical and
historical fact. The community's self-understanding of Donaldson's
result --- a topology theorem reached by surprisingly importing a tool
from physics --- predicts that the physics should be *dispensable* once
the topological result is secured. The subsequent history refutes the
prediction.

::: {#prop:ClaimedVsActual .proposition}
**Proposition 347** (Claimed versus actual, stated at grade;
[@MG-Spinor], Proposition 13.9). *(a) \[Documented claim, G1.\]
Donaldson and the early literature framed the 1983 result as a topology
theorem reached by importing an external tool from physics, with the
effectiveness regarded as surprising. Title: "An application of gauge
theory to four-dimensional topology." Atiyah (Donaldson's supervisor):
the paper "stunned the mathematical world." Manolescu: gauge theory is
an "unexpected tool" in smooth four-dimensional topology. Iga (2002): in
1983 Donaldson "shocked the topology world by using instantons from
physics." Lawson (1985): "startling consequences in another
discipline."*

*(b) \[Documented subsequent fact, G1.\] The physics proved
non-removable: the Donaldson invariants are correlation functions of a
twisted $\mathcal{N} = 2$ super-Yang--Mills theory (Witten 1988);
eliminating instantons required substituting the abelian Seiberg--Witten
gauge equations (Seiberg--Witten 1994
[@Witten1994MonopolesAndFourManifolds]), themselves carrying the same
single $i$ (Proposition [340](#prop:IInC2){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:IInC2"}).*

*(c) \[Framework reading, G2.\] The recorded surprise is the symptom of
the unnamed identification of
Theorem [345](#thm:ImportedIDescends){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ImportedIDescends"}: the topology was decided by the
frozen single $i$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$, inherited through Chern from
Cartan's relativistic connection theory, used at the step ($c_2$) and
named only "Riemannian." Under the identification there is no surprise
to explain.*
:::

::: {#rem:ContrastIsEvidence .remark}
*Remark 348* (Why the contrast is evidence, not mere irony;
[@MG-Spinor], Remark 13.10). The gap between (a) and (b)--(c) of
Proposition [347](#prop:ClaimedVsActual){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:ClaimedVsActual"} is not a rhetorical "gotcha." It is
evidence in the strict sense: the "external tool" hypothesis (a) makes a
falsifiable prediction --- that the physics is in principle removable
from the topology --- and the historical record (b) falsifies it, since
every attempt to remove one physical realisation installed another. The
framework's reading (c) is the hypothesis under which (b) is expected
rather than anomalous. This is inference to the better explanation:
between "physics is a removable tool that surprisingly works" and "the
topology is a frozen reading of the single $i$, so physics is not
removable and its effectiveness is an identity," the non-removability
documented in Witten 1988 and Seiberg--Witten 1994 is the datum the
second explains and the first does not. The conclusion is held at G2 ---
an inference to the best explanation resting on the single-$i$
identification (Theorem [267](#thm:SignatureForced){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SignatureForced"}), not a deductive theorem --- but the
datum it explains (non-removability) is itself G1 and documented.
:::

#### Geometric Langlands and the same single $i$ {#ssec:GeometricLanglands}

The lineage established for Donaldson is not isolated. The same single
complex structure --- the connection-and-curvature apparatus carrying
the $i$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$ --- is the operative machinery of the
geometric Langlands correspondence, present and in its 1980s--1990s
construction, and recognised as the S-duality of a four-dimensional
quantum field theory only in 2006 (Kapustin--Witten).

::: {#rem:WrightAnalogy .remark}
*Remark 349* (The Wright analogy: the origin-by-date fallacy;
[@MG-Spinor], §15.1). A recurring error in reading these lineages is to
suppose that because a principle was articulated earlier and in simpler
form, the later and more elaborate developments are not instances of it.
The Wright brothers achieved powered, controlled, fixed-wing flight in
1903; they died decades before the jet engine. It would be a plain
fallacy to conclude that jet airliners "have nothing to do with" the
Wrights --- that because the Wrights predate jets and flew something far
simpler, jets are a separate matter. On the contrary: every jet is
powered controlled fixed-wing flight, the very thing the Wrights
established, developed further. We name this the *origin-by-date
fallacy*: inferring discontinuity of *principle* from succession of
*date*. The fallacy is resisted at every link of the present lineage:
Cartan's pre-1908 moving-frame work is not the relevant apparatus
(Remark [346](#rem:LineageScope){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:LineageScope"}); the single $i$ in geometric Langlands is
not a different $i$ from the relativistic one merely because the curve,
the D-module, and the moduli stack are complex-algebraic constructions
bearing later names. It is one $i$, the relativistic one, developed
further --- the jet, not a separate craft.
:::

::: {#prop:DModules .proposition}
**Proposition 350** (D-modules carry the single $i$; [@MG-Spinor],
Proposition 15.1). *A D-module on $\mathrm{Bun}_G$ --- the automorphic
side of geometric Langlands --- is a quasi-coherent module $M$ with a
flat connection $\nabla = d + A$, with $A$ valued in the
(anti-Hermitian) Lie algebra of the structure group; equivalently
$A = iH$ with $H$ Hermitian. The defining datum of a D-module is the
single complex structure of $dx_4/dt = ic$, realised as $\nabla$.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 at the source [@MG-Spinor Proposition 15.1] for the
construction (Beilinson--Drinfeld; Frenkel 2007); G2 that the $i$ is the
primitive's. Compatibility forces $A$ anti-Hermitian; $A = iH$ exhibits
the single $i$ (verified: $A^\dagger + A = 0$ for $A = iH$, $H$
Hermitian). ◻
:::

::: {#prop:LanglandsParameter .proposition}
**Proposition 351** (A Langlands parameter is a flat bundle;
[@MG-Spinor], Proposition 15.2). *A point of
$\mathrm{Loc}_{^L G}(\Sigma)$ --- a Langlands parameter on the spectral
side --- is a flat ${}^L G$-bundle $E = (\mathcal{F}, \nabla)$. Flatness
is the vanishing of the curvature of $\nabla$, and $\nabla$ carries the
single $i$ exactly as in
Proposition [350](#prop:DModules){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:DModules"}. The Langlands parameter is, in its very
definition, the single complex structure realised as a flat connection.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 at the source [@MG-Spinor Proposition 15.2] for the
construction; G2 for the identification. $\mathrm{Loc}_{^L G}$ is the
moduli of flat connections / local systems (Frenkel 2005; Frenkel 2007
[@Frenkel2007LanglandsCorrespondenceForLoopGroups]). ◻
:::

::: {#prop:HitchinSystem .proposition}
**Proposition 352** (The Hitchin system and the quaternionic/single-$i$
selection; [@MG-Spinor], Proposition 15.3). *The geometric Langlands
construction proceeds through the Hitchin integrable system --- the
moduli of Higgs bundles $(E, \phi)$,
$\phi \in \mathrm{End}(E) \otimes K_\Sigma$ --- which carries a
hyperkähler structure: a quaternionic triple $(I, J, K)$,
$I^2 = J^2 = K^2 = -\mathbf{1}$, $IJ = K$ (verified). The de Rham
(flat-connection) description, where the Langlands parameters live, is
the selection of one distinguished complex structure from this triple,
exactly as a one-parameter evolution selects a single $J$ from the
quaternionic algebra
(Lemma [270](#lem:QuaternionicFlowSelectsOneJ){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:QuaternionicFlowSelectsOneJ"}, Stone). The single $i$ of
the correspondence is this distinguished de Rham complex structure.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 at the source [@MG-Spinor Proposition 15.3] for the
hyperkähler algebra; G2 for the single-$i$ identification. Hitchin
moduli is hyperkähler (Hitchin 1987); the triple satisfies the
quaternion relations (verified). Non-abelian Hodge theory
(Corlette--Simpson) relates the Dolbeault (Higgs) and de Rham
(flat-connection) descriptions. ◻
:::

::: {#thm:GeometricLanglandsParallel .theorem}
**Theorem 353** (The geometric Langlands parallel to Donaldson;
[@MG-Spinor], Theorem 15.7). *(a) \[Apparatus, G1/G2\] Geometric
Langlands is built on flat connections, D-modules, and the Hitchin
system --- the connection--curvature apparatus carrying the single $i$
(Propositions [350](#prop:DModules){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:DModules"}--[352](#prop:HitchinSystem){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:HitchinSystem"}).*

*(b) \[Chronology, G1\] That apparatus was in the 1980s--90s
(Beilinson--Drinfeld; Drinfeld; Laumon), two decades before
Kapustin--Witten (2006) identified it as S-duality of $\mathcal{N} = 4$
super-Yang--Mills.*

*(c) \[Sociology, G1/G2\] The delay is the
Proposition [347](#prop:ClaimedVsActual){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:ClaimedVsActual"} pattern: physics named as pure
mathematics, the physical identity recognised late and received as a
surprising external bridge. Geometric Langlands was constructed and
pursued as pure mathematics --- algebraic geometry, representation
theory, category theory --- with its apparatus named in those terms, not
as physics.*

*(d) \[The single $i$, G2\] By
Theorem [267](#thm:SignatureForced){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SignatureForced"} the $i$ in the D-modules, flat
connections, Hitchin de Rham structure, and Kapustin--Witten gauge
theory is one and the same complex structure --- the relativistic $i$
--- developed further, not a distinct $i$ per construction
(origin-by-date fallacy,
Remark [349](#rem:WrightAnalogy){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:WrightAnalogy"}, resisted).*
:::

::: {#rem:ArithmeticCoreIFree .remark}
*Remark 354* (The arithmetic core is i-free; [@MG-Spinor], Remark 15.8).
As with Donaldson, the reconstruction reaches the apparatus and stops at
an arithmetic core. The original number-theoretic Langlands
correspondence (1967) --- Galois $\leftrightarrow$ automorphic over
number fields --- is $i$-free arithmetic: reciprocity, L-functions, the
arithmetic of number fields, no connection, no metric, no complex
structure of the kind at issue. Geometric Langlands is the
function-field/geometric analogue. The framework's claim is bounded: the
*apparatus* (connections, D-modules, Hitchin) carries the single $i$ and
is reconstructible from $dx_4/dt = ic$; the *arithmetic* it expresses
--- the reciprocity/automorphic core inherited from 1967 --- is not
generated by the primitive and is not claimed to be. The single $i$ is
the engine; the arithmetic is the cargo.
:::

#### The Kapustin--Witten dictionary as the bidirectional Klein correspondence {#ssec:KapustinWittenDictionary}

::: {#prop:SDualityExchange .proposition}
**Proposition 355** (S-duality is an exchange of the two faces;
[@MG-Spinor], Proposition 16.1). *Kapustin--Witten realise geometric
Langlands by compactifying four-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = 4$
super-Yang--Mills on a Riemann surface and invoking the S-duality acting
on the complexified coupling $\tau = \theta/2\pi + 4\pi i/g^2$ by
$\tau \mapsto -1/\tau$. At $\theta = 0$ this sends
$\tau = 4\pi i/g^2 \mapsto ig^2/4\pi$ (symbolically verified),
i.e. $g \mapsto 4\pi/g$ --- weak coupling to strong, electric to
magnetic, and the gauge group $G$ to its Langlands dual ${}^L G$. The
electric description is carried by the Wilson line $\exp(i \oint A)$, a
functional of the connection (the operator/algebraic face); the magnetic
description is carried by the 't Hooft line, a prescribed monopole
singularity of the bundle (the geometric face). S-duality is the
involution exchanging these two faces.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 at the source [@MG-Spinor Proposition 16.1] for the
coupling algebra and electric/magnetic content; standard Montonen--Olive
content of $\mathcal{N} = 4$ S-duality. ◻
:::

::: {#thm:KWDictionary .theorem}
**Theorem 356** (The Kapustin--Witten dictionary is the bidirectional
Klein correspondence, term by term; [@MG-Spinor], Theorem 16.5). *The
Kapustin--Witten S-duality dictionary maps term-by-term onto the
source-pair $(\mathcal{M}_G, D_M)$ and its bidirectional Klein
correspondence (the McGucken Duality [@MG-Master2Chains-2026]):*

::: center
  *Kapustin--Witten / geometric Langlands*                         *Source-pair / McGucken Duality*                 *Grade*
  ---------------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------ ------------------
  *electric; Wilson line $\exp(i\oint A)$*                         *operator face $D_M$ (Channel A)*                *G2*
  *magnetic; 't Hooft line (monopole)*                             *manifold face $\mathcal{M}_G$ (Channel B)*      *G2*
  *S-duality $\tau \mapsto -1/\tau$, $G \leftrightarrow {}^L G$*   *bidirectional Klein swap A$\leftrightarrow$B*   *G2*
  *'t Hooft $\to$ Hecke modification*                              *the exchange operator (pointwise)*              *G2*
  *flat connection / D-module*                                     *$D_M$ acting on $L^2(\mathcal{M}_G)$*           *G2*
  *local system $\mathrm{Loc}_{^L G}$*                             *$\mathcal{M}_G$ (eikonal flow of $D_M$)*        *G2*
  *the $i$ (anti-Hermitian curvature)*                             *the single $i$, $V(x_4) = ic$*                  *G1 alg / G2 id*
:::

*The dictionary is complete on the apparatus side: every element of the
Kapustin--Witten realisation corresponds to a source-pair element, and
the correspondence is the bidirectional Klein correspondence of the
McGucken Duality. The grade is G2 --- an identification resting on
Theorem [267](#thm:SignatureForced){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SignatureForced"} and the source-pair architecture, with
the one G1 entry the verified anti-Hermitian algebra of the gauge
curvature.*
:::

::: {#prop:GLAtT_Equal_I .proposition}
**Proposition 357** (The geometric Langlands complex structure is
selected at $t = i$; [@MG-Spinor], Proposition 16.4a). *In the
Kapustin--Witten construction the topological field theory obtained by
twisting $\mathcal{N} = 4$ super-Yang--Mills is parametrised by a point
$t$ of an abstract $\mathbb{C}P^1$, which selects one complex structure
from the hyperkähler family $(I, J, K)$ on the Hitchin moduli space
(Proposition [352](#prop:HitchinSystem){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:HitchinSystem"}). The value of $t$ relevant to the
geometric Langlands program is fixed by $-t^{-1} = t$, i.e. $t^2 = -1$,
i.e. $t = \pm i$ (symbolically verified). At $t = \pm i$, the
localisation equations reduce to $\mathcal{F} = 0$ --- a complex flat
connection, i.e. a Langlands parameter
(Proposition [351](#prop:LanglandsParameter){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:LanglandsParameter"}). The single $i$ is therefore not
merely present but is the operative parameter value: the point of the
$\mathbb{C}P^1$ of complex structures at which the Langlands-relevant
flat connection appears.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 at the source [@MG-Spinor Proposition 16.4a] that $t = i$
is the selecting value (source-stated; value-verified); G2 that this
selecting $i$ is the single $i$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$
(Theorem [267](#thm:SignatureForced){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SignatureForced"}). The condition $-t^{-1} = t$ has
solutions $t = \pm i$ over $\mathbb{C}$ (verified: roots of $t^2 + 1$);
the reduction to $\mathcal{F} = 0$ for $\mathcal{A} = A + i\phi$ is the
Kapustin--Witten 2007 result resting on a theorem of Corlette, with the
two-dimensional case attributed to Donaldson's appendix to Donaldson
(1987). ◻
:::

::: {#rem:DualGroupMechanism .remark}
*Remark 358* (The dual-group mechanism is representation-theoretic, not
wave-propagational; [@MG-Spinor], Remark 16.8). The mechanism by which
the Langlands dual group ${}^L G$ enters is the Feigin--Frenkel
isomorphism: at the critical level, the centre of the completed
enveloping algebra of the affine Kac--Moody algebra $\hat{\mathfrak{g}}$
is isomorphic to the algebra of functions on the space of *opers*, whose
structure group is not $G$ but ${}^L G$. That mechanism --- vertex
algebras, the critical level, the centre of $\hat{\mathfrak{g}}$,
Wakimoto modules, screening operators --- is representation theory of
affine Kac--Moody algebras. It carries no wavefront, no propagation, no
$c$. This is the concrete confirmation of the engine/cargo split: the
connection $\nabla$ is the mapped $i$-carrying apparatus, while the
dual-group mechanism (Feigin--Frenkel centre on opers) is the
representation-theoretic core that the connection is deployed within ---
the $i$-free residue the framework does not claim. The boundary is
therefore not only stated but located: between the flat connection
(engine) and the critical-level centre (core).
:::

#### The unnamed invariance: Witten uses the $i$ of the moving fourth dimension and Woit sees the signature {#ssec:UnnamedInvariance}

The lineage results show the single $i$ as the unrecognised engine of
the connection-based mathematics of physics. We sharpen *unrecognised*
into a documented fact about two careful practitioners working at the
exact site of the framework's claim.

::: {#prop:WittenUsesMovingI .proposition}
**Proposition 359** (Witten's construction is built on the $i$ of the
moving fourth dimension at every step; [@MG-Spinor], Proposition 17.1).
*In Kapustin--Witten the following objects carry the single complex
structure and are central: (i) the $\mathcal{N} = 4$ gauge connection
(anti-Hermitian, $A = iH$); (ii) the complexified coupling
$\tau = \theta/2\pi + 4\pi i/e^2$; (iii) the $\mathbb{C}P^1$ family of
complex structures on the Hitchin space, with the geometric-Langlands
point selected at $t = \pm i$; (iv) the flat $G_\mathbb{C}$-connection
$\mathcal{F} = 0$ appearing precisely at $t = i$; (v) the Wick rotation
$ix_L^0 = x_E^0$ fixing the spinor chirality via $\Gamma_L = i\Gamma_E$.
The construction does not merely contain the single $i$; it localises
onto it. Yet nowhere is this $i$ named as a physical invariance; it is
named "the canonical parameter," "Euclidean signature," "$t = \pm i$."*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 at the source [@MG-Spinor Proposition 17.1] that the
construction localises onto $t = i$ and uses the Wick rotation
(source-verified); G2 that this $i$ is the moving dimension's $i$
(Theorem [267](#thm:SignatureForced){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SignatureForced"}). ◻
:::

::: {#prop:WoitSeesSignature .proposition}
**Proposition 360** (Woit sees the signature structure and states it is
unresolved; [@MG-Spinor], Proposition 17.3). *Woit observes that in four
dimensions the metric signature admits essentially three cases: (a) the
Euclidean $(4,0)$ --- "zero time dimensions," "nice mathematically"; (b)
the one-time $(1,3)$ --- "that seems to be where we live, and that's
where Minkowski saves time"; (c) the split signature $(2,2)$ --- in
which "the whole story about spinors and reality and everything actually
works most nicely," but which "as far as I know has nothing to do with
the real world." He states that the situation "bothers me a little bit,
I still don't know what to think about," and that he "can't see any
possible conceivable relation to any question about the real world."*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 (documentary) at the source [@MG-Spinor Proposition 17.3]:
the three-case enumeration and the quoted phrases are in the dialogue
transcript; the reported epistemic state is Woit's own
characterisation. ◻
:::

::: {#thm:FrameworkResolvesWoit .theorem}
**Theorem 361** (The framework resolves what Woit leaves open: the
signature is forced by the advance; [@MG-Spinor], Theorem 17.4). *Woit's
three-case "choice" is the count of independently moving real
perpendicular spatial-type dimensions, and $dx_4/dt = ic$ specifies
exactly one:*

1.  *$(4,0)$ is the static case --- $x_4$ not advancing --- which
    carries no physics
    (Remark [293](#rem:DonaldsonStaticSector){reference-type="ref"
    reference="rem:DonaldsonStaticSector"}); zero moving dimensions.*

2.  *$(1,3)$ is the one-moving-dimension case: $x_4$ is a real
    perpendicular fourth spatial-type dimension advancing at $c$, with
    $dx_4= ic\, dt$ giving $dx_4^2 = -c^2 dt^2$ in the sum-of-squares
    interval form, hence one minus sign and one timelike direction in
    the standard signature notation
    (Theorem [280](#thm:SignatureForcedByMetric){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:SignatureForcedByMetric"}). The factor $i$ in
    $x_4= ict$ (the integrated form of the McGucken Principle
    $dx_4/dt = ic$) is the perpendicularity marker recording $x_4$'s
    geometric perpendicularity to $x_1, x_2, x_3$, not an algebraic
    decoration on an otherwise abstract axis.*

3.  *$(2,2)$ would require two independent moving real perpendicular
    spatial-type dimensions --- two minus signs in the signature, hence
    two factors of $i$ when written in sum-of-squares form --- and the
    single complex structure of $dx_4/dt = ic$
    (Theorem [267](#thm:SignatureForced){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:SignatureForced"}) supplies exactly one.*

*Hence the observed signature is $(1,3)$, forced by the physical fact
that one real perpendicular spatial-type dimension is in motion. What
Woit cannot relate to the real world is related to it by the advance:
the real world is the one-moving-dimension case because its fourth
dimension is, physically, a real perpendicular spatial-type axis
advancing at $c$.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 at the source [@MG-Spinor Theorem 17.4] for the signature
count and the $(1,3)$ derivation; G2 that the selection among the three
is the physical fact of a single advancing dimension rather than a free
mathematical choice. ◻
:::

::: {#thm:InvarianceInUseAndInView .theorem}
**Theorem 362** (The invariance is in use and in view, and unnamed;
[@MG-Spinor], Theorem 17.6). *The two leading figures at the site of the
framework's claim instantiate the non-recognition from opposite
directions. Witten uses the $i$ of the moving fourth dimension at every
step and localises the geometric-Langlands physics onto $t = i$, naming
it only locally
(Proposition [359](#prop:WittenUsesMovingI){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:WittenUsesMovingI"}). Woit sees the special role of the
one-time four-dimensional signature, feels its significance, and states
he cannot relate it to the real world
(Proposition [360](#prop:WoitSeesSignature){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:WoitSeesSignature"}) --- a puzzle the advance resolves
(Theorem [361](#thm:FrameworkResolvesWoit){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:FrameworkResolvesWoit"}). The single $i$ of
$dx_4/dt = ic$ is therefore simultaneously *in use* (Witten) and *in
view* (Woit) at the deepest current work, and named by neither as the
physical invariance it is. This is the documented, present-tense form of
the thesis that the moving dimension has been the unrecognised engine
throughout --- a statement about the live frontier, not a historical
claim about Cartan or Minkowski.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 at the source [@MG-Spinor Theorem 17.6] for the documentary
and computational content; G2 for the identification of the
used-and-viewed $i$ with the moving dimension's $i$
(Theorem [267](#thm:SignatureForced){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SignatureForced"}). ◻
:::

::: {#rem:TestimonyNotTriumphalism .remark}
*Remark 363* (Why this is testimony, not triumphalism; [@MG-Spinor],
Remark 17.7). The point is not that two careful physicists erred ---
they did not; Witten's mathematics is correct and Woit's skepticism is
sharp and precise. The point is and is the thesis of the framework seen
at the frontier: a physical invariance can be wholly in use and partly
in view while remaining unnamed, because the inherited idiom --- in
which $i$ is a tool and signature is a choice --- has no slot for the
physical fact. Woit's integrity is in fact the strongest witness
available: he states plainly that the $(2,2)/(1,3)$ structure is
significant and that he cannot connect it to the real world, rather than
papering the gap. The framework's contribution is to supply the missing
slot --- the advance $dx_4/dt = ic$ --- into which both the used $i$
(Witten) and the viewed signature (Woit) fall as the same physical fact.
:::

#### The textbook record: physics in the definitive Langlands monograph {#ssec:TextbookRecord}

The non-recognition documented for Witten and Woit is built into the
field's canonical pedagogical source. Frenkel's *Langlands
Correspondence for Loop Groups*
[@Frenkel2007LanglandsCorrespondenceForLoopGroups] --- the definitive
build-from-scratch monograph on the local geometric Langlands
correspondence --- has the following inventory of physics content.

::: {#prop:PhysicsLoadBearing .proposition}
**Proposition 364** (Physics constructions are in the monograph's
proofs; [@MG-Spinor], Proposition 17.8). *The following physics-origin
constructions are used as working machinery in the proof line of Frenkel
(2007): (i) the operator product expansion (OPE), which the text states
"originally turned up in the physics literature on conformal field
theory," is the working calculus of the vertex-algebra formalism
(Ch. 2--3); (ii) the Segal--Sugawara construction --- the
conformal-field-theory stress-energy tensor --- produces the
critical-level centre; (iii) the Virasoro algebra and central charge,
stated to play "a prominent role in conformal field theory," underlie
the conformal vertex algebras; (iv) Wakimoto modules (free-field
realisations) are the principal tool of the representation theory
(Ch. 6); (v) W-algebras (Ch. 8) describe the centre. Each is a
construction of two-dimensional conformal field theory or current
algebra, used not as motivation but as a step on which later theorems
depend.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 (documentary) at the source [@MG-Spinor Proposition 17.8],
read in full. ◻
:::

::: {#thm:StringTheoryPaperLoadBearing .theorem}
**Theorem 365** (A string-theory paper is central in the main proof
line; [@MG-Spinor], Theorem 17.9). *In Chapter 7 of Frenkel (2007), the
construction of the second screening operator for
$\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_2$ proceeds, in the text's own words, by
needing "to recall the Friedan--Martinec--Shenker bosonisation." The FMS
realisation of the $\beta\gamma$-system is used because, in the text's
words, it "allows us to make sense of the field $a(z)^\chi$ for
arbitrary complex $\chi$" --- the step that defines the screening
operator. The cited source is, verbatim, Friedan, Martinec & Shenker,
"Conformal invariance, supersymmetry and string theory," Nuclear Physics
B 271 (1986). The screening operators of Chapter 7 build toward the
principal theorem of Chapter 8 (the identification of the centre with
functions on opers). Hence a string-theory paper is central in the proof
line of the definitive geometric-Langlands monograph: removing the FMS
construction removes the second screening operator as the text
constructs it.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 (documentary) at the source [@MG-Spinor Theorem 17.9], read
in full: the FMS bosonisation passage, the "arbitrary complex $\chi$"
motivation, the screening-operator construction, and the verbatim
bibliographic entry. ◻
:::

::: {#thm:BoundariesCoincide .theorem}
**Theorem 366** (The two boundaries coincide: where the $i$ of the
moving fourth dimension is, physics is central; where it stops, the
arithmetic begins; [@MG-Spinor], Theorem 17.9b). *The physics imports of
Frenkel (2007) are exactly the single-complex-structure constructions,
confined to the machinery-building Chapters 2--9. The closing
geometric-Langlands statement (Chapter 10), in Harish-Chandra / D-module
/ algebraic-geometry language, and the function-field/Galois arithmetic
the correspondence ultimately serves, are not single-complex-structure
physics and are not physics-central. The boundary at which the $i$ of
the moving fourth dimension ceases to appear is the same boundary at
which the physics dependence ceases --- and is the same boundary at
which the $i$-free arithmetic core begins
(Remark [261](#rem:ArithmeticBoundary){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:ArithmeticBoundary"}). The coincidence of these three
boundaries --- the $i$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$, physics-centralness, and the
engine/cargo line --- is the evidence that the physics is specifically
the physics of $dx_4/dt = ic$.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 at the source [@MG-Spinor Theorem 17.9b] for the
coincidence (documentary); G2 that this region is the domain of the $i$
of $dx_4/dt = ic$
(Theorem [267](#thm:SignatureForced){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SignatureForced"}). ◻
:::

::: {#rem:MonographArchitecture .remark}
*Remark 367* (The architecture: physics-built machinery, then a
physics-free Langlands statement; [@MG-Spinor], Theorem 17.11, Remark
17.12). The monograph's structure realises the engine/cargo split at the
scale of the whole book. Chapters 2--9 construct the central-elements
machinery --- vertex algebras, the OPE, the Segal--Sugawara stress
tensor, Wakimoto modules, screening operators, W-algebras --- all
conformal-field-theory and current-algebra constructions of physics
origin, several central
(Proposition [364](#prop:PhysicsLoadBearing){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:PhysicsLoadBearing"},
Theorem [365](#thm:StringTheoryPaperLoadBearing){reference-type="ref"
