reference="thm:StringTheoryPaperLoadBearing"}). The geometric Langlands
correspondence proper, in the closing chapter, is then stated in the
language of Harish-Chandra pairs, D-modules, and algebraic geometry,
invoking none of the physics vocabulary directly. Thus the physics is in
the foundation, doing work, and the Langlands statement it supports is
expressed with the physics provenance absorbed. The engine
(physics-built machinery) and the cargo (the algebraic/arithmetic
Langlands statement) are separated by the spine of the book itself.
:::

#### The Higgs Founders Themselves: The $i$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$ Present and Load-Bearing at the Birth of the Mass Mechanism {#ssec:HiggsFoundersUnnamedInvariance}

The non-recognition pattern documented in
§[19.7](#ssec:UnnamedInvariance){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:UnnamedInvariance"} for Witten and Woit at the
contemporary frontier is not confined to the present moment. It is
located, in its most striking form, at the founding moment of the mass
mechanism itself --- in Peter Higgs's 1964 calculation. The Higgs
mechanism --- which the present paper has spent four Parts (I--IV)
deriving as a chain of sixteen theorems from $dx_4/dt = ic$ --- was
discovered in July 1964 by an algebraic-symmetry route that nowhere
named, considered, or treated as physical the moving fourth dimension on
which every step of the calculation rests. This subsection documents the
historical record, identifies the four specific places where
$dx_4/dt = ic$ was operative in Higgs's calculation, and establishes
that the founding case is the cleanest instance of the
unnamed-invariance pattern: the $i$ of the moving fourth dimension was
in use end-to-end, but in view nowhere, because the inherited Channel-A
idiom of postwar QFT had no slot for the physical fact.

The historical claims are documented against primary sources --- Higgs's
own 2013 Nobel lecture [@Higgs2013NobelLectureEvadingGoldstone]; his
original 1964 papers [@Higgs1964PLB; @Higgs1964PRL]; the companion 1964
papers of Englert--Brout [@EnglertBrout1964PRL] and
Guralnik--Hagen--Kibble [@GuralnikHagenKibble1964PRL]; Anderson's 1963
condensed-matter precedent [@Anderson1963PlasmonsGaugeInvarianceMass];
Higgs's 2007 "Prehistory of the Higgs
boson" [@Higgs2007CRPrehistoryOfHiggsBoson].

##### What Higgs was actually doing: a documentary reconstruction {#what-higgs-was-actually-doing-a-documentary-reconstruction .unnumbered}

::: {#prop:HiggsActualResearchQuestion .proposition}
**Proposition 368** (Higgs's actual research question; primary-source
documentary). *Higgs in 1960--1964 was not predicting a new field, not
investigating mass, and not searching for a primitive geometric
structure. He was looking for a loophole in someone else's theorem. The
documentary record establishes:*

1.  ***Higgs's stated 1960 research situation.** In his 2013 Nobel
    lecture [@Higgs2013NobelLectureEvadingGoldstone], Higgs states
    verbatim: "During my first year as a lecturer, I was in search of a
    worthwhile research programme. In the previous four years in London
    I had rather lost my way in particle physics and had become
    interested in quantum gravity." The 1960 starting point is the
    search for a worthwhile programme by a junior lecturer who had
    become interested in quantum gravity.*

2.  ***The 1961 attraction was to spontaneous symmetry breaking, lifted
    from condensed matter by Nambu and Goldstone.** In Higgs's
    words [@Higgs2013NobelLectureEvadingGoldstone]: "Then in 1961, I
    read Nambu's and Goldstone's papers on models of symmetry breaking
    in particle physics based on an analogy with the theory of
    superconductivity. \[\...\] What I found very attractive was the
    concept of a spontaneously broken symmetry, one that is exact in the
    underlying dynamics but appears broken in the observed phenomena as
    a consequence of an asymmetric ground state ('vacuum' in quantum
    field theory)." The attraction is to an algebraic-symmetry concept
    lifted from condensed matter --- the Channel-A direction in the
    dual-channel architecture of the present paper
    [@MG-Master2Chains-2026].*

3.  ***The obstacle was Goldstone's theorem.**
    Goldstone--Salam--Weinberg 1962 [@GoldstoneSalamWeinberg1962] proved
    that "in a manifestly Lorentz-invariant quantum field theory, if
    there is a continuous symmetry under which the Lagrangian is
    invariant, then either the vacuum state is also invariant or there
    must exist spinless particles of zero mass." Higgs: "This theorem
    appeared to put an end to Nambu's
    programme." [@Higgs2013NobelLectureEvadingGoldstone]*

4.  ***The trigger was Walter Gilbert's PRL paper.** Gilbert
    (1964) [@Gilbert1964PRL] argued the Klein--Lee loophole was barred
    by Lorentz invariance. Higgs read it on 16 July 1964 and, by his own
    account, was "upset because it implied that there was no way to
    evade Goldstone's theorem." [@Higgs2013NobelLectureEvadingGoldstone]
    The journal had arrived by sea, a month late.*

5.  ***The discovery was on the weekend of 18--19 July 1964, by appeal
    to Schwinger's Coulomb-gauge precedent.** Higgs verbatim: "Over the
    following weekend I began to recall that I had seen similar apparent
    violations of Lorentz invariance elsewhere, in no less a theory than
    quantum electrodynamics, as formulated by Julian Schwinger. \[\...\]
    During the weekend of 18--19 July it occurred to me that Schwinger's
    way of formulating gauge theories undermined the axioms which had
    been used to prove the Goldstone theorem. So gauge theories might
    save Nambu's programme." [@Higgs2013NobelLectureEvadingGoldstone]*

6.  ***Higgs explicitly denies a "eureka moment."** Higgs is on
    record [@Wikipedia_PeterHiggs] stating that "there was no 'eureka
    moment' in the development of the theory." The work was technical,
    incremental, and concluded with a final-paragraph remark on the
    residual spin-zero boson, added to the revised PRL paper after the
    initial Physics Letters rejection.*

7.  ***The Higgs boson appears as a final-paragraph addition to a paper
    whose main content is gauge-boson mass.** Higgs verbatim on the
    revision of his rejected second paper: "I decided to augment the
    paper by some remarks on possible physical consequences, and to send
    the revised version across the Atlantic to Physical Review Letters.
    Among the additional material was the remark, 'It is worth noting
    that an essential feature of this type of theory is the prediction
    of incomplete multiplets of scalar and vector
    bosons.' " [@Higgs2013NobelLectureEvadingGoldstone] The Higgs boson
    --- the particle that took 48 years to detect and that the present
    paper has spent Part IV deriving --- enters the historical record as
    a sentence added to a revised paper because the main paper had been
    rejected as "of no obvious relevance to particle physics" by the
    CERN Physics Letters referee.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 (documentary) at every clause: each is a verbatim statement
of Higgs's own primary source [@Higgs2013NobelLectureEvadingGoldstone]
or a documented fact about the 1964
sequence [@Higgs1964PLB; @Higgs1964PRL; @Gilbert1964PRL; @GoldstoneSalamWeinberg1962].
The reconstruction is mechanical, not interpretive: Higgs was looking
for a loophole in Goldstone's theorem and found it in Schwinger's
Coulomb-gauge precedent. The Higgs boson is a side effect of that
loophole-hunting exercise. ◻
:::

##### The four places where $dx_4/dt = ic$ was in Higgs's calculation {#the-four-places-where-dx_4dt-ic-was-in-higgss-calculation .unnumbered}

We now identify, with theorem-level specificity, the four points in
Higgs's 1964 calculation where $dx_4/dt = ic$ was operative. Each was
named in Channel-A terms (Lagrangian, gauge fixing, scalar field, vacuum
expectation value); none was recognised as a physical fact about a
moving fourth dimension. This is the unnamed-invariance pattern of
§[19.7](#ssec:UnnamedInvariance){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:UnnamedInvariance"} located now at the founding moment.

::: {#thm:FourPlacesInHiggsCalculation .theorem}
**Theorem 369** (Four places where $dx_4/dt = ic$ was in Higgs's
calculation; identification). *In Higgs's 1964 paper [@Higgs1964PRL] and
its illustrative model (the complex scalar field with Mexican-hat
potential coupled to an electromagnetic gauge field), the $i$ of
$dx_4/dt = ic$ was operative at four identifiable points:*

1.  ***The Klein--Gordon kinetic term encodes $x_4$'s perpendicular
    advance through the marker $i$.** Higgs's Lagrangian contains the
    standard relativistic kinetic term
    $$\partial_\mu \phi^* \partial^\mu \phi = -\frac{1}{c^2}\,|\partial_t \phi|^2 + |\nabla \phi|^2,$$
    where the minus sign on the time derivative is the
    Lorentzian-signature minus sign. By
    Theorem [280](#thm:SignatureForcedByMetric){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:SignatureForcedByMetric"} (H11.5), this minus sign
    *is* the perpendicularity-marker $i$ of $x_4= ict$ --- the unique
    scalar effecting the Lorentzian-to-Euclidean form change when $x_4$,
    a real perpendicular fourth spatial-type dimension advancing at $c$,
    is written into the four-square interval. Higgs's Lagrangian is
    therefore the Lagrangian of a field on the $(x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4)$
    four-space with $x_4$'s advance encoded by the standard $x_4= ict$
    shadow; in his treatment it is named "the standard relativistic
    scalar Lagrangian," with no statement about the underlying physical
    fourth dimension.*

2.  ***The Schwinger Coulomb-gauge "apparent violation of Lorentz
    invariance" is the signature of the real perpendicular fourth
    dimension's advance.** The insight of 18--19 July 1964 was
    Schwinger's demonstration that the Coulomb gauge ---
    non-manifestly-Lorentz-covariant --- produces relativistic physics.
    The reason for this
    (Theorem [280](#thm:SignatureForcedByMetric){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:SignatureForcedByMetric"}, H11.5;
    Theorem [284](#thm:NecessityBoundary){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:NecessityBoundary"}, H11.9): the fourth dimension
    $x_4$ is a real perpendicular spatial-type direction advancing at
    velocity $c$, with the factor $i$ in $x_4= ict$ as its
    perpendicularity marker, not an independent imaginary slot. The
    Coulomb gauge is the $x_4$-fixed gauge with the timelike direction
    encoded in $i$ rather than in a separate independent coordinate. The
    "apparent violation of Lorentz invariance" that Higgs and Schwinger
    both worked through is the shadow of the same physical fact: once
    one sees that $x_4^2 = -c^2 t^2$ records the real perpendicular
    fourth dimension's advance, the "apparent violation" is no violation
    at all. Higgs reached the right conclusion (no observable violation)
    via the right calculation; the underlying physical reason (the
    timelike direction is the real perpendicular fourth dimension in
    motion) was not part of the calculation or its interpretation.*

3.  ***The complex scalar field is a single-complex-structure object
    forcing signature (1,3) and the Born-norm timelike direction.**
    Higgs's field $\phi$ is a single-complex-structure object: one $i$,
    one Hermitian inner product, Born-norm probability $|\phi|^2$. By
    Theorem [267](#thm:SignatureForced){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:SignatureForced"} (H14, MG-Spinor Theorem 5.6), the
    single-complex-structure forces signature $(1,3)$ with exactly one
    timelike direction --- the Born-norm direction built from the same
    $i$ that marks $x_4$'s perpendicular advance in $x_4= ict$. The
    complex scalar field on which Higgs's mechanism is built is, the
    field-theoretic object whose existence requires and encodes a real
    perpendicular fourth spatial-type dimension in motion at $c$.
    Higgs's calculation made no use of this fact and named it nowhere.*

4.  ***The vacuum expectation value is the field-theoretic encoding of
    the $+ic$ direction.** The mathematics of Higgs's mechanism is that
    the vacuum expectation value $\langle H \rangle = (0, v)^\top$ picks
    out a specific direction in the $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ doublet space. By
    Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:HiggsPointer"} (H1, the identification of Part IV of
    the present paper), this direction *is* the $+ic$ direction of
    $x_4$'s expansion at each spacetime event. In Higgs's 1964 reading,
    the vev's direction is "a direction in field space" --- a Channel-A
    algebraic direction, with no Channel-B geometry. The two readings
    agree on every empirical prediction (gauge-boson masses, fermion
    Yukawa couplings, Higgs-boson mass) and disagree on the physical
    referent of the direction.*

*At every one of (P1)--(P4), the operative $i$ is the same single
complex structure: by
Theorem [267](#thm:SignatureForced){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SignatureForced"} (H14), there is exactly one $i$, the
one of $dx_4/dt = ic$, and every use of $i$ in Higgs's calculation is an
instance of this same complex structure. *The 1964 Higgs calculation is,
end-to-end, a calculation in the $i$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$ --- in the
algebraic-symmetry idiom that names the $i$ locally and does not see it
as a physical invariance.**
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 for each Channel-An identification (the relativistic
Lagrangian, the Coulomb-gauge structure, the complex scalar field, the
vev direction --- standard textbook physics, verified against Higgs's
1964 PRL paper [@Higgs1964PRL]). G2 for the cross-link identification
that the same $i$ appears at all four points and is the $i$ of
$dx_4/dt = ic$ (Theorem [267](#thm:SignatureForced){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SignatureForced"}, the single-complex-structure result;
Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"}, the Higgs-as-pointer identification of
Part IV). The G2 reading is the present paper's contribution; the G1
underlying algebra is Higgs's own 1964 calculation. ◻
:::

##### What Higgs and the other 1964 founders did *not* say {#what-higgs-and-the-other-1964-founders-did-not-say .unnumbered}

::: {#prop:HiggsNeverAssociatedWithMovingDimension .proposition}
**Proposition 370** (Higgs nowhere associates the field with a moving
fourth dimension, time as primitive, or expansion; primary-source
documentary). *A direct reading of Higgs's 2013 Nobel
lecture [@Higgs2013NobelLectureEvadingGoldstone], his 1964
papers [@Higgs1964PLB; @Higgs1964PRL], his 1966 full
development [@Higgs1966PR], and his 2007 "Prehistory of the Higgs
boson" [@Higgs2007CRPrehistoryOfHiggsBoson] reveals zero instances of
any of the following:*

1.  *Any treatment of *time* as a primitive geometric structure beyond
    its standard role as a coordinate $t$ in Lorentz-invariant
    equations.*

2.  *Any treatment of a *fourth dimension* (extra-spatial or otherwise)
    as the carrier of the Higgs field's structure.*

3.  *Any treatment of *cosmological or spatial expansion* as the
    physical source of the Higgs vev or the mass-generation mechanism.*

4.  *Any treatment of the imaginary unit $i$ as anything other than a
    calculational ingredient in the standard QFT formalism --- a phase
    factor in $e^{-iEt/\hbar}$, a generator factor in $e^{-iHt/\hbar}$,
    a unit in the complex scalar field, never a physical invariance with
    its own geometric interpretation.*

5.  *Any treatment of the velocity of light $c$ as anything other than
    the standard speed parameter in the Lorentz-invariant action, never
    a forced advance rate of a fourth dimension.*

*The same null finding holds for the companion 1964 papers of
Englert--Brout [@EnglertBrout1964PRL] and
Guralnik--Hagen--Kibble [@GuralnikHagenKibble1964PRL], and for
Anderson's 1962--63 condensed-matter
precedent [@Anderson1963PlasmonsGaugeInvarianceMass]. None of the
founding figures of the Higgs mechanism associated the Higgs field with
a moving fourth dimension, with time as a primitive geometric structure,
or with cosmological expansion. The Higgs field was treated, from 1964
to the present day, as a static scalar field with a non-zero,
Lorentz-invariant (hence spacetime-constant) vacuum expectation value,
sitting in spacetime.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 (documentary, null-finding) at the source: the absence of
any such treatment in the cited primary sources is the documented
record. The reading of the 1964 PRL paper [@Higgs1964PRL] confirms:
$\phi$ is a complex scalar field; the Lagrangian is the standard
relativistic form; the vev breaks $U(1)$; the longitudinal mode of the
gauge boson eats the would-be Goldstone; a residual scalar remains. No
mention of moving dimensions, foundational $i$, or geometry beyond the
standard relativistic-field-theory setup. ◻
:::

##### Three pressures that drove the algebraic-only reading {#three-pressures-that-drove-the-algebraic-only-reading .unnumbered}

::: {#rem:WhyHiggsFoundersDidNotSee .remark}
*Remark 371* (Why the Higgs founders did not see the moving dimension:
three documented pressures). The non-recognition is a consequence of
three documented features of postwar particle physics that jointly
directed Higgs and his contemporaries toward an algebraic-only reading
of the mass mechanism.

::: description
By 1960, particle physics had moved from the Channel-B geometric picture
of relativity (Einstein 1915; Minkowski 1908; Cartan 1922--25,
§[19.2](#ssec:HistoricalDescent){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:HistoricalDescent"}) to the Channel-A algebraic-symmetry
picture of QFT (Heisenberg, Wigner, Yang--Mills). Higgs himself notes
the field-theoretic context [@Higgs2013NobelLectureEvadingGoldstone]:
"Quantum field theory was out of fashion, despite its successes in
quantum electrodynamics; it was failing to describe either the strong or
the weak interactions." When QFT came back into fashion in the late
1960s through 't Hooft's renormalisation proof, the Channel-A apparatus
was already the standard idiom. The Channel-B reading of the Higgs ---
as the field-theoretic encoding of $+ic$ --- had no advocate.

Higgs's entire programme is built on the analogy with
superconductivity [@Anderson1963PlasmonsGaugeInvarianceMass; @Higgs2013NobelLectureEvadingGoldstone].
The Goldstone-mode-becoming-massive in a superconductor is the Anderson
mechanism, derived in 1962--63 from the structure of the Cooper-pair
condensate. The relativistic case treated by Higgs is the lift of this
algebraic mechanism from a condensed-matter system to a
Lorentz-invariant gauge theory. The condensed-matter system is sitting
in a fixed external spacetime --- there is no fourth-dimension content
to port. The analogy carries the algebra (Goldstone modes; gauge
invariance; vev structure) but loses the geometry that the relativistic
case actually has but the condensed-matter case does not. The Higgs
mechanism inherited the algebra and not the geometry, because the
geometry was not in the source case to inherit.

Higgs's central insight was that gauge fixing in QED introduces apparent
Lorentz-non-invariance that washes out in observables. The Lorentz
invariance was treated as an *algebraic* symmetry --- a constraint on
the form of the action --- rather than as a *geometric* statement about
the spacetime metric and its forced timelike advance at $c$. The
MG-Spinor §11 theorems (now
Theorems [276](#thm:CausalStructureExpansion){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:CausalStructureExpansion"}--[284](#thm:NecessityBoundary){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:NecessityBoundary"} of the present paper) make exactly
this distinction: the Lorentzian metric forces the advance at $c$ as a
geometric fact about every event; treating it as an algebraic symmetry
constraint loses the physics. Higgs's 1964 calculation was correct in
the algebraic idiom and silent in the geometric idiom because the
algebraic idiom was the only one available in the postwar
particle-physics culture.
:::

Each of (D1), (D2), (D3) is a documented feature of the field's culture
and Higgs's own methodology; none is an interpretive overlay. Jointly
they explain --- without imputing personal failure to any of the
founders --- why the $i$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$ that was operative at every
step of Higgs's calculation was nowhere recognised as a physical
invariance.
:::

##### The pattern at the founding: the deepest case of the unnamed invariance {#the-pattern-at-the-founding-the-deepest-case-of-the-unnamed-invariance .unnumbered}

::: {#thm:HiggsFoundingCase .theorem}
**Theorem 372** (The 1964 Higgs calculation as the founding case of the
unnamed-invariance pattern). *The
§[19.7](#ssec:UnnamedInvariance){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:UnnamedInvariance"} pattern --- the $i$ of
$dx_4/dt = ic$ in use end-to-end and named only locally --- is
documented at three sites by the present paper:*

1.  ***The contemporary frontier
    (Theorem [362](#thm:InvarianceInUseAndInView){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:InvarianceInUseAndInView"}, H17.6).** Witten uses the
    $i$ of the moving fourth dimension at every step of the
    Kapustin--Witten construction and localises the geometric-Langlands
    physics onto $t = i$, naming it only locally; Woit sees the special
    role of the one-time four-dimensional signature and states he cannot
    relate it to the real world.*

2.  ***The textbook record
    (Theorem [366](#thm:BoundariesCoincide){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:BoundariesCoincide"}, H17.9b).** The definitive
    geometric-Langlands
    monograph [@Frenkel2007LanglandsCorrespondenceForLoopGroups] is
    built on conformal-field-theory and current-algebra constructions of
    physics origin --- all single-complex-structure constructions over
    $\mathbb{C}$ --- with the physics provenance absorbed into the
    mathematical citations.*

3.  ***The founding moment
    (Proposition [368](#prop:HiggsActualResearchQuestion){reference-type="ref"
    reference="prop:HiggsActualResearchQuestion"},
    Theorem [369](#thm:FourPlacesInHiggsCalculation){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:FourPlacesInHiggsCalculation"},
    Proposition [370](#prop:HiggsNeverAssociatedWithMovingDimension){reference-type="ref"
    reference="prop:HiggsNeverAssociatedWithMovingDimension"},
    Remark [371](#rem:WhyHiggsFoundersDidNotSee){reference-type="ref"
    reference="rem:WhyHiggsFoundersDidNotSee"}).** The 1964 Higgs
    calculation, end-to-end, is a calculation in the $i$ of
    $dx_4/dt = ic$ --- the relativistic kinetic term carries the
    perpendicularity-marker $i$ of $x_4$'s advance; the Coulomb-gauge
    structure is the gauge with the timelike direction encoded as
    $x_4$'s perpendicular advance rather than as a separate independent
    slot; the complex scalar field is the single-complex-structure
    object; the vev is the $+ic$-direction encoder --- with the
    underlying physical fact (the real perpendicular fourth dimension
    advancing at $c$) named nowhere in Higgs's
    papers [@Higgs1964PLB; @Higgs1964PRL; @Higgs1966PR], his 2013 Nobel
    lecture [@Higgs2013NobelLectureEvadingGoldstone], or any of the
    companion 1964
    papers [@EnglertBrout1964PRL; @GuralnikHagenKibble1964PRL].*

*The founding case is the deepest instance of the pattern: the moving
dimension was present, operative, and not at a contemporary frontier or
in a textbook reconstruction, but at the very point of birth of the mass
mechanism that the entire Standard Model now depends on. The Higgs
mechanism --- the centerpiece of the Standard Model, the discovery that
motivated forty-eight years of experimental effort culminating in the
2012 LHC observation --- was discovered as the algebraic shadow of
$dx_4/dt = ic$ by a researcher who had become interested in quantum
gravity, who was looking for a loophole in Goldstone's theorem, who
explicitly denied a "eureka moment," and whose contribution entered the
historical record as a sentence added to a revised paper after the
original had been rejected as "of no obvious relevance to particle
physics."*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 (documentary) at each clause for the historical content; G2
for the cross-link identification of the 1964 founding case with the
§[19.7](#ssec:UnnamedInvariance){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:UnnamedInvariance"} pattern, which rests on
Theorem [267](#thm:SignatureForced){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SignatureForced"} (the single-complex-structure result)
and Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"} (the Higgs-as-pointer identification) of
the present paper. ◻
:::

::: {#rem:GlashowCoda .remark}
*Remark 373* (The Glashow non-recognition coda). A documented coda
sharpens the founding-case pattern. In March 1966 Higgs gave a talk at
Harvard on the mechanism, in the same room as Sheldon Glashow, who had
proposed electroweak unification in 1961 [@Glashow1961]. Higgs's own
report [@Higgs2013NobelLectureEvadingGoldstone]: "After the seminar
Shelly Glashow complimented me on having invented 'a nice model,' but he
did not recognise its relevance to his electroweak theory --- a missed
opportunity!" The mass mechanism that the entire Standard Model now
depends on was not recognised as central to electroweak unification by
the very theorist who had proposed electroweak unification, three years
after the Higgs paper, in the same room with its author. The
non-recognition pattern at the founding is therefore not a peculiarity
of Higgs's own reading; it is the standard pattern of the field's
reception of the result. The Higgs mechanism's full significance was
recognised only in 1967 by Weinberg and Salam, who incorporated it into
the electroweak Lagrangian; the renormalisability that made the theory
predictive was established by 't Hooft in 1971; the weak neutral
currents predicted by Glashow--Weinberg--Salam were discovered in 1973;
the $W$ and $Z$ bosons at their predicted masses in 1983; the Higgs
boson itself in 2012. The 48-year gap from 1964 prediction to 2012
detection is also a measure of the non-recognition gap: it took half a
century to confirm experimentally what the framework of the present
paper now reads as a chain of theorems descending from $dx_4/dt = ic$.
:::

::: {#rem:HiggsFoundersContrastWithMcGucken .remark}
*Remark 374* (The contrast with the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's
account). The present paper's account of the Higgs sector (Part IV,
Theorems H1--H16) is what the 1964 calculation *would have read as* had
the $i$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$ been recognised at the founding.
Theorem [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HiggsPointer"} (H1: Higgs as field-theoretic pointer to
$+ic$) supplies the physical referent for the vev's direction-selection
(P4 of
Theorem [369](#thm:FourPlacesInHiggsCalculation){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:FourPlacesInHiggsCalculation"}).
Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"} (H10: Compton-$x_4$ coupling)
supplies the physical referent for the Yukawa-coupling-as-mass-rate (the
species-specific rate at which fermions wind perpendicular through
$x_4$, observed as the Compton frequency).
Theorem [254](#thm:GravitationalComptonClock){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:GravitationalComptonClock"} (H12: gravitational redshift
as gravitational slowing of the Compton-$x_4$-clock) supplies the
connection to general relativity that the standard
Standard-Model-plus-GR architecture leaves disconnected.
Theorems [265](#thm:FourthRoot){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:FourthRoot"}--[286](#thm:DoubleCoverDerived){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:DoubleCoverDerived"} (H13--H16: the spinor as the fourth
root of the McGucken interval) supply the connection to matter content's
spinorial structure.

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework is not in competition with the
1964 calculation; it *contains* the 1964 calculation as the Channel-A
algebraic shadow of a Channel-B geometric reading. Each piece of the
1964 calculation reads as the algebraic-symmetry shadow of a piece of
$dx_4/dt = ic$. The Higgs mechanism --- which Higgs himself attributed
to the loophole in Goldstone's theorem and the Schwinger Coulomb-gauge
precedent --- is, in the present framework's reading, the
field-theoretic record of $x_4$'s expansion at velocity $c$ in spherical
symmetry from every spacetime event, with the Higgs vev as the local
direction-encoder and the Yukawa couplings as species-specific winding
rates. The 1964 calculation and the present paper's account differ in
idiom and in stated physical referent, agree on every empirical
prediction, and stand in the same relation as the Coulomb-gauge
formulation and the Lorentz-gauge formulation of QED: the same
observable physics, with one formulation transparent to a particular
piece of the underlying physics and the other formulation transparent to
a different piece.
:::

#### Atiyah Endorses the Lineage: The 2010 IMPA Lecture and the Atiyah--Moore Shifted Dirac Equation {#ssec:AtiyahEndorsesTheLineage}

The unnamed-invariance pattern documented in
§[19.7](#ssec:UnnamedInvariance){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:UnnamedInvariance"} for Witten and Woit, in
§[19.8](#ssec:TextbookRecord){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:TextbookRecord"} for Frenkel's monograph, and in
§[19.9](#ssec:HiggsFoundersUnnamedInvariance){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:HiggsFoundersUnnamedInvariance"} for the Higgs founders,
is sharpened to its most direct primary-source form by a single 2010
lecture of Sir Michael Atiyah at the Instituto Nacional de Matemática
Pura e Aplicada (IMPA), Rio de Janeiro, titled *From Quantum Physics to
Number Theory: A Geometer Explores the
Universe* [@Atiyah2010IMPALecture]. In that lecture Atiyah states
verbatim:

1.  the Dirac--Lorentz--complex-variable identification as "a remarkably
    accurate prediction" of Dirac's 1939
    lecture [@Dirac1939RelationMathPhysics];

2.  the four-dimensional uniqueness of physical space as "a remarkable
    prophecy" of the same Dirac lecture, with the modern Donaldson
    exotica as the predicted vindication;

3.  the Dirac operator as the unique first-order Lorentz-invariant
    differential operator, hence the unique relativistic
    motion-generator (the operator-theoretical structure of
    Proposition [263](#prop:GeneratorFlow){reference-type="ref"
    reference="prop:GeneratorFlow"} of the present paper, predating that
    proposition by sixteen years);

4.  his own positioning in the Schrödinger--Dirac school (Channel B in
    the present paper's dual-channel terminology) and Connes's
    positioning in the Heisenberg school (Channel A);

5.  the existence and identifiability of a quantum-gravitational
    Hamiltonian whose spectrum should be the non-trivial Riemann zeros
    (Hilbert's dream, made specific to quantum gravity);

6.  his classification of himself as a follower of Einstein and Dirac.

The 2010 lecture is therefore a primary-source document in which the
leading geometer of his generation enunciates, as conjecture and as
research programme, six identifications that the present paper executes
as theorems and open problems. We document the lecture verbatim where
central, establish four identifications between Atiyah's positions and
the present paper's theorems, examine the contemporaneous Atiyah--Moore
paper [@AtiyahMoore2010ShiftedView] which proposes the shifted Dirac
equation, address Atiyah's gravity-from-octonions Magic-Square proposal
against the present paper's gauge-group derivation, and state as Open
Problem 3 the connection to the Riemann Hypothesis. Each new result is
named, graded, and bounded.

##### Atiyah's verbatim statements on the Dirac--Lorentz--complex-variable identification {#atiyahs-verbatim-statements-on-the-diraclorentzcomplex-variable-identification .unnumbered}

::: {#prop:AtiyahEndorsesDiracLorentz .proposition}
**Proposition 375** (Atiyah 2010 endorses the Dirac 1939
Lorentz--complex-variable identification; primary-source documentary).
*In [@Atiyah2010IMPALecture transcript timestamps 13:02--14:07], Atiyah
reads aloud and explicitly endorses the following Dirac 1939
prediction [@Dirac1939RelationMathPhysics §3]:*

> *"I would suggest as a more hopeful idea for getting an improved
> quantum theory that one takes in \[some specific\] way the theory of
> functions of a complex variable. This branch of mathematics is of
> exceptional beauty and further the conformal transformations in the
> complex plane is the same as the Lorentz group governing the spacetime
> of restricted relativity. One is then led to suspect the existence of
> some deep hidden connection between the theory of functions of a
> complex variable and the spacetime of restricted relativity, the
> working out of which will be a difficult task for the future."*

*Atiyah's commentary, verbatim: "That is a remarkably accurate
prediction. What has happened in physics in the last twenty years? The
use of complex variables inside present-day physics, string theory, is
widespread; but it's also the work around Penrose, which is tangential
but part of the same story. So complex variable theory has become a
very, very important part of modern theoretical physics, and part of the
reason is, as Dirac points out, its connection with the Lorentz group."*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 (documentary) at the source [@Atiyah2010IMPALecture
13:02--14:07]: a verbatim quotation of Atiyah's reading of Dirac and
Atiyah's stated endorsement. Dirac's 1939 source
is [@Dirac1939RelationMathPhysics]. ◻
:::

::: {#thm:AtiyahDiracIsTheSingleI .theorem}
**Theorem 376** (The Dirac--Lorentz--complex-variable connection Atiyah
endorses *is* the single $i$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$; identification). *The
"deep hidden connection between the theory of functions of a complex
variable and the spacetime of restricted relativity" that Dirac 1939
predicted and Atiyah 2010 endorses is identical to the single complex
structure $J^2 = -\mathbf{1}$ associated with $x_4$ in $dx_4/dt = ic$
(Theorems [267](#thm:SignatureForced){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SignatureForced"},
[280](#thm:SignatureForcedByMetric){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SignatureForcedByMetric"} of the present paper). The
conformal-transformations-equals-Lorentz-group fact is the statement
that the Möbius group $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C})$ of conformal
transformations of the Riemann sphere is isomorphic to the proper
orthochronous Lorentz group $\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$ --- which by
Theorem [286](#thm:DoubleCoverDerived){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:DoubleCoverDerived"}(iii) (H16) is the universal Lorentz
double cover via the single complex structure of $S = \mathbb{C}^2$. The
Riemann sphere of complex-variable theory and the celestial sphere of
restricted relativity are the same $\mathbb{C}P^1$ acted on by
$\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$, with the action mediated by the single complex
structure that is the same $J$ as in $x_4= ict$.*

*Hence Dirac's 1939 conjectured "deep hidden connection" and Atiyah's
2010 endorsed "part of the reason" are the present paper's
Theorems [267](#thm:SignatureForced){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SignatureForced"},
[286](#thm:DoubleCoverDerived){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:DoubleCoverDerived"}, and
[280](#thm:SignatureForcedByMetric){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SignatureForcedByMetric"} stated as a research programme
rather than as theorems: Dirac saw the connection in 1939, Atiyah
ratified it in 2010, the present paper supplies it as a chain of G1
theorems descending from $dx_4/dt = ic$.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 for the Möbius--Lorentz isomorphism (standard;
Penrose--Rindler 1984):
$\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C}) \cong \mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$, verified by
direct computation that any $A \in \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{C})$ acting on
a Hermitian $2 \times 2$ matrix $H$ by $H \mapsto AHA^\dagger$ preserves
$\det H$, the Lorentzian quadratic form
(Theorem [267](#thm:SignatureForced){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SignatureForced"}(i)); the action descends to
$\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C})$ since $-A$ and $A$ act identically. G2 for
the identification of this $J$ with the $J$ of $x_4= ict$, which rests
on Theorems [267](#thm:SignatureForced){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SignatureForced"} and
[280](#thm:SignatureForcedByMetric){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SignatureForcedByMetric"}. ◻
:::

##### Atiyah's verbatim statement on four-dimensional uniqueness {#atiyahs-verbatim-statement-on-four-dimensional-uniqueness .unnumbered}

::: {#prop:AtiyahEndorsesFourDimensionalUniqueness .proposition}
**Proposition 377** (Atiyah 2010 endorses the Dirac 1939
four-dimensional-uniqueness prediction; primary-source documentary). *In
[@Atiyah2010IMPALecture transcript timestamps 12:05--12:51], Atiyah
reads aloud and explicitly endorses the following further Dirac 1939
prediction [@Dirac1939RelationMathPhysics §3]:*

> *"Only four-dimensional space is of importance to physics, while
> spaces of other numbers of dimensions are of about equal interest in
> mathematics. It may well be, however, that this discrepancy is due to
> the incompleteness of present-day knowledge, and that future
> developments will show four-dimensional space to be of far greater
> mathematical interest than all the others."*

*Atiyah's commentary, verbatim: "That's a remarkable prophecy, as some
of you know. The last 20--30 years, remarkable facts have been
discovered about four-dimensional space which are quite unique and not
true of other dimensions. This was one of the most remarkable
discoveries of the last half of the 20th century, and here is Dirac
forecasting it in some sense as a possibility, very, very deep thinker
indeed, Dirac."*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 (documentary) at [@Atiyah2010IMPALecture 12:05--12:51].
Dirac source [@Dirac1939RelationMathPhysics]. ◻
:::

::: {#rem:AtiyahFourDimUniquenessIsTheFramework .remark}
*Remark 378* (The four-dimensional uniqueness Atiyah identifies *is* the
four-dimensional structure of $dx_4/dt = ic$). The four-dimensional
uniqueness Atiyah identifies has at least three independent witnesses in
the present paper: (i) the Donaldson exotic-smooth-structures result on
$\mathbb{R}^4$ (§[19.1](#ssec:MathematicalDescent){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:MathematicalDescent"},
§[19.4](#ssec:NonRemovability){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:NonRemovability"}), which is the specific Atiyah refers
to; (ii) the static $(4,0)$ Donaldson sector hosting no physics until
the $i$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$ injects relativity, QM, and the symmetries
(Remark [293](#rem:DonaldsonStaticSector){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:DonaldsonStaticSector"}); (iii) the exterior-closure
identity
$16 = 16 = \dim(S \otimes S^*) = \dim \Lambda^\bullet(\mathbb{R}^4)$ of
Theorem [265](#thm:FourthRoot){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:FourthRoot"}(iv) which holds only in four dimensions and
forces the spinor to be the fourth root of the four-dimensional
interval. The framework's commitment to four dimensions is therefore
Dirac's 1939 prediction made explicit: $dx_4/dt = ic$ is a
four-dimensional equation because the substrate of physics is the
four-dimensional arena, with $x_4$ as the real perpendicular fourth
dimension advancing at $c$ and the three spatial dimensions
$x_1, x_2, x_3$ as static. Atiyah identifies the dimension; the
framework supplies the content (the moving fourth, the static three)
that makes the dimension unique.
:::

##### The Atiyah--Moore shifted Dirac equation: relativistic retardation forced by the one-way orientation $dx_4/dt = ic$ {#the-atiyahmoore-shifted-dirac-equation-relativistic-retardation-forced-by-the-one-way-orientation-dx_4dt-ic .unnumbered}

The most operational content in the 2010 talk is Atiyah's discussion of
the Atiyah--Moore shifted Dirac equation [@AtiyahMoore2010ShiftedView],
submitted to arXiv on 16 September 2010 (15 pages, latex), with
abstract: "We speculate on the role of relativistic versions of delayed
differential equations in fundamental physics. Relativistic invariance
implies that we must consider both advanced and retarded terms in the
equations, so we refer to them as shifted equations. The shifted Dirac
equation has some novel properties. A tentative formulation of shifted
Einstein--Maxwell equations naturally incorporates a small but nonzero
cosmological constant."

The construction. To introduce retardation $f(t) \to f(t-r)$ in a
relativistically invariant way, the shift operator
$\exp(-r\, \partial/\partial t)$ of one-dimensional analysis must be
generalised to an operator that is Lorentz-invariant in four-dimensional
Minkowski space. The unique first-order Lorentz-invariant differential
operator on spinor fields is the Dirac operator $D$ (Atiyah's verbatim
statement: "there's only one first-order differential operator which is
invariant under \[the\] Lorentz group --- that was discovered by Dirac,
it is called the Dirac operator"). Atiyah and Moore therefore propose
the *shifted Dirac equation*
$$\{i\hbar D - mc + ik\exp(-rD)\}\psi = 0,$$ with $r$ a length scale and
$k$ a real parameter, and apply the same logic to Einstein and
Einstein--Maxwell equations.

::: {#prop:AtiyahMooreFromOneWay .proposition}
**Proposition 379** (Atiyah--Moore retardation is forced by the one-way
orientation aspect A4 of $dx_4/dt = ic$; identification). *The
Atiyah--Moore shifted Dirac equation, in the framework's reading, is a
consequence of the one-way orientation A4 of the McGucken Principle
(Proposition [257](#prop:AspectDecomposition){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:AspectDecomposition"}). The argument proceeds in three
steps:*

1.  ***The one-way orientation is the substrate fact.** Aspect A4 of
    $dx_4/dt = ic$ states that the advance is $+ic$, not $-ic$, not
    direction-varying --- a uniform single direction with no
    time-reversal symmetry at the substrate level. By
    Theorem [283](#thm:AdvanceIsForced){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:AdvanceIsForced"} (H11.8) the observed metric forces
    this advance at $c$ at every event.*

2.  ***One-way orientation implies asymmetric advanced/retarded
    structure.** On a substrate with a single distinguished forward
    direction (here $+ic$), the field equations governing propagation
    cannot be symmetric under $t \to -t$ at the substrate level: the
    past and the future are not interchangeable at the layer. The
    retardation/advance asymmetry that Atiyah--Moore introduce by hand
    --- "relativistic invariance implies that we must consider both
    advanced and retarded terms" [@AtiyahMoore2010ShiftedView], with the
    asymmetry inherited from the structure of plane-wave components ---
    is the field-theoretic shadow of the substrate's one-way
    orientation.*

3.  ***The Dirac operator is the unique first-order Lorentz-invariant
    operator, hence the unique relativistic motion-generator.** Atiyah's
    statement (verbatim, 2010): "There's only one first-order
    differential operator which is invariant under \[the\] Lorentz group
    --- that was discovered by Dirac. So I like things \[that are\]
    unique because there is the only solution to a basic question you
    ask." This is the operator-theoretical structure of
    Proposition [263](#prop:GeneratorFlow){reference-type="ref"
    reference="prop:GeneratorFlow"} (Generator and Flow) and
    Remark [264](#rem:AtiyahFirstOrder){reference-type="ref"
    reference="rem:AtiyahFirstOrder"} of the present paper: the
    first-order operator is the generator of the one-parameter motion,
    and in the relativistic case there is exactly one such operator (the
    Dirac operator), which is therefore the unique generator of the
    relativistic-invariant motion that is, in the framework's reading,
    the $x_4$-advance.*

*Combining (S1)--(S3): the one-way orientation A4 forces
retardation/advance asymmetry; relativistic invariance forces the
retardation operator to be $\exp(-rD)$ for $D$ the Dirac operator; the
shifted Dirac equation is the consequence. The Atiyah--Moore equation is
therefore not in competition with $dx_4/dt = ic$ but is its
field-theoretic consequence in the spinor sector. Atiyah and Moore have,
without naming it, written down a field equation that records the same
one-way $x_4$-orientation that is aspect A4 of the McGucken Principle.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 (documentary) for the Atiyah--Moore construction and
Atiyah's verbatim uniqueness
statement [@AtiyahMoore2010ShiftedView; @Atiyah2010IMPALecture]; G2 for
the identification of A4-orientation with the retardation asymmetry,
which rests on
Proposition [257](#prop:AspectDecomposition){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:AspectDecomposition"} (A1--A5) and
Proposition [263](#prop:GeneratorFlow){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:GeneratorFlow"}. ◻
:::

::: {#rem:AtiyahMooreCCMcGuckenGravity .remark}
*Remark 380* (Atiyah--Moore obtain a small nonzero cosmological
constant; the framework supplies the gravitational referent
Atiyah--Moore did not yet have). A striking quantitative outcome of
[@AtiyahMoore2010ShiftedView] is that the shifted Einstein--Maxwell
equations "naturally incorporates a small but nonzero cosmological
constant." Atiyah's verbatim statement in the 2010 talk: "We found we
had some relationship to Einstein's equations and to the cosmological
constant. So we got a scale for this number $k$, or rather its ratio to
Planck's constant, of 10 to the minus 56. All this cosmological-constant
smallness is one of the mysteries of cosmology --- why it's so small,
why it's there. And in this little model we have it \[coming out
naturally\]; we meet both nuclear physics on this level and cosmology at
that level, just on the idea of using this operator."

This is empirically significant: the shifted-Dirac construction, born
from operator-theoretic uniqueness (Atiyah's repeated emphasis),
produces the cosmological-constant scale as a natural output. The
framework's reading: the cosmological constant is the cosmic-scale
signature of the same $x_4$-advance that locally produces Compton
frequencies (Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}, H10) and the gravitational redshift
(Theorem [254](#thm:GravitationalComptonClock){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:GravitationalComptonClock"}, H12 with the MG-Cosmology
empirical record [@MG-Cosmology]). The Atiyah--Moore retardation
parameter $r$ and the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's expansion rate
$c$ are tied at the cosmological-constant scale because both record the
same one-way $x_4$-orientation reaching to the cosmological domain.

However, Atiyah explicitly stated [@Atiyah2010IMPALecture 58:14--58:34]
that the shifted-equations construction "hasn't quite touched gravity
properly" --- the cosmological constant emerges but the origin of
gravity itself is not derived. The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework
supplies what Atiyah--Moore did not yet have: gravity as a consequence
of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via the Gravitational Compton Clock theorem
(Theorem [254](#thm:GravitationalComptonClock){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:GravitationalComptonClock"}, H12), with general
relativity recovered as the integrated description of
cosmologically-varying $x_4$-clock rates in curved spacetime, and the
cosmological domain handled (MG-Cosmology twelve first-place finishes
including DESI DR2, ACT DR6, Bullet Cluster, RAR at 50.3$\sigma$, SPARC
BTFR slope=4) [@MG-Cosmology]. The Atiyah--Moore cosmological-constant
scale is the empirical fingerprint of the same $x_4$-advance that the
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework derives gravity from; Atiyah--Moore
identified the fingerprint, McGucken identifies the hand.
:::

##### Atiyah's Schrödinger--Dirac vs Heisenberg--Connes split: the dual-channel architecture made explicit by Atiyah {#atiyahs-schrödingerdirac-vs-heisenbergconnes-split-the-dual-channel-architecture-made-explicit-by-atiyah .unnumbered}

The 2010 lecture contains, at [@Atiyah2010IMPALecture 59:08--59:46], a
remarkable methodological self-statement that locates Atiyah's own
philosophy against Alain Connes's, and which maps onto the dual-channel
architecture of the present paper.

::: {#prop:AtiyahNamesSchroedingerHeisenbergSplit .proposition}
**Proposition 381** (Atiyah 2010 names the Schrödinger--Dirac vs
Heisenberg--Connes split; primary-source documentary). *Atiyah's
verbatim statement [@Atiyah2010IMPALecture 59:08--59:46]: "The
difference between my philosophy and Connes's philosophy lies in \[a\]
difficulty in the philosophy of Heisenberg and the philosophy of
Schrödinger and Dirac. Heisenberg developed algebra, non-commutative
algebra, and the commutation relations, \[and\] Connes is very much in
the spirit of Heisenberg; whereas Schrödinger wrote down a differential
equation, and Dirac wrote down an even better equation, and this
equation later on was shown to be equal to Heisenberg formulation but a
different point of view. So I belong to the Schrödinger--Dirac school,
and Connes belongs to the Heisenberg school. We may be more or less
equivalent for many purposes, but for the purposes of gravity I think
Heisenberg doesn't work --- I mean \[there is\] something missing here
as yet."*

*This is a primary-source self-classification: Atiyah locates himself in
the Schrödinger--Dirac school (differential-operator, geometric,
Channel-B-style approach) and locates Connes in the Heisenberg school
(algebraic, spectral, noncommutative, Channel-A-style approach), and
asserts that the equivalence breaks down at gravity, where the
Schrödinger--Dirac school has more access to the content. Atiyah does
not name the split as a dichotomy that could be *contained* by a single
source; he treats it as a real disagreement.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 (documentary) at the source [@Atiyah2010IMPALecture
59:08--59:46]. The Schrödinger--Heisenberg equivalence Atiyah refers to
is the formal equivalence of the Schrödinger and Heisenberg pictures of
quantum mechanics (Dirac 1930), which is true at the level of equal-time
predictions for fixed Hamiltonians. ◻
:::

::: {#thm:AtiyahSplitIsDualChannel .theorem}
**Theorem 382** (Atiyah's split is the dual-channel architecture; the
source-pair $(\mathcal{M}_G, D_M)$ contains both channels). *Atiyah's
Schrödinger--Dirac vs Heisenberg--Connes split
(Proposition [381](#prop:AtiyahNamesSchroedingerHeisenbergSplit){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:AtiyahNamesSchroedingerHeisenbergSplit"}) is identical
to the dual-channel architecture of the present paper: the
Schrödinger--Dirac side is Channel B (differential-operator, manifold
$\mathcal{M}_G$, geometric, $x_4$-flow); the Heisenberg--Connes side is
Channel A (algebraic, spectral, noncommutative operator $D_M$, gauge
groups). The source-pair $(\mathcal{M}_G, D_M)$ of
[@MG-Master2Chains-2026] is the structure that contains both channels as
the two readings of a single underlying primitive.*

::: center
  *Atiyah's 2010 split*                     *Present paper's dual-channel*                                *Common source*
  ----------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------- ------------------
  *Schrödinger--Dirac school (Atiyah)*      *Channel B: $\mathcal{M}_G$, $x_4$-flow, spinor, geometric*   *$dx_4/dt = ic$*
  *Heisenberg school (Connes)*              *Channel A: $D_M$, spectral, algebraic, gauge groups*         *$dx_4/dt = ic$*
  *"equivalent for many purposes"*          *source-pair Klein correspondence*                            *one principle*
  *"Heisenberg doesn't work for gravity"*   *gravity via Channel B's $x_4$-clock (H12)*                   *one principle*

*Where Atiyah identifies a disagreement (gravity is harder for
Heisenberg/Connes), the framework's reading identifies the cause
(Channel A captures the algebraic-symmetry but not the $x_4$-flow, so

identification (the source-pair $(\mathcal{M}_G, D_M)$ produces both
channels and ties their predictions); the split is real but is the split
of one source into two readings, not the split of physics into two

identification of Atiyah's stated dichotomy with the dual-channel

##### Atiyah's Magic-Square / octonion-gravity proposal and the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's gauge-group derivation {#atiyahs-magic-square-octonion-gravity-proposal-and-the-mcgucken-dx_4dt-ic-frameworks-gauge-group-derivation .unnumbered}

The most substantial competing proposal in the 2010 lecture is Atiyah's
gravity-from-octonions Magic-Square programme.

::: {#prop:AtiyahMagicSquareGravityFromOctonions .proposition}
**Proposition 384** (Atiyah's Magic-Square / four-division-algebras /
four-forces proposal; primary-source documentary). *At
[@Atiyah2010IMPALecture 28:43--31:55], Atiyah proposes: "The four
division algebras \[$\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{C}, \mathbb{H}, \mathbb{O}$\]
correspond to the four fundamental forces of nature. The four
fundamental forces of nature, if you read the popular literature you
should know by now, they are the electromagnetic force, \[the\] weak
force, the strong force --- these are the forces involved in \[the\]
structure \[of\] the nucleus of nuclear material --- and then finally
you have gravity. \[\...\] These first three are the ones we have
nowadays well understood in quantum mechanics: there is a unified theory
of these first three; it's called the Standard Model. Gravity doesn't
fit, and people have been trying \[for\] the last 20 or 30 years to
bring gravity to the same framework as these three and unify it; that's
the search. \[\...\] The key idea is that gravity corresponds to the
octonions. These \[$\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{C}, \mathbb{H}$\] correspond to
the classical fields, real-complex-quaternions; this one \[octonions\]
corresponds to gravity, because the octonions are much harder. Gravity
is much harder; but because the octonions are also very beautiful looked
at the right way, gravity should also be very beautiful too. So the real
theory which we would like to get to \[\...\] should aim to include
gravity with all these theory in such a way that gravity is seen to be
very much a consequence of the octonions and the exceptional groups.
This would be a really beautiful end to the search, because it ends here
\[at $\mathbb{O}$\] because we never --- they are the last division
algebra; there is nothing beyond."*

*Atiyah further proposes that the eight-dimensional manifolds with
$\mathrm{Spin}(7)$ holonomy and the seven-dimensional $G_2$-holonomy
manifolds (the last row of the Magic Square) are the natural geometries
for gravity's hard content, and that "this is \[the\] key part of
understanding what we need to do quantum gravity."*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 (documentary) at the source [@Atiyah2010IMPALecture
28:43--31:55, 52:09--54:22]. The Magic Square
(Freudenthal--Tits--Vinberg) is a classical mathematical structure; the
four-division-algebra correspondence to the four forces is Atiyah's
proposal, stated as a conjecture rather than a derivation. ◻
:::

::: {#rem:McGuckenResponseToMagicSquareGravity .remark}
*Remark 385* (The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's response: gravity
is already a consequence of $dx_4/dt = ic$, while the Magic Square
content is addressable). Atiyah's proposal and the McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework agree on the target (gravity must be a

other three forces, with the architecture closed by some uniqueness

*The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's position.* Gravity is not an
additional force requiring a new division-algebra beyond what produces
the Standard Model. By
Theorem [254](#thm:GravitationalComptonClock){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:GravitationalComptonClock"} (H12), general-relativistic
gravity is the integrated geometric description of
cosmologically-varying $x_4$-clock rates --- a Channel-B consequence of
the same $dx_4/dt = ic$ that produces the Standard Model gauge group on
the Channel-A side via the Connes spectral-triple internal algebra
$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$. The
McGucken cosmology paper [@MG-Cosmology] establishes empirically that
this account handles the cosmological-domain phenomena that the
Standard-Model-plus-GR architecture cannot (twelve first-place finishes:
H$_0$ tension, $S_8$ tension, RAR at 50.3$\sigma$ improvement, SPARC
BTFR slope $= 4$, Bullet Cluster, ACT DR6, DESI DR2, $w(z=0) = -0.983$,
etc.).

*The relation to the Magic Square.* The framework's internal algebra
$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$ is
built from three of the four division algebras (real, complex,
quaternionic, in the form of $\mathbb{C}$, $\mathbb{H}$, and
$M_3(\mathbb{C})$); the octonions $\mathbb{O}$ are absent. The McGucken
Sphere $\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}$ is a smooth two-sphere (with the
$x_4$-direction perpendicular to the three spatial dimensions, not an
octonion-related 7-sphere or 8-manifold). The framework's first-order
operator $D_M$ is the Dirac operator on a complex-spin-structure
4-manifold (not an octonion-related $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$ manifold).

*The hint from the framework's unique geometry.* The McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's geometry has a feature distinct from either
standard $(3+1)$ Minkowski or the static $(4,0)$ Euclidean case: $x_4$
is quantised at the Compton scale (with the Compton-frequency
identification of
Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}, H10) while the three spatial
dimensions $x_1, x_2, x_3$ remain smooth. This is a hybrid
quantised-and-smooth-mixed geometry: discrete in the perpendicular
advance direction (where mass is the rate of perpendicular winding,
quantised in units of $\hbar / (m_f c^2)^{-1}$ for species $f$),
continuous in the three spatial directions. This is distinct from both
string theory's smooth higher-dimensional substrate and loop quantum
gravity's uniformly quantised spacetime; it may be the kind of structure
that addresses the gravitational hardness Atiyah identifies via
octonions, but does so without requiring the octonions. The
Compton-quantisation of $x_4$ is itself the content Atiyah was reaching
for through the octonions: a hardness in the gravitational direction
that is absent in the smooth-spatial directions.

*The open question.* It remains open whether the framework's gauge-group
derivation $G_{SM} = U(1) \times SU(2) \times SU(3)$ from the
substrate-scale exhaustion of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via the internal algebra
$\mathcal{A}_F = \mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$ is
the *full* story, or whether the Magic-Square / exceptional-group /
octonion content Atiyah identifies is a deeper layer that contains the
framework's gauge content as a sub-structure. The empirical predictions
of the framework (no GUT, no proton decay, the chirality structure, the
Compton-frequency of mass) are at present in agreement with all
observations; the Magic-Square exceptional-group proposal has not yet
produced specific predictions agreeing with observation. The McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's position is that the gauge-group content is
closed at the $\mathbb{C}\oplus \mathbb{H}\oplus M_3(\mathbb{C})$ level
(no GUT theorem; the substrate-scale exhaustion of $dx_4/dt = ic$ is at
this internal algebra), with gravity emerging from the same source.
Atiyah's position is that the exceptional groups and octonions await
their place. The two positions agree empirically on the Standard Model
and disagree on the source of gravity.
:::

##### Atiyah's Hilbert--Pólya / quantum-gravity / Riemann-Hypothesis programme {#atiyahs-hilbertpólya-quantum-gravity-riemann-hypothesis-programme .unnumbered}

The most ambitious content in the 2010 lecture comes at the close:
Atiyah's identification of quantum gravity as the candidate source of
the Hilbert--Pólya operator whose spectrum is the Riemann zeros.

::: {#prop:AtiyahHilbertPolyaQuantumGravity .proposition}
**Proposition 386** (Atiyah 2010 conjectures the Hilbert--Pólya operator
comes from quantum gravity; primary-source documentary). *At
[@Atiyah2010IMPALecture 1:00:38--1:01:35], Atiyah states: "Hilbert's
dream was \[that\] if you can find an actual physical interpretation of
the operator whose spectrum gives you the zeros, \[it would even prove\]
the Riemann Hypothesis. Well, this is the dream; it's still a dream.
Alain Connes has tried to get \[even\] the Riemann Hypothesis out of his
framework; he hasn't quite succeeded. And I'm expecting that Connes has
not succeeded because he has \[not\] really touched gravity properly,
because \[he is\] dealing with associative algebras. So if I want to
leap to a \[very brave\] big conjecture, I want to \[say\] this: the
Riemann Hypothesis should come out of quantum gravity. It should somehow
correspond to the Hamiltonian of quantum gravity, if we know what that
means. We don't know quantum gravity yet --- its theory does not yet
exist. If we do have the theory, then we may be in the heart of the
question what is the Hamiltonian of that theory. That would be very
fundamental operator \[\...\] \[it\] obviously has to be self-adjoint,
and \[if it is\] so fundamental, it might be related \[to\] number
theory. So you close a circle, and you achieve Hilbert's \[dream\]."*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 (documentary) at the source [@Atiyah2010IMPALecture
1:00:38--1:01:35]. ◻
:::

##### Why quantum gravity? The seven reasons {#why-quantum-gravity-the-seven-reasons .unnumbered}

The conjecture that quantum gravity supplies the Hilbert--Pólya
Hamiltonian is the convergence of several independent arguments in
mathematics and physics. We collect them, both for documentation and to
identify the framework's specific contribution to each.

::: {#rem:SevenReasonsQuantumGravityRiemann .remark}
*Remark 387* (The seven reasons quantum gravity is the candidate source
of the Hilbert--Pólya operator).

**Reason 1: The Hilbert--Pólya conjecture itself (Pólya c. 1910s,
Hilbert c. 1910s).** The non-trivial Riemann zeros lie on the critical
line $\Re(s) = 1/2$ --- i.e., they have the form $\rho_n = 1/2 + iE_n$.
If there existed a self-adjoint operator $H$ whose spectrum was
$\{E_n\}$, then the zeros would automatically lie on the critical line,
because self-adjoint operators have purely real spectra. The Riemann
Hypothesis would reduce to "find this $H$." Self-adjoint operators are
the Hamiltonians of quantum mechanics; hence the search is for a
quantum-mechanical system whose Hamiltonian has the right spectrum.

**Reason 2: Montgomery--Odlyzko (1972/1987) --- GUE statistics,
empirical.** Hugh Montgomery, studying pair correlations of the Riemann
zeros, met Freeman Dyson at tea at Princeton. Dyson recognised
Montgomery's pair-correlation function as identical to the
pair-correlation of eigenvalues of large random Hermitian matrices in
the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble (GUE) --- matrices that arise in quantum
chaos. Andrew Odlyzko's numerical computations of millions of Riemann
zeros confirmed the GUE statistics to extraordinary
precision [@Odlyzko1987Riemann]. This is empirical evidence that the
Riemann zeros are the eigenvalues of a quantum chaotic system whose
time-reversal symmetry is broken (GUE arises specifically when
time-reversal symmetry is broken; if it were preserved, one would expect
the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble).

**Reason 3: Berry--Keating (1999) --- the $H = xp$ Hamiltonian.**
Michael Berry and Jonathan Keating proposed [@BerryKeating1999Riemann]
that the classical Hamiltonian $H_{\rm cl} = xp$ (the dilation operator)
regularised to a finite phase space gives, semiclassically, the smooth
counting function of the Riemann zeros. The trajectories of
$H_{\rm cl} = xp$ are hyperbolas in phase space. The Berry--Keating
model satisfies two of the three conditions required of the
Hilbert--Pólya Hamiltonian: it breaks time-reversal symmetry (under
$T: x \to x, p \to -p$, $H = xp \to -xp$) and is quasi-one-dimensional.
It fails the chaos condition because the classical trajectories are not
closed periodic orbits.

**Reason 4: Connes (1996--present) --- the adelic spectral
interpretation.** Alain Connes [@Connes1999Trace] constructed an
operator (acting on a certain adelic adèle-class space) whose "spectrum
is the Riemann zeros" in the sense that the zeros appear as missing
modes --- an absorption-spectrum-like construction. Connes showed the
Riemann Hypothesis is equivalent to a trace formula for this operator.
This is the noncommutative-geometry route, which Atiyah explicitly
discusses in the 2010 talk and identifies as not having succeeded.

**Reason 5: The Riemann--Weil explicit formula --- primes are classical,
zeros are quantum.** The Riemann--Weil explicit formula relates the
Riemann zeros to the prime numbers via a precise functional identity. In
the quantum-chaos interpretation: the primes correspond to classical
periodic orbits with periods $\log p$, and the zeros are quantum
eigenvalues. The Gutzwiller trace formula relates the eigenvalues of a
quantum chaotic system to its classical periodic orbits in exactly this
form. The conclusion: a quantum chaotic system whose classical periodic
orbits are the primes (with periods $\log p$) would yield the Riemann
zeros as eigenvalues. The Gutzwiller formula connects quantum mechanics
on a chaotic Hamiltonian to a number-theoretic object (the primes); this
is the foundation for the Hilbert--Pólya programme.

**Reason 6: Why quantum gravity specifically (Atiyah 2010).** Three
sub-arguments converge:

-   *Quantum gravity produces a fundamental Hamiltonian.* Atiyah's
    verbatim argument [@Atiyah2010IMPALecture 1:00:50--1:01:20]: "If we
    do have the theory \[of quantum gravity\], then we may be in the
    heart of the question what is the Hamiltonian of that theory. That
    would be very fundamental operator \[\...\] \[if it is\] so
    fundamental, it might be related \[to\] number theory."

-   *Black-hole physics produces chaos at the right scale.*
    Quantum-chaos work on black holes (the Maldacena chaos bound; the
    SYK model; JT gravity) explicitly produces chaotic Hamiltonians.
    Recent work (Betzios--Gaddam--Papadoulaki
    2020 [@BetziosGaddamPapadoulaki2020]) explicitly proposes the
    near-horizon dynamics of Schwarzschild black holes as the source of
    the Berry--Keating-type Hamiltonian, with the spectrum approximately
    matching the Riemann zeros.

-   *The Atiyah--Moore shifted-Einstein--Maxwell equations produce the
    cosmological constant scale.* The Atiyah--Moore retardation
    construction produces a small but nonzero cosmological constant of
    the right order naturally [@AtiyahMoore2010ShiftedView], suggesting
    the relevant gravitational physics is at the cosmological-constant
    scale --- the same scale that quantum-gravity models for the Riemann
    zeros operate at.

**Reason 7: Recent realisations --- the Dirac operator in Rindler
spacetime.** A 2017 result by Sierra [@Sierra2017RiemannZerosSpectrum]
constructs a massless Dirac fermion propagating in Rindler spacetime,
under the action of delta-function potentials at the square-free
integers, whose spectrum is exactly the Riemann zeros (in a precise
limit). A 2025 paper [@Majorana2025] extends this to a Majorana
relativistic quantum spectral approach in $(1+1)$-dimensional Rindler
spacetime, claiming a Hilbert--Pólya operator with the correct spectrum.
*The Dirac operator --- the unique first-order Lorentz-invariant
differential operator that Atiyah 2010 identifies, and the
operator-theoretic foundation of
Proposition [263](#prop:GeneratorFlow){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:GeneratorFlow"} of the present paper --- is the natural
object* producing Riemann zeros as eigenvalues in Rindler-type
spacetimes with broken time-reversal symmetry.

**Summary.** The seven reasons converge to the same picture: the
Hilbert--Pólya operator should be a self-adjoint,
time-reversal-symmetry-broken, chaotic Hamiltonian associated to a
dilation-like dynamics; the candidate is the Hamiltonian of quantum
gravity; the natural first-order operator is the Dirac operator; the
natural spacetime is Rindler-like with a horizon, with broken
time-reversal symmetry at the substrate level.
:::

##### The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's specific contribution to each of the seven reasons {#the-mcgucken-dx_4dt-ic-frameworks-specific-contribution-to-each-of-the-seven-reasons .unnumbered}

::: {#thm:McGuckenSuppliesSevenReasons .theorem}
**Theorem 388** (The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework supplies the
content of each of the seven Riemann-via-quantum-gravity reasons). *The
framework's candidate Hilbert--Pólya operator is the McGucken operator
$D_M$ acting on $L^2(\mathcal{M}_G, S)$, where $S$ is the spinor bundle
and $\mathcal{M}_G$ is the McGucken-extended four-space. We document the
framework's specific contribution to each of the seven reasons of
Remark [387](#rem:SevenReasonsQuantumGravityRiemann){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:SevenReasonsQuantumGravityRiemann"}:*

1.  ***Hilbert--Pólya self-adjointness:** The McGucken operator $D_M$ is
    constructed in [@MG-Master2Chains-2026] as a self-adjoint operator
    on $L^2(\mathcal{M}_G, S)$ by the standard symmetric-extension
    procedure
    (Theorem [282](#thm:QuantumIIsEvolutionGenerator){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:QuantumIIsEvolutionGenerator"}, H11.7); the
    requirement is met by construction.*

2.  ***GUE statistics / broken time-reversal:** Aspect A4 of the
    McGucken Principle
    (Proposition [257](#prop:AspectDecomposition){reference-type="ref"
    reference="prop:AspectDecomposition"}) is the one-way orientation of
    the $+ic$ advance, which is intrinsically
    time-reversal-symmetry-broken at the substrate level (not introduced
    ad hoc as in Berry--Keating). The framework therefore predicts GUE
    statistics for its spectrum at the substrate level: the Riemann
    zeros' GUE-statistical pattern is the expected statistical signature
    of the framework's substrate.*

3.  ***$H = xp$ / dilations:** The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}$
    expands at $c$ spherically symmetrically from every event --- this
    is a dilation flow on the spherical $S^2$ slice times an inflating
    radial coordinate. The Hamiltonian for the radial expansion of the
    McGucken Sphere has the structure of an $xp$-type dilation operator,
    but with the dilation built into the substrate rather than imposed
    by hand on a fixed background.*

4.  ***Connes adelic / spectral:** The framework already integrates the
    Connes spectral-triple machinery as a Channel-A reading of
    $dx_4/dt = ic$ (the present paper's Theorems A--H,
    bibitem [@MG-Connes]). Connes's adelic Riemann construction is in
    this language a Channel-A noncommutative-geometric construction; the
    framework's reading is that Connes's construction is correct as far
    as it goes, but the gravitational content (which the source-pair
    Channel B supplies through the Compton clock H12) is missing from
    the Connes side. This is Atiyah's diagnosis
    (Proposition [386](#prop:AtiyahHilbertPolyaQuantumGravity){reference-type="ref"
    reference="prop:AtiyahHilbertPolyaQuantumGravity"}) made precise.*

5.  ***Riemann--Weil / primes-as-classical-orbits / Gutzwiller:** The
    framework's Compton-frequency identification of mass
    (Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}, H10) gives every massive species
    a fundamental winding rate $\omega_C^{(f)} = m_f c^2 / \hbar$ around
    the $x_4$-direction. The set of these winding rates, taken as
    classical periodic orbits in the Gutzwiller correspondence, is a
    candidate orbit-set for the quantum-chaos picture. This is an
    empirically grounded set: the species spectrum of the Standard
    Model. Whether the prime-number-orbit structure of the Riemann--Weil
    formula descends from the species-mass Compton structure of the
    framework is an open question.*

6.  ***Quantum gravity / cosmological-constant scale:** The framework's
    gravitational Compton clock
    (Theorem [254](#thm:GravitationalComptonClock){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:GravitationalComptonClock"}, H12) supplies gravity
    from Channel B; the MG-Cosmology paper [@MG-Cosmology] produces the
    cosmological-domain observations (including the dark-energy density
    $w(z=0) = -0.983$, the cosmological constant scale empirically
    pinned). The Atiyah--Moore shifted-equations cosmological-constant
    scale
    (Remark [380](#rem:AtiyahMooreCCMcGuckenGravity){reference-type="ref"
    reference="rem:AtiyahMooreCCMcGuckenGravity"}) is the same physics
    seen at the field-theoretic level. The framework is one of the few
    candidates that simultaneously has a derivation of the Standard
    Model gauge group, a derivation of gravity, and a working
    cosmological-constant scale.*

7.  ***Dirac in Rindler:** The framework's $x_4$-direction is precisely
    a Rindler-type horizon structure: $x_4$ advances at $c$ from every
    event, and the wavefront $S^3$ of expanding spheres is the surface
    on which causal connection breaks down --- a Rindler-like horizon at
    every event. The framework's Dirac operator is therefore
    intrinsically a Dirac operator in a Rindler-type spacetime, with the
    one-way A4 orientation breaking time-reversal symmetry at the
    substrate level. The Sierra--Majorana realisations are accessible
    from the framework's substrate directly.*

*The framework's contribution to the Hilbert--Pólya / quantum-gravity /
Riemann-zeros programme is therefore: the candidate operator $D_M$ is
constructible at the framework's substrate, the GUE statistics is
intrinsic to the one-way orientation A4, the chaotic dilation structure
is intrinsic to the McGucken Sphere's expansion, the Connes integration
is already accomplished at the Channel-A level, the species spectrum is
empirically grounded, gravity is derived (H12 with empirical
MG-Cosmology corroboration), and the Rindler-Dirac structure is
intrinsic to the $x_4$-direction.*
:::

::: proof
*Grade..* G1 for each of (R1) (operator construction), (R2) (A4
orientation), (R7) (Rindler-Dirac structure) where the framework's
structure is theorem-graded in the present paper or in cited papers. G2
for (R3) (dilation structure of $\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}$), (R5)
(Compton-spectrum-as-orbits identification), (R6) (cosmological-constant
scale identification with Atiyah--Moore). The G2 elements are candidates

and the MG-Cosmology empirical record; promotion to G1 would require

of Open Problem 3 below. ◻
