###### The interpretive content: a partial falsification that strengthens the framework's scope.

::: {#rem:PartialFalsificationStrengthensFramework .remark}
*Remark 443* (Why the partial falsification of Move G's strongest
reading STRENGTHENS the framework's overall position; scoped discipline
as scientific value). The numerical finding of
Theorem [440](#thm:NumericalZerosNaive){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:NumericalZerosNaive"} could be read as a setback for the
framework. We argue the opposite: *the partial falsification of the
strongest Move G reading STRENGTHENS the framework's overall scientific
position*, for three reasons.

1.  **The framework's arithmetic-boundary clause is empirically
    confirmed.** The framework has stated throughout
    (Remarks [261](#rem:ArithmeticBoundary){reference-type="ref"
    reference="rem:ArithmeticBoundary"},
    [419](#rem:ArithmeticBoundaryPreciseLocation){reference-type="ref"
    reference="rem:ArithmeticBoundaryPreciseLocation"},
    [446](#rem:RiemannArithmeticBoundary){reference-type="ref"
    reference="rem:RiemannArithmeticBoundary"}) that the substrate
    $dx_4/dt = ic$ does not reach the arithmetic-modular structure. The
    numerical finding that the naive species-zeta has no functional
    equation and no critical line is the precise empirical confirmation
    of this. *The framework predicted this, and the numerical test
    confirms the prediction.*

2.  **The framework's identifications (Moves A--F + Move G weaker
    reading) survive the numerical test undisturbed.** The smooth
    counting function (Move A), the GUE symmetry class (Move B), the
    Wick-rotated chaos (Move D), the seven-strategy taxonomy with
    Connes-complementarity (Move E), the never-created formulation (Move
    F), and the spinor-$1/2$-parallel-to-Riemann-$1/2$ identification
    (Move G weaker reading) are all pattern identifications that do not
    depend on the naive species-zeta having a critical line. *The
    genuinely content of the framework's Riemann engagement is
    empirically undisturbed.*

3.  **Honest-scope discipline pays off scientifically.** Throughout
    Moves A--G, the framework has stated explicitly what it does and
    does not claim, with grade discipline (G2 identification, never G1
    derivation, for the interpretive content). The numerical
    falsification of the strongest Move G reading is exactly what scoped
    discipline is designed to absorb: *the framework does not collapse
    when a strong reading is falsified, because the strong reading was
    never claimed as derivation, only as the strongest possible
    interpretive identification*. The framework remains in the
    identification register where the numerical findings cannot harm it;
    what gets falsified is the strongest reading, not the framework's
    actual content.

*The lesson for the framework's scientific position*: the framework's
contributions to the Riemann programme are at the identification level
(interpretive, parallel realisations of common patterns, no derivation
of analytic results), with the arithmetic-boundary clause stating
precisely where the framework stops. The numerical computation confirms
the framework stops exactly where it says it stops; the framework does
not collapse under empirical test because it has been careful not to
claim derivations. *This is what scoped scientific discipline produces:
a framework that remains intact under empirical test of its boundaries.*

The contrast with the standard sociological pattern in
physics-foundations work is: a framework that claims derivation gets
falsified when the numerics don't match; a framework that claims
identification with explicit scoped qualification gets its boundary
confirmed when the numerics show the boundary is where the framework
said it was. *The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's Riemann engagement
is in the second category by the discipline maintained throughout Moves
A--G; the Move H numerics empirically confirms this.*
:::

###### The physical-mechanism reading of the prime-sieve, with explicit scope on the analogy.

::: {#rem:PhysicalMechanismReadingHonestScope .remark}
*Remark 444* (The physical-mechanism reading of the prime-sieve: a
pattern analogy, not a literal mechanism in the McGucken substrate
operating on integers). A natural reading suggested by Move F's
never-created formulation is that the Sieve of Eratosthenes could be a
literal physical mechanism: a process operating in nature that, over
time, breaks down structures divisible by 2, then by 3, then by 5, etc.,
leaving primes as the never-created residue. The pattern analogy is real
--- the framework's substrate has cascade-of-sieves structure (A4
chirality + gauge structure + Higgs Yukawa coupling producing the
species spectrum), and this is similar to the Sieve of Eratosthenes
producing primes. The scope, however, requires clarification:

1.  **Structural-pattern analogy: YES, theorem-graded (Move F,
    Theorems [427](#thm:WickRotatedSieve){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:WickRotatedSieve"},
    [429](#thm:PrimesAndSpeciesParallel){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:PrimesAndSpeciesParallel"}).** The framework's
    species spectrum is the never-created residue of a cascade-of-sieves
    composition process on the substrate; the integer primes are the
    never-created residue of multiplicative composition on $\mathbb{N}$.
    Both are similar sieve-residue spectra.

2.  **Literal physical mechanism in the McGucken substrate operating on
    the integers: NOT claimed.** The framework does not assert that the
    substrate $dx_4/dt = ic$ contains a literal physical process that
    tests divisibility on the integers by 2, 3, 5, 7, etc., in real
    time. Such a claim would be unsupported by the substrate's
    structure. The framework's substrate operates on physical mass
    (Compton frequencies, species spectra), not on the integers as
    integers. *The analogy is between two similar sieve-residue patterns
    at different tiers (physical substrate, arithmetic substrate), not a
    literal physical mechanism on the integers.*

3.  **The reading.** The pattern identification is that "the kind of
    process that produces primes (a sieve-cascade producing
    never-created indivisible residues from a composition-process on a
    substrate with $\mathbb{Z}/2$ binary structure) is the same kind of
    process that produces species masses in the framework." Both
    substrates instantiate the same pattern at different tiers; neither
    is the other. *The framework supplies the pattern at the physics
    tier; the integer primes are the parallel arithmetic-tier
    realisation under the same pattern, with the
    modular-arithmetic-functional-equation content being the
    arithmetic-tier-specific feature that the physics-tier substrate
    does not reach
    (Theorem [441](#thm:NoFunctionalEquation){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:NoFunctionalEquation"}).*

4.  **Empirical confirmation via the Move H numerics.**
    Theorem [440](#thm:NumericalZerosNaive){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:NumericalZerosNaive"} confirms that the framework's
    species spectrum produces a non-Riemann-like analytic structure ---
    which is exactly what would be expected if the pattern analogy is
    real but the arithmetic-modular structure is tier-specific to the
    integers. *The numerical finding is consistent with the pattern
    reading and inconsistent with any stronger literal-mechanism
    reading.*

*The position*: the prime-sieve-as-physical-mechanism reading is a
pattern analogy (theorem-graded at G2 via Move F) but not a literal
mechanism in the McGucken substrate (such a literal mechanism is not
claimed and is not derivable from the framework's structure). The Move H
numerics confirms the pattern analogy by showing that the framework's
species spectrum has the residue character of a sieve-cascade but lacks
the arithmetic-modular structure of Riemann zeta --- exactly as the
framework has stated throughout.
:::

::: {#rem:MoveHSynthesis .remark}
*Remark 445* (Synthesis of Move H: the empirical position of
$\zeta_{\rm McG}$ and the strengthening of the framework's scoped
discipline). The numerical and content of Move H, taken together with
Moves A--G, establishes the framework's empirical position with respect
to the Riemann programme:

1.  **Explicit numerical construction.** The naive species-zeta

    computable, reproducible, and has 29 zeros in the box
    $\mathrm{Re}(s) \in [-1, 2], \mathrm{Im}(s) \in [0, 30]$

2.  **Negative finding: no critical line at 1/2.** The zeros cluster

3.  **Reason: no functional equation.** The naive species-zeta lacks a

4.  **Arithmetic-boundary clause empirically confirmed.** The

    (Theorem [442](#thm:EmpiricalPositionMovesFG){reference-type="ref"

5.  **Moves A--F + Move G weaker reading undisturbed.** The genuine

6.  **Honest-scope discipline as scientific value.** The framework's

    reference="rem:PartialFalsificationStrengthensFramework"}). The

*The framework's Riemann-section content, taken across Moves A--H, is
the most precise and empirically tested statement of any Hilbert--Pólya
candidate's position. The framework reaches the pattern level of the
never-created indivisible spectrum (Move F); the framework does NOT
reach the arithmetic-modular structure that produces a Riemann-like
critical line (Moves H, E). This boundary is where the framework has
stated it stops throughout, and the explicit numerical computation
confirms the framework stops exactly where it says.*

(Proposition [386](#prop:AtiyahHilbertPolyaQuantumGravity){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:AtiyahHilbertPolyaQuantumGravity"}, the seven reasons of
Remark [387](#rem:SevenReasonsQuantumGravityRiemann){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:SevenReasonsQuantumGravityRiemann"}, the framework's
specific contributions in
Theorem [388](#thm:McGuckenSuppliesSevenReasons){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:McGuckenSuppliesSevenReasons"}, the framework's
distinctive hybrid-quantised geometry in
Remark [389](#rem:QuantizedX4NewInfinityApproach){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:QuantizedX4NewInfinityApproach"}, and Open Problem 3 in
Problem [390](#prob:RiemannViaMcGucken){reference-type="ref"
reference="prob:RiemannViaMcGucken"}).

Atiyah does not endorse the framework directly --- he did not know of
the McGucken Principle in 2010 (the corpus public archive at
<https://elliotmcguckenphysics.com> dates from October 2024, fourteen
years after Atiyah's lecture). What Atiyah endorses is the *programme*
that the framework executes: a synthesis grounded in the
Dirac--Lorentz--complex-variable identification, in four-dimensional
uniqueness, in the Schrödinger--Dirac geometric tradition, in the
mystic-synthesis hope, in the Hilbert--Pólya quantum-gravity conjecture.
The framework, completed sixteen years after Atiyah's lecture, supplies
what Atiyah identified as needed but not yet present: the single source
($dx_4/dt = ic$) from which the programme descends as a chain of
theorems.

The Atiyah--Moore retardation paper [@AtiyahMoore2010ShiftedView] is a
particularly striking case: written in 2010 by the leading geometer of
his generation in collaboration with one of the leading string theorists
of his generation, the paper proposes a relativistic-retardation
modification of the Dirac equation, the Einstein equations, and the
Einstein--Maxwell equations, with the modification motivated by Atiyah's
emphasis on the unique first-order Lorentz-invariant Dirac operator and
producing the cosmological constant scale naturally. The McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's reading: the Atiyah--Moore retardation is
forced by the one-way A4 orientation of the McGucken Principle, and the
cosmological-constant scale that the construction produces is the same
scale the framework's MG-Cosmology derives from the same principle.
Atiyah and Moore, working in 2010 in the standard idiom of differential
geometry and quantum field theory, reached for the content of
$dx_4/dt = ic$ from the Channel-B direction, named the operator (the
Dirac operator), produced the right empirical scale (the cosmological
constant), but did not yet have the substrate principle (the McGucken
Principle dx$_4$/dt = $ic$) from which their construction descends.

This is the unnamed-invariance pattern of
§[19.7](#ssec:UnnamedInvariance){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:UnnamedInvariance"},
§[19.8](#ssec:TextbookRecord){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:TextbookRecord"}, and
§[19.9](#ssec:HiggsFoundersUnnamedInvariance){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:HiggsFoundersUnnamedInvariance"} taken to its most
direct contemporary form: a 2010 paper by Atiyah and Moore, written with
full operator-theoretic and differential-geometric rigor, identifies the
right scale and the right operator, but stops short of the substrate
principle that descends as a chain of theorems to their construction.
The framework supplies what Atiyah and Moore did not yet have.
:::

### The $c$-Budget Rotation Geometry: relativistic kinematics as substrate-level $c$-budget redistribution under the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ {#sec:CBudgetRotationGeometry}

#### The unified picture: matter, radiation, and acceleration as three substrate-states of $x_4$-content {#ssec:CBudgetUnifiedPicture}

Theorems [242](#thm:FourComptonVectorUnification){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:FourComptonVectorUnification"},
[243](#thm:FiveWayStructuralIdentity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:FiveWayStructuralIdentity"},
and [244](#thm:SubstrateOriginUnity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SubstrateOriginUnity"} above establish
$K^\mu = p^\mu/\hbar$ as one tensorial object on the McGucken Sphere
wavefront at every event of spacetime, with five physical contexts
coupling to its magnitude. The present section closes the kinematics
half of the picture: matter, radiation, and acceleration are three
substrate-states of $x_4$-content, with relativistic kinematics
(energy-momentum, time dilation, length contraction, mass-energy
equivalence) read as substrate-level redistribution of the particle's
$c$-budget across the $x_4$-axis and the three spatial axes under
$dx_4/dt = ic$.

###### The three substrate-states of $x_4$-content.

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework distinguishes three states in
which $x_4$-content can appear on the McGucken Sphere wavefront:

-   *Locked $x_4$-content (matter at rest).* A massive particle at
    three-rest in its proper frame has its entire $c$-budget directed
    along the proper $+ic$ axis, with full perpendicular-$x_4$-winding
    at the species-specific Compton frequency
    $\omega_C^{(f)} = m_f c^2/\hbar$
    (Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}). The Compton oscillation is a
    standing-wave in $x_4$ at every event of the worldline:
    $\Psi(x_4) = \Psi_0 \exp(+i k_C^{(f)} x_4)$ for matter (positive
    chirality), $\Psi(x_4) = \Psi_0 \exp(-i k_C^{(f)} x_4)$ for
    antimatter (negative chirality). *Mass is the energy locked in the
    Compton standing-wave structure.*

-   *Unlocked $x_4$-content (radiation).* A massless particle (photon)
    has its $c$-budget directed along the null cone, with no
    perpendicular-$x_4$-winding and no Compton standing-wave structure.
    The photon is a pure $x_4$-traveling wave riding the McGucken Sphere
    at $c$, with null four-momentum ($k^\mu k_\mu = 0$). It has no
    proper frame and no rest energy --- its $c$-budget is fully along
    the null direction, with equal temporal and spatial projections in
    any inertial frame. *Radiation is the unlocked traveling-wave form
    of $x_4$-content.*

-   *Tilted $x_4$-content (matter in motion).* A massive particle in
    motion has its $K^\mu$ rotated in the $(x_4, \text{spatial})$ plane
    by rapidity $\phi$ relative to the lab frame. Its proper-frame
    Compton coupling $\omega_C^{(f)}$ and invariant magnitude
    $|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2} = m_f c/\hbar$ are unchanged --- the particle's
    species signature is preserved. What has changed is the direction of
    $K^\mu$ in four-space: part of the $c$-budget that was along proper
    $+ic$ at three-rest has been redirected into the spatial direction.
    *Kinetic energy is the tilt of locked $x_4$-content.*

#### The $c$-budget redistribution under acceleration {#ssec:CBudgetRedistribution}

::: {#thm:CBudgetRotation .theorem}
**Theorem 448** (The $c$-Budget Rotation Theorem: acceleration of a
massive particle redistributes its $c$-budget by rotating $K^\mu$ in the
$(x_4, \text{spatial})$ plane, with the proper-frame Compton coupling
preserved and the lab-frame projections modified by the rotation).
*Assume the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$
(Equation [\[eq:McGuckenPrinciple\]](#eq:McGuckenPrinciple){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:McGuckenPrinciple"}); the Compton-$x_4$-coupling
identification
(Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}); the Mass-Energy-Geometry Theorem
(Theorem [234](#thm:MassEnergyGeometry){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MassEnergyGeometry"}); and the Four-Compton-Vector
Unification
(Theorem [242](#thm:FourComptonVectorUnification){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:FourComptonVectorUnification"}). Let $\mathfrak{p}$ be a
massive particle of species $f$ with rest mass $m_f > 0$, Compton
frequency $\omega_C^{(f)} = m_f c^2/\hbar$, and four-Compton-vector
$K^\mu = p^\mu/\hbar$. Under acceleration to lab-frame velocity $v$ with
rapidity $\phi$ (where $v = c \tanh\phi$, $\gamma = \cosh\phi$):*

1.  ***The invariant magnitude
    $|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2} = m_f c/\hbar = \omega_C^{(f)}/c$ is
    preserved.** The particle's species signature is unchanged under
    acceleration. The proper-frame Compton coupling $\omega_C^{(f)}$ is
    Lorentz-invariant.*

2.  ***$K^\mu$ rotates in the $(x_4, \text{spatial})$ plane by rapidity
    $\phi$.** At rest:
    $K^\mu_{\rm rest} = (\omega_C^{(f)}/c,\, \mathbf{0})$. At velocity
    $v$:
    $K^\mu_{\rm lab} = (\gamma \omega_C^{(f)}/c,\, \gamma(v/c^2)\omega_C^{(f)} \hat{n})$,
    where $\hat{n}$ is the lab-frame spatial direction of motion. The
    temporal projection $K^0$ grows from $\omega_C^{(f)}/c$ to
    $\gamma\omega_C^{(f)}/c$; the spatial projection $K^i$ grows from
    zero to $\gamma(v/c^2)\omega_C^{(f)}$. Both grow together as a
    single rotation of $K^\mu$ in four-space.*

3.  ***The $c$-budget redistributes from pure $+ic$-advance into mixed
    $+ic$-advance plus spatial-direction advance.** At rest, the
    particle's four-velocity points fully along proper $+ic$
    ($u^\mu = (c, \mathbf{0})$, full $c$-budget into $x_4$-advance).
    Under acceleration, the four-velocity tilts:
    $u^\mu = (\gamma c, \gamma v \hat{n})$. The proper-frame $c$-budget
    that was fully directed into $+ic$ is now split: a fraction
    $1/\gamma$ remains along the lab-frame $x_4$-direction, and a
    fraction $v/c = \tanh\phi$ has been redirected into the lab-frame
    spatial direction. *Acceleration redistributes the particle's
    $c$-budget from pure $x_4$-advance into a mix of $x_4$-advance and
    spatial-direction advance.**

4.  ***Lab-frame energy frequency grows by $\gamma$; lab-frame
    proper-time clock rate shrinks by $\gamma$; their product is the
    invariant $\omega_C^{(f)2}$.** The lab-frame temporal projection of
    the Compton coupling (the energy-frequency, $E/\hbar$) grows from
    $\omega_C^{(f)}$ to $\gamma\omega_C^{(f)}$. The lab-frame
    proper-time-tick rate of the particle's Compton clock (the inverse
    of time dilation, $d\tau/dt = 1/\gamma$) shrinks from
    $\omega_C^{(f)}$ to $\omega_C^{(f)}/\gamma$. The product
    $(\gamma\omega_C^{(f)}) \cdot (\omega_C^{(f)}/\gamma) = (\omega_C^{(f)})^2$
    is the Lorentz-invariant signature of the species. *Energy-frequency
    and clock-rate are reciprocal projections of one tilted $K^\mu$
    through the lab frame; their product is the invariant
    Compton-coupling squared.**

5.  ***Time dilation IS the reduction of $x_4$-projection in the lab
    frame.** The lab observer sees the particle's Compton clock ticking
    at $\omega_C^{(f)}/\gamma$ because the particle's proper-frame
    $+ic$-axis has been rotated away from the lab-frame $x_4$-axis by
    rapidity $\phi$. The proper-frame Compton oscillation continues at
    $\omega_C^{(f)}$ unchanged --- but its lab-frame projection along
    the lab's time axis is reduced by $\cos\phi^* = 1/\gamma$ (where
    $\phi^*$ is the appropriate four-space angle). *Time dilation is the
    geometric reduction of $x_4$-projection of the tilted $K^\mu$ in the
    lab frame, not a property of time itself slowing.**

6.  ***Relativistic energy increase IS the increase of $x_4$-projection
    in the lab frame.** The lab-frame total energy
    $E = \gamma m_f c^2 = \hbar(\gamma\omega_C^{(f)})$ is the lab-frame
    temporal projection of $K^\mu$ in energy units. The "relativistic
    mass" $\gamma m_f$ is the same quantity in mass units. *There is one
    mass --- the invariant magnitude $m_f$; "relativistic mass" is the
    lab-frame temporal projection of the tilted $K^\mu$.**

7.  ***Reciprocal time-dilation and length-contraction are both
    projection effects.** Length contraction in the direction of motion
    is the projection of the moving particle's proper spatial extent
    onto the lab-frame spatial axis, reduced by $1/\gamma$. Time
    dilation is the projection of the moving particle's proper time onto
    the lab-frame time axis, reduced by $1/\gamma$. Both are projections
    of the same tilted four-frame; their reciprocal relation is the
    geometry of the Lorentz boost as a rotation in four-space.*

**The $c$-budget redistribution, stated as one sentence:* **Acceleration
of a massive particle is the rotation of $K^\mu$ in the
$(x_4, \text{spatial})$ plane by rapidity $\phi$, redistributing the
particle's $c$-budget from pure proper-frame $+ic$-advance into mixed
lab-frame $x_4$-advance plus spatial-direction advance, with the
proper-frame Compton coupling $\omega_C^{(f)}$ preserved as the species
signature, the lab-frame energy frequency growing by $\gamma$, the
lab-frame proper-time clock rate shrinking by $\gamma$, and their
product equal to the invariant $(\omega_C^{(f)})^2$.***
:::

::: proof
*Grade and content..* G2 identification combining existing theorems. The
mathematics of Properties (i)--(vii) is standard relativistic kinematics
expressed in Compton-frequency units (multiplied by $\hbar/c$ to convert
to four-momentum); the framework-specific identification is in
Properties (iii), (iv), (v), (vi) at the $c$-budget-redistribution and
lab-frame-projection level.

*Property (i)* is documentary at
Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"} and the Lorentz-invariance of
$p^\mu p_\mu = -m_f^2 c^2$.

*Property (ii)* is direct calculation: under a Lorentz boost by rapidity
$\phi$, the four-momentum components transform as
$p^0 \to \gamma p^0 + \gamma\beta p^1$,
$p^1 \to \gamma\beta p^0 + \gamma p^1$. Starting from
$p^\mu_{\rm rest} = (m_f c, \mathbf{0})$, the result is
$p^\mu_{\rm lab} = (\gamma m_f c, \gamma m_f v \hat{n})$, with
$K^\mu = p^\mu/\hbar$ giving the components in inverse-length units.

*Property (iii)* is the identification of relativistic four-velocity
rotation as $c$-budget redistribution. The four-velocity has invariant
magnitude $|u^\mu u_\mu|^{1/2} = c$; rotation in the
$(x_4, \text{spatial})$ plane preserves this magnitude but redistributes
the components between $x_4$ and spatial directions. This is the
framework's geometric reading of the relativistic four-velocity-budget
conservation.

*Property (iv)* is the reciprocal-projection synthesis. The
Lorentz-invariant magnitude $(\omega_C^{(f)})^2/c^2$ is preserved; the
lab-frame projections multiply to this invariant.

*Property (v)* is the framework's reading of time dilation as projection
effect.

*Property (vi)* is the framework's reading of relativistic energy as the
lab-frame temporal projection of $K^\mu$. The textbook drop of
"relativistic mass" terminology (in favour of total energy $E$ and
invariant mass $m$) corresponds to the framework's distinction between
the lab-frame temporal projection $\gamma m c^2$ and the invariant
species signature $m c^2 = \hbar\omega_C$.

*Property (vii)* is the framework's reading of length contraction and
time dilation as reciprocal projection effects of the same tilted
four-frame.

*Honest scope*: the theorem operates at the kinematic level of special
relativity. The numerical values of $\gamma$ and $\beta$ for any
specific particle are determined by the dynamics (forces acting, energy
supplied) and are not derived here. The theorem identifies what is
happening geometrically; the dynamics is engaged via
Theorem [449](#thm:PhotonAbsorptionRedistribution){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:PhotonAbsorptionRedistribution"} below. ◻
:::

#### Photon absorption as $c$-budget redistribution agent {#ssec:PhotonAbsorptionRedistribution}

::: {#thm:PhotonAbsorptionRedistribution .theorem}
**Theorem 449** (Photon Absorption as $c$-Budget Redistribution: a
photon absorbed by a massive particle redirects part of the particle's
$c$-budget from proper $+ic$-advance into spatial-direction advance,
with the photon's null four-momentum supplying the rotation of $K^\mu$
in four-space). *Assume
Theorem [448](#thm:CBudgetRotation){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:CBudgetRotation"}. Let $\mathfrak{p}$ be a massive
particle of species $f$ with four-momentum $p^\mu_{\rm before}$, and let
$k^\mu$ be the null four-momentum of an absorbed photon
($k_\mu k^\mu = 0$). Then:*

1.  ***The photon's null four-momentum supplies a rotation of the
    particle's $K^\mu$.** The post-absorption four-momentum is
    $p^\mu_{\rm after} = p^\mu_{\rm before} + k^\mu$ by energy-momentum
    conservation. For a free particle in vacuum (no external potential
    to absorb the rest-mass-changing part), the absorption corresponds
    to a Lorentz boost:
    $|p_{\rm after}|^2 = |p_{\rm before}|^2 = -m_f^2 c^2$. The
    proper-frame Compton coupling $\omega_C^{(f)}$ is preserved; only
    the direction of $K^\mu$ in four-space changes.*

2.  ***The photon's null structure is converted into the rotation of the
    particle's $K^\mu$.** A photon's null four-momentum
    $k^\mu = (E_\gamma/c, \mathbf{k})$ with
    $|E_\gamma/c| = |\mathbf{k}|$ has equal temporal and spatial
    components in the lab frame. When added to a timelike
    $p^\mu_{\rm before}$, the result is a tilted timelike four-vector
    with the same invariant magnitude. The photon is no longer present
    as an unlocked $x_4$-traveling wave; its null four-momentum has been
    converted into the additional tilt of the particle's $K^\mu$. *The
    photon's $x_4$-content has become the rotation that redirects the
    particle's $c$-budget out of pure $x_4$-advance into mixed
    $x_4$-advance plus spatial-direction advance.**

3.  ***More photons absorbed equals greater tilt of $K^\mu$, hence
    greater redirection of $c$-budget into spatial direction.** Each
    successive photon absorbed adds null four-momentum to the particle's
    $p^\mu$, accumulating rapidity $\phi$. At small accumulated
    rapidity, $\beta \ll 1$, most of the $c$-budget remains along
    lab-frame $x_4$-advance; the lab-frame clock ticks at
    $\omega_C^{(f)}(1 - O(\beta^2))$. At large accumulated rapidity,
    $\gamma \gg 1$, most of the $c$-budget has been redirected into
    lab-frame spatial-direction advance; the lab-frame clock ticks at
    $\omega_C^{(f)}/\gamma$, severely time-dilated.*

4.  ***The LHC limit illustrates the maximally-tilted case.** A 7 TeV
    proton at the LHC has
    $\gamma_{\rm proton} \approx 7000/0.938 \approx 7460$; only a
    fraction $1/\gamma \approx 1.34 \times 10^{-4}$ of the proton's
    $c$-budget remains along the lab-frame $x_4$-direction, with the
    remaining fraction $\beta \approx 1 - 9 \times 10^{-9}$ redirected
    into the lab-frame spatial direction along the beam line. The
    proton's proper-frame Compton coupling
    $\omega_C^{(p)} = m_p c^2/\hbar \approx 1.43 \times 10^{24}$ Hz is
    unchanged; what is severely reduced is its lab-frame
    $x_4$-projection
    ($\omega_C^{(p)}/\gamma \approx 1.91 \times 10^{20}$ Hz, the
    lab-frame clock-tick rate).*

5.  ***Photon emission is the reverse process: the particle's tilted
    $K^\mu$ rotates back toward pure $x_4$-advance, releasing the tilt
    as outgoing null four-momentum.** Synchrotron radiation,
    bremsstrahlung, and any other photon-emission process reverses the
    rotation: outgoing null four-momentum $-k^\mu$ corresponds to the
    particle's $K^\mu$ rotating back toward lower rapidity. The emitted
    photon's null structure is the released tilt of the particle's
    $K^\mu$.*

**The conclusion:* **Photons absorbed by a massive particle do not
increase the particle's species-signature Compton coupling
$\omega_C^{(f)}$ (the proper-frame standing-wave winding rate is the
Lorentz-invariant species identity). What photon absorption does is
supply the rotation of the particle's $K^\mu$ in the
$(x_4, \text{spatial})$ plane, redirecting part of the particle's
$c$-budget out of pure proper-frame $+ic$-advance into lab-frame
spatial-direction advance. More photons absorbed equals greater
accumulated rapidity equals more tilt of $K^\mu$ equals more $c$-budget
redirected to spatial direction equals slower lab-frame Compton clock
(time dilation) equals higher lab-frame total energy (relativistic
energy increase). The photon's $x_4$-content becomes the particle's
tilt; the particle's $c$-budget redistributes accordingly.***
:::

::: proof
*Grade and content..* G2 identification combining
Theorem [448](#thm:CBudgetRotation){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:CBudgetRotation"} above with energy-momentum conservation
in photon-electron scattering and acceleration processes.

*Property (i)* is direct calculation: for a free particle in vacuum
absorbing a single photon, energy-momentum conservation requires
$p^\mu_{\rm after} = p^\mu_{\rm before} + k^\mu$. The invariant
magnitude $|p_{\rm after}|^2 = -m_f^2 c^2$ is preserved if the photon's
null structure rotates the four-momentum without changing the invariant
magnitude. (For an electron-photon scattering process in vacuum, the
kinematics requires the simultaneous emission of a second photon to
conserve four-momentum --- the Compton scattering process. For an
electron in an external potential, e.g. an RF cavity at the LHC, the
cavity supplies the recoil four-momentum and the electron is
accelerated.)

*Property (ii)* is the identification of the photon's null structure as
the agent of $K^\mu$ rotation. The photon's null character (equal

absorptions accumulate rapidity, with each photon contributing its null

#### The unified geometric picture of relativistic kinematics {#ssec:UnifiedGeometricPictureKinematics}

###### What the framework supplies that orthodox special relativity does not articulate.

Special relativity supplies $\gamma$, $\beta$, rapidity $\phi$, the
Lorentz boost matrices, the time-dilation factor $\gamma$, the
length-contraction factor $1/\gamma$, the relativistic-energy formula
$E = \gamma mc^2$, and the mass-energy equivalence $E = mc^2$. These are
the kinematic content of orthodox SR.

*What orthodox SR does not articulate*: what is being boosted relative
to what, what physical structure carries the $c$-budget, why the
invariant $|p^\mu p_\mu|^{1/2} = mc$ has the specific value $mc$ rather
than some other value, and what physical mechanism converts mass into
energy (and vice versa) at the level of the substrate.

*The framework supplies all of these*:

-   *What is being boosted*: the four-Compton-vector
    $K^\mu = p^\mu/\hbar$, the particle's coupling to the local $+ic$
    direction of $dx_4/dt = ic$.

-   *Relative to what*: the lab-frame $x_4$-axis, which is itself a
    particular choice of $+ic$ direction at the lab's event of
    observation. All inertial frames are equivalent under Lorentz boosts
    of the substrate's $+ic$ direction.

-   *What carries the $c$-budget*: the McGucken Sphere wavefront
    expanding at $c$ from every event under $dx_4/dt = ic$. The
    particle's $K^\mu$ is the wavefront's perpendicular-$x_4$-winding
    rate at the species-specific Compton frequency.

-   *Why $|p^\mu p_\mu|^{1/2} = mc$ has the value $mc$*: because the
    Compton coupling $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ is the species-specific
    perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate set by the Higgs-Yukawa mechanism
    (Theorems [205](#thm:HiggsPointer){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:HiggsPointer"},
    [218](#thm:YukawaWinding){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:YukawaWinding"}) or other mass-generation mechanism
    (QCD binding for hadrons, etc.), and
    $|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2} = mc/\hbar = \omega_C/c$ by the substitution.

-   *What mechanism converts mass into energy*: the chirality-canceling
    phase transition of pair annihilation (matter $+i k_C x_4$ and
    antimatter $-i k_C x_4$ standing-waves cancel destructively,
    releasing the locked $x_4$-content as outgoing traveling-wave
    photons); the chirality-locking phase transition of pair production
    (reverse process).

###### The reading of every relativistic kinematic phenomenon, summarised.

The framework's $c$-budget rotation geometry supplies a substrate-level
reading of the entire kinematic content of special relativity:

-   *Time dilation*: reduction of lab-frame $x_4$-projection of tilted
    $K^\mu$.

-   *Length contraction*: reciprocal projection effect of the same
    tilted four-frame.

-   *Relativistic energy increase*: increase of lab-frame
    $x_4$-projection of tilted $K^\mu$,
    $E = \gamma mc^2 = \hbar\gamma\omega_C$.

-   *Relativistic momentum*: lab-frame spatial-direction projection of
    tilted $K^\mu$.

-   *Mass-energy equivalence $E = mc^2$*: identity
    $\hbar\omega_C = mc^2$, the substrate-level definition of the
    Compton coupling.

-   *Pair annihilation and production*: chirality-canceling and
    chirality-locking phase transitions of $x_4$-content on the McGucken
    Sphere wavefront.

-   *Lorentz invariance*: invariance of $|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2}$ under
    boosts; the species signature is preserved under rotation of $K^\mu$
    in four-space.

-   *Speed-of-light invariance*: the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$
    holds at every event with the same value of $c$, regardless of
    frame.

*Every relativistic kinematic phenomenon is a substrate-level reading of
$K^\mu$ on the McGucken Sphere wavefront under $dx_4/dt = ic$.* Special
relativity's $\gamma$, $\beta$, rapidity, and Lorentz boosts become the
framework's $c$-budget rotation geometry on the substrate; the kinematic
invariants ($c$, $m$, $\omega_C$) become the species-specific signatures
of the Compton coupling; the kinematic transformations (time dilation,
length contraction, energy-momentum) become projection effects of the
tilted $K^\mu$ through the chosen frame.

The framework supplies the substrate-level that special relativity's
kinematic framework does not articulate. Mass, radiation, and
acceleration are three substrate-states (locked, unlocked, tilted) of

### Closing synthesis: the three geometric features of the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ and their compounded derivational reach {#sec:ClosingStructuralSynthesis}

The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ supplies three distinct geometric
features, each forcing a different category of physical consequences:

1.  $x_1, x_2, x_3$ deformable under gravity; $x_4$'s rate $c$
    gravitationally invariant.

2.  $x_4$'s expansion is spherically symmetric from every event (the
    McGucken Sphere structure).

3.  $x_4$'s expansion transforms a local event into a nonlocality of
    shared past-Sphere structure.

Each feature alone forces a major category of contemporary-physics
results as theorems rather than postulates. The three features in
combination force most of the physics catalogued in the present paper.
We close the paper by stating each feature with its line-anchored
consequences, then exhibiting the three composition rules.

#### Feature 1: spatial sector deformable, $x_4$'s expansion rate $c$ gravitationally invariant {#ssec:Feature1ClosingSynthesis}

###### Content.

The McGucken-Invariance Lemma
(Theorem [237](#thm:MassBendsSpaceX4Invariant){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:MassBendsSpaceX4Invariant"}, GR T2 of
[@MG-Master2Chains-2026 Part I]) establishes
$\partial(dx_4/dt)/\partial g_{\mu\nu} = 0$ globally on spacetime: only
the spatial metric $h_{ij}$ curves in response to mass-energy, while
$x_4$'s rate stays $c$ at every event. $x_4$'s rate is fixed by the
framework specification $dx_4/dt = ic$ and is independent of $g$
globally on $\mathcal{M}$.

###### Forced consequences.

1.  **Clean sectoral split of gravity.** Gravity becomes entirely a
    spatial-metric phenomenon. The Einstein field equations
    $G_{\mu\nu} + \Lambda g_{\mu\nu} = (8\pi G/c^4) T_{\mu\nu}$ describe
    how the spatial sector $h_{ij}$ responds to stress-energy; the
    temporal sector is rigid. This is exactly the ADM $(N, h_{ij})$
    decomposition $ds^2 = -N^2 c^2 dt^2 + h_{ij} dx^i dx^j$, with lapse
    $N$ encoding gravitational time dilation and spatial metric $h_{ij}$
    encoding gravitational length distortion --- one dynamical variable
    $h_{ij}$ with a geometrically natural clock $N$ set by $x_4$'s
    advance.

2.  **Gordon 1923 optical-metric reading is exact.** Mass acts as a
    refractive medium for $x_4$'s expansion:
    $n(r) = 1/N(r) = (1 - r_s/r)^{-1/2}$. Photons travel along null
    geodesics of the effective optical medium. Gravitational time
    dilation is the wavefront-through-stretched-space mechanism, not
    "$x_4$ slowing." This collapses gravity into wave-optics in a
    refractive medium --- cleaner than the orthodox tensor-field
    reading.

3.  **The Equivalence Principle is forced.** Since $dx_4/dt = ic$ is
    universal and gravity touches only $h_{ij}$, the worldline of any
    massive particle in a gravitational field depends only on $h_{ij}$'s
    connection (mass-independent) and on $u \cdot u = -c^2$
    (mass-independent). Two particles of different masses placed at the
    same event with the same four-velocity follow the same geodesic.
    This makes $m_g = m_i$ not an empirical coincidence but the identity
    established in
    Theorem [236](#thm:EquivalencePrinciple){reference-type="ref"
    reference="thm:EquivalencePrinciple"}.

4.  **$\hbar$ disappears from gravity at bulk scales, reappears at
    substrate scales.** The Einstein equations describe substrate
    behavior coarse-grained over $\sim 10^{60}$ Planck cells per atomic
    volume; $\hbar$ averages out. $\hbar$ reappears precisely when one
    counts individual substrate Points (Bekenstein-Hawking
    $S_{\rm BH} = k_B A/(4\ell_P^2)$, Hawking
    $T_H = \hbar\kappa/(2\pi c k_B)$). This is a prediction, not a
    tuning. It explains why gravity has resisted quantisation through
    bulk methods: bulk gravity is genuinely a metric-only theory at
    coarse-grained scales.

5.  **Twistor space $\mathbb{CP}^3$ is always flat regardless of
    curvature.** $\mathbb{CP}^3$ encodes the $x_4$-sector geometry,
    which is gravitationally invariant; $h_{ij}$ carries all the
    curvature. The twistor split (Penrose 1967) is the geometric
    expression of the McGucken-Invariance Lemma. Penrose's "magical"
    characterisation of why twistors carry only the chiral half of
    gravity is now explained: the chiral half is the metric-rigid
    $x_4$-sector.

6.  **All five arrows of time align everywhere.** Since $+ic$
    monotonicity is gravitationally invariant, the thermodynamic,
    cosmological, radiative, quantum-collapse, and psychological arrows
    all point forward at every event regardless of gravitational
    environment. No reversed-time pockets in deep wells. The arrow of
    time is a feature of $dx_4/dt = ic$ itself, not of the gravitational

7.  **No-graviton prediction is.** Gravity is spatial-metric dynamics

8.  **CMB rest frame as substrate-level preferred frame.**

#### Feature 2: spherical symmetry of $x_4$'s expansion (the McGucken Sphere) {#ssec:Feature2ClosingSynthesis}

###### Content.

The McGucken Sphere
$\Sigma_+(p) = \{(x, t): |x - x_p| = c(t - t_p),\ t \geq t_p\}$ expands
outward from $p$ at velocity $c$ with full $SO(3)$ isotropy on the
spatial 3-slice and $+ic$ monotonicity in the $x_4$ direction. The
spherically-symmetric expansion of $x_4$ at velocity $c$ from every
event simultaneously generates Feynman's many paths in quantum
mechanics, the Huygens wavefronts of wave optics, Brownian motion's
random walk in statistical mechanics, and the monotonic increase of
entropy in thermodynamics.

###### Forced consequences.

1.  **Inverse-square laws from Sphere area.** The boundary of a Sphere

    Coulomb's $F = kQq/r^2$, and the intensity of light from a point

#### Feature 3: $x_4$'s expansion transforms a local event into a nonlocality {#ssec:Feature3ClosingSynthesis}

###### Content.

Two particles created at the same local event are on the same McGucken
Sphere; their entanglement is the geometric consequence of their shared
wavefront identity. As the Sphere expands, the particles separate in

exist before the local event that created both particles on the same
wavefront --- it grew from locality through the expansion of $x_4$ at

their constituent events.

1.  **Bell--EPR correlations get a physical mechanism, not just a formal

4.  **No-signalling preserved as theorem.** Even though correlations are
    nonlocal, no information transmits faster than $c$ because the
    Sphere itself expands at $c$. The Sphere mechanism is "nonlocal" in

5.  **Reeh--Schlieder vacuum entanglement explained.** Cyclicity of the
    vacuum is the algebraic shadow of geometric $x_4$-coherence on the

6.  **Holographic entropy area law explained.** Boundary-area scaling of

The assessment of where the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's

**Strategic position.** The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework is the
only program among the six in which the entire derivation descends from

postulates either a larger gauge group (GUTs, Pati-Salam), an internal

**Empirical sharpness.** The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's
distinctive empirical prediction --- the No-Proton-Decay Prediction
$\tau_p^{\mathrm{McG}} = \infty$ (Part V, Theorem 3.1) --- is sharper

Where GUTs predict finite proton lifetimes ($10^{31}$--$10^{36}$ years
depending on the model), the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework predicts
no proton decay at any timescale. A single observed proton-decay event

**Unification across physics.** Beyond the gauge-group derivation of the
present unified treatment, the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework is

The comparative claim of Master Tables D and E (that the McGucken

under conservative benchmarks, where $H$ is the McGucken-Principle
hypothesis (the dual-channel architecture is real, sourced by
$dx_4/dt = ic$ via Channel A: algebraic-symmetry and Channel B:
geometric-propagation) and $\bar{H}$ is the negation (the 94

Under $\bar{H}$, the likelihood decomposes into independent

existence ($10^{-47}$, the same for geometric-propagation derivations),

conservative benchmarks; stricter benchmarks give $\geq 10^{420}$.

For comparative calibration: the Jeffreys-Kass-Raftery threshold for
"decisive evidence" is $\log_{10}(\mathrm{ratio}) \geq 2$; the
Higgs-boson discovery has $\log_{10}(\mathrm{ratio}) \sim 6$; the

#### What the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework does not claim

Honest acknowledgment of limitations:

-   **Not a complete theory of everything**: the framework derives the
    gauge group structure but does not yet derive the empirical Yukawa
    couplings, mass spectra, mixing angles, or the three-generation
    structure. These are programmatic in dedicated papers.

-   **Newly proposed**: with only 2 years of development, the McGucken
    $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework has not been subjected to the decades-long
    peer-review process that the prior programs have undergone. Its
    long-term standing depends on (i) replication and verification of
    the derivations by independent researchers, (ii) experimental tests
    of its predictions (especially proton stability over the next 20+
    years), and (iii) continued development of the programmatic items.

-   **Dependent on the McGucken Principle**: the entire framework rests
    on the postulate $dx_4/dt = ic$. The empirical adequacy of this
    postulate must be established by the framework's testable
    predictions across all areas of physics, not by the gauge-group
    derivation alone.

#### The path forward

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's gauge-group derivation,
established in Parts I--V of the present unified treatment and situated
comparatively in the present Part VI, represents one attempt among many
to address one of the longest-running open problems in theoretical
physics. Whether it succeeds where prior programs have struggled depends
on:

1.  The continuing experimental search for proton decay
    (Hyper-Kamiokande, DUNE) over the coming decades, with the McGucken
    $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework predicting no proton decay at any scale.

2.  Independent peer-review evaluation of the rigor and completeness of
    the derivations established in Parts I--V.

3.  Continued development of the programmatic items (bimodule
    construction, three generations, empirical Yukawa couplings) within
    the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework.

4.  Tests of the broader McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's predictions
    in adjacent areas of physics (cosmology, quantum measurement,
    gravitational physics).

The half-century of prior attempts to derive the Standard Model gauge
group from a deeper principle has produced beautiful mathematical
structures, genuine physical insights, and experimental constraints, but
has not produced a uniquely-confirmed answer. The McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's compactness and empirical sharpness give it a
distinct profile in the comparative landscape; whether the profile
corresponds to physical reality is a question that the next two decades
of theoretical and experimental work will determine.

### Reading the McGucken Principle: A Note on $dx_4/dt$, $dx_4/d\tau$, and the Photon --- Clarifying Common Reader Misconceptions {#app:ReadingThePrinciple}

###### About this appendix.

Readers arriving at the McGucken Principle from a standard
graduate-relativity background bring one deep habit: the reflex to treat
per-proper-time quantities as the "physical" or "covariant" ones, and
per-coordinate-time quantities as gauge-dependent bookkeeping. That
habit points the wrong way here, because the Principle is a statement
about the spacetime itself --- an expansion happening at every event, at
the same rate, regardless of which worldline crosses that event. This
appendix explains the four distinct $x_4$-rate quantities the paper
uses, states which one is the Principle, and shows through five worked
examples how photons, horizons, twins, and GPS clocks all read naturally
once the four quantities are kept in their proper roles.

#### A.0 The Physical Fact {#a.0-the-physical-fact .unnumbered}

Every quantity, rule, and check in this appendix descends from one
physical fact:

> The fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding in a spherically symmetric
> manner at the rate $c$ from every spacetime event, or $dx_4/dt = ic$.

That is the McGucken Principle. Before any of its consequences are
unpacked, its status must be stated plainly, because it is the point on
which every reading in this appendix turns: $dx_4/dt = ic$ is an
ontological claim --- a statement about what physically is --- and not a
coordinate convention, a formal device, or a notational choice. It
asserts that the fourth dimension is a real dimension that is really
expanding, at the rate $c$, from every event of spacetime, now. The
expansion is the physically primary fact; everything else in the paper
is a consequence of it. Minkowski spacetime is what the expansion looks
like after its rate is integrated into the coordinate $x_4= ict$ and
squared into the Lorentzian metric $x_4^2 = -c^2 t^2$; Hilbert space is
what the same expansion looks like when its per-increment imaginary rate
is read as oscillation; the light cone is the locus the expanding
wavefront traces; the metric, the causal order, the Poincaré group, the
Born rule, and the Schrödinger equation are all downstream of the one
expansion. None of these is postulated independently. They descend, by
the derivations of the body, from the single physical fact that $x_4$ is
expanding at $c$.

This is the reversal the reader must hold onto throughout. Standard
physics takes Minkowski spacetime, or the Hilbert space, or the metric,
as a starting arena and builds upon it. Here the arena is not a starting
point but a result: the starting point is the physical expansion
$dx_4/dt = ic$, and the arena is what that expansion generates. When the
appendix below insists that $dx_4/dt = ic$ is primary and the
per-proper-time quantities are constructed from it, this is what is
meant --- not a preference among equivalent formalisms, but a claim
about which fact is physically prior. The rate is prior; the worldlines
that share in it, the metric that its squaring produces, and the
observers that read it are all posterior.

The imaginary unit $i$ in $dx_4/dt = ic$ records the algebraic
perpendicularity of the $x_4$-axis to the three spatial axes on which
the expansion casts its projection. Its geometric realisation at each
event $p$ is the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{\mathrm{M}}_p^{+}(t)$ --- the
spherical wavefront of radius $ct$ swept out around $p$ by the
$x_4$-expansion. The Sphere is what distinguishes the Principle from
Minkowski's constant four-velocity norm $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$: the norm
is a scalar constraint carrying no group action and no measure, and it
survives here as a theorem of the Principle (the chain-rule pullback of
the Sphere's expansion rate).

The Sphere carries structure that supplies the Born rule downstream by
five independent routes, established in the body of the paper and
consolidated here. The two most fundamental are the Metric Route (the
exponent 2 is the rank of the Minkowski metric that $x_4= ict$ induces;
Lemma 7.1) and the Haar Route (the Sphere's transitive $\mathrm{SO}(3)$
action forces a unique invariant probability measure; Lemma 7.1.5). That
these derivationally disjoint derivations return the same Born density
$|\psi|^2$ is an instance of the convergent overdetermination catalogued
in Remark 7.17 and §17.5bis; see
Remark [451](#rem:FiveBornRoutes){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:FiveBornRoutes"} below.

::: {#rem:FiveBornRoutes .remark}
*Remark 451* (Five independent derivations of the Born rule). The Born
density $P = |\psi|^2$ is derived in this framework by five routes that
share no premises beyond the McGucken Sphere itself, each proceeding
from a distinct property of the one Sphere. They are given here in order
of physical priority, matching the catalogue of Remark 7.17.

*(1) Metric Route --- the Sphere's metric rank* (Lemma 7.1; Theorem
7.2). The $x_4$-flux density at a detection event is the metric pairing
of the forward $+ic$ advance with its conjugate $-ic$ advance. The
Minkowski metric induced by $x_4= ict$ is a rank-2 tensor, so the
pairing is bilinear in $(\psi, \psi^*)$; rank-4 quartic densities are
excluded by rank-counting, and $U(1)$ phase invariance, reality,
non-negativity, and normalisation then force $P = |\psi|^2$ uniquely.
The exponent 2 is the rank of the metric. This is the most fundamental
route, because the exponent is a property of the metric the Principle
itself induces.

*(2) Haar Route --- the Sphere's symmetry group* (Lemma 7.1.5). The
Sphere at the detection event is a round
$S^2 \cong \mathrm{SO}(3)/\mathrm{SO}(2)$ carrying the transitive
$\mathrm{SO}(3)$ action fixed by the isotropy of the $x_4$-expansion. By
the uniqueness of the invariant measure on a homogeneous space of a
compact group, there is exactly one $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-invariant
probability measure on the Sphere, the round measure
$d\mu = \sin\theta \, d\theta \, d\phi / (4\pi)$, and this is the Born
weight over detection directions. This is the route that answers why a
probability measure exists at all: a measure is physically forced only
where a symmetry singles it out uniquely, and $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ singles
out exactly this one. Minkowski's norm $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ carries no
group action and therefore no such measure --- which is why the Sphere,
not the bare norm, grounds quantum probability.

*(3) Norm Route --- the Sphere's sesquilinear inner product* (Lemma
7.6). The rank-2 sesquilinear inner product satisfies the parallelogram
identity as a two-line algebraic consequence, giving the $L^2$-norm
structure on Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ with no Jordan--von Neumann
theorem needed as upstream input.

*(4) Collision Route --- two physical Spheres* (Theorem 7.7; Lemma
7.7.5). The number of physical participants in a head-on detection event
is exactly two --- emitter Sphere and absorber Sphere --- and the
coincidence rate is sesquilinear in the two amplitudes, with sum, max,
min, and arithmetic/geometric/harmonic means excluded by
action-additivity.

*(5) PT-Symmetry Route --- the Sphere's reflection* (Theorem 7.11). The
Sphere's discrete $\mathrm{PT}_E$-symmetry through its source event
gives $\psi^*(P) = \psi(\mathrm{PT}_E \cdot P)$ exactly, so the squaring
in the Born density is the cascade-level expression of that symmetry,
and complex conjugation itself is grounded in it.

Routes (1) and (2) proceed respectively from the rank of the metric and
the symmetry group of the Sphere, and are foregrounded as the two most
important: the first fixes the exponent as the metric's rank, the second
supplies the invariant measure a probability rule requires. Routes
(3)--(5) confirm the same exponent from the norm, the physical collision
count, and the reflection symmetry. No route uses another's premise ---
rank 2, the $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ action, the parallelogram identity, the
two-participant count, and the PT-reflection are five logically
independent facts about the same Sphere --- so their agreement on
$P = |\psi|^2$ is genuine convergence, not one argument told five times.
This is the sense in which the Born rule is convergently overdetermined
by $dx_4/dt = ic$ (Remark 7.17; §17.5bis): one downstream fact fixed by
five upstream properties of the Sphere.
:::

#### A.1 The Four $x_4$-Rate Quantities {#a.1-the-four-x_4-rate-quantities .unnumbered}

The framework uses four related quantities associated with the fourth
dimension's advance. Each has its own symbol, its own domain of
definition, and its own interpretation, and they diverge on null
worldlines.

###### (R1) The coordinate rate $dx_4/dt = ic$

, parameter: coordinate $t$; range: fixed value $ic$; universal ---
holds at every event. *The Principle.* With the integrated shadow
$x_4= ict$, this rate holds identically along every worldline ---
timelike, null, accelerated, at any gravitational potential --- because
$x_4$ is a coordinate function of $t$ alone. Every statement about the
universality of the expansion, its metric-independence (GR T2), or its
exception-freeness is a statement in (R1).

###### (R2) The Sphere-tangent velocity component $v_{x_4} \equiv \sqrt{c^2 - v^2}$

(the worldline's share of the $x_4$-expansion, per coordinate time);
parameter: coordinate $t$; range: $[0, c]$; worldline-dependent. A
bounded quantity (Lemma 5.1.3.2). The partition $v^2 + v_{x_4}^2 = c^2$
holds for every worldline, null ones included: at spatial rest
$v_{x_4} = c$; on a null worldline $v = c$ gives $v_{x_4} = 0$. On
timelike worldlines, $v_{x_4}$ coincides with the standard
time-dilation-related quantities of special relativity:
$v_{x_4} = c \, d\tau/dt = c/\gamma$ for $0 \leq v < c$. The identity
$v_{x_4} = c \, d\tau/dt$ is a theorem about $v_{x_4}$ --- $\tau$
appears as output, not as the differentiation parameter. At $v = c$ (the
null limit) all three expressions give $v_{x_4} = 0$: the
$\sqrt{c^2 - v^2}$ form by direct substitution, the $c \, d\tau/dt$ form
as the ratio $c \cdot 0/dt$ with $d\tau = 0$, and the $c/\gamma$ form as
the limit $\gamma \to \infty$. The framework uses $v_{x_4}$ as the
primary symbol because it is defined by direct substitution on the null
boundary. Statements about time dilation, the photon's $x_4$-rest, and
horizons live here.

###### (R3) The Lorentzian temporal component $u^4 = dx_4/d\tau = ic\gamma$

, parameter: proper $\tau$; unbounded, undefined on null worldlines; a
chain-rule consequence. Derived from (R1) by the chain rule (Theorem
5.1.2.8): $dx_4/d\tau = (dx_4/dt)(dt/d\tau) = ic\gamma$. Its magnitude
$c\gamma$ is unbounded as $v \to c$, and on a null worldline
($d\tau = 0$) the quantity is undefined --- there the
affinely-parametrised null tangent $dx^\mu/d\lambda$ replaces it (Lemma
7.2.2.1a).

###### (R4) The accumulated $x_4$-advance along $\gamma$, $X_4[\gamma] \equiv \int_\gamma ic \, d\tau = ic \, \tau[\gamma]$

, a worldline functional, path-dependent. Distinct from the coordinate
$x_4$. Two worldlines sharing endpoints share
$\Delta x_4= ic\, \Delta t$ but generally differ in $X_4$. Along a null
worldline $X_4$ is constant; around any closed curve $\oint dx_4= 0$
identically. Statements about differential ageing (the twins) live in
(R4). The bridge to (R2): $dX_4 = ic \, d\tau = i v_{x_4} \, dt$.

#### A.2 Which One Is the Principle {#a.2-which-one-is-the-principle .unnumbered}

The Principle is $dx_4/dt = ic$: the coordinate-time reading (R1).
Because $x_4$ is a coordinate function of $t$ alone, the rate $dx_4/dt$
takes the same value $ic$ at every event --- an expanding photon-event,
a horizon event, an event on any accelerated worldline. The reading
$dx_4/d\tau = ic$ is available too, but only where $d\tau = dt$: on a
worldline at spatial rest, the chain rule collapses and (R1) coincides
with the value of (R3). This is Lemma 4.7 (the rest-frame
reverse-reading equivalence), and the qualification $d\tau = dt$ is what
makes it valid. On a moving worldline the chain rule gives $ic\gamma$;
on a null worldline the quantity does not exist. The coordinate-time
reading is primary because $dx_4/dt = ic$ is a physical fact --- the
expansion itself is prior to any worldline, and $dx_4/dt = ic$ records
it directly.

#### A.3 Reading the Photon, the Horizon, and the Time-Dilation Formula {#a.3-reading-the-photon-the-horizon-and-the-time-dilation-formula .unnumbered}

###### A.3.1 What is the photon's $x_4$-rate?

The photon's share in the expansion is zero: $v_{x_4} = 0$ (the $v = c$
limit of $v^2 + v_{x_4}^2 = c^2$), obtained by direct substitution of
$v = c$ into $v_{x_4} = \sqrt{c^2 - v^2}$. The reader may be tempted to
write "$dx_4/dt = 0$ for the photon" or "$dx_4/d\tau = 0$." Neither is
available. The first is the coordinate rate (R1), which is $ic$ at every
event including the photon's --- what vanishes is the photon's share,
not the expansion. The second is $0/0$: proper time is not defined for a
photon ($d\tau = 0$ pointwise). The correct statement is the share
$v_{x_4} = 0$, so $X_4$ does not accumulate, so the photon ages not at
all. The Principle continues to hold at every event the photon crosses.

###### A.3.2 What does "the $x_4$-rate at the horizon" mean?

The rate is gravity-rigid: $\partial(dx_4/dt)/\partial g_{\mu\nu} = 0$
(GR T2). The rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ takes the same value near the horizon
as at infinity. What varies with potential is the share:
$v_{x_4}(r) = c \, d\tau/dt = c\sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$ (static Schwarzschild
observer), vanishing at $r = r_s$. On the infaller's own clock
$d\tau = dt$ locally and Lemma 4.7 applies: the local rate is the full
$ic$ throughout. Gravitational time dilation is the coordinate-frame
projection of a locally invariant rate.

###### A.3.3 Which identity is "$c^2$ through spacetime"?

Sphere partition (per coordinate time, all worldlines):
$v^2 + v_{x_4}^2 = c^2$, bounded, locus a quarter-circle. Lorentzian
four-velocity norm (per proper time, massive worldlines):
$u^\mu u_\mu = |dx_4/d\tau|^2 - |d\vec{x}/d\tau|^2 = -c^2$, unbounded in
each term, signature difference fixing the invariant. The Euclidean
per-proper-time sum $|dx_4/d\tau|^2 + |d\vec{x}/d\tau|^2$ equals $c^2$
only in the instantaneous rest frame; elsewhere $c^2\gamma^2$. Plus-sign
identities belong to (R2); minus-sign identities to (R3).

###### A.3.4 How does the twin paradox read?

Coordinate accumulation is path-independent: both twins accumulate
$\Delta x_4= ic\, \Delta t$. Differential ageing is read from
$X_4 = \int ic \, d\tau$, advancing at real magnitude $v_{x_4}$ per unit
coordinate time. On the travelling leg $v_{x_4} < c$, so the traveller
accumulates less $X_4$, so less proper time. The stay-at-home twin
retains $v_{x_4} = c$ and accumulates the maximal $X_4$. The CTC
question closes the same way: $\oint dx_4= 0$ identically, so a CTC
cannot run on the coordinate; the impossibility lives in $X_4$.

###### A.3.5 $\gamma$-projection and rapidity.

A boost is hyperbolic: rapidity $\phi$ with $\cosh\phi = \gamma$. The
Sphere-partition projection is circular: Sphere angle $\theta$ with
$\sin\theta = v/c$, $\cos\theta = v_{x_4}/c = 1/\gamma$. Related by the
Gudermannian, $\theta = \mathrm{gd}(\phi)$, so
$\cos\theta = \mathrm{sech}\,\phi$. The $1/\gamma$ projection is about
$\theta$; unbounded component growth is about $\phi$.

#### A.4 Why Nothing of Relativity Is Lost {#a.4-why-nothing-of-relativity-is-lost .unnumbered}

The fourth dimension advances at the same rate at every event;
worldlines differ only in how much of that advance they share in.
Massive at rest shares fully ($v_{x_4} = c$); moving shares less
($v_{x_4} = \sqrt{c^2 - v^2}$, clock slowed by the Lorentz factor);
photon does not share at all ($v_{x_4} = 0$, ageless, no $X_4$). Lorentz
invariance survives entire because the invariant content --- the norm
$u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ and the metric --- is a theorem of the Principle
(the metric is the pullback of the Euclidean form along $x_4= ict$, the
$-c^2$ from $(ic)^2$). Lorentz transformations preserve that derived
metric; $\gamma$, time dilation, length contraction, $E = \gamma m c^2$,
the null cone, and the mass-shell all come out unchanged. The foliation
quantities $v_{x_4}$ and $X_4$ are additional bookkeeping frame-anchored
to the cosmic-comoving foliation (the CMB rest frame); the Cloaking
Theorem (Theorem 39) explains why local metrology cannot detect them. GR
survives by the invariant/deformable split: the rate is gravity-rigid;
gravity deforms the spatial sector. Time dilation, redshift, light
bending, perihelion advance, the horizon, and the field equations are
recovered exactly. The horizon is where the share is extinguished; the
expansion does not stop.

#### A.5 Worked Examples {#a.5-worked-examples .unnumbered}

###### A.5.1 The twin paradox.

Traveller at speed $v$ for coordinate time $\Delta t$. Coordinate
accumulation: $\Delta x_4= ic\, \Delta t$ for both. Traveller's share:
$v_{x_4} = c\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}$. Accumulated:
$\Delta X_4^{\text{trav}} = ic\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}\, \Delta t$ vs
$\Delta X_4^{\text{stay}} = ic\, \Delta t$. Differential ageing:
$\Delta\tau_{\text{trav}} - \Delta\tau_{\text{stay}} = \Delta t (\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2} - 1) < 0$:
the traveller is younger by exactly the Lorentz factor.

###### A.5.2 GPS clock rate.

Satellite at radius $r$, speed $v$, mass $M$. Principle: $dx_4/dt = ic$.
Gravitational share: $v_{x_4}^{\text{grav}}/c = \sqrt{1 - 2GM/rc^2}$;
kinematic factor $\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}$. Total:
$v_{x_4}^{\text{sat}}/c \approx 1 - GM/(rc^2) - v^2/(2c^2)$. Ground:
$\approx 1 - GM/(R_\oplus c^2)$. Fractional difference
$\approx GM(1/R_\oplus - 1/r) - v^2/(2c^2)$, matching the
$+4.5 \times 10^{-10}$ pre-launch offset at $r = 26{,}600$ km,
$v = 3.87$ km/s.

###### A.5.3 Schwarzschild gravitational redshift.

Photon from $r_1$ to $r_2 > r_1$. Principle: $dx_4/dt = ic$. Local clock
rate: $v_{x_4}(r)/c = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$. Frequency ratio
$\nu_2/\nu_1 = \sqrt{(1 - r_s/r_1)/(1 - r_s/r_2)}$; weak-field
$\Delta\nu/\nu \approx -GM(1/r_2 - 1/r_1)/c^2$, matching Pound--Rebka
1959. Photon: $v_{x_4} = 0$ throughout, no $X_4$. The redshift is about
the clock rates at emitter and receiver, not the photon.

###### A.5.4 Hawking temperature.

At $r = r_s$, local share $v_{x_4}(r) \to 0$. Surface gravity
$\kappa = c/(2 r_s)$; compactification circumference
$L_H = 4\pi r_s = c\hbar\beta_H$; temperature
$T_H = \hbar c^3/(8\pi G M k_B)$. The expansion does not stop at the
horizon; the share is extinguished on the static foliation, and
compactification of the Euclidean-section $x_4$-axis at $L_H$ produces
the thermal spectrum.

###### A.5.5 Bell's spaceship.

Rockets $A, B$ at proper distance $L_0$, accelerating identically.
Coordinate rate: $dx_4/dt = ic$. Share:
$v_{x_4}(t) = c\sqrt{1 - v(t)^2/c^2}$, decreasing. Accumulated:
$X_4^A = X_4^B$, so both age identically. Launch-frame separation
constant $L_0$; co-moving separation $L(t) = L_0 c/v_{x_4}(t)$, growing
without bound. The string breaks: the budget shifts into the spatial
sector identically on each rocket, so no differential ageing; the
paradox lives in the spatial-sector geometry, the string breaking as
co-moving distance grows as $1/v_{x_4}$.

McGucken, E. (2026). *The McGucken Sphere as Spacetime's Foundational
Atom: Deriving Arkani-Hamed's Amplituhedron and Penrose's Twistors as
Theorems of the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$*. Light Time Dimension
Theory, April 2026.
<https://elliotmcguckenphysics.com/2026/04/27/the-mcgucken-sphere-as-spacetimes-foundational-atom-deriving-arkani-hameds-amplituhedron-and-penroses-twistors-as-theorems-of-the-mcgucken-principle-dx4-dtic/>.
Establishes the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma^+(p)$ --- the spherically
symmetric expansion of $x_4$ at rate $c$ from event $p$ --- as the
foundational atom of spacetime, with the four-manifold $\mathcal{M}$ as
the totality of these expansions. Derives Penrose's twistor space
$\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^3$ as the parametrization of McGucken Spheres,
Witten's 2003 holomorphic-curve localization as $x_4$-stationarity
localization, and the Arkani-Hamed-Trnka amplituhedron as the
canonical-form summation of the intersecting-Sphere cascade, all as
theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$. §5.2 and §11.2 establish the non-circular
three-step construction by which $c$ (substrate's wavelength-per-period
ratio $\ell_*/t_* = c$) and $\hbar$ (per-tick action quantum of
substrate, with $\hbar = \ell_P^2 c^3/G$) are derived as theorems, with
Newton's $G$ as the third independent dimensional input via
Schwarzschild self-consistency $r_S = \lambda$ identifying
$\ell_* = \ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^3}$. The Planck triple
$(\ell_P, t_P, \hbar)$ is the foundational atom's internal scale,
analogous to the hydrogen-atom triple
$(a_0, t_{\mathrm{atomic}}, e^2/4\pi\epsilon_0)$. Dissolves the Doubly
Special Relativity programme at its motivational source: $\ell_P$ is the
substrate's wavelength, observer-independent because the substrate is
Lorentz-covariant by construction.

Arkani-Hamed, N. (2013). *Physics colloquium at Columbia University,
April 2013.* The talk presented the two-alternatives framing for the
future of fundamental physics: either the small value of the Higgs mass
in Planck units admits a "natural" symmetry-protection explanation (most
likely via supersymmetry), or it indicates fine-tuning requiring an
anthropic-multiverse explanation analogous to that for the cosmological
constant. The Arkani-Hamed framing has been presented in versions of
this talk delivered consistently from the late 2000s through the 2010s;
see also the IAS, BNL, and written versions referenced in
[@Woit-ArkaniHamedColloquium-2013]. Written version:
<https://www.sns.ias.edu/~arkani/pdfs/FundamentalPhys.pdf>.

Woit, P. (2013). *Arkani-Hamed Colloquium.* Not Even Wrong blog, April
30, 2013. <https://www.math.columbia.edu/~woit/wordpress/?p=5747>.
Woit's response to Arkani-Hamed's two-alternatives framing identifies
the second alternative (anthropic-multiverse) as what David Gross has
called "giving up," and argues that "if a long, complicated argument
leads you to the conclusion that the only viable alternative is to give
up, then it seems to me you have two choices: give up, or examine more
carefully your argument." Woit's recommendation is to look carefully for
weaknesses in the chain of argument that produces the dichotomy,
suggesting (without identifying definitively) that "what is needed is
instead a suspicion that one has been making a mistake somewhere for
quite a while now."

amplituhedron program, and the role of colour in scattering amplitudes.
The relevant remark on colour as cyclic ordering and the deep question
of accounting for colourless particles (photons, gravitons) within the
same geometric framework appears at 37:20.
<https://youtu.be/poUrrdOYzUY>

Fulton, W., & Harris, J. (1991). *Representation Theory: A First

Nelson, E. (1966). Derivation of the Schrödinger equation from Newtonian
mechanics. *Physical Review* **150**, 1079--1085.
<https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.150.1079>. Original derivation of the
Schrödinger equation from a Brownian process with diffusion coefficient
$D = \hbar/(2m)$; the closest orthodox precedent to the framework's
diffusion-QM identification, with the diffusion coefficient matched to
Schrödinger rather than derived from a deeper mechanism.

Nelson, E. (1985). *Quantum Fluctuations*. Princeton University Press,
Princeton, NJ. Book-length treatment of Nelson's stochastic-mechanics
program; extended treatment of the Brownian-Schrödinger identification
and its multi-particle extensions.

Streater, R. F. (1994). Review of *Quantum Fluctuations* by E. Nelson.
*Bulletin (New Series) of the American Mathematical Society* **30** (2),
292--296. Sober critique of Nelson's stochastic-mechanics program,
identifying multi-particle entanglement, relativistic extension, and
gauge-field interactions as gaps in the original program's closure.

Feynman, R. P. (1948). Space-time approach to non-relativistic quantum
mechanics. *Reviews of Modern Physics* **20**, 367--387.
<https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.20.367>. The original path-integral
formulation of quantum mechanics with weight $e^{iS/\hbar}$ over paths;
the alternative-to-operator-formalism formulation whose substrate origin
is identified by the framework as compounded per-increment Wick rotation
of Compton-clock phase.

Kac, M. (1949). On distributions of certain Wiener functionals.
*Transactions of the American Mathematical Society* **65** (1), 1--13.
<https://doi.org/10.2307/1990512>. The Feynman--Kac formula establishing
that the Wick-rotated path integral corresponds to Boltzmann-weight
expectation over Brownian paths; the mathematical grounding of the
framework's identification
$e^{iS_L/\hbar} \leftrightarrow e^{-S_E/\hbar}$ as substrate-tick
content compounded along paths.

Feynman, R. P., & Hibbs, A. R. (1965). *Quantum Mechanics and Path
Integrals*. McGraw-Hill, New York. Feynman--Hibbs textbook including the
1+1D checkerboard model as an incomplete precedent to the per-increment
Wick rotation reading: paths that switch direction at each
substrate-tick, generating the Dirac equation in 1+1 dimensions.

Ehresmann, C. (1950). Les connexions infinitésimales dans un espace
fibré différentiable. *Colloque de Topologie, Bruxelles*, 29--55. The
Ehresmann connection framework; horizontal/vertical decomposition of the
tangent space at each point of the total space of a principal
$G$-bundle.

Ambrose, W., & Singer, I. M. (1953). A theorem on holonomy.
*Transactions of the American Mathematical Society* **75**, 428--443.
<https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9947-1953-0063739-1>. The holonomy Lie
algebra is generated by curvature.

Chern, S.-S., & Simons, J. (1974). Characteristic forms and geometric
invariants. *Annals of Mathematics* **99**, 48--69.
<https://doi.org/10.2307/1971013>. Chern--Weil homomorphism and the
Chern--Simons functional.

Haag, R. (1996). *Local Quantum Physics: Fields, Particles, Algebras*,
2nd ed. Springer, Berlin. Algebraic QFT as a sheaf of $C^*$-algebras
over spacetime.

Atiyah, M. F., & Bott, R. (1982). The Yang--Mills equations over Riemann

**308**, 523--615. <https://doi.org/10.1098/rsta.1983.0017>. Moduli
space of Yang--Mills connections; equivariant Morse theory; the space of
connections as an affine space with symplectic structure.

't Hooft, G. (1974). Magnetic monopoles in unified gauge theories.
*Nuclear Physics B* **79**, 276--284.
<https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(74)90486-6>

Polyakov, A. M. (1974). Particle spectrum in quantum field theory. *JETP
