<http://jetpletters.ru/ps/1789/article_27297.shtml>

Clay Mathematics Institute. *Yang--Mills & The Mass Gap (Millennium
Problem)*.
<https://www.claymath.org/millennium/yang-mills-the-maths-gap/>. The
Clay Millennium Problem statement: "The successful use of Yang--Mills
theory to describe the strong interactions of elementary particles
depends on a subtle quantum mechanical property called the mass gap: the
quantum particles have positive masses, even though the classical waves
travel at the speed of light. This property has been discovered by
physicists from experiment and confirmed by computer simulations, but it
still has not been understood from a theoretical point of view. Progress
in establishing the existence of the Yang--Mills theory and a mass gap
will require the introduction of fundamental new ideas both in physics
and in mathematics."

Jaffe, A., & Witten, E. (2000). *Quantum Yang--Mills Theory*. Clay
Mathematics Institute Millennium Problem official problem description.
<https://www.claymath.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/yangmills.pdf>. The
official problem statement: "Prove that for any compact simple gauge
group $G$, a non-trivial quantum Yang--Mills theory exists on
$\mathbb{R}^4$ and has a mass gap $\Delta > 0$. Existence includes
establishing axiomatic properties at least as strong as those cited in
\[Streater--Wightman, Osterwalder--Schrader\]." The paper surveys the
constructive-quantum-field-theory program (Glimm--Jaffe two-dimensional
results, Magnen--Sénéor three-dimensional Yukawa, Balaban
four-dimensional renormalization-group), the Wilson lattice
approximation, asymptotic freedom, and identifies the need for
"fundamental new ideas in physics and mathematics" (§6.6).

Streater, R. F., & Wightman, A. S. (1964). *PCT, Spin and Statistics,
and All That*. W. A. Benjamin, New York. The foundational reference for
the Wightman axioms of quantum field theory on Minkowski space.

Osterwalder, K., & Schrader, R. (1973). Axioms for Euclidean Green's
functions. *Communications in Mathematical Physics* **31**, 83--112.
<https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01645738>. Part II: *Communications in
Mathematical Physics* **42** (1975), 281--305.
<https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01608978>. The foundational reference for the
Osterwalder--Schrader axioms establishing equivalence between Euclidean
and Lorentzian formulations of quantum field theory, with the
"reflection positivity" condition replacing the Markov property.

Visser, M. (2017). How to Wick rotate generic curved spacetime.
*Preprint,* arXiv:1702.05572 \[gr-qc\].
<https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.05572>. (Earlier version: Visser, M. (1991).
Wormholes, baby universes and causality. *Physical Review D* **43**,
402--409.) Explicit statement that "*the effects of the causal structure
of the Lorentzian signature theory seem to disappear completely as no
analogue of OS positivity is manifest*" under the standard Wick
prescription in curved spacetime; Visser's interpretation identifies
this as "*profoundly disturbing*" and proposes to regard Wick rotation
"*as a complex deformation of the spacetime metric*" rather than a
complex deformation of the time coordinate.

Kontsevich, M., & Segal, G. (2021). Wick rotation and the positivity of
energy in quantum field theory. *The Quarterly Journal of Mathematics*
**72**(1--2), 673--699 (special issue for Michael Atiyah's 90th
birthday). <https://doi.org/10.1093/qmath/haab027>. Preprint
arXiv:2105.10161. Proposes a new axiom system for unitary quantum field
theories on curved space-time backgrounds by postulating that partition
functions and correlators extend analytically to a domain of
complex-valued metrics; ordinary Riemannian metrics are contained in the
allowable domain while Lorentzian metrics lie on its boundary. The
closest orthodox precedent for a formally asymmetric-status framing of
Lorentzian versus Riemannian metrics.

Witten, E. (2021). A note on complex spacetime metrics. *Preprint,*
arXiv:2111.06514 \[hep-th\]. <https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.06514>.
Extension of the Kontsevich--Segal framework to gravity: proposes that
allowable complex metrics in gravitational path integrals are those for
which some scalar action associated with a $p$-form has positive real
part, generalizing the Kontsevich--Segal condition on quantum field
theory to include dynamical metrics.

Woit, P. (2023). Spacetime is right-handed. *Preprint,* arXiv:2311.00608
\[hep-th\]. <https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.00608>. Proposes that Wick
rotation should be understood via the right-handed $SU(2)_R$ chirality
factor of $\mathrm{Spin}(4) \cong SU(2)_L \times SU(2)_R$ (Euclidean
signature) rather than by analytic continuation of spinors in complex
spacetime; observes explicitly that "*only the diagonal $SU(2)$ subgroup
of $\mathrm{Spin}(4)$ acts non-trivially on Wick-rotated spacetime*"
with the other factor behaving as an internal symmetry.

Brydges, D., Fröhlich, J., & Seiler, E. (1979, 1980, 1981). On the
construction of quantized gauge fields. *Annals of Physics* **121**
(1979), 227--284; *Communications in Mathematical Physics* **71**
(1980), 159--205; *Communications in Mathematical Physics* **79**
(1981), 353--399. The construction of the two-dimensional continuum
Higgs model (abelian gauge field interacting with a charged scalar
field) satisfying the Osterwalder--Schrader axioms.

Balaban, T. (1987). Renormalization group approach to lattice gauge
field theories. I: generation of effective actions in a small field
approximation and a coupling constant renormalization in 4D.
*Communications in Mathematical Physics* **109**, 249--301.
<https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01215223>. The four-dimensional extension of
Balaban's lattice-gauge-theory renormalization-group analysis, including
asymptotic freedom and quantitative estimates on effects arising from
large values of the gauge field.

Magnen, J., Rivasseau, V., & Sénéor, R. (1993). Construction of $YM_4$
with an infrared cutoff. *Communications in Mathematical Physics*
**155**, 325--383. <https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02097398>. The
continuum-regularization construction of four-dimensional Yang--Mills
theory with an infrared cutoff.

Glimm, J., & Jaffe, A. (1987). *Quantum Physics: A Functional Integral
Point of View* (Second Edition). Springer-Verlag, New York. ISBN
978-0387964775. The foundational reference for constructive quantum
field theory, covering the existence proofs for $\phi^4_2$ and
$\phi^4_3$ theories, cluster expansions, the Osterwalder--Schrader
theorem, and the program for extending these methods toward
four-dimensional gauge theories.

McGucken, E. (2026). *The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ Necessitates
the Wick Rotation and $i$ Throughout Physics: A Reduction of Thirty-Four
Independent Inputs of Quantum Field Theory, Quantum Mechanics, and
Symmetry Physics to a Single Physical Principle, with the Imaginary Unit
$i$ Identified Across All of Physics --- Including Penrose's Twistors,
the Arkani-Hamed--Trnka Amplituhedron, Feynman Diagrams, AdS/CFT, String

Renou, M.-O., Trillo, D., Weilenmann, M., Le, T. P., Tavakoli, A.,
Gisin, N., Acín, A., & Navascúes, M. (2021). Quantum theory based on
real numbers can be experimentally falsified. *Nature* **600**, 625--629

Nature article establishing the theoretical procedure for the empirical

network test of real-versus-complex Hilbert-space formulations of

real-Hilbert-space restriction; (iii) a specific Bell-type functional
$T$ has complex-quantum-theory bound $T = 6\sqrt{2} \approx 8.49$ versus

Li, Z.-D., Mao, Y.-J., Weilenmann, M., Tavakoli, A., Chen, H., Feng, L.,
Yang, S.-J., Renou, M.-O., Trillo, D., Le, T. P., Gisin, N., Acín, A.,

Abstract verbatim: "We experimentally demonstrate quantum correlations
in a network of three parties and two independent EPR sources that

Chen, M.-C., Wang, C., Liu, F.-M., Wang, J.-W., Ying, C., Shang, Z.-X.,
Wu, Y., Gong, M., Deng, H., Liang, F.-T., Zhang, Q., Peng, C.-Z., Zhu,

Renou, M.-O., as interviewed in: Pultarova, T. (2021). *Imaginary
numbers could be needed to describe reality, new studies find*.

<https://www.livescience.com/imaginary-numbers-needed-to-describe-reality>.

Einstein, A., Podolsky, B., & Rosen, N. (1935). Can quantum-mechanical

terminology: "If, without in any way disturbing a system, we can predict

Einstein, A. (1905). Ist die Trägheit eines Körpers von seinem
Energieinhalt abhängig? \[Does the inertia of a body depend on its

(Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"}(v) and
Remark [233](#rem:EinsteinAnchor){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:EinsteinAnchor"}): $E = mc^2$ is the energy of

with the $c^2$ factor being the velocity-magnitude-squared of
perpendicular-$x_4$-motion in the McGucken-Sphere wavefront expansion.
Empirical confirmation in nuclear binding energies, mass defects in
fission and fusion, and matter-antimatter annihilation events.

ATLAS Collaboration (2012). Observation of a new particle in the search
for the Standard Model Higgs boson with the ATLAS detector at the LHC.

<https://doi.org/10.1016/j.physletb.2012.08.020>. The ATLAS observation

CMS Collaboration (2012). Observation of a new boson at a mass of 125
GeV with the CMS experiment at the LHC. *Physics Letters B* **716**,
30--61. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.physletb.2012.08.021>. The

Manton, N. S. (1979). A new six-dimensional approach to the
Weinberg-Salam model. *Nuclear Physics B* **158**, 141--153.
<https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(79)90192-5>. The foundational paper

be identified with the extra-dimensional component of a
higher-dimensional gauge field. The historical precedent for "Higgs as

supersedes by identifying the Higgs with the encoding of the expanding

Hosotani, Y. (1983). Dynamical mass generation by compact extra
dimensions. *Physics Letters B* **126**, 309--313.

vev arises as an Aharonov-Bohm phase $\theta_H$ along a compact,
non-simply-connected fifth dimension. Comparison with McGucken: the
compact non-expanding fifth dimension of gauge-Higgs unification differs

Hosotani, Y. (2007). *Gauge-Higgs Unification and LHC/ILC*.

Higgs is identified with the extra-dimensional component $A_5$ of a
higher-dimensional gauge field, with electroweak symmetry breaking
arising via the Wilson loop $\theta_H$ along the compact fifth
dimension.

Hosotani, Y. (2016). *Gauge-Higgs EW and Grand Unification*.
arXiv:1606.08108. <https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.08108>. The

unification. The 4D Higgs field is identified with the zero mode of the
extra-dimensional component of higher-dimensional gauge potentials. The
Higgs appears as an Aharonov-Bohm phase $\theta_H$ in the fifth
dimension. The framework predicts $Z'$ bosons in the 6--10 TeV range and
is observationally distinguishable from the Standard Model for
$\theta_H \gtrsim 0.1$. Closest historical precedent to the McGucken
identification of the Higgs with a fourth dimension, but the dimension
is compact, space-like, and non-expanding.

de Rújula, A. (2007). *Is the Vacuum Empty? --- the Higgs Field and the
Dark Energy.* EPL Symposium "Physics In Our Times," Fondation Del Duca
de l'Institut de France, Paris, May 10, 2007. The articulation of the
open question of whether the Higgs field is connected to the
cosmological-constant dark energy responsible for the observed
accelerated expansion of the universe, framed as a foundational-physics
question at the boundary of particle physics and cosmology. The
historical precedent for "Higgs as related to cosmological expansion"

Nesbet, R. K. (2010). *Dark energy density predicted and explained*.
arXiv:1004.5097. <https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.5097>. A proposal that the
cosmological dark energy density is produced by dressing the bare Higgs
scalar field by the neutral gauge boson field induced by weak
cosmological time dependence of the conformal Higgs model. One of
several historical precedents for identifying the Higgs with the driver
of cosmological accelerated expansion.

Brans-Dicke gravity and Higgs cosmology literature, ca. 2018,
exemplified by treatments in which the Higgs potential structure can be
motivated from solutions of generalised Brans-Dicke field equations
carrying harmless cosmological vacuum energy, with the late-time cosmic
evolution effectively appearing as an universe filled with mildly
evolving dynamical dark energy mimicking quintessence or phantom dark

Brans-Dicke + Higgs treats the Higgs vacuum energy as related to

The Higgs cosmology field of inquiry, reviewed in: Markkanen, T.,
Rajantie, A., & Stopyra, S. (2018). *Cosmological Aspects of Higgs
Vacuum Metastability*. *Frontiers in Astronomy and Space Sciences*
**5**, 40. <https://doi.org/10.3389/fspas.2018.00040>. Available at

cosmology field, including connections to inflation, baryogenesis, and

Higgs-cosmology connections but does not arrive at the McGucken

de Broglie, L. (1924). *Recherches sur la théorie des quanta*. Doctoral

corresponds to an internal oscillation at the Compton frequency: "a
standing wave at the Compton scale would undergo Doppler shifting and
exhibit a beating frequency," with the de Broglie wavelength arising as
the lab-frame manifestation of the rest-frame Compton oscillation. The
foundational reference for the Compton-frequency identification of rest
mass that the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework deepens by supplying the

perpendicular-$x_4$-motion).

Hestenes, D. (1990). The zitterbewegung interpretation of quantum
mechanics. *Foundations of Physics* **20**, 1213--1232.
<https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01889466>. The Zitterbewegung interpretation:
the electron is identified with a confined electromagnetic field
arranged in a loop or double-loop structure at the Compton scale, with
rest mass arising from the kinetic foundation of the internal
Compton-frequency oscillation. The principal articulation of the
Zitterbewegung programme as a competing alternative to the Higgs
mechanism for the origin of electron mass: "These facts suggest that the
electron mass, spin and magnetic moment are manifestations of a local
circular motion of the electron\... Evidently that would obviate the
need for including Higgs bosons in the theory, since the zitterbewegung
provides an alternative mechanism to account for the electron mass."
Closest historical precedent to the McGucken identification of mass with
Compton-frequency $x_4$-winding; differs in lacking the physical
referent ($x_4$'s expansion) and in treating Zitterbewegung and Higgs as
competing alternatives rather than as the same physical fact viewed from
two angles. See also
[@Hestenes2010ZitterbewegungElectronsPhotons; @Hestenes2019ZitterbewegungElectronsPhotons]
for the later developments and the spacetime-algebra formalism. The
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's
Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"

Zitterbewegung-as-mass-origin and the Higgs-mechanism-as-mass-origin

Maruani, J. (2012). The Dirac electron: spin, zitterbewegung, the

Eckstein, M., Franco, N., & Miller, T. (2017). Noncommutative geometry
of Zitterbewegung. *Physical Review D* **95**, 061701(R).
<https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.95.061701>. Preprint:

analogue of the bound. Abstract verbatim: "Based on the mathematics of
noncommutative geometry, we model a 'classical' Dirac fermion
propagating in a curved spacetime. We demonstrate that the inherent
causal structure of the model encodes the possibility of
Zitterbewegung---the 'trembling motion' of the fermion. We recover the
well-known frequency of Zitterbewegung as the highest possible speed of
change in the fermion's 'internal space.' Furthermore, we show that the
bound does not change in the presence of an external electromagnetic
field and derive its explicit analogue when the mass parameter is
promoted to a Yukawa field." Comparison with the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework: Eckstein-Franco-Miller connect Compton-frequency
(Zitterbewegung bound) to Higgs coupling (promoted Yukawa field) within
Connes' noncommutative geometry, but the connection is technical and the

referent that Eckstein-Franco-Miller leave abstract: the internal space
is the perpendicular $x_4$-direction, the Zitterbewegung is the
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding, the Higgs-like field is the field-theoretic
encoding of the $+ic$-direction reference at every spacetime event, and

Biswas, T. (2009). *Another Alternative to the Higgs Mechanism*.
arXiv:0909.1848. <https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.1848>. The title itself

designed to generate mass for massless particles. The mass comes from
the interaction of observed particles with an external field --- the
Higgs field. In the past, several alternatives to the Higgs mechanism
for mass generation have been proposed to avoid the postulation of the
Higgs field. This article proposes yet another one. This alternative is
distinctly different from the others because it considers mass
generation through internal interactions of a particle rather than
interactions with external fields. This requires particles to have an
internal structure beyond intrinsic spin." Representative of the broader
Higgs-alternative tradition that arose around the
Compton-scale-internal-structure account of mass. Comparison with the

Hestenes, D. (2010). Zitterbewegung in Quantum Mechanics. *Foundations

Cartan, É. (1913). Les groupes projectifs qui ne laissent invariante
aucune multiplicité plane. *Bulletin de la Société Mathématique de
France* **41**, 53--96. The original introduction of spinors as
projective representations of rotation groups, characterised by their

identification: spinors are the natural carriers of the spin double
