$\mathrm{Spin}(n)$, with the cover being two-to-one and the spinor
representations being faithful representations of $\mathrm{Spin}(n)$
that descend to projective representations of $\mathrm{SO}(n)$. The
foundational reference for the algebraic definition of spinors. The
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's advance: supplying the geometric
referent for the transformation behaviour that Cartan defined
algebraically --- spinors are the natural transformation objects of the
wavefront $S^3 \cong \mathrm{SU}(2)$, with the wavefront being the
substrate-scale geometry of $dx_4/dt = ic$.

Penrose, R. (1967). Twistor algebra. *Journal of Mathematical Physics*
**8(2)**, 345--366. <https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1705200>. The
foundational reference for the twistor programme. Penrose introduces
twistors as the fundamental geometric objects of physics, with both
spacetime points and physical fields derivative from twistor structure.
Projective twistor space is $\mathbb{C}P^3$, the space of massless
particles with spin. In twistor formalism, massless particles are simple
twistors; massive particles are pairs of twistors. The mass of a massive
particle arises from the relative orientation of the two twistor
components; spin is encoded by the twistor's helicity. The historical
line that connects mass and spinors most directly prior to the McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework. Comparison with McGucken: Penrose works in
complex projective twistor space; McGucken works in real
four-dimensional spacetime with the $+ic$ direction as perpendicularity
marker. Both make spinors fundamental; the geometric setting differs.

Penrose, R., & Rindler, W. (1984). *Spinors and Space-Time, Volume 1:
Two-Spinor Calculus and Relativistic Fields*. Cambridge University
Press. ISBN 978-0521245272. The systematic development of two-spinor
calculus in general relativity, establishing spinors as the natural
carriers of relativistic field structure. The treatment emphasises that
spinors are the "square roots of geometry" in the sense that vectors
$v^\mu \sim \bar\psi\gamma^\mu\psi$ are quadratic spinor bilinears
(Brauer-Weyl construction). Volume 1 of the two-volume Penrose-Rindler
treatment.

Penrose, R., & Rindler, W. (1986). *Spinors and Space-Time, Volume 2:
Spinor and Twistor Methods in Space-Time Geometry*. Cambridge University
Press. ISBN 978-0521347860. Volume 2 of the Penrose-Rindler treatment,
developing the twistor programme as a candidate foundation for spacetime
geometry and physical fields. Establishes the connection between
twistors and the geometry of null lines in Minkowski space, with the
projective twistor space $\mathbb{C}P^3$ identified as the space of
massless particles with spin. The most comprehensive prior treatment of
spinors-as-fundamental-objects, adjacent to the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework's wavefront-$S^3$ identification but distinct in geometric
setting (complex projective vs. real expanding fourth dimension).

Hestenes, D. (1971). Vectors, spinors, and complex numbers in classical
and quantum physics. *American Journal of Physics* **39**, 1013--1027.
<https://doi.org/10.1119/1.1986364>. Hestenes' early articulation of the
spacetime-algebra programme: $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)$ is the fundamental
algebraic structure of physics, with spinors represented as even
multivectors of this algebra. The claim: the geometry of spinors is
recovered from the Clifford-algebraic structure of spacetime itself.
Foundational for the Hestenes treatment of the Dirac equation as a real
Clifford-algebraic equation rather than a complex matrix equation. Read
in conjunction with
[@Hestenes1990ZitterbewegungInterpretation; @Hestenes2010ZitterbewegungElectronsPhotons; @Hestenes2019ZitterbewegungElectronsPhotons]
for the full development of the spacetime-algebra programme. Comparison
with McGucken: Hestenes treats $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)$ as foundational;
McGucken treats $\mathrm{Cl}(1,3)$ as the algebraic shadow of the
wavefront $S^3$ geometry.

Hamilton, A. J. S. (2023). The supergeometric algebra. *Advances in
Applied Clifford Algebras* **33(1)**, 1.
<https://doi.org/10.1007/s00006-022-01256-6>. The 2023 paper
articulating the position that spinors are more fundamental than
Clifford algebra. Abstract verbatim: "Spinors are central to physics:
all matter (fermions) is made of spinors, and all forces arise from
symmetries of spinors. It is common to consider the geometric (Clifford)
algebra as the fundamental edifice from which spinors emerge. This paper
advocates the alternative view that spinors are more fundamental than
the geometric algebra. The algebra consisting of linear combinations of
scalars, column spinors, row spinors, multivectors, and their various
products, can be termed the supergeometric algebra. The inner product of
a row spinor with a column spinor yields a scalar, while the outer
product of a column spinor with a row spinor yields a multivector, in
accordance with the Brauer-Weyl theorem." Closest historical precedent
to Theorems [265](#thm:FourthRoot){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:FourthRoot"}--[286](#thm:DoubleCoverDerived){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:DoubleCoverDerived"} of the present paper. Comparison
with McGucken: Hamilton makes spinors algebraically fundamental without
supplying the geometric referent; McGucken identifies the wavefront
$S^3 \cong \mathrm{SU}(2)$ from $dx_4/dt = ic$ as the physical source of
the spinor structure that Hamilton's programme leaves abstract.

Brauer, R., & Weyl, H. (1935). Spinors in $n$ dimensions. *American
Journal of Mathematics* **57(2)**, 425--449.
<https://doi.org/10.2307/2371218>. The foundational reference for the
spinor-bilinear construction of vectors and higher tensors: a vector is
quadratic in spinors via $v^\mu \sim \bar\psi\gamma^\mu\psi$, a
second-rank tensor is a bilinear $\bar\psi\gamma^{\mu\nu}\psi$, and so
on. The consequence: in any framework where spinors are fundamental,
vectors and higher tensors are derived rather than independently
postulated. The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's position is
consistent with the Brauer-Weyl construction: matter (fermions) is
spinorial at substrate scale (wavefront-quanta in the fundamental
$\mathrm{SU}(2)$ representation), and gauge bosons (vectors of the gauge
group) are derived from matter content. The Brauer-Weyl construction is
the algebraic engine of this derivation; the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework supplies the geometric referent (the wavefront $S^3$) that the
Brauer-Weyl algebraic construction does not address.

The Kaluza-Klein spinor lift programme, exemplified in: Bailin, D., &
Love, A. (1987). Kaluza-Klein theories. *Reports on Progress in Physics*
**50**, 1087--1170. <https://doi.org/10.1088/0034-4885/50/9/001>. Review
of Kaluza-Klein theories with extra spatial dimensions, in which the
four-dimensional Dirac spinor is embedded as a slice of a
higher-dimensional spinor. In 5D Kaluza-Klein, the 4D spinor is a slice
of a 5D spinor; in 11D supergravity, the 4D spinor is a slice of an 11D
spinor. The claim: 4D spinor structure is inherited from a
higher-dimensional spinor structure, with the extra dimensions being
compact and space-like. Comparison with McGucken: Kaluza-Klein extra
dimensions are small/compact/space-like; the McGucken $x_4$ is the
expanding fourth dimension at velocity $c$. Kaluza-Klein generates mass
from extra-dimensional momenta of higher-dimensional massless fields;
McGucken generates mass from Compton-frequency
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding with the Higgs vev as direction encoder. The
two pictures are ontologically inverted.

McGucken, E. (2026). *The Spinor as the Fourth Root of the McGucken
Interval: Dirac's "Square Root of Klein--Gordon" and Atiyah's "Square
Root of Geometry" as the Single Operation of $x_4$-Extraction*. Light
Time Dimension Theory. The foundational reference for the McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's account of why matter is spinorial.
Establishes the central result: *the spacetime interval is quartic in
the spinor field, and its unique geometric square root is the
$x_4$-stationary null cone of the Light Time Dimension Theory primitive
$dx_4/dt = ic$*. Two square-root operations compose: the Clifford/Dirac
root (the gamma matrices square-root the metric so that the Dirac
operator squares to the d'Alembertian; Theorem 3.1, G1, symbolically
verified); and the Fierz/twistor root (the spinor bilinear
$\bar\psi\gamma^\mu\psi$ is a vector quadratic in the spinor; Theorem
3.2, G1). Their composition makes the interval $ds^2$ a quartic form in
$\psi$, so $\psi$ is the fourth root of $ds^2$ (Theorem 3.3, G1). Within
Light Time Dimension Theory, where $ds^2$ is the integrated shadow of
$dx_4/dt = ic$, a single Weyl spinor squares to a null four-vector, and
the null direction is the $x_4$-rest locus where the photon rides the
wavefront (Theorems 5.1, 5.3, G1). The tensor square of the Dirac spinor
reproduces the full exterior algebra of the $x_4$-extended arena
($2^4 = 16 = 1+4+6+4+1$; Theorem 4.1, G1), making Atiyah's slogan exact:
every geometric measure of the arena is a spinor bilinear. Theorem 5.4
(the rigidity theorem, G1): the spinor's null cone and the
$x_4$-expansion are mutually determined by a single constant $c$ --- the
empirically-fixed spinor lightcone pins the expansion magnitude to $c$,
and conversely any change in the expansion would relocate the spinor's
null square. Theorem 5.6 (the signature-forced theorem, G1): a
single-complex spinor with one $i$ and Hermitian norm forces a
four-space of signature (1,3) with exactly one moving (timelike)
dimension, since its bilinear lives in the Hermitian $2\times 2$
matrices whose unique invariant form is the Lorentzian determinant; the
timelike direction is the Born norm $\langle\psi|\psi\rangle$, built
from the same $i$ that is $x_4= ict$; a fully static four-space is the
quaternionic $\mathrm{SU}(2)\times\mathrm{SU}(2)$ world. Theorem 9.4
(the double cover derived, G1): granting Theorem 5.6, the spinor double
cover, the half-angle behaviour, and the $2\pi \mapsto -1$ sign are
derived rather than postulated --- the double cover is the
conjugation-square of the $x_4$-carrying transport, just as the vector
is the bilinear-square of the spinor. Theorem 8.3 (Pauli exclusion as
$x_4$-half-circuit phase, G2): under the exchange-as-$2\pi$-rotation
equivalence, the statistics sign $(-1)^{2s}$ is the $x_4$-half-circuit
phase, so Pauli exclusion is the cancellation of states carrying
opposite $x_4$-phase, and the fermion/boson dichotomy is the
single-$i$/quaternionic dichotomy of Theorem 5.6. Theorems 10.2 and 10.3
(the static sector hosts no physics; the $i$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$ injects
relativity, QM, and the symmetries; G1): Donaldson's exotic
four-manifold topology lives in the static (4,0) sector which contains
neither relativity, nor quantum mechanics, nor the Lorentz or unitary
symmetries either requires; the single $i$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$ is exactly
the operation that injects all three at once via the Wick rotation
$x_4= ict$, carrying $\mathrm{SO}(4) \to \mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$,
$\mathrm{SU}(2)\times\mathrm{SU}(2) \to \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{C})$, and
the cone, the Born norm, and unitary evolution into existence. The
geometric meaning of $\sqrt{-1}$ and the geometric meaning of the spinor
are the same (Proposition 6.1): the single $i$ doing all of this is the
$i$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$. Dirac's square root of Klein--Gordon and Atiyah's
square root of geometry are the same operation: the extraction of the
$x_4$ axis. The residual primitivity question is stated as Open Problem
1$'$: derive from $dx_4/dt = ic$ that admitting one complex structure
(one moving $x_4$) makes the single-complex spinor $S$ a primitive ---
that the square-root/generator layer is fundamental and the
vector/tensor layer is its degree-two image. In Atiyah's own terms:
"what is a spinor when there is no complex structure?" --- which by
Theorem 5.6 is "what is geometry with no moving dimension?", the static
quaternionic sector. The programme Atiyah named --- a "spinor analysis"
standing to the spinor as complex analysis stands to $\sqrt{-1}$ --- is,
in Light Time Dimension Theory, the calculus of the first-order
$x_4$-generator whose exponential is motion.

Donaldson, S. K. (1983). An application of gauge theory to
four-dimensional topology. *Journal of Differential Geometry* **18(2)**,
279--315. <https://doi.org/10.4310/jdg/1214437665>. The Fields
Medal--winning paper establishing the diagonalisation theorem for
definite intersection forms on closed, simply-connected, smooth
four-manifolds. Combined with Freedman's topological classification
[@Freedman1982TopologicalManifolds], the theorem reveals the existence
of exotic smooth structures on $\mathbb{R}^4$ and on many other
four-manifolds. Donaldson's proof runs entirely on the moduli space of
anti-self-dual instantons --- a structure existing only in Euclidean
(4,0) signature, where $\star^2 = +1$ on $\Lambda^2$ permits the real
ASD equation $F = -\star F$ (Proposition 10.7 of [@MG-Spinor]). In the
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, Donaldson's static (4,0) sector hosts
no relativity, no quantum mechanics, and no Lorentz/unitary symmetries
(Theorem 10.2 of [@MG-Spinor]); the single $i$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$ is
exactly the operation that injects all three (Theorem 10.3 of
[@MG-Spinor]). The exotic four-manifold topology is a static gift; the
physics is in the $i$ that marks the moving $x_4$.

Freedman, M. H. (1982). The topology of four-dimensional manifolds.
*Journal of Differential Geometry* **17(3)**, 357--453.
<https://doi.org/10.4310/jdg/1214437136>. The Fields Medal--winning
topological classification of simply-connected four-manifolds: every
unimodular symmetric bilinear form over $\mathbb{Z}$ is the intersection
form of a unique closed simply-connected topological four-manifold. The
classification is blind to smooth structure --- a homeomorphism
invariant cannot detect a diffeomorphism difference --- which is why
combining Freedman's topological classification with Donaldson's smooth
obstruction ([@Donaldson1983]) revealed the existence of exotic smooth
structures on $\mathbb{R}^4$ and on many four-manifolds. In the McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, the topological classification is i-free; the
smooth-structure obstruction Donaldson detects is accessible only
through the imported Euclidean $i$ ([@MG-Spinor], Remark 10.8).

Witten, E. (1994). Monopoles and four-manifolds. *Mathematical Research
Letters* **1(6)**, 769--796.
<https://doi.org/10.4310/MRL.1994.v1.n6.a13>. The Seiberg--Witten
reformulation of Donaldson invariants, reducing the moduli-space
calculation of [@Donaldson1983] to the much simpler Seiberg--Witten
equations. The content is unchanged: the calculation runs on Euclidean
(4,0) signature, the moduli space of solutions is finite-dimensional via
ellipticity (a Euclidean property), and Uhlenbeck-type compactness is a
Euclidean Yang--Mills fact. In the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework,
the Witten Seiberg--Witten reformulation, like Donaldson's original
proof, is parasitic on the Euclidean signature that is the spent form of
the single physical $i$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$ ([@MG-Spinor], §10.6).

Adler, S. L. (1995). *Quaternionic Quantum Mechanics and Quantum
Fields*. International Series of Monographs on Physics 88, Oxford
University Press. ISBN 978-0-19-506643-1. The foundational reference for
quaternionic quantum mechanics --- the attempt to ground physics in
three anticommuting complex structures rather than the single complex
structure of standard QM. Establishes Adler's complex-S-matrix theorem:
the quaternionic S-matrix is complex (no dependence on $j, k$) for
appropriate ray choices, the reason for which is closed by
Theorem [271](#thm:HilbertEntailsSingleI){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:HilbertEntailsSingleI"} of the present paper: the single
complex structure is selected at the first axiom by Born-conserving
evolution. Adler's program reaches into the static $(4,0)$ sector for a
structure that, in the McGucken framework, is the shadow of the single
$i$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$ --- and then cannot supply the $i$ that casts it
(Remark [273](#rem:WhyH){reference-type="ref" reference="rem:WhyH"}).

Gisin, N. (1991). Bell's inequality holds for all non-product states.
*Physics Letters A* **154**, 201--202.
<https://doi.org/10.1016/0375-9601(91)90805-I>. Establishes that every
pure entangled state of a bipartite quantum system violates a Bell
inequality --- the fact underlying
Corollary [272](#cor:AdlerGisin){reference-type="ref"
reference="cor:AdlerGisin"}(b): a quaternionic Hilbert space with
multiparticle structure carries Bell nonlocality necessarily, because
the dimension gap $d_A d_B - (d_A + d_B - 1) = (d_A - 1)(d_B - 1) > 0$
makes entanglement generic and Gisin's theorem supplies the Bell
violation on every entangled pure state.

Renou, M.-O., Trillo, D., Weilenmann, M., Le, T. P., Tavakoli, A.,
Gisin, N., Acín, A., & Navascués, M. (2021). Quantum theory based on
real numbers can be experimentally falsified. *Nature* **600**,
625--629. <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-021-04160-4>. Preprint:
arXiv:2101.10873. <https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.10873>. Establishes the
theoretical Bell-like inequality whose violation falsifies
real-Hilbert-space quantum mechanics. Subsequent experimental
confirmations by
[@Li2022CertificationGenuineComplex; @Chen2022RulingOutRealNumberQuantumTheory]
have demonstrated the falsification at multi-$\sigma$ significance,
providing the empirical necessity content of
Theorem [282](#thm:QuantumIIsEvolutionGenerator){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QuantumIIsEvolutionGenerator"}(iii): the $i$ is an
empirically necessary feature of the observed state space, not a
calculational convenience.

Li, Z.-D., Mao, Y.-L., Weilenmann, M., Tavakoli, A., Chen, H., Feng, L.,
Yang, S.-J., Renou, M.-O., Trillo, D., Le, T. P., Gisin, N., Acín, A.,
Navascués, M., Wang, Z., & Fan, J. (2022). Testing real quantum theory
in an optical quantum network. *Physical Review Letters* **128**,
040402. <https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.128.040402>. Experimental
falsification of real-Hilbert-space quantum theory at 4.5$\sigma$ via
the Renou--Li--Chen protocol, in an optical quantum network. Combined
with [@Chen2022RulingOutRealNumberQuantumTheory] the joint significance
is 5.30$\sigma$.

Chen, M.-C., Wang, C., Liu, F.-M., Wang, J.-W., Ying, C., Shang, Z.-X.,
Wu, Y., Gong, M., Deng, H., Liang, F.-T., Zhang, Q., Lü, C.-Y., Zhu, Y.,
& Pan, J.-W. (2022). Ruling out real-valued standard formalism of
quantum theory. *Physical Review Letters* **128**, 040403.
<https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.128.040403>. Independent
experimental falsification of real-Hilbert-space quantum theory via the
Renou--Li--Chen protocol on a superconducting quantum processor,
complementing [@Li2022CertificationGenuineComplex] and providing the
joint 5.30$\sigma$ empirics of
Theorem [282](#thm:QuantumIIsEvolutionGenerator){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:QuantumIIsEvolutionGenerator"}(iii).

Frenkel, E. (2007). *Langlands Correspondence for Loop Groups*.
Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics 103, Cambridge University
Press. ISBN 978-0-521-85443-6. The definitive build-from-scratch
monograph on the local geometric Langlands correspondence. Establishes
the canonical architecture of the field: Chapters 2--9 construct the
central-elements machinery (vertex algebras, the OPE, the
Segal--Sugawara stress tensor, Wakimoto modules, screening operators,
W-algebras) --- conformal-field-theory and current-algebra constructions
of physics origin, several in the proof line as documented in
[@MG-Spinor §17.4]. The closing chapter states the geometric Langlands
correspondence in the language of Harish-Chandra pairs, D-modules, and
algebraic geometry, with the physics provenance absorbed. Provides the
documentary basis for
Proposition [364](#prop:PhysicsLoadBearing){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:PhysicsLoadBearing"} (physics centrality),
Theorem [365](#thm:StringTheoryPaperLoadBearing){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:StringTheoryPaperLoadBearing"} (the
Friedan--Martinec--Shenker string-theory paper in the
second-screening-operator construction), and
Theorem [366](#thm:BoundariesCoincide){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:BoundariesCoincide"} (the $i$ of the moving fourth
dimension, the physics-region, and the engine/cargo line coincide).

Higgs, P. W. (2014). Nobel Lecture: Evading the Goldstone theorem.
*Reviews of Modern Physics* **86**, 851--853.
<https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.86.851>. Nobel Lecture delivered 8
December 2013 at Aula Magna, Stockholm University. PDF:
<https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2018/06/higgs-lecture.pdf>. The
primary-source documentary record of Higgs's own account of the
discovery of the mass mechanism, used verbatim in
Proposition [368](#prop:HiggsActualResearchQuestion){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:HiggsActualResearchQuestion"} of the present paper.
Establishes the documentary basis for: (i) Higgs's 1960 starting
research situation ("in search of a worthwhile research programme"
having "become interested in quantum gravity"); (ii) the 1961 attraction
to spontaneous symmetry breaking via the Nambu--Goldstone
superconductivity analogy; (iii) the 16 July 1964 reading of Gilbert's
paper; (iv) the weekend 18--19 July 1964 Schwinger-Coulomb-gauge insight
("Schwinger's way of formulating gauge theories undermined the axioms
which had been used to prove the Goldstone theorem"); (v) the 24 July
1964 submission to Physics Letters; (vi) the 31 July 1964 second paper,
its rejection by the CERN Physics Letters referee as "of no obvious
relevance to particle physics," the revision for Physical Review Letters
with the added final-paragraph remark on the residual massive spin-zero
boson; (vii) the 1966 Harvard seminar where Glashow "did not recognise
its relevance to his electroweak theory." The lecture contains zero
references to time as a primitive structure, a fourth dimension,
expansion, or the imaginary unit $i$ as anything other than a
calculational ingredient --- the null-finding documented in
Proposition [370](#prop:HiggsNeverAssociatedWithMovingDimension){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:HiggsNeverAssociatedWithMovingDimension"}.

Higgs, P. W. (1964). Broken symmetries, massless particles and gauge
fields. *Physics Letters* **12**, 132--133.
<https://doi.org/10.1016/0031-9163(64)91136-9>. Higgs's first 1964
paper, written during the week following the 18--19 July weekend
insight, sent to Physics Letters on 24 July 1964 and accepted. Contains
the loophole result: the axioms used in the Goldstone--Salam--Weinberg
1962 proof do not hold for relativistic gauge theories, so the Goldstone
theorem is evaded. Does not yet contain the Higgs boson; the central
content is the loophole demonstration.

Higgs, P. W. (1964). Broken symmetries and the masses of gauge bosons.
*Physical Review Letters* **13**(16), 508--509.
<https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.508>. The famous 1964 paper
containing the longitudinal-mode-becoming-massive computation and the
final-paragraph remark on the residual massive spin-zero boson (the
Higgs boson). Submitted to Physics Letters on 31 July 1964 and rejected;
revised, augmented with "remarks on possible physical consequences"
including the residual-boson remark, and submitted to Physical Review
Letters; received 31 August 1964, published 19 October 1964. Refereed by
Nambu, who requested the comparison footnote to the contemporaneous
Englert--Brout paper. The complete primary-source of the 1964 Higgs
paper consists of (i) the introduction noting that the Goldstone theorem
fails when the conserved currents are coupled to gauge fields; (ii) the
simplest illustrative model: a complex scalar field with Mexican-hat
self-interaction coupled to an electromagnetic gauge field; (iii) the
symmetry-breaking analysis showing the Goldstone mode becomes the
longitudinal polarisation of the now-massive "photon"; (iv) the
final-paragraph remark on the residual "incomplete multiplets of scalar
and vector bosons," implying the existence of a massive spin-zero boson.
The mathematics is the Channel-A algebraic-symmetry shadow of the
Channel-B geometric reading developed in Part IV of the present paper.

Higgs, P. W. (1966). Spontaneous symmetry breakdown without massless
bosons. *Physical Review* **145**(4), 1156--1163.
<https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.145.1156>. Higgs's longer 1966 paper,
written autumn 1965 at Chapel Hill, North Carolina, during a sabbatical
year invited by Bryce DeWitt as a consequence of Higgs's interest in
quantum gravity. Develops the full classical and quantum theory of the
mechanism introduced in the 1964 papers. The talks given at Princeton
(March 1966) and Harvard (March 1966) presenting this work are the
occasions of the documented non-recognition by Glashow
(Remark [373](#rem:GlashowCoda){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:GlashowCoda"}).

Englert, F., & Brout, R. (1964). Broken symmetry and the mass of gauge
vector mesons. *Physical Review Letters* **13**(9), 321--323.
<https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.321>. The contemporaneous
companion paper to Higgs 1964 [@Higgs1964PRL], received by PRL on 26
June 1964 and published on 31 August 1964. Independently derived the
gauge-boson-mass mechanism via spontaneous symmetry breaking. Unlike
Higgs's revised paper, does not explicitly mention the residual massive
scalar boson. The companion 2013 Nobel Lecture by Englert ("The BEH
Mechanism and Its Scalar Boson") confirms the same algebraic-symmetry
methodology: the entire mechanism is treated in the Channel-A idiom of
gauge invariance, vacuum expectation values, and scalar field dynamics,
with no association of the mechanism to time as foundational, to a
fourth dimension, or to cosmological expansion.

Guralnik, G. S., Hagen, C. R., & Kibble, T. W. B. (1964). Global
conservation laws and massless particles. *Physical Review Letters*
**13**(20), 585--587. <https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.585>. The
third 1964 PRL paper on the mass mechanism, received 12 October 1964 and
published 16 November 1964. Independent derivation of the
gauge-boson-mass result emphasising the modification of the
conservation-law structure. The three 1964 PRL papers (Englert--Brout 26
June; Higgs 31 August; Guralnik--Hagen--Kibble 12 October) are the
record of the mass mechanism. None of the three associates the mechanism
with a moving fourth dimension, time as primitive, or cosmological
expansion.

Anderson, P. W. (1963). Plasmons, gauge invariance, and mass. *Physical
Review* **130**(1), 439--442. <https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.130.439>.
Anderson's 1963 condensed-matter precedent for the mass mechanism,
developed at Bell Labs in the summer of 1962, received November 1962,
published April 1963. Establishes that in a superconductor where the
local gauge symmetry is broken spontaneously, the Goldstone (plasmon)
mode becomes massive due to the gauge-field interaction, with the
electromagnetic modes also acquiring mass (Meissner effect). Anderson's
verbatim remark, quoted by
Higgs [@Higgs2013NobelLectureEvadingGoldstone]: "We conclude, then, that
the Goldstone zero-mass difficulty is not a serious one, because we can
probably cancel it off against an equal Yang--Mills zero-mass problem."
However, Anderson did not show that there was a flaw in the Goldstone
theorem and did not discuss any relativistic model, so particle
theorists received the remark with skepticism. The condensed-matter
source case is what ports the algebra (Goldstone modes; gauge
invariance; vev structure) into the relativistic Higgs mechanism, and is
the reason (D2 of
Remark [371](#rem:WhyHiggsFoundersDidNotSee){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:WhyHiggsFoundersDidNotSee"}) that the geometry of the
moving fourth dimension is not in the source case to inherit.

Goldstone, J., Salam, A., & Weinberg, S. (1962). Broken symmetries.
*Physical Review* **127**(3), 965--970.
<https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.127.965>. The Goldstone theorem proper,
building on Goldstone's 1961 conjecture (Nuovo Cimento 19, 154).
Statement: in a manifestly Lorentz-invariant quantum field theory, if
there is a continuous symmetry under which the Lagrangian is invariant,
then either the vacuum state is also invariant or there must exist
spinless particles of zero mass. The obstacle Higgs evaded in July 1964
by appeal to the Schwinger Coulomb-gauge precedent.

Gilbert, W. (1964). Broken symmetries and massless particles. *Physical
Review Letters* **12**(25), 713--714.
<https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.12.713>. The Gilbert paper that
Higgs read on 16 July 1964 (the journal having arrived by sea, a month
late) and that triggered the discovery the following weekend. Gilbert
argued that the Klein--Lee proposal for evading Goldstone's theorem by
adding an extra term to the conservation-law equation was barred in a
Lorentz-invariant theory. Higgs's response over the weekend of 18--19
July: "Oh yes you could." Gilbert subsequently transitioned to molecular
biology and later received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry (1980).

Glashow, S. L. (1961). Partial-symmetries of weak interactions. *Nuclear
Physics* **22**(4), 579--588.
<https://doi.org/10.1016/0029-5582(61)90469-2>. Glashow's 1961
electroweak unification proposal, predating the Higgs mechanism by three
years. The unification required a mechanism for gauge-boson mass that
Glashow did not supply; Higgs's 1964 mechanism supplied it, but Glashow
did not recognise its relevance to his own theory at the March 1966
Harvard seminar where Higgs presented the work
(Remark [373](#rem:GlashowCoda){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:GlashowCoda"}). The full electroweak Lagrangian
incorporating the Higgs mechanism was assembled by Weinberg (1967) and
Salam (1968), three years after Higgs's papers.

Higgs, P. W. (2007). Prehistory of the Higgs boson. *Comptes Rendus
Physique* **8**(9), 970--972.
<https://doi.org/10.1016/j.crhy.2006.12.006>. Higgs's own 2007
historical reconstruction of the prehistory of the discovery, organised
as a chronological list: 1928 Heisenberg (ferromagnetism,
nearest-neighbour interaction); 1947 Bogoliubov (superfluidity, Bose
condensation); 1950 Ginzburg--Landau (superconductivity, Bose
condensation of charged quasi-particles); 1957 BCS theory; 1960 Nambu
(relativistic models, scalar condensate breaks symmetry); 1961 Goldstone
(spinless zero-mass excitations); 1962 Goldstone--Salam--Weinberg
(proved Goldstone's theorem); 1963 Anderson (the mechanism in
superconductors); 1964 Higgs (local gauge invariance fails axioms of
Goldstone). The chronological pre-history confirms the documentary
record: every precedent on which the Higgs mechanism rests is from the
condensed-matter or algebraic-symmetry tradition; none associates the
mechanism with a moving fourth dimension, time as primitive, or
cosmological expansion. The source case (D2 of
Remark [371](#rem:WhyHiggsFoundersDidNotSee){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:WhyHiggsFoundersDidNotSee"}) is condensed-matter
throughout.

Wikipedia (2024). Peter Higgs.
<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Higgs>. The Wikipedia article on
Peter Higgs, consulted as a secondary source for the documented quote
"there was no 'eureka moment' in the development of the theory" (Higgs's
own characterisation, also recorded in interviews and obituaries). The
article also documents the failed weekend camping trip to the Scottish
Highlands during which Higgs developed the basic fundamentals of his
theory after returning to his Edinburgh New Town apartment, the obituary
record on his passing in April 2024 at age 94, and his discomfort with
the "God particle" nickname.

Atiyah, M. F. (2010). *From Quantum Physics to Number Theory: A Geometer
Explores the Universe*. Palestra Especial (Special Lecture) at the
Instituto Nacional de Matemática Pura e Aplicada (IMPA), Rio de Janeiro,
August 2010. Video: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lp2cXnNt0Xs>. The
primary-source documentary record of Atiyah's research-programme talk at
IMPA in 2010, used verbatim throughout
§[19.10](#ssec:AtiyahEndorsesTheLineage){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:AtiyahEndorsesTheLineage"} of the present paper.
Atiyah's statements: (i) endorsement of Dirac's 1939 prediction of the
deep connection between complex-variable theory and the Lorentz group
(Proposition [375](#prop:AtiyahEndorsesDiracLorentz){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:AtiyahEndorsesDiracLorentz"}); (ii) endorsement of
Dirac's 1939 four-dimensional-uniqueness prediction with Donaldson
exotica as vindication
(Proposition [377](#prop:AtiyahEndorsesFourDimensionalUniqueness){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:AtiyahEndorsesFourDimensionalUniqueness"}); (iii) the
Atiyah--Moore shifted-Dirac equation with the Dirac operator as unique
first-order Lorentz-invariant motion generator
(Proposition [379](#prop:AtiyahMooreFromOneWay){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:AtiyahMooreFromOneWay"}); (iv) the Schrödinger--Dirac vs
Heisenberg--Connes split
(Proposition [381](#prop:AtiyahNamesSchroedingerHeisenbergSplit){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:AtiyahNamesSchroedingerHeisenbergSplit"}); (v) the
gravity-from-octonions Magic-Square proposal
(Proposition [384](#prop:AtiyahMagicSquareGravityFromOctonions){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:AtiyahMagicSquareGravityFromOctonions"}); (vi) the
Hilbert--Pólya / quantum-gravity / Riemann-Hypothesis conjecture
(Proposition [386](#prop:AtiyahHilbertPolyaQuantumGravity){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:AtiyahHilbertPolyaQuantumGravity"}); (vii)
self-classification as a follower of Einstein and Dirac; (viii)
mystic-synthesis programme
(Remark [383](#rem:AtiyahMysticSynthesis){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:AtiyahMysticSynthesis"}); (ix) constructivist commitment
that physical quantities should never be infinite or infinitesimally
small. The lecture is the most direct contemporary primary-source
endorsement of the programme the present paper executes from
$dx_4/dt = ic$.

Atiyah, M., & Moore, G. W. (2010). A Shifted View of Fundamental
Physics. arXiv preprint arXiv:1009.3176.
<https://arxiv.org/abs/1009.3176>. Submitted 16 September 2010, based on
Atiyah's lecture at the Singer 85 conference. Proposes relativistic
versions of delayed differential equations: the shifted Dirac equation
$\{i\hbar D - mc + ik\exp(-rD)\}\psi = 0$ where $D$ is the Dirac
operator, and corresponding shifted Einstein--Maxwell equations. Key
result: the shifted Einstein--Maxwell equations naturally incorporate a
small but nonzero cosmological constant of order $10^{-56}$ in natural
units. The construction is motivated by the uniqueness of the Dirac
operator as the only first-order Lorentz-invariant differential operator
(the same uniqueness identified in
Proposition [263](#prop:GeneratorFlow){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:GeneratorFlow"} of the present paper). The framework's
reading
(Proposition [379](#prop:AtiyahMooreFromOneWay){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:AtiyahMooreFromOneWay"}): the retardation/advance
asymmetry that Atiyah--Moore introduce by hand is the field-theoretic
shadow of the one-way orientation A4 of the McGucken Principle. The
cosmological-constant scale that emerges naturally is the same scale the
framework's MG-Cosmology paper [@MG-Cosmology] derives the dark-energy
density from. Atiyah and Moore identified the right operator (the Dirac
operator) and the right scale (the cosmological constant) but did not
yet have the substrate principle from which their construction descends.

Dirac, P. A. M. (1939). The relation between mathematics and physics.
*Proceedings of the Royal Society of Edinburgh* **59** (Part II),
122--129. Address delivered on presentation of the James Scott prize, 6
February 1939. Reprinted in *The Collected Works of P. A. M. Dirac,
1924--1948* (R. H. Dalitz, ed.), Cambridge University Press, 1995.
Available at <https://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/events/jamesscott/dirac.pdf>.
The primary-source document containing Dirac's two prophetic statements
that Atiyah 2010 endorses as "remarkably accurate predictions": (i) the
four-dimensional uniqueness statement (vindicated by Donaldson's
exotic-smooth-structures result); (ii) the prediction of a "deep hidden
connection between the theory of functions of a complex variable and the
spacetime of restricted relativity" (vindicated by twistor theory,
string theory, and --- in the present paper --- by the Möbius--Lorentz
isomorphism that descends from the single complex structure of
$dx_4/dt = ic$,
Theorem [376](#thm:AtiyahDiracIsTheSingleI){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:AtiyahDiracIsTheSingleI"}).

Berry, M. V., & Keating, J. P. (1999). The Riemann Zeros and Eigenvalue
Asymptotics. *SIAM Review* **41**(2), 236--266.
<https://doi.org/10.1137/S0036144598347497>. The foundational paper
proposing the $H = xp$ Hamiltonian as the candidate Hilbert--Pólya
source. Establishes: (i) the dilation Hamiltonian $H = xp$ in a
regularised phase space gives, semiclassically, the smooth counting
function of the Riemann zeros; (ii) the conjectured Hilbert--Pólya
Hamiltonian must be chaotic with isolated periodic orbits related to
prime numbers (periods $\log p$), must break time-reversal symmetry, and
must be quasi-one-dimensional; (iii) the Berry--Keating $H = xp$ model
satisfies time-reversal-symmetry-breaking and quasi-one-dimensionality
but not chaos, because the classical trajectories are open hyperbolas.
The model has driven a large subsequent literature including Sierra's
2017 Dirac-in-Rindler realisation [@Sierra2017RiemannZerosSpectrum] and
the Atiyah-endorsed quantum-gravity conjecture [@Atiyah2010IMPALecture].

Connes, A. (1999). Trace formula in noncommutative geometry and the
zeros of the Riemann zeta function. *Selecta Mathematica* **5**(1),
29--106. <https://doi.org/10.1007/s000290050042>. The foundational paper
on Connes's adelic Riemann construction. Establishes a
noncommutative-geometric framework in which the Riemann Hypothesis is
equivalent to a trace formula on a certain adèle-class space, with the
Riemann zeros appearing as "absorption spectrum" (missing modes) rather
than as direct eigenvalues. The construction is the Channel-A
(Heisenberg-school, in Atiyah's terminology of [@Atiyah2010IMPALecture])
approach to the Hilbert--Pólya programme. Atiyah's 2010
diagnosis [@Atiyah2010IMPALecture]: "Connes has not succeeded because he
has not really touched gravity properly, because \[he is\] dealing with
associative algebras." The framework's reading: Connes's construction is
correct at the Channel-A level; the Channel-B (gravity, the $x_4$-flow,
the Compton clock) is the missing content that the framework supplies.

Odlyzko, A. M. (1987). On the distribution of spacings between zeros of
the zeta function. *Mathematics of Computation* **48**(177), 273--308.
<https://doi.org/10.1090/S0025-5718-1987-0866115-0>. The empirical work
establishing the GUE statistics of the Riemann zeros. Odlyzko computed
millions of Riemann zeros numerically and compared their
pair-correlation function to the GUE prediction; the agreement is to
extraordinary precision. This is the empirical foundation of the
Hilbert--Pólya / quantum-chaos correspondence: the Riemann zeros
statistically look exactly like the eigenvalues of a random Hermitian
matrix from a time-reversal-symmetry-broken ensemble. The framework's
reading (Reason 2 of
Remark [387](#rem:SevenReasonsQuantumGravityRiemann){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:SevenReasonsQuantumGravityRiemann"}): the GUE statistics
is the empirical signature of the time-reversal-symmetry-broken
substrate, which in the framework is the one-way orientation A4 of
$dx_4/dt = ic$.

Sierra, G. (2017). The Riemann Zeros as Spectrum and the Riemann
Hypothesis. *Symmetry* **11**(4), 494.
<https://doi.org/10.3390/sym11040494>. Earlier preprint
arXiv:1601.01797. A construction of a self-adjoint operator on a Dirac
fermion in Rindler spacetime under delta-function potentials localised
at the square-free integers, whose spectrum is the non-trivial Riemann
zeros in a precise limit. The Dirac-in-Rindler construction is exactly
the kind of structure the framework's substrate produces (Reason 7 of
Remark [387](#rem:SevenReasonsQuantumGravityRiemann){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:SevenReasonsQuantumGravityRiemann"}): the $x_4$-advance
produces Rindler-type horizons at every event, and the Dirac operator on
this substrate is the framework's $D_M$. Open
Problem [390](#prob:RiemannViaMcGucken){reference-type="ref"
reference="prob:RiemannViaMcGucken"} states this connection explicitly
as the candidate Hilbert--Pólya realisation via the McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework.

Berra-Montiel, J., & Molgado, A. (2025). A Majorana Relativistic Quantum
Spectral Approach to the Riemann Hypothesis in $(1+1)$-Dimensional
Rindler Spacetimes. arXiv preprint arXiv:2503.09644.
<https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.09644>. A construction of an essentially
self-adjoint Hamiltonian whose spectrum aligns with the non-trivial
zeros of the Riemann zeta function, via a Majorana relativistic quantum
spectral approach in $(1+1)$-dimensional Rindler spacetimes. Establishes
a spectral correspondence via Mellin--Barnes integral formulation
preserved under CPT symmetry across entangled Rindler wedges. Together
with [@Sierra2017RiemannZerosSpectrum], this is the most direct recent
realisation of the Hilbert--Pólya programme through Rindler-Dirac
structures (Reason 7 of
Remark [387](#rem:SevenReasonsQuantumGravityRiemann){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:SevenReasonsQuantumGravityRiemann"}); the framework's
substrate naturally supplies the Rindler-Dirac structure required (Open
Problem [390](#prob:RiemannViaMcGucken){reference-type="ref"
reference="prob:RiemannViaMcGucken"}).

Betzios, P., Gaddam, N., & Papadoulaki, O. (2020). Black holes, quantum
chaos, and the Riemann hypothesis. *SciPost Physics Core* **4**, 032.
arXiv preprint arXiv:2004.09523. <https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.09523>.
Proposes that the near-horizon dynamics of Schwarzschild black holes
produces a quantum chaotic Hamiltonian whose spectrum is in
correspondence with the zeros of the Riemann zeta and Dirichlet beta
functions. Explicit black-hole-physics realisation of the Hilbert--Pólya
programme through quantum gravity, directly supporting Atiyah's 2010
conjecture [@Atiyah2010IMPALecture] that the Riemann Hypothesis should
come out of quantum gravity (Reason 6 of
Remark [387](#rem:SevenReasonsQuantumGravityRiemann){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:SevenReasonsQuantumGravityRiemann"}). The framework's
reading: the near-horizon dynamics is the Channel-B reading of the
$x_4$-advance at the black-hole horizon, where the gravitational Compton
clock (H12) reaches the Schwarzschild radius.

Sierra, G., & Townsend, P. K. (2011). Landau levels and Riemann zeros.
*Physical Review Letters* **101**, 110201. The $H = xp$ model revisited
with modifications $H = x(p + \ell_p^2/p)$ producing closed periodic
orbits whose spectrum matches the average Riemann zeros. The
modification adds a length scale $\ell_p$ by hand; the framework's
reading (Feature M3 of
Remark [400](#rem:ThreeMcGuckenChaosFeatures){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:ThreeMcGuckenChaosFeatures"}) is that the natural
infrared scale from MG-Cosmology might play this role, derived rather
than postulated.

Bogomolny, E., Georgeot, B., Giannoni, M.-J., & Schmit, C. (1992).
Chaotic billiards generated by arithmetic groups. *Physical Review
Letters* **69**, 1477. The seminal observation that arithmetic chaos
(classical chaos on quotients of hyperbolic space by arithmetic groups,
e.g., the modular group $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$) does *not* produce
GUE statistics despite the chaos being present, but rather produces
Poisson-like statistics. The arithmetic is precisely what disrupts the
GUE universality. Relevant to the framework's arithmetic-boundary
clause: if the framework's substrate were to reach into the arithmetic
core, it would not produce GUE; the fact that the Riemann zeros do show
GUE statistics is evidence that the Hilbert--Pólya substrate is not pure
arithmetic chaos.

Mehta, M. L. (2004). *Random Matrices* (3rd edition). Pure and Applied
Mathematics 142, Elsevier. ISBN 978-0-12-088409-4. The standard
reference for the Wigner--Dyson random-matrix classification: GOE
(orthogonal, $T$-symmetric integer spin), GUE (unitary, broken $T$), GSE
(symplectic, $T$-symmetric half-integer spin). The framework's substrate
is in the GUE class by
Theorem [399](#thm:McGuckenGUESymmetryClass){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:McGuckenGUESymmetryClass"}: aspect A4 of $dx_4/dt = ic$
breaks $T$
(Proposition [397](#prop:McGuckenBreaksTimeReversal){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:McGuckenBreaksTimeReversal"}), placing the substrate in
GUE rather than GOE.

Sierra, G. (2007). A quantum mechanical model of the Riemann zeros.
arXiv preprint arXiv:0712.0705. The quantisation of the $H = xp$
Hamiltonian with phase-space delimited by two boundary functions,
producing a continuum spectrum with embedded resonances at the average
Riemann-zero positions. The boundary functions are imposed by hand to
produce closed orbits; the framework's Feature M3
(Remark [400](#rem:ThreeMcGuckenChaosFeatures){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:ThreeMcGuckenChaosFeatures"}) is the candidate
substrate-derived version of these boundary functions, with the Hubble
scale and the Compton scale supplying the natural boundaries.

McGucken, E. (2026). *The Mothership Identification --- The Orthodox
Quantum Measurement Problem and the Orthodox Navier--Stokes
Smoothness-vs-Blowup Problem as the Same Foundational-Geometric Problem
under $dx_4/dt = ic$*. Light Time Dimension Theory.
<https://elliotmcguckenphysics.com/>. The principal identification of
the McGucken corpus joining the QM matter-dynamics tier with the NS
fluid-dynamics tier under $dx_4/dt = ic$. Articulates: (a) the
identification of the orthodox QM measurement problem
(Schrödinger/Born/Heisenberg 1925--1926, von Neumann Prozess 1/Prozess 2
1932, Schrödinger cat 1935) with the orthodox NS smoothness-vs-blowup
problem (Navier 1822, Stokes 1845, Leray 1934, Hopf 1951,
Beale-Kato-Majda 1984, Fefferman/Clay 2000) as the same geometric
problem realised at two distinct finite-mode tiers (Theorem 33 at G2
grade); (b) the dual-channel structure (Channel A: Schrödinger/Euler,
time-symmetric, conservative; Channel B: Born/viscous-Laplacian,
time-asymmetric, dissipative) descending from $dx_4/dt = ic$ via the
categorical-functorial Noether-functor/entropy-monotonicity-functor
construction at \[42, Theorem 80\] of the source paper; (c) the McWick
rotation $x_4= ict \mapsto \tau = it$ as the transformation taking the
QM tier into the fluid-dynamics tier with the $i$ exteriorised; (d)
Madelung 1927's hydrodynamic formulation of quantum mechanics as the
closest the orthodox tradition came to the QM $\equiv$ NS
identification, with ninety-nine years of orthodox non-recognition; (e)
the McGucken-Compton coupling at the molecular level supplying the
per-molecule diffusion constant
$D^{(\mathrm{McG})} = \varepsilon^2 m c^4/(2\hbar \gamma^2)$ whose
Maxwell--Boltzmann averaging produces the macroscopic viscosity
$\mu \sim \rho \lambda \bar v$; (f) the Reynolds-number transition as
the empirical operational signature of the Channel A / Channel B
asymmetry at the fluid-dynamics tier. The mothership reference for
Theorem [405](#thm:McWickRotationSuppliesChaos){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:McWickRotationSuppliesChaos"} of the present paper,
supplying the content that Feature M1 of
Remark [400](#rem:ThreeMcGuckenChaosFeatures){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:ThreeMcGuckenChaosFeatures"} reaches the chaos required
for GUE statistics through the Wick-rotated thermodynamic shadow rather
than through the QM substrate directly.

McGucken, E. (2026). *The McGucken-Compton Coupling: Mass as the Rate of
Perpendicular $x_4$-Winding, with the Per-Molecule Diffusion Constant
$D^{(\mathrm{McG})} = \varepsilon^2 m c^4/(2\hbar \gamma^2)$ as the
Foundational-Geometric Source of the Maxwell--Boltzmann Viscosity
$\mu \sim \rho \lambda \bar v$*. Light Time Dimension Theory.
<https://elliotmcguckenphysics.com/>. The technical-level treatment of
the McGucken-Compton coupling: mass identified as the rate of
perpendicular-$x_4$ winding
(Theorem [232](#thm:ComptonX4Coupling){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ComptonX4Coupling"} of the present paper, H10), with each
species $f$ winding at Compton frequency
$\omega_C^{(f)} = m_f c^2/\hbar$ and Compton wavelength
$\lambda_C^{(f)} = \hbar/(m_f c)$. The per-molecule diffusion constant
at the molecular level is derived from the Wick-rotated Compton-coupling
structure as
$D^{(\mathrm{McG})} = \varepsilon^2 m c^4/(2\hbar \gamma^2) > 0$, with
$\varepsilon$ the McGucken-Wick coupling and $\gamma$ the Lorentz factor
of the molecule. The Maxwell--Boltzmann kinetic-theory averaging
produces the macroscopic viscosity $\mu \sim \rho \lambda \bar v$ as the
averaged shadow of $D^{(\mathrm{McG})}$ operating at every molecule,
supplying the geometric source of the viscous Laplacian of Navier 1822
and Stokes 1845 that the orthodox tradition has not identified in the
two centuries since. Used in
Theorem [405](#thm:McWickRotationSuppliesChaos){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:McWickRotationSuppliesChaos"} of the present paper as the
content of Feature M1's chaos-generation avenue.

Madelung, E. (1927). Quantentheorie in hydrodynamischer Form.
*Zeitschrift für Physik* **40**(3--4), 322--326.
<https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01400372>. The foundational paper deriving
the equivalence of the Schrödinger equation with a pair of hydrodynamic
equations (continuity equation + Euler-type equation with
quantum-potential force $Q$). *The closest the orthodox tradition has
come to the QM $\equiv$ NS identification*, articulated in print in
1927, two years after the birth of quantum mechanics. The orthodox
tradition has had ninety-nine years to recognise the Madelung equations
as the operational evidence of the QM $\equiv$ NS identification and has
not done so for the three reasons articulated in [@MG-NSQM-Mothership
§15B.6]. Used in
Theorem [405](#thm:McWickRotationSuppliesChaos){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:McWickRotationSuppliesChaos"} of the present paper as the
anchor for the QM-to-fluid-dynamics correspondence.

Maxwell, J. C. (1867). On the Dynamical Theory of Gases. *Philosophical
Transactions of the Royal Society of London* **157**, 49--88.
<https://doi.org/10.1098/rstl.1867.0004>. The kinetic-theory derivation
of the macroscopic viscosity as an averaged microscopic quantity, with
the identification $\mu \sim \rho \lambda \bar v$ that the framework
reads as the macroscopic shadow of the underlying McGucken-Compton
coupling at the molecular level.

Boltzmann, L. (1872). Weitere Studien über das Wärmegleichgewicht unter
Gasmolekülen. *Sitzungsberichte der Akademie der Wissenschaften zu Wien*
**66**, 275--370. The kinetic-theory derivation of the H-theorem and the
Stosszahlansatz molecular-chaos assumption, supplying the empirically
grounded Channel B injection at the statistical-mechanical tier that the
framework reads as the content of Feature M1's Wick-rotated chaos
avenue.

Reynolds, O. (1883). An Experimental Investigation of the Circumstances
which Determine whether the Motion of Water shall be Direct or Sinuous,
and of the Law of Resistance in Parallel Channels. *Philosophical
Transactions of the Royal Society of London* **174**, 935--982.
<https://doi.org/10.1098/rstl.1883.0029>. The experimental establishment
of the laminar-to-turbulent transition at a critical Reynolds number
$\mathrm{Re} = \rho U L / \mu$, supplying the empirical operational
signature of the Channel A / Channel B asymmetry at the fluid-dynamics
tier --- with the turbulent regime being the classical-chaotic content
that the McWick-rotated $dx_4/dt = ic$ produces through the shadow
Maxwell--Boltzmann statistical-mechanical content.

Poincaré, H. (1905). Sur la dynamique de l'électron. *Comptes Rendus de
l'Académie des Sciences* **140**, 1504--1508. The foundational paper
introducing $x_4= ict$ as a mathematical formalism for treating
spacetime as a four-dimensional Euclidean manifold. The orthodox
tradition's classification of $x_4= ict$ as a mathematical formalism
(rather than as a real perpendicular fourth dimension advancing at $c$)
traces to Poincaré 1905 and was consolidated by Minkowski 1908
[@Minkowski1908]; the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's correction of
this classification is at
Theorem [276](#thm:CausalStructureExpansion){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:CausalStructureExpansion"} (H11.1) and aspect A2 of
Proposition [257](#prop:AspectDecomposition){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:AspectDecomposition"} of the present paper.

Minkowski, H. (1908). Die Grundgleichungen für die elektromagnetischen
Vorgänge in bewegten Körpern. *Nachrichten von der Königlichen
Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen* 53--111. The consolidation
of $x_4= ict$ as the four-dimensional spacetime formalism of special
relativity, with the philosophical position that "henceforth space by
itself, and time by itself, are doomed to fade away into mere shadows."
Minkowski's geometric vision of four-dimensional spacetime is correct in
its mathematics; the orthodox interpretation that the imaginary unit $i$
in $x_4= ict$ is a notational convenience rather than a perpendicularity
marker of a real fourth dimension is what the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework corrects via aspect A2 of
Proposition [257](#prop:AspectDecomposition){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:AspectDecomposition"}.

Selberg, A. (1956). Harmonic analysis and discontinuous groups in weakly
symmetric Riemannian spaces with applications to Dirichlet series.
*Journal of the Indian Mathematical Society* **20**, 47--87. The
foundational paper on the Selberg trace formula and Selberg zeta
function for compact hyperbolic surfaces. Establishes the formal
identity between primitive closed geodesics on a hyperbolic surface and
Laplacian eigenvalues, with the Selberg zeta function
$Z(s) = \prod_{\{\gamma_0\}} \prod_k (1 - N(\gamma_0)^{-(s+k)})$ as the
Euler-product realisation of the structure. *The Selberg trace formula
is the case in which the primes-as-orbits and zeros-as-eigenvalues
identification of the Hilbert--Pólya programme is established as a
theorem rather than a conjecture*, in the specific context of geodesic
flow on hyperbolic surfaces. The arithmetic-chaos pathology
(Bogomolny--Georgeot--Giannoni--Schmit 1992
[@BogomolnyGeorgeotGiannoniSchmit1992ArithmeticChaos]) shows that the
Selberg-style construction for arithmetic surfaces produces Poisson-like
statistics rather than GUE, ruling out the arithmetic-surface route for
the actual Riemann zeros
(Theorem [413](#thm:SelbergArithmeticChaosLimitation){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SelbergArithmeticChaosLimitation"} of the present paper).

Marklof, J. (2003). Selberg's Trace Formula: An Introduction. arXiv
preprint math-ph/0407059. <https://arxiv.org/abs/math-ph/0407059>.
Pedagogical introduction to the Selberg trace formula, the Selberg zeta
function, the relationship to Riemann via the Gutzwiller--Riemann-Weil
analogy, and the prime-geodesic theorem on hyperbolic surfaces. Used as
the standard reference for the Selberg structure in the present paper.

Sarnak, P. (1981). Asymptotic behavior of periodic orbits of the
horocycle flow and Eisenstein series. *Communications on Pure and
Applied Mathematics* **34**(6), 719--739. Establishes the asymptotic
behaviour of periodic orbits of the horocycle flow on arithmetic
hyperbolic surfaces, with the identification of primitive horocycle
orbits with primes in the modular-group setting. Used in the present
paper's Selberg-trace-formula engagement
(Proposition [412](#prop:SelbergTraceFormula){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:SelbergTraceFormula"}) as a reference for the
prime-orbit content on arithmetic hyperbolic surfaces.

Maldacena, J., Shenker, S. H., & Stanford, D. (2016). A bound on chaos.
*Journal of High Energy Physics* **2016**, 106. arXiv preprint
arXiv:1503.01409. <https://doi.org/10.1007/JHEP08(2016)106>. Establishes
the sharp bound on the rate of growth of chaos in thermal quantum
systems: $\lambda_L \leq 2\pi k_B T/\hbar$, with the bound saturated by
black holes (the canonical maximally-chaotic system in the AdS/CFT
picture). The bound is central to the holographic correspondence and to
the SYK model's role as the canonical many-body realisation of maximal
chaos. Used in
Theorem [415](#thm:McGuckenSaturatesMaldacena){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:McGuckenSaturatesMaldacena"} of the present paper: the
McGucken substrate's Rindler-type horizon structure at every event
positions the framework to saturate this bound in the McWick-rotated
thermodynamic regime, placing the framework in the same
maximally-chaotic universality class as black holes and SYK and
consistent with Atiyah's 2010 quantum-gravity conjecture
(Proposition [386](#prop:AtiyahHilbertPolyaQuantumGravity){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:AtiyahHilbertPolyaQuantumGravity"}).

Kitaev, A. (2015). A simple model of quantum holography. Talks given at
the KITP, University of California, Santa Barbara, April 2015.
<http://online.kitp.ucsb.edu/online/entangled15/kitaev/>. With Sachdev,
S., & Ye, J. (1993). Gapless spin-fluid ground state in a random quantum
Heisenberg magnet. *Physical Review Letters* **70**, 3339--3342.
<https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.70.3339>. The SYK
(Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev) model: a many-body fermion system that saturates
the Maldacena chaos bound and is conjectured to be holographically dual
to JT (Jackiw--Teitelboim) gravity. The canonical many-body realisation
of maximal chaos in the Strategy 4 picture of
Remark [410](#rem:SixChaosStrategies){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:SixChaosStrategies"}. Used in the present paper as the
standard reference for the holographic-chaos universality class.

Bost, J.-B., & Connes, A. (1995). Hecke algebras, type III factors and
phase transitions with spontaneous symmetry breaking in number theory.
*Selecta Mathematica New Series* **1**(3), 411--457.
<https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01589495>. The foundational paper on the
Bost--Connes system: a $C^*$-dynamical system constructed from Hecke
algebras of the $ax+b$ groups over the rationals, with partition
function the Riemann zeta function
$Z(\beta) = \zeta(\beta) = \prod_p (1 - p^{-\beta})^{-1}$ in its Euler
product form. The system exhibits a phase transition with spontaneous
symmetry breaking at inverse temperature $\beta = 1$ (the pole of
$\zeta$), with the Galois group
$\mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}^{\mathrm{cycl}}/\mathbb{Q})$ of the cyclotomic
extension as symmetry group. *The primes are encoded in the construction
from the start* via the adelic structure
$\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q}= \mathbb{R}\times \prod_p^{\rm restricted} \mathbb{Q}_p$.
Used throughout
§[19.10](#ssec:AtiyahEndorsesTheLineage){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:AtiyahEndorsesTheLineage"} of the present paper as the
canonical Strategy-2 / Strategy-6 reference for the
noncommutative-geometric Hilbert--Pólya approach
(Remark [410](#rem:SixChaosStrategies){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:SixChaosStrategies"}), and as the basis for the
Connes-complementarity identification
(Theorem [417](#thm:ConnesComplementarity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ConnesComplementarity"}): Connes has the primes built
into the adelic substrate by construction; the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework supplies the physical-dynamics (gravity, $x_4$-flow, Compton
clock) that the Connes algebraic-spectral substrate lacks. The Atiyah
2010 conjecture
(Proposition [386](#prop:AtiyahHilbertPolyaQuantumGravity){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:AtiyahHilbertPolyaQuantumGravity"}) that the
Hilbert--Pólya source requires both halves is the diagnosis of the
complementarity.

Titchmarsh, E. C. (1986). *The Theory of the Riemann Zeta-Function* (2nd
edition, revised by D. R. Heath-Brown). Oxford University Press. ISBN
0-19-853369-1. The standard reference for the analytic theory of the
Riemann zeta function: functional equation, critical line, von Mangoldt
expansion, Riemann's explicit formula, the logarithmic derivative
$\zeta'/\zeta$ and its residues at zeros, and the connection between the
prime distribution and the zero spectrum. Used in
Proposition [432](#prop:ResidueZeroPrimeConnection){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:ResidueZeroPrimeConnection"} of the present paper as the
documentary reference for the standard analytic-number-theory content
that the Move-G identifications interpret.

Edwards, H. M. (1974). *Riemann's Zeta Function*. Pure and Applied
Mathematics 58, Academic Press. (Reprinted 2001, Dover Publications,
ISBN 0-486-41740-9.) Comprehensive treatment of the zeta function
organised around Riemann's original 1859 paper, with detailed
development of the functional equation derivation from the
theta-function modular transformation, the explicit formula, the prime
number theorem, and the historical development of the Riemann
Hypothesis. Used in
Proposition [432](#prop:ResidueZeroPrimeConnection){reference-type="ref"
reference="prop:ResidueZeroPrimeConnection"} as a secondary documentary
reference, and in
Theorem [434](#thm:SpinorCriticalLineIdentification){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SpinorCriticalLineIdentification"} clause (i) for the
modular-weight-$1/2$ origin of the critical line in the functional
equation.

Gross, D. J. (2015). The Frontiers of Fundamental Physics. Della Pietra
Lecture, Simons Center for Geometry and Physics, Stony Brook University,
January 28, 2015. Video recording:
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jmPciVdKrFs>. David Gross (2004 Nobel
Prize in Physics for the discovery of asymptotic freedom in quantum
chromodynamics) supplies a comprehensive contemporary survey of the
orthodox-tradition position on fundamental physics: the Standard Model
as "standard theory" on a single t-shirt with $\sim 19$ parameters,
working across 60 orders of magnitude; the enumeration of
orthodox-tradition unanswered questions (origin of particles and their
masses/mixings, dark matter, neutrino masses, matter-vs-antimatter
asymmetry, accelerated cosmological expansion, hints of unification,
hierarchy of scales, vacuum-energy puzzle); the canonical
orthodox-tradition position that spacetime is "probably eventually going
to be understood as an emergent concept, approximate," with the question
"emergent from what?" named explicitly as the open problem. Used in
Theorem [408](#thm:GrossEmergenceVsMcGuckenPrimitive){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:GrossEmergenceVsMcGuckenPrimitive"} of the present paper
as the contemporary Nobel-laureate exemplar of the orthodox-tradition
position on spacetime ontology, with the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework's disagreement statement establishing the opposite ontological
position: $x_4$ is real, perpendicular to the three spatial axes, and
physically advancing at $c$ from every event, with the McGucken
Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ as the primitive from which the rest of physics
descends as theorems.

McGucken, E. (2026). *Thermodynamics Derived from the McGucken Principle

Thermodynamics as a Chain of Theorems of the McGucken Principle of a
Fourth Expanding Dimension $dx_4/dt = ic$*. Light Time Dimension Theory,

<https://elliotmcguckenphysics.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/1_thermodynamics_derived_from_the_mcgucken-principle_-a-unique-simple-and-complete-derivation-of-thermodynamics-as-a-chain-of-theorems-of-the-mcgucken-principle-of-a-fourth-expanding-dim.pdf>.
The principal corpus reference for the macroscopic chain of the unified
T-violation derivation: establishes the strict Second Law
$dS/dt = (3/2)k_B/t > 0$ as Theorem 9, doubly forced by $dx_4/dt = ic$
via two derivationally disjoint analytic routes plus a numerical
confirmation. Channel A proof (Theorem 9 Steps A1--A4): the
Lindeberg--Lévy central limit theorem applied to ISO(3)-invariant
i.i.d. increments (algebraic-symmetry of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via Theorem 2
and Haar uniqueness on $S^2$ via Theorem 5) gives the Gaussian
phase-space density
$\rho(\mathbf{r}, t) = (4\pi Dt)^{-3/2}\exp(-|\mathbf{r}|^2/4Dt)$; the
Boltzmann--Gibbs differential entropy of this Gaussian computes to
$S(t) = (3/2)k_B + (3/2)k_B \ln(4\pi Dt)$, yielding
$dS/dt = (3/2)k_B/t > 0$ as strict positivity forced by the $+ic$
orientation of $dx_4/dt = ic$ rather than as a statistical tendency.
Channel B proof (Theorem 9 Steps B1--B6): the McGucken Sphere from event
$p_0$ has radius $R(t) = c(t-t_0)$ growing strictly because
$dx_4/dt = +ic$ (not $-ic$); iterated Huygens-wavefront propagation with
isotropic angular distribution produces the same Gaussian density via
Chapman--Kolmogorov plus Taylor expansion; the Shannon entropy
$S_{\rm Sphere}(t) = k_B \ln V_{\rm eff}(t)$ of the effective
phase-space volume $V_{\rm eff}(t) = (4\pi Dt)^{3/2} e^{3/2}$ produces
the identical result $S(t) = (3/2)k_B + (3/2)k_B \ln(4\pi Dt)$ by the
Klein correspondence between algebra and geometry. The chain of
supporting theorems: Theorem 1 (wave equation as theorem of $x_4$'s
spherically symmetric expansion), Theorem 2 (algebraic-symmetry of
$dx_4/dt = ic$ as $\mathrm{ISO}(3)$), Theorem 3 (geometric-propagation
as Huygens-wavefront propagation on the McGucken Sphere), Theorem 4
(Compton coupling between matter and the expanding fourth dimension),
Theorem 5 (spatial-projection isotropy of $x_4$-driven displacement),
Theorem 6 (Brownian motion as iterated isotropic displacement), Theorem
7 (probability measure as unique Haar measure on $\mathrm{ISO}(3)$),
Theorem 8 (ergodicity as Huygens-wavefront identity), Theorem 9 (the
strict Second Law itself), Theorem 11 (the five arrows of time as
projections of $+ic$), Theorem 12 (Loschmidt's paradox as dissolution:
Channel A time-symmetric microscopic dynamics descend separately from
Channel B time-asymmetric Second Law, dissolving the conflict ), Theorem
13 (the Past Hypothesis as geometric initial condition), Theorem 19 (the
Universal McGucken Channel B Theorem). *The primary-source reference for

reference="thm:UnifiedTViolationChain"} of the present paper at G1
grade: the macroscopic chain is established at theorem-grade in this

from the Channel-B Carnot--Kelvin--Clausius content to Channel A

The early-2025 corpus articulation of the mechanism (particles dragged

Kobayashi, M. & Maskawa, T. (1973). *CP Violation in the Renormalizable

Wilczek, F. (1999). *Mass Without Mass I: Most of Matter*. Physics Today
**52**(11), 11--13 (November 1999). DOI:
[10.1063/1.882879](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.882879).
<https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v52.i11.11_1.online.pdf>. The
foundational Reference Frame column on the QCD-binding-energy mass of
ordinary matter, establishing that "the bulk of the mass of ordinary
matter (better than 99%) comes from the masses of protons and neutrons,"
with the truncated parameter-free QCD (massless up and down quarks,
gluons only) reproducing the observed proton/neutron masses to within
10% accuracy via the mechanism: "energy stored in the motion of the
quarks, and energy in the color gluon fields that connect them. This
bundling of energy makes the proton's mass." Wilczek attributes the
phrase "mass without mass" to John Archibald Wheeler
[@Wheeler1962Geometrodynamics]. The primary-source reference for the
QCD-binding-energy contribution to proton mass cited in
Corollary [248](#cor:WilczekMassWithoutMass){reference-type="ref"
reference="cor:WilczekMassWithoutMass"} of the present paper.

Wilczek, F. (2000). *Mass without Mass II: The Medium is the Mass-age*.
Physics Today **53**(1), 13--14 (January 2000). DOI:
[10.1063/1.882927](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.882927).
<https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v53.i1.13_1.online.pdf>. The
follow-up Reference Frame column establishing the complementary role of
the Higgs-condensate medium for electron and W/Z masses: "Most of the
mass of ordinary matter, for sure, is the pure energy of moving quarks
and gluons. The remainder, a quantitatively small but qualitatively
crucial remainder --- it includes the mass of electrons --- is all
ascribed to the confounding influence of a pervasive medium, the Higgs
field condensate." The primary-source reference for the Higgs-vs-QCD
splitting of mass cited in
Remark [249](#rem:UnifiedMassReading){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:UnifiedMassReading"} of the present paper.

Wilczek, F. (2012). *Origins of Mass*. Central European Journal of
Physics **10**(5), 1021--1037 (October 2012).
arXiv:[1206.7114](https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.7114) \[hep-ph\].
MIT-CTP/4379. <https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/76733>. The
comprehensive 33-page review of the origins-of-mass problem, established
as an Invited Review for the Central European Journal of Physics and
adapted from Wilczek's April 2012 Atlanta APS meeting talk, with the
August 2012 update covering the CERN Higgs discovery. Establishes: (i)
"Most ($\sim 95\%$) of the mass of protons and neutrons, and thus of
ordinary matter, is due to the back-reaction of color gluon fields
resisting accelerated motion of the quarks and gluons inside"; (ii) the
"QCD Lite" theory --- QCD with three lightest quark masses set to zero
and heavy quarks decoupled --- "is a theory containing no explicit mass
parameters; its only dimensional scale is set by the coupling evolution.
Yet it supports a rich spectrum of massive excitations, notably
including protons and neutrons, that closely resembles the spectrum of
QCD proper"; (iii) the distinction between the QCD "mass without mass"
mechanism and the Higgs-condensate "gauged broken symmetry" mechanism,
with both treated as instances of the same underlying pattern (Lorentz's
1904 electromagnetic-mass programme realised at the QCD level); (iv) the
standard textbook derivation of $W, Z$ masses from the doublet Higgs
condensate; (v) Wilczek's catalogue of open problems: "nothing in these
ideas explains the origin of the mass of the Higgs particle itself, nor
do they greatly elucidate the observed complicated structure of quark
and lepton masses and mixings" and "the origin of most of the mass in
the universe, that in dark matter and dark energy, remains deeply
mysterious." The principal corpus reference for
Theorem [247](#thm:CompositeStateMass){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:CompositeStateMass"},
Corollary [248](#cor:WilczekMassWithoutMass){reference-type="ref"
reference="cor:WilczekMassWithoutMass"}, and
Remark [249](#rem:UnifiedMassReading){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:UnifiedMassReading"} of the present paper.

Wheeler, J. A. (1962). *Geometrodynamics*. Academic Press, New York. The
original source of the phrase "mass without mass," coined by Wheeler to
advertise the goal of deriving mass as a secondary, emergent property
rather than postulating it as a primary irreducible property of matter
(Geometrodynamics, p. 25, cited in [@Wilczek1999MassWithoutMassI
ref. 1]). Wheeler's framing precedes the QCD-based realisation by
Wilczek 1999 [@Wilczek1999MassWithoutMassI] and connects to the broader
Wheeler programme of geometric reduction of physical concepts, in the
same spirit as the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's reduction of mass
to perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate. Cited as historical reference in
Corollary [248](#cor:WilczekMassWithoutMass){reference-type="ref"
reference="cor:WilczekMassWithoutMass"} and
Remark [249](#rem:UnifiedMassReading){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:UnifiedMassReading"}.

Strassler, M. (2024). *Waves in an Impossible Sea: How Everyday Life
Emerges from the Cosmic Ocean*. Basic Books (Hachette Book Group), New
York. 370 pp. ISBN 9781541603295.
<https://www.hachettebookgroup.com/titles/matt-strassler/waves-in-an-impossible-sea/9781541603295/>.
The 2024 popular-literature articulation of the post-Higgs-discovery
mass problem, named Big Think's Best Science Book of 2024
[@Siegel2024WavesReview]. Strassler establishes for a general audience
the multi-mechanism picture of mass that Wilczek 1999/2000/2012
[@Wilczek1999MassWithoutMassI; @Wilczek2000MassWithoutMassII; @Wilczek2012OriginsOfMass]
had developed in the primary literature: (a) Higgs-Yukawa mass for
elementary fermions; (b) QCD-binding-energy mass for composite hadrons;
(c) the open neutrino-mass mechanism. Strassler's metaphor of the Higgs
field as a medium through which leptons and quarks propagate is the
contemporary popularisation of Wilczek 2000's "the Medium is the
Mass-age." Cited as contemporary popular-literature articulation in
Remark [249](#rem:UnifiedMassReading){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:UnifiedMassReading"} of the present paper.

Siegel, E. (2024). *Waves in an Impossible Sea: the 2024 science book of
the year*. Big Think / Starts With A Bang, December 17, 2024.
<https://bigthink.com/starts-with-a-bang/waves-in-an-impossible-sea-science-book-year/>.
The named-Best-Science-Book-of-2024 attribution for Strassler 2024
[@Strassler2024Waves], cited as the contemporary-reception evidence for
the popular-literature framing of the mass problem.

"Why the Higgs Boson Still Hasn't Solved the Mass Problem." YouTube,
2026. <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iK6wEpg5vVo>. A contemporary
popular-science video presentation of the Wilczek-Strassler picture of
mass, articulating: (a) Higgs-Yukawa mass for elementary fermions as
"free parameters" that the Standard Model accepts without explaining;
(b) the QCD-binding-energy contribution as $\sim 98\%$ of proton mass,
with the Higgs-Yukawa valence-quark contribution at $\lesssim 2\%$; (c)
the hierarchy problem ($m_H$ vs $M_{\rm Pl}$, $10^{32}$ fine-tuning
requirement); (d) neutrino mass as new physics beyond the Standard
Model. Cited as a contemporary general-audience articulation of the
three-mass-mechanism picture, third in order after the
primary-literature sources
[@Wilczek1999MassWithoutMassI; @Wilczek2000MassWithoutMassII; @Wilczek2012OriginsOfMass]
and the contemporary book-length popularisation [@Strassler2024Waves].

Yang, Y.-B., Liang, J., Bi, Y.-J., Chen, Y., Draper, T., Liu, K.-F.,
Liu, Z. (2018). *Proton Mass Decomposition from the QCD Energy Momentum
Tensor*. Physical Review Letters **121**, 212001. DOI:
[10.1103/PhysRevLett.121.212001](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.121.212001).
arXiv:[1808.08677](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.08677). Modern lattice-QCD
decomposition of the proton mass into quark-condensate ($\sim 9\%$),
quark-energy ($\sim 32\%$), gluon-field-energy ($\sim 36\%$), and
trace-anomaly ($\sim 23\%$) contributions; the modern primary source for
the numerical breakdown cited in
Corollary [248](#cor:WilczekMassWithoutMass){reference-type="ref"
reference="cor:WilczekMassWithoutMass"} of the present paper.

Lorcé, C. (2018). *On the hadron mass decomposition*. European Physical
Journal C **78**, 120. DOI:
[10.1140/epjc/s10052-018-5561-2](https://doi.org/10.1140/epjc/s10052-018-5561-2).
arXiv:[1706.05853](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.05853). The treatment of
the multiple inequivalent proton-mass-decomposition schemes (Ji
decomposition, trace-decomposition, kinetic-energy-decomposition),
establishing that the qualitative pattern "valence-quark Higgs-mass
contribution is small; gluon-field-energy and quark-kinetic
contributions dominate" is robust across schemes although the exact
numerical percentages depend on the scheme chosen. Cited in
Corollary [248](#cor:WilczekMassWithoutMass){reference-type="ref"
reference="cor:WilczekMassWithoutMass"} of the present paper alongside
[@Yang2018ProtonMassDecomposition] for the lattice-QCD numerical
decomposition.

Wick, G. C. (1954). *Properties of Bethe-Salpeter Wave Functions*.
Physical Review **96**(4), 1124--1134 (November 15, 1954). DOI:
[10.1103/PhysRev.96.1124](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.96.1124). The
original paper introducing what came to be called the "Wick rotation,"
establishing that the four-dimensional wave function of a Bethe-Salpeter
two-body bound state can be continued analytically to complex values of
the relative time variable, with the wave equation in this
analytically-continued form obtained by rotation of the integration path
in the complex plane of the relative-energy variable. The abstract
explicitly invokes the canonical identification "real values of
$x_4 = ict$" --- the same identity used as the integral
first-consequence of $dx_4/dt = ic$ throughout the present paper. Cited
in
Section [\[ssec:WickConundrum\]](#ssec:WickConundrum){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:WickConundrum"} as the original technical source for the
Wick-rotation operation whose orthodox-formalism breakdown Woit
[@Woit2024Unification] identifies and which the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework resolves at the physical-principle level via
Theorem [1](#thm:McGuckenWickResolution){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:McGuckenWickResolution"}.

Wightman, A. S. (1956). *Quantum Field Theory in Terms of Vacuum
Expectation Values*. Physical Review **101**(2), 860--866 (January 15,
1956). DOI:
[10.1103/PhysRev.101.860](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.101.860). The
foundational paper establishing the Wightman-function formulation of
quantum field theory: vacuum expectation values of products of neutral
scalar field operators are characterised by their properties under
Lorentz invariance, the absence of negative energy states, and the
positive definiteness of the scalar product, and are shown to be
boundary values of analytic functions. Local commutativity is
established as a symmetry property of the analytic functions. Together
with the Osterwalder--Schrader axiomatisation [@OsterwalderSchrader1973]
of the Euclidean dual framework, Wightman's formulation establishes the
two-formalism structure that Woit [@Woit2024Unification] identifies as
the technical site of the broken-analytic-continuation conundrum. Cited
in
Section [\[ssec:WickConundrum\]](#ssec:WickConundrum){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:WickConundrum"} as the primary source for the Lorentzian
operator/Wightman-function formalism whose analytic-continuation
relationship to the Euclidean path-integral formalism is the subject of
Theorem [1](#thm:McGuckenWickResolution){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:McGuckenWickResolution"}.

Kontsevich, M., & Segal, G. (2021). *Wick Rotation and the Positivity of
Energy in Quantum Field Theory*. Quarterly Journal of Mathematics
**72**(1-2), 673--699 (June 2021). DOI:
[10.1093/qmath/haab027](https://doi.org/10.1093/qmath/haab027).
arXiv:[2105.10161](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.10161) \[hep-th\]. The
contemporary axiomatic treatment of the Wick rotation for unitary
quantum field theories on curved spacetime backgrounds, proposing a new
axiom system in which the partition function and correlators extend
analytically to a certain domain of complex-valued metrics. Ordinary
Riemannian metrics are contained in the allowable domain, while
Lorentzian metrics lie on its boundary. The Kontsevich--Segal admissible
domain of complex metrics is identified in [@MG-Connes Theorem C] as the
algebraic image of the real geometric McGucken-Wick rotation family
$\theta \in [0, \pi/2]$ on $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}$, supplying
physical grounding for the otherwise purely-axiomatic mathematical
structure. Cited in
Section [\[ssec:WickConundrum\]](#ssec:WickConundrum){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:WickConundrum"},
Theorem [1](#thm:McGuckenWickResolution){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:McGuckenWickResolution"} Property (i).

Woit, P. (2024). *Rethinking the Foundations of Physics: Unification*.
Talk delivered August 15, 2024, Columbia University Mathematics
Department; slides at
<https://www.math.columbia.edu/~woit/unification.pdf>. Podcast
presentation released September 2024 on *Theories of Everything with
