Curt Jaimungal*: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TTSeqsCgxj8>. Woit's
contemporary articulation of (i) the unanswered questions left open by
the Standard Model and General Relativity --- why
$U(1) \times \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathrm{SU}(3)$, why three
generations, why the specific charge pattern, why the Higgs potential
shape, why the Yukawa pattern; (ii) the half-century failure of the
orthodox unification paradigm (GUTs falsified by proton-decay
non-observation; SUSY falsified by superpartner non-observation at LHC;
extra-dimensions falsified by null Kaluza--Klein results; string theory
failing to deliver after 40 years); (iii) the technical conundrum of the
broken Wick rotation: "There is no such thing as any kind of full theory
formalism which depends upon complex time analytically and allows you to
analytically continue between time and imaginary time. There just is no
such thing." Woit's own positive proposal is a
mathematical-reorganisation of orthodox quantum field theory via
Osterwalder--Schrader reconstruction starting from Euclidean signature,
with the imaginary-time direction introduced as external mathematical
data; the proposal does not derive quantum mechanics, general
relativity, thermodynamics, the second law, time's arrows, nonlocality,
or any other physics from a physical-geometric law. *The McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's relationship to Woit's articulation is
asymmetric and central: Woit identifies the technical site of the
conundrum (within orthodox QFT) and proposes a mathematical-cleanup; the
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework supplies the physical-principle
resolution by identifying the imaginary-time direction with the physical
$x_4$-direction expanding at $+ic$ at every event of
$\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}$ [@MGWick Theorem 22.1, Theorem 21.6bis.1,
Theorem 21.7.12.1], [@MG-Connes Theorem C].* Cited as the contemporary
sharply-named external interlocutor in
Section [\[ssec:WickConundrum\]](#ssec:WickConundrum){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:WickConundrum"},
Theorem [1](#thm:McGuckenWickResolution){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:McGuckenWickResolution"}, and
Remarks [2](#rem:WoitMcGuckenAsymmetry){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:WoitMcGuckenAsymmetry"}
and [3](#rem:TwelveIsAndWick){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:TwelveIsAndWick"} of the present paper.

Coleman, S. & Mandula, J. (1967). *All Possible Symmetries of the S
Matrix*. Physical Review **159**(5), 1251--1256 (July 25, 1967). DOI:
[10.1103/PhysRev.159.1251](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.159.1251).
Received 16 March 1967; Lyman Laboratory of Physics, Harvard University,
Cambridge, Massachusetts. The no-go theorem of orthodox quantum field
theory establishing "the impossibility of combining space-time and
internal symmetries in any but a trivial way" --- specifically, that the
only Lie group symmetries possible in a relativistic theory of
interacting particles with a mass gap are direct products of the
Poincaré group and an internal symmetry group. The theorem rests on five
technical conditions: (1) $G$ contains a subgroup locally isomorphic to
the Poincaré group, (2) for any $M > 0$, only finitely many one-particle
states with mass less than $M$, (3) elastic scattering amplitudes
analytic in $s$ and $t$ in some neighbourhood of the physical region,
(4) non-trivial $S$-matrix, (5) generators of $G$ representable as
integral operators. Cited in
Theorem [8](#thm:ColemanMandulaAsPerpendicularity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:ColemanMandulaAsPerpendicularity"} of the present paper
as the orthodox-formalism statement of the internal/external symmetry
commutativity that the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework reads as the
geometric disjointness of $x_4$-perpendicular and three-space-parallel
substrate features.

Atiyah, M. (2000). *The Millennium Problems II: Poincaré Conjecture,
Hodge Conjecture, Yang--Mills Theory, Navier--Stokes Equations*. Lecture
delivered at the Millennium Meeting of the Clay Mathematics Institute,
May 24, 2000, amphithéatre Marguerite de Navarre, Collège de France,
Paris. Companion to John Tate's preceding lecture on
Birch--Swinnerton-Dyer, the Hodge Conjecture (joint coverage), P versus
NP, and the Riemann Hypothesis. Video recording:
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=trxjCOmg8GY>. The official launch
lecture for the Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Problems, in which
Atiyah --- one of the seven-member scientific advisory committee that
selected the problems (with Wiles, Tate, Witten, Connes, Yau, Faltings)
--- presented four of the seven problems with primary-source
identification of indicated research directions: (i)
physics-of-gravitation as the route for Poincaré/Thurston; (ii) bridging
algebraic and transcendental methods as the content of Hodge, with
Hodge's machinery (exterior derivative, adjoint, Laplace operator on a
curved background) explicitly identified as "motivated by Maxwell's
equations and the \[elastic\] equations... the fundamental equations of
mathematical physics put in the geometrical context"; (iii)
duality-of-formal-structures as a route for Yang--Mills ("a problem that
can be described in two different ways by duality --- the two dual
pictures might look quite different, one of them might be tractable and
the other one might be intractable"); (iv) vortex topology as the route
for Navier--Stokes ("the topology of vortices may explain a possible
blow up... treating a differential equation purely as a piece of
analysis or algebra can ignore some fundamental reality of those
equations which may be topological"). Cited in
Sections [16.11](#ssec:Atiyah2000YangMillsRoute){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:Atiyah2000YangMillsRoute"},
[18](#sec:HodgeMillennium){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:HodgeMillennium"} (sub-sections
[18.1](#ssec:DeligneStatementFull){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:DeligneStatementFull"},
[18.2](#ssec:HodgeSingleComplexStructure){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:HodgeSingleComplexStructure"},
[18.3](#ssec:HodgeChernClasses){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:HodgeChernClasses"}), and
Section [\[ssec:McWickRotationSuppliesChaos\]](#ssec:McWickRotationSuppliesChaos){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:McWickRotationSuppliesChaos"} of the present paper as
primary-source identification of the Yang--Mills
duality-of-formal-structures route, the Hodge algebraic/transcendental
bridge framing with the Maxwell-equations-to-Hodge-machinery historical
content, and the Navier--Stokes vortex-topology route.

Clay Mathematics Institute. *The Hodge Conjecture (Millennium Problem)*.
<https://www.claymath.org/millennium/hodge-conjecture/>. The official
Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Problem statement page for the
Hodge Conjecture, the second of the seven problems announced at the May
24, 2000 Millennium Meeting at the Collège de France. The page
articulates the problem in the form: "In the twentieth century
mathematicians discovered powerful ways to investigate the shapes of
complicated objects. The basic idea is to ask to what extent we can
approximate the shape of a given object by gluing together simple
geometric building blocks of increasing dimension... Unfortunately, the
geometric origins of the procedure became obscured in this
generalization. In some sense it was necessary to add pieces that did
not have any geometric interpretation. The Hodge conjecture asserts that
for particularly nice types of spaces called projective algebraic
varieties, the pieces called Hodge cycles are actually (rational linear)
combinations of geometric pieces called algebraic cycles." The page
identifies the conjecture as known in dimension less than four and open
in higher dimensions. Cited in
Section [18](#sec:HodgeMillennium){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:HodgeMillennium"} of the present paper.

Deligne, P. (2000). *The Hodge Conjecture*. Official Clay Mathematics
Institute Millennium Problem description. In *The Millennium Prize
Problems*, J. A. Carlson, A. Jaffe, and A. Wiles, eds., Clay Mathematics
Institute / American Mathematical Society, 2006. PDF:
<https://www.claymath.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/hodge.pdf>. The
official problem statement and survey for the Hodge Conjecture, prepared
by Pierre Deligne (Fields Medal 1978, Abel Prize 2013), articulating the
precise mathematical statement: for $X$ a non-singular complex
projective variety, every Hodge class on $X$ (a class in
$H^{2p}(X, \mathbb{Q}) \cap H^{p,p}(X)$ under the Hodge decomposition
$H^{2p}(X, \mathbb{C}) = \bigoplus_{a+b=2p} H^{a,b}(X)$) is a rational
linear combination of cohomology classes of algebraic subvarieties of
complex codimension $p$. The integral version is established as false
(Atiyah--Hirzebruch 1962 counterexamples); the rational version stated
above is the Millennium-Prize-eligible statement. Deligne's exposition
includes Grothendieck's motivic framework and the parallel conjectures
from $\ell$-adic and de Rham cohomology theories. Cited in
Section [18](#sec:HodgeMillennium){reference-type="ref"
reference="sec:HodgeMillennium"} of the present paper as the official
primary-source statement of the Hodge Conjecture, against which the
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's pattern relationship is established.

Weyl, H. (1949). *Philosophy of Mathematics and Natural Science*.
Princeton University Press, Princeton, NJ. 311 pages. Reissued by
Princeton University Press, 2009 (with new foreword by Frank Wilczek).
The verbatim source of the Tile Argument against discrete physical space
(p. 43): "If a square is built up of miniature tiles, then there are as
many tiles along the diagonal as there are along the side; thus the
diagonal should be equal in length to the side." Weyl's argument asserts
that a discrete spatial lattice cannot reproduce the Pythagorean theorem
$a^2 + b^2 = c^2$ on a square, and cannot reproduce the isotropy of
three-space, because a measuring rod or moving particle would change
physical length depending on its angle relative to the underlying grid.
The argument has been the no-go obstacle against discrete-spacetime
physical models for over seventy years. Cited in
Section [\[ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis\]](#ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis"} and
Theorem [13](#thm:WeylTileEvaded){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:WeylTileEvaded"} of the present paper as the no-go
obstacle against discrete-spacetime models, with the evasion of Weyl's
argument established at theorem grade via the framework's placement of
discreteness on $x_4$ (a Lorentz-scalar axis) and on the McGucken Sphere
($\mathrm{SO}(3)$-Haar-symmetric 2-surface), with three-space
continuous.

Nielsen, H. B., & Ninomiya, M. (1981). *Absence of Neutrinos on a
Lattice: (I). Proof by Homotopy Theory*. Nuclear Physics B **185**(1),
20--40 (13 July 1981). DOI:
[10.1016/0550-3213(81)90361-8](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(81)90361-8).
Erratum: Nuclear Physics B **195**, 541 (1982). The first proof of the
Nielsen--Ninomiya theorem via homotopy theory, establishing that any
interacting fermion theory on a Kogut--Susskind lattice satisfying (a)
hermiticity, (b) locality, (c) regular lattice with translational
invariance and Lorentz-recovered continuum limit, (d) bilinear action of
the form $\bar\psi M \psi$, and (e) locally conserved quantized charge,
must have an equal number of species (types) of left- and right-handed
Weyl particles (neutrinos) in the continuum limit (fermion doubling).
The principal consequence: it is not possible, in strong interaction
models, to solve the species doubling problem of Dirac fermions on a
lattice in a chirally invariant way; equivalently, no lattice
formulation of the weak interaction (which is intrinsically chiral) is
possible under the five technical conditions. Cited in
Section [\[ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis\]](#ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis"} and
Theorem [14](#thm:NielsenNinomiyaEvaded){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:NielsenNinomiyaEvaded"} of the present paper as the no-go
obstacle against discrete formulations of chiral gauge theory, with the
evasion established at theorem grade via the framework's placement of
chiral fermions in continuous Lorentzian spacetime (Channel A content),
with the discreteness orthogonal to chirality (on $x_4$-stepping and
Sphere mode count, not on a 3-space lattice).

Nielsen, H. B., & Ninomiya, M. (1981). *Absence of Neutrinos on a
Lattice: (II). Intuitive Topological Proof*. Nuclear Physics B
**193**(1), 173--194. DOI:
[10.1016/0550-3213(81)90524-1](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(81)90524-1).
The second proof of the Nielsen--Ninomiya theorem via intuitive
topological methods, complementing the homotopy-theory proof of
[@NielsenNinomiya1981I]. Companion paper to the first proof, providing
geometric and physical intuition for the reasons why chiral fermions
must double on a regular lattice. Cited together with
[@NielsenNinomiya1981I] in
Section [\[ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis\]](#ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis"} and
Theorem [14](#thm:NielsenNinomiyaEvaded){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:NielsenNinomiyaEvaded"} of the present paper.

Bekenstein, J. D. (1973). *Black Holes and Entropy*. Physical Review D
**7**(8), 2333--2346 (15 April 1973). DOI:
[10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2333](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2333).
Joseph Henry Laboratories, Princeton University; based on the author's
Ph.D. thesis (Princeton University, 1972). The foundational paper
establishing black-hole entropy as a thermodynamic quantity proportional
to the horizon area: "Considerations of simplicity and consistency, and
dimensional arguments indicate that the black-hole entropy is equal to
the ratio of the black-hole area to the square of the Planck length
times a dimensionless constant of order unity." The dimensionless
constant was subsequently fixed to $1/4$ by Hawking's calculation of
horizon temperature [@Hawking1975Particle], yielding the
Bekenstein--Hawking entropy $S_{\rm BH} = k_B A/(4\ell_P^2)$. The
Generalized Second Law (entropy outside black hole plus black-hole
entropy never decreases) is established as the physics of the area law.
Cited in
Section [\[ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis\]](#ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis"} of the present paper as
primary-source establishment of Lorentz-invariant discreteness in
horizon entropy.

Hawking, S. W. (1975). *Particle Creation by Black Holes*.
Communications in Mathematical Physics **43**(3), 199--220 (August
1975). DOI: [10.1007/BF02345020](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02345020).
Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics, University of
Cambridge. The foundational paper establishing black-hole thermal
radiation at the Hawking temperature $T_H = \hbar \kappa/(2\pi c k_B)$,
with $\kappa$ the surface gravity. The derivation fixes the
dimensionless constant in the Bekenstein 1973
[@Bekenstein1973BlackHoleEntropy] area-law conjecture to $1/4$,
completing the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy formula
$S_{\rm BH} = k_B A/(4\ell_P^2)$. Hawking's analysis derives the thermal
emission from quantum-field-theory effects in curved spacetime around a
collapsing star; the resulting Generalized Second Law states
$S + (1/4)A$ never decreases, with $S$ the entropy of matter outside
black holes and $A$ the sum of the surface areas of event horizons.
Cited in
Section [\[ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis\]](#ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis"} of the present paper.

't Hooft, G. (1993). *Dimensional Reduction in Quantum Gravity*. In
*Salam Festschrift: A Collection of Talks*, World Scientific Series in
20th Century Physics, vol. 4, eds. A. Ali, J. Ellis, S. Randjbar-Daemi,
World Scientific, Singapore.
arXiv:[gr-qc/9310026](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9310026) \[gr-qc\].
Preprint THU-93/26 (19 October 1993). Essay dedicated to Abdus Salam.
The foundational paper proposing the holographic principle: "The
requirement that physical phenomena associated with gravitational
collapse should be duly reconciled with the postulates of quantum
mechanics implies that at a Planckian scale our world is not 3+1
dimensional. Rather, the observable degrees of freedom can best be
described as if they were Boolean variables defined on a two-dimensional
lattice, evolving with time." This observation, deduced from unitarity,
entropy, and counting arguments, implies severe restrictions on possible
models of quantum gravity. Cited in
Section [\[ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis\]](#ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis"} of the present paper as
primary-source identification of the area-law mode count carrying
Lorentz-invariant discreteness.

Susskind, L. (1995). *The World as a Hologram*. Journal of Mathematical
Physics **36**(11), 6377--6396 (November 1995). DOI:
[10.1063/1.531249](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.531249).
arXiv:[hep-th/9409089](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9409089) \[hep-th\].
The contemporary formulation of the holographic principle as a
constraint on quantum gravity: the number of degrees of freedom in a
region of space scales with the area of the boundary rather than the
volume, with the boundary degrees of freedom counted at Planck-area
resolution. Together with 't Hooft 1993 [@tHooft1993Dimensional], the
source of the modern holographic-principle literature. Cited in
Section [\[ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis\]](#ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis"} of the present paper.

Gibbons, G. W., & Hawking, S. W. (1977). *Action Integrals and Partition
Functions in Quantum Gravity*. Physical Review D **15**(10), 2752--2756
(15 May 1977). DOI:
[10.1103/PhysRevD.15.2752](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.15.2752).
Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics, University of
Cambridge. The foundational paper establishing the
Euclidean-partition-function formulation of black-hole thermodynamics:
"One can evaluate the action for a gravitational field on a section of
the complexified spacetime which avoids the singularities. In this
manner we obtain finite, purely imaginary values for the actions of the
Kerr-Newman solutions and de Sitter space." The Euclidean saddle-point
evaluation of the gravitational partition function recovers the
Bekenstein--Hawking entropy $S_{\rm BH} = A/(4\ell_P^2)$ for black holes
and de Sitter space, establishing the Wick-rotated cigar (Euclidean
Schwarzschild) as the canonical saddle-point geometry for horizon
thermodynamics. Cited in
Section [\[ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis\]](#ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis"} of the present paper as the
empirical anchor for the discrete Euclidean reading of the five-readings
table.

Bousso, R. (2002). *The Holographic Principle*. Reviews of Modern
Physics **74**(3), 825--874 (August 2002). DOI:
[10.1103/RevModPhys.74.825](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.74.825).
arXiv:[hep-th/0203101](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0203101) \[hep-th\].
The comprehensive review of the holographic principle in the orthodox
literature, covering the historical development from Bekenstein--Hawking
entropy through 't Hooft 1993 and Susskind 1995 to the covariant entropy
bound and AdS/CFT applications. Establishes the holographic principle as
a substrate-emergence postulate within the orthodox tradition. Cited in
Section [\[ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis\]](#ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:ResolutionContentDiagnosis"} and
Remark [15](#rem:OrthodoxCarriesDiscretenessUnrecognised){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:OrthodoxCarriesDiscretenessUnrecognised"} of the present
paper as the orthodox-tradition treatment of the area-law discreteness
that the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework supplies the reading of.

Tong, D., & Carroll, S. M. (2025). *Mindscape 321: David Tong on Open
Questions in Quantum Field Theory*. Mindscape Podcast hosted by Sean M.
Carroll (Homewood Professor of Natural Philosophy, Johns Hopkins
University; Fractal Faculty, Santa Fe Institute), with guest David Tong
(Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics, University
of Cambridge). Released 14 July 2025. Blog post with show notes and full
transcript: <https://www.preposterousuniverse.com/podcast/2025/07/14/>.
Video: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RhiYYk784w>. A 76-minute
interview engaging open questions in quantum field theory at the level
of contemporary research. Central primary-source for the present paper:
(i) gauge symmetry as fundamentally redundancy in our description of the
laws of physics (35:28--37:54): "All the laws of physics that we
currently have, Maxwell's theory of electromagnetism, Einstein's theory
of general relativity, quantum mechanics, quantum field theory, every
single one of them is built on objects that we could not measure even in
principle... It's a redundancy in our description of the laws of
physics. I don't really understand why the laws of physics are like
this." (ii) locality and unitarity as mutually-incompatible features
visible only one-at-a-time through gauge redundancy (37:54--39:30):
"There are these two crucial features of the laws of physics, and you
can see one of them or you can see the other one, but somehow it's very
hard to see both at the same time. And it's this redundancy that allows
you to see both. So it's a very deep principle. It's what all of our
laws of physics are based on. I think we don't really understand why
it's the case. I've never heard anybody say, oh, it's got to be like
this for some reason." (iii) monopoles versus gauge symmetry as "almost
mutually exclusive" with Dirac's quantisation condition as the
orthodox-tradition "loophole" (1:12:34--1:13:00). (iv) Nielsen--Ninomiya
theorem as Tong's three-to-four-year research obsession on how to evade
the no-go (50:30--54:05): "I don't believe the conclusion of the
mathematical theorem is right. I think there must be a way to evade it.
Nice thing about theorems is they come with certain assumptions." Cited
in
Section [\[ssec:TongLocalityUnitarity\]](#ssec:TongLocalityUnitarity){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:TongLocalityUnitarity"} of the present paper as the
contemporary-orthodox-QFT primary-source observation of the dual-channel
architecture and the two-source RHS of $dx_4/dt = ic$, with the
McGucken-framework reading of Tong's articulation established at theorem
grade in
Theorem [17](#thm:LocalityUnitarityTwoSource){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:LocalityUnitarityTwoSource"}. Also cites the
comment-thread observation by Nathan Argaman (13 August 2025) that
"unitarity and causality... do not hold in all gauges" with reference to
[@WhartonArgaman2020] for the future-input-dependent modeling of
entanglement; this gauge-projection-dependent observation is engaged in
Remark [20](#rem:ArgamanGaugeDependent){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:ArgamanGaugeDependent"}.

Wharton, K. B., & Argaman, N. (2020). *Colloquium: Bell's Theorem and
Locally Mediated Reformulations of Quantum Mechanics*. Reviews of Modern
Physics **92**(2), 021002 (published 18 May 2020). DOI:
[10.1103/RevModPhys.92.021002](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.92.021002).
arXiv:[1906.04313](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.04313) \[quant-ph\].
K. B. Wharton (Department of Physics and Astronomy, San José State
University); N. Argaman (Department of Physics, Nuclear Research
Center---Negev, Israel). Abstract verbatim: "Bell's theorem rules out
many potential reformulations of quantum mechanics, but within a
generalized framework it does not exclude all locally mediated models.
Such models describe the correlations between entangled particles as
mediated by intermediate parameters that track the particle worldlines
and respect Lorentz covariance. These locally mediated models require
the relaxation of an arrow-of-time assumption that is typically taken
for granted. Specifically, some of the mediating parameters in these
models must functionally depend on measurement settings in their future,
i.e., on input parameters associated with later times. This option,
often called retrocausal, has been repeatedly pointed out in the
literature, but the exploration of explicit locally mediated toy models
capable of describing specific entanglement phenomena has begun only in
the past decade." Cited in
Remark [20](#rem:ArgamanGaugeDependent){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:ArgamanGaugeDependent"} of the present paper as the
primary-source reference for the gauge-formulation-dependence of
unitarity and causality observation that the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework supplies the reading of: the gauge-dependence of unitarity and
causality is the orthodox formalism's correct registration that locality
and unitarity are two projections of the same two-source RHS of
$dx_4/dt = ic$.

Tong, D. (2024). *On Quarks and Turbulence*. Public Lecture,
International Centre for Theoretical Sciences (ICTS) of the Tata
Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR), Bengaluru, India. Video URL:
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E0xKaLRgcUY>. Delivered during the ICTS
programme on quarks and turbulence. David Tong is Professor of
Theoretical Physics at the Department of Applied Mathematics and
Theoretical Physics, University of Cambridge, UK. The lecture presents
the connection between quark confinement (QCD) and three-dimensional
turbulence (Navier-Stokes) as a unifying theme, with the
Migdal-Iyer-Sreenivasan turbulent-circulation area-law as the candidate
empirical signature. Central primary-source for the present paper: (a)
at lecture timestamp 37:00--39:39, Tong identifies the analytic
derivation of the linear confining potential from first principles as
one of the major unsolved problems of contemporary theoretical physics:
"it's been 50 years of people trying people trying and making
progress... nothing definitive that we can say... it's an open problem
it's one of the major unsolved problems in theoretical physics"; (b) at
54:50--59:14, Tong presents the connection between Wilson's QCD area law
and the Migdal-Iyer-Sreenivasan turbulent-circulation area law,
attributing the original proposal to A. A. Migdal (present in the
audience) and the empirical confirmation to K. P. Iyer,
K. R. Sreenivasan, and P. K. Yeung: "the new thing that happened only in
the last few years is that there's suggestions that there's something
very similar in turbulence... the suggestion was made by professor
migdal... Sasha migdal was inspired by the ideas from quarks and qcd to
propose that this area law might also hold in fluid mechanics so as I
said it's speculative... honestly I don't know if this is a great
breakthrough or if it'll just be a a dead end." Cited in
§[\[ssec:TongQuarksTurbulence\]](#ssec:TongQuarksTurbulence){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:TongQuarksTurbulence"} and
Theorem [401](#thm:AreaLawCommonStructure){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:AreaLawCommonStructure"} of the present paper as the
contemporary-orthodox-physics primary-source articulation of the QCD/NS
unification that the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework supplies as a
theorem via the McWick rotation.

Wilson, K. G. (1974). *Confinement of Quarks*. Physical Review D
**10**(8), 2445--2459 (15 October 1974). DOI:
[10.1103/PhysRevD.10.2445](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.10.2445).
Laboratory of Nuclear Studies, Cornell University, Ithaca, New York.
Received 12 June 1974. The foundational paper establishing the lattice
formulation of gauge field theories and the area-law criterion for quark
confinement. Abstract verbatim: "A mechanism for total confinement of
quarks, similar to that of Schwinger, is defined which requires the
existence of Abelian or non-Abelian gauge fields. It is shown how to
quantize a gauge field theory on a discrete lattice in Euclidean
space-time, preserving exact gauge invariance and treating the gauge
fields as angular variables (which makes a gauge-fixing term
unnecessary). The lattice gauge theory has a computable strong-coupling
limit; in this limit the binding mechanism applies and there are no free
quarks. There is unfortunately no Lorentz (or Euclidean) invariance in
the strong-coupling limit. The strong-coupling expansion involves sums
over all quark paths and sums over all surfaces (on the lattice) joining
quark paths." The area-law criterion:
$\langle W(C)\rangle \sim e^{-K A_{\min}(C)}$ for large loops $C$ in the
strong-coupling limit, yielding linear confining potential $E(R) = K R$
between static quarks separated by distance $R$, with $K$ the string
tension. Cited in
Theorem [401](#thm:AreaLawCommonStructure){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:AreaLawCommonStructure"} of the present paper as the
primary-source for the QCD-tier area law in the proposed unification
with Migdal's turbulent-circulation area law.

Migdal, A. A. (1993). *Loop Equation in Turbulence*.
arXiv:[hep-th/9303130](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9303130), Princeton
University preprint PUPT-1383 (March 1993). The original loop-equation
paper for incompressible fluid dynamics. The verbatim primary-source
statement of the difference between the QCD area-law mechanism and the
proposed turbulent area-law mechanism (§5): "The Wilson loop in QCD
decreases as exponential of the minimal area, encircled by the loop,
leading to the quark confinement. What is the similar asymptotic law in
turbulence? *The physical mechanisms leading to the area law in QCD are
absent here.* Moreover, there is no guarantee, that $\Psi[C]$ always
decreases with the size of the loop." Migdal's turbulent area-law ansatz
is constructed via the assumption that the loop functional depends on
the tensor area $\Sigma_{\mu\nu}^C = \oint_C r_\mu dr_\nu$, combined
with Kolmogorov scaling and isotropy, yielding
$\Psi[C] \propto \exp(-B(\varepsilon/\nu^3)(\Sigma^C_{\alpha\beta})^2)^{1/3})$
with $B$ a universal positive constant. Cited in
Theorem [401](#thm:AreaLawCommonStructure){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:AreaLawCommonStructure"} of the present paper as the
primary-source for Migdal's own caveat that the physical mechanisms
producing the QCD area law are explicitly stated to be absent in his
turbulence treatment.

Migdal, A. A. (1994). *Loop Equation and Area Law in Turbulence*.
International Journal of Modern Physics A **9**(8), 1197--1238 (1994).
DOI:
[10.1142/S0217751X94000558](https://doi.org/10.1142/S0217751X94000558).
arXiv:[hep-th/9310088](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9310088), Princeton
University preprint PUPT-1426. Extended version based on lectures at the
Cargèse Summer School and Chernogolovka Summer School in 1993. Abstract
verbatim: "The incompressible fluid dynamics is reformulated as dynamics
of closed loops $C$ in coordinate space. We derive explicit functional
equation for the pdf of the circulation $P_C(\Gamma)$ which allows the
scaling solutions in the inertial range of spatial scales. The pdf
decays as exponential of some power of $\Gamma^3/A^2$, where A is the
minimal area inside the loop." The journal paper establishing the
loop-equation formulation of Navier-Stokes turbulence and the area-law
conjecture for circulation PDF tails. Cited in
Theorem [401](#thm:AreaLawCommonStructure){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:AreaLawCommonStructure"} of the present paper as the
primary-source for the turbulent-circulation area-law functional form.

Migdal, A. A. (2019). *Universal Area Law in Turbulence*.
arXiv:[1903.08613](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.08613) \[hep-th\] (20
March 2019). Re-derivation of the area law in turbulence (originally
Migdal 1993-1994
[@Migdal1993LoopEquationTurbulence; @Migdal1994LoopEquation]) in a
simpler form, with explicit relation to vorticity correlations and
minimal-surface geometry. Abstract verbatim (portion on scope): "We
derive this law in a simpler way, at the same time outlining the limits
of its applicability... The scaling dimension of velocity circulation as
a function of large area remains unknown. Numerical experiments suggest
transition for log-log derivative of circulation moments
$\langle \Gamma^p\rangle$ by the loop area from Kolmogorov index
$\frac{2p}{3}$ at $p < 4$ down to approximately $0.58 p$ for
$4 \leq p \leq 10$ within available Reynolds numbers. We argue that Area
Law applies to these moments only in the limit $p \to \infty$ when they
are dominated by the tails of the PDF. So, these numerical experiments
suggest that the scaling index in Area law is less than $\frac{2}{3}$."
Cited in Theorem [401](#thm:AreaLawCommonStructure){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:AreaLawCommonStructure"} of the present paper.

Migdal, A. A. (2019). *Exact Area Law for Planar Loops in Turbulence in
Two and Three Dimensions*.
arXiv:[1904.05245](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.05245) \[hep-th\] (10
April 2019). Establishes that the area law holds *exactly* for 2D
turbulence and for arbitrary planar loops in higher dimensions, relying
on the scaling index $\alpha = 1/2$ derived in companion work. In 3D,
the Stokes condition $\partial_i \omega_i(r) = 0$ is exactly satisfied
for the minimal-surface solution via vanishing mean curvature of the
minimal surface. For general (non-planar) loops in 3D, a self-consistent
conformal metric on the minimal surface is required to compensate the
loop-equation terms while preserving the Stokes condition. Cited in
Theorem [401](#thm:AreaLawCommonStructure){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:AreaLawCommonStructure"} of the present paper as
primary-source for the vanishing-mean-curvature minimal-surface content.

Migdal, A. A. (2019). *Analytic and Numerical Study of Navier-Stokes
Loop Equation in Turbulence*.
arXiv:[1908.01422](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.01422) \[hep-th\] (4
August 2019). Develops the analytic approach to the non-planar loop
equation, deriving a quadratic integral equation for the vorticity
distribution $\Omega(r)$ on a minimal surface, with the minimal surface
defined by mean external curvature equal to zero for arbitrary
non-planar loops. The viscosity term in Navier-Stokes creates a boundary
condition for $\Omega(r \in C)$ on the loop. The leading viscosity
correction mixes the moments $\langle\Gamma^p\rangle$ with
$\langle\Gamma^{p-1}\rangle$, resembling the bi-fractal behaviour
observed by Iyer-Sreenivasan-Yeung 2019
[@IyerSreenivasanYeung2019Bifractal] and explicitly breaking
time-reversal symmetry. Includes a numerical Mathematica notebook for
triangulated minimal surfaces. Cited in
Theorem [401](#thm:AreaLawCommonStructure){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:AreaLawCommonStructure"} of the present paper as
primary-source for the vorticity-distribution-on-minimal-surface
content.

Iyer, K. P., Sreenivasan, K. R., & Yeung, P. K. (2019). *Circulation in
High Reynolds Number Isotropic Turbulence is a Bifractal*. Physical
Review X **9**(4), 041006 (October 2019). DOI:
[10.1103/PhysRevX.9.041006](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevX.9.041006).
arXiv:[1902.07326](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.07326)
\[physics.flu-dyn\]. The first DNS-empirical confirmation of Migdal's
proposal that circulation PDF depends on loop area rather than loop
shape. Abstract verbatim: "The turbulence problem at the level of
scaling exponents is hard in part because of the multifractal scaling of
small scales... We show that velocity circulation around closed loops is
such a quantity. By using a large databases of isotropic turbulence,
generated from numerical simulations of the Navier-Stokes equations over
a wide range of Reynolds numbers, we show that circulation exhibits a
bifractal behavior at the highest Reynolds number considered: space
filling for moments up to order $3$ and a mono-fractal with an
unchanging dimension of about $2.5$ for higher orders; this change in
character roughly at the third-order moment is reminiscent of a 'phase
transition'... We confirm that the circulation properties depend on only
the area of the loop, not its shape; and, for a figure-$8$ loop, the
relevant area is the scalar sum of the two segments of the loop." Cited
in Theorem [401](#thm:AreaLawCommonStructure){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:AreaLawCommonStructure"} of the present paper as
primary-source for the empirical area-rule content with bifractal
scaling.

Iyer, K. P., Bharadwaj, S. S., & Sreenivasan, K. R. (2021). *The Area
Rule for Circulation in Three-Dimensional Turbulence*. Proceedings of
the National Academy of Sciences USA **118**(43), e2114679118 (26
October 2021). DOI:
[10.1073/pnas.2114679118](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2114679118).
arXiv:[2007.06723](https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.06723)
\[physics.flu-dyn\]. Abstract verbatim: "An important idea underlying a
plausible dynamical theory of circulation in three-dimensional
turbulence is the so-called Area Rule, according to which the
probability density function (PDF) of the circulation around closed
loops depends only on the minimal area of the loop, not its shape. We
assess the robustness of the Area Rule, for both planar and non-planar
loops, using high-resolution data from Direct Numerical Simulations. For
planar loops, the circulation moments for rectangular shapes match those
for the square with only small differences, these differences being
larger when the aspect ratio is further from unity, and when the
moment-order increases. The differences do not exceed about $5\%$ for
any condition examined here. The aspect-ratio dependence observed for
the second-order moment are indistinguishable from results for the
Gaussian Random Field (GRF) with the same two-point correlation function
(for which the results are order-independent by construction). When
normalized by the SD of the PDF, the aspect ratio dependence is even
smaller $(< 2\%)$ but does not vanish unlike for the GRF. We obtain
circulation statistics around minimal area loops in three dimensions and
compare them to those of a planar loop circumscribing equivalent areas,
and we find that circulation statistics match in the two cases only when
normalized by an internal variable such as the SD. This work highlights
the hitherto unknown connection between minimal surfaces and
turbulence." Cited in
Theorem [401](#thm:AreaLawCommonStructure){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:AreaLawCommonStructure"} and
Remark [402](#rem:HithertoUnknown){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:HithertoUnknown"} of the present paper as primary-source
for the empirical area-rule scope with non-vanishing residual structure
and for the explicit "hitherto unknown connection between minimal
surfaces and turbulence" statement that the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$
framework supplies a candidate physical-mechanism source for.

Kibble, T. W. B. (1976). *Topology of Cosmic Domains and Strings*.
Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and General **9**(8), 1387--1398
(August 1976). DOI:
[10.1088/0305-4470/9/8/029](https://doi.org/10.1088/0305-4470/9/8/029).
The foundational paper establishing that the topological defects formed
in spontaneously broken gauge theories --- domain walls, cosmic strings,
and monopoles --- are determined by the homotopy groups of the manifold
of degenerate vacua. Abstract verbatim: "The possible domain structures
which can arise in the universe in a spontaneously broken gauge theory
are studied. It is shown that the formation of domain walls, strings or
monopoles depends on the homotopy groups of the manifold of degenerate
vacua. The subsequent evolution of these structures is investigated. It
is argued that while theories generating domain walls can probably be
eliminated (because of their unacceptable gravitational effects), a
cosmic network of strings may well have been formed and may have had
important cosmological effects." The Kibble mechanism for cosmological
defect formation is now standard physics. Cited in
Theorem [214](#thm:SevenHiggsPuzzlesCatalog){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SevenHiggsPuzzlesCatalog"} Puzzle P7 of the present paper
as primary-source for the orthodox-tradition position that topological
defects generically arise in spontaneous symmetry breaking, with the
framework's Theorem [228](#thm:NoDomainWall){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:NoDomainWall"} establishing that the Higgs sector is
exempt from this conclusion by virtue of the global uniformity of $+ic$.

Vilenkin, A. (1985). *Cosmic Strings and Domain Walls*. Physics Reports
**121**(5), 263--315 (May 1985). DOI:
[10.1016/0370-1573(85)90033-X](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-1573(85)90033-X).
The comprehensive review of topological defects in cosmology, building
on Kibble 1976 [@KibbleMechanism1976]. Abstract verbatim: "Phase
transitions in the early universe can give rise to microscopic
topological defects: vacuum domain walls, strings, walls bounded by
strings, and monopoles connected by strings. This article reviews the
formation, physical properties and the cosmological evolution of various
defects. A particular attention is paid to strings and their
cosmological consequences, including the string scenario of galaxy
formation and possible observational effects of strings." Cited in
Theorem [214](#thm:SevenHiggsPuzzlesCatalog){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:SevenHiggsPuzzlesCatalog"} Puzzle P7 of the present paper
as primary-source for the orthodox-tradition treatment of cosmological
topological defects, with the framework's prohibition
(Theorem [228](#thm:NoDomainWall){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:NoDomainWall"}) operating at a principle level rather
than at the homotopy-group level of the orthodox treatment.

Synge, J. L. (1960). *Relativity: The General Theory*. By J. L. Synge,
School of Theoretical Physics, Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies.
North-Holland Publishing Company, Amsterdam; sole distributors for
U.S.A.: Interscience Publishers Inc., New York. Printed in the
Netherlands. 1960. Primary-source text verified at the Internet Archive
scan
<https://archive.org/details/john-synge-relativity-general-theory-1960>
(full OCR-extracted text of the 1960 first edition; signed off Dublin,
1960, by J. L. S.). Cited in
§[5.14](#ssec:EquivalencePrincipleUnification){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:EquivalencePrincipleUnification"} and
Theorem [236](#thm:EquivalencePrinciple){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:EquivalencePrinciple"} of the present paper for Synge's
verbatim Preface (pp. IX--X) statement of the open-problem status of the
equivalence principle as postulate of general relativity. Verbatim from
the Preface (read in full at primary source): "When, in a relativistic
discussion, I try to make things clearer by a space-time diagram, the
other participants look at it with polite detachment and, after a pause
of embarrassment as if some childish indecency had been exhibited,
resume the debate in their own terms. Perhaps they speak of the
Principle of Equivalence. If so, it is my turn to have a blank mind, for
I have never been able to understand this Principle. Does it mean that
the signature of the space-time metric is +2 (or --2 if you prefer the
other convention)? If so, it is important, but hardly a Principle. Does
it mean that the effects of a gravitational field are indistinguishable
from the effects of an observer's acceleration? If so, it is false. In
Einstein's theory, either there is a gravitational field or there is
none, according as the Riemann tensor does not or does vanish. This is
an absolute property; it has nothing to do with any observer's
world-line. Space-time is either flat or curved, and in several places
in the book I have been at considerable pains to separate truly
gravitational effects due to curvature of space-time from those due to
curvature of the observer's world-line (in most ordinary cases the
latter predominate). The Principle of Equivalence performed the
essential office of midwife at the birth of general relativity, but, as
Einstein remarked, the infant would never have got beyond its
long-clothes had it not been for Minkowski's concept. I suggest that the
midwife be now buried with appropriate honours and the facts of absolute
space-time faced." Synge's identification: the equivalence principle in
its post-1916 orthodox formulation is a postulate that has never been
derived from a deeper principle; Synge's proposal to "bury the midwife"
reflects the orthodox-tradition recognition that the equivalence
principle, while empirically extraordinarily well-confirmed, is a
postulate rather than a theorem in the orthodox framework. Synge's
two-pronged disjunctive question ("Does it mean X? If so, it is
important but hardly a Principle. Does it mean Y? If so, it is false.")
sharpens the open-problem articulation: the orthodox formulation either
reduces to a trivial signature condition or is empirically false in its
acceleration-equals-gravity reading.

Ostoma, T., & Trushyk, M. (1999). *A Brief Summary of Electromagnetic
Quantum Gravity*.
arXiv:[physics/9902066](https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/9902066)
\[physics.gen-ph\] (22 February 1999). Companion summary paper to
[@OstomaTrushyk1999EMQGEP]. Cited in
§[5.14](#ssec:EquivalencePrincipleUnification){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:EquivalencePrincipleUnification"} and
Theorem [236](#thm:EquivalencePrinciple){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:EquivalencePrinciple"} of the present paper for the
primary-source recognition of the open-problem status of the
equivalence-principle derivation, verbatim from §B: "IN GENERAL
RELATIVITY, THE PRINCIPLE OF EQUIVALENCE MUST BE ACCEPTED ONLY AS A
POSTULATE, AND CANNOT BE DERIVED. Why should there be equivalence
between inertial and gravitational mass? After all, both these mass
types are defined differently in conventional Newtonian physics.
Inertial mass involves accelerated motion, but there appears to be no
motion involved in the definition of gravitational mass. In general
relativity, equivalence has still remained a postulate as first proposed
by Einstein, in spite of 70 years of investigation, albeit a very well
tested postulate."

Ostoma, T., & Trushyk, M. (1999). *Quantum Field Theoretic Derivation of
the Einstein Weak Equivalence Principle Using EMQG Theory*.
arXiv:[physics/9902073](https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/9902073)
\[physics.gen-ph\] (9 February 1999). The Ostoma--Trushyk
electromagnetic-quantum-gravity programme paper attempting a
quantum-vacuum-fluctuations derivation of the equivalence principle.
Cited in
§[5.14](#ssec:EquivalencePrincipleUnification){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:EquivalencePrincipleUnification"} of the present paper
as primary-source articulation of the
equivalence-principle-as-open-problem status and as an
alternative-proposal-not-adopted-in-mainstream-physics. The
Ostoma--Trushyk opening epigraph cites Synge 1960 [@Synge1960] verbatim.
The EMQG programme has not been adopted in mainstream physics; we record
the primary-source recognition of the open-problem status while noting
the alternative-proposal status of the EMQG programme.

Unnikrishnan, C. S., & Gillies, G. T. (2015). *Is the Higgs Mechanism
true to the Equivalence Principle?* International Journal of Modern
Physics D **24**(14), 1544009 (2015). DOI:
[10.1142/S0218271815440095](https://doi.org/10.1142/S0218271815440095).
Gravitation Group, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, Mumbai, India
(Unnikrishnan); School of Engineering and Applied Science, University of
Virginia, Charlottesville (Gillies). Essay received honourable mention
in the Gravity Research Foundation 2015 Awards for Essays on
Gravitation. The primary-source articulation of the
Higgs-equivalence-principle open problem. Verbatim abstract: "We raise
and discuss the fundamental issue whether the interaction-induced
inertia in the Higgs mechanism is the same as the charge of gravity, or
the gravitational mass. True physical mass has to fulfill the dual role
of inertia and the gravitational charge and should respect the weak
equivalence principle. This is not yet addressed in the standard model
that does not incorporate gravity. Hence the Higgs scenario still
requires a gravitational completion. Some relevant analogies where
interaction-induced inertia is not the same as the gravitational charge
are mentioned. Probing this line of thought will provide valuable clues
and perhaps a remarkable answer to the place and role of gravity in the
standard model of particle physics." Load-bearing technical argument
verbatim from the body: "interaction-induced inertia need not always
generate equivalent gravity, as we now argue from a familiar
example... the effective mass of an electron in a solid can be negative
or even diverge in magnitude, seemingly without any gravitational
signature, signifying that the inertia generated by interaction in that
case is only a pseudo-mass without a gravitational implication... This
fact instructs us to be cautious about any scheme that merely provides
inertia in the sense of enhanced reluctance to free motion, without
generating enhanced gravitational field." Verbatim conclusion: "Inertia
that does not contribute its full gravitational equivalence is not true
mass. Gravitational mass could be more fundamental than inertial mass
and the hardest task of the theory is to explain the origin of the
gravitational mass." Cited in
§[5.14](#ssec:EquivalencePrincipleUnification){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:EquivalencePrincipleUnification"} and
Theorem [236](#thm:EquivalencePrinciple){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:EquivalencePrinciple"} of the present paper as
primary-source documentation of the Higgs-equivalence-principle open
problem, and as primary-source articulation of the heavy-fermion
effective-mass-versus-gravitational-mass distinction that
Theorem [236](#thm:EquivalencePrinciple){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:EquivalencePrinciple"} Property (v) of the present paper
engages.

Li, B. (2025). *Revisiting Mass Generation: Higgs Mechanism and a
Topological Alternative via Chronon Field Theory*. Preprints.org
202506.2073, version 1 (25 June 2025). DOI:
[10.20944/preprints202506.2073.v1](https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202506.2073.v1).
Single-author preprint (Bin Li, ORCID 0009-0001-6956-3165). Not yet
peer-reviewed. The 2025 contemporary primary-source articulation of the
Higgs-equivalence-principle open problem and the alternative proposal
closest in spirit to the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework (a unit-norm
future-directed timelike vector field $\Phi^\mu(x)$ as ontological
substrate, with mass arising from solitonic excitations producing both
inertial and gravitational mass). Verbatim from §3.4 (Lack of Insight
into Equivalence Principle): "Another deep shortcoming of the Higgs
mechanism is its failure to illuminate the equivalence between inertial
and gravitational mass. In general relativity (GR), gravitational mass
is the source of spacetime curvature, while inertial mass determines an
object's resistance to acceleration. The equivalence principle posits
that these two quantities are identically equal for all objects---a
principle verified to extremely high precision in experiments. However,
in the SM framework, mass arises from interactions with the Higgs field,
a scalar field that does not couple to spacetime curvature in any
fundamental way. The mechanism is agnostic about gravity: it describes
how particles resist acceleration due to Higgs-mediated interactions,
but not how they gravitate. There is no derivation within the SM showing
why a particle's inertial mass, generated by the Higgs field, should
also be the quantity appearing in the geodesic equation of GR." Cited in
§[5.14](#ssec:EquivalencePrincipleUnification){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:EquivalencePrincipleUnification"},
Theorem [236](#thm:EquivalencePrinciple){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:EquivalencePrinciple"}, and
Remark [245](#rem:FrameworkFirstInLiterature){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:FrameworkFirstInLiterature"} of the present paper. The
Chronon Field Theory and McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework are distinct
(CFT has no derivation of $c, \hbar$, no McGucken-Sphere wavefront, no
dual-channel architecture, no derivation of Standard Model gauge group)
but share the insight that the equivalence-principle problem is closed
by identifying inertial and gravitational mass as having a common
source.

Touboul, P., Métris, G., Rodrigues, M., André, Y., Baghi, Q., Bergé, J.,
Boulanger, D., Bremer, S., Carle, P., Chhun, R., Christophe, B.,
Cipolla, V., Damour, T., Danto, P., Dittus, H., Fayet, P., Foulon, B.,
Gageant, C., Guidotti, P.-Y., Hagedorn, D., Hardy, E., Huynh, P.-A.,
Inchauspé, H., Kayser, P., Lala, S., Lämmerzahl, C., Lebat, V., Leseur,
P., Liorzou, F., List, M., Löffler, F., Panet, I., Pouilloux, B.,
Prieur, P., Rebray, A., Reynaud, S., Rievers, B., Robert, A., Selig, H.,
Serron, L., Sumner, T. J., Tanguy, N., & Visser, P. (2017). *MICROSCOPE
Mission: First Results of a Space Test of the Equivalence Principle*.
Physical Review Letters **119**(23), 231101 (4 December 2017). DOI:
[10.1103/PhysRevLett.119.231101](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.119.231101).
arXiv:[1712.01176](https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.01176). The
state-of-the-art space-based test of the weak equivalence principle from
the MICROSCOPE satellite (launched April 2016, by CNES with
collaboration from ONERA, OCA, DLR, ZARM, and ESA). Verbatim abstract:
"According to the weak equivalence principle, all bodies should fall at
the same rate in a gravitational field. The MICROSCOPE satellite,
launched in April 2016, aims to test its validity at the $10^{-15}$
precision level, by measuring the force required to maintain two test
masses (of titanium and platinum alloys) exactly in the same orbit. A
nonvanishing result would correspond to a violation of the equivalence
principle, or to the discovery of a new long-range force. Analysis of
the first data gives \[no detection of\] (with $1\sigma$ statistical
uncertainty) for the titanium-platinum Eötvös parameter characterizing
the relative difference in their free-fall accelerations." Cited in
§[5.14](#ssec:EquivalencePrincipleUnification){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:EquivalencePrincipleUnification"},
Theorem [236](#thm:EquivalencePrinciple){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:EquivalencePrinciple"}, and
Remark [246](#rem:EquivalenceHonestScope){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:EquivalenceHonestScope"} of the present paper as
primary-source documentation of the empirical equivalence-principle
confirmation at one part in $10^{15}$, consistent with the framework's
identification of inertial-and-gravitational-mass equivalence.

Mancini, C., Tino, G. M., & Capozziello, S. (2025). *Equivalent
Gravities and Equivalence Principle: Foundations and experimental
implications*. Foundations of Physics **55**, 69 (2025). DOI:
[10.1007/s10701-025-00882-x](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10701-025-00882-x).
Received 19 January 2025; Accepted 28 July 2025.
arXiv:[2501.06487](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.06487) \[gr-qc\] (11
January 2025). Affiliations: Mancini at Scuola Superiore Meridionale,
Napoli, and INFN Sezione di Napoli; Tino at Università di Firenze,
European Laboratory for Non-Linear Spectroscopy (LENS), and INFN Sezione
di Firenze; Capozziello at Scuola Superiore Meridionale, Napoli, INFN
Sezione di Napoli, and Dipartimento di Fisica "E. Pancini" at Università
di Napoli "Federico II." The 2025 contemporary peer-reviewed
primary-source review of the equivalence principle in the Geometric
Trinity of Gravity (general relativity GR, teleparallel-equivalent
gravity TEGR, symmetric-teleparallel-equivalent gravity STEGR). Verbatim
abstract content: "In contrast, TEGR and STEGR recover the EP, in
particular in its strong formulation, but do not rely on it as a
principle. The fact that GR, TEGR, and STEGR are equivalent in
non-trivial predictions, but the EP is not necessary for TEGR and STEGR,
suggests that it may not be a fundamental feature but an emergent one."
Verbatim from §2, Problem (vii) "Epistemic justification of the
coincidence between $m_G$ and $m_I$": "There is the problem of how we
can justify the coincidence between gravitational and inertial mass,
which is the basis of the formulation of the WEP... Today, for many
people, this equivalence might seem obvious, but back then, it was not,
and it would not be even today if we 'forgot' to acknowledge this
principle. In other words, *prima facie*, there are no reasons to
postulate the identity $m_G \equiv m_I$, and it is not related to some
fundamental symmetry. Einstein himself embraced it from empirical
reasons. So apart from observations, how one could even imagine this
equivalence?" Verbatim closing line of the introduction: "This, in some
sense, is in line with the intuition by Synge, who considered it only a
midwife and not a fundamental feature of the world." Cited in
§[5.14](#ssec:EquivalencePrincipleUnification){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:EquivalencePrincipleUnification"} and
Remark [245](#rem:FrameworkFirstInLiterature){reference-type="ref"
reference="rem:FrameworkFirstInLiterature"} of the present paper as
primary-source documentation of contemporary peer-reviewed engagement of
the equivalence principle as open problem, with the
Mancini--Tino--Capozziello identification of the $m_G \equiv m_I$
coincidence as the seventh of eight foundational EP problems being the
closest contemporary primary-source articulation of the open problem the
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework closes via
Theorem [236](#thm:EquivalencePrinciple){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:EquivalencePrinciple"} of the present paper. TEGR and
STEGR engage the EP at the pure-gravity level without engaging the Higgs
mechanism, distinct from the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework which
engages both.

London, F., & London, H. (1935). *The Electromagnetic Equations of the
Supraconductor*. Proceedings of the Royal Society of London, Series A:
Mathematical and Physical Sciences **149**(866), 71--88 (1 March 1935).
DOI: [10.1098/rspa.1935.0048](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1935.0048).
Bibcode: 1935RSPSA.149\...71L. The primary-source paper establishing the
London equations for the supraconducting state, postulating
$\vec{j}_s = -(n_s e^2/m_e c) \vec{A}$ which (together with the Maxwell
equations) produces the modified wave equation
$\nabla^2 \vec{B} = (1/\lambda_L^2)\vec{B}$ explaining the Meissner
effect. From the verbatim opening of the paper: "Electric currents are
commonly believed to persist in a supra-conductor without being
maintained by an electromagnetic field. Thus the relation between the
field strength $\vec{E}$ and the current density $\vec{J}$ in a
supraconductor has sometimes been described by means of an 'acceleration
equation,' of the form $\Lambda \dot{\vec{J}} = \vec{E}$;
$\Lambda = m/ne^2$. This equation, which might replace Ohm's law for
supraconductors, simply expresses the influence of the electric part of
the Lorentz force on freely movable electrons of the mass $m$ and charge
$e$." Recognized as "THE FIRST SUCCESSFUL ATTEMPT AT CHARACTERIZING THE
ELECTRODYNAMIC BEHAVIOR OF SUPERCONDUCTORS." Cited in
§[5.17](#ssec:PhotonMassSuperconductor){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:PhotonMassSuperconductor"} of the present paper as the
primary-source origin of the modified-wave-equation content that,
retrospectively (via Anderson 1963
[@Anderson1963PlasmonsGaugeInvarianceMass]), is interpreted as the
photon's effective mass in a superconductor.

Ginzburg, V. L., & Landau, L. D. (1950). *On the Theory of
Superconductivity (K teorii sverkhprovodimosti)*. Zhurnal
Eksperimental'noi i Teoreticheskoi Fiziki (Journal of Experimental and
Theoretical Physics) **20**, 1064--1082 (1950). English translation in:
D. ter Haar (ed.), *Collected papers of L. D. Landau*, Pergamon, Oxford
(1965), pp. 546--568. The primary-source paper establishing the
Ginzburg-Landau phenomenological theory of superconductivity,
introducing the complex order parameter $\psi_s$ (the "superconducting
wave function") and the free energy functional $F[\psi_s, \vec{A}]$
governing it. The Ginzburg-Landau order parameter $\psi_s$ is recognized
in the contemporary literature [@deBruynOuboterOmelyanchouk2017] as the
condensed-matter analogue of the Higgs field: "the relevant
Ginzburg-Landau free energy density $F$ versus $|\psi_s|^2$, which is
often called the 'Higgs field', for both $T > T_c$ and $T < T_c$ when
the symmetry of the 'Higgs field' is broken." Cited in
§[5.17](#ssec:PhotonMassSuperconductor){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:PhotonMassSuperconductor"} of the present paper as the
primary-source origin of the Higgs-field-analogue scalar order parameter
that supplies the photon's perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate contribution
in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's reading of the Anderson-Higgs
mechanism in superconductors. Cited by the 2003 Nobel Prize award to
Ginzburg (with Abrikosov and Leggett) "for pioneering contributions to
the theory of superconductors and superfluids."

Wilczek, F. (2005). *In search of symmetry lost*. Nature **433**(7023),
239--247 (20 January 2005). DOI:
[10.1038/nature03281](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature03281). Read at
primary source. Frank Wilczek (then at MIT; subsequently 2004 Nobel
laureate in physics, with Politzer and Gross, "for the discovery of
asymptotic freedom in the theory of the strong interaction"). The
canonical Wilczek formulation of the equivalence between the electroweak
Higgs sector and the conventional electromagnetic superconductor.
Verbatim from p. 243: "Unlike the photon, which acquires mass only
inside superconductors, $W$ and $Z$ are massive particles even in empty
space. The equations of gauge symmetry, in their pristine form, predict
the existence of these particles, but require that their masses vanish.
To account for the masses of $W$ and $Z$, we must suppose that what we
perceive as empty space is, in reality, a new form of superconductor,
not for electromagnetism, but for its near-relation gauge interactions.
With this interpretation, what we perceive as empty space is not so
empty." Cited in
§[5.17](#ssec:PhotonMassSuperconductor){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:PhotonMassSuperconductor"} of the present paper as
primary-source articulation of the "empty space is a superconductor"
identification that the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework supplies at
deeper grade via the McGucken-Sphere wavefront identification
(Theorem [251](#thm:PhotonMassSuperconductor){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:PhotonMassSuperconductor"} Property (iv) and the
paragraph closure "Wilczek's 'empty space is a superconductor' is the
McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's identity").

Allen, R. E. (2013). *The
London-Anderson-Englert-Brout-Higgs-Guralnik-Hagen-Kibble-Weinberg
mechanism and Higgs boson reveal the unity and future excitement of
physics*. arXiv:[1306.4061](https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.4061) \[hep-ph\]
(18 June 2013). Read in full at primary source. Roland E. Allen, Physics
and Astronomy Department, Texas A&M University, College Station, TX
(email: allen@tamu.edu). The contemporary primary-source articulation of
the eight-figure unification chain --- London, Anderson, Englert, Brout,
Higgs, Guralnik, Hagen, Kibble, Weinberg --- that traces the modern
mass-generation mechanism from the 1935 London superconductor equations
to the 1967 Weinberg electroweak Yukawa coupling. Verbatim from the
introduction: "In 1935, Fritz and Heinz London effectively gave mass to
the photon in a superconductor, and thereby provided a macroscopic
explanation of the Meissner effect --- the expulsion of a magnetic field
from a superconductor. From a modern perspective, this mechanism for
giving mass to a vector boson can be interpreted as implying an
effective breaking of gauge invariance. In 1963, following closely
related treatments by himself and others, Philip Anderson pointed out
another aspect important for the construction of models in particle
physics: A would-be zero-mass Nambu-Goldstone boson in a superconductor
is effectively eaten by the photon to become a finite-mass longitudinal
mode, which appears as a plasmon in a nonrelativistic treatment."
Verbatim from §2: "It is a true demonstration of the unity of physics
that this Meissner effect in a superconducting metal and the short range
of the weak nuclear force in the universe have the same origin: In each
case the vector bosons (photons or $W$ and $Z$ bosons) grow masses
because they are coupled to a field which forms a condensate at low
temperature, as the metal is cooled in the laboratory or the universe
expands and cools after the Big Bang." Allen quotes Weinberg's 2005
*Quantum Theory of Fields Volume 2* (pp. 332--352) verbatim: "A
superconductor is simply a material in which electromagnetic gauge
invariance is spontaneously broken." Cited in
§[5.17](#ssec:PhotonMassSuperconductor){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:PhotonMassSuperconductor"} of the present paper as
primary-source documentation of the orthodox-literature recognition of
the same-mathematical-equations of the electroweak Higgs mechanism and
the Anderson-Higgs superconductor mechanism.

Weinberg, S. (2005). *The Quantum Theory of Fields, Volume 2: Modern
Applications*. Cambridge University Press, Cambridge. ISBN
978-0-521-67054-8 (paperback, originally published 1996). Steven
Weinberg (1933--2021), University of Texas at Austin; 1979 Nobel
laureate in physics with Glashow and Salam "for their contributions to
the theory of the unified weak and electromagnetic interaction between
elementary particles." Chapter 21 ("Spontaneously Broken Gauge
Symmetries"), pp. 332--352, contains Weinberg's full treatment of the
electroweak symmetry-breaking sector with the verbatim assertion (quoted
via Allen 2013 [@Allen2013LAEBHGHKW], p. 2): "A superconductor is simply
a material in which electromagnetic gauge invariance is spontaneously
broken." Cited in
§[5.17](#ssec:PhotonMassSuperconductor){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:PhotonMassSuperconductor"} of the present paper as
primary-source standard-modern-physics articulation of the
gauge-invariance-breaking-as-superconductor identification of the
electroweak Higgs sector. Citation via Allen 2013 (which I have read in
full at primary source); the full Weinberg textbook treatment is the
standard graduate QFT reference and is the canonical orthodox treatment.

de Bruyn Ouboter, R., & Omelyanchouk, A. N. (2017). *On massive photons
inside a superconductor as follows from London and Ginzburg-Landau
theory*. Low Temperature Physics / Fizika Nizkikh Temperatur **43**(7),
1109--1112 (Received 3 April 2017, published online 25 May 2017).
[scholarlypublications.universiteitleiden.nl/access/item:2903308/view](https://scholarlypublications.universiteitleiden.nl/access/item:2903308/view).
Read in full at primary source. Affiliations: R. de Bruyn Ouboter at
Kamerlingh Onnes Laboratory, Leiden Institute of Physics, Leiden
University, P.O. 9506, 2300 RA Leiden, The Netherlands (email:
r.de.bruijn.ouboter@umail.leidenuniv.nl); A. N. Omelyanchouk at B.
Verkin Institute for Low Temperature Physics and Engineering, National
Academy of Sciences of Ukraine, 47 Nauky Ave., Kharkiv 61103, Ukraine.
The 2017 primary-source derivation of the photon's effective mass inside
a superconductor as the Compton frequency of the
photon-Cooper-pair-condensate composite system. Verbatim core structure
(p. 1109): "A phenomenological derivation is given that photons behave
inside a superconductor as if they have mass by comparison of the
original first equation of the London's and the equations for the
electromagnetic field with the time-dependent relativistic Schrödinger
equation. The photons move through a medium, the Ginzburg-Landau free
energy density, inside the superconductor in which they acquire mass.
*The Compton wave length of the massive photons is equal to $2\pi$ times
the London penetration depth and the mass of the photon is equal to
$\hbar/c\lambda_L$.*" Verbatim from p. 1110 on the Ginzburg-Landau
"Higgs field" identification: "In the spirit of the 'Higgs mechanism'
and the principle of broken symmetry which starts when the temperature
is lowered from $T > T_c$ to $T < T_c$ we plot the relevant
Ginzburg-Landau free energy density $F$ versus $|\psi_s|^2$, which is
often called the 'Higgs field'... The photon in the superconductor does
interact with the Ginzburg-Landau or 'Higgs field', it interacts with
this field, gains energy, slows down, the 'field' dragged on the photon
and the interaction with the particle photon and the field is manifested
as a resistance of the photon particle acceleration. When the photon
particle moves at constant velocity it is not affected by the
'field'...During the cooling of the superconductor from $T > T_c$ to
$T < T_c$ each photon inside the superconductor acquires an energy
$mc^2$." Verbatim numerics (p. 1111): for $\lambda_L(0) = 500$ Å=
$5 \times 10^{-8}$ m, the photon effective mass is
$m = \hbar/(c\lambda_L) = 10^{-34}/(3 \times 10^8 \times 5 \times 10^{-8}) \approx 7 \times 10^{-36}$ kg,
with the plasma frequency
$\omega_p(0) = c/\lambda_L = mc^2/\hbar \approx 6 \times 10^{15}$ Hz.
Cited in §[5.17](#ssec:PhotonMassSuperconductor){reference-type="ref"
reference="ssec:PhotonMassSuperconductor"} of the present paper as the
primary-source identification of the photon's effective mass in a
superconductor with its Compton frequency at $\omega_C = c/\lambda_L$,
which the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's
Theorem [251](#thm:PhotonMassSuperconductor){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:PhotonMassSuperconductor"} reads as direct
condensed-matter empirical confirmation of the
perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate identification of mass applied at the
eV scale.

Moffat, J. W. (1993). *Spontaneous violation of Lorentz invariance and
ultra-high-energy cosmic rays*. Foundations of Physics **23**(3),
411--437 (March 1993). DOI:
[10.1007/BF01883725](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01883725).
arXiv:[gr-qc/9209001](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9209001). John W.
Moffat, Department of Physics, University of Toronto; subsequently at
the Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics, Waterloo, Ontario.
Moffat is the founder of the Modified Gravity (MOG /
Scalar-Tensor-Vector-Gravity) programme and has a sustained
mainstream-physics publication record in gravitational physics. Read in
full at primary source. The 1993 paper proposes a Higgs-mechanism
construction in which a scalar field with a vector index $\phi^a$ (NOT
the electroweak Higgs of the Standard Model) acquires a vacuum
expectation value in the time direction of the local tangent frame,
breaking the local Lorentz symmetry $SO(3,1) \to O(3)$ spontaneously.
Verbatim from the abstract: "The time direction of the vacuum
expectation value of the scalar Higgs field generates a time asymmetry,
which defines the cosmological arrow of time and the direction of
increasing entropy." Cited in
§[5.15.2](#sssec:FourComptonVectorUnification){reference-type="ref"
reference="sssec:FourComptonVectorUnification"} of the present paper as
the primary-source contemporary precedent that comes closest in the
orthodox-tradition literature to identifying "the Higgs vacuum
expectation value points in the time direction." *The Moffat 1993
framework is distinct from the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework*:
Moffat's $\phi^a$ is a separate gravitational scalar field (NOT the
electroweak Higgs doublet $H$ of the Standard Model); Moffat's "time
direction" is the standard general-relativity time coordinate $x^0 = ct$
in the local tangent frame (NOT a separate $x_4$ axis expanding at
velocity $c$ from every event); Moffat does not have $dx_4/dt = ic$ as
principle; Moffat does not identify the electroweak Higgs with the $+ic$
direction; Moffat does not derive the Standard Model gauge group, the
principle of least action, or the equivalence principle from a single
principle. The distinction between Moffat's
gravitational-scalar/time-coordinate identification and the McGucken
$dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's electroweak-Higgs/$x_4$-axis/$+ic$-direction
identification is central: the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework's
Four-Compton-Vector Unification
(Theorem [242](#thm:FourComptonVectorUnification){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:FourComptonVectorUnification"} of the present paper)
operates on $K^\mu = p^\mu/\hbar$ as one tensorial object on spacetime
under $dx_4/dt = ic$, with the actual electroweak Higgs as the
field-theoretic encoding of where the magnitude $|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2}$
comes from for fundamental fermions, distinct from any
time-coordinate-direction identification of a separate gravitational
scalar.

Müller, H., Peters, A., & Chu, S. (2010). *A precision measurement of
the gravitational redshift by the interference of matter waves*. Nature
**463**(7283), 926--929 (18 February 2010). DOI:
[10.1038/nature08776](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature08776). Holger
Müller (Department of Physics, University of California, Berkeley),
Achim Peters (Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin), Steven Chu (Lawrence
Berkeley National Laboratory and Stanford University; 1997 Nobel
laureate in physics for laser cooling of atoms). The 2010 *Nature* paper
that reinterprets atom-interferometry experiments as precision
measurements of the gravitational redshift at the Compton frequency of
the atom. Verbatim from the abstract: "Atoms can be considered as clocks
operating at the Compton frequency $\nu_C = mc^2/h$, with $m$ the rest
mass and $h$ Planck's constant. By analysing previous experiments with
$\textsuperscript{133}$Cs atoms, we obtain a 7-million-fold improvement
of the precision of gravitational redshift tests." Cited in
§[5.15.3](#sssec:FiveWayStructuralIdentity){reference-type="ref"
reference="sssec:FiveWayStructuralIdentity"} of the present paper as
primary-source articulation of the Compton-frequency phase-accumulation
reading of atom interferometry, with the framework's Five-Way Structural
Identity reading this as Context B (the proper-time integrand of the
wavefunction phase) of
Theorem [243](#thm:FiveWayStructuralIdentity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:FiveWayStructuralIdentity"}.

Wolf, P., Blanchet, L., Bordé, C. J., Reynaud, S., Salomon, C., &
Cohen-Tannoudji, C. (2011). *Does an atom interferometer test the
gravitational redshift at the Compton frequency?* Classical and Quantum
Gravity **28**(14), 145017 (21 July 2011). DOI:
[10.1088/0264-9381/28/14/145017](https://doi.org/10.1088/0264-9381/28/14/145017).
arXiv:[1012.1194](https://arxiv.org/abs/1012.1194). Authors: Peter Wolf
(LNE-SYRTE, Observatoire de Paris); Luc Blanchet (Institut
d'Astrophysique de Paris); Christian J. Bordé (LNE-SYRTE); Serge Reynaud
(Laboratoire Kastler Brossel); Christophe Salomon (LKB); Claude
Cohen-Tannoudji (Collège de France; 1997 Nobel laureate in physics with
Chu and Phillips for laser cooling of atoms). The 2011 *Classical and
Quantum Gravity* primary-source critique of Müller--Peters--Chu
[@MullerPetersChu2010Nature] arguing that the Compton-phase difference
between atom-interferometer paths is zero in any consistent metric
theory using a single Lagrangian and the principle of least action.
Verbatim from the abstract: "We show that the difference of 'Compton
phases' between the two paths of the interferometer is actually zero in
a large class of theories, including general relativity, all metric
theories of gravity, most non-metric theories and most theoretical
frameworks used to interpret the violations of the equivalence
principle. Therefore, in most plausible theoretical frameworks, there is
no redshift effect and atom interferometers only test the universality
of free fall. We also show that frameworks in which atom interferometers
would test the redshift pose serious problems, such as (i) violation of
the Schiff conjecture, (ii) violation of the Feynman path integral
formulation of quantum mechanics and of the principle of least action
for matter waves, (iii) violation of energy conservation, and more
generally (iv) violation of the particle-wave duality in quantum
mechanics." Cited in
§[5.15.3](#sssec:FiveWayStructuralIdentity){reference-type="ref"
reference="sssec:FiveWayStructuralIdentity"} of the present paper as
primary-source articulation of the magnitude-cancellation
(universality-of-free-fall) reading of atom interferometry, with the
framework's Five-Way Structural Identity reading this as Context D (the
equivalence-principle identity, with the magnitude factoring out of the
geodesic equation) of
Theorem [243](#thm:FiveWayStructuralIdentity){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:FiveWayStructuralIdentity"}. The framework's reading
dissolves the Wolf et al. vs. Müller--Peters--Chu controversy: both
sides are reading the same five-way identity from different angles, with
the Compton-phase accumulation (Müller--Peters--Chu, Context B) and the
magnitude-cancellation in the geodesic equation (Wolf et al., Context D)
being simultaneous consequences of one magnitude $|K^\mu K_\mu|^{1/2}$
playing multiple roles.
:::
